sections.heading: Permits, invoices and the questions that change what you pay
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the federal portal states it is granted free of charge for two years, covering teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service listing, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time via the smart app, website and e-services system.

Two commercial consequences follow. Because the permit is free, any line on an invoice describing a licensing, registration or compliance fee is a markup with a story attached, and you are entitled to ask what it is for. And because the permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, a cheap arrangement with your child's own subject teacher is the one deal that is not worth the saving. Abu Dhabi's ADEK ethics rules for school staff point the same way, prohibiting paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school.

Four questions will tell you most of what you need before you pay anything. Does the tutor hold the MoHRE permit. Is the quoted dirham figure inclusive of any tax, and is it per hour or per session. What exactly happens to the fee if a session is cancelled by either side within twenty-four hours. And what the replacement arrangement is if the tutor becomes unavailable mid-term. Those four answers predict the total cost of a term far better than the headline rate does. For the record, IB Gram holds no licence, accreditation or partnership from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or any awarding body, and operates no office in the UAE.
bullets: The permit is free of charge for two years; no licensing fee should appear on an invoice
The permit's code of conduct bars tutoring students from the tutor's own school
Ask whether the figure is per hour or per session, and whether any tax is included

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the stage
process.description: Which subject, Higher or Standard Level, which Diploma year, and what the last marked assessment said. Three lines is enough. Without the level and stage any figure quoted at you is a guess, and we would rather not guess at you.

process.description: We come back with the format we think fits, how many sessions, over how many weeks, and what the alternative to tutoring would be. The plan names the review date up front, which is what makes the spend auditable later.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the proposed tutor
process.description: One full session with the tutor who would do the work, using your child's own marked paper, before any card details are taken. The note afterwards shows you what the weekly record would look like.

process.title: Agree the terms in writing before the first payment
process.description: Rate per session, session length, cancellation window, replacement arrangement if the tutor becomes unavailable, and whether any tax applies. Four lines, agreed once, that remove most of what goes wrong commercially later.

process.title: Review at week six against the school's marks
process.description: We read the school's assessment marks from the block next to the session notes and say plainly whether to continue, change subject, change format, or stop. Extending a block without that reading is how a budget quietly doubles.

whyPoints.title: Format matched to the diagnosis
whyPoints.description: A deadline block, a technique sprint and weekly content teaching cost different amounts and fix different problems. We name which one the marked work points to before quoting anything, because the mismatch is where families overspend.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the rate

faqs.question: What does an IB Diploma tutor cost per hour for a family living in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Published figures in this market cluster into bands. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33 to 65 an hour, qualified online subject tutors from AED 150 to 300, in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate, and named IB specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with premium examiner-led tutors quoted as high as AED 650. Those are other providers' published rates read in October 2026, not ours. A Sharjah quote lands inside those bands according to subject, level, hour of the evening and how scarce the specialism is locally, which is why nobody can responsibly give you one figure before asking.

faqs.question: Why do Higher Level subjects cost more per term than Standard Level ones?
faqs.answer: Two multiplying effects rather than one. The hourly rate is higher because Higher Level courses carry option topics and additional papers, which narrows the pool of tutors who can teach them confidently, and in Sharjah that pool is thin to begin with. The hour count is also higher, because there is more taught content and the internal assessment expects greater independence. Families who budget only for the rate difference are surprised by the term total. The practical response is to concentrate sustained support in the one Higher Level subject that gates the university plan rather than spreading hours thinly across three.

faqs.question: Is a package of ten sessions genuinely cheaper than paying week by week?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the saving is usually smaller than the risk. Monthly packages advertised in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. The discount against an hourly rate is real, but a package bought before any diagnosis commits you to a format that may be wrong, and the sessions you do not use are rarely refundable. The lower-risk sequence is a diagnostic session, a short block, a review at week six, and a package only once you know the format and the tutor are right.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP2 student usually need?
faqs.answer: One a week in the subject being supported through the autumn, moving to two a week in the eight to twelve weeks before the examination session, in that subject only. Three subjects at two sessions a week is a volume almost no student can absorb alongside Diploma coursework, and it is the pattern that produces exhausted students and no measurable change. If marked mocks suggest three subjects all need intensive work, the realistic conversation is about subject level or candidate strategy with the school, not about buying eighteen hours a month.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate go up as the May examination session gets closer?
faqs.answer: Availability tightens sharply and effective prices rise with it, across every provider in this market. Demand concentrates into the same twelve-week window for every Diploma candidate in the UAE, so the specialists in scarce subjects fill their evening slots first and discounting disappears. The practical consequence is about booking rather than about rate: diagnose in the autumn and secure the pre-examination block early. A family that starts looking for Higher Level Chemistry support in March is competing for the last slots in the thinnest subject market in the emirate.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects are hardest to find locally, and does that change the price?
faqs.answer: Higher Level Chemistry and Physics, Mathematics Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, Psychology, Arabic A at Higher Level and Theory of Knowledge are the thin markets in the northern emirates. In a thin market the binding constraint is availability rather than the hourly figure, and an in-home requirement frequently produces no match at all. Diploma cohorts at individual Sharjah campuses are small, so recent experience of a particular Higher Level option topic is genuinely rare. Removing the geographic constraint by taking lessons online is what turns an empty search into a match, and it does so without a scarcity premium for travel.

faqs.question: If lessons are online, am I still paying for a tutor's travel somewhere in the rate?
faqs.answer: No, and that is most of the gap between the published bands. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180 to 500 an hour in this market and qualified online one-to-one at AED 150 to 300. A tutor driving to Al Majaz for a 5pm start spends around ninety minutes in traffic to teach sixty, and that time is priced into the rate, the minimum session length and the cancellation terms. Online delivery removes it, and it removes the cap on how many sessions a tutor can take in an evening, which is why online availability in the contested 7pm hour is better.

faqs.question: Do the dirham figures quoted to us include tax?
faqs.answer: Ask, every time, of every provider, and get the answer in writing before the first payment. It is a fair and simple question and a reluctance to answer it tells you something. What this page will not do is state the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees as settled fact, because that position should come from the Federal Tax Authority rather than from a tutoring website. Keep the question narrow and answerable: is the figure you have quoted me inclusive, is it per hour or per session, and what is the cancellation window. Those three answers predict a term's actual cost better than the rate does.

faqs.question: What does Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge support cost compared with a subject?
faqs.answer: Less in total, because it is bought as a finite block rather than a term. Published specialist rates apply per session, but the volume is four to eight sessions for an Extended Essay across two deadlines, or fortnightly sessions for Theory of Knowledge, rather than a weekly commitment across two years. At mid-band online rates that is roughly AED 1,200 to 2,400 for the Extended Essay work spread over both Diploma years. The reason Sharjah families buy it is thin supervisor coverage in specialised essay subjects at schools with small Diploma cohorts, not dissatisfaction with their school.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take two of my child's six Diploma subjects, and does that save money?
faqs.answer: It can work for a pair within one discipline, such as Mathematics and Physics, or Economics and Business Management, and the saving is in scheduling rather than in rate. A single tutor who sees the same student twice a week carries the context across, which reduces wasted setup time at the start of each session. Across unrelated subjects it is usually a false economy: a tutor genuinely strong at Higher Level Chemistry and at English A Language and Literature is rare, and the weaker of the two subjects is where the hours quietly stop working.

faqs.question: What does supporting one Higher Level subject across both Diploma years add up to?
faqs.answer: At published mid-band online rates and a realistic volume, a plan that runs a bridge block, weekly content support through DP1, an internal assessment block and a pre-examination sprint comes to somewhere in the region of AED 10,000 to 21,000 across two years. That range is illustrative of market rates rather than a quotation, and the spread is wide because it depends entirely on how long the weekly phase runs. The controllable variable is the review: families who reassess at week six and stop or narrow when the evidence says so land near the bottom of that range.

faqs.question: Is group tutoring worth the saving for a Diploma subject in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: The saving is real, with published small-group rates roughly a third to a half of one-to-one, but availability locally is the problem. A group needs three or four students at the same subject, the same level, the same school option topic and the same free evening, and Diploma cohorts at individual Sharjah campuses are small enough that this rarely assembles outside Mathematics and Standard Level Biology. Where it does assemble it suits content revision and suits technique work poorly, because mark recovery depends on which specific papers each student is dropping marks in.

faqs.question: Should we pay for support in DP1 or wait until DP2?
faqs.answer: DP1, and earlier than most families do. The cheapest hours in the whole plan are the bridging ones before DP1 starts and the content ones in the first two terms, because that work is preventive and sits at the lower end of the rate band. The most expensive hours are the corrective ones bought in the DP2 autumn, when a content gap from DP1 has to be closed at the same time as new material and the internal assessment. Waiting also means competing for scarce specialists in the busiest twelve weeks of the market's year.

faqs.question: Do private candidates in Sharjah pay examination entry separately from tutoring?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the two are entirely unconnected. School candidates have entry handled by the school, either inside fees or as an itemised charge. A private candidate arranges entry through a registered examination centre and pays that centre directly, at rates the centre sets. The binding constraint is the deadline rather than the money: entry closes months before the papers are sat, so confirm the route and the date before buying teaching hours. No tutoring provider, including this one, can register a candidate or guarantee a seat at a centre.

faqs.question: Could a tutor charge us for their UAE permit?
faqs.answer: They should not, because the permit costs nothing. The UAE government portal states that the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page for Private Tutor Licensing lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Any invoice line describing a licensing, registration or compliance charge is therefore a markup, and asking what it covers is reasonable. The related question worth asking is whether the tutor holds the permit at all, since anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to support a Diploma student on a tight budget?
faqs.answer: Buy a diagnosis, then buy narrowly. One diagnostic session with a written plan costs a fraction of a month of weekly tutoring and frequently shows that the problem is one paper's technique or one unfinished internal assessment rather than a subject. Then buy the smallest intervention that addresses it: a four-session block, or an eight-week sprint before the examination session, in one subject. Set a review date before you start and treat stopping as a legitimate result. Spreading a small budget weekly across three subjects is the one approach that reliably produces no visible change.

sharjah/ib-diploma-tutor.closingHeading: Get the number before you get the pitch
sharjah/ib-diploma-tutor.closingBody: Send three lines: the subject, whether it is Higher or Standard Level, and which Diploma year your child is in, with the last marked assessment if you have it. We will come back with a format, a session count, a review date and a figure, and we will say where the published market bands put that work so you can compare it against anyone else. If the marked paper says the problem is one paper's technique rather than a term of teaching, we will say that instead and the plan will be shorter and cheaper. The trial lesson is free, runs one-to-one over live video on Sharjah time, and comes before any payment.

intro.heading: What a Sharjah parent can actually check, six weeks in
paragraphs: Biology is the Diploma subject where it is easiest to feel productive and hardest to prove progress. The content is enormous, the vocabulary is specialised, and a student who has read the chapter and highlighted it genuinely feels better prepared. Then a test comes back at 4. The weekly tutoring hour starts, the student reports that the sessions are useful, the next test comes back at 4, and nobody can say what has gone wrong, because nothing in the arrangement produces evidence.

This page is built around the opposite arrangement. The question we think a Sharjah parent should be able to answer after six weeks is not whether your child likes the tutor. It is narrower: what did a marked script say in week one, what does a marked script say now, and which specific thing accounts for the difference. That is answerable only if marked work exists, dated, at both ends. So the sessions here are designed around producing it rather than around covering content and hoping.

In practice that means three artefacts. The first is the timed script. Each session ends with questions sat under time, returned marked before the next lesson, with the mark scheme logic written on the page rather than a score at the top. The second is the draft log on the scientific investigation: four drafts, each with a stated purpose, each comment dated and keyed to a criterion, so the movement between drafts is visible rather than remembered. The third is a one-line weekly note naming the topic or the criterion that moved - the dullest of the three and the most useful, because it is the one that reveals a plateau.

A plateau is the thing this arrangement is designed to catch early. Six weeks of pleasant sessions with no measurable change is a real outcome, and it usually means one of three things: the match is wrong, the diagnosis was wrong, or the student is not doing the between-session work. All three are fixable, and all three are invisible without a record. We would rather hand you the evidence that a tutor is not working than keep a comfortable arrangement going for a term.

The Sharjah specifics sit on top of that. Many of our Diploma biology students attend SPEA-regulated campuses inside the emirate; many others commute across the Dubai boundary from Al Nahda and Al Qasimia, which changes the school calendar and the realistic session time. Lessons are delivered online over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE - home visits are an India-only service - and for Higher Level biology that means the specialist pool is national rather than whatever is within a twenty-minute drive of your building.

sharjah/ib-dp-biology-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Higher Level biology is reached from two directions in Sharjah - through the Middle Years Programme or through an IGCSE science - and the evidence a student arrives with differs sharply between them.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Biology
programmes.description: The two-year course at Higher or Standard Level, running 240 taught hours at Higher Level against 180 at Standard Level, with around forty hours of practical work. Assessment combines written papers with the scientific investigation, a single internally assessed report capped at 3,000 words and marked against four criteria. The written papers reward precise terminology, data interpretation and structured extended responses in roughly equal measure.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah the evidence a student brings to a first session varies by campus. Some schools return marked papers with mark scheme annotations; others return a percentage and a comment. Where the school provides the first kind, we build on it rather than duplicating it. Where it provides the second, the first fortnight is spent generating a marked baseline of our own, because without one there is nothing to measure the term against.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme sciences
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria that reward inquiry design, scientific communication and reflection. Students arrive in DP1 from the MYP with strong investigation instincts and often with less practice at the dense, terminology-exact short answers the Diploma papers want. The first marked Diploma script usually shows this clearly: good structure, insufficient precision.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah campuses run the MYP directly into the Diploma, and those students can usually show two years of criterion-referenced feedback. That history is useful evidence and we ask for it. A student joining DP1 in Sharjah from an IGCSE route has no criterion-referenced record at all, which makes an early baseline script more important rather than less.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE Biology
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Biology carries syllabus code 0610 and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology is 4BI1. Both cover cell biology, transport, respiration, genetics and ecology, and both reward recall more heavily than the Diploma does. Neither requires error bars to be interpreted or a statistical test to be discussed, which is why data-handling questions ambush DP1 students who scored A grades at IGCSE.
programmes.countryNote: The Sharjah IGCSE cohort is large, and the biology bridge into DP1 is specific rather than general: statistical reasoning, error bars, the habit of quoting data when describing a trend, and the shift from naming to explaining. Six to eight sessions in the summer before DP1 close most of it, and they produce a marked baseline that the whole of DP1 can then be measured against.

programmes.name: The Diploma core alongside biology
programmes.description: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS run alongside the six subjects. Biology students write a disproportionate share of Extended Essays, because the subject feels approachable, and a good number of those essays stall on method feasibility. The core deadlines also compete directly with the biology investigation for the same weeks of DP2.
programmes.countryNote: In a Sharjah DP2 autumn term the internal deadline calendar is the real constraint on a biology plan. Investigation deadlines, Extended Essay drafts and mock examinations tend to land within a few weeks of each other, and the schedule differs between SPEA-regulated campuses and the Dubai schools Sharjah families commute to. We ask for the school's internal deadline list before setting the term plan.

sharjah/ib-dp-biology-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Higher Level biology rarely arrives alone. These are the courses our Sharjah biology students most often carry alongside it, and the note says what each one does to the evidence picture.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The subject on this page. Higher Level losses concentrate in extended responses, genetics problems and data interpretation rather than in recall. A marked Standard Level script shows a different pattern, mostly terminology and incomplete explanations, so the two levels need separate plans.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The usual second science in a medicine-facing choice. Chemistry rewards exact numerical work; biology rewards precise terminology and structured argument. Students who carry both often import chemistry brevity into biology extended responses and lose marks for insufficient development.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Shares the research-methods vocabulary with biology and the evaluation habit that biology extended responses reward. Students taking both get a real advantage on questions about experimental design, provided they keep the two sets of terminology apart.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Overlaps heavily with human physiology. The overlap is genuine and the assessment style is not: a student who revises physiology once for both subjects often writes a sports science answer in a biology paper and loses the detail marks.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Covers ecology, energy flow and biodiversity from a systems perspective. Biology students find it familiar and under-answer it, because a systems question wants a different kind of response from a biology ecology question.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The statistics content supports the data-handling side of biology directly: correlation, significance, sampling. A biology student who is secure on this course reads error bars and test results with far less hesitation in a Paper 2 data question.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: More algebraic and less statistical. It supports the quantitative parts of biology adequately but leaves the statistical reasoning to be taught in the biology sessions, which is worth knowing when planning hours across both subjects.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The extended response in biology is a writing task with a science mark scheme. Students whose English A work is strong usually structure biology essays well; students who struggle there tend to lose biology marks for organisation rather than for content.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in biology
subjects.description: A popular and risky choice. Biology essays need a workable method and often primary data, and the ones that stall do so because the question could not be answered with available organisms, equipment or time. The feasibility conversation belongs in DP1.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Biology supplies some of the strongest Theory of Knowledge examples available - models, classification, the status of evidence from a single study - and students rarely use them, because they treat the course as unrelated to their sciences.

sections.heading: A marked script tells you things a school report cannot
paragraphs: A school report compresses a term into a grade and two sentences. It is written by a teacher carrying twenty-five students, and it is accurate at the level of resolution it was designed for. It cannot tell you that your child is losing four marks a paper on command terms, or that their genetics problems are right but their extended responses are unstructured, or that they are answering biology questions in sports science vocabulary. A marked script tells you all three, because the marks are lost in visible places.

This is why the first fortnight with a new Higher Level biology student produces a baseline rather than a lesson plan. The student sits a short timed set under conditions, and the tutor marks it against the published mark scheme and writes the reasoning on the page. The output is a short list of named failure modes with a mark cost attached to each. Not a general impression that the student needs to work on data questions, but a note that in this script, data questions lost six marks and extended responses lost nine, and the nine are the cheaper nine to recover.

The second thing the baseline does is make the rest of the term falsifiable. Six weeks later the same failure modes get retested, and one of three things is true: they have closed, they have narrowed, or they have not moved. The third outcome is the valuable one, because it arrives early enough to change something. A tutoring arrangement with no baseline cannot produce that finding at all, which is why unproductive arrangements in this market tend to run for a full term before anyone notices.

We keep the scripts in one place and dated, and we are happy for a school's biology department to read them. Nothing in the record is written for the parent's comfort. A plateau written down plainly is more use to you than a reassuring message after a lesson, and in our experience Sharjah parents who have paid for a term of tutoring that produced nothing measurable are the ones who ask for this arrangement first.

sections.heading: Reading a marked biology paper, question type by question type
paragraphs: Higher Level biology papers assess several distinguishable skills, and a marked script shows which of them is leaking marks. Multiple-choice questions test recognition and the ability to eliminate under time. Data-based questions test whether a student can read an unfamiliar graph or table, describe a trend while quoting the data, and reason about error bars and significance. Short-answer questions test precision of terminology. Extended responses test structured biological argument with named examples. These fail independently of one another.

The most common pattern we see in a Sharjah DP1 script is strong multiple choice, acceptable short answers, and a collapse in the data and extended-response sections. That pattern is diagnostic: it means the content is largely in place and the examinable skills around it are not. It also means the recoverable marks are concentrated and cheap, because describing a trend with data quoted and structuring an extended response are both trainable in weeks rather than months.

The opposite pattern - weak multiple choice with reasonable extended responses - points at content gaps rather than technique, and needs a different term plan: topic-by-topic repair with retrieval practice between sessions, and no point at all in drilling essay structure yet. Running the wrong plan is the most expensive mistake available in Diploma biology tutoring, and it is almost always caused by nobody having looked at a marked script before deciding.

The table below sets out what each question type rewards, what a script reveals when that type goes wrong, and the drill we use. Component names, section structures and weightings should be confirmed against your own cohort's biology subject guide through the school's science department, because these details are revised between cohorts.

sections.heading: The command term audit, run on one marked paper
paragraphs: Of all the evidence exercises we run, the command term audit changes the most marks for the least effort. It takes one marked paper and one session. Every question is tagged with its command term, and then each answer is judged against what that term demanded rather than against whether the biology was correct. The output is a count: how many marks were lost on questions where the biology was right and the answer shape was wrong.

In Higher Level biology that count is usually between six and twelve marks a paper, and it is almost entirely recoverable. The recurring errors are consistent. State and outline attract a full explanation, which wastes minutes that the extended response then lacks. Explain attracts a description, so the causal chain is missing and half the marks go. Distinguish attracts two separate descriptions rather than a stated difference. Suggest, which signals that the examiner expects reasoning about unfamiliar material, attracts a blank because the student decided they had not been taught it.

Once the count exists, the fix is a habit rather than a course of study. The student underlines the command term before writing anything, and writes to its shape. We rehearse it on short question sets for a fortnight, then re-audit a fresh marked paper and compare the counts. That before-and-after pair is some of the clearest evidence of movement this subject produces, and it is readable by a parent who has never studied biology.

The audit also tends to settle an argument that runs in a lot of households. A student who insists they knew the material is frequently correct, and the marked paper proves it. That changes the conversation at home from effort to method, which is both more accurate and considerably more productive.

sections.heading: A term-by-term ledger: what should have changed, and by when
paragraphs: Evidence is only useful if there is an expectation to compare it against. Without one, any result can be narrated as progress. So we set out, at the start of a block, what should have changed by which week, and we write it down where you can see it. The expectations are deliberately modest and specific, because specific modest claims can be checked and large vague ones cannot.

The pattern that holds for most Higher Level biology students runs roughly like this. In the first fortnight, a baseline script and a named list of failure modes. By week four, the command term count should have fallen measurably on a fresh paper. By week six, data-based questions should show trends described with figures quoted - a change visible on the page, whether or not the mark has moved yet. By week ten, extended responses should be planned before being written, and the structure marks should be arriving. Grade movement, where it comes, usually becomes visible between weeks eight and fourteen rather than earlier, and anyone promising it sooner is describing luck.

The ledger matters most when it is not met. If the command term count has not fallen by week four, the problem is not biology content and more biology content will not fix it. Either the habit is not being practised between sessions, or the tutor is teaching rather than drilling, or the student does not yet believe the audit. Each of those has a different remedy and all of them are cheaper to apply in week four than in week twelve.

Two Sharjah-specific adjustments apply to the timeline. A student who commutes into a Dubai campus loses genuine working time in the car, and the ledger should be set against their available hours rather than a notional evening. And a block that runs across Ramadan should expect a flatter month, with post-Iftar sessions and lighter between-session work, rather than treating the dip as a failure of the plan.

sections.heading: The investigation draft log: four drafts, four jobs
paragraphs: The scientific investigation is written months before the papers are sat, counts for a fifth of the grade, and is the single largest piece of evidence a biology student produces during the Diploma. It is also where feedback most often turns into something vaguer than feedback. A student sends a draft, receives a page of comments on everything at once, changes a few sentences, and sends it again. Four rounds of that produce a tidier document and no movement against the criteria.

We structure it as four drafts with four jobs. The first draft is about method feasibility only, and it happens before data collection: can this question be answered with the organisms, equipment and time actually available, and will the dependent variable produce a range rather than two values. Comments on writing quality at this stage are a distraction. The second draft is about data adequacy: enough points, enough repeats, uncertainty recorded, processing appropriate. The third is about whether the conclusion is supported by the data in front of it, which is where most reports quietly overreach. The fourth is the evaluation, which is where biology investigations most often fall short.

Each comment is dated and quotes the criterion it belongs to, so the log shows what changed between drafts and what did not. That record is useful to the student, and it is the thing that keeps the boundary visible: the comments name gaps, and the student decides what to do about them. No part of the report is authored by the tutor, no sentences are supplied for pasting, and no section is rewritten. The student types every word.

The school supervisor remains the authority throughout. Their internal deadlines govern the schedule, their reading of the criteria governs the interpretation, and where ours differs we say so to the student and defer. Biology investigations involving organisms also carry ethical constraints set by the school, which is a conversation that belongs with the supervisor before a method is settled rather than after.

sections.heading: Where the Higher Level biology content actually sits
paragraphs: Evidence-led tutoring still needs content teaching, and it is worth being concrete about where the Higher Level material concentrates. The course is organised into broad themes covering unity and diversity, form and function, interaction and interdependence, and continuity and change, each carrying additional content for Higher Level candidates only. As in chemistry, the additional sixty hours are not spread evenly: they cluster in the molecular and quantitative parts of the course and in the detail of physiological systems.

In practice the HL-only material produces a recognisable set of marked-script failures. Questions on gene expression and regulation, on the detail of nerve and muscle function, on plant transport and on quantitative ecology are the ones where a student with Standard Level depth writes a plausible answer that scores one mark out of four. The content is learnable; what makes it expensive is that these questions often sit at the end of long questions, so they are also where timing pressure is worst.

The sequence we use is dull and effective. Identify the HL-only topics costing marks on the baseline script. Teach each one, then test it cold two weeks later rather than immediately, because immediate retesting measures short-term recall and nothing else. Retest again at six weeks. A topic that survives both delayed tests is secure; one that passes immediately and fails at two weeks was never learned, and the weekly note records that distinction honestly.

The theme names, content boundaries and hour allocations above should be checked against the biology subject guide for your own child's cohort. Guides are revised, and the version your school's science department holds is the one that governs the examination your child will sit.

sections.heading: Keeping an evidence trail across the Sharjah school week
paragraphs: Private schools in Sharjah sit under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The practical consequence for a biology plan is that the internal calendar - term dates, mock windows, internal assessment deadlines - is set within that framework, and it differs from the calendar at a Dubai campus under KHDA. Since a large share of Sharjah Diploma students attend school in Dubai, the two calendars have to be handled as separate cases.

The journey home is the other variable, and it has a direct effect on the evidence trail rather than only on convenience. A timed script requires a student who can concentrate for forty minutes. A student who reached Al Taawun at a quarter past six after a slow crossing from Al Qusais cannot produce useful timed work at half past six, and pretending otherwise contaminates the record. For commuting families we put the timed element at the start of the following session instead, or shift the slot later and shorten it.

Ramadan reorganises the month. School hours shorten, afternoon concentration drops and families want the evening protected. Our Sharjah Diploma students typically move to post-Iftar sessions or a weekend-weighted pattern, and the ledger for that month is set lower deliberately. In a DP2 year the month frequently lands near an internal deadline or a mock, so the shift is planned in advance rather than improvised in the first week.

Scarcity is the final Sharjah constraint and the reason the delivery model is what it is. Higher Level biology specialists are spread thinly across the emirates, and a specialist reachable in person from Khor Fakkan inside a school evening does not exist in practice. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service. For this subject at this level, the model is what makes a level-matched match possible at all.

sections.heading: What the evidence trail must never be used to hide
paragraphs: A documented process can be used to launder a dishonest one, so the boundaries need stating as plainly as the method. The investigation must be the student's own work. A tutor may teach the biology, explain what a criterion asks for, test whether a method is feasible, challenge a conclusion that the data cannot support, and point at a paragraph and say that it does not yet answer the research question. A tutor may not author any part of the report, supply sentences for insertion, rewrite a section, or hand over a method for the student to adopt as their own.

The draft log makes that boundary easier to hold rather than harder, because it records who wrote what and when. A report that improves between drafts in ways the comments can account for is a student learning. A report that changes character overnight is a different thing, and a documented sequence of drafts is exactly what makes the difference visible - to us, and to a school that asks.

Two related boundaries. We do not supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables as downloads; those are the boards' material, and we reference the official source instead of reproducing it. And we do not describe tutors as examiners for any board unless that status can be evidenced, because in this market examiner status is routinely used to imply access to marking and boundaries that nobody has.

The last point is about claims. We do not publish satisfaction percentages, average score improvements or a count of students taught, because we could not show you the underlying data, the sample or the method. What we can show you is one student's dated scripts and the note that says what moved. That is a smaller claim than the ones this market usually makes, and it is the only one we can put in your hands.

process.title: Send the subject, the year and a recent marked paper
process.description: Higher Level biology, which DP year, which campus - and, if you have one, a recent marked paper or test script. A real marked script shortens the diagnosis by a fortnight, because the failure modes are already visible on it rather than needing to be reproduced.

process.title: A free diagnostic lesson that produces a baseline
process.description: The first session is free and ends with a short timed set sat under conditions. You receive the marked script with the mark scheme logic shown and a written list of named failure modes with a mark cost against each, whether or not you continue with us. That list is the baseline everything afterwards is measured against.

process.title: Agree the ledger, not just the schedule
process.description: We set out what should have changed by week four, week six and week ten, in terms specific enough to be wrong. A plan that says the student will improve in biology cannot be checked. A plan that says the command term count will fall on a fresh paper by week four can.

process.title: Weekly sessions, weekly marked work, weekly note
process.description: Each session produces a dated marked script and one line naming what moved. All of it stays in one place, and you are welcome to share it with the school's biology department. Nothing in the record is written to reassure you; a plateau is recorded as a plateau.

process.title: Six-week review where you decide
process.description: At six weeks we put the baseline and the current script side by side and tell you which failure modes closed and which did not. If two of them have not moved, we change the tutor or the diagnosis rather than asking you to persist for another term on the strength of good lessons.

whyPoints.title: Evidence you can read without knowing biology
whyPoints.description: A marked script with mark scheme logic on the page, a dated draft log and a one-line weekly note are all readable by a parent who last studied biology decades ago. That is deliberate. Progress reporting that only the tutor can interpret is not reporting.

whyPoints.title: A baseline before a plan
whyPoints.description: We produce a marked baseline in the first fortnight and name the failure modes with a mark cost attached. Teaching before diagnosing is the most common way a term of Diploma biology tutoring produces nothing, and it is avoidable in one session.

whyPoints.title: A plateau reported as a plateau
whyPoints.description: Six pleasant sessions with no measurable change is a finding, and we write it down. Knowing at week six that something has to change is worth considerably more than a reassuring message at week twelve.

whyPoints.title: Level-matched rather than locally available
whyPoints.description: Higher Level biology losses sit in the HL-only content and in extended responses, so we match on level as tightly as on subject. Delivery is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE homes, as home visits are an India-only service.

whyPoints.title: The investigation documented, not drafted for the student
whyPoints.description: Four drafts with four jobs, each comment dated and keyed to a criterion, and every word of the report typed by the student. The log protects the student's Diploma and makes the boundary auditable by the school.

whyPoints.title: Market rates named, our figure given against a plan
whyPoints.description: Published market rates for Diploma subject tutoring in the UAE run roughly AED 150-450 an hour by tier and format, with cheaper online options below and premium named tutors above. We quote our own figure after the trial, against the agreed ledger, rather than publishing a rate that ignores the diagnosis.

faqs.question: What does a marked Higher Level biology script tell us that a school report does not?
faqs.answer: It tells you where the marks went, which a grade cannot. A marked script shows whether the loss was command terms, undeveloped extended responses, data questions answered without quoting figures, or genuine content gaps - and those four have entirely different remedies. A school report compresses a term into a grade and two sentences written by a teacher carrying a full cohort, which is accurate at the resolution it was built for. We produce a baseline marked script in the first fortnight precisely so that the term plan is built on visible mark losses rather than on an impression.

faqs.question: Which biology question type costs Sharjah students the most marks?
faqs.answer: On the scripts we see, extended responses first and data-based questions second. Extended responses lose marks for structure rather than content: a long paragraph of accurate but undeveloped statements, with no plan behind it. Data questions lose marks because students describe a trend without quoting the figures that show it, and ignore error bars entirely. Both are technique rather than knowledge, which is why they are the cheapest marks on the paper to recover. A command term audit usually finds a further six to twelve marks a paper where the biology was right and the answer shape was wrong.

faqs.question: How do error bars and statistical significance come up in biology papers?
faqs.answer: They appear in data-based questions, where candidates are shown unfamiliar results and asked to interpret them. The recurring loss is that students describe the means and ignore the bars, then assert a difference the data does not support. What earns marks is noticing overlap, saying what overlap implies about the difference, and using whatever test result is provided rather than restating the numbers. Students taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation usually handle this well. Everyone else needs it taught in the biology sessions, on five unfamiliar graphs a week with the trend sentences marked.

faqs.question: How many drafts should a biology internal assessment go through?
faqs.answer: Four, each with a distinct job rather than a general review. The first looks only at method feasibility and happens before data collection: can the question be answered with the organisms, equipment and time available. The second checks data adequacy - points, repeats, uncertainty, processing. The third asks whether the conclusion is actually supported by the data. The fourth works on the evaluation, where biology reports most often fall short. Four rounds of comments on everything at once produce a tidier document and no movement against the criteria, which is the pattern we are trying to avoid.

faqs.question: What counts as real grade movement in a single term?
faqs.answer: On a whole paper sat under time, a sustained one-grade movement inside fourteen weeks is a good term for a student who started with technique problems rather than content gaps. Before that, the honest evidence is narrower: a falling command term count by week four, trends described with figures quoted by week six, planned extended responses by week ten. Those are visible on the page whether or not the mark has caught up. Anyone promising grade movement in a month is describing luck, and we would rather name the intermediate markers that can actually be checked.

faqs.question: Why does my son write long biology answers and still score poorly?
faqs.answer: Length is not what the mark scheme rewards. An extended response earns marks for a structured argument in which each point is developed and supported with a named example, not for volume of accurate statements. The usual script shows a dense paragraph where four separate points sit side by side, none of them taken past the assertion stage. The fix is to mark the plan separately from the prose for a few weeks: the student writes a four-point plan, the plan is marked, and only then do they write. Marks move before the writing gets any longer.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level biology more memorising than understanding?
faqs.answer: It is both, and the balance shifts between question types. Short answers reward exact terminology, so recall matters and vague paraphrase loses marks that the student feels they deserved. Data questions and extended responses reward reasoning, and no amount of recall rescues them. Students who treat the whole subject as memorisation score well on the first third of a paper and lose the rest, which is a pattern a marked script makes obvious in one reading. The sequence that works is to secure terminology with delayed retesting, then spend the hours on reasoning.

faqs.question: How quickly should we expect to see evidence that the tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Within four weeks you should see something on paper, even if the grade has not moved. The earliest reliable marker is the command term count falling on a fresh marked paper, because that is a habit rather than a body of knowledge. By week six, data-question answers should be quoting figures. By week ten, extended responses should be planned before written. If none of those has happened by week six, the problem is the match, the diagnosis or the between-session work, and all three are cheaper to fix then than at the end of a term.

faqs.question: Which Sharjah schools do your Diploma biology students come from?
faqs.answer: Inside the emirate, mainly the Diploma campuses around Muwaileh, University City and the city centre, all under SPEA, the Sharjah Private Education Authority. A second large group lives in Sharjah and attends school across the Dubai boundary under KHDA, commuting from Al Nahda, Al Qasimia and Al Taawun. The two groups keep different term dates and internal deadline calendars, so we ask for the school's internal deadline list before setting a plan. Schools are named on this page as context for the local education ecosystem; no affiliation with any of them is claimed.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both biology and chemistry for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth testing rather than assuming. A tutor genuinely strong at Higher Level in both sciences exists but is not common, and a tutor who is strong in one and adequate in the other produces a visible asymmetry in the marked scripts within a month. Where the evidence shows that asymmetry, we split the subjects between two tutors even though it is less convenient. The scheduling saving from one tutor is real; it is not worth a term of mediocre marking in the second subject.

faqs.question: Can a biology investigation be run without greenhouse space or animal work?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most of the strongest reports we see avoid both. Investigations using yeast, germinating seeds, enzyme activity, simple human physiology within the school's ethical guidelines, or published ecological and genomic databases are assessed against the same four criteria. The binding question is whether the dependent variable produces a usable range with enough repeats in the time available, not whether the organism is impressive. Ethical constraints on any work involving organisms are set by the school, so that conversation belongs with the supervisor before a method is settled.

faqs.question: What does the weekly session note actually contain?
faqs.answer: One or two lines, written to be read in ten seconds: the topic or criterion worked on, what the marked work showed, and what changed since last week. If nothing changed, it says so. It is deliberately not a summary of the lesson, because a lesson summary tells you what the tutor did rather than what the student can now do. Across a term the notes form a short record that makes a plateau visible as clearly as a gain, and you are welcome to pass them to the school's biology department.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work for a subject with so much practical content?
faqs.answer: For the assessed skills, yes. Data interpretation, extended response structure, genetics problems, terminology and investigation feedback all work at least as well over live video, because everything that matters is on a page that both people can see and annotate. What online delivery cannot replace is bench time, which belongs at school in any case - a tutor arriving at a Sharjah home could not provide laboratory access either. What it does provide is a Higher Level biology specialist on Gulf Standard Time rather than whoever is reachable from your building.

faqs.question: How do we decide whether to change tutor after six weeks?
faqs.answer: On the evidence, not on the relationship. At the six-week review we put the baseline script beside the current one and report which named failure modes closed, which narrowed and which did not move. If two or more have not moved and the between-session work was done, the match or the diagnosis is wrong, and we change the tutor rather than asking you to continue. A student who enjoys the sessions is a good sign and not a result; the scripts are the result.

faqs.question: What happens to the evidence trail during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It continues, with lower expectations written in advance. School hours shorten, late-afternoon concentration drops and families want the evening protected, so our Sharjah Diploma students usually move to post-Iftar sessions or a weekend-weighted pattern with lighter between-session work. The ledger for that month is set deliberately low, so a flat month is recorded as expected rather than as a plateau. In a DP2 year the month often sits close to an internal deadline or a mock, which is a reason to plan the shift before it starts.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level biology required for medicine or biomedical science?
faqs.answer: Many medical, dental and biomedical programmes expect biology or chemistry at Higher Level, and a good number expect both, but requirements are set by each university and revised between admission cycles. Check the published entry requirements for every programme on your child's list, including the universities in Sharjah, Abu Dhabi and abroad, rather than relying on a general rule or on what applied two years ago. From the teaching side, the Higher Level course is the better preparation for a first-year university module whatever the stated minimum turns out to be.

sharjah/ib-dp-biology-hl-tutor.closingHeading: Ask for the baseline script before you commit to a term
sharjah/ib-dp-biology-hl-tutor.closingBody: If you are considering Higher Level biology support in Sharjah, the thing to ask any tutor for is a marked baseline and a written list of what it shows. Our first lesson is free and produces exactly that: a short timed set sat under conditions, marked with the mark scheme logic on the page, and a list of named failure modes with a mark cost against each - yours to keep whether or not you continue with us. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, booked around the Sharjah or Dubai school run. Send the DP year, the campus and a recent marked paper if you have one.

sharjah/ib-dp-business-management-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Business Management at Standard and Higher Level. Each one works from the current subject guide, marks past Paper 2 questions against the published criteria, and coaches the business research project as a process rather than a product. Ask for a trial before you commit to a block.

intro.heading: Business Management is a numerate essay subject, and that is why it catches students out
paragraphs: Most students who struggle with IB Diploma Business Management are not struggling with business. They are struggling with a subject that asks them to calculate a break-even point in one question and argue about organisational ethics in the next, and that marks the two in completely different ways. A student who is comfortable with numbers writes thin evaluation. A student who writes beautifully loses marks because the cash-flow forecast does not balance. Both arrive at a 4 or a 5 and nobody can quite say why.

The current guide, taught in Sharjah schools alongside the rest of the Diploma, organises the course into five units and runs a set of analytical tools across all of them. Unit 1 sets up business organisation, objectives and the external environment. Unit 2 is human resource management. Unit 3 is finance and accounts, which is where the arithmetic lives. Unit 4 is marketing. Unit 5 is operations management. Sitting over the top are the four concepts the course is built on: creativity, change, ethics and sustainability. Those concepts are not decoration. They are the spine of the extended-response marks.

The assessment has three parts. One written paper is built on a case study that schools receive before the examination, so the organisation is known in advance and the questions are not. A second written paper is unseen and carries the data-response work, where candidates read a stimulus, run a calculation and then interpret what the number means for the business. The third part is the business research project, internally marked by the school and externally moderated by the IB, and it is worth a quarter of the grade at both levels. Higher Level students study additional content and sit longer papers.

For a Sharjah family, the practical problem is usually access rather than ability. Business Management is a popular Diploma choice, but the pool of tutors in the emirate who have taught the current guide and marked against its criteria is small. A parent in Al Majaz or Muwaileh who wants a Business Management specialist, rather than a general commerce tutor, is choosing from whoever happens to live within a reasonable drive. That is a geography problem, and it is the one problem online delivery genuinely solves. IB Gram matches your child to a Business Management specialist and the lesson runs over live video, one to one, on your schedule.

This page is written to be useful before you contact anyone. It sets out what each component rewards, where the marks actually go missing, what the Sharjah tutoring market charges in AED, what SPEA and the Ministry of Education require, and exactly what a tutor is allowed to do with a research project. If you read nothing else, read the section on command terms. More Business Management marks are lost to misreading the instruction word than to not knowing the content.

sharjah/ib-dp-business-management-tutor.programmesIntro: Business Management sits at the end of a longer path. A Sharjah student usually arrives in the Diploma from the Middle Years Programme or from an IGCSE Business Studies course, and the gap between those starting points and Diploma expectations is the first thing a tutor should diagnose.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Business Management
programmes.description: Business Management sits in Group 3, individuals and societies, and can be taken at Standard or Higher Level. Both levels cover the five units and the four concepts; Higher Level adds depth and a wider set of quantitative tools, including the more demanding investment appraisal and budgeting work. The assessment combines a paper built on a pre-released case study, an unseen paper carrying the data-response questions, and the internally assessed business research project. Students choose it expecting an easier Group 3 option and discover a subject with real arithmetic in it.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah, Business Management is frequently taken by students who intend to apply to the American University of Sharjah, the University of Sharjah or a UK business school, and the subject's reputation as a soft option is the source of most of the trouble. Tutors working with Sharjah candidates spend the first sessions checking whether the student can actually produce a correct contribution-per-unit figure under time pressure, because that single skill props up a third of the data-response marks.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme - individuals and societies
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme does not teach Business Management as a named subject. It teaches individuals and societies against four criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. Students who did well under those criteria arrive in the Diploma able to structure an argument but unused to applying a named analytical tool to a specific organisation, and unused to being marked on a calculation. The transition is less about new content than about new precision.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah has a smaller MYP cohort than Dubai, so a Diploma Business Management class in the emirate often mixes students from an MYP background with students arriving from CBSE, from a British Year 11 and from the American track. A Sharjah tutor has to establish which of those four routes a student came through before deciding whether the first problem is quantitative confidence, essay structure or the habit of writing about a business in general terms rather than the one in the stimulus.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE Business Studies - the pre-Diploma route
programmes.description: Many Sharjah students reach Diploma Business Management from Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies or the Pearson equivalent. Those courses cover similar territory, including business objectives, stakeholders, marketing mix and basic finance, but reward recall and short application far more heavily than the Diploma does. A student with a strong IGCSE grade can still lose marks in DP1 for writing a correct textbook definition where the question asked for an evaluation of a decision the stimulus organisation has already taken.
programmes.countryNote: Because so many Sharjah schools run a British lower-secondary programme and then offer either A-Levels or the Diploma, a student may be choosing between Cambridge International A-Level Business and DP Business Management in Year 11. The decision matters for university applications in the UAE and abroad, and it changes what tutoring is for: an A-Level route is content-heavy and modular, while the Diploma route spreads one research project across two years.

sharjah/ib-dp-business-management-tutor.subjectsIntro: Business Management is rarely the only subject in play. A Sharjah Diploma student typically wants one or two subjects supported in the same term, and the combinations below are the ones that come up most often alongside Business Management in this emirate.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The five units, the four concepts, and the toolkit of named analytical models. Marks are most often lost in the finance and accounts calculations and in extended responses that describe rather than evaluate. Sessions typically alternate between a timed calculation set and a marked written answer.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Taken together with Business Management by a large share of Sharjah Diploma students. The overlap is smaller than families assume: Economics wants diagrams, models and evaluation of policy, while Business Management wants application to a named organisation. Confusing the two writing styles costs marks in both.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The usual mathematics pairing for a business-leaning Diploma. Its statistics and financial mathematics content supports the ratio, depreciation and investment appraisal work directly, which is why a weak Applications and Interpretation grade usually shows up as weak data-response marks as well.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Extended-response marks in Business Management depend on being able to build and sustain a judgement in writing. Students who are weak in the English A extended-response work are rarely strong in the Business Management essay questions, and the two can be supported in parallel.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: A frequent third Group 3 choice. Its research-methods content transfers usefully into the business research project, particularly the parts about sampling, questionnaire design and the limits of what a small sample can show about an organisation.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Taken by Sharjah students aiming at technology and management degrees. The overlap with Business Management shows up in the operations management unit and in any research project that examines a company's systems, data handling or automation decisions.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic language provision runs alongside the international curriculum in Sharjah private schools under federal requirements. For a Business Management student doing primary research with a local company, Arabic ability also changes which organisations can realistically be interviewed.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Shares the data-interpretation discipline with Business Management: read the resource, use the figure, then say what it means. Students often transfer good Geography resource technique into their business data-response answers once it is pointed out to them.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Theory of Knowledge marks combine with the Extended Essay for additional Diploma points. Business Management students frequently use the subject as a Theory of Knowledge example, which makes the two easy to support in the same term.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Business Management is a common Extended Essay subject in Sharjah because local organisations are accessible for research. Supervision belongs to the school; a tutor's role is question framing, research design and feedback on the student's own drafts.

sharjah/ib-dp-business-management-tutor.regionsTitle: Where in Sharjah we work with Diploma Business Management students
sharjah/ib-dp-business-management-tutor.regionsIntro: Sharjah is not one tutoring market. A family on the Dubai border is scheduling around a cross-emirate school run; a family in University City is next door to two universities; a family in Kalba is on the east coast with a different set of schooling options altogether. Each of those changes when a session can start.

regions.name: Al Majaz and Al Khan
regions.note: Dense corniche apartment districts close to the Dubai boundary. Many students here attend school in Sharjah city but have parents commuting into Dubai, so the realistic session window opens after 5pm on weekdays and is much wider at the weekend.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: The most Dubai-facing part of Sharjah, with a large share of children bussed to schools in Al Qusais and Mirdif. A 4pm start is rarely workable in term time; a 6.30pm or 7.30pm slot usually is, which is one reason online scheduling fits this area.

regions.name: Muwaileh and Al Zahia
regions.note: Newer villa and townhouse communities with several large private schools within a short drive. Business Management demand here tends to cluster in DP1 term two, when the research project proposal is first due.

regions.name: Aljada and Al Mamsha
regions.note: Recent mixed-use developments inside Sharjah city with a young resident profile. Families here are often new arrivals mid-Diploma, which produces a specific tutoring brief: catch up on a unit already taught and taught differently elsewhere.

regions.name: University City and Al Tai
regions.note: Built around the University of Sharjah and the American University of Sharjah. Students in this area frequently have a clear destination degree in mind, so Business Management tutoring here is often aimed at a specific admissions requirement rather than at rescuing a grade.

regions.name: Al Qasimia and Al Taawun
regions.note: Older central districts with heavy evening traffic on Al Wahda Street and the Al Ittihad corridor. Travel time is the deciding factor for in-home arrangements here; an online session removes it from the calculation entirely.

regions.name: Kalba, Khor Fakkan and Dibba Al-Hisn
regions.note: Sharjah's east-coast exclaves on the Gulf of Oman, still regulated by SPEA but with far fewer private-school options within reach. Subject-specialist Diploma tutoring is close to unavailable locally, and live video is what makes a Business Management specialist reachable at all.

regions.name: Tilal City, Al Suyoh and Sharjah Garden City
regions.note: Outlying residential developments where a tutor travelling from Dubai would spend longer in the car than in the lesson. Families in these communities are usually the quickest to accept online delivery once the arithmetic of travel time is spelled out.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah city centre - Al Majaz, Al Khan, Al Taawun and Al Qasimia

sharjah/ib-dp-business-management-tutor.modesIntro: There are three realistic ways to run Business Management support for a Sharjah Diploma student, and they suit different points in the two-year course. The research project needs a different rhythm from exam preparation, and paying for weekly hours when a student needs a concentrated block is the most common way families waste money.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across the Diploma
modes.description: A fixed sixty or ninety minute slot each week, running with the school's teaching order so the tutor reinforces the unit being taught rather than a different one. This is the right shape for DP1, when the aim is to build the finance and accounts arithmetic and the habit of applying a named tool to a named organisation before the research project starts.

sections.heading: What an IB DP Business Management tutor in Sharjah actually does in a session
paragraphs: An IB DP business management tutor in Sharjah does three things in a typical hour: fixes a calculation the student cannot yet produce reliably, marks a written answer against the published criteria, and names the specific error that will repeat in the examination. Nothing else in a session is worth the money. Content delivery is what the school is for, and a tutor who spends the hour re-teaching the marketing mix is usually filling time rather than diagnosing.

The diagnosis comes first. In a trial lesson a Business Management specialist will typically hand a student a short stimulus with a table of figures and ask for a contribution per unit, a break-even quantity and one sentence on what that number means for the organisation. The response tells the tutor almost everything. A student who gets the arithmetic right but writes nothing about the business has an application problem. A student who writes fluently about the business and produces the wrong figure has a numeracy problem. A student who asks which formula to use has not built the habit of reading a stimulus for the data it actually contains.

After that, the work is cumulative and narrow. The finance and accounts unit gets drilled until the student can move between a profit and loss account, a balance sheet and a cash-flow forecast without re-reading the headings. The named analytical tools get attached to real organisations rather than learned as lists. Extended-response answers get marked, returned with criteria references, and rewritten. The same three errors get written down and revisited until they stop appearing. This is unglamorous and it is the whole job.

For a Sharjah family the delivery detail matters as much as the pedagogy. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, with screen sharing so the tutor and the student annotate the same stimulus at the same time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. What a Sharjah family gets instead is a Business Management specialist rather than whoever can reach Al Majaz by half past five.

sections.heading: The five units, and the analytical toolkit that runs across all of them
paragraphs: The current Business Management guide is organised into five units, and the thing that trips students up is that the examination does not respect those boundaries. A single extended-response question can ask about a change of organisational structure in Unit 2, its effect on operations capacity in Unit 5, and its implications for cash flow in Unit 3. Students who have revised unit by unit, with a separate set of notes for each, often cannot cross those boundaries under time pressure.

Running across the units is a set of named analytical tools. Some are familiar from IGCSE, such as SWOT analysis and the marketing mix. Others are specific to this course and are where the easy marks sit, because they are concrete and examinable: a STEEPLE analysis of an external environment, an Ansoff matrix for a growth decision, a decision tree with expected values, a force field analysis for a change proposal, Hofstede's cultural dimensions for an organisation operating across borders. A student who names the right tool and applies it to the stimulus organisation is already most of the way to the analysis marks.

The four concepts sit above everything. Creativity, change, ethics and sustainability are the lenses the extended-response questions are framed through. A student who can discuss a sustainability decision in terms of the organisation's actual operations, rather than in general terms about the environment, writes a materially better answer. In Sharjah this is easier than it sounds, because the emirate has a large manufacturing and logistics base in Hamriyah and Sharjah Airport International Free Zone, and students can reason about real operational trade-offs rather than invented ones.
The table below maps each unit to the tools that attach to it and to the error pattern that shows up most often in that unit. It is the sheet to keep next to the student's own notes while revising.

sections.heading: How the three assessed components reward completely different things
paragraphs: Business Management is assessed through two written papers and one piece of internally assessed work, and each rewards a different skill. Students who prepare for all three in the same way underperform in at least one. The paper built on the pre-released case study rewards deep familiarity with one organisation and the discipline to answer the question asked rather than reciting what was researched. The unseen paper rewards speed of reading, correct calculation and the ability to interpret a figure in context. The business research project rewards research design and sustained analysis over months.

The pre-released case study is the component families misunderstand most. Schools receive the case in advance, students research the organisation thoroughly, and then a predictable failure occurs in the examination hall: the candidate writes everything known about the company instead of answering the question in front of them. Preparation for this paper should be half research and half restraint. A tutor's job here is to set questions on the released case that the student has not seen, and mark the discipline of answering them.

The business research project is worth a quarter of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level, which makes it the single largest assessed item in the course. It is marked by the school's teacher and then externally moderated by the IB, so the school's judgement can move either way after moderation. This is why the project is worth tutoring early. A project built on a question that cannot be researched, or on primary data that was never realistically collectable, cannot be rescued in the final month however well it is written.

The table sets out what each component rewards and where candidates lose marks. Durations, section structures and exact weightings are set in the current subject guide and have changed with recent revisions, so confirm those details with your child's Diploma coordinator rather than with a tutoring website.

sections.heading: The business research project: what a tutor may do, and what a tutor must never do
paragraphs: This section exists because the Sharjah search results for Business Management tutoring include services that will supply a finished piece of coursework for a fee. That is academic malpractice under IB rules, the consequence falls on the student rather than the provider, and it can end a Diploma. IB Gram does not supply written work for any assessed component, and no tutor working through this platform may write, edit to completion, or hand over text for a research project.

What a tutor may do is substantial. A tutor may interrogate the research question until it is answerable with data the student can actually obtain. A tutor may explain what the published criteria reward and what they penalise. A tutor may teach questionnaire design, sampling and the arithmetic needed to analyse the results. A tutor may read the student's own draft and say, in writing, that the analysis section describes data rather than interpreting it. A tutor may teach referencing conventions and the difference between citing a source and leaning on it. All of that is teaching, and all of it is permitted.

What a tutor may not do is write a sentence that then appears in the submitted work, restructure the student's draft into a new document, or supply a question, a method or an analysis the student has not reasoned through. The practical test is simple and worth applying at home: if the student cannot explain in their own words why a paragraph says what it says, that paragraph should not be in the project. Schools in Sharjah, like schools everywhere, require a declaration of authenticity, and the supervising teacher is required to judge whether the work is the student's own.

There is a Sharjah-specific opportunity in all of this. Primary research is easier here than families assume. The emirate has a large base of small and medium-sized businesses in Industrial Area, Al Qasimia and the free zones, many of them family-run and willing to answer a student's questions if the approach is professional. A project built on a short interview with an operations manager in Hamriyah, with a small questionnaire and honest acknowledgement of the sample size, usually outperforms a project built entirely on a multinational's published annual report.
