sections.heading: What an IB DP computer science tutor in Sharjah fixes in the first month
paragraphs: An IB DP computer science tutor in Sharjah should spend the first month on three things: hand-tracing, pseudocode notation, and written precision. Those three carry a large share of the written paper marks and almost none of them are improved by writing more code. A student who can build a working application but cannot fill in a trace table for a nested loop will sit a paper and lose marks on questions that look, to them, trivially easy.

Hand-tracing is the fastest fix available in this subject. Given a fragment of pseudocode and a trace table, a candidate has to record the value of each variable after each iteration. There is no insight required and no creativity rewarded; it is a procedure, and students who have never been drilled in it make arithmetic and sequencing errors under time pressure. Twenty minutes a week for a month usually closes it completely. Tutors who skip this because it feels mechanical are skipping the single highest-yield intervention in the course.

Pseudocode notation is the second. The examination uses its own notation, with specific conventions for output, loops, collections and arrays, and candidates are expected to write in it rather than in Python or Java. A student who writes fluent Python in the answer booklet is relying on an examiner's goodwill. Practising the notation until it feels natural takes a handful of sessions and removes an entire category of avoidable loss.

The third is written explanation. Many questions ask candidates to explain why, not to state what, and the difference between a 4 and a 7 in this subject is frequently the difference between naming a technology and explaining its behaviour and trade-offs. A tutor's contribution here is marking: a written answer returned with the missing step identified, rewritten, and marked again. Sessions run one-to-one over live video with a shared editor and a shared trace table, which for this subject is arguably better than sitting side by side, because both parties can see and edit the same code at once.
bullets: Ask any prospective tutor to set a trace table exercise in the trial lesson
Ask whether they will mark written answers in the examination's own notation
A month of tracing drills is usually worth more than a term of new content

sections.heading: The syllabus topic by topic, and what each paper does with it
paragraphs: The course content is grouped into topics that the papers treat very differently, and knowing which topic is examined how changes revision priorities. The systems topics reward precise terminology and are heavily factual: a candidate either knows what a cache does or does not. The computational thinking topic rewards procedure and practice. The Higher Level topics on abstract data structures reward the ability to reason about a structure in the abstract, draw it, and explain why it suits a problem better than the alternative.

Abstract data structures are where Higher Level students most often come unstuck, and the reason is usually that they learned them as code rather than as diagrams. A linked list question may ask a candidate to draw the pointer changes when a node is inserted in the middle. A tree question may ask for a traversal order. A stack question may ask what happens to the call stack during recursion. None of those are answered by having written a working implementation; all of them are answered by being able to draw the structure and step through it on paper.

Networks is the topic students most consistently underestimate. It is factual, it is examinable in extended written form, and it carries vocabulary that must be used precisely: protocol, packet, layer, handshake, bandwidth, latency, compression. A student who writes about a network in everyday language instead of the subject's language loses marks even when the underlying understanding is sound. This topic is also the easiest to revise efficiently, because the content is finite and well bounded.

The table below sets out each topic, what it covers, whether it is Standard Level or Higher Level only, and the specific error pattern that recurs in examination answers on it. Use it to decide what a term of tutoring should be spent on rather than working through the syllabus in its printed order.

sections.heading: Three papers, two levels, and the questions candidates skip
paragraphs: Standard Level students sit two written papers; Higher Level students sit three, with the extra one devoted to the case study. Both levels submit the computational solution. The exact weightings and durations are set in the current subject guide and have changed across revisions, so ask the Diploma coordinator for the current figures rather than taking them from any website. What does not change is the character of each paper, and that is what revision should be shaped around.

The first written paper is the broad one, mixing short factual questions across the whole syllabus with longer structured questions that require extended explanation. Its characteristic failure is uneven preparation: a candidate who revised computational thinking thoroughly and networks lightly cannot avoid the networks questions, because they are not optional. Reading the whole paper before starting, and spending the first two minutes allocating time by mark tariff, recovers more marks in this paper than any content revision does in the final week.

The second written paper is where the option or applied content sits, and where the extended written answers carry the most weight per question. Candidates lose marks here by writing at length without structure. A fifteen-mark question is not a request for fifteen sentences; it is a request for a structured argument with named concepts, a worked example and a judgement. Practising two or three of these a week, marked and rewritten, moves a grade faster than anything else available in DP2.

The Higher Level case study paper rewards something unusual in the Diploma: independent research done months in advance. The scenario is published before the examination year, it assumes technical knowledge beyond the document itself, and candidates who have read widely around it write visibly better answers. This is the most prepare-able component in the entire course and the most commonly neglected.

sections.heading: The Higher Level case study: the one component you can prepare a year early
paragraphs: The Higher Level case study is set annually, published ahead of the examination year, and examined in a paper of its own. That combination makes it unique in the Diploma: a student knows roughly what the questions will be about twelve months before sitting them. In practice most candidates open the document a few weeks before the paper, learn the vocabulary in it, and sit an examination that assumes a far wider reading. The gap between those two approaches is worth more than a grade.

Preparation has three layers. The first is the document itself: the scenario, the organisation described, the technologies named, and the constraints the scenario sets out. The second is the terminology the paper assumes but the document does not fully define, which the IB expects students to research independently. The third is the wider technical context, which is where the strongest answers come from. A candidate who can discuss a named technology's limitations, its alternatives and the trade-offs between them writes a different answer from one reciting the document.

A tutor's contribution here is structure and discipline rather than content delivery. The useful shape is a reading plan running across DP2: a list of terms to research, a record of sources, and a weekly extended-response practice question on the material covered so far. The record of sources matters more than it sounds, because a student who has written notes in their own words from identified sources is both better prepared and clearly working inside academic-honesty expectations.

For Sharjah students there is a practical advantage worth using. University City is home to institutions with public library access and technical talks, and students aiming at computing degrees locally can often find relevant reading and occasionally a conversation with someone working in the field. For east-coast families in Kalba or Khor Fakkan that is impractical, which is where a tutor with the subject's reading list substitutes for geography.

sections.heading: The computational solution, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The computational solution is the internally assessed component: a piece of software the student plans, designs, develops, demonstrates on a screencast and evaluates, with documentation at each stage, marked by the school's teacher and externally moderated by the IB. It is a substantial undertaking and it is where the most avoidable grade loss in the subject happens, almost always for the same two reasons: the project was scoped too ambitiously to finish, or the documentation was treated as paperwork rather than as the thing being marked.

Scope is the first conversation. A solution needs a genuine client with a genuine problem, it needs to be complex enough to demonstrate real techniques, and it has to be finishable alongside five other Diploma subjects and the core. Students routinely propose a full mobile application with a cloud backend and deliver a broken prototype. A well-scoped project with thorough documentation and complete testing outperforms an ambitious one every time, because the criteria reward the process and the evidence, not the ambition.

Documentation is where the marks live. The planning stage needs a recorded conversation with the client and a defensible set of success criteria. The design stage needs diagrams, a record of the techniques chosen and the reasoning behind them. Development needs the student's own account of what was built, which techniques were used and why, with evidence. The demonstration screencast has to actually show the solution meeting its success criteria, which means rehearsing it rather than recording whatever happens on a first attempt. The evaluation needs honest judgement against the original criteria, not a summary of what was built.

On academic honesty, the boundary is strict and worth stating plainly. No tutor working through IB Gram will write, supply or complete code, documentation or any other part of a computational solution. A tutor may teach a technique, explain a criterion, review the student's own work and say in writing what is missing, and ask the questions that force a design decision to be reasoned through. Using a generative tool or a stranger's code without attribution carries the same consequence as any other malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student. Keep the source record and keep the work the student's own.

sections.heading: Which language should a Sharjah student actually work in?
paragraphs: Families ask this constantly, and the honest answer has two parts. For the written papers, the language is the examination's own pseudocode notation, and no real language is accepted as a substitute. For the computational solution, the choice is the student's and the school's, and what matters is that the chosen language can demonstrate the techniques the criteria reward and that the student is fluent enough in it to finish.

Java is the traditional choice in this subject and remains the language most of the IB's own historical teaching material assumes, which is why its conventions turn up in examination-style questions about object-oriented concepts. Python is far more common as a first language among students arriving from CBSE or from a British Year 11, and it is entirely workable for a computational solution. The practical consideration is not elegance but completion: a student who knows Python well will finish a Python project, and a half-finished Java project scores worse than a complete Python one regardless of which language the school prefers.

Where language choice does matter is in demonstrating the Higher Level content. Abstract data structures are easier to show convincingly in a language with explicit references and typing, and a student intending to build a solution that exercises linked structures should think about that before starting. A tutor's job here is to ask the question early, while the choice is still free, rather than three months in when changing language means restarting.

One Sharjah-specific practicality. Shared code editors and screen sharing are what make remote sessions in this subject work well, and both depend on a reasonable connection and a device the student can actually type on. A tablet is not sufficient for a two-hour development session. Before the first lesson, check that your child has a laptop, a working development environment installed, and somewhere quiet; in a shared apartment in Al Majaz or Al Qasimia that last one is often the real constraint, and it is easier to solve before the sessions start than after.

sections.heading: What Computer Science tutoring costs in Sharjah, in dirhams
paragraphs: This market publishes almost nothing in dirhams, which is unhelpful when dirhams are what you pay in. The bands below are drawn from providers' own published pages and from a 2026 Dubai tutoring rate survey, with the source named in each row. They are market observations, not IB Gram's prices. Their purpose is to let you recognise whether a quote is ordinary, high or suspiciously low before you commit.

Computer Science sits towards the upper part of any tutoring market for a simple supply reason. The population of tutors who can teach the systems content precisely, drill tracing, read a student's code and coach a computational solution is much smaller than the population who can teach Diploma mathematics. In Sharjah, where Diploma Computer Science is offered by a limited number of schools, that scarcity is sharper than in Dubai. Expect the specialist band rather than the general band, and treat a very low quote for this subject specifically as a signal to ask what the tutor has actually taught.

The second thing that moves the number is timing. A specialist with open slots in September has none in March, and rates rise accordingly as a session approaches. The third is the component: ongoing weekly theory support and a concentrated block of computational solution coaching are priced differently by most providers, because the second involves reading and responding to the student's documentation between sessions. Ask explicitly whether written feedback between sessions is included or billed.

Three questions to put to any quote. Is it per hour or per session, and how long is a session? Does it include marked written work returned with criteria references? And what is the cancellation position during Ramadan, examination leave and the Sharjah school holidays, when half of a booked block can otherwise disappear?

sections.heading: Online versus in-home when the specialism is scarce
paragraphs: Sharjah parents searching for a Computer Science home tutor are asking a fair question and deserve a direct answer. In-home tutoring is a genuine market here and it has real benefits: nothing to set up, a visible session, and a younger student kept in a familiar room. It also has costs that are not usually itemised. The tutor's travel time is inside the hourly fee. Evening congestion along Al Ittihad Road and Al Wahda Street turns two short journeys a week into a real cost. And most importantly for this subject, the requirement that someone drive to your community collapses the pool of people who could teach it at all.

That collapse is the decisive factor here in a way it is not for primary mathematics. Diploma Computer Science is taught in a limited number of Sharjah schools, so the number of people in the emirate who have taught the current syllabus, marked a computational solution and prepared students for the case study paper is small. Requiring them also to be free at 6.30pm and within driving distance of Kalba, Tilal City or Al Nahda reduces it close to zero. Opening the search to live video restores a real choice of specialist.

There is also a positive technical case, not merely a consolation. A shared code editor lets tutor and student type in the same file. Screen sharing lets both watch a program fail in real time. A session can be recorded for revision. Documentation can be commented on directly in the student's own file, with the comments visibly separate from the student's text, which is exactly the separation academic honesty requires. For a subject conducted on a screen anyway, remote delivery costs almost nothing in fidelity.

To be explicit about the limit: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video. That is a constraint on what we sell, stated before you book rather than after, so you can weigh it against the alternative.

sections.heading: Verifying a tutor in Sharjah: the permit, the regulator and the plan
paragraphs: Before the first paid session, there is one check worth making and one worth understanding. The check is the permit. Anyone providing private tuition in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Eligibility is deliberately broad, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. If a provider quotes you a permit fee or suggests the permit is optional, they are wrong on a matter of public record, and tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts has been published, so a specific figure you see quoted is unverified.

The thing worth understanding is who regulates what. Private schools in Sharjah answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai's schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi's and Al Ain's to ADEK, Ras Al Khaimah's to its Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. None of those bodies accredits private tutors or tutoring platforms. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, operates no office or centre in the UAE, and does not claim the KHDA educational services permit that a training institute with premises would require.

One more boundary worth knowing. The permit carries a code of conduct, and a teacher at your child's own school tutoring your child privately is the arrangement most likely to fall foul of it; in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for school staff are reported to prohibit exactly that. If a Computer Science teacher at your child's school offers private sessions, that is a question for the school, not for a tutoring platform.

With the checks done, the planning is straightforward, and the table sets it out counted backwards from the examination session. Note that no IB session or results dates appear on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so any date restated here would be unverified; ask the Diploma coordinator or read ibo.org directly. For comparison, the boards that do publish openly show how far ahead entries close: a Cambridge June entry is fixed in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, with the November series as the resit route, and Pearson Edexcel's November 2026 International GCSE timetable finished on 19 November 2026 with results held back to January. Whatever the board, the entry decision is made a season before the revision.

process.title: Send us the level, the school and the sticking point
process.description: Standard or Higher Level, which school, which topics have been taught, and what is going wrong. If the computational solution is under way, say what stage it has reached and what the teacher has said. A marked past paper answer tells a specialist more than any description of the problem.

process.title: We match a Computer Science specialist, or tell you we cannot
process.description: Matching is by subject and level, not by postcode. If no Diploma Computer Science specialist is free in the Gulf Standard Time window you need, we say so and offer the nearest workable slot. Filling the hour with a general science tutor would waste your money and your child's term.

process.title: Use the free trial as a diagnostic
process.description: Expect a trace table, a pseudocode fragment and one extended written answer in the first hour. That is enough for a specialist to identify whether the problem is procedure, notation, terminology or written structure. Ask for the diagnosis in writing before you book anything.

process.title: Pick the right shape for the term
process.description: DP1 usually wants weekly theory and tracing work. The computational solution wants a block of eight to twelve sessions. Higher Level case study preparation wants its own block from the point the document is published. DP2 wants short, frequent, timed practice with marked answers.

process.title: Check progress against marked work
process.description: Ask monthly for the marked answers and the list of recurring errors. In this subject the error list is the honest measure, because content knowledge can look fine while trace tables and notation quietly cost marks. If the list is not shrinking after six weeks, change the plan or the tutor.

whyPoints.title: A scarce specialism, matched on subject rather than distance
whyPoints.description: Diploma Computer Science is taught in a limited number of Sharjah schools, so the local tutor pool is thin. Matching online means your child works with someone who has taught this syllabus and marked a computational solution, rather than the nearest available science graduate.

whyPoints.title: The high-yield basics drilled first
whyPoints.description: Hand-tracing, pseudocode notation and written precision carry marks that coding fluency does not reach, and all three respond quickly to drilling. Sessions start there rather than with new content, because that is where the fastest grade movement in this subject is available.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on the computational solution
whyPoints.description: No tutor working through IB Gram will supply code, documentation or text for any assessed component. Coaching covers scoping, techniques, criteria interpretation, test planning and written feedback on the student's own work. Several providers in this search result do otherwise, and the consequence falls on the student.

whyPoints.title: Case study preparation started early enough to matter
whyPoints.description: The Higher Level case study is published ahead of the examination year and is the single most prepare-able component in the course. Sessions build a terminology list, a recorded reading plan and weekly extended-response practice, instead of a panic read in the final month.

whyPoints.title: Rates published in dirhams, with the source named
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page come from providers' own pages and a 2026 Dubai rate survey, each attributed. Almost nobody in this market publishes dirham figures at all, which leaves parents unable to judge a quote. You should be able to before you call.

whyPoints.title: Clear about the limits of the service
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no UAE office, no regulator accreditation and no school partnerships. Home visits are offered in India and not in the UAE. Stating the constraints up front is more useful than a longer list of claims.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP Computer Science tutor in Sharjah charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Specialist Diploma subject tutoring in this market runs roughly AED 200 to AED 450 an hour, and Computer Science sits in the upper part of that band because the supply of tutors who have taught the syllabus is small. For reference, Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase publishes AED 270, and a 2026 Dubai rate survey reaches AED 450 and above for examination-year specialists. Rates below about AED 150 generally mean a generalist rather than someone who can coach a computational solution. Those are market figures from published sources, not IB Gram's price list; take the free trial before committing to a block.

faqs.question: My child codes well but scores 4s in Computer Science. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the written papers test things coding does not. They ask candidates to trace an algorithm by hand into a trace table, to write pseudocode in the examination's own notation, to use precise systems and networks terminology, and to explain behaviour and trade-offs in extended written answers. A student who builds working software can fail all four. The good news is that each one responds quickly to drilling, and tracing in particular usually improves within a month. A tutor's first job is establishing which of those four is actually costing the marks rather than assuming it is content knowledge.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the computational solution without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may help scope a finishable problem, teach a programming technique, explain what each criterion rewards, teach test planning, review the student's own code and documentation, and state in writing what is missing. A tutor may not write code or documentation that appears in the submission, nor restructure the student's work into new text. The practical test is whether your child can explain every design decision in their own words. Using an unattributed generative tool carries the same malpractice consequence as any other, and it falls on the student.

faqs.question: When is the Higher Level case study published and when should preparation start?
faqs.answer: The case study is set annually and published ahead of the examination year, which makes it the one component a student can prepare a long way out. Preparation should start as soon as the document is available, usually during DP1 or the start of DP2. Build a list of the technical terms the paper assumes, research each one from identified sources, keep a record of what was read, and practise one extended-response question a week on the material covered so far. Candidates who first open the document in the final weeks are sitting a paper that assumes months of independent reading they have not done.

faqs.question: Should my child use Java or Python for the computational solution?
faqs.answer: Whichever one they will actually finish in. The written papers use the examination's own pseudocode notation, so no real language helps there. For the solution, the criteria reward the process, the documentation and the techniques demonstrated, not the language's prestige. Java has a longer history in this subject and makes some Higher Level structures easier to show convincingly; Python is more common among students arriving from CBSE or a British Year 11 and is entirely workable. Decide before the design stage, because changing language mid-development usually means restarting and losing a term.

faqs.question: Which Sharjah schools offer Diploma Computer Science?
faqs.answer: Provision is selective rather than universal. Diploma schooling in the emirate clusters around Muwaileh, University City and Aljada plus the long-established schools in the city centre, and Computer Science is offered by some of those schools and not others, with availability changing year to year. The only reliable answer is from the school itself, so ask the Diploma coordinator which Group 4 subjects run at which levels this year. IB Gram has no affiliation with or endorsement from any school, and we support students regardless of where they are enrolled.

faqs.question: Does remote teaching actually work for a coding subject?
faqs.answer: For this subject it works unusually well, because the work already happens on a screen. A shared editor lets the tutor and student type in the same file. Screen sharing lets both watch a program fail and fix it together. Documentation can be commented on in the student's own file, with the comments visibly separate from the student's text, which is the separation academic honesty requires. Sessions can be recorded for revision. What matters practically is a laptop rather than a tablet, a working development environment installed before the first session, and somewhere quiet to work.

faqs.question: What do abstract data structures require that programming experience does not?
faqs.answer: The ability to draw a structure and step through it on paper. A Higher Level question may ask for the pointer changes when a node is inserted into the middle of a linked list, a traversal order for a binary tree, or what happens to the call stack during recursion. None of those are answered by having written a working implementation. Students who learned these topics as code rather than as diagrams consistently lose marks. The fix is drawing practice: structures sketched by hand, operations stepped through, and the reasoning for choosing one structure over another written out.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Diploma Computer Science need?
faqs.answer: One ninety-minute session a week suits DP1, where the aim is building tracing, notation and systems vocabulary steadily. The computational solution usually needs a concentrated block of eight to twelve sessions rather than an extra weekly hour, because the work between sessions is the student's own development time. DP2 often moves to two shorter sessions for timed practice. Diploma students in the UAE also carry mandatory Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies on top of six subjects and the core, so two subjects supported at ninety minutes each is the practical ceiling for most students.

faqs.question: Is Computer Science accepted for engineering and computing degrees in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It is a recognised Group 4 science and is commonly taken by students applying to computing and engineering programmes locally and abroad. What varies is the mathematics requirement attached: some engineering programmes specify the Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches route rather than Applications and Interpretation, and that specification matters more to an admissions decision than the Group 4 choice does. Check the published entry requirements for the specific universities your child is targeting, including the American University of Sharjah and the University of Sharjah. Tutoring is not a requirement for admission and no provider can influence an admissions outcome.

faqs.question: Is my child's tutor legally allowed to teach privately in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Anyone providing private tuition in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Working without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Verify through MoHRE's own channels rather than accepting a provider's claim.

faqs.question: What should a Computer Science trial lesson actually contain?
faqs.answer: Three things, inside an hour. A trace table exercise on a short pseudocode fragment, to test procedure. A pseudocode writing task, to test notation. And one extended written answer on a systems or networks topic, to test terminology and structure. A specialist can diagnose from those three. You should receive a written note afterwards naming the specific errors found and what the first few sessions would target. If the trial is spent discussing packages and promises instead, that is information about the provider and the sensible response is to try another.

faqs.question: Can you help if my child joined DP2 in Sharjah mid-course?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is a common situation in the newer Sharjah communities where families arrive mid-Diploma. The first session is triage: which topics the previous school covered, what stage the computational solution has reached, whether the planning documentation exists, and whether the case study has been opened. Mid-course arrivals most often have a half-scoped solution built under different guidance, and the honest question is whether to continue it or rescope. That decision is better taken in the first fortnight than in the final term, which is why early contact matters more here than elsewhere.

faqs.question: Do you cover a Computer Science Extended Essay as well?
faqs.answer: Yes, as coaching rather than production. A Computer Science Extended Essay needs a genuinely answerable technical question with a defensible method, and most failures happen at the question stage rather than in the writing. A tutor can help frame the question, sanity-check whether the proposed investigation is feasible with the student's resources, teach the analytical approach, and give written feedback on the student's own drafts. The supervisor is assigned by the school. The 4,000 words must be the student's own work, and we will not supply text for any part of it.

faqs.question: What happens to sessions during Ramadan and the Sharjah school holidays?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten during Ramadan and household routines shift, so sessions normally move to a post-Iftar slot for the month. Agree that timetable before Ramadan begins, including any weeks you want to pause, rather than rescheduling week by week and losing sessions. Sharjah's public-sector working week also differs from Dubai's, which changes which evenings a working parent is home, so confirm your own school and household calendar before fixing a recurring slot. Holiday periods are often the most productive time for computational solution work, because the student has uninterrupted development time.

sharjah/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.closingHeading: Start with a trace table, not a package
sharjah/ib-dp-computer-science-tutor.closingBody: If your child is sitting Diploma Computer Science in Sharjah and the grade is stuck, the most useful next step is one free trial lesson with a subject specialist, built around a trace table, a pseudocode task and one extended written answer. That hour will tell you whether the problem is procedure, notation, terminology or written structure, and you will get the diagnosis in writing. From there you can choose a weekly theory slot, a computational solution block, or a case study programme. All teaching is one-to-one over live video with a shared editor, set on Gulf Standard Time. Tell us the level, the school and what the last marked paper said.

sharjah/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma Programme Economics at Higher Level: the HL policy paper, the quantitative extensions, and the three-commentary portfolio. Each works one-to-one over live video with Sharjah students, in slots that survive a Dubai school run.

intro.heading: What an Economics HL quote in Sharjah is actually made of
paragraphs: Parents in Sharjah ask the price first, and nobody in this market answers it. Of the agency and platform pages ranking for IB tutoring in the UAE, three publish no figure at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Sharjah family transacts in. So this page starts with the number. Market rates for a qualified subject tutor working online in the UAE run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour. An IB or IGCSE specialist with Diploma-level subject depth runs roughly AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500. Those are the bands published by providers and rate trackers in this market, not an IB Gram price list, and every one of them is a range rather than a price because the same hour of Economics teaching is worth different amounts depending on what it has to do.

Economics HL is unusual in how sharply its price curve bends. A Year 12 student who wants the four units sequenced and the diagrams drawn properly needs a competent subject teacher, and that sits at the lower end of the specialist band. A Year 13 student eight weeks from the May session who has to learn the HL policy paper from scratch, with a portfolio that has already been submitted, needs somebody who has marked that paper and can diagnose a script in ten minutes. That is a different hour and it is priced like one. Most of the cost variance families see between two quotes for the same subject is not a difference in quality claim. It is a difference in what the hour is being asked to do.

Sharjah adds its own arithmetic. The emirate's private schools are regulated by SPEA, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and which, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That matters for a tutoring budget because the set of Sharjah schools running the full Diploma Programme is small. A large share of Sharjah Diploma candidates sit in Dubai classrooms and commute, from Al Nahda, Al Majaz and Al Khan in the morning and back through Al Ittihad Road in the afternoon. A tutor who has to be physically present in the room is competing with that commute for the same two hours of the evening, and the travel gets priced in whether the invoice itemises it or not.

This is where delivery format stops being a preference and starts being a line item. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Sharjah lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The honest case for that is not that it is cheaper, although removing travel from the quote usually makes it so. The case is that a student in Muwaileh gets an Economics HL specialist who has taught Paper 3 rather than the best generalist willing to drive to Muwaileh at seven in the evening. The subject pool stops being a function of the map.

What follows is the full breakdown: the band table, the nine things that move a quote inside a band, the HL versus SL assessment split that determines how many hours you are actually buying, the way a Sharjah school calendar and Ramadan reshape the timetable, and what a tutor may and may not touch on an Economics commentary. Every AED figure carries its source. Every claim about SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education is traceable to the authority's own page, because a number without a source is worth nothing to a parent comparing three quotes.

sharjah/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: Economics sits inside a Diploma that has to be budgeted as a whole. A family paying for HL Economics support in Year 13 is usually also paying for something else, so here is what each programme stage costs in hours rather than in adjectives.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Economics HL runs across both years: the four units are usually taught in sequence through Year 12, with the HL quantitative extensions and the policy paper weighted into Year 13. Internal deadlines for the three commentaries are set by the school, not the IB, which is why two Sharjah students in the same year group can be on completely different portfolio timelines.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah has a smaller DP cohort than Dubai, and several Sharjah families drive into Dubai or Ajman schools for the Diploma. For a tutoring plan that means two things: the subject teacher at school may be covering Economics alongside Business Management, and the evening window is short because the commute eats it. Online sessions at 7.30pm or 8.30pm GST are the slots that actually hold.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and Societies in MYP is the feeder for DP Economics, but it is assessed against four criteria on a 1-8 scale rather than by paper. Students arriving in DP1 from MYP are usually strong on investigation and weak on diagram discipline, because MYP never asked them to draw a correctly labelled market diagram under timed conditions. That gap is six to eight hours of work, not a term.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run MYP without the full Diploma above it, so students transfer at Year 11 into a DP1 cohort in Dubai or Abu Dhabi. Those transfers arrive mid-September having missed the first unit, and the economics diagram set is the first thing to rebuild. Cost-wise this is the cheapest intervention on the whole list and the one families most often skip.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE Economics is syllabus 0455. It overlaps the DP introduction unit on supply, demand, elasticity and market failure, but stops well short of the DP's nine key concepts and its evaluation demands. A student with a strong 0455 grade still has to learn to write a 15-mark part (b) with a judgement in it. Pearson's International GCSE equivalent follows a comparable structure with different paper codes.
programmes.countryNote: Most Sharjah families on the British track sit IGCSE in the Cambridge June series or the Pearson May/June series before deciding on HL Economics. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, which is after DP1 subject choices are usually locked. Families who want the IGCSE grade to inform the HL decision need to have that conversation in May.

programmes.name: A Level Economics, for comparison
programmes.description: Some Sharjah schools offer A Level rather than the Diploma, and parents comparing the two want to know whether Economics is harder in one. The A Level goes deeper on micro theory of the firm; DP HL Economics goes wider across the global economy and adds the policy paper and a portfolio of three commentaries. The DP route costs more tutoring hours in Year 13 and fewer in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: The practical Sharjah point is university recognition, not difficulty. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track a student must show five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. No IB points threshold has been published on a source we can cite, so verify the IB route on moe.gov.ae.

sharjah/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Economics HL is the page, but the quote almost always covers more than one subject. These are the DP courses Sharjah families most often pair with it, with what each actually assesses and where the marks go missing.

subjects.name: Economics HL
subjects.description: Four units, nine key concepts, and three papers. Paper 1 is a 25-mark extended response, Paper 2 is a 40-mark data response, and Paper 3 is the HL-only policy paper with two compulsory questions. The portfolio of three commentaries carries 20 per cent. Marks are lost on evaluation, not on knowledge.

subjects.name: Economics SL
subjects.description: Same four units, no Paper 3, and the portfolio weighted up to 30 per cent. SL students lose marks in the same two places as HL students - unlabelled diagrams and part (b) answers that explain instead of judging - but have fewer marks to recover them from.

subjects.name: Business Management HL and SL
subjects.description: Frequently taken alongside Economics, and frequently confused with it in revision. Business Management rewards application to a named organisation; Economics rewards theory applied to a market. Students who revise them together tend to write business answers in an economics paper and lose the theory marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The usual maths partner for Economics. AI HL covers the statistical and modelling work that makes Paper 3 calculations straightforward: percentage change, index numbers, elasticity arithmetic and reading a regression output without panicking.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Chosen by Economics students heading for quantitative degrees. AA is heavier on calculus and proof and lighter on the applied statistics an Economics paper rewards, so AA students sometimes need the index-number and elasticity arithmetic taught separately.

subjects.name: Geography HL and SL
subjects.description: Shares the global economy material on trade, development and inequality, and shares the evaluation command terms. A student strong in Geography essays usually transfers that judgement writing into Economics part (b) answers faster than a student strong in Maths.

subjects.name: Global Politics HL and SL
subjects.description: Overlaps the fourth Economics unit on interdependence, trade blocs and intervention. The engagement activity rewards exactly the kind of sourced, dated evidence that an Economics commentary needs, so the two courses reinforce each other if they are revised deliberately.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Not a content overlap but a marks overlap. The Economics 15-mark part (b) and the Paper 3 policy recommendation are both argument-with-judgement tasks. Students who cannot structure a paragraph in English A rarely score well on evaluation in Economics.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: TOK asks how economic models can be knowledge if their assumptions are false, which is a question Paper 1 part (b) rewards directly. A student who has thought about the limits of ceteris paribus writes better evaluation than one who has memorised a definition of it.

subjects.name: Economics Internal Assessment coaching
subjects.description: Three commentaries of up to 800 words, each on a different unit, each built on a published news article from a different source, each engaging a different key concept. Coaching means article selection, diagram choice, criterion-by-criterion feedback and process discipline - never text supplied by anybody but the student.

sharjah/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.regionsIntro: Sharjah is not one tutoring market. The distance to a Dubai school gate, the direction of the morning commute and the school's own calendar change what time a session can start, and that in turn changes what an hour costs.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Central, dense, and heavily commuter. Families here often hold Dubai school places, so the student is home late and the realistic first slot is 7.30pm GST or later. An online session starts on time; a visiting tutor arrives when Al Ittihad Road allows.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Effectively on the Dubai border and the single most Dubai-dependent part of Sharjah for schooling. The commute is short in distance and long in minutes. Weekend morning sessions are easier to hold here than weekday evening ones, especially in exam term.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: Home to several of the emirate's larger private campuses and a big share of its IGCSE and Diploma cohort. Enough students in one postcode that a visiting tutor can run back-to-back sessions, which is why in-home quotes here sit lower in the band than on the east coast.

regions.name: University City and Al Zahia
regions.note: Newer housing next to the university cluster, with a mixed school set across Sharjah and Dubai. Postgraduate availability locally pushes down the price of general maths help and does nothing for Economics HL, which has almost no local specialist pool.

regions.name: Al Khan and Al Mamzar side
regions.note: Coastal, close to the Dubai boundary, and a short run to Dubai schools. Families here compare Sharjah and Dubai tutoring prices directly because they already shop in both emirates, which makes them the most price-aware part of this market.

regions.name: Al Qasimia and Halwan
regions.note: Older established districts with a strong CBSE and British presence and a smaller Diploma cohort. Economics HL candidates here are usually the only one or two in their year group taking it, which is exactly the case for one-to-one rather than a group class.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan and Kalba
regions.note: Sharjah's east-coast exclaves, still under SPEA, and roughly two hours from the city by road. No realistic in-home specialist market exists here at any price. Online delivery is not the cheaper option on this coast; it is the only option.

regions.name: Tilal City and Sharjah Garden City
regions.note: Outlying new communities with long school runs in both directions. Evening slots are tight and tend to settle at 8.30pm GST. Saturday morning is the most reliable recurring slot for a two-hour Paper 3 clinic.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah city and Muwaileh
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's main private-school concentration, regulated by SPEA, spanning British, Indian and American curricula with a smaller IB presence than Dubai. Students we support attend schools across this cluster; naming them is context for how the market works, not a claim of any relationship.

sections.heading: What IB DP Economics HL tutoring costs in Sharjah, in AED
paragraphs: An IB DP Economics HL tutor working online with a Sharjah family sits in the specialist band: roughly AED 200 to 450 and above per hour at market rates, with named or examiner-level tutors quoted above that. The budget end of the market, typically university students teaching general subjects, runs AED 45 to 150 an hour and does not reliably cover the HL policy paper. In-home one-to-one with travel included is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour in this market. Monthly packages seen across UAE providers include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are published provider figures and rate-tracker bands as of October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

The table below splits the market by what is being bought rather than by who is selling it, because the single biggest driver of an Economics HL quote is component scope. A tutor teaching the four units in sequence is doing a different job from one marking Paper 3 scripts eight weeks out, and a portfolio coach working to criterion letters is doing a third. Families who ask for a price without naming the component get the middle of the band quoted at them, which is almost never the right number for their situation.

IB Gram's own position on price is deliberately not a table. Rates depend on the tutor matched, the level, the component and the session length, and the first lesson is free so that the comparison is made against a real session rather than a promise. What we will publish is the method: you see the tutor's subject and level before booking, you keep the same tutor week to week, and the rate is quoted per 60 minutes with no travel element, because there is no travel. Nothing on this page should be read as a guaranteed outcome at any price - no tutor at any rate can promise a grade, and anybody who does is selling something the IB does not let them deliver.

sections.heading: Nine things that move an Economics HL quote inside the band
paragraphs: A band is not a price. Two Sharjah families can be quoted AED 220 and AED 420 for the same subject in the same week and both quotes can be honest, because the hour is being asked to do different work. The nine levers below are the ones that actually move the number, ordered roughly by how much they move it. Component scope moves it most; the day of the week moves it least.

Timing is the lever families control and underuse. The pre-session window, when every Diploma candidate in the Gulf wants the same four evening slots, is when specialist availability is thinnest and quotes sit at the top of the band. The same tutor teaching the same material in October has more slots and less marking backlog. Families who buy Economics HL support in DP1 at the lower end of the band and keep it running usually spend less in total than families who buy nothing until February and then buy everything at once.

Level is the second lever, and it is not a small one. Paper 3 is HL-only and carries 30 per cent, which means an HL quote is buying a component an SL quote does not contain. The pool of tutors who can mark Paper 3 against the published criteria is markedly smaller than the pool who can teach the four units, and scarcity shows up in the rate. This is the one place where paying the specialist band is clearly the cheaper choice: a generalist teaching Paper 3 badly costs the full hourly rate and produces nothing a marker rewards.

sections.heading: The HL assessment split, and how many hours it implies
paragraphs: Buying tutoring without knowing the assessment split is how families end up paying for the wrong hours. At Higher Level, Economics is examined by Paper 1 at 20 per cent, Paper 2 at 30 per cent, Paper 3 at 30 per cent and the Internal Assessment portfolio at 20 per cent. At Standard Level there is no Paper 3, and the portfolio rises to 30 per cent with Paper 1 at 30 and Paper 2 at 40. That single structural difference is why HL and SL tutoring plans should not look alike, and why an HL student who has had no Paper 3 teaching has a 30 per cent hole regardless of how well the units went.

Paper 1 is a single extended response chosen from three, worth 25 marks, with a 10-mark part (a) and a 15-mark part (b). Part (a) is explanation with diagrams; part (b) is judgement. Students routinely score well on (a) and poorly on (b), because (b) is the only place the paper asks them to decide something and defend it. Paper 2 is data response, 40 marks, built on an unseen text and figures, and rewards reading the extract properly far more than it rewards recall. Paper 3 is the HL policy paper: two compulsory questions, each 30 marks, mixing calculation with a policy recommendation that has to be defended against its own trade-offs.

The hours follow from that. Diagram and terminology work is cheap and fast and lifts Paper 1 part (a) and Paper 2 together. Evaluation work is slower, because it is a writing habit rather than a fact set, and it lifts every paper and the commentaries at once. Paper 3 is the most teachable component on the list in the sense that its question structure repeats, and the least teachable in the sense that it needs somebody who has marked it. A sensible HL plan weights roughly a third of its hours onto Paper 3 and the portfolio combined, because together they are half the grade.

sections.heading: The three commentaries, by criterion letter
paragraphs: The Economics Internal Assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries, each a maximum of 800 words, each built on a published news article the student finds, each drawn from a different unit of the syllabus and engaging a different key concept. Each commentary is marked out of 14 against five criteria - diagrams, terminology, application and analysis, key concept, and evaluation - and the portfolio carries 45 marks in total once the rubric requirements are counted. Not one competitor page in this market names a single criterion letter, which is why most students arrive at their first commentary knowing the word limit and nothing else.

Where marks go is predictable. Diagram marks are lost to unlabelled axes, missing units and a diagram pasted in without being referred to in the text. Terminology marks are lost to definitions that sit in a block at the start instead of being used where they are needed. Application and analysis marks are lost to commentary that summarises the article rather than explaining the economics behind it. Key concept marks are lost to a concept named in the title and never used again. Evaluation marks are lost to a final paragraph that lists advantages and disadvantages without reaching a judgement. Every one of those is diagnosable from a draft in fifteen minutes.

The boundary matters here more than anywhere else on the page. A tutor reads the student's own draft and gives feedback against the criteria: this diagram is not referred to in the text, this key concept is decorative, this evaluation has no judgement. A tutor does not supply sentences, choose the article on the student's behalf, or hand back a rewritten version. Nobody at IB Gram will write, redraft or supply text for an assessed commentary, and no reputable provider should - one operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments, which is an academic-integrity breach and an IB malpractice trigger that puts the student's whole Diploma at risk, not the provider's.

sections.heading: Sharjah's school calendar, Ramadan and when the hours actually happen
paragraphs: A tutoring budget that ignores the calendar overspends. Sharjah Diploma candidates sit the May session, and the work that moves a grade happens in the twelve weeks before it - which in the Gulf collides with Ramadan in most recent years and with a shortened school day. Sessions that worked at 5pm in November do not work at 5pm during Ramadan, and families who do not re-plan simply lose those weeks and then buy them back at pre-session prices.

The practical rebuild is straightforward. During Ramadan, post-Iftar sessions hold far better than late-afternoon ones, and online delivery is what makes a 9pm or 9.30pm GST slot possible at all. Across the rest of the year, the Sharjah constraint is the Dubai school run: a student at a Dubai campus living in Al Nahda or Al Majaz is not realistically available before 7pm on a weekday. Saturday mornings are the most reliable recurring slot in this emirate for anything that needs ninety minutes or more, which is to say for every timed Paper 3 question.

Counting backwards from the session is the discipline nobody in this SERP teaches. The portfolio deadlines are internal and set by the school, so they sit earlier than parents expect, often with the final commentary due before the mock window. Mocks then act as the real diagnostic, and the eight weeks after mocks are the only window in which a Paper 3 technique block changes anything. sections.heading: SPEA, KHDA and why a Sharjah family has two regulators
paragraphs: Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate. SPEA and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so in Sharjah the regulator's reach goes beyond inspection into what a school may teach and charge. Dubai's private schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a supervisory role in those three emirates.

The Sharjah complication is that a large number of families live under SPEA and school their children under KHDA. That split explains two things parents find baffling. First, the inspection report they read may be published by a different authority from the one that regulates their emirate, so comparing a Sharjah school's rating to a Dubai school's is not comparing like with like. Second, term dates and assessment calendars follow the school's regulator, not the family's address, which is why two neighbours in Al Nahda can be on different half-term weeks.

The federal baseline sits underneath all of it: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement, and it means an Economics HL student is also carrying UAE-mandated subjects that compete for the same study hours. IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation or endorsement from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and any provider telling you otherwise should be asked to show the permit number.

sections.heading: Is your Economics tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question with the clearest answer and the least coverage. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time and no listed fee.

Two things follow for a Sharjah parent comparing quotes. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws - no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted at you by anybody, and a provider quoting one is guessing. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor: a training institute in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific document issued to a specific entity. Nobody should describe themselves using a regulator's name as a credential without producing the number.

There is one more boundary worth knowing because it protects your child, not us. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than read off the policy document, so verify it against current ADEK material before relying on it. The practical rule is the same in any emirate: do not hire your child's own classroom teacher privately, however convenient it looks.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group in this emirate - the comparison that decides the budget
paragraphs: Home tutoring is a real market in Sharjah and the question deserves a real answer rather than a sales line. In-home one-to-one in the UAE is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions appear on provider pages in this market. What that money buys is a tutor in the room and a tutor who had to get there. In Muwaileh, where a visiting tutor can run back-to-back sessions in one community, the travel overhead is small. In Khor Fakkan or Kalba it is prohibitive, and in Al Nahda at 6pm it is unpredictable in a way no price can fix.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. That is not a hedge; it is the model. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE page on this site says the same thing. Sharjah lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week. The argument for it is specific rather than general: Economics HL Paper 3 has a small specialist pool anywhere in the world and an almost non-existent one inside a 20-minute drive of any given Sharjah address. Online delivery replaces the question of who is nearby with the question of who can mark the paper.

The format also changes what a session can contain. A shared screen holds the extract, the diagram and the marked script at once; a student can be given a timed Paper 3 question, hand it in as a photograph, and get it back annotated before the next session. None of that depends on being in the room, and all of it depends on the tutor having marked the component before. Group classes at a tuition centre remain the cheapest option per hour in this market and the weakest fit for a student who is the only Economics HL candidate in their year group, which in Sharjah is common.

sections.heading: Where Economics HL marks are actually lost, by topic
paragraphs: Economics HL candidates rarely fail on knowledge. They lose marks on four repeatable, diagnosable habits, and a tutor who knows the component can name which one is costing a given student their grade from two marked scripts. The first is diagram discipline: axes unlabelled, units missing, the new equilibrium not marked, and the diagram never referred to in the prose. In a 10-mark part (a) that is a straightforward loss of marks that cost nothing to secure.

The second is command-term blindness. Explain, analyse, evaluate, discuss and to what extent are not synonyms, and a student who answers all of them the same way scores the explanation marks and forfeits the judgement marks. The 15-mark part (b) and the Paper 3 recommendation both require a position taken and defended against its own trade-offs. The third is the HL quantitative extensions: the Keynesian multiplier, the Phillips curve, the Lorenz curve and the Gini coefficient, tariff, quota and subsidy calculations, terms of trade and exchange-rate arithmetic. These are mechanical and highly scorable, and they are routinely taught last and revised least.

The fourth is the portfolio, which sits at 20 per cent of the HL grade and is the only component where the student controls the conditions entirely. Commentaries that summarise an article instead of applying theory to it, that name a key concept without using it, or that miss the rubric requirements on unit coverage and source variety, lose marks that were available for free. A plan that fixes diagrams, command terms, the HL extensions and the portfolio in that order tends to move more marks per hour than one that re-teaches the syllabus from unit one.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: Say whether the priority is the four units, Paper 2 technique, the HL policy paper or the portfolio, and say which level. Component scope is the biggest driver of what the hour costs and of which tutors are a sensible match, so naming it in the first message saves a wasted trial lesson.

process.title: See the tutor's subject and level before you book
process.description: You see who is teaching, at what level, and which components they have taught before the first session is scheduled. For Economics HL that means confirming Paper 3 and portfolio experience specifically, because a tutor can be strong on the four units and have never marked the policy paper.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: The first lesson is free and is used as a diagnostic rather than a sales call. Bring a marked script or a commentary draft if there is one. By the end of it you should have a named weakness and a count of sessions, not a brochure. There is no card requirement and no commitment attached.

process.title: Fix the slot around the school run and Ramadan
process.description: Sharjah evenings are short. Pick a recurring slot in Gulf Standard Time that survives a Dubai commute, and agree in advance how it shifts during Ramadan, when post-Iftar sessions hold far better than late-afternoon ones. A slot that moves every week is the main reason tutoring plans quietly stop.

process.title: Review against marked work, not impressions
process.description: Progress is read off annotated scripts and criterion-level commentary feedback, not off how the sessions felt. Agree at the start what gets marked and how often, and ask whether marking time sits inside the quoted rate. If after a few weeks the marked work is not moving, change the tutor rather than adding hours.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP Economics HL tutor cost per hour in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Market rates for an IB specialist working online in this market run roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour, with premium named tutors quoted higher - one provider publishes AED 650. Our own rate depends on the tutor, level, component and session length, and the first lesson is free so you compare against a real session.

faqs.question: Why is Economics HL quoted higher than Economics SL in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Because HL contains a component SL does not sit. Paper 3, the policy paper, is Higher Level only and carries 30 per cent of the grade: two compulsory questions worth 30 marks each, mixing calculation with a defended policy recommendation. The pool of tutors who have actually marked Paper 3 against the published criteria is much smaller than the pool who can teach the four units competently, and that scarcity is what you are paying for. An HL quote that matches an SL quote is usually a signal that Paper 3 is not covered.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an Economics tutor to our home in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE - that is a service we run only in India. Sharjah lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week. The in-home market does exist here and is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel, and for a common subject in a dense community like Muwaileh it can work well. For an HL policy paper, the specialist you need is unlikely to live within a 20-minute drive of any particular Sharjah address, and on the east coast nobody does.

faqs.question: What exactly does the Economics Internal Assessment portfolio involve?
faqs.answer: Three commentaries, each a maximum of 800 words, each based on a published news article the student selects, each drawn from a different unit of the syllabus and engaging a different key concept. Each commentary is marked out of 14 across five criteria - diagrams, terminology, application and analysis, key concept and evaluation - and the portfolio carries 45 marks in total once the rubric requirements are counted. At HL it is 20 per cent of the grade; at SL it rises to 30 per cent. Most marks are lost to summarising the article instead of applying theory to it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Economics commentaries without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that should be stated rather than assumed. A tutor can teach the criteria, explain what a key concept has to do in a commentary, show how a diagram earns its marks, and give criterion-by-criterion feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor must never supply sentences, rewrite a draft, or choose and summarise the article. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; under IB rules that exposes the student to a malpractice finding affecting their whole Diploma, not just one grade.

faqs.question: How many Economics HL sessions does a Sharjah student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on when you start. A DP1 student taking one weekly session alongside the school's teaching order typically uses 25 to 30 sessions across the year and buys fewer total hours than a DP2 student who starts in February. A targeted block is smaller: six to eight sessions to repair diagrams and terminology, eight to twelve for Paper 3 technique, three per commentary for portfolio work. A final eight-week programme runs 16 to 24 sessions and is the most expensive way to buy the same marks.

faqs.question: Which Sharjah areas do your Economics tutors cover?
faqs.answer: All of them, because lessons are delivered over live video rather than by road. In practice we work with students in Al Majaz, Al Nahda, Al Khan, Muwaileh, University City, Al Zahia, Al Qasimia, Halwan, Tilal City and the east-coast towns of Khor Fakkan and Kalba. What changes by area is not availability but timing: a student at a Dubai school living in Al Nahda is rarely free before 7pm on a weekday, while a Muwaileh student at a local campus can often take a 5.30pm slot.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Sharjah, and does that affect tutoring?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge it approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. It does not regulate private tutors; that sits with MoHRE through the private tuition work permit. The practical effect for a Sharjah family is calendar confusion rather than cost: if your child attends a Dubai school, the term dates, assessment calendar and inspection report all follow KHDA while you live under SPEA.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Sharjah need a permit from the government?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted as invented. Apply through the MoHRE app, website or e-services.

faqs.question: Is the HL policy paper really worth paying a specialist rate for?
faqs.answer: On the arithmetic, usually yes. Paper 3 is 30 per cent of the HL grade, it exists only at HL, and its question structure repeats enough that technique transfers quickly once somebody who has marked it shows the student what earns the marks. A generalist teaching it badly costs the same hourly rate and produces answers that show calculation without units and recommendations without defended trade-offs. If your budget forces a choice, spending it on Paper 3 and the portfolio covers half the grade between them.

faqs.question: How do sessions work during Ramadan and the Sharjah school run?
faqs.answer: They move, deliberately, and they are agreed in advance rather than cancelled week by week. During Ramadan, post-Iftar slots at around 9pm or 9.30pm Gulf Standard Time hold far better than late afternoon, and online delivery is what makes that time workable at all. Outside Ramadan, the Sharjah constraint is the commute: students at Dubai schools living in Al Nahda, Al Majaz or Al Khan are usually free from 7.30pm. Saturday mornings are the most reliable recurring slot for anything needing ninety minutes, which includes every timed Paper 3 question.

faqs.question: What should I send when asking for an Economics HL tutoring quote?
faqs.answer: Four things, and the quote gets sharper immediately. The level, HL or SL. The component you want covered - units, Paper 2 technique, Paper 3 or the portfolio. The school's internal deadlines for the three commentaries, because those sit earlier than families expect. And a recent piece of marked work: a mock script or a commentary draft with the teacher's comments. Without the marked work, any provider is guessing at the diagnosis, and a guessed diagnosis is how families buy the wrong hours at the right price.

faqs.question: My child is eight weeks from the May session with no Paper 3 practice. Is it too late?
faqs.answer: It is late, not too late, and the plan has to change shape. Eight weeks will not re-teach the four units, so it should not try. It will cover Paper 3 structure, the HL quantitative extensions - multiplier, Phillips curve, Gini, tariff and exchange-rate arithmetic - and timed questions marked against the criteria, because those are mechanical and scorable. Expect scarcity pricing at the top of the specialist band in this window. Nobody can promise a particular grade from eight weeks, and any provider who does is describing something the IB does not allow them to deliver.

faqs.question: Are IB results recognised for university entry in the UAE, and does tutoring affect that?
faqs.answer: Recognition runs through Ministry of Education equivalency, which is a process the ministry operates and no tutoring provider performs or influences. On the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. No IB points threshold has been published on a source we are willing to cite, so verify the IB route on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority. Tutoring is never a requirement for equivalency.

faqs.question: Can two Sharjah students share Economics HL sessions to lower the cost?
faqs.answer: Yes, where both sit the same level and the same school year, and ideally the same school so the internal deadlines align. Small-group rates in this market sit well below one-to-one per student, so a pairing is the clearest way to reduce cost per family without dropping to a tuition-centre class. The constraint is real: HL Paper 3 cannot be taught usefully to an SL student sitting in the same session, so we do not pair across levels. Both students' scripts still get marked individually.

sharjah/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the diagnosis, then the number
sharjah/ib-dp-economics-hl-tutor.closingBody: The sensible order for a Sharjah family is diagnosis first, price second. Book the free trial lesson, bring a marked Paper 2 script or a commentary draft, and let an Economics HL specialist name which of the four habits is costing the marks: diagrams, command terms, the HL quantitative extensions, or the portfolio. From that you get a component, a session count and a quote you can compare against the AED bands published on this page. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the same tutor each week, from Al Majaz to Khor Fakkan. No home visits, no promised grade, and no number we are not willing to source.
