sharjah/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-lit.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach English A: Language and Literature at Standard and Higher Level for Sharjah students. Matching is by component and by the works your child's school has chosen, because a tutor who knows the set text and the criterion wording is worth more than a tutor who knows English.

intro.heading: The grade is four separate marks, not one impression
paragraphs: Most Sharjah parents arrive at this search after a report card that says something like "fluent but descriptive". That phrase is doing a lot of work and explaining almost nothing. In English A: Language and Literature it usually means the student can describe what a text says and cannot yet show how the text constructs its meaning for a particular reader. Those are two different skills, and only the second one is being marked.

The course is built from three areas of exploration - readers, writers and texts; time and space; intertextuality - and seven concepts that run through all of them: identity, culture, creativity, communication, perspective, transformation and representation. A student studies literary works alongside non-literary bodies of work: advertising campaigns, political speeches, opinion columns, cartoons, infographics, photographs with captions. Standard Level reads a minimum of four literary works and Higher Level six, with non-literary material running in parallel. The literary half is familiar territory for a strong reader. The non-literary half is where confident students in Sharjah schools most often come unstuck, because nobody has ever asked them to analyse a supermarket advertisement for its implied audience.

Then there is the mark scheme. Four components, each assessed against four criteria with letters attached: understanding and interpretation, analysis and evaluation, focus and organisation, and language. Paper 1 and the Higher Level essay carry five marks per criterion. Paper 2 carries ten, ten, five and five. The Individual Oral carries ten on every criterion. A student losing marks on criterion B across every component has one problem; a student losing them on criterion C has a completely different one, and the two need different lessons. A school report rarely tells you which letter is leaking.

Sharjah adds its own shape to this. SPEA, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, regulates private schools in the emirate, and a large number of Sharjah families drive into Dubai schools each morning from Al Nahda, Al Taawun and Al Majaz. That commute decides when a session can realistically start - a 4pm slot on paper is a 5.30pm slot in practice for a family coming back over the border in the evening peak. Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies also sit in the week alongside the Diploma, so the hours available for English A work are narrower than a timetable suggests.

What a tutor can do inside those hours is specific. Teach the unseen-text method until it is automatic. Rehearse the closed-book comparative essay so quotation and structure are not being invented in the exam room. Question the global issue chosen for the Individual Oral until it is narrow enough to argue. Read a Higher Level essay draft and say, in criterion language, where the argument stops being an argument. What a tutor must never do is produce any of that work. The student writes it; the tutor teaches, questions and comments. That boundary is not a disclaimer, it is the IB's academic-honesty rule and your child's diploma depends on it.

Paper 2 is a closed-book comparative essay on two studied works, answered from one general question
The Individual Oral runs ten minutes plus five minutes of questions, on a global issue you choose
The Higher Level essay is 1,200 to 1,500 words and is examined externally
Criterion letters A to D carry different mark totals in different components - the leak has a letter

sharjah/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-lit.programmesIntro: English A: Language and Literature sits at the top of a language pathway that begins years earlier. Where your child currently sits on that pathway changes what a session should spend its hour doing, so the four stages below are described in terms of what they prepare for rather than what they cover.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: English A: Language and Literature is taken in Group 1 as Standard or Higher Level and can be the student's best-language course or one half of a bilingual diploma. Four components are assessed: Paper 1 guided analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay, the Individual Oral, and at Higher Level an externally examined essay of 1,200 to 1,500 words. The learner portfolio runs across both years and is not itself assessed, which is exactly why it gets neglected and why the Oral then has nothing to draw on.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma cohorts in Sharjah schools are small compared with Dubai, so a single teacher often carries both Language and Literature and Literature across two year groups. That means the set works are chosen once for everyone and a student who dislikes the chosen novel has no second option. A tutor who has taught the specific works your child's school selected saves several weeks of ground-laying.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Language and Literature marks against four criteria - analysing, organising, producing text, and using language - which is the structural ancestor of the Diploma criteria but with much gentler expectations about evidence. An MYP 5 student who scores 7s on criterion A can still arrive in DP1 unable to write a comparative paragraph, because MYP rewards personal response more generously than the Diploma does.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run MYP to Year 11 and then enter students for the Diploma, while others switch to IGCSE for the two years before DP. The handover is where Sharjah students most often lose a term: MYP writing habits are not wrong, they are simply marked differently, and nobody tells the student that in September.

programmes.name: IGCSE First Language English
programmes.description: The usual route into Language and Literature in British-curriculum Sharjah schools. IGCSE First Language English rewards directed writing and reading for explicit and implicit meaning, and it trains students to answer the question asked. It does not train them to evaluate how a text positions its audience, which is the whole of Diploma criterion B, so a grade 8 at IGCSE predicts fluency rather than analysis.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah students sit IGCSE in both the June and November Cambridge series, and the November entry group arrives in DP1 having just finished examinations. Those students are the ones most likely to coast through the first term of the Diploma on IGCSE habits and then be surprised by the first Paper 1 mock.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: An Extended Essay in English, in category 1, 2 or 3, is the most common companion to this course and the most common timetable collision. The essay demands sustained independent argument on 4,000 words while the Individual Oral is being prepared, and both want the same skill: a claim held steady under evidence. Students who plan them together usually do better at both than students who treat them as separate emergencies.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah schools with small Diploma cohorts the Extended Essay supervisor may not be an English specialist, because supervision is allocated by availability. That is a reason to get the research question right early rather than a reason to doubt the school; a subject-specialist read of the question before it is submitted is usually enough.

sharjah/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-lit.subjectsIntro: A Language and Literature student rarely needs help only in English. The subjects below are the ones Sharjah Diploma families most often add alongside, and each note says what the subject actually assesses rather than what it is called.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Four components, four criterion letters. Marks are usually lost on analysis and evaluation at Standard Level and on focus and organisation at Higher Level, where the essay has to sustain one line of argument for 1,500 words rather than list observations about a text.

subjects.name: English A: Literature
subjects.description: The same assessment architecture without the non-literary material: Paper 1 is literary analysis, Paper 2 is comparative, and Higher Level adds the essay. Students who love novels and dislike advertisements often belong here, but the choice is usually made by the school's timetable rather than by the student.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language-acquisition course with reading, writing, listening and an oral based on a visual stimulus. A student placed in English B who is in fact a fluent speaker will cap out quickly; a student placed in English A who thinks in Arabic at home may spend two years fighting the wrong course. The diagnosis is worth doing properly.

subjects.name: Arabic A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The mirror course for Arabic-speaking students and the other half of a bilingual diploma. The criterion wording is the same; the literary tradition and the register expectations are not. Students taking both language A courses need their revision sequenced, because the two Individual Orals often fall in the same window.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: For non-native speakers continuing Arabic through the Diploma. Useful to separate from the Arabic that SPEA-regulated and KHDA-regulated schools must deliver as a mandatory subject, which follows the Ministry of Education's own programme and is assessed by the school rather than by the IB.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The closest cousin to Language and Literature in marking style: both reward an argument held under evidence and both punish narrative drift. Students who learn to write a Paper 2 comparative essay usually improve in History essays within weeks, which is a reason to buy English hours rather than two separate sets.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Heavy on command terms and on evaluating studies rather than describing them, which is the same criterion B problem wearing a different uniform. Sharjah students often take it as a third Group 3 option, and the extended-response paper is where the English skills transfer or do not.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects. Students who can hold a counterclaim in English A tend to find the essay manageable; students who cannot find both tasks hard at once. TOK and the Extended Essay together contribute up to three points to the diploma total.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in English
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent study in category 1, 2 or 3. The research question is the whole job: too broad and the essay describes, too narrow and there is nothing to argue. Supervision belongs to the school, and a tutor's role is to question the question, not to supply the content.

The notes below are about the evening, not about postcodes - which schools a district feeds, and what the drive home does to a 4pm slot.

regions.note: Dense apartment living on the Khalid Lagoon, with children spread across Sharjah city schools and a sizeable group crossing into Dubai. Evening slots after 6pm are the realistic ones here, and quiet space for a recorded Oral rehearsal usually means a bedroom rather than a study.

regions.note: The Dubai border strip, where a large share of students attend schools on the Dubai side and return through the Al Nahda crossing at peak. Families here routinely ask for 7pm English sessions, which works well for Paper 1 timed practice but badly for a tired student.

regions.note: Villas and newer apartment blocks feeding the Muwaileh and University City school cluster. Short journeys mean a 4.30pm start is genuinely possible, and this is the district where we most often run twice-weekly blocks in the final term.

regions.name: Aljada
regions.note: A newer mixed-use district drawing families from across the emirate, with a high proportion of first-year Diploma students who moved schools when they moved home. Set works often differ from what a student studied before, so the first session here is usually a works audit.

sections.heading: What "Language and Literature" asks that a literature course does not
paragraphs: The title of the course is the syllabus. Half of it is literary works, studied the way any literature course studies them. The other half is non-literary: advertising campaigns, political speeches, opinion columns and editorials, editorial cartoons, infographics and data visuals, photographs with captions, travel writing, blogs, interviews, public-information material. These are studied as bodies of work by a single producer or on a single theme, not as one-off texts, and they are examinable in exactly the same way as a novel.

That is the shift that catches strong readers in Sharjah schools. A student who can write beautifully about a poem will often freeze in front of a charity appeal, because nobody has taught them that an appeal has a structure, an implied reader, a register and a set of choices that can be analysed. The question is never whether the advertisement is effective. The question is how it constructs the audience it wants, and what the choices of image, lexis and layout do to that audience. Effectiveness is an opinion; construction is evidence.

The practical consequence for tutoring is that the first session on this course is usually diagnostic rather than instructional. Give the student an unseen non-literary text and fifteen minutes. If the response describes content, criterion B is the problem and the work is method. If the response notices technique but cannot organise the noticing, criterion C is the problem and the work is structure. If the response is accurate but the expression is loose, criterion D is the problem and the work is sentence-level. Three different diagnoses, three different terms of lessons, and no way to choose between them from a report card that says "fluent but descriptive".
bullets: Non-literary text types are examinable: advertisements, speeches, cartoons, infographics, blogs, photographs
The guiding question on Paper 1 is a help, not a constraint - it tells the student which door to go through
Bodies of work are studied as sets, so a single advertisement is read against its campaign
A strong literature student is not automatically a strong Language and Literature student

sections.heading: The four criterion letters, and the marks behind each one
paragraphs: Every component in this course is marked against four criteria, and the letters mean the same thing throughout: A is understanding and interpretation, B is analysis and evaluation, C is focus and organisation, D is language. What changes is how many marks each letter carries, and that changes what a student should practise. On Paper 1 all four letters carry five marks, so twenty marks are evenly spread and a student cannot afford to be weak anywhere. On Paper 2 the first two letters carry ten marks each and the last two carry five, so thirty marks tilt heavily towards knowing the works and arguing from them.

The Individual Oral is the outlier and the most valuable component to work on, because all four criteria carry ten marks for a total of forty and the task is known months in advance. A student who prepares the Oral properly is competing against their own preparation rather than against an unseen text. At Higher Level the essay carries twenty marks across the same four letters and is externally examined, which means a school's generous internal marking is no guide at all.

Read the weightings column below next to the marks column and the tutoring priority usually answers itself. A Higher Level student is carrying Paper 1 at thirty-five per cent and Paper 2 at twenty-five, with the Oral and the essay at twenty each. A Standard Level student has no essay, so Paper 1 and Paper 2 sit at thirty-five each and the Oral at thirty. The same student at the two levels therefore has different revision priorities, which is why a tutor should never be booked for "IB English" without the level and the component named.

Weightings and mark totals are published in the subject guide your child's school works from, and guides are revised between cohorts. Confirm the figures below against the guide the school is actually teaching before building a revision plan on them.

table.caption: ENGLISH A: LANGUAGE AND LITERATURE - COMPONENTS, CRITERION MARKS AND WEIGHTINGS. CONFIRM AGAINST YOUR COHORT'S SUBJECT GUIDE
rows: Paper 1 - guided textual analysis of unseen material
Paper 2 - comparative essay on two studied works, closed book
Individual Oral - 10 minutes plus 5 minutes of questions
HL essay - 1,200 to 1,500 words, externally examined

sections.heading: Paper 2 is closed book, and that changes how your child revises
paragraphs: In the Paper 2 examination there are no texts in the room. The student answers one general question, chosen from a short list, by comparing two of the literary works studied during the course, from memory. An hour and forty-five minutes, thirty marks, no page to flick back to. Almost every revision failure we see on this component comes from students revising as though the books will be there.

What that means in practice is that quotation has to be banked, not looked up, and banked in a usable form. A student who memorises twenty long quotations will use none of them. A student who memorises forty short, flexible fragments - four or five words that can be bent to several questions - walks in with material. The same goes for structure: because the question is general, the essay has to be built in the room, which only works if the student has a repeatable shape to build into and has practised comparing the same two works across five or six different questions.

Choosing which two works to pair is a real decision and not always the school's. Two works that share a theme but differ in form give a student more to say than two that are simply both novels. The pairing should be stress-tested against past general questions before DP2 ends, not in the week before the paper. In a Sharjah cohort where everyone studied the same four or six works, the pairing is also a way for a student to stop writing the same essay as the person next to them, which matters more than it sounds for the analysis and evaluation criterion.

A tutor's job on this component is narrow and useful: run timed questions, mark them against the criteria, and make the student rebuild the same essay a different way until the structure survives a question nobody predicted.
bullets: One general question, two studied works, no texts in the examination room
Short, flexible quotations beat long ones that only fit one argument
Pair works that differ in form, not just in title
Practise the same pairing across several past questions before the mocks

sections.heading: Non-literary text types and the toolkit each one needs
paragraphs: Unseen non-literary texts are the most teachable part of this course, because each type has a small number of moves that account for most of the marks. A student who knows that an editorial cartoon works through caricature, labelling, juxtaposition and a visual metaphor does not need inspiration in the examination room; they need fifteen minutes and a method. The table below sets out the types that appear most often and the misreading that costs most marks in each.

The pattern across all of them is the same error in different clothing. Students write about what the text is about instead of how it works, and the guiding question is treated as a topic rather than as an instruction. A question asking how the text constructs the reader's sympathy is asking for the mechanism. Naming the mechanism, quoting it and then saying what it does to a reader is the whole of criterion B, and it can be drilled.

Timing is the second half of the method. At Standard Level the student annotates and writes on one text; at Higher Level, on two, which means two complete analyses in the same examination. Students who annotate for twenty minutes write a brilliant plan and an unfinished essay. We work to a fixed split - a short annotation window, a one-line thesis, then writing - and we practise it until it stops feeling rushed. The split itself is less important than having one at all.

Sharjah students coming from an American-curriculum middle school or from a CBSE background are usually the ones who find this hardest, not because they read less but because their earlier courses rewarded personal response. Unlearning that takes a term, and it is better done in DP1 than in the final weeks.

table.caption: UNSEEN NON-LITERARY TEXT TYPES - THE USUAL MOVE AND THE USUAL MISREADING
columns: What the question usually turns on
rows: How image, lexis and layout construct an implied reader and a call to action
Judging whether the advertisement works instead of showing how it positions the reader
Register, pronoun use, patterning and the audience being built in real time
Summarising the politics of the speech rather than analysing its rhetoric
Stance, concession, the handling of counter-argument and the controlled voice
Agreeing or disagreeing with the writer's position in the response
Caricature, labelling, juxtaposition, scale and visual metaphor

sections.heading: The Individual Oral: one global issue, two extracts, ten minutes
paragraphs: The Individual Oral asks the student to explore, through one literary extract and one non-literary extract, the ways a global issue is presented in the works from which the extracts are taken. Ten minutes of prepared speaking, then five minutes of questions from the teacher. Forty marks, ten on each criterion, which makes it the single heaviest mark block in the course at Standard Level and equal-heaviest at Higher Level. It is also the only component where the student controls almost every variable.

The global issue is where most of the marks are won or lost before the student speaks. "Climate change" is not a global issue for this purpose; it is a topic, and a topic produces ten minutes of general comment. A global issue has to be narrow enough to be argued and wide enough to matter in both texts: how domestic labour is made invisible in advertising and in a particular novel, for instance. Getting from a topic to an issue usually takes two or three sessions of hard questioning, and it is the highest-value tutoring in the whole course.

The extracts are bounded, and the boundary is worth knowing: each extract runs to no more than forty lines, chosen by the student, and they must come from a literary work and a non-literary body of work studied on the course. The student brings the extracts and a brief outline into the room, not a script. Reading a script aloud wrecks criterion C and is audible instantly. Rehearsal should therefore be structured but unscripted - the same ten minutes delivered four or five times from the same outline, each time questioned harder by the tutor.

Once the recording is made, the mark is the mark. The school marks it internally and the IB moderates. There is no redraft, which is why the work belongs in the weeks before the recording window rather than after it. Ask the school for the recording date in DP2's first term and count backwards from there.

sections.heading: English A alongside Arabic under the UAE mandatory-subject rules
paragraphs: A Sharjah Diploma student is rarely studying one language. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools, and the federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. For families whose children cross into Dubai schools from Al Nahda or Al Taawun, KHDA's published mandatory-subject requirements add further detail, including separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited.

The language of instruction is specified too. KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes.

None of that is an IB requirement, and that is the point. The mandatory subjects are assessed by the school, not by the IB, and they occupy real hours in a week that also has to contain Paper 1 practice and an Individual Oral. A revision plan built as though the Diploma were the whole timetable will fail in February. When we plan English A hours for a Sharjah family, the Arabic and Islamic Education commitments go into the calendar first, because they are fixed and the tutoring is not.

There is a second consequence for bilingual households. A student who is strong in both Arabic and English may be a candidate for a bilingual diploma, taking two language A courses. That is a serious workload decision with two Individual Orals and potentially two sets of Paper 2 works, and it should be made with the school's Diploma coordinator rather than on a tutor's advice.

sections.heading: What English A support costs around Sharjah
paragraphs: Start with the smallest thing a family actually buys, because almost nobody buys a year. A block of six sessions on the Individual Oral, at the qualified-online rate the market publishes, lands between roughly AED 900 and AED 1,800 depending on who you book - and that block, scheduled in the right weeks, touches a component worth forty marks. The same money spent on general English conversation across a term touches nothing in particular. The figure that matters is not the hourly rate but what the hours are pointed at.

The published rates themselves are easy enough to assemble, and no competitor page in this market does it. Budget online tuition and university-student tutors advertise from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit between AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted between AED 180 and AED 500, with Bestimate's Dubai rate table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase published at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-level tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those are market figures published by other providers, read in October 2026, and not an IB Gram price list. We quote after a free trial lesson and a diagnosis, because an hourly number given before anyone has seen the student's writing is a guess with a decimal point. What the bands are genuinely useful for is sanity-checking a quote: a rate at the bottom of the budget band for Higher Level essay supervision should raise a question about who is teaching, and a rate above the specialist band should come with something specific attached.

Context helps as well. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package. School fees are the large number in a family's education budget; tutoring is the small one, and it is the one that can be aimed.

sections.heading: Online delivery, and the home-tutor question answered plainly
paragraphs: Parents searching for English help in Sharjah are often searching for someone to come to the villa, so here is the position without decoration. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Tuition for Sharjah families is delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with screen-shared texts and marked work returned in writing.

That is a design decision rather than an apology, and for this subject it is a strong one. The tutor pool for English A: Language and Literature inside the emirate of Sharjah is small, and the subset of that pool who have taught the Higher Level essay and who know the non-literary half of the course properly is smaller again. A family in Al Majaz choosing from tutors who can reach Al Majaz by car at 5pm is choosing from a dozen people. The same family choosing online is choosing from specialists who have marked hundreds of Paper 1 responses, and that difference shows up in the feedback long before it shows up in a grade.

There are practical advantages that are specific to English rather than generic. An unseen text can be put on a shared screen and annotated by both people at once, which is exactly how the skill is taught. A recorded session lets a student re-watch the moment an argument was built. The Individual Oral can be rehearsed to camera, which is nearer to the real recording condition than a conversation across a kitchen table. And a 7pm slot after the drive back from a Dubai school costs nothing in travel time for anyone.

What online does not fix is attention. A student who will not read the novel will not read it over video either. We ask for the last two marked pieces of work before the first session so that the trial lesson can be spent diagnosing rather than introducing, and we say plainly in the first week if what the student needs is not a tutor but a conversation with the school.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on the HL essay and the Oral
paragraphs: This subject has two assessed pieces that the student produces outside an examination room, and both are places where the line between support and malpractice gets crossed. The Higher Level essay is written at home over weeks. The Individual Oral is prepared at home and delivered once. Both are the student's own work under the IB's academic-honesty rules, and a diploma can be withheld where that is not the case.

So the boundary is drawn in writing before any work starts. A tutor may teach the method, discuss the global issue until the student can defend it, question an argument, point at a paragraph and say that the claim is not supported, explain what a criterion rewards, and mark a draft the way an examiner would. A tutor may not write any part of the essay, may not supply a thesis for the student to adopt, may not rewrite sentences into their own prose, and may not script the Oral. No tutor should offer to draft the essay or produce the commentary, and any service that does is selling the student a risk they cannot see.

In practice the honest version is also the more useful one. A student who has had an argument questioned until it holds can defend it in the five minutes of Oral questioning, which is where a scripted student falls apart. A student handed a thesis cannot. The same is true of the essay: the external examiner is reading for a line of argument sustained by a particular mind, and an adult's prose dropped into a sixteen-year-old's essay is visible in a paragraph.

We also tell families what not to buy. Services advertising completed Internal Assessments and finished essays exist in this market at advertised prices, and they are an academic-integrity breach rather than a shortcut. If a page offers to produce assessed work, the right response is to close the page.

faqs.question: My daughter's English report in her Sharjah school says "fluent but descriptive". What does that mean for Language and Literature?
faqs.answer: It almost always means criterion B. The writing is accurate and readable, so criterion D is fine, and she understands the text, so criterion A is fine. What is missing is analysis and evaluation: naming the technique, quoting it, and saying what it does to a reader. Description earns the lower bands however elegantly it is written. The fix is method rather than vocabulary, and it is one of the faster things to shift - usually six to eight weeks of marked unseen responses where every paragraph has to name a choice the writer made and the effect of that choice.

faqs.question: How many marks does each criterion carry in this course, and does it change between components?
faqs.answer: It changes, and that is the useful part. Paper 1 carries five marks on each of the four criteria, for twenty. Paper 2 carries ten on understanding and interpretation, ten on analysis and evaluation, five on focus and organisation and five on language, for thirty. The Individual Oral carries ten on all four, for forty. The Higher Level essay carries five on each, for twenty. A student weak on analysis loses twice as much on Paper 2 as on Paper 1, which is why revision priorities differ by component. Confirm the figures against your cohort's subject guide.

faqs.question: Why is my son allowed no texts in the Paper 2 examination?
faqs.answer: Paper 2 is a closed-book comparative essay by design. The student answers one general question by comparing two literary works studied on the course, in an hour and forty-five minutes, with nothing in front of them. The point is to test understanding held in the head rather than the ability to find a quotation. For revision this changes everything: quotations have to be banked short and flexible, and the essay structure has to be practised until it can be built in the room. Students who revise as though the books will be available are the ones who run out of material by the second page.

faqs.question: What counts as a global issue for the Individual Oral, and how narrow should it be?
faqs.answer: Narrow enough to argue and significant beyond one text. "Migration" is a topic and will produce ten minutes of general comment. "How a city renders migrant domestic labour invisible" is an issue, because both extracts can be shown doing something specific with it. The test we use is whether the student can state the issue in one sentence and then immediately say what each extract does with it. If the second half of that sentence is vague, the issue is still a topic. Getting from one to the other usually takes two or three sessions of hard questioning.

faqs.question: How long can the extracts for the Individual Oral be, and who chooses them?
faqs.answer: The student chooses them, and each runs to no more than forty lines. One comes from a literary work studied on the course and one from a non-literary body of work. The choice matters as much as the speaking: an extract with nothing to say about the global issue leaves the student padding for ten minutes. We usually test three or four candidate pairings against the stated issue before settling, then rehearse the same ten minutes several times from an outline. Notes are allowed in the room; a full script is audible and damages the organisation mark.

faqs.question: Is the Higher Level essay marked by the school or by an examiner?
faqs.answer: Externally, which is the detail that catches families out. The essay runs to 1,200 to 1,500 words on one of the literary works or non-literary bodies of work studied, carries twenty marks across the four criteria and twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade, and goes to an IB examiner rather than to the class teacher. Generous internal marking on earlier drafts is therefore no guide to the final outcome. The learner portfolio is where the essay should come from: a student who has kept it has a year of ideas to choose between, and a student who has not starts from nothing.

faqs.question: My child reads novels happily but freezes in front of an advertisement. Why does that happen?
faqs.answer: Because nobody has taught them that an advertisement has a structure worth analysing. Literary training transfers to Paper 1 only when the student has a method for non-literary text types, and most schools spend more time on the literary half of the course. The remedy is mechanical and it works: learn the handful of moves each text type depends on, then practise naming the move, quoting it and stating its effect on the implied reader. Charity appeals, speeches, cartoons and infographics each have four or five recurring features. A term of weekly unseen practice usually settles it.

faqs.question: Should my child be taking Language and Literature or Literature?
faqs.answer: Literature studies literary works only. Language and Literature studies literary works alongside non-literary bodies of work - advertising, journalism, speeches, visual media - and the assessment architecture is the same four components with the same criterion letters. A student who thinks in terms of media, politics and persuasion is usually better served by Language and Literature; a student who wants to live inside novels and poetry is usually better served by Literature. In most Sharjah schools the Diploma cohort is small enough that only one of the two is timetabled, so the honest answer is often that the school has decided.

faqs.question: How do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect an English tutoring schedule in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: They occupy fixed hours that the Diploma timetable does not control. Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools under the federal regulations, and for children at Dubai schools KHDA sets further requirements, including separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and specified languages of instruction. When we plan English A hours, those commitments go into the calendar before the tutoring does. A plan that treats the Diploma as the whole week looks fine in October and falls apart in February.

faqs.question: We live in Al Nahda and our children attend a Dubai school. When can an English session realistically start?
faqs.answer: Usually after 6.30pm on weekdays, sometimes later. The return journey through the Al Nahda crossing in the evening peak routinely turns a 4pm plan into a 5.45pm arrival, and a student who sits down exhausted gets little from timed Paper 1 practice. For this group we often put the heavier work into weekend blocks and keep weekday sessions shorter and more focused, or run ninety minutes once a week rather than sixty twice. Because lessons are online there is no additional travel at either end, which is most of the reason the later slot works at all.

faqs.question: What may an English tutor legitimately do with my son's Higher Level essay?
faqs.answer: Teach, question, and mark. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards, discuss which work or body of work would support a stronger argument, challenge the thesis until it holds, mark a draft as an examiner would and name the marks lost. A tutor may not write any section, may not hand over a thesis to be adopted, and may not rewrite sentences into their own prose. The essay is externally examined and must be the student's own under the IB's academic-honesty rules. Any provider offering to produce it is selling a risk to your child's diploma.

faqs.question: What does a block of Individual Oral preparation cost in this market?
faqs.answer: Published market rates give you the arithmetic. Qualified subject tutors working online advertise between AED 150 and AED 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200, and IB specialists between AED 200 and AED 450 and above, with TutorChase published at AED 270. Six sessions therefore sits roughly between AED 900 and AED 2,700 depending on which band you book. Those are other providers' figures, read in October 2026, not ours. We quote after a free trial lesson, because a rate given before anyone has read the student's writing is a guess.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an English tutor to our villa in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE - in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Sessions for Sharjah families are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with texts shared on screen and annotated by both people, and marked work returned in writing. For this subject the trade is a good one: the pool of tutors who can drive to your district is small, while the pool who have taught the Higher Level essay and marked unseen non-literary texts at volume is not limited by geography at all.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Language and Literature student usually need?
faqs.answer: One a week is the normal shape across DP1 and most of DP2, at sixty or ninety minutes. Ninety suits this course better than sixty once timed writing starts, because a Paper 1 response and its marking do not fit comfortably into an hour. Two a week makes sense in two situations: a component block in the weeks before the Individual Oral recording or the Higher Level essay deadline, and the final term, where timed papers under exam conditions are the whole job. More than two a week rarely helps, because the student needs reading and drafting time in between.

faqs.question: It is ten weeks to the May papers and my child's English is a grade below target. What is realistically improvable?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 method and Paper 2 structure, in that order. Both are technique rather than content, and technique moves inside ten weeks when it is practised under timed conditions and marked properly. What will not move much in ten weeks is the depth of knowledge of the literary works, so the plan should lean on what is already known rather than attempting new reading. If the Individual Oral has already been recorded, that mark is fixed and energy should go elsewhere. We say which of those applies after reading two marked scripts, not before.

faqs.question: Will English sessions keep running through Ramadan and the Sharjah summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing changed. During Ramadan most families move to post-iftar slots, and we keep sessions shorter and more focused rather than cancelling the week; the Higher Level essay and Oral preparation often sit well in that quieter evening period. Over the long summer, families travelling out of the emirate usually keep a reduced schedule across time zones, since nothing about a video lesson depends on either person being in Sharjah. What we do ask is that the plan is agreed in advance, because a term with two unplanned gaps in it is a term without momentum.

sharjah/ib-dp-english-a-language-and-lit.closingBody: Those two things are enough to start properly. A marked script shows which criterion letter is leaking; the recording date shows how many weeks there are before the forty-mark component closes. Send them with the level - Standard or Higher - and we will set up a free trial lesson with a Language and Literature specialist who has taught the works your child's school chose. The trial is a working session, not a sales call, and you get a written diagnosis afterwards naming the criterion to attack first. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the evening commute back into Sharjah.

sharjah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.tutorsIntro: The mentors below work on Diploma core components: research questions, source handling, argument structure, the reflections and viva preparation. Each is matched to the subject the essay is registered in, because a History essay and a Biology essay fail in different places.

intro.heading: What an Extended Essay actually costs a Sharjah family, and why quotes vary so much
paragraphs: A Sharjah parent asking about Extended Essay support is rarely asking for a term of weekly lessons. The essay is a single piece of work, roughly 40 hours of student effort, submitted once. So the honest unit of purchase is not a term - it is a stage. A topic-scoping conversation is one hour. Rescuing a research question that has already been approved and already failed is three. Reading a 4,000-word draft properly, against the criteria, and writing usable feedback on it is two to three hours of mentor time whether or not any of that time is spent in a lesson.

That is why quotes for the same essay arrive at wildly different numbers. Published market rates in the UAE run from roughly AED 45-150 an hour at the budget and university-student end, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, and AED 200-450 or more for an IB or IGCSE specialist. One UK-based agency publishes AED 270 an hour; one premium provider publishes AED 650. None of those figures is wrong. They are rates for different things, and most of them are quoted without saying how many hours the job takes - which is the number that decides what you actually pay.

Sharjah adds two specifics. The first is that the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and, unusually among UAE regulators, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A Sharjah school's fee structure is therefore a reviewed figure, which makes it a useful anchor when you are deciding what a private mentoring hour is worth alongside it. The second is geography: a large share of Sharjah Diploma candidates attend campuses in Dubai, commuting from Al Nahda, Al Majaz or Al Taawun. Their supervisor is 40 minutes away in traffic, and a supervisor meeting they cannot easily reach is one of the commonest reasons a Sharjah family starts paying someone else.

The essay itself is worth understanding before you price it. Thirty-four marks are available across five criteria. Criterion C, critical thinking, carries 12 of them on its own - more than a third of the essay - and it is the criterion that cannot be fixed in the last fortnight, because it is a property of the research question rather than of the prose. Criterion A, focus and method, carries 6. Criterion B, knowledge and understanding, carries 6. Criterion D, presentation, carries 4. Criterion E, engagement, carries 6 and is assessed from the reflections rather than the essay. Confirm the current mark allocation against the Extended Essay guide your child's cohort is working to; the IB revises these documents between cohorts.

What follows is priced in dirhams at published market bands, broken down by stage, by subject family and by how late you start. Every figure is presented as a market rate from a named band, not as an IB Gram price list. Our own position is a free trial lesson first, then a quote for the specific job, which is a different conversation from an hourly sticker. Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not send a mentor to a home address anywhere in Sharjah - that is a service we run only in India.

sharjah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.programmesIntro: The Extended Essay belongs to the Diploma Programme core, but the research habit it tests is built earlier. Families in Sharjah usually meet it in one of these four places, and the support each needs is priced differently.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma carries six subjects plus three core components. The Extended Essay is the independent research piece: a 4,000-word argument in one approved subject, supervised in school, marked externally. It is graded A to E and combines with Theory of Knowledge to award up to three of the 45 Diploma points. A grade E is a failing condition, which is why a weak essay costs more than three points - it can cost the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah's Diploma cohorts are small by Dubai standards, so a candidate writing in Psychology or Economics may be the only one in the year doing so. Supervision load falls on a teacher covering several subjects, and that is the gap private mentoring usually fills in this emirate rather than any shortage of teaching quality.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS
programmes.description: The three core components run alongside the six subjects and are the part of the Diploma most often left until it is expensive. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge are graded and feed the same three-point matrix; CAS is a completion requirement. Buying support for the core is cheaper per point than buying it for a subject, because three points from the core cost far fewer hours than three grade boundaries across three papers.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah schools set internal core deadlines months earlier than the IB's own submission window, and those internal dates are the ones that bind. Families who ask the coordinator for the written internal calendar in DP1 generally spend less, because the costly purchases are the ones made after a school deadline has already been missed.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP Personal Project in Year 11 is the closest thing to an Extended Essay a student meets before DP1. It demands a goal, a process journal, a product and a report, all assessed on criteria. Students who treated the Personal Project as a formality arrive in DP1 without a research habit, and the first Extended Essay deadline exposes it. Mentoring at MYP is cheap per hour and avoids the expensive rescue later.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah campuses run the MYP and hand students to a Diploma in Dubai or Abu Dhabi, so the Personal Project and the Extended Essay are sometimes supervised by different schools entirely. Where that happens, nobody owns the continuity, and a mentor who has seen both tasks is doing a genuinely different job.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme sets a Reflective Project rather than an Extended Essay. It is shorter, built around an ethical dilemma arising from the student's career-related study, and assessed on its own criteria. Parents who search for Extended Essay help and find themselves in a CP cohort are buying a different task: the research discipline transfers, the mark scheme does not, and a mentor who has only coached Extended Essays will misdirect the work.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is thinly represented in Sharjah, which means a CP candidate has almost no peers to compare notes with and almost no local mentoring market. This is the clearest case in the emirate for online matching on subject expertise rather than on postcode.

sharjah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.subjectsIntro: The essay is registered in one subject, and that choice changes both the mark profile and the hours. These are the registrations Sharjah candidates most often bring, with what each one costs in mentor time and where it leaks marks.

subjects.name: History
subjects.levels: Essay registered at HL or SL
subjects.description: A History essay needs a question with a defensible argument and a body of secondary sources that disagree with each other. Candidates lose criterion C marks by narrating rather than evaluating. Mentor hours go on historiography and on cutting the narrative, not on finding more sources. Usually the cheapest subject family to support well.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.levels: Essay registered at HL or SL
subjects.description: Requires a real-world situation, a defined economic concept and diagrams that carry argument rather than decoration. The commonest failure is a question that cannot be answered with available data. Hours go on scoping and on quantitative honesty. A Sharjah-specific question - port throughput, retail rents, school fee regulation - is often stronger than a global one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: Essay registered at HL or SL
subjects.description: Primary data raises the cost: an experimental Biology essay needs a protocol, a risk assessment, replication and a statistical test chosen before the data is collected. Where school laboratory access is limited, a database or secondary-data essay is the honest route. Hours go on method design and on uncertainty, and that work has to happen early.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: Essay registered at HL or SL
subjects.description: The hardest subject family to support late, because the chemistry has to be correct at a level above the taught course. Candidates lose marks for a question that is really a Year 11 practical in longer form. Mentor time goes on narrowing the question to something measurable and on error propagation in the results section.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.levels: Essay registered at HL or SL
subjects.description: Attractive to students and risky in practice. Primary research involving human participants brings ethical requirements that most school settings cannot clear, so the workable route is a critical review of published studies. Hours go on turning a topic into a question with competing evidence, and on resisting the urge to summarise textbooks.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.levels: Essay registered at HL or SL
subjects.description: A literary or language essay needs a close-reading argument, not a theme hunt. The commonest cost is a text choice too thin to support 4,000 words. Mentor hours go on selecting the extracts the essay will actually analyse and on keeping the argument from collapsing into plot summary in the middle third.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Essay registered at HL or SL
subjects.description: Rarely chosen and often rewarded, because the field is less crowded. A Mathematics essay must contain mathematics beyond the syllabus, properly explained, with the student's own worked development rather than a transcription. Hours go on checking that the mathematics is both correct and the candidate's own, and on presentation of notation.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.levels: Essay registered at HL or SL
subjects.description: Needs a forward-looking question about a real organisation and primary or secondary evidence to answer it. Candidates lose marks when the essay becomes a company profile. Mentor time goes on framing a question the available evidence can settle, which for a Sharjah-based organisation often means an interview that must be arranged weeks ahead.

subjects.name: World Studies
subjects.description: An interdisciplinary essay on a global issue examined through two subjects. It can score well and it can fail badly, because the two disciplines must genuinely interact rather than sit in separate halves. The highest-supervision option on the list, and the one most often chosen for the wrong reason - that no single subject appealed.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.levels: Essay registered at HL or SL
subjects.description: An essay written in Arabic is assessed on the same criteria in that language, and it needs a mentor who reads the language at academic level. In Sharjah this is a thinner market than in Dubai, and it is one of the registrations where matching online rather than locally changes what is available at all.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.levels: Essay registered at HL or SL
subjects.description: A Visual Arts essay is an art-historical or theoretical argument, not a portfolio commentary. Candidates who expect to write about their own practice are usually in the wrong component. Hours go on building a question around works the student can actually see or access reproducibly, and on referencing images correctly for criterion D.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: Essay registered at HL or SL
subjects.description: Experimental Physics essays live or die on whether the quantity being measured can be measured to useful precision with school equipment. A simulation or data-analysis route is often stronger. Mentor time goes on uncertainty analysis, which is where most Physics essays lose both criterion B and criterion C marks at once.

sharjah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.regionsTitle: Where Sharjah Extended Essay candidates actually live, and what changes locally
sharjah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.regionsIntro: Sharjah is not one market. The side of the emirate a family lives on changes which school the candidate attends, how reachable the supervisor is, and when a session can realistically start on a weekday.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Pressed against the Dubai border, and the clearest example of the cross-emirate pattern: many Al Nahda students attend Dubai campuses. A supervisor meeting means a trip back across Al Ittihad Road, and that journey is why evening online sessions here start at 19:00 rather than 17:00.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Dense towers around Khalid Lagoon with a short run to both Sharjah and Dubai schools. Flats rather than villas, which matters for an essay needing a quiet recorded interview or a long uninterrupted drafting block. Public library access nearby is a genuine advantage for source work.

regions.name: Al Taawun
regions.note: Another border community with heavy commuter flow, and a candidate population split between Sharjah and Dubai campuses. Families here often discover the internal Extended Essay deadline late, because school communication reaches them through a campus they rarely visit in person.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: Close to several large Sharjah campuses and to University City, so school-run distances are short and after-school slots can start earlier. Science essays benefit here: proximity to the campus makes a second laboratory session practical in a way it is not from Al Nahda.

regions.name: Aljada and Al Zahia
regions.note: Newer master-planned districts with young school catchments and a growing Diploma cohort. Candidates often come from campuses that have only recently started authorising Diploma cohorts, so supervisor experience with a given subject registration can be genuinely thin.

regions.name: University City and Al Nouf
regions.note: Adjacent to the University of Sharjah and the American University of Sharjah. Candidates here have unusually good access to academic libraries, which is a real advantage for a History, Economics or Psychology essay built on published literature rather than primary data.

regions.name: Al Qasimia and Al Khan
regions.note: Older central districts with a mix of Indian, British and American curriculum schools and a long-established tutoring market. Expect more local in-home offers here than elsewhere in the emirate, and therefore more price variance between quotes for the same job.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan and Kalba
regions.note: The east coast exclaves, under the same SPEA regulation but two hours from the main city. No realistic local mentoring market for a specialist subject registration, and the clearest case in Sharjah for online delivery rather than a search for someone nearby.

regions.name: Al Suyoh and Tilal City
regions.note: Outer residential growth areas with longer school runs in both directions. Session timing here is set by the return journey rather than by the student's preference, and clustering two sessions at a weekend often costs less in practice than four scattered weekday hours.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah campuses running the Diploma or the MYP
schoolClusters.note: Named for context only. Cohort size is the relevant fact: a Sharjah Diploma year group is often a fraction of a comparable Dubai one, so a candidate registering an essay in a less common subject may have no peer and a supervisor stretched across several registrations.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai campuses that Sharjah families commute to
schoolClusters.note: A large share of Sharjah Diploma candidates sit their papers at Dubai-licensed campuses regulated by KHDA rather than SPEA. That split matters for deadlines and for supervisor access, and it is the reason a Sharjah postcode tells you little about which calendar a family is actually working to.

schoolClusters.city: Where Sharjah Diploma leavers commonly apply
schoolClusters.note: Useful context for parents weighing what three core points are worth. Local admissions treat the Diploma total and the Higher Level grades as the primary signals; the Extended Essay grade matters mainly through the points it contributes and occasionally as evidence of research capacity.
schools: Universities abroad entered through the Diploma total

sharjah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools and universities are named here as context for the Sharjah education market; no affiliation, endorsement or relationship with IB Gram is implied or claimed.
sharjah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways to buy Extended Essay support, priced differently because they are different products. The stage your child is at usually decides which one is sensible rather than which one is cheapest per hour.

modes.title: Stage blocks: buy the job, not the term
modes.description: The most common arrangement for an essay. A block is scoped to one stage - question design, method design, draft review, reflections and viva preparation - with a fixed number of hours and a written output at the end. It suits a single submitted piece of work far better than an open-ended weekly slot, and it makes the total cost visible before you commit to it.
bullets: Each block names its hours and what you receive in writing
Draft review includes mentor reading time, which a bare hourly rate usually hides
Blocks can be bought out of order if a deadline has already moved
No block includes any writing of the essay itself

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through DP1 and DP2
modes.description: A standing weekly hour from the term the essay is introduced until submission. More expensive in total than stage blocks and usually better value per mark, because criterion C is built over months rather than rescued in weeks. Families who also want subject support in the registered subject tend to choose this, since the same mentor can carry both without duplicating context.
bullets: Suits a candidate who has not yet settled a research question
Allows the reflections to be written at the points the IB intends
Session notes accumulate into a record of the student's own process
Pauses around mock weeks without losing the slot

modes.title: Single diagnostic session
modes.description: One hour on a finished or near-finished draft, with written feedback mapped to the five criteria and a short list of the changes worth making in the time left. The cheapest honest intervention available and the right first purchase for a family unsure whether they need anything at all. It is also the only sensible purchase inside the final fortnight before an internal deadline.
bullets: Written criterion-by-criterion notes the student can act on alone
Identifies whether the problem is the question or the prose
No commitment to further hours
Available for a draft in English or Arabic

sections.heading: What Extended Essay support costs in Sharjah, stage by stage
paragraphs: An Extended Essay is a fixed job with a known shape, so it can be priced by stage rather than by term. The table below takes the published market bands for the UAE - roughly AED 150-300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online and AED 200-450 or more for a Diploma specialist - and applies them to the five stages an essay actually passes through. The hours column is the useful one. Most quotes you receive will name a rate and leave the hours to your imagination, which is how an AED 200 hour becomes an AED 2,400 essay without anybody saying so.

Read it as a ceiling rather than a plan. Very few candidates buy all five stages. A student whose question is sound and whose school supervision is attentive may need nothing beyond a single draft review. A student who arrives in DP2 with a question that cannot be answered is buying stages one and two over again, which is the single most expensive position to be in and the one most easily avoided by spending one hour early.

Two cost lines in the table are routinely left out of quotes. The first is mentor reading time: a 4,000-word draft read properly against five criteria takes longer than the lesson that follows it, and a provider who charges only for contact time is either absorbing that cost or not doing the reading. The second is the reflections. They carry six marks, they are assessed from a form of no more than 500 words, and they are almost always written in a rush the night before a deadline, which is a cheap place to lose marks and a cheap place to protect them.
bullets: Hours, not hourly rate, is the number that decides what you pay
Stage one bought late is paid for twice
Draft review that excludes reading time is not draft review
The 500-word reflection form carries six of the 34 marks

rows: Narrowing a subject interest into an answerable question with competing evidence
Protocol, ethics, data availability or the reading list the argument will rest on

sections.heading: Why the subject the essay is registered in changes the bill
paragraphs: Parents usually expect the level to drive the price. For an Extended Essay it does not - there is no Higher or Standard version of the essay. What drives the price is the registered subject, because subjects differ in how much of the work has to happen before a single word of argument is possible. A History essay needs a reading list. A Chemistry essay needs a measurable reaction, a risk assessment and equipment that exists in the school. Those are not the same purchase.

The pattern across the market is consistent. Essays built on published literature - History, Economics, English, Psychology as a critical review - are the cheapest to support properly, because the expensive early decisions are decisions about reading rather than about apparatus. Essays requiring primary data are dearer, and the cost is front-loaded: a method designed in week two is cheap, and the same method redesigned in week twelve because the first set of results was unusable is not. World Studies is the outlier, because an interdisciplinary question needs two subject perspectives to interact rather than alternate, and that integration is the part students cannot see is missing.

There is a Sharjah-specific line in this. Where a registration is uncommon in the emirate - Arabic A at academic level, Mathematics, Visual Arts theory - the local pool of people able to supervise it closely is small, and scarcity moves a quote more than subject difficulty does. That is also the clearest argument for matching on expertise rather than proximity: a candidate in Khor Fakkan registering a Mathematics essay is not choosing between a local specialist and an online one. There is no local specialist to choose.

table.caption: SUPPORT LOAD BY REGISTERED SUBJECT - WHAT THE HOURS BUY
rows: Question design, source evaluation, cutting narrative from argument
Framing a question the available evidence can settle; ethics screening
Method design, replication, uncertainty and error propagation
Verifying the mathematics is correct, beyond syllabus and the student's own
Academic-level argument in Arabic, assessed on the same criteria
Making two disciplines genuinely interact rather than sit in halves

sections.heading: Thirty-four marks, five criteria, and what each one costs to repair
paragraphs: If you are paying by the hour, it helps to know which marks the hours can still reach. The five criteria are not equally repairable late. Criterion C carries 12 marks for critical thinking and is largely decided by the research question: an essay asking a question that only has one answer cannot demonstrate evaluation however well it is written. By the time a full draft exists, criterion C is mostly fixed, and the money spent on prose polishing is buying criterion D.

Criterion A, focus and method, carries 6 marks and is also a question-level property, though a draft can still be re-framed around a sharper version of the same question if there are weeks rather than days left. Criterion B, knowledge and understanding, carries 6 and is the one most responsive to targeted reading - a student who has used the subject's own terminology loosely can be taught to use it precisely in a couple of sessions. Criterion D, presentation, carries 4 marks and is genuinely cheap to secure: consistent referencing, a contents page, correct labelling, no appendix doing the work of the body.

Criterion E, engagement, carries 6 marks and is assessed from the reflections rather than from the essay. This is the most mispriced criterion in the market. Six marks out of 34 is almost 18 per cent of the essay, and it is awarded for evidence of the student's own intellectual process - decisions taken, routes abandoned, what the setbacks taught them. A reflection written retrospectively to fill a box reads exactly like one. Dated, specific reflections written at the time cost almost nothing and are worth the same marks as a chunk of the argument.
bullets: Criterion C: 12 marks, set by the question, hardest to repair late
Criterion A: 6 marks, re-framing possible with weeks in hand
Criterion B: 6 marks, most responsive to targeted subject reading
Criterion D: 4 marks, cheapest to secure and most often conceded
Criterion E: 6 marks, from the reflections, not from the essay

sections.heading: A tutoring dirham in context: Sharjah fees, SPEA and the marginal hour
paragraphs: Private tutoring is bought alongside a school fee that is already being paid, so the useful question is not whether an hour is expensive in the abstract but what it buys relative to everything else on the bill. Sharjah has a specific feature here. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fee levels in Sharjah are reviewed figures rather than free-market ones, which makes them a more stable benchmark than in markets where they are not.

For comparison on the Dubai side of the border, where many Sharjah Diploma candidates actually attend school, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That matters to a Sharjah family with a child at a Dubai campus: the school line on the household budget is flat for the year, which is the context in which a new tutoring line is being considered.

The table below sets out the comparison honestly. Note what is not in it: an IB Gram price. We publish market bands because they are checkable, and we quote for a specific job after a free trial lesson rather than from a sticker. The one figure worth more attention than the rest is the bottom row. Three core points bought through the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge generally cost fewer hours than three subject grade boundaries, which is the arithmetic most families have never had put in front of them.

sections.heading: The Sharjah commute is a line item on an Extended Essay
paragraphs: In most emirates the online-versus-in-home question is about convenience. In Sharjah it is partly about which emirate the school is in. A family in Al Nahda or Al Taawun whose child attends a Dubai campus is already absorbing a cross-border journey twice a day on Al Ittihad Road or the E311. Adding a third journey - a supervisor meeting, a tuition centre, a mentor travelling in - is not a neutral decision about preference. It is an hour of someone's day, and in an in-home rate it is an hour somebody is paying for.

That is visible in the published numbers. In-home one-to-one visits in the UAE market run roughly AED 180-500 an hour including travel, against AED 150-300 for a qualified tutor working online. The gap is not a quality gap. It is a travel gap, and it compounds: a mentor with four in-home clients across Sharjah can fit fewer sessions into an evening than one working online, so the scarce evening slots go to whoever pays most for them. For a specialist subject registration, the practical effect in Sharjah is that the slot you want does not exist locally at any price.

Online one-to-one removes the travel from both sides and changes what the pool contains. An Extended Essay registered in Arabic A, Mathematics or Visual Arts theory needs someone who reads that subject at academic level. Matching on expertise rather than on driving distance is the whole argument, and it is a stronger argument in Khor Fakkan and Kalba than anywhere else in the emirate. Lessons run over live video with screen sharing, which for a research essay means the draft, the sources and the mentor's annotations are all on one screen and all saved.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from submission: when an hour is worth most
paragraphs: The deadline that binds a Sharjah candidate is almost never the IB's. It is the internal date the school sets so that supervisors can complete their own obligations before the external submission window. Schools in this emirate set those dates differently, and families who have the written internal calendar in hand from DP1 spend less than families who learn the date when it has nearly passed. Ask the Diploma coordinator for it in writing, and ask for the three reflection points as well, because those are the moments criterion E is actually earned.

No IB session or results date is published on this page. The IB's own assessment pages block automated checking, so nothing about the May or November window here has been confirmed from the source, and an unverified date on a page like this is worse than no date. Confirm every IB deadline with your child's coordinator or on ibo.org directly. What can be said with confidence is the shape: the essay is a DP1-into-DP2 task, the question should be settled before the long summer between the two years, and the reflections are spread across the whole period rather than collected at the end.

Where the money goes furthest is early and unglamorous. One hour spent testing whether a question can actually be answered is the highest-return hour available, because it is the hour that protects 12 criterion C marks and prevents the whole of stage one being bought twice. The lowest-return hours are the ones bought in the final fortnight, which can secure criterion D and tidy criterion B but cannot change what the essay is about. If you only ever buy one hour, buy it in DP1.
bullets: Get the school's internal Extended Essay calendar in writing during DP1
Settle the research question before the summer between DP1 and DP2
Write each reflection at its own point, not retrospectively
Confirm every IB date with the coordinator or ibo.org, not with a tutoring page

sections.heading: What the fee never buys, however much it is
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is the component where academic honesty is tested hardest, because it is the only one produced largely out of sight over many months. There is a clean line and it is worth having in writing before any money changes hands. A mentor may teach research method, explain the criteria, ask questions about an argument, point to where reasoning is thin, model referencing conventions and rehearse the concluding interview. A mentor may not produce text that appears in the essay, restructure the argument on the student's behalf, supply a research question as a finished item, or edit a draft to completion.

Some providers in this market sell the other thing. One operation found in research for these pages sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Buying that is an academic malpractice case against the student, not against the seller, and the consequence sits with the candidate. The IB's authenticity declaration is signed by the student, and the viva voce exists in part so a supervisor can satisfy themselves that the work is the student's own. A candidate who cannot discuss the decisions in their own essay has a problem no fee can solve.

School supervision has its own limits, and they are worth knowing so you can see what you are buying on top. Supervisors are permitted a defined amount of comment on one draft, and the rest of the support is conversation rather than annotation. That is by design. A paid mentor does not increase the amount of commenting a supervisor may do; what a mentor adds is time, subject depth and an outside reading. Anyone offering more than that is offering something the IB does not permit, and the person who pays for it is the student.
bullets: A mentor teaches method, asks questions and gives feedback on the student's own work
A mentor never supplies text, a finished question or a restructured argument
The authenticity declaration is signed by the candidate, not by any tutor
The viva voce tests whether the student can discuss their own decisions

sections.heading: Permits, invoices and the questions to ask before paying anyone
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted work, not unregulated work. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers working in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The official route is the service listed by MoHRE as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the ministry's app, website and e-services system, with no fee and a stated two-working-day completion time.

Two consequences for a Sharjah parent. A tutor who tells you the permit is expensive and that the cost is inside your rate is describing something that does not exist - the permit is free. And individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no figure is quoted here; a number circulating online could not be verified against any ministry source and should be treated with caution wherever you see it.

On invoices, ask three plain questions. Does the quoted figure include reading time for a draft, or only contact time? Is the figure per hour or per session, and how long is a session? And is the quote inclusive of any tax that applies - a question to put to the provider in writing, since the tax treatment of tuition is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring page to assert. Separately, be careful of any offer routed through a non-UAE phone number as the only contact path, and of any claim of regulator endorsement. IB Gram holds no permit or accreditation from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge, and says so plainly. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is not the same as being endorsed by one.
