sections.heading: What a grade rise is worth in points, and what it costs to buy
paragraphs: The Extended Essay does not produce points on its own. It combines with Theory of Knowledge in a matrix that awards up to three of the 45 Diploma points, and a grade E in either is a failing condition that can prevent the Diploma being awarded regardless of subject grades. So the value of a paid hour is not one grade letter in isolation - it is the movement in the matrix, plus the removal of a failing condition that would otherwise cost everything. Confirm the current matrix with your child's coordinator; it is published in the IB's assessment procedures and the IB revises those documents.

The arithmetic is worth seeing because it points money in an unexpected direction. Moving from a D to a C in the Extended Essay, with Theory of Knowledge steady, is usually a one-point movement and costs a handful of hours - mostly spent on criterion B and criterion D, which are the responsive ones. Moving from a C to an A is a larger job, because it requires criterion C marks, and criterion C is a question-level property. Meanwhile lifting a Higher Level subject by one grade generally means lifting performance across two or three papers. Three core points are routinely cheaper in hours than three subject points.

The one case where cost should not be the deciding factor is a candidate heading for an E. That is not a points conversation. It is a Diploma-award conversation, and it is the situation where a single diagnostic session on an existing draft is the most useful AED 150 to AED 450 a Sharjah family can spend, because it establishes quickly whether the problem is the prose, the question, or the fact that there is not yet an essay. No mentor can promise a grade, and anybody who offers one should be questioned on exactly that point.

process.title: Tell us the registration and the deadline
process.description: Two facts decide almost everything: the subject the essay is registered in, and the school's internal submission date. Send those with a short note on what exists already - a topic, a question, a draft, nothing. A Sharjah family with a child at a Dubai campus should say so, because the calendar that binds you is that school's.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a subject-matched mentor
process.description: One session at no charge, with a mentor who reads the registered subject at academic level. The purpose is diagnostic: whether the question will hold, whether the available evidence can answer it, and which criteria are currently at risk. You get that read whether or not you continue afterwards.

process.title: A quote for the job, not a rate card
process.description: After the trial we quote for the stages your child actually needs, with the hours named and the written outputs listed. If the honest answer is a single diagnostic session and nothing more, that is the quote. If the honest answer is that school supervision is already covering it, we say so.

process.title: Work in blocks against the school's dates
process.description: Sessions are timed to the internal calendar rather than to a fixed weekly slot, which suits a single submitted piece of work. Drafts and annotations stay on a shared screen and are saved, so what the mentor wrote in week four is still readable in week fourteen when the viva comes round.

process.title: Reflections and viva, then stop
process.description: The last stage is the one most families skip: writing the three reflections at their proper points, clearing presentation and referencing, and rehearsing the concluding interview. After submission there is nothing useful left to buy, and we end the engagement rather than extend it into the subject.

whyPoints.title: Prices quoted in dirhams, with the hours attached
whyPoints.description: Every figure on this page is a published market band from a named source, applied to a stated number of hours. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. A Sharjah family transacts in AED and deserves to see the total, not the rate.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the registered subject, not on your district
whyPoints.description: An Extended Essay in Arabic A, Mathematics or Visual Arts theory needs a mentor who reads that field at academic level. Online delivery means the pool is the pool of specialists rather than the pool of people who can reach Al Suyoh by 17:00, which for several registrations is the difference between support and no support.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: We teach method, question arguments and give written feedback on the student's own work. We do not supply text, finished research questions or restructured arguments. One operation in this market sells completed coursework outright; the malpractice case from that lands on the candidate, and we will not put a student there.

whyPoints.title: No claim of regulator or board endorsement
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation or partnership from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no page here implies otherwise. We explain what each regulator does because parents need to know, which is a different thing from borrowing its authority.

whyPoints.title: Sources cited, dates attached, nothing invented
whyPoints.description: Regulator positions here come from u.ae, web.khda.gov.ae and mohre.gov.ae. No IB exam or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own pages cannot be checked automatically and an unverified date would be worse than none. Where a figure could not be verified, including the fine schedule, it is left out.

whyPoints.title: A free trial before any commitment
whyPoints.description: One session at no charge with a subject-matched mentor, with no card required and no obligation to continue. For many Sharjah families the trial is the whole purchase: it establishes whether the research question holds, which is the one piece of information that changes what everything else costs.

faqs.question: What should a Sharjah family budget for Extended Essay support from start to submission?
faqs.answer: Budget by stage rather than by term. Published UAE market rates run roughly AED 150-300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor working online and AED 200-450 or more for a Diploma specialist. The five stages of an essay - question design, method or reading plan, draft review, reflections, viva preparation - typically total seven to fourteen hours. That puts a complete stage-block route between about AED 1,050 and AED 3,600 at those bands. A standing weekly hour across both Diploma years costs considerably more and is better value per mark only if it starts early. Most families spend far less than the full range, because few need all five stages.

faqs.question: Is Extended Essay coaching charged by the hour or by the draft?
faqs.answer: Both models exist in this market and they are not equivalent. An hourly figure usually covers contact time only, which hides a real cost: reading a 4,000-word draft properly against five criteria takes two to three hours before any lesson happens. A per-draft or per-stage price includes that reading and makes the total visible before you commit. Ask any provider directly whether reading time is inside the quoted figure. If the answer is no, add it yourself when you compare quotes, otherwise you are comparing a complete price against a partial one.

faqs.question: Does an essay in a science cost more to support than one in History?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the reason is where the work sits rather than how hard the subject is. A Biology, Chemistry or Physics essay needs a method, replication, a risk assessment and equipment that actually exists in the school, and all of that has to be settled before writing. Those hours are front-loaded, and a method redesigned after unusable results is paid for twice. Essays built on published literature - History, English A, Economics - concentrate their hours on question design and source evaluation, which is cheaper and more forgiving of a late start.

faqs.question: We live in Sharjah but our son's school is in Dubai. Does that change what we pay?
faqs.answer: It changes the calendar more than the price. The internal submission date that binds your son is set by his Dubai campus under KHDA, not by anything in Sharjah, and families who learn that date late are the ones who end up buying emergency hours. Practically, the commute also sets your session times: an Al Nahda or Al Taawun family is usually looking at a 19:00 start rather than 17:00 once the return journey on Al Ittihad Road is accounted for. Online delivery removes a third journey from the day entirely.

faqs.question: Our daughter's research question has been approved but clearly will not work. How many hours is a rethink?
faqs.answer: One to three hours if there is still time, and it is the best-value money in the whole process. A question that only has one answer cannot earn criterion C marks, and criterion C is 12 of the 34 available. Reworking it usually means keeping the subject area and narrowing to something with competing evidence and reachable sources. If a full draft already exists and the deadline is weeks away, a partial re-frame around a sharper version of the same question is often possible. If the deadline is days away, the honest advice is to protect criteria B and D instead.

faqs.question: Does SPEA set or approve what a private tutor in Sharjah can charge?
faqs.answer: No. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for private schools. That authority covers schools, not individual tutors. A private tutor's rate is a commercial matter between the tutor and the family. What SPEA's role does give you is a stable benchmark: school fees in Sharjah are reviewed figures rather than freely set ones, which makes them a useful comparison point when you are deciding what an extra private hour is worth alongside the fees already paid.

faqs.question: At what point in the two Diploma years is Extended Essay money best spent?
faqs.answer: Early and on the question. One hour spent testing whether a research question can actually be answered protects the 12 criterion C marks and prevents the whole of the scoping stage being bought a second time in DP2. The research question should be settled before the long break between the two Diploma years. Hours bought in the final fortnight can secure criterion D presentation marks and tighten criterion B, but they cannot change what the essay is about. If you only ever buy one hour, buy it in the first Diploma year.

faqs.question: Can we pay for a single session just to have a finished draft checked?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most sensible first purchase for a family who is not sure they need anything. One hour on a complete draft, with written feedback mapped to the five criteria, establishes whether the problem is the prose, the question or the absence of an argument. At published market bands that is roughly AED 150-450 with no commitment to anything further. The output is a short list of changes the student can make alone. For a candidate at risk of a grade E it is the single most useful hour available.

faqs.question: How many hours does an essay with primary data usually need?
faqs.answer: More than a literature-based one, and the hours arrive earlier. Expect two to four hours on method design alone: what will be measured, how often, with what equipment, with what risk assessment, and which statistical test was chosen before any data was collected. Add the usual two to three hours of draft review and one to two on the reflections. Twelve hours across the project is common for an experimental science registration against six to eight for a History or Economics essay. The difference is almost entirely in the front half.

faqs.question: What does a tutoring quote in this market usually leave out?
faqs.answer: Three things. Reading time on a draft, which is where the real hours of a review sit. The number of hours the job actually takes, so you see a rate without a total. And whether the figure is per hour or per session, since a 45-minute session quoted hourly is not what it appears to be. Ask about all three in writing. On tax, ask the provider directly whether their figure is inclusive; the tax treatment of tuition is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority and not something a tutoring page should assert on your behalf.

faqs.question: Does the Extended Essay grade move the Diploma total enough to justify the spend?
faqs.answer: It can, and the arithmetic is more favourable than parents expect. The Extended Essay combines with Theory of Knowledge in a matrix awarding up to three of the 45 points, and a grade E in either is a failing condition that can stop the Diploma being awarded at all. Three points earned through the core generally cost fewer hours than lifting a Higher Level subject by three grades, because that means moving performance across two or three papers. Confirm the current matrix with your child's Diploma coordinator rather than relying on any third-party summary.

faqs.question: Are Extended Essay sessions better weekly, or clustered around deadlines?
faqs.answer: Clustered, for most candidates. The essay is a single submitted piece of work with distinct stages rather than a syllabus that needs covering, so a standing weekly hour often ends up filling time between the moments that matter. Two hours in the week a question is being settled are worth more than eight spread over two months. The exception is a student who has not yet found a question at all, or one taking subject tuition in the registered subject anyway, where a weekly slot lets criterion C build gradually instead of being rescued.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to support the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together?
faqs.answer: Often, because the two feed the same three-point matrix and a mentor who understands one has most of the context for the other. The saving is in shared context rather than a discounted rate: the same conversation about what counts as evidence, what an unsupported claim looks like and how to evaluate a source serves both components. Whether one mentor can cover both depends on the subject the essay is registered in. A science registration usually needs a subject specialist for the essay, with Theory of Knowledge handled separately.

faqs.question: Does an Extended Essay mentor in Sharjah need a MoHRE permit, and is its cost in our fee?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it costs nothing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. So any tutor telling you their rate carries the cost of a permit is describing an expense that does not exist. Ask to see the permit document before a first paid session. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule has been published and no figure should be quoted to you.

faqs.question: Can a mentor collect or process our child's data to save time?
faqs.answer: No, and the saving would be worthless. The essay must be the candidate's own work, the authenticity declaration is signed by the student, and the viva voce exists partly so a supervisor can confirm the student can discuss their own decisions. A mentor may teach how to design a protocol, explain which statistical test suits a data set and show what a clean results table looks like. The student collects, enters and analyses. A candidate who cannot account for where a number came from has a problem that no amount of paid support can repair.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is free who reads our child's registered subject?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than offering a near-match. For some registrations in Sharjah - Arabic A at academic level, Visual Arts theory, Mathematics - the pool is genuinely thin, and a general essay mentor placed on a specialist registration gives you confident advice about the wrong things. The honest options are a wait for the right person, a single diagnostic session with a generalist to triage criteria B and D only, or a clear recommendation that school supervision plus the student's own work is the better route. All three are preferable to a mismatch.

sharjah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one hour on the research question
sharjah/ib-dp-extended-essay-tutor.closingBody: If your child's Extended Essay question is not yet settled, that is where a Sharjah family's money goes furthest: one hour, early, protecting the 12 marks that cannot be recovered later. If a draft already exists, a single diagnostic session will tell you whether the problem is the prose, the question or the argument, and what the remaining weeks can realistically reach. Either way the first session is free, matched to the subject the essay is registered in, and delivered online over live video on Gulf Standard Time. You will get a quote for the stages your child needs, with the hours named - not an hourly rate with the total left to guesswork.

intro.heading: Why AA HL tutors are hard to find in Sharjah, and what to do about it
paragraphs: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the IB's most demanding mathematics course. The IB recommends 240 teaching hours for a Higher Level subject against 150 at Standard Level, and that extra ninety hours is not revision of familiar material. It is complex numbers in polar and Euler form, proof by induction and contradiction, vectors with lines and planes in three dimensions, Maclaurin series, implicit differentiation, L'Hopital's rule and differential equations. None of that exists in AA SL.

Which creates a supply problem specific to this emirate. Sharjah's Diploma cohort is small. Victoria International School of Sharjah is the emirate's best-known IB continuum school, and a large number of Sharjah families send their children into Dubai IB schools instead, commuting daily from Al Nahda, Al Majaz and Al Taawun. A tutor who teaches AA HL properly, as opposed to teaching maths in general, is therefore a rare thing to find within driving distance of any particular Sharjah address.

That scarcity is the single strongest argument for online delivery, and it is not a marketing argument. IB Gram delivers AA HL support as live one-to-one video lessons. IB Gram does not run home visits in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE, because home visits are a service offered only in India. Maths works unusually well over video: a shared whiteboard holds working that both people can annotate, a graphing display can be mirrored directly, and the written solution survives the lesson rather than vanishing into a notebook.

The rest of this page is organised around money, because that is the decision most families are actually making. Private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which u.ae describes as regulating private education in the emirate and which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. School fees are a known quantity; tutoring is not, because almost nobody in this market publishes a rate. Three of the six most visible providers researched publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars.

So below you will find the AED bands with the source of each figure named, a breakdown of what raises and lowers the number in Sharjah specifically, and an honest account of what the in-home premium buys here. There is no IB Gram price list on this page. Our quote follows a free trial lesson, once we know whether the problem is Paper 1 fluency, Paper 3 technique or an exploration that has not started. Those three need very different numbers of hours, and a figure offered before that question has been asked is not a quote so much as a guess. One other thing worth saying early: the IB blocks automated checking of its own pages, so no exam or results date appears anywhere on this page. Confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: AA HL sits at the end of a route rather than at the start of one, and the courses on either side of it decide how much ground a student has to make up. The grid below covers the Diploma, the programme that feeds it, and the alternatives families in Sharjah weigh against it.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across two years, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Mathematics is compulsory, which is why the AA HL decision is the one most likely to be made for the wrong reason: students pick it because it keeps options open rather than because the course suits them. Grades run 1 to 7 per subject, with bonus points from TOK and the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah's Diploma cohort is smaller than Dubai's, and many students commute across the border to Dubai IB schools from Al Nahda and Al Majaz. That has two consequences for tutoring: a Sharjah student's school deadlines may run on a Dubai school's calendar, and a weekday session realistically starts after the return journey rather than at four in the afternoon.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five-year programme feeding the Diploma, with mathematics assessed against four criteria rather than by examination. Extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5 is the intended preparation for AA HL. The transition catches students out because MYP rewards investigation and communication while AA HL Paper 1 rewards fast, accurate algebra without a calculator, and the second skill is not built by the first.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Sharjah student has come through MYP at a continuum school, the gap to AA HL is usually algebraic fluency rather than conceptual understanding. A bridging block over the summer between MYP 5 and DP1, focused on manipulation without technology, is the cheapest intervention available and almost nobody buys it.

programmes.name: IGCSE Mathematics and Additional Mathematics
programmes.description: The other common feeder, where students arrive from Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher tier, sometimes with Additional Mathematics alongside. Students who took an additional maths qualification arrive in AA HL with calculus already seen and find DP1 manageable. Students who took only the core qualification meet differentiation, integration and radian measure in the same term and feel the course accelerate away from them.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run a British route to Year 11 before students move into a Diploma elsewhere, so a student may change school and curriculum in the same September. Where that happens, a short diagnostic on algebraic fluency before DP1 begins saves a term of guessing at where the gaps are.

programmes.name: International A Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The alternative sixth-form route some Sharjah families consider against AA HL. It is modular rather than terminal in structure, carries no compulsory investigative coursework and allows a student to concentrate on fewer subjects at depth. Against that, the Diploma gives a broader profile and the Extended Essay. Neither route is harder in the abstract; they are differently shaped and suit different students.
programmes.countryNote: Where a family in Sharjah is weighing the two, the deciding factor is usually the destination rather than the maths. Ask the universities you are aiming at how they treat each qualification, and ask the school whether it can actually teach the subject combination you want, since a small cohort limits option blocks more than a prospectus admits.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-aa-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: AA HL is five topic areas plus an exploration, and the HL-only content sits inside those areas rather than in a separate module. The grid below splits the course into the parts a tutor works on separately, with where each is examined.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences, series, the binomial theorem extended to rational exponents, logarithms, partial fractions, counting principles and complex numbers in Cartesian, polar and Euler form. Marks go missing on algebraic manipulation in Paper 1 rather than on understanding, because without a calculator every slip compounds through the rest of the question.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Transformations, rational functions with oblique asymptotes, modulus functions, inverse functions and solving inequalities including those involving absolute value. The HL demand is graphing by reasoning rather than by technology, which Paper 1 tests directly. Sketching a rational function from its asymptotes and intercepts is a drillable skill most students never practise.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Trigonometric identities and equations, compound and double angle formulae, inverse trigonometric functions, and vectors extended to lines and planes in three dimensions with scalar and vector products. Three-dimensional vector geometry is where HL students most often lose whole questions, usually because the diagram was never drawn.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Discrete and continuous random variables, probability density functions, expectation and variance, the binomial and normal distributions, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem. The HL content is procedurally heavy, which makes it reliable marks for a student who drills it and a dependable loss for one who treats it as reading.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Limits, L'Hopital's rule, implicit differentiation, related rates, integration by substitution and by parts, volumes of revolution, Maclaurin series and differential equations including separation of variables and Euler's method. This is the heaviest single block of HL-only material and the one where DP2 students most often run out of teaching time at school.

subjects.name: Proof by induction and contradiction
subjects.description: Formal proof methods that do not appear at Standard Level. Induction in particular is a fixed structure with a small number of moves, which makes it among the most efficient marks in the course to secure. Students lose them by omitting the inductive step's explicit statement rather than by failing to understand the method.

subjects.name: Complex numbers in polar and Euler form
subjects.description: Modulus-argument form, De Moivre's theorem, roots of unity and connections to trigonometric identities. Conceptually unfamiliar and procedurally regular, which is a combination that rewards tutoring: once a student sees the geometry on an Argand diagram, the algebra tends to follow within two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Differential equations and numerical methods
subjects.description: Separation of variables, homogeneous substitutions, the integrating factor method and Euler's method for numerical solutions. These frequently appear in Paper 3 as the backbone of an extended investigation, so a student who has only met them as isolated techniques struggles when they arrive embedded in a longer problem.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: An individual written investigation of roughly twelve to twenty pages, assessed against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. It is a fifth of the final grade, it is the component students plan last, and use of mathematics carries the largest share of its marks.

subjects.name: Non-calculator fluency
subjects.description: Not a topic in the guide but the skill Paper 1 actually measures alongside the content. Exact values, surd and logarithm manipulation, differentiation by rule and algebraic rearrangement all have to be fast and accurate without technology. Students who rely on a graphing display through DP1 discover this in the DP2 mock, which is late.

sections.heading: What AA HL contains and how it is assessed
paragraphs: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is examined through three written papers plus an exploration. Paper 1 allows no technology and runs two hours for 30% of the grade. Paper 2 requires a graphing calculator and also runs two hours for 30%. Paper 3 is Higher Level only: one hour, two extended problem-solving questions, 20% of the grade. The exploration carries the remaining 20%. A graphing calculator is required for the course and a formula booklet is supplied in the papers.

The content sits in five topic areas: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Higher Level does not add a sixth area. It deepens all five, and the additions are substantial: proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers in polar and Euler form, three-dimensional vector geometry, Maclaurin series, implicit differentiation, L'Hopital's rule, continuous random variables and differential equations including Euler's method.

The split between Paper 1 and Paper 2 is the structural fact most students underestimate. The same topic is examined twice, once where every step has to be done by hand and once where a graphing display can do the heavy lifting. A student who has worked through DP1 leaning on technology can know the content and still lose a third of the available marks. Verify current weightings and durations with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, since the IB blocks automated checking of its own pages and no date or figure should be taken from a tutoring site without confirmation.

sections.heading: Paper 3: the hour that decides the grade
paragraphs: Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level and it is unlike the other two. One hour, two questions, and each question is an extended investigation that builds from an accessible opening into something genuinely demanding. The content is drawn from across the course, which means no topic list helps. What helps is technique for the first five minutes of a problem nobody has seen before.

The predictable failure is freezing on part (a). Students trained on Paper 1 and Paper 2 expect to recognise the question type, and a Paper 3 question is designed not to be recognisable. A student who waits for recognition loses the opening minutes and then rushes a question whose later parts depend on the earlier ones. The alternative is a habit: write down what is given, write down what is being asked, try the smallest case, look for a pattern, and only then reach for a general method.

The second predictable failure is writing too little. Paper 3 carries method marks through long chains of reasoning, so a student who reaches a dead end and crosses out their work throws away marks they had already earned. Showing the attempt, naming the method, and stating what was concluded even when the final answer does not arrive is worth real credit. Both habits are trainable in a short block of six to eight sessions using full past questions under the real time limit, which is why Paper 3 deserves its own series rather than a mention inside general revision.

sections.heading: Where AA HL marks are lost, topic by topic
paragraphs: The pattern across Higher Level cohorts is consistent enough to be worth tabulating. Losses cluster in a small number of places, and almost all of them are procedural rather than conceptual. A student who understands vectors in three dimensions still loses the question if the diagram was never drawn. A student who understands induction still loses marks by not stating the inductive step explicitly.

The most expensive loss across the whole course is non-calculator fluency. Paper 1 is 30% of the grade and it tests the same content as Paper 2 with the tools removed. Three terms of leaning on a graphing display produces a student who can do AA HL and cannot do Paper 1, and the first clear signal is usually a DP2 mock. Keeping non-calculator work running weekly from the start of DP1 costs almost nothing and prevents the single largest recoverable loss in the course.

They need a habit installed and then rehearsed under time, which is a different kind of session from the one most families imagine when they book a maths tutor. It is also why marked written work between sessions matters more here than discussion inside them. A student who nods through an explanation of integration by parts and then cannot execute it cold has learned nothing yet, and only a marked attempt reveals which of those two states they are in.

paragraphs: Monthly is the figure that matters, so start there. The Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table estimates a weekly one-hour session at AED 240 to 600 a month for budget tutoring, AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. For a two-year Higher Level course, that is the number to model rather than an hourly rate.

Hourly, the bands are distinct. Budget online tutoring is published from AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online is AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB specialist is AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits across the UAE are quoted at AED 180 to 500 with travel included, and premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes.

For AA HL specifically, the useful observation is that the budget band rarely contains anybody who can teach the HL-only content. A university student can help with SL calculus; Maclaurin series, De Moivre's theorem and Euler's method need somebody who has taught the course. That is not an argument for the most expensive option either, since the premium band above AED 500 is largely brand and scarcity. sections.heading: What moves that number in Sharjah specifically
paragraphs: Four things change a Sharjah quote. The first is scarcity, and it is sharper here than in Dubai. The emirate's Diploma cohort is small and a share of it is enrolled across the border, so the number of people within driving distance who have actually taught AA HL to examination is low. Scarcity raises an in-home price and limits choice at any price, which is a worse problem than the cost.

The second is the commute. A Sharjah student attending a Dubai school is not home until five on a weekday, and a tutor travelling to Al Nahda or Al Taawun in that window is in the heaviest traffic in the country. The in-home band of AED 180 to 500 carries that journey. Remove it and the same hour of teaching sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, which is most of the gap between the two.

The third is which component the student needs. An exploration feedback block is a small number of sessions; rebuilding non-calculator fluency across all five topic areas is a year of weekly work; Paper 3 technique is a short intense series in DP2. Quoting before diagnosing is therefore meaningless, and a provider who gives you a figure before asking which it is has not looked at the problem. The fourth is what the hour contains: marked written work returned between sessions by the teaching tutor is a different product from an hour of conversation, and the market prices them as though they were the same.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against the in-home visit Sharjah families are quoted
paragraphs: In-home tutoring deserves a fair comparison rather than a dismissal. It removes any technology question, suits a younger student who needs supervision as much as teaching, and gives a parent a visible sense of what happened in the hour. Those are real advantages, and they explain why the AED 180 to 500 band exists and why many Sharjah families instinctively ask for it first.

For AA HL the trade-off is unusually stark, because of who is available. A tutor who can reach Al Nahda by six in the evening is selected from the tutors who live near Al Nahda and have that evening free. On a course this specialised, that pool may contain nobody who has taught Paper 3. Online, the pool is every AA HL specialist available in a compatible time zone. For a student stuck on Maclaurin series, that is not a convenience difference; it is the difference between getting help and not.

IB Gram does not sell in-person tutoring in Sharjah, and states that rather than implying otherwise. Lessons run over live video with a shared whiteboard, which for mathematics is genuinely strong: working stays visible, both people annotate the same lines, a graphing display can be mirrored, and the solution is still available the next day. sections.heading: SPEA, the Sharjah school map and the MoHRE permit
paragraphs: Private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. The federal portal u.ae states that SPEA regulates private education in the emirate, and that Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader remit than inspection alone, and it extends across the emirate including the Kalba and Khor Fakkan exclaves on the east coast. SPEA is named by almost no tutoring page competing for these searches.

Private tutoring itself is regulated federally. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. The route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Anybody tutoring without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so a specific amount quoted at you online should be treated as unverified. Two practical points for a Sharjah family: ask any prospective tutor whether they hold the permit, since it costs nothing and there is no reason not to, and do not arrange for your child to be privately tutored by a teacher at their own school, which is barred by the permit's code of conduct. IB Gram holds no approval or licence from SPEA, MoHRE or the International Baccalaureate.

sections.heading: The exploration: a fifth of the grade, planned last
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration carries 20% of the AA HL grade and is assessed against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest single allocation, and at Higher Level the mathematics has to be commensurate with the course. A beautifully written exploration built on Standard Level content will be capped on the criterion that matters most, and students discover this after submission rather than before.

Which makes the topic choice the highest-leverage conversation in the whole component. The right test is not whether a topic is interesting but whether it carries enough HL mathematics to be developed rather than described. A tutor can and should help a student apply that test before any drafting begins, because a topic that fails it cannot be rescued by better writing later. Explorations in Sharjah frequently start too late, with the school's internal deadline arriving in the middle of DP2 mocks.

The honesty boundary is firm. A tutor may teach the mathematics, explain the criteria, question a plan, probe whether the mathematics is genuinely at Higher Level, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, complete or produce any part of the exploration, nor perform its calculations. One provider found in this market sells completed internal assessments outright; that is a malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student whose name is on the work. IB Gram does not do it.

sections.heading: AA HL and engineering admission in the UAE
paragraphs: Many Sharjah families choose AA HL for a destination rather than for the mathematics, and the destination is often an engineering or computing programme. The emirate itself houses two of the country's larger universities, with the American University of Sharjah and the University of Sharjah both in University City, and families in Muwaileh and Al Zahia often have one of them in mind from DP1 onwards.

The honest position is that admission requirements are set by each university and each department, they change, and nobody should take them from a tutoring page. Ask the programme directly and ask in writing. What can be said generally is that analysis-heavy mathematics routes are the ones engineering, mathematics, physics and computing departments most often ask for, while applications-and-interpretation routes are more commonly accepted for business, social science and design programmes. Some departments accept either with a stated grade. Others do not.

Two cautions. Tutoring is not a requirement for admission to any programme, whatever urgency a tutoring advertisement implies, and IB Gram claims no influence over any admissions decision. And a student should not be pushed into AA HL purely to keep a door open: a 4 in AA HL and a 7 in AA SL are not equivalent signals, and the better outcome for a specific student may be the Standard Level course taken well. That conversation belongs with the school's Diploma coordinator before the option blocks close, and in a small Sharjah cohort the blocks close early because fewer combinations can be timetabled at all.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP Math AA HL tutor cost in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Published market rates rather than ours: a qualified subject tutor online is advertised at AED 150 to 300 an hour, an IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 with travel included, and premium named tutors at AED 500 to 650. Monthly, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates put a weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. faqs.question: Is Paper 3 sat only by Higher Level maths students?
faqs.answer: Yes. Paper 3 is a Higher Level component in both IB mathematics courses and Standard Level students do not sit it. It runs one hour, asks two extended problem-solving questions and carries 20% of the grade, which makes it worth as much as the exploration. The content is drawn from anywhere in the course, so revising topics does not prepare it; practising the entry into an unfamiliar investigation does. Confirm the current structure with your school's IB coordinator, because the IB blocks automated checking of its own pages and no figure should be taken from a tutoring site unverified.

faqs.question: How much of the AA HL grade sits in the exploration?
faqs.answer: The internal assessment carries 20%, the same share as Paper 3, and it is assessed against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest single allocation and at Higher Level the mathematics has to match the level of the course, which is where otherwise well-written explorations get capped. The practical consequence is that topic choice matters more than writing quality, because a topic that cannot carry Higher Level mathematics cannot be rescued later. Check your school's internal deadline early, since it usually lands during DP2 mocks.

faqs.question: My son is in DP1 at a Sharjah school and already behind in AA HL. Is that recoverable?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and DP1 is much the better time to act. The common cause is algebraic fluency rather than understanding: a student who came through MYP or a core IGCSE route meets differentiation, radians and logarithms in the same term and the course accelerates away. That is a gap in manipulation, and manipulation responds quickly to weekly marked problem sets. Leaving it until DP2 is harder, because the HL-only calculus arriving that year assumes the earlier fluency. A diagnostic on one marked Paper 1 attempt will show which it is within a single session.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 1 harder than Paper 2 when the content is the same?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 1 removes the graphing calculator and the same content then has to be done by hand with exact values. Surds, logarithms, differentiation by rule, algebraic rearrangement and sketching from reasoning rather than from a display all become the assessed skill. A student who leaned on technology through DP1 can know the whole course and still lose a large share of a paper worth 30% of the grade. Keeping a weekly non-calculator problem set running from the beginning of the course is the cheapest preventive measure in AA HL and almost nobody does it.

faqs.question: Which AA HL topics do not appear in AA SL at all?
faqs.answer: The Higher Level additions are substantial. Proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers in modulus-argument and Euler form with De Moivre's theorem, vectors extended to lines and planes in three dimensions, Maclaurin series, implicit differentiation, related rates, L'Hopital's rule, integration by parts and volumes of revolution, continuous random variables with probability density functions, and differential equations including separation of variables, integrating factors and Euler's method. That is roughly where the extra ninety recommended teaching hours go. A tutor who has only taught Standard Level will not cover them, which is the single most important thing to check before booking.

faqs.question: Do engineering programmes at Sharjah universities expect Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: Requirements are set by each university and each department, they change, and no tutoring page should be your source. Ask the programme directly and get the answer in writing. What can be said generally is that engineering, mathematics, physics and computing departments most often ask for the analysis-heavy route, while business, social science and design programmes more commonly accept applications and interpretation. The American University of Sharjah and the University of Sharjah are both in University City and both publish their own entry criteria. Tutoring is not a requirement for admission to any of them.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write part of my daughter's maths exploration?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider offering to is putting her certificate at risk rather than helping her. A tutor may teach the mathematics, explain the five criteria, question her plan, test whether her chosen topic carries enough Higher Level content and give written feedback on a draft she has written herself. A tutor may not produce text or perform the calculations that get submitted. One provider found in this market sells completed internal assessments; that is an academic-integrity breach and the consequence falls on the student. IB Gram does not supply exploration content in any form.

faqs.question: Our home is in Sharjah but our son studies in Dubai. Does that change session timing?
faqs.answer: It usually sets it. A student leaving a Dubai campus in the early afternoon and travelling home to Al Nahda, Al Majaz or Al Taawun is often not back before five, and a weekday session therefore starts at six or later. He also runs on a Dubai school's internal deadlines for the exploration and for mocks while living under SPEA's jurisdiction at home, which matters when planning a schedule. Because lessons are delivered over live video, none of this requires a tutor to make the same journey, which is most of the reason the model works for commuting families.

faqs.question: Does SPEA license the private tutor we hire in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No, that is MoHRE. SPEA regulates private education in the emirate, and the federal portal notes that Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is a wider remit than inspection. The tutor's permit is separate: the private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's own service. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted online as unverified.

faqs.question: How many AA HL sessions a week do DP2 students in Al Majaz usually book?
faqs.answer: Most begin with one session a week in DP1 and move to two in DP2, with a short third weekly slot appearing during Paper 3 preparation and again while the exploration deadline approaches. Families in Al Majaz commonly take one weekday evening after the commute home plus a weekend morning, since a 4pm weekday start is not realistic for a student travelling back from a Dubai school. Starting earlier at a lower intensity moves more marks per dirham than starting late at a higher one, especially on a course where the content builds for two years.

faqs.question: Is proof by induction really examined in AA HL?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most efficient sets of marks in the course to secure. Induction is a fixed structure with a small number of required moves: establish the base case, assume the statement for some value, prove it for the next, and state the conclusion. Students almost never lose these marks through misunderstanding. They lose them by using the inductive assumption without explicitly stating it, or by omitting the final concluding sentence. Learning to write all four moves every time is a one or two session job that pays back a full question on Paper 1.

faqs.question: What does the in-home premium buy for maths tutoring in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Mostly travel and supervision. In-home visits in the UAE market are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online, and in this emirate the gap is largely a drive through the heaviest traffic in the country at the hour families want. It also narrows the choice to tutors living nearby with a free evening, which on a course as specialised as AA HL can mean nobody who has taught Paper 3. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case; lessons run over live video.

faqs.question: Can AA HL sessions run for the November session as well as May?
faqs.answer: Yes. UAE schools predominantly sit the May session, and a November session also runs, which matters for students resitting or on a different school calendar. Specific IB exam and results dates are not published on this page on purpose: the IB blocks automated checking of its own pages, so any date you see on a tutoring site should be confirmed against ibo.org or your school's IB coordinator before you plan around it. What we can commit to is scheduling, including post-Iftar slots during Ramadan and weekend morning blocks in the final term.

faqs.question: Given how few AA HL tutors there are in this emirate, what if none is available when we need one?
faqs.answer: We tell you. The honest options are a different time in the same week, a specialist in a compatible time zone whose availability fits yours, or a short wait until one frees up after an exam session ends. What we will not do is put a general maths tutor into an AA HL brief and leave you to discover in February that Maclaurin series were never covered. Specialist availability in this emirate is genuinely limited, and disclosing that is more useful than a promise that cannot be kept.

intro.heading: Is Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level the right course?
paragraphs: Mathematics is compulsory in the IB Diploma, and Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level is where a large share of students land. Sometimes that is a considered choice. More often it is what the option block allowed, or what a Year 11 teacher suggested, or what a parent assumed looked better than the alternative. Before buying any tutoring, it is worth establishing which of those happened, because the answer changes what the hours should be spent on.

AA SL recommends 150 teaching hours against 240 for a Higher Level course. It covers the same five topic areas as Higher Level, at less depth, and without the content that defines HL: no vector geometry, no formal proof by induction, no Maclaurin series, no differential equations, no complex numbers in polar form. Assessment is two written papers of an hour and a half each, worth 40% apiece, plus an exploration worth the remaining 20%. There is no Paper 3 at Standard Level.

There is also a sideways choice that matters as much as the level. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level covers different content with a different emphasis, and for a student heading towards business, psychology, design or many social sciences it is frequently the better fit. The two courses are not a ladder with AA above AI. They are different courses, and a student doing well in the one that suits them is a stronger outcome than a student struggling in the one that sounded more rigorous.

Sharjah adds its own practical layer. Private education in the emirate is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which the federal portal u.ae describes as regulating private education in the emirate, and which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The Diploma cohort here is smaller than Dubai's, with Victoria International School of Sharjah the emirate's best-known IB continuum school and many families commuting daily into Dubai schools from Al Nahda and Al Majaz. Small cohorts mean tight option blocks, so a switch between maths routes can be blocked by a timetable rather than by ability.

IB Gram teaches AA SL as live one-to-one video lessons. IB Gram does not run home visits in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE, because home visits are a service offered only in India. What follows is the route decision with its deadline, the paper structure, a subject-by-subject map of the gap from IGCSE, the exploration criteria mark by mark, and the AED bands the Sharjah market publishes with the source of each named. No IB Gram price appears here; the quote follows a free trial lesson. One deliberate omission: no IB examination or results date appears anywhere on this page, because the IB blocks automated checking of its own pages. Confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org rather than from any tutoring site, including this one.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.programmesIntro: The maths decision sits inside a wider set of programme choices, and in a small Sharjah cohort those choices interact. The grid below covers the Diploma, the programme that feeds it, the qualification most students arrive from, and the course-by-course route some families take instead.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects over two years, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service alongside. Mathematics is compulsory and must be taken from one of the four maths courses. Subject grades run 1 to 7 and bonus points come from Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Standard Level maths is the most commonly taken of the four routes.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah the cohort is small enough that option blocks constrain combinations more than published guidance suggests. A student wanting to move between maths routes may find the timetable decides it, so the conversation with the Diploma coordinator should happen before the blocks are confirmed rather than after a disappointing first report.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five-year feeder programme, with mathematics assessed against four criteria rather than through examination. Standard and extended mathematics streams exist in MYP 4 and 5, and the stream a student took is the single best predictor of how AA SL will feel in the first term. MYP rewards investigation and communication; AA SL Paper 1 rewards accurate algebra with no calculator, which the first does not build.
programmes.countryNote: Students coming through MYP at a Sharjah continuum school usually arrive with good mathematical reasoning and weaker manipulation. A short bridging block in the summer before DP1, spent entirely on algebra by hand, is the cheapest intervention available in the whole two years and almost nobody buys it.

programmes.name: IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The commonest feeder into AA SL for students arriving from a British-curriculum school, whether Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher tier. Both cover algebra, trigonometry and graphs thoroughly and neither covers calculus, radian measure or probability distributions. The first term of AA SL therefore introduces several genuinely new ideas at once, which is why DP1 feels steeper than students expect.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run a British route to Year 11 before students move into a Diploma, sometimes at a different school across the border. Where a student changes school and curriculum in the same September, a diagnostic on algebraic fluency before term starts is worth more than a term of guessing where the gaps are.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme courses taken individually
programmes.description: Students may take individual Diploma courses and receive certificates without completing the full Diploma. Mathematics is often one of them. The assessment for the course itself is identical, including the exploration, so the tutoring need is the same; what changes is that the student carries fewer competing deadlines, which usually makes the exploration easier to schedule properly.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah this route appears most often where a student has moved systems mid-sixth-form or is combining study with something else. Ask the school's coordinator what a course certificate means for the universities you are aiming at, because treatment varies and nobody publishes a general rule.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-aa-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: AA SL is five topic areas plus an exploration, assessed across two papers that test the same content under opposite conditions. The grid below splits the course into the parts a tutor works on separately.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences and series with sigma notation, exponents and logarithms, the binomial theorem for positive integer indices, and numerical approximation. The commonest loss is log manipulation on Paper 1, where a student who can solve an exponential equation with a calculator cannot rearrange it by hand into a form that gives an exact answer.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Function notation, domain and range, composite and inverse functions, transformations of graphs, quadratics and simple rational functions. Composite and inverse functions are new to most students arriving from IGCSE and they are examined every year, which makes them reliable marks once the notation stops being intimidating.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangles, the sine and cosine rules, radian measure, arc length and sector area, the unit circle, trigonometric identities and equations, and three-dimensional solids. Radians are the shock: a student who has only ever worked in degrees loses marks across several questions until the switch becomes automatic.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Descriptive statistics, correlation and linear regression, probability including conditional probability and tree diagrams, and the binomial and normal distributions. This is the most calculator-dependent topic in the course and therefore the one most exposed on Paper 1, where distribution work has to be reasoned rather than looked up.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Limits informally, differentiation including the chain, product and quotient rules, tangents and normals, optimisation, kinematics, and integration including definite integrals and areas. Entirely new to most IGCSE students and the largest single block of the course, which is why DP1 accelerates away from anybody who arrives with shaky algebra.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: An individual written investigation assessed against five criteria out of a total of 20 marks. It is worth twice as much as a typical examination question cluster and it is the component students schedule last. Topic choice determines the ceiling, because the use of mathematics criterion carries the largest allocation.

subjects.name: Non-calculator technique
subjects.description: Exact values with surds and in terms of pi, logarithm and index manipulation, differentiation by rule, and sketching from reasoning rather than from a display. Not a topic in the guide but the skill the paper measures alongside the content, and the most common hidden cause of a disappointing Standard Level grade.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: Using a graphing display well: solving numerically, finding intersections, evaluating definite integrals, running distribution calculations and reading a graph for behaviour. Students lose marks by not writing down the expression they entered, since a correct answer with no supporting line can lose the method marks behind it.

subjects.name: Command terms
subjects.description: Write down, find, show that, hence, hence or otherwise, and justify each demand a different response. Hence in particular instructs the student to use the previous part, and ignoring it both wastes time and risks the marks. Sorting past questions by command term is a single-session exercise that keeps paying.

subjects.name: Modelling and context questions
subjects.description: Longer questions set in a real or invented context, where the mathematics has to be extracted before it can be done. Students who can execute every technique still lose these by mistranslating the context. Practising the translation step on its own, without finishing the calculation, is a surprisingly effective drill.

sections.heading: AA SL against AA HL and AI SL, and when the switch window closes
paragraphs: The most valuable session a Sharjah family can buy in the first term of DP1 is sometimes not a maths lesson at all. It is a conversation about whether the student is on the right maths course, held early enough to act on. There are four IB maths routes and three of them are plausible for most students: Analysis and Approaches at Higher or Standard Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level.

The distinction between AA and AI is emphasis rather than difficulty. Analysis and Approaches leans towards algebraic methods, proof-adjacent reasoning and calculus; Applications and Interpretation leans towards modelling, statistics, and mathematics used on real data, with technology integrated throughout. A student who thinks in structures and enjoys manipulation is better served by AA. A student who thinks in data and context is better served by AI, and will usually score higher there.

The practical constraint is the deadline. Schools allow movement between routes for a limited period in DP1, after which the registration and the taught content make a change impractical. In a small Sharjah cohort that window can be shorter than published guidance implies, because a timetable with one Standard Level maths block cannot absorb a student moving across. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the actual cut-off date in writing, in the first month, before anybody needs it. A move made inside the window is administrative; one attempted afterwards usually means a student finishing a course that was never the right one, which costs points in a way no amount of tutoring recovers.

sections.heading: The two papers and the 40 / 40 / 20 split
paragraphs: Standard Level is assessed through two written papers and an exploration. Paper 1 runs an hour and a half with no technology permitted and carries 40% of the grade. Paper 2 runs an hour and a half with a graphing calculator required and also carries 40%. The exploration carries the remaining 20%. There is no Paper 3; that component exists only at Higher Level. A formula booklet is supplied in the examinations and a graphing calculator is required for the course.

The structural point students miss is that the two papers test the same content under opposite conditions. A topic met once in class is examined twice, once where every step must be executed by hand and once where a display can carry the arithmetic. A student who has worked through DP1 with the calculator always available may know the course and still lose a large share of a paper worth two fifths of the grade, and the first clear evidence of that is usually a DP2 mock.

Which has a simple operational consequence. Paper 1 and Paper 2 should be prepared as separate disciplines from early in DP1, not merged into general revision in the final term. sections.heading: The gap from IGCSE to AA SL, subject by subject
paragraphs: Students arriving in AA SL from Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher tier are generally well prepared in algebra, graphs and trigonometry, and entirely unprepared for several things the course assumes by half term. The transition is not hard in principle. It is just front-loaded, and nobody warns families that the first eight weeks introduce four unfamiliar ideas simultaneously.

Radian measure is the first. A student who has worked exclusively in degrees for five years meets radians, the unit circle and exact trigonometric values in quick succession, and the resulting errors look like carelessness rather than a conceptual gap. Function notation is the second: composite and inverse functions are examined every year and are new to most IGCSE candidates. Calculus is the third and largest, because neither IGCSE route covers differentiation. Probability distributions are the fourth.

The table below maps each gap to what closes it and roughly how long that takes. The useful conclusion is that almost all of this can be dealt with before DP1 begins, in a short block over the summer, at a fraction of the cost of repairing it during DP2. That is the single clearest piece of advice on this page and it is the one families most often hear too late to use. The reason it works is sequencing rather than volume: calculus taught in October onto secure algebra and automatic radians is a normal topic, while the same calculus taught onto shaky foundations becomes two problems at once and the student stops being able to tell which one is failing.

sections.heading: Where Standard Level students actually lose marks
paragraphs: Standard Level losses are rarely about difficulty. They cluster around four habits, and all four are visible in a single marked paper. The first is calculator dependence, which shows up as a strong Paper 2 and a weak Paper 1 on the same content. The second is working in degrees when the question is in radians, or the reverse, which produces answers that are nearly right and earn nothing.

The third is ignoring the word hence. In IB mathematics, hence instructs a student to use the result of the previous part, and a student who starts a question again from scratch both runs out of time and risks losing the marks that depended on the connection. Hence or otherwise permits a fresh approach; hence does not. That single distinction is worth teaching explicitly in a session of its own.

The fourth is not writing down the calculator step on Paper 2. A numerical answer standing alone can lose the method marks behind it, because the marker cannot see what was solved. A student who writes the integral or the equation they entered before reading off the value keeps those marks even when the final number is wrong. None of these four requires new content. They require a habit installed and then rehearsed under timed conditions, which is why marked written work between sessions does more here than explanation during them. All four are also visible to a parent who looks at a returned script: a weak Paper 1 beside a strong Paper 2, an answer that is out by a factor involving pi, a question restarted from scratch after the word hence, and a bare number with no working above it.

sections.heading: The exploration criteria, mark by mark
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration carries 20% of the Standard Level grade and is marked out of 20 across five criteria. Almost no competing page in this market names a single one of them, which is strange, because a student who knows the mark allocation writes a different exploration from one working on an impression of what is wanted.

The allocation tells a student where to spend their effort. Use of mathematics carries the largest share, which means a topic that cannot sustain real mathematical development caps the grade however carefully it is written. Presentation and mathematical communication are each worth the same as one another and respond to simple discipline: a clear structure, defined notation, labelled graphs, consistent symbols. Personal engagement and reflection are the smaller criteria and the ones students most often miss entirely, because they require the student to say why they chose this and what they made of the result.

The table below sets out the five criteria with their marks and what each actually rewards. Confirm the current allocation with your school's IB coordinator, since the IB blocks automated checking and criteria can be revised between guides. The practical sequence is unchanged either way: choose a topic that can carry the mathematics, then write to the criteria, then act on feedback on your own draft. Reversing that order is what produces the exploration a student has worked hard on and still cannot push past the middle band, because the problem was settled at the topic stage and no amount of polishing reaches back to it.

sections.heading: What AA SL tutoring costs in Sharjah, in AED
paragraphs: Think in blocks rather than hours, because that is how Standard Level support is actually bought: a transition block before DP1, a run of weekly sessions, an exploration block, a run-up to the papers. A twelve-session block at the qualified subject tutor rate of AED 150 to 300 an hour is the most common purchase in this market, and the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates frame the same spend monthly at AED 600 to 1,200 for a weekly hour at that level.

The bands either side of it are worth knowing. Budget online tutoring is published from AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, and monthly estimates of AED 240 to 600. For Standard Level, unlike Higher Level, this band can genuinely work for some needs: a capable university student can supervise non-calculator practice. What it will not reliably do is give criterion-level feedback on an exploration. An IB specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and monthly estimates of AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more in an exam year.

Above that, in-home one-to-one visits across the UAE are quoted at AED 180 to 500 with travel included, and monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits are advertised, against around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes. Every figure here belongs to the provider named beside it; none is an IB Gram price. sections.heading: Ramadan, the Sharjah school calendar and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: Nobody competing for these searches writes about the UAE academic calendar, and it is one of the more useful things a family can plan around. School days shorten during Ramadan, concentration in the late afternoon drops, and the evening reorganises itself around Iftar. A tutoring schedule that ignores this produces sessions nobody is able to use.

Ramadan also moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so its position relative to the Diploma examination season changes from one cohort to the next. In some years it sits comfortably clear of the papers; in others it lands in the final revision window. That is worth checking against your school's published calendar at the start of DP2 rather than discovering in March, because it determines whether the heaviest revision block should sit before Ramadan or after it.

The practical adjustments are small and they work. Sessions move to post-Iftar slots or to late morning at weekends. Non-calculator drilling, which needs alertness, goes earlier in the day; reviewing marked work, which does not, goes later. Session length shortens and frequency holds, because consistency matters more than duration for algebraic fluency. Because lessons are delivered over live video, none of this requires renegotiating a tutor's drive across the emirate: the change takes one message and costs nothing. The same logic applies to the rest of the UAE academic year. Winter and spring breaks are the two windows where a student can get ahead of a topic rather than catch up with one, and families who book a short block into one of those breaks generally spend fewer hours overall than families who hold the same weekly slot through a term and then add sessions in April.

sections.heading: The honest case for taking Standard Level well
paragraphs: A persistent idea in Diploma option conversations is that Higher Level maths is always the stronger choice because it keeps more doors open. That is true for a narrow set of destinations and misleading for most students. Engineering, mathematics, physics and computing departments do frequently ask for an analysis-heavy Higher Level route, and families aiming there should check the programme's own published requirement rather than taking anybody's word for it. Outside that set, Standard Level with a strong grade is very often the better profile.

The arithmetic is straightforward. A 4 in AA HL and a 7 in AA SL are not equivalent signals, and the three Higher Level subjects a student takes should be the three where they will perform. A student who takes Higher Level maths and loses points there, and loses attention from two other Higher Levels in the process, has made a worse decision than one who took Standard Level and did it properly. The American University of Sharjah and the University of Sharjah both publish their own criteria and both sit in University City, a short drive from most of this emirate.

Two cautions belong here. Tutoring is not a requirement for university admission, school progression or anything else, whatever urgency a tutoring advertisement implies, and IB Gram claims no influence over an admissions decision. And no provider should push a student towards Higher Level to sell more hours. Where Standard Level is the right course, the useful purchase is the transition block before DP1 and a steady weekly hour, which is a smaller sale and a better outcome.

If the route looks wrong we say so and tell you to ask the Diploma coordinator for the switch deadline in writing. That conversation is free and it is sometimes worth more than a term of tutoring.

process.description: A marked non-calculator attempt separates a fluency problem from a content gap faster than any discussion. A mock grade shows neither. We read the working rather than the total, which usually identifies the first six sessions before anybody has been booked.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then a written plan

Afterwards you get a short written plan naming what is costing marks, which block is needed, and roughly how many sessions that is. The quote arrives attached to the plan rather than before it.

More criterion work if the draft is thin, more timed Paper 1 practice if the mock exposed calculator dependence. If the tutor is the wrong match for your child, we change the tutor rather than asking you to persist with it.

whyPoints.title: The route question asked first
whyPoints.description: AA SL, AA HL and AI SL suit different students, and a tutor who starts teaching without asking which one fits is selling hours rather than solving a problem. We ask, and where the answer suggests a switch we tell you to get the deadline from the Diploma coordinator in writing before the window closes.

A student who knows the allocation writes a different exploration, and topic choice stops being a matter of taste and becomes a question of whether the mathematics can be developed.

whyPoints.title: Paper 1 treated as its own discipline
whyPoints.description: Forty per cent of the grade is examined with no calculator, and calculator dependence is the most common hidden cause of a disappointing Standard Level result. We run non-calculator work weekly from the start rather than reviving it in the final term, which is the cheapest preventive measure available in the course.

Most pages competing for this search publish no rate at all. Our own number follows a free trial lesson, once the block is known.
