IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses and holds no approval from SPEA, MoHRE or the International Baccalaureate. Where no Standard Level specialist is free in your slot we say so and offer the nearest workable option rather than substituting someone unsuitable.

whyPoints.title: No pressure towards Higher Level
whyPoints.description: A 7 at Standard Level is a stronger profile than a 4 at Higher Level for most destinations, and we will say so even though the Higher Level course sells more hours. Where a family is aiming at engineering or mathematics, we tell them to check the programme's own published requirement rather than relying on a tutoring page.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP Math AA SL tutor cost in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Published market rates rather than ours: budget online tutoring from AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, an IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more, and an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 including travel. Monthly, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates put a weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Standard Level support is usually bought as a block rather than open-ended, and IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson once we know which block is needed.

faqs.question: Is Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level the right course if my child is not heading for engineering?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level deserves a look first. AA leans towards algebraic method and calculus; AI leans towards modelling, statistics and mathematics applied to real data with technology used throughout. For business, psychology, design and many social science destinations, AI is frequently the better fit and usually produces a higher grade for the same effort. The two are different courses rather than a ladder. Ask the Diploma coordinator what the school can timetable and ask your target universities which routes they accept, in writing.

faqs.question: Can my daughter move down from Higher Level to Standard Level maths, and when does that close?
faqs.answer: Schools allow movement between maths routes for a limited period in DP1, after which registration and the taught content make it impractical. In a small Sharjah cohort the real window can be shorter than general guidance suggests, because a timetable with a single Standard Level block may not absorb another student. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the actual cut-off date in writing during the first month of DP1, before anybody needs it. A move made in time is routine; a move attempted in DP2 usually is not.

faqs.question: Does Standard Level Analysis and Approaches include vectors or proof by induction?
faqs.answer: No. Vector geometry, formal proof including induction and contradiction, Maclaurin series, differential equations and complex numbers in polar form all sit at Higher Level only. Standard Level covers the same five topic areas, at less depth: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. That is roughly where the ninety-hour difference in recommended teaching time goes. Confirm the current content with your school's IB coordinator, since the IB blocks automated checking of its own pages and content can be revised between subject guides.

faqs.question: How many examination papers does a Standard Level maths student sit?
faqs.answer: Two. Paper 1 runs an hour and a half with no technology permitted and carries 40% of the grade. Paper 2 runs an hour and a half with a graphing calculator required and also carries 40%. The exploration carries the remaining 20%. Paper 3, which asks two extended investigations in an hour, is a Higher Level component and Standard Level students do not sit it. The practical implication is that Paper 1 and Paper 2 should be prepared separately, because they examine the same content under opposite conditions.

faqs.question: What are the five criteria the mathematics exploration is marked against?
faqs.answer: Presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, totalling 20 marks. Use of mathematics carries the largest allocation, which is why a topic that cannot sustain real mathematical development caps the grade however well it is written. Presentation and mathematical communication reward structure, defined notation and labelled graphs. Personal engagement and reflection are smaller and most often omitted entirely. Confirm the current allocation with your school's IB coordinator, since criteria can be revised between subject guides and the IB blocks automated checking of its own pages.

faqs.question: My son came from Cambridge 0580 Extended. What will he meet in AA SL that he has not seen?
faqs.answer: Four things, mostly in the first half of DP1. Radian measure with the unit circle and exact trigonometric values, after five years working only in degrees. Composite and inverse functions with formal function notation. Differentiation and integration, which neither IGCSE route covers at all. And the binomial and normal distributions. On top of those, Paper 1 bans the calculator for 40% of the grade, which is a bigger adjustment than it sounds for a student used to having one in most IGCSE papers. A short summer block closes most of this cheaply.

faqs.question: Is Analysis and Approaches SL harder than Applications and Interpretation SL?
faqs.answer: They are differently shaped rather than ranked. AA SL demands more algebraic manipulation and includes calculus at moderate depth, with a paper that bans technology. AI SL integrates technology throughout and leans on modelling and statistics, which some students find more demanding because the mathematics has to be extracted from a context before it can be done. A student strong in manipulation will usually score higher in AA; a student strong in interpretation will usually score higher in AI. Grade distributions vary by cohort and should not be used to decide this.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well with a calculator and badly without one?
faqs.answer: Because Paper 1 and Paper 2 examine the same content under opposite conditions, and the second one has been doing the work. Exact values with surds and in terms of pi, logarithm and index manipulation, differentiation by rule and sketching from reasoning are all skills the calculator has been substituting for. The gap is almost always fluency rather than understanding, and it responds to weekly non-calculator problem sets rather than to re-teaching. Started in DP1 it is a minor habit; discovered in a DP2 mock it is a term of work.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect Standard Level maths revision in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, late-afternoon concentration drops and the evening reorganises around Iftar, so sessions move to post-Iftar slots or to late morning at weekends. Ramadan also shifts roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so its position relative to the examination season differs between cohorts. Check your school's published calendar at the start of DP2 rather than in March, because it determines whether the heaviest revision block sits before Ramadan or after it. Shorten sessions and hold the frequency: consistency matters more than duration for algebra.

faqs.question: Do universities in Sharjah accept Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Entry requirements are set by each university and each department, they change, and no tutoring page should be your source. The American University of Sharjah and the University of Sharjah both sit in University City and both publish their own criteria. Ask the specific programme and get the answer in writing. Generally, engineering, mathematics, physics and computing departments most often ask for a Higher Level analysis route, while business, social science and design programmes more commonly accept Standard Level. Tutoring is not a requirement for admission to any programme.

faqs.question: Is a 7 at Standard Level better than a 4 at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: For most destinations, yes, and the two are certainly not equivalent signals. The three Higher Level subjects a student takes should be the three where they will perform, because a Higher Level grade earned at the cost of attention to two other Higher Levels is an expensive point. Where a programme explicitly requires Higher Level mathematics, that requirement governs and should be checked on the programme's own page. Outside those cases, taking Standard Level and doing it properly is usually the stronger profile, and it is the advice most tutoring providers avoid giving.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the exploration deadline should sessions start?
faqs.answer: Before the topic is chosen, which in practice means several months ahead of the school's internal deadline. Topic choice determines the ceiling, because the use of mathematics criterion carries the largest allocation and a topic that cannot sustain Standard Level mathematics cannot be rescued by later rewriting. Four to six sessions is a realistic block: criteria explained, topic viability tested, structure planned, then feedback on the student's own draft. Explorations started after the DP2 mocks are usually written in the gaps between other deadlines, which shows in the presentation and reflection criteria.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Standard Level maths for two siblings in the same Sharjah household?
faqs.answer: Yes, and families in Al Qasimia and Muwaileh often ask for exactly that, usually as two back-to-back one-to-one slots on the same evening rather than as a shared session. Teaching two students together rarely works past the first term, because Diploma students diverge quickly: one needs calculus and the other needs the exploration criteria. Two consecutive individual slots keeps the teaching individual while saving the household a second interruption, and the tutor already has the context from the earlier lesson.

faqs.question: What does a per-term block of Standard Level maths support usually cover?
faqs.answer: It depends which block. A transition block before DP1 is six to eight sessions on radians, function notation, logs and algebra by hand. A weekly block through DP1 follows the school's scheme with a marked problem set between sessions. An exploration block is four to six sessions on the criteria, topic viability and draft feedback. An exam run-up in DP2 is two sessions a week for around ten weeks on timed papers marked to the mark scheme. Pricing by block rather than by open-ended hour is how most Sharjah families keep this predictable.

intro.heading: How to know whether AI HL tutoring is working, in weeks rather than terms
paragraphs: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is the IB's modelling-heavy mathematics course. Technology is required in all three written papers, the content runs from eigenvalues and transition matrices through graph theory and network algorithms to hypothesis testing and coupled differential equations, and 20% of the grade sits in an exploration the student writes themselves. It is a demanding course and it is also one where tutoring can look busy while achieving nothing.

That is the problem this page addresses. Most families in Sharjah buy maths tutoring and then wait for a report card to tell them whether it worked, which means a decision made in October gets evaluated in March. By then two terms of fees have gone and the recoverable window has narrowed. The alternative is to agree in advance what evidence should exist and when, and to look at it rather than at a grade.

Evidence in this subject is concrete. A marked problem set with comments on the working rather than the answers. A timed section of a past paper marked against the mark scheme. A one-page written plan naming the two topics being targeted and why. A full past paper at week six with the losses broken down by topic, comparable with the one from week one. An exploration topic tested against the use of mathematics criterion before any drafting begins. Each of those is something you can hold and read without knowing what a Voronoi diagram is.

IB Gram delivers AI HL support as live one-to-one video lessons. IB Gram does not run home visits in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE, because home visits are a service offered only in India. For an evidence-led approach the online format helps rather than hinders: the shared whiteboard keeps the working visible, marked scripts are returned as files rather than carried in a bag, and the written record of what was taught in week three is still there in week nine when you want to check it.

Private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which the federal portal u.ae describes as regulating private education in the emirate, and which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The Diploma cohort here is small and many students commute into Dubai schools from Al Nahda and Al Majaz. What that means for an AI HL family is that specialists are scarce locally, which makes it more important, not less, to check that the one you have found is actually producing evidence. Scarcity is the condition under which families accept the least proof, because the alternative appears to be nothing, and that is exactly when a written list of expected artefacts is worth most.

One deliberate omission: no IB examination or results date appears anywhere on this page. The IB blocks automated checking of its own pages, so any session or results date you read on a tutoring site has not been confirmed at source. Confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before planning a revision schedule around it.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.programmesIntro: AI HL sits inside a programme structure that decides how much time a student actually has for it. The grid below covers the Diploma, the career-related alternative, the programme that feeds it and the qualification most students arrive from.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across two years with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Mathematics is compulsory and taken from one of four courses. Choosing Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is a deliberate decision rather than a default, since it is the least commonly timetabled of the four routes in many schools.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah the cohort is small enough that an AI Higher Level block may not exist at every school, and some students end up in Analysis and Approaches because that is what the timetable offered. Ask the Diploma coordinator which maths blocks are actually running before option forms are returned, not afterwards.

programmes.name: IB Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A framework combining Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and personal and professional skills. Where mathematics is taken as one of the Diploma courses within it, the assessment is identical to a full Diploma student's, including the exploration. The difference is the surrounding workload, which is shaped differently and usually leaves the internal assessment easier to schedule properly.
programmes.countryNote: The Career-related Programme is far less widespread in the UAE than the Diploma, so check directly with any school you are considering rather than assuming availability. For tutoring purposes the maths requirement is unchanged: the same three papers and the same exploration criteria apply.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five-year feeder, with mathematics assessed against four criteria rather than by examination. MYP's emphasis on investigation and real-world application is closer to Applications and Interpretation than to Analysis and Approaches, which makes it a natural feeder into this course. What MYP does not build is speed with technology under examination time, and that gap shows in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Students coming through MYP at a Sharjah continuum school often take to AI HL modelling comfortably and then lose marks on calculator discipline: a correct answer written down with no record of what was entered. That is a two-session habit fix and it is worth doing in the first term rather than the last.

programmes.name: IGCSE Mathematics
programmes.description: The commonest feeder from a British-curriculum school, usually Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson 4MA1 Higher tier. Both prepare a student well for the statistics and modelling side of AI HL and neither covers matrices, graph theory, hypothesis testing or calculus. The first year therefore introduces several genuinely unfamiliar branches of mathematics rather than deepening familiar ones.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run a British route to Year 11 before students move into a Diploma, sometimes across the border in Dubai. Where a student changes school and curriculum in the same September, a marked diagnostic in the first fortnight is the fastest way to find out what actually transferred.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.subjectsIntro: AI HL covers five topic areas, and a large part of what sits inside them appears in no other IB mathematics course. The grid below splits it into the parts a tutor works on separately, with where each is examined.

subjects.name: Matrices, determinants and inverses
subjects.description: Matrix algebra, determinants, inverses and matrix powers, used for solving systems and for geometric transformations. Procedurally regular once the notation settles, which makes it reliable marks. Students lose them by mis-ordering a product, since matrix multiplication does not commute and the error produces a plausible-looking wrong answer.

subjects.name: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors and transition matrices
subjects.description: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors, powers of matrices, and transition matrices used to model systems that evolve in steps towards a steady state. This appears in no other IB maths course. It is conceptually unfamiliar and highly examinable, and a student who has seen the geometric meaning of an eigenvector handles the algebra far better.

subjects.name: Graph theory and network algorithms
subjects.description: Adjacency matrices, walks and trees, minimum spanning trees by Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms, the Chinese postman problem and the travelling salesman problem with nearest-neighbour and lower-bound methods. Algorithmic rather than analytic, so marks come from executing a procedure cleanly and showing every step.

subjects.name: Voronoi diagrams and spatial reasoning
subjects.description: Constructing Voronoi diagrams, perpendicular bisectors, nearest-neighbour interpolation and the largest-empty-circle problem. Visual and quick to learn, and a common source of straightforward marks. Students lose them through imprecise construction rather than misunderstanding, which practice on squared axes fixes quickly.

subjects.name: Functions and model choice
subjects.description: Linear, exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric, logistic and piecewise models, with parameters estimated from data. The assessed skill is choosing a model and justifying the choice, not just fitting it. Students who reach for the model they saw last week, rather than reading the behaviour of the data, lose the justification marks every time.

subjects.name: Geometry, trigonometry and vectors
subjects.description: Three-dimensional geometry, trigonometry in context, and vectors applied to position, velocity and kinematics including scalar and vector products. Context-heavy and diagram-dependent: questions set on a real situation are lost by students who start calculating before drawing anything.

subjects.name: Regression and the coefficient of determination
subjects.description: Least-squares and non-linear regression, Spearman's rank correlation, and interpretation of the coefficient of determination. The marks sit in interpretation rather than computation, since the calculator does the fitting. Confusing correlation with causation in a written interpretation is the loss examiners see most often.

subjects.name: Hypothesis testing
subjects.description: Chi-squared tests for independence and goodness of fit, and t-tests, with hypotheses stated, a significance level chosen and a conclusion written in context. Highly structured, so it is efficient to secure. Students lose marks by concluding in statistical language without translating the result back into the situation it came from.

subjects.name: Calculus and differential equations
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration in applied contexts, numerical methods, differential equations solved with Euler's method, coupled systems and phase portraits. This is the heaviest HL-only block after matrices and frequently where DP2 students run out of taught time at school.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: An individual written investigation marked out of 20 across five criteria, with use of mathematics carrying the largest allocation. In AI the data-led topics available are an advantage and a trap: real data is easy to find and easy to describe without developing any Higher Level mathematics from it.

subjects.name: Calculator discipline across all three papers
subjects.description: Every AI paper allows technology, which means every paper rewards recording what was entered. A numerical answer standing alone can lose the method marks behind it. Writing the equation, integral or test being run before reading off the value is the single cheapest habit available in this course.

sections.heading: What progress in AI HL looks like, week by week
paragraphs: Agree the evidence before the first lesson, because afterwards every conversation becomes a judgement about effort rather than about output. The useful question to put to any tutor in this market is simple: what will I have in my hands at the end of week one, week three and week six, and what will each of those things tell me? A tutor with an answer has a plan. A tutor without one is selling hours.

The reason six weeks matters is that one marked paper is a single data point. A student can score badly because of a topic they had not yet been taught, or well because the paper happened to favour the two topics covered that fortnight. Two full papers marked the same way, several weeks apart, with the losses broken down by topic, is the first thing in this process that can honestly be called a baseline and a comparison.

The table below sets out the artefacts and what each proves. Note the final column, which is the honest half of the picture: a marked diagnostic in week one proves the tutor can diagnose, and proves nothing at all about whether the grade will move. Anybody offering certainty about an outcome at week one is describing a sales process rather than a teaching one. Keep the artefacts in one folder as they arrive. Three months in, that folder is the only record that can settle an argument about whether the arrangement is earning its cost, and it takes no effort to assemble if the pieces were produced as they went.

sections.heading: What exists in AI HL and in no other IB maths course
paragraphs: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is not a lighter version of anything. It contains whole branches of mathematics that appear in none of the other three IB maths courses, and that has a direct practical consequence: a tutor experienced in Analysis and Approaches may never have taught half of this syllabus. Checking which of these topics a prospective tutor has taught to examination is the single most useful screening question available.

The distinctive content falls into a few groups. Matrices, with determinants, inverses, powers, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and transition matrices modelling systems moving towards a steady state. Graph theory, with adjacency matrices, minimum spanning trees by Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms, the Chinese postman problem and the travelling salesman problem. Hypothesis testing, with chi-squared and t-tests. Differential equations solved numerically with Euler's method, including coupled systems and phase portraits. Voronoi diagrams and the spatial reasoning around them.

Much of this is algorithmic rather than analytic, which changes how it should be taught and marked. A network algorithm earns marks for being executed cleanly with every step shown, not for elegance. A hypothesis test earns marks for stating the hypotheses, choosing a significance level and writing a conclusion in the context of the original situation. These are procedures a student can be drilled on and then checked against, which fits an evidence-led approach well: the marked script shows immediately whether the procedure is intact. The table below pairs each distinctive topic with the loss it produces and with what a marked attempt reveals, which is the level of detail a weekly artefact should be giving you.

sections.heading: The three papers, and why none of them bans the calculator
paragraphs: AI HL is assessed through three written papers plus the exploration. Paper 1 runs two hours and carries 30% of the grade. Paper 2 runs two hours and carries 30%. Paper 3 runs one hour, asks two extended problem-solving questions and carries 20%. The exploration carries the remaining 20%. Unlike Analysis and Approaches, technology is required throughout: there is no non-calculator paper in this course.

That single difference reshapes what tutoring should target. In Analysis and Approaches the most common hidden loss is calculator dependence exposed by a technology-free paper. In Applications and Interpretation the equivalent loss is calculator opacity: a student who finds the right answer and writes only the answer, leaving the marker unable to see what was solved. The method marks behind that figure are then unavailable, and the student has no idea it happened until a marked script says so.

Which is why the artefact matters more here than the explanation. A student who has been told to record their calculator steps will agree that it is sensible and continue not doing it. A student whose marked script has three questions where a correct final answer scored partial marks changes the habit within a fortnight. Confirm current weightings and durations with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, since the IB blocks automated checking of its own pages and nothing here should be taken on a tutoring site's word. The structure itself is stable enough to plan around: three papers all permitting technology, and a fifth of the grade in an exploration written outside the examination hall.

sections.heading: Reading a marked script: what the working tells a parent
paragraphs: You do not need to understand eigenvectors to read a marked AI HL script usefully. What you are looking for is the shape of the losses, and four patterns are visible to anybody. The first is marks lost at the end of long questions rather than at the start, which usually means time rather than knowledge. The second is correct final answers with no working above them, which is the calculator-opacity problem and is the fastest thing in this course to fix.

The third pattern is losses concentrated in one or two topics with everything else intact. That is good news, because it is a teaching problem with a clear target, and the plan should name those topics explicitly by week four. The fourth is losses scattered evenly across every topic at a similar rate, which usually points at something general: examination technique, reading the question, or a student who has been keeping up with class work but never consolidating it.

The question to ask a tutor about a marked script is which of those four patterns they see, and what the next three sessions will do about it. A tutor who answers in terms of needing to work harder has not read the script. A tutor who says the losses sit in network algorithms and hypothesis-test conclusions, and that the next three sessions will drill both with a timed check in week three, has. That is the difference you are paying for, and it is audible in one conversation.

Losses in one or two topics are good news: a clear target exists

sections.heading: Paper 3: a modelling investigation, not a puzzle
paragraphs: Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level and it is unlike the other two papers in this course. One hour, two questions, each an extended investigation that opens accessibly and builds. In Applications and Interpretation those investigations are usually modelling scenarios: a situation is described, data or a structure is given, and the student has to choose an approach, carry it through and comment on what it means.

Two failures recur. The first is freezing at the opening, because a student trained on Papers 1 and 2 waits to recognise the question type and a Paper 3 scenario is designed not to be recognisable. The habit that fixes it is mechanical: write down what is given, write down what is asked, do the smallest case, look for the structure, then choose a method. The second failure is abandoning working after a dead end. Method marks run through long chains of reasoning here, so crossing out a wrong attempt discards marks that had already been earned.

Both are trainable, and both are trained by attempting full past questions under the real one-hour limit and then reading the marked script. Six to eight sessions is a realistic block. The evidence that it is working is specific and visible: the first attempt usually has a blank opening and an abandoned second question, and by the fourth attempt there is writing in both, including in the parts the student could not finish. That change appears on paper weeks before it appears in a grade.

sections.heading: The exploration draft cycle, and the line a tutor cannot cross
paragraphs: The exploration carries 20% of the AI HL grade and is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Use of mathematics carries the largest allocation, and in this course there is a specific trap attached to it. Real data is easy to find, and an exploration can describe a data set at length while developing almost no Higher Level mathematics from it. Topic choice therefore sets the ceiling.

There is also an integrity line, and in this market it is not hypothetical. One provider found in this research sells completed internal assessments outright. That is an academic malpractice trigger, and the consequence falls on the student whose name is on the submission rather than on the business that took the payment. A tutor teaches, explains the criteria, questions a plan and comments on a draft. A tutor does not produce text or perform the calculations that are submitted.

The table below sets out the draft cycle stage by stage, with what the student does, what a tutor may do and what a tutor may not. It is published here so that a parent can check the arrangement they are buying against it, including with us. The practical point is that this division of labour is also the one that scores better: an exploration carrying a tutor's phrasing reads unlike the rest of a student's work, and a teacher who has taught them for two years notices immediately.

sections.heading: What you can verify about cost yourself, in AED
paragraphs: Cost claims in this market are almost entirely unverifiable, which is odd given how checkable the underlying numbers are. Three of the six most visible providers researched publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars rather than the currency a Sharjah family actually transacts in. So rather than another rate card, here is each common claim alongside what you can ask to test it and what the published market says.

The figures themselves are not in dispute. Budget online tutoring is published from AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online is AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. An IB specialist is AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits across the UAE are quoted at AED 180 to 500 with travel included, and premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes.

Monthly, the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits and online packages around AED 799 a month for eight sessions. Every figure belongs to the provider named beside it and none is an IB Gram price. Our own number follows a free trial lesson, because the hours depend on which of Paper 3, the HL-only content or the exploration is the live problem.

sections.heading: SPEA, University City and where AI HL actually leads
paragraphs: Private education in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. The federal portal u.ae states that SPEA regulates private education in the emirate, and that Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is a wider remit than inspection alone. That coverage extends across the emirate including the Kalba and Khor Fakkan exclaves on the east coast. Almost no tutoring page competing for these searches names SPEA at all.

Private tutoring itself is regulated federally. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without the permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, any specific amount quoted at you is unverified.

On destinations, the honest position is that requirements are set by each university and department, they change, and no tutoring page should be the source. The American University of Sharjah and the University of Sharjah both sit in University City and both publish their own criteria. Generally, Applications and Interpretation is more commonly accepted for business, economics, psychology, design and data-facing programmes, while engineering, mathematics and physics departments more often specify an analysis route. Ask the programme directly and in writing. Tutoring is not a requirement for admission anywhere, and IB Gram claims no influence over any admissions decision.

sections.heading: What progress does not look like, and the claims to refuse
paragraphs: An evidence-led approach also means knowing which evidence is worthless, and this market supplies plenty of it. No tutor can guarantee a grade, a score, a 7 or a specific improvement, and anybody offering one is describing a marketing position rather than a teaching method. Treat a promised outcome as a reason to walk away rather than as reassurance, however confidently it is presented.

Three more claims deserve the same treatment. A star rating a provider has written about itself is not evidence; two of the pages researched for this project publish contradictory review figures on the same page, one of them alongside a student count the ratings could not support. A statistic without a sample size, a date and a method is not evidence either, so a figure such as ninety-six per cent satisfaction tells you nothing you can check. And a claim of approval, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education or the International Baccalaureate should be tested by asking for the permit or centre number, because these bodies license schools and training institutes rather than endorsing tutoring platforms. IB Gram holds none of them and says so.

What is left after all that is unglamorous and checkable. A marked script with comments on the working. Two comparable papers six weeks apart with the losses broken down by topic. A written plan naming the targets. An exploration topic tested against a criterion before a word is drafted. Those are small, dull, verifiable things, and they are what the difference between a 4 and a 6 in this course is actually made of.

process.title: Agree the evidence before the first lesson
process.description: Tell us the year, the school and which component is the live problem, and we will tell you what you should be holding at the end of week one, week three and week six. That list is the contract. If the artefacts do not appear, you have a concrete reason to change something rather than a feeling that it is not working.

process.title: Send one marked paper or problem set
process.description: A marked script shows the shape of the losses: at the end of long questions, or answers without working, or concentrated in one topic, or spread evenly. Each of those four patterns leads to a different first six sessions, and none of them is visible in a mock grade.

process.title: Free trial lesson, then a written plan
process.description: A full lesson at no cost with the matched tutor, with no card details taken to reserve it. Afterwards you get a one-page plan naming the two topics being targeted, the habit being changed and the check that will test it. The quote comes attached to the plan rather than before it exists.

process.title: Weekly sessions, with a marked artefact each week
process.description: Live one-to-one video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, chosen around the commute where one applies and moved to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan. Written work from each session is marked before the next by the teaching tutor, with comments on the working rather than a tick and a total.

process.title: Compare at week six, then re-plan
process.description: A second full paper marked the same way as the first, with the losses broken down by topic. That comparison is the first honest read on whether the arrangement is working. If it is not, we change the plan or the tutor rather than asking you to wait for a report card to confirm it.

whyPoints.title: Evidence agreed in advance
whyPoints.description: A named list of artefacts for week one, week three and week six, settled before the first lesson. Most tutoring is evaluated by a report card two terms later, which is far too late to change anything. Agreeing what should exist, and when, is free and it is the single most useful thing a parent can insist on.

whyPoints.title: The AI HL-only content actually taught
whyPoints.description: Eigenvalues, transition matrices, graph theory, network algorithms, hypothesis testing and Euler's method with coupled systems appear in no other IB maths course. A tutor trained on Analysis and Approaches may never have taught any of them. Our match is made on that content, and you are welcome to ask which topics a tutor has taken to examination.

whyPoints.title: Marking on the working, not the answer
whyPoints.description: Every AI paper allows technology, which makes recording the step entered a scored habit. Comments written on the working show whether a loss was method, interpretation or arithmetic. A tick and a total cannot distinguish those, and a student cannot change a habit they have not seen cost them marks.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 rehearsed, not mentioned
whyPoints.description: A fifth of the grade sits in one hour of extended modelling investigation. We run it as its own block with full past questions under the real time limit, because the skill being tested is entering an unfamiliar scenario. The progress is visible on paper: writing appears in the parts the student previously left blank.

whyPoints.title: The exploration boundary published
whyPoints.description: The draft cycle on this page sets out stage by stage what the student does, what a tutor may do and what a tutor may not. It is published so you can check any arrangement against it, ours included. Nothing is written or calculated for your child, which protects the certificate and scores better anyway.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: No guaranteed grade, no self-written star rating, no statistic without a sample size and a date, and no claim of approval from SPEA, MoHRE or the International Baccalaureate, since IB Gram holds none. Where no specialist is free in your slot we say so and offer the nearest workable option instead of filling the gap quietly.

faqs.question: How will I know within a month whether AI HL tutoring is working?
faqs.answer: Agree the artefacts before the first lesson. By the end of week one you should hold a marked diagnostic that says which of method, interpretation or calculator technique is failing. By week three, a timed section of a past paper marked to the mark scheme. By week four, a one-page plan naming the two topics being targeted. By week six, a second full paper marked the same way as the first with losses broken down by topic. That comparison is the first honest read available, and it arrives two terms before a report card would.

faqs.question: Which AI HL topics appear in no other IB mathematics course?
faqs.answer: Matrices with determinants, inverses, powers, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, and transition matrices for systems evolving towards a steady state. Graph theory with adjacency matrices, minimum spanning trees by Kruskal's and Prim's algorithms, the Chinese postman problem and the travelling salesman problem. Hypothesis testing with chi-squared and t-tests. Differential equations solved numerically with Euler's method, including coupled systems and phase portraits. Voronoi diagrams and the spatial reasoning around them. A tutor trained on Analysis and Approaches may never have taught any of these, so ask which they have taken to examination.

faqs.question: Does Applications and Interpretation have a paper without a calculator?
faqs.answer: No. Technology is required throughout all three AI papers, which is one of the clearest differences from Analysis and Approaches. That changes where marks are lost: instead of calculator dependence exposed by a technology-free paper, the recurring loss is calculator opacity, where a student finds the right answer and writes only the answer. The method marks behind it then cannot be awarded because the marker cannot see what was solved. Writing down the equation, integral or test being run before reading off the value is the cheapest habit available in this course.

faqs.question: How do I read a marked AI HL script if I do not understand the mathematics?
faqs.answer: Look for the shape of the losses rather than the content. Marks lost at the end of long questions usually mean time rather than knowledge. Correct final answers with no working above them are lost method marks and the quickest thing to fix. Losses concentrated in one or two topics are good news, because a clear target exists. Losses spread evenly across every topic point at technique: reading the question, examination pacing, or keeping up with class work without consolidating it. Then ask the tutor which pattern they see and what the next three sessions will do about it.

faqs.question: What makes Paper 3 in Applications and Interpretation different from Papers 1 and 2?
faqs.answer: It asks two extended investigations in one hour and carries 20% of the grade, and in this course those investigations are usually modelling scenarios rather than abstract puzzles. A situation is described, data or a structure is supplied, and the student chooses an approach, carries it through and comments on what the result means. The content can come from anywhere, so revising topics does not prepare it. Practising entry into an unfamiliar scenario does: write what is given, write what is asked, do the smallest case, then choose a method.

faqs.question: Why do students lose marks on network algorithms when they know the method?
faqs.answer: Because the marks are awarded for the procedure being visible, not for the final route being right. A student running Kruskal's algorithm in their head and writing down the spanning tree loses the steps that carried the credit. The same applies to the travelling salesman problem, where upper and lower bounds get confused and the written reasoning is what distinguishes them. Algorithmic topics reward clean, complete execution on paper, which is exactly the kind of thing a marked script exposes in one reading and a conversation about effort never will.

faqs.question: What is the trap with data-led explorations in Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Real data is easy to find and easy to describe at length without developing any Higher Level mathematics from it. The use of mathematics criterion carries the largest share of the twenty available marks, so an exploration that collects a data set, draws graphs and computes summary statistics will be capped regardless of how well it is written. Topic choice sets the ceiling. Test any idea against that criterion before drafting begins: ask what Higher Level mathematics the topic will force you to develop, and if the answer is vague, change the topic.

faqs.question: Exactly where does a tutor have to stop on my child's exploration?
faqs.answer: At feedback. A tutor may ask whether a topic can carry Higher Level mathematics, explain each of the five criteria, question a structure, point to gaps in reasoning, give written feedback against the criteria on a draft your child has written, and confirm later whether that feedback was addressed. A tutor may not hand over a topic with a method, supply the structure, rewrite paragraphs, correct the calculations or edit a draft to completion. One provider in this market sells completed internal assessments; the consequence of that falls on the student. IB Gram does not do it.

faqs.question: What should I ask to test a tutoring provider's cost claim in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Four questions. What is the AED figure per sixty minutes, in writing. What is the monthly cost of one session a week. Which AI HL-only topics has the tutor taught to examination. Is individual written work marked, and by the person teaching the lesson. Against those, the published market is: budget online AED 45 to 150, qualified subject tutor AED 150 to 300, IB specialist AED 200 to 450 or more, in-home AED 180 to 500 with travel. Monthly estimates run AED 240 to 600, AED 600 to 1,200 and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more by band.

faqs.question: Is a promised grade improvement ever a reasonable thing to accept?
faqs.answer: No tutor can guarantee a grade, a score or a specific improvement, and an offer of one is a reason to decline rather than reassurance. The same applies to a star rating a provider has written about itself, and to any statistic published without a sample size, a date and a method. Two of the pages researched for this project show contradictory review figures on the same page. What can honestly be offered is a method, an evidence trail and a willingness to change the plan or the tutor when the evidence says to.

faqs.question: How many AI HL sessions a week do students in Muwaileh usually take?
faqs.answer: Most start at one a week in DP1 and move to two in DP2, with a short additional slot appearing during the Paper 3 block and again while the exploration draft cycle runs. Families in Muwaileh can often hold an earlier weekday slot than those commuting back from Dubai schools, which matters because marked-paper work needs a student still alert. Consistency does more than volume here: a weekly slot that holds for two terms produces an evidence trail, while four sessions crammed into April produce only an opinion.

faqs.question: Do Sharjah universities accept Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Requirements are set by each university and each department, they change, and no tutoring page should be your source. The American University of Sharjah and the University of Sharjah both sit in University City and both publish their own criteria, so ask the specific programme and get the answer in writing. Generally, Applications and Interpretation is more commonly accepted for business, economics, psychology, design and data-facing programmes, while engineering, mathematics and physics departments more often specify an analysis route. Tutoring is not a requirement for admission to any programme.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in Khor Fakkan work with my child, or is the east coast a problem?
faqs.answer: For an online arrangement the east coast makes no difference at all, which is most of the argument for it here. Khor Fakkan and Kalba are regulated by SPEA like the rest of Sharjah but sit hours by road from any Diploma specialist, so an in-home arrangement for a course this specialised is not realistic. Lessons run over live video, marked scripts arrive as files rather than in a bag, and the evidence trail is identical to a family in Al Majaz. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: My son is in DP1 and his marks are inconsistent rather than low. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Usually that the losses are technique rather than content, which is the better of the two problems to have. Inconsistency across topics at a similar rate points at reading the question, examination pacing, or keeping up with class work without ever consolidating it. Inconsistency between papers on the same content points at calculator discipline. A marked diagnostic separates those two within a single session, and both respond faster than a genuine content gap would. DP1 is also much the better time to act, because the course content builds for two years.

faqs.question: What happens to the evidence trail during Ramadan and the exam term?
faqs.answer: It continues, with the timing changed. School days shorten during Ramadan and late-afternoon concentration drops, so sessions move to post-Iftar slots or to late morning at weekends, and because lessons run over live video that change takes one message. Timed papers get scheduled for weekend mornings rather than weekday evenings, since a full paper attempted when a student is tired produces misleading evidence. Through the exam term the artefacts shift from problem sets towards full marked papers with topic breakdowns, which is what the final weeks should be measured by.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.closingHeading: Agree the first six weeks of evidence
sharjah/ib-dp-math-ai-hl-tutor.closingBody: If your child is taking Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level in Sharjah, start by sending one marked script and asking a single question: what will I be holding at the end of week one, week three and week six, and what will each of those prove? Book a free trial lesson with an AI HL specialist and you will leave with that list in writing, along with a view of which of the four loss patterns the script shows. The AED bands above are the market, publisher by publisher. Lessons run live, one-to-one and online.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level for Sharjah Diploma students. Each works the same way: a marked diagnostic first, then weekly timed questions, then exploration comments against the published criteria. You see who is teaching before you commit.

intro.heading: Judge an AI SL tutor on what comes back marked, not on what is promised
paragraphs: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL is the DP maths course built around real data, modelling and a calculator. Two papers carry 80 per cent of the grade between them and the mathematical exploration carries the remaining 20 per cent. A Sharjah family looking for an IB DP Math AI SL tutor in Sharjah is usually reacting to one of three signals: a predicted grade that dropped a band, an exploration draft the supervisor sent back with a short note, or a mock paper where the arithmetic was right and the marks were not. None of those three is solved by more explaining. They are solved by looking at the script.

That is why this page is organised around evidence rather than reassurance. Every claim a tutoring page makes about progress should be checkable by you, on paper, within four weeks. A marked question set shows where method marks were awarded and where an answer earned nothing because the working jumped. A commented exploration draft shows which of the five criteria is actually holding the mark down, which is almost never the one a student assumes. A weekly session note shows whether the same topic keeps reappearing, which is the single most useful diagnostic a parent can hold.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For AI SL that constraint turns out to be an advantage rather than a compromise. The course is calculator-dependent in a way that AA is not, so a tutor who can share a screen, drive the same graphic display calculator emulator your child uses, and annotate a marked script live is doing something a tutor sitting at a kitchen table with a pen cannot do as cleanly. The marked work is saved, dated and sent, rather than left behind in a notebook.

Sharjah adds its own scheduling problem. A large number of families living in Al Nahda, Al Taawun and Al Majaz send children to schools across the Dubai border, and the return journey down Al Ittihad Road decides whether a four o'clock session is realistic or fictional. Families in Muwaileh, Al Zahia and University City have shorter runs but later activity schedules. Online slots can be set at 6.30pm or 8pm without a tutor's travel time being priced into the hour, and they can move during Ramadan without the week collapsing.

Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That matters for a maths tutor in a practical way: your child's internal assessment calendar, reporting windows and mock timings are set inside a school working to SPEA's approved framework, and tutoring evidence is only useful if it arrives before those windows rather than after them.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.programmesIntro: AI SL sits at the end of a long run through the IB continuum, and the habits that decide an AI SL mark are usually formed two programmes earlier. Here is how the earlier stages feed into it for a Sharjah student, and what the evidence looks like at each one.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP teaches mathematics inside units of inquiry rather than as a separate subject sequence, which means a child can arrive in Year 7 confident at reasoning and thin on written method. For an AI SL student eight years later, the residue shows up as working that is correct in the head and invisible on the page. Evidence at this stage is a portfolio and a teacher conference, not a mark.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah's IB continuum provision is small compared with Dubai's, so PYP families in Muwaileh and Al Zahia often choose between a continuum school and a British primary followed by a DP switch later. Either route works, but the second one makes the written-method gap more likely, and that gap is worth closing in Year 9 rather than in DP1.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is marked against four criteria — knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts — each out of eight. Criterion C and criterion D are the direct ancestors of the AI SL exploration, because both reward a student who explains a method and comments on whether the answer is reasonable. An MYP student who scores well on A and badly on C is a predictable AI SL problem.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run MYP to Year 11 and then move students into the Diploma, so your child may reach AI SL without ever having sat an external written paper under timed conditions. The first marked timed set a tutor sends back is often the first one a Sharjah MYP-route student has ever seen with method marks annotated.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: AI SL is one of two routes through DP mathematics, taken alongside five other subjects, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Paper 1 is short-response, Paper 2 is extended-response, and both are sat with a graphic display calculator and the formula booklet. The exploration is submitted to the school, marked internally against five criteria and moderated externally, which is why the supervisor's comments and a tutor's comments must point the same way.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah DP cohorts are small, which cuts both ways. A student gets more attention from a subject teacher than a Dubai cohort of ninety would allow, but there may be only one AI SL teacher in the building and no second opinion on an exploration topic. An outside reader who knows the criteria is doing the job a second department colleague would do elsewhere.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. A CP student taking AI SL as one of their DP courses faces the same two papers and the same exploration as a full Diploma candidate, but with a different workload shape around it and a different deadline map. The exploration still carries 20 per cent of the AI SL grade.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision across the UAE is thin and in Sharjah it is rarer still, so a CP student taking AI SL is often the only one in the year group doing exactly that combination. Scheduling support around a career-related placement is easier online than around a tutor's drive time between Al Qasimia and Al Suyoh.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.subjectsIntro: Most families who ask about AI SL are also weighing one or two other DP subjects in the same conversation, usually because the timetable forces a choice. These are the courses that sit closest to AI SL in a Sharjah DP block, and what each actually assesses.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Built on modelling, statistics and technology. SL sits two 90-minute papers worth 40 per cent each; HL adds a Paper 3 of two extended problem-solving questions. Marks are lost on interpretation sentences, on conclusions to statistical tests stated without a comparison, and on rounding that drifts from three significant figures.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic and proof-led route. SL covers calculus and trigonometry in more analytical depth than AI SL and expects exact answers in surd and radian form. Students who switch from AA SL to AI SL mid-course usually gain on statistics and lose nothing on functions, but need the modelling language rebuilt from scratch.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Shares the uncertainty and graph-linearisation work with AI SL statistics, which is why one tutor can often serve both. Paper 1 is multiple choice plus data analysis, Paper 2 is extended response. The scientific investigation carries 20 per cent and is assessed on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Calculation-heavy in a way that rewards AI SL habits: significant figures, propagated uncertainty and unit discipline carry real marks. Organic mechanisms and energetics are where most Sharjah students lose ground, and the data-analysis half of Paper 1 is the part that moves fastest with practice on marked questions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The statistics overlap with AI SL is larger than students expect. Standard deviation, error bars, the t-test and chi-squared all appear in biology data questions, so a student taking AI SL and Biology together is learning the same tests twice and should be made to notice it.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: HL economics includes quantitative questions on elasticities, costs and national income accounting that sit squarely inside AI SL number and algebra. The three internal assessment commentaries are marked on diagrams, terminology and evaluation rather than on arithmetic, which surprises students who chose it for the maths.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The quantitative toolkit — break-even, investment appraisal, ratio analysis — is AI SL number and algebra under different names. Marks are lost on the evaluation command terms rather than the calculations, so the tutoring need is usually structure and judgement, not method.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a replication of a simple experimental study with a statistical test, inferential reasoning and a written report. Students taking AI SL alongside psychology can reuse their understanding of significance and sampling, provided they keep the two write-up conventions apart.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Shares the algorithmic thinking and the modelling cycle with AI SL, and the internal assessment is a solution developed for a real client. Students who can reason about complexity and iteration tend to find the AI SL calculus and sequences topics straightforward.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Mathematics is a common knowledge-question route in TOK and a common Extended Essay subject. An AI SL student writing a maths Extended Essay is handling two independent pieces of mathematical writing in the same year, with different word limits and different supervisors, and the two calendars need to be mapped side by side.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a Sharjah family lives decides what time a session can start and how much slack there is in the week. These notes are about logistics rather than scenery, because logistics is what decides whether a weekly slot survives to March.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Dense apartment blocks around Khalid Lagoon with a short run to the Al Taawun and Al Mamzar crossings. Families with children at Dubai schools are often not home before six, so AI SL slots here tend to settle at 6.30pm or later.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: Sits directly on the Dubai border next to Al Qusais, with the heaviest cross-border school traffic in the emirate. Evening slots work; a 4pm slot almost never survives a term. Weekend morning sessions are popular here for exploration work.

regions.name: Al Taawun
regions.note: Tower living beside Al Mamzar with the same Dubai commute as Al Nahda and slightly more parking friction. Students here often fit a session between arriving home and an evening activity, which argues for a fixed 60-minute slot rather than a flexible 90.

regions.name: Al Khan
regions.note: Coastal and central, close to Al Khan lagoon and the Sharjah Aquarium, with several Indian-curriculum and British schools within ten minutes. Shorter school runs mean a 5pm AI SL session is realistic, which is useful in the weeks before a mock.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: Inland and growing fast, next to University City and Al Zahia. Commutes are short but after-school clubs run late at the newer schools, so families here often split the week into one taught session and one shorter marking review.

regions.name: Al Zahia
regions.note: Masterplanned villa community beside City Centre Al Zahia with a young DP cohort and a short run to Muwaileh schools. A 5.30pm slot is usually safe, and the household is normally quiet enough for a 90-minute Paper 2 practice under timed conditions.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: Sharjah's academic cluster around the University of Sharjah and the American University of Sharjah. Many DP students here have a parent on campus, which tends to mean homework supervision is strong and the gap is exam technique rather than content.

regions.name: Al Qasimia
regions.note: Older, central and well served by schools, with a short commute and heavy evening traffic around Al Wahda Street. Early-evening slots work, and the proximity of several schools means a shared tutor timetable across siblings is straightforward.

schoolClusters.city: Al Majaz, Al Khan and Al Taawun
schoolClusters.note: The older central and coastal districts, where a large share of students attend Indian-curriculum and British schools and a significant minority cross into Dubai daily. DP students from this cluster usually come to AI SL from an IGCSE or CBSE background rather than from MYP, which changes what the first marked diagnostic needs to test.

DP students here are more likely to have come through MYP, so the written-method and timed-paper gaps are the ones that show up first on a marked AI SL question set.

schoolClusters.note: The commuting belt. Students living here may attend a Sharjah school, a Dubai school, or a Sharjah school with half their friends in Dubai, and the resulting calendar clash is the main reason a weekly slot gets rescheduled. Fixed evening slots hold better than afternoon ones.

sharjah/ib-dp-math-ai-sl-tutor.modesIntro: Three shapes of support cover almost every AI SL request we receive from Sharjah. All are delivered online and one-to-one over live video; the difference is what the hour is spent on and what comes back marked.

modes.title: Weekly taught session with marked work returned
modes.description: The default for a student in DP1 or early DP2. One 60- or 90-minute session a week, built around a short timed question set set in advance and marked before the lesson, so the hour is spent on the two or three things the marking found rather than on a tour of the topic. The marked script and a written note are sent after every session.
bullets: Timed questions set between sessions and marked with method marks shown
A running record of which syllabus topic each lost mark belongs to
A short written note after each lesson naming what changed

modes.title: Exploration supervision alongside the school's own
modes.description: A short block of sessions timed to the school's internal exploration deadlines. The tutor reads your child's own draft, comments against criteria A to E, and asks the questions a moderator would ask. The tutor does not supply a topic, supply data or add mathematics to the document; the work submitted must be the student's own, and the school's supervisor remains the person who signs the authenticity declaration.

modes.title: Pre-mock and pre-session intensive
modes.description: A compressed block in the weeks before a mock or the May session: two or three sessions a week, each built on a full paper sat under timed conditions and marked against the published mark scheme. Useful where the content is largely known and the loss is in timing, rounding, notation or calculator fluency rather than in understanding.
bullets: Full Paper 1 and Paper 2 attempts under timed conditions
Marks reconciled against the mark scheme line by line

sections.heading: What an AI SL tutor in Sharjah should hand back in the first month
paragraphs: An IB DP Math AI SL tutor in Sharjah should produce four pieces of evidence inside four weeks. A timed question set, sat under exam conditions and returned marked with method marks shown. A one-page written diagnosis naming the two syllabus topics costing the most marks and the error type behind each. Comments on your child's own exploration draft, keyed to criteria A to E rather than to general writing advice. And a short note after each session saying what was worked on and what moved. If none of that exists by week four, there is nothing to judge the tutoring on.

Most families arrive with a school report instead. A report gives a predicted grade on the 1 to 7 scale, a brief comment and sometimes an effort grade. What it almost never gives is the distribution of lost marks across the five AI SL topics, which is the only thing that tells you where an hour a week should go. A student predicted a 4 might be losing everything in statistics and nothing in functions, or losing two marks in every topic through rounding. Those two students need completely different terms, and only the marked scripts distinguish them.

The second reason to insist on marked work is that it makes progress arguable. A student who drops eleven marks on a timed set in week one and six marks on a comparable set in week eight has moved, and you can see on which questions. A student whose marked sets show the same interpretation error in weeks one, four and eight has not moved, however well the lessons felt. That is an uncomfortable thing for a tutor to put on paper every week, and it is exactly why it is worth insisting on.

Keep the evidence in one place. Families who hold a dated folder of marked sets, draft comments and session notes are the ones who can walk into a parents' evening and ask a specific question. Families who hold only a feeling about whether things are improving tend to change tutor at the wrong moment, usually in February, when continuity matters more than anything else.

sections.heading: The Applications and Interpretation SL syllabus, by hours and by paper
paragraphs: AI SL is 150 taught hours: 120 on the five content topics and 30 on the toolkit and the exploration. The distribution is the single most useful fact about the course and the one students most often have not been told. Statistics and probability is the largest topic at 36 hours, which is almost a third of the content time. Functions follows at 31 hours, then calculus at 19, geometry and trigonometry at 18, and number and algebra at 16. A revision plan that gives equal time to all five is already misallocated.

Both papers are 90 minutes and each carries 40 per cent of the grade. Paper 1 is a sequence of shorter questions covering the whole syllabus; Paper 2 is a smaller number of extended questions that run across topics. There is no non-calculator paper in AI SL, which is a structural difference from AA that changes how practice should be organised. A graphic display calculator is assumed throughout, and a student who can run a chi-squared test from a frequency table in twenty seconds has time to think about the interpretation sentence that carries the mark.

The exploration carries the remaining 20 per cent. It is marked by the school against five published criteria and moderated by the IB, which means the mark your child sees on the draft is not necessarily the mark that reaches the final grade. That is worth understanding early, because it reframes what a tutor's comments are for: not to raise the school's internal mark, but to make the document defensible to a moderator who has never met the student.
The table below maps each topic to the hours the course allows it, what AI SL actually asks of it, and how far the calculator does the work. It is the planning document we build a term around.

sections.heading: Where AI SL marks actually go missing on a marked script
paragraphs: Marked AI SL scripts fail in a small number of repeatable ways, and almost none of them are failures of understanding. The largest single category is the missing interpretation sentence. A student runs the regression, writes down the gradient, and stops. The mark was for saying what the gradient means in the context of the data, in a sentence, with units. A tutor can fix that in two sessions once the marked evidence shows it is happening, and cannot fix it at all while the only evidence is a grade.

The second category is statistical conclusions stated without the comparison that justifies them. A chi-squared value is calculated correctly and the conclusion is written as a bare assertion, with no reference to the critical value or the significance level, and no statement of what the null hypothesis was. The third is rounding drift: an intermediate value rounded early, carried forward, and an answer that is accurate to two significant figures where three were wanted. Over a full Paper 1 that pattern can cost more than any single topic.

Then there is calculator notation. Writing down what appeared on the screen is not working, and a question that asks for a method will not accept a screenshot in place of one. Students who have been taught to trust the device sometimes present no reasoning at all on a six-mark question. The reverse problem exists too, in students who migrated from AA SL and insist on doing by hand what AI SL expects the technology to do, running out of time in the process.

The fix for all four is the same, and it is dull: timed questions, marked honestly, logged by error type, repeated until the log stops showing the same line. The log is the deliverable. A student who can name their own three recurring errors before an exam is in a different position from one who has been told to be careful.
bullets: No interpretation sentence after a calculated value — the most common single loss

sections.heading: The mathematical exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, and the marks are not evenly spread. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six marks on its own. Criteria A and B carry four each, and criteria C and D carry three each. A student polishing presentation while criterion E sits at two out of six is spending effort in the wrong place, and only a criterion-keyed comment sheet makes that visible.

The most common structural mistake is length. The guidance points to a concise document of roughly twelve to twenty pages, and students routinely produce twice that by moving raw data, calculator output and repeated calculations into the body. The remedy is an appendix and a stated aim in the first paragraph. The second most common is criterion C, personal engagement, which cannot be rescued by adding a sentence about why the topic is interesting. It is earned by independent choices visible in the work: data the student collected, a method the student selected, a direction the student changed after a result.

Criterion D, reflection, is the one Sharjah students most often lose cheaply. Reflection written as a single paragraph at the end reads as a conclusion, not as reflection. Reflection distributed through the document — after a result that did not behave as expected, after a model that fitted badly, after a decision to change approach — is what the criterion describes. A tutor's job here is to ask the question that produces the reflection, not to supply the paragraph.
The table below sets out what each criterion rewards, what it is worth, and what we most often see costing marks on a Sharjah student's first draft.

sections.heading: What twelve weeks of evidence looks like in practice
paragraphs: A term of AI SL support has a shape, and it is worth knowing the shape so you can tell whether a term has gone as it should. Weeks one and two are diagnostic. A timed question set covering all five topics, marked with method marks shown, plus a read of whatever exploration material exists. The output is a written diagnosis: two priority topics, three recurring error types, and a calendar working backwards from the school's internal deadlines.

Weeks three to six are the topic block. Each week one priority topic, one timed set on it, marked before the session and worked through during it. The session note records which error types reappeared. By week six the log either shows an error type dropping out or it does not, and if it does not, the approach changes rather than the hours increasing. This is the part of a term where a parent should be able to open the folder and see the same three error labels getting rarer.

Weeks seven to nine move to the exploration while the topic work continues at a lower intensity. The tutor reads the student's own draft, comments against the criteria, and asks the questions that generate criterion C and criterion D material. Weeks ten to twelve are mixed papers: full Paper 1 and Paper 2 attempts under timed conditions, marked line by line against the mark scheme, with the error log reviewed at the end of every session rather than at the end of the block.

Twelve weeks is not a guarantee of anything and no honest tutor will tell you otherwise. What it is, is a long enough period to know whether the marked evidence is moving. If it is, the same shape repeats with harder material. If it is not, the diagnosis was wrong and should be redone from a fresh timed set rather than defended.

sections.heading: What Sharjah families pay for DP mathematics support, and what comes back
paragraphs: Published rates for tutoring in the UAE are scarce, and most pages ranking for these searches quote none at all or quote in US dollars. The figures below are market rates in AED collected from providers' own published pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. They are not IB Gram's prices; they are what the market around a Sharjah family looks like, so you can judge a quote against something.

Two things drive an AED figure more than anything else. The first is whether travel is in the hour. An in-home visit priced at AED 300 includes a drive from somewhere, and in the Sharjah-to-Dubai corridor that drive can be 45 minutes each way at six in the evening. The second is scarcity. A Sharjah family wanting AI SL specifically, rather than general DP maths, is drawing from a smaller pool than a family in Dubai Marina, and scarcity shows up in the rate before it shows up in the availability.

The column worth reading closely is not the rate; it is what comes back marked. A tutor at AED 150 who returns no marked work and a tutor at AED 280 who returns a marked set and a criterion-keyed comment sheet every week are not selling the same product, and comparing them on price per hour hides that completely. Ask any prospective tutor what you will physically hold at the end of four weeks, and compare the answers rather than the rates.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages. The honest reason is that the figure depends on level, subject scarcity and session length, and a number printed here would be wrong for most readers.
