sections.heading: The Sharjah calendar: Ramadan, the commute and when work actually lands
paragraphs: A Psychology plan that ignores the Sharjah calendar loses weeks it then rebuys at the worst time of year. Diploma candidates here sit the May session, and the twelve weeks before it collide in most recent years with Ramadan and a shortened school day. A 5pm slot that worked in November does not work in Ramadan, and families who do not re-plan simply stop for a month. The functional answer is post-Iftar sessions at around 9pm or 9.30pm Gulf Standard Time, which exist as an option only because delivery is over video.

Outside Ramadan the binding constraint is the commute. A Sharjah student at a Dubai school is not realistically available before 7pm on a weekday, and students in Al Taawun, Al Majaz and Al Nahda are the most affected. Saturday mornings are the most dependable recurring slot in this emirate and are where the long jobs belong: IA data analysis, which needs an unbroken stretch, and timed Paper 3 questions, which need marking time afterwards. Local-campus students in Muwaileh have genuine midweek afternoon availability and should use it.

Counting backwards is the part nobody in this market teaches, so here it is. The IA deadline is internal and set by the school, which puts it earlier than parents expect and usually before the mock window. Mocks are the real diagnostic. The eight to ten weeks after mocks are the only period in which Paper 3 technique and option-essay structure genuinely move. sections.heading: Who regulates what in Sharjah, and who regulates your tutor
paragraphs: Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate, and which along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That reach beyond inspection is unusual and worth knowing. Dubai's private schools answer to KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there; and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Private tutors are regulated separately, by MoHRE. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The official route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, via the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services, with a stated two-working-day completion time and no listed fee. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted at you is somebody's guess.

Two boundaries follow. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; nobody should use a regulator's name as a credential without producing the number. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct barring the same thing - press-reported, so verify against current ADEK material. IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or endorsement from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and says so on every page.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or group for Psychology in this emirate
paragraphs: The in-home market in Sharjah is real and the question deserves a straight answer rather than a sales line. In-home one-to-one across the UAE is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and in-home monthly packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions appear on provider pages in this market. What that premium pays for is a person in the room and the time it took them to get there. In Muwaileh, where consecutive sessions in one community are possible, the overhead is modest. On the east coast it is prohibitive, and on the Dubai-border commute at 6pm it is unpredictable in a way price cannot fix.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and every UAE page on this site says the same. Sharjah Psychology lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor each week. The argument is subject-specific rather than general: what a Psychology student needs is somebody who has marked Paper 3 and can justify a Wilcoxon over a Mann-Whitney in two sentences, and the chance that such a person lives near any particular Sharjah address is close to nil. Video removes the map from the matching problem entirely.

Format also changes what a session can hold. A shared screen carries the unseen stimulus, the mark scheme and the student's annotated answer at the same time. A timed Paper 3 answer can be photographed, submitted and returned marked before the next session. Statistics work is easier over a shared spreadsheet than over a kitchen table. Tuition-centre group classes stay the cheapest option per hour in this market and the worst fit for Psychology specifically, because the option, the level and the IA topic differ student by student even inside one school.

sections.heading: Getting started, including what happens if no specialist is free
paragraphs: The honest version of the matching process has a failure case in it, and no competitor page in this market discloses one. Psychology at Higher Level with a specific option and Paper 3 experience is a narrow requirement. Most weeks it is available within a couple of days. Occasionally, in the pre-session window when every Gulf Diploma candidate wants the same four evening slots, the right specialist is not free at the time a Sharjah family needs. When that happens we say so rather than substituting a generalist and hoping.

The alternatives we offer in that case are stated up front: a different slot with the right specialist, including a post-Iftar or weekend-morning time; a shorter targeted block on the component that moves most while you wait; or a tutor based outside the UAE working in Gulf Standard Time, which for this subject changes nothing material because delivery was always over video. What we will not do is put a general studies tutor on an HL Paper 3 brief, because that is how a family pays specialist money for hours that do not move a mark.

Everything before that is simple. Tell us the level, the option the school teaches, and the component you are worried about. Send a recent marked essay or an IA draft if one exists. Take the free first lesson and use it as a diagnostic: by the end you should have a named weakness, a session count and a slot that survives a Sharjah school run. Then review against marked work every few weeks rather than against how the sessions felt, and change the tutor rather than adding hours if the marked work is not moving.

faqs.question: What does an IB DP Psychology tutor charge per hour in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Market rates for an IB specialist working online in this market run roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour, and a premium named tutor is published at AED 650 by one provider. A qualified subject tutor without Diploma component depth sits nearer AED 150 to 300, and budget general tutors run AED 45 to 150. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500. Our rate depends on the tutor, level, option and component, and the first lesson is free.

faqs.question: Which Psychology option does my child need a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Whichever one their school teaches, and that is not a rhetorical answer. The four options are abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, health psychology and the psychology of human relationships. Standard Level students answer on one, Higher Level on two, and the school chooses. Check the option headings in the student's own folder rather than a prospectus, because a tutor teaching the wrong option produces a student who is better at psychology and no better at their exam. In small Sharjah cohorts this mismatch often goes unnoticed until a mock paper comes back in term two.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 in IB Psychology and why do HL students need it taught separately?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is Higher Level only and is worth 20 per cent of the grade. The student reads an unseen stimulus describing a piece of research and answers three short-answer questions about how the research was done: the sampling method and what it implies, ethical considerations, the credibility of the findings, researcher and participant bias, and whether results generalise or transfer. Almost no content knowledge is involved. It has a repeating answer shape, which makes it highly teachable, and it is taught last in most schools, which makes it the component most often missing from a revision plan.

faqs.question: How long is the Psychology internal assessment and how is it marked?
faqs.answer: It is a report on a replication of a simple experimental study, written in 1,800 to 2,200 words and marked out of 22 across four criteria. Criterion A, introduction, carries 6 marks; criterion B, exploration, carries 4; criterion C, analysis, carries 6; and criterion D, evaluation, carries 6. It is 25 per cent of the Standard Level grade and 20 per cent at Higher Level. Most marks are lost in criterion C, to a mean reported without a measure of dispersion and an inferential test chosen without justification.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Psychology IA without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, inside a clear boundary. A tutor can explain each criterion, interrogate a weak hypothesis, teach how to choose between a Mann-Whitney U, a Wilcoxon, a chi-square and a t-test, and give criterion-letter feedback on a draft the student wrote from their own data. A tutor must never run the analysis, supply sentences or return a rewritten version. One operator in this market sells completed internal assessments; under IB academic-honesty rules the malpractice finding lands on the student and affects the whole Diploma, not one grade.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Psychology tutor to our home in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Sharjah lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor each week. The in-home market does exist and is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel. For Psychology specifically the trade is poor: the constraint is finding somebody who has marked the HL research-methods paper and taught your child's exact option, and that person is unlikely to live within driving distance of any particular Sharjah address.

faqs.question: My child can describe studies but keeps scoring badly on essays. What fixes that?
faqs.answer: The problem is almost certainly critical thinking rather than content, and more studies will not fix it. Paper 1 Section B and the option paper pay for evidence weighed against itself: methodology, sample, cultural limits, whether the finding replicates, what it does not show. The intervention is eight to twelve sessions of structured essay work on paragraphs that carry a claim, a study and a limitation, with every essay marked and returned annotated. Students usually see movement in the second or third marked essay, not the first.

faqs.question: How many short-answer questions are in Paper 1 and how long should each take?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 Section A is three short-answer questions, one on each of the biological, cognitive and sociocultural approaches, followed by Section B, which is one essay chosen from three. The practical problem is almost never knowledge; it is that students write essay-length answers to short-answer questions, run out of time and lose Section B marks they could have earned. Timing drills are four to six sessions of work, which makes them the cheapest high-yield intervention in the subject at any of the market rates on this page.

faqs.question: What ethics rules apply to the Psychology IA experiment?
faqs.answer: The IB's ethical guidelines require informed consent, a clear right to withdraw, debriefing after participation, anonymity in reporting, and protection from harm or undue stress, with certain participant groups and procedures ruled out entirely. The consent script and debriefing materials belong in the appendices. The breaches we see are mundane: an experiment run on classmates with no written consent, a debrief written after the data was collected, or anonymity defeated by naming a class. Every one is fixable at the design stage and only fixable afterwards by collecting the data again.

faqs.question: Can Psychology sessions work around Ramadan and a Dubai school run from Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should be planned that way rather than cancelled week by week. During Ramadan, post-Iftar slots around 9pm or 9.30pm Gulf Standard Time hold far better than late afternoon, and video delivery is what makes that time workable at all. Outside Ramadan, students at Dubai schools living in Al Taawun, Al Majaz or Al Nahda are rarely free before 7pm, so the weekday slot settles at 7.45pm. Saturday mornings take the long jobs: IA data analysis and timed Paper 3 answers that need marking afterwards.

faqs.question: Is Psychology an easy IB subject to take at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: It reads as approachable and marks as demanding, which is why it catches families out. There is no mathematics in the written papers and the vocabulary is familiar, so students choose it expecting a lighter load. Then the grade turns out to rest on criticising research rather than recalling it, on a second option at Higher Level, on a whole paper about methodology, and on a statistics report. Higher Level Psychology is a real HL subject with four components and a 20 per cent research-methods paper that does not exist at Standard Level.

Eligible applicants include teachers at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's smart app, website or e-services, under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time. faqs.answer: Only where the option and the level match exactly, and ideally where both students are in the same class so the internal deadlines align. Small-group rates in this market sit well below one-to-one per student, so a pairing is the clearest route to a lower cost per family. sharjah/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here read Theory of Knowledge drafts for Sharjah Diploma students: prescribed-title essays, exhibition commentaries and the object choices underneath them. Matching is by the task in front of your child and by the areas of knowledge their essay will actually use, not by a general interest in philosophy.

intro.heading: What you can read for yourself, and what you have to take on trust
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge is the subject where parents have the least idea whether anything is working. There is no textbook to check, no past paper score to compare, no weekly test. A student can talk fluently about knowledge for six months and submit an essay that scores in the bottom band, and nothing before the result will have told you. That is the problem this page is about: not what TOK is, but what evidence a family can actually hold in their hands while the course is running.

The good news is that TOK produces more readable evidence than almost any other part of the Diploma, because both assessed tasks are written at home over weeks. The essay runs to a maximum of 1,600 words on one of the prescribed titles released by the IB for the session, and it is marked externally against a single assessment instrument - one holistic judgement out of ten, not a tally of sub-scores. The exhibition asks for three objects, each linked to one of the published knowledge-and-knowing prompts, with a commentary of up to 950 words; it is marked by the school and moderated by the IB, also out of ten. Two-thirds of the TOK grade comes from the essay and one-third from the exhibition.

Both of those exist as drafts long before they exist as submissions. A draft is evidence. It can be read in September and read again in November and compared. If the September draft asserted things and the November draft argues them, something has changed and you can see it on the page. If the November draft is the September draft with better sentences, nothing has changed and the sentences are hiding it. This is why we return marked work from every session rather than a progress rating, and why the first thing we ask a Sharjah family for is whatever draft already exists, however rough.

The stakes are specific rather than vague. TOK is graded A to E and combines with the Extended Essay grade to contribute up to three points to the diploma total, and a grade E in either is a failing condition for the diploma. So a student sitting at a D in TOK is not losing a decoration; they are one grade away from a condition that can cost the whole qualification. That changes how urgently a weak draft should be treated, and it is the part most families have never been told plainly.

Sharjah shapes the practical side. SPEA, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, regulates private education in the emirate, while a large share of families living in Al Nahda, Al Taawun and Al Majaz send children into Dubai schools and come back across the border in the evening peak. TOK is usually timetabled in thin slices - one period a week in many schools, sometimes less - so the internal deadlines arrive without much lesson time behind them. A plan that puts a draft deadline in the same fortnight as the school's mock examinations will not be met, and the fix is to know both calendars before anything is promised.

sharjah/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.programmesIntro: Theory of Knowledge has no equivalent anywhere else in a student's schooling, which is why it so often arrives as a shock. The stages below are described by what they do and do not prepare a student for, because that mismatch is the thing a first session usually has to repair.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: TOK is compulsory for every Diploma candidate and runs across both years. The syllabus is built from the core theme knowledge and the knower, two optional themes chosen from five, and five areas of knowledge: history, the human sciences, the natural sciences, mathematics and the arts. The exhibition is usually completed in DP1 or early DP2 and the essay in DP2, so the two tasks sit in different years and get planned as though they were unrelated, which they are not.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah Diploma cohorts are small, so TOK is often taught by a teacher whose main subject is something else entirely, and the exhibition and essay deadlines are set by the school rather than by the IB. Two Sharjah schools three kilometres apart can therefore run internal TOK deadlines two months apart, which is why no generic timeline is any use here.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Personal Project in MYP 5 is the nearest ancestor of the exhibition: an independent piece with a process journal and a written report. Students who took it seriously arrive able to document their own thinking, which is most of what the exhibition commentary asks for. MYP also teaches interdisciplinary units, which is where the idea of knowledge differing between disciplines first appears, usually without being named.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Sharjah student arrives through MYP. Many come through IGCSE or an Indian board, where nothing resembles the Personal Project at all, and those students need the documenting habit built from scratch in DP1 rather than assumed.

programmes.name: The two years before TOK
programmes.ageRange: Ages 14-16 - Years 10-11 - IGCSE, CBSE or American middle years
programmes.description: IGCSE, CBSE and American-curriculum courses reward well-organised recall of established material. None of them asks a student whether a discipline's methods are reliable, or who decides what counts as evidence in it. That is not a criticism of those courses; it is a straightforward explanation of why a student with a row of grade 8s can write a TOK draft that scores in the lowest band.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah has a large Indian and British-curriculum school population, so most TOK students in the emirate arrive from exactly these routes. The first two months of DP1 are therefore spent on a habit change, and the students who are told that explicitly handle it better than the ones left to work it out.

programmes.name: TOK and the Extended Essay together
programmes.description: The two core components share a points matrix, so the grades combine rather than stand alone. They also share one skill - holding a claim steady while evidence is tested against it - and they compete for the same weeks of a student's DP2. Planning them in the same conversation usually produces a better outcome in both than treating each as a separate crisis when its deadline arrives.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah schools where the Extended Essay supervisor is allocated by availability rather than by subject, the TOK teacher and the Extended Essay supervisor may be the same overstretched person. A family who knows both internal deadlines in September can at least stop the two from landing in the same fortnight.

sharjah/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.subjectsIntro: TOK draws its examples from the subjects a student is already taking, and the quality of those examples is most of the difference between a C and an A. The notes below say what each subject contributes to an essay or an exhibition, which is also how we match a tutor to a student.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Two tasks, ten marks each, one externally assessed and one internally assessed and moderated. Most lost marks come from the essay drifting off the exact wording of the prescribed title, or from an exhibition object that is a category rather than a specific thing.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words of independent research, graded A to E and combined with TOK in the points matrix. Students usually find that the research question discipline learned here is exactly what rescues a drifting TOK essay, and the two tasks reinforce one another when sequenced deliberately.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The richest source of knowledge questions a student already owns: selection of sources, the role of hindsight, competing narratives of the same event. A History student who cannot find TOK examples usually has not realised that their Paper 2 essays are already arguing about method.

subjects.name: Global Politics
subjects.description: Supplies the optional theme knowledge and politics with concrete material, from contested statistics to the framing of international reporting. Useful for the exhibition, where a politically specific object tends to produce a sharper commentary than an abstract one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The natural sciences area of knowledge becomes usable once a student can describe how a claim is actually established - replication, controls, peer review, the handling of anomalous data. Students who have run a real scientific investigation have the examples; they just have not labelled them.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Good for the human sciences, especially around models that are useful rather than true. A student who has applied a framework and watched it fail against a real company has a TOK example about the limits of models that nobody else in the class will have.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The natural home of the knowledge and technology optional theme: algorithmic bias, what a dataset leaves out, whether a machine can be said to know anything. Specific and current, which the assessment instrument rewards far more than general observations.

subjects.name: Visual Arts
subjects.description: The arts as an area of knowledge is the one most students handle worst, because they default to taste. An arts student can usually explain instead how meaning is made and judged within a practice, which is the version that earns marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Mathematics gives TOK its clearest case of certainty inside a system, through proof and axioms. Students who have met proof by induction or contradiction have the material for the strongest paragraph in a typical essay, and almost never think to use it.

sharjah/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.regionsIntro: Lessons are online, so where a family lives does not limit which tutor reads the drafts. It does decide which evenings are usable and how much quiet a student has for an exhibition recording or a draft review. The notes below deal with that rather than with geography.

regions.name: Al Taawun
regions.note: High-rise living along the Sharjah-Dubai boundary, with a large share of students at Dubai schools. Draft reviews here work best as fortnightly ninety-minute slots at the weekend, since weekday evenings are eaten by the return journey.

regions.name: Al Qasimia
regions.note: Older established neighbourhoods feeding the Sharjah city schools, with short school runs and usable 5pm slots. Most TOK work for this group happens midweek, and parents here more often ask to see the session notes themselves.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: Academic households and a cluster of schools within a few minutes' drive. Students here often have access to university libraries through family, which is useful for the essay's examples and occasionally a temptation towards sources far above the word limit.

regions.name: Al Suyoh and Al Rahmaniya
regions.note: Newer villa communities further inland, where school journeys are longer in both directions. Evening slots from 6.30pm are standard, and we tend to schedule exhibition work here in school holidays when there is daylight to photograph objects.

regions.name: Tilal City
regions.note: A newer development with families spread across several school systems, so TOK internal deadlines in one household rarely match the next. Each plan here is built from that school's own dates rather than from a district pattern.

regions.name: Sharjah Garden City
regions.note: Villa living towards the Al Dhaid road with longer commutes and fewer nearby tutors of any kind. For a thinly taught subject like TOK this is where online delivery changes what is available rather than merely what is convenient.

regions.name: Al Nahda
regions.note: The densest Dubai-border district, where students frequently leave home before 6.30am and return after 4pm. Shorter, more frequent draft checks work better here than long sessions, because the reading can be done in the car and the talking kept to forty-five minutes.

regions.name: Khor Fakkan
regions.note: On the east coast, roughly two hours from Sharjah city, under SPEA like the rest of the emirate. There is effectively no local market for a TOK specialist, so a family here is choosing between online support and the school's own provision.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah city and Muwaileh campuses running the Diploma
schoolClusters.note: The campuses where a TOK cohort exists at all. Internal deadlines, the number of TOK periods a week and whether the exhibition runs in DP1 or DP2 all differ between them, so the first session is spent establishing what this school actually requires and when.
schools: International School of Creative Science, Muwaileh

schoolClusters.note: Families living in the emirate but schooling across the boundary, which puts the child under KHDA's school rules while the household runs on a two-emirate commute. For these students the binding constraint on TOK work is the evening road rather than the syllabus.

sharjah/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways Sharjah families buy TOK hours. Each one is defined by what it hands back, because a subject with no tests needs a different proof of work: a marked draft, a set of object decisions, or a written read-through before submission.

modes.title: Weekly session with one marked draft returned
modes.description: Sixty minutes a week during the drafting months. The student submits whatever they have forty-eight hours before the session, it comes back annotated against the published assessment instrument, and the session is spent on the two or three comments that matter most. The written trail accumulates and can be read in order at any point.

modes.title: Object selection and commentary workshop
modes.description: A short block of two to four sessions aimed entirely at the exhibition: choosing the knowledge-and-knowing prompt, finding three specific objects that genuinely connect to it, and getting the 950-word commentary to say something about each one. Most of the mark is decided by the object choices, so this is where the hours go.

modes.description: One session on a near-final essay or commentary, with written comments returned. No teaching, no restructuring, no rewriting - a diagnostic read that names what an external examiner is likely to penalise and leaves the decisions with the student. Families who have had support from the school often want only this.

sections.heading: What an evidence-led Theory of Knowledge plan puts in front of you in the first month
paragraphs: In the first four weeks a family should receive four things, and they should all be readable by someone who has never studied TOK. A baseline comment on whatever draft or notes already exist, written against the assessment instrument rather than as encouragement. A one-page statement of which of the two tasks is nearest and what its internal deadline is. A dated list of what the student will produce in each of the next six sessions. And the marked version of whatever they produced in session one.

That last item is the one that gets skipped, and it is the one that matters. A tutor who talks well for an hour a week and hands nothing back is unverifiable. A tutor who returns an annotated draft every week has given you an audit trail: you can put the first and fourth drafts side by side and see whether the argument got stronger or only longer. For a subject with no test scores, that comparison is the only honest measure available before the result arrives.

What a baseline should name is specific. Whether the student is asserting or arguing. Whether the examples are doing work or decorating. Whether the essay is answering the prescribed title as written or a paraphrase of it that is easier to write about. Whether the two areas of knowledge are genuinely compared or simply described in turn. Each of those is a different repair with a different timescale, and lumping them together as "needs to go deeper" is how a term gets wasted.

We also say in the first month if the problem is not one a tutor should be paid to fix. Sometimes a student has not understood the task at all and needs twenty minutes with their own TOK teacher. Sometimes the draft is fine and the student is anxious. Telling a family that is better business than selling them a term.
bullets: A baseline comment on existing work, in assessment-instrument language
The nearest internal deadline, in writing, from the school's own calendar
A dated list of what each of the next six sessions will produce
An annotated draft back from session one, not a verbal summary

sections.heading: Two tasks, two marks out of ten, two different markers
paragraphs: The whole TOK grade comes from two submissions and nothing else. The essay is written on one of the prescribed titles the IB releases for each examination session, runs to a maximum of 1,600 words, and is assessed externally against a single global-impression instrument that produces one mark out of ten. The exhibition consists of three objects and a commentary of up to 950 words linking each object to one of the published knowledge-and-knowing prompts; it is marked by the school out of ten and moderated by the IB. The essay carries two-thirds of the grade and the exhibition one-third.

Two consequences follow from the marking arrangements and both are worth knowing early. Because the essay is marked holistically rather than criterion by criterion, there is no partial credit to collect by covering more ground - a wide essay that never settles scores below a narrow one that argues. And because the exhibition is marked internally first, a school's generosity or severity is a real variable, which moderation adjusts but does not erase. Families whose children are in schools with small cohorts sometimes see exhibition marks move at moderation, and it is better to expect that than to be surprised.

The prescribed title must be used exactly as published. Students may not alter the wording, and the most common single failure in a TOK essay is quietly rewriting the title into something more comfortable in the opening paragraph and then answering that instead. We check for this on every draft, by putting the published title and the student's thesis next to each other and asking whether the second answers the first.

Word limits are hard limits in practice: material beyond them is not read, so a 2,000-word essay is a 1,600-word essay with its conclusion thrown away. Confirm the limits, the number of prescribed titles and the exact submission mechanics against the current TOK guide your child's school is working from, since the core is revised between cohorts.

sections.heading: The points at stake: how the TOK grade and the Extended Essay combine
paragraphs: TOK is not graded in isolation. Its letter grade is read against the Extended Essay letter grade in a published matrix that awards between zero and three points towards the diploma total, and a grade E in either component is a failing condition for the diploma regardless of what the rest of the transcript looks like. That is the sentence most families have never had put to them directly, and it changes the priority a weak TOK draft deserves.

Read across the matrix below and the planning logic appears. A student holding a B in the Extended Essay gains a point by moving TOK from C to B, and gains nothing by moving TOK from B to A. A student holding a C in the Extended Essay gains a point by moving TOK from D to C, and the same again from C to B. For a family deciding whether to spend hours on TOK or on the Extended Essay, the matrix tells you which of the two is currently cheaper to improve, and the answer is often not the one the student is more worried about.

The failing condition is the floor under all of this. An E in TOK will stop a diploma that is otherwise comfortably passed, so a student whose exhibition came back at the bottom of the range has a different problem from a student chasing a third point. We treat those two cases completely differently: the first is triage on the nearest submission, the second is a considered choice about where the remaining weeks go.

Point matrices are published in the diploma handbook and have been revised before. Check the current version with your child's Diploma coordinator before making a decision that depends on a particular cell, and treat the table below as the shape of the rule rather than as the rule itself.

sections.heading: Reading a marked Theory of Knowledge draft: the five things to look for
paragraphs: A parent can learn to read a TOK draft usefully in about ten minutes, and it is worth doing, because it lets you judge the tutoring rather than trusting it. Five checks cover most of what the assessment instrument rewards, and none of them requires knowing the subject.

First, the title test. Put the published prescribed title beside the student's thesis sentence. If the thesis answers a slightly different and easier question, the essay is already capped however well it is written. Second, the assertion test. Pick any paragraph and ask what evidence supports its central claim. If the answer is "it says so again later", the paragraph is assertion. Third, the example test. Examples should be specific enough to be checked - a named study, a named historical dispute, a named work - and each one should be doing a job in the argument rather than illustrating a general point about the world.

Fourth, the areas-of-knowledge test. A strong essay compares how two areas of knowledge handle the same problem; a weak one describes each in turn and leaves the comparison to the reader. If the draft could be cut in half and each half still made sense alone, there is no comparison in it. Fifth, the counterclaim test. Look for a point where the essay takes the opposing view seriously and then explains why it does not prevail. A draft with no such moment reads as a position paper, and the instrument rewards discussion.

Those five checks also tell you what a session should be about. Different failures need different weeks: a title problem is a one-session fix, an assertion habit is a six-week fix, and a missing counterclaim is somewhere in between. A marked draft that names which of the five is the live problem is worth more than an hour of discussion that names none of them.

sections.heading: The exhibition: three real objects, one prompt, 950 words
paragraphs: The exhibition is the task where the marks are mostly decided before any writing happens, because weak objects cannot be rescued by good prose. The student selects one of the published knowledge-and-knowing prompts, then three specific objects, and writes up to 950 words explaining how each object illustrates the prompt in a real-world context. Ten marks, internally assessed, externally moderated.

The word "specific" is where most of the damage is done. An object has to be a particular thing with a particular history - this photograph, taken on this date; this family's hand-written recipe card; this piece of surveying equipment from this project - and not a category such as "social media" or "maps". Categories produce commentary that could have been written about anything, and the moderator sees a hundred of them a season. Objects with a real, checkable context give the student something to argue from in two hundred words, which is all each object gets.

The order of decisions matters too. Students who pick three objects they like and then hunt for a prompt that fits usually end up stretching all three. Choosing the prompt first narrows the search in a way that makes the commentary easier to write, and lets a tutor ask the only question that counts about each candidate object: what does this let you argue that the other two do not? An object that fails that question should be replaced in week one rather than defended in week six.

Everything about the exhibition belongs to the student. The objects are theirs to choose, the connections theirs to make, the commentary theirs to write. A tutor's job is to keep asking what each object is for until the answers get sharper, and then to mark the draft honestly against the prompt.

sections.heading: A twelve-week ledger: what should have changed, and by when
paragraphs: Evidence only means something against an expectation, so we agree one in writing at the start. The table below is the shape of a twelve-week essay block for a student starting from a weak or absent draft. The dates are set from the school's own internal deadline rather than from an IB date, because the school's deadline is the one that binds and it differs by campus across Sharjah.

Two features of this ledger are deliberate. The thesis is fixed early and then left alone, because students who keep reopening the central claim never get to the argument. And the word count comes down rather than up in the final weeks: a draft at 1,900 words cut to 1,580 is almost always better than a draft that grew to 1,600, since cutting forces a judgement about what is load-bearing.

If a milestone is missed, that is information rather than a failure. A student who cannot produce a counterclaim paragraph in week six has a diagnosable problem, and the honest response is to change what the sessions are doing, not to move the milestone and hope. We report a missed milestone in the session note on the day it is missed, which is the difference between a plan and a hope.

The same ledger logic applies to the exhibition in a shorter form: prompt in week one, three candidate objects in week two, two hundred words on each by week four, full commentary by week six, cut and referenced by week seven. Both ledgers get built backwards from whatever date the school has actually set.

sections.heading: Keeping the evidence trail across a Sharjah school week
paragraphs: A ledger survives contact with reality only if it was built around the actual week. In Sharjah that week contains a few fixed things. SPEA regulates private education in the emirate, and for families whose children cross into Dubai schools the daily reality is a commute through the border crossings at both peaks. Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies run alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools under the federal regulations, taking hours that the Diploma timetable does not control. TOK itself is often timetabled thinly, so the internal deadlines arrive with little lesson time behind them.

Practically, that means draft deadlines go into the gaps rather than onto the peaks. The fortnight containing school mock examinations is a bad fortnight to expect a counterclaim paragraph. Ramadan changes the whole evening: most of our Sharjah families move to post-iftar slots, and TOK suits that period better than most subjects because a draft discussion is less punishing at 9pm than a timed maths paper. The long summer is when exhibition objects actually get found and photographed, because there is time and daylight.

Delivery is online for every UAE family and that is stated plainly rather than buried. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is something we run only in India. For Sharjah students, sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, drafts are shared and annotated on screen, and the written trail is the product. For a subject taught thinly in small cohorts, this is also the only realistic way to reach someone who reads TOK drafts regularly rather than someone who teaches another subject and covers TOK on a Tuesday.

One more scheduling point specific to the core: the Extended Essay and TOK deadlines are usually set by the same school and often within weeks of one another. Ask for both dates in the first term of DP2, put them on one page, and plan the TOK ledger around the Extended Essay rather than in competition with it.

sections.heading: What Theory of Knowledge support costs around Sharjah
paragraphs: Price this by the deliverable, not by the term, because TOK is a subject with two finite jobs rather than a syllabus to be covered. A single diagnostic read of a near-final essay is one hour. An exhibition block is two to four. A full twelve-week essay ledger is twelve. Multiply by whichever market band you intend to book and the budget resolves itself in one line of arithmetic, which is more than most providers in this market will give you.

Taking the cheapest band first: budget online tuition and university-student tutors publish from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online publish AED 150 to AED 300, Unitors showing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. IB and IGCSE specialists sit at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase published at AED 270. In-home one-to-one visits with travel included are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500, Bestimate's Dubai table at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Premium named or examiner-level provision reaches AED 500 to 650 and beyond, BartyED at AED 650. Monthly packages advertised include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those figures come from other providers' own pages, read in October 2026. They are not an IB Gram price list, and we quote only after a free trial lesson has produced a diagnosis, because the number of hours a student needs is the thing that actually determines the bill. The bands are still useful: they tell you that a twelve-session essay ledger with a specialist is a four-figure decision, and that the single read-through is not.

For context on where tutoring sits in a UAE education budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For Sharjah families with children at Dubai schools, that is the large number held steady; the TOK decision is the small, targetable one.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do to a draft, and the line running through the middle of it
paragraphs: Both TOK submissions are produced at home over weeks, which makes this the part of the Diploma where support is most easily mistaken for substitution. The boundary is set by the IB's academic-honesty rules and it is not negotiable: the essay and the commentary must be the student's own work, and a diploma can be withheld where that is not the case.

So we write down what happens to a draft. A tutor may read it, mark it against the published assessment instrument, ask what evidence supports a claim, point out where the thesis has drifted from the prescribed title, explain what a counterclaim is for, flag that an exhibition object is a category rather than a thing, and say that a paragraph does not work. A tutor may not write the TOK essay or any section of it, may not supply a thesis for the student to adopt, may not rewrite the student's sentences into their own prose, and may not choose the exhibition objects. No tutor should offer to draft the commentary either.

The honest version is also the one that scores. The essay is marked as a single global judgement about whether a discussion is sustained and genuinely linked to areas of knowledge, and a student who has had their own argument questioned until it holds produces exactly that. A student carrying an adult's paragraph produces an essay that changes voice halfway down page two, which an experienced examiner reads as a warning rather than as quality.

Finally, a word about what to avoid buying. There are providers in this market advertising completed internal assessments and finished essays at a stated price. That is an academic-integrity breach rather than a service, and for a core component carrying a failing condition it puts the entire diploma at risk. If a page offers to produce your child's assessed work, the right move is to leave it.
bullets: The thesis, the objects, the sentences and the decisions stay the student's
A tutor reads, marks, questions and explains - in writing, so it can be checked

process.title: Send whatever draft exists, however rough
process.description: Notes, a half paragraph, a rejected thesis, the prescribed title with nothing under it - all of it is more useful than a description of the problem. We read it before the trial lesson so that the hour can be spent working rather than gathering background.

process.title: Send the school's two internal dates
process.description: The exhibition deadline and the essay deadline as your child's own school has set them. These differ between Sharjah campuses by weeks, sometimes months, and every plan we build is counted backwards from them rather than from a generic calendar.

process.title: A free trial lesson that produces a baseline
process.description: Sixty minutes with the tutor who would read the drafts, spent on the existing work and the title. You receive a written baseline afterwards naming which of the five draft failures is live and how many weeks the repair usually takes.

process.title: Agree the ledger in writing
process.description: A dated list of what the student will produce each week up to the school's deadline, with the word-count curve and the milestone that matters most marked on it. Nothing in the plan depends on our judgement being taken on trust.

process.title: Report against the ledger, not around it
process.description: Each session note says what was produced, what was marked and whether the week's milestone was met. If two consecutive milestones are missed we change the approach or the tutor, and we say so rather than quietly extending the timeline.

whyPoints.title: The marked draft is the product
whyPoints.description: Every session returns annotated work and a dated note. A family can read the sequence in order and judge whether the argument strengthened, which is the only evidence available in a subject with no tests and no past papers.

whyPoints.title: Core specialists rather than general subject tutors
whyPoints.description: TOK drafts are read by tutors who read TOK drafts regularly. In small Sharjah cohorts the subject is often covered by a teacher whose specialism is elsewhere, and a reader who sees dozens of these essays a season notices different things.

whyPoints.title: The matrix explained before the hours are sold
whyPoints.description: We show a family where their child sits in the TOK and Extended Essay points matrix, including the failing condition, before recommending anything. Sometimes that conversation ends with us saying the Extended Essay is the cheaper point to buy.

whyPoints.title: Built around the school's own deadlines
whyPoints.description: Plans start from the internal dates your child's school has set, not from an IB session date. Those internal dates vary between Sharjah campuses, and the commute, the mandatory subjects and Ramadan all go into the calendar before the sessions do.

whyPoints.title: A written honesty boundary
whyPoints.description: What a tutor will and will not do with a TOK draft is agreed in writing before the first draft arrives. We will not produce assessed work, choose the objects or supply a thesis, and we say so on the page rather than only in a contract.

whyPoints.title: Sourced figures and no invented numbers
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is attributed to the provider that published it, with the month it was read. We publish no statistic about our own students, because we would then owe you the sample size, the date and the method.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether Theory of Knowledge tutoring is actually working, when there are no test scores?
faqs.answer: By comparing drafts. Keep every version with its date, and read the first and the fourth side by side against two questions: does the thesis still answer the published prescribed title, and do the central claims now have evidence that is not a restatement? If the later draft argues where the earlier one asserted, the work is landing. If it is the same content in better sentences, it is not. A tutor who returns annotated drafts makes this check possible; one who only talks for an hour a week leaves you nothing to judge.

faqs.question: What exactly is submitted for Theory of Knowledge, and how is each part marked?
faqs.answer: Two things. An essay of up to 1,600 words on one of the prescribed titles the IB releases for the session, marked externally out of ten as a single holistic judgement. And an exhibition: three specific objects with a commentary of up to 950 words linking them to one published knowledge-and-knowing prompt, marked by the school out of ten and moderated by the IB. The essay carries two-thirds of the TOK grade and the exhibition one-third, and the overall grade is reported as a letter from A to E. Confirm the limits against your cohort's TOK guide.

faqs.question: Can a weak Theory of Knowledge grade genuinely cost my son the whole diploma?
faqs.answer: A grade E in TOK is a failing condition for the diploma, so yes - a student who passes everything else can still be refused the qualification on that basis. Short of an E, TOK combines with the Extended Essay grade in a published matrix worth between zero and three points towards the total. That is why we treat a bottom-band exhibition mark as triage rather than as a disappointment, and why the first conversation with a family is about where the child currently sits in that matrix.

faqs.question: My daughter's exhibition commentary came back far lower than she expected. What usually causes that?
faqs.answer: Object choice, in most cases. The commentary is capped by what the three objects allow her to argue, and the commonest problem is objects that are categories rather than things: social media rather than one dated post, maps rather than one specific map with a history. A category produces two hundred words that could have been written about anything. The repair is to replace the weakest object, test each remaining one by asking what it lets her argue that the others do not, and rewrite from there. It is usually two or three sessions of work, not a term.

faqs.question: How many drafts should a Theory of Knowledge essay go through before submission?
faqs.answer: Four substantial ones is a reasonable expectation across twelve weeks, plus a final read-through. A thesis-and-two-paragraphs draft, a full-length draft that is over the word limit, a cut version, and a final polished version. The number matters less than the sequence: the thesis should be fixed early and left alone, and the word count should come down at the end rather than up. A student still arguing with their own central claim in week ten will submit something unfinished however many versions exist.

faqs.question: Why does my son's essay score badly when his teacher says his ideas are interesting?
faqs.answer: Interesting ideas and a sustained discussion are different things, and the assessment instrument rewards the second. The usual pattern is an essay that raises four promising thoughts and develops none of them, or one that describes two areas of knowledge in turn without ever comparing how they handle the same problem. Both read as intelligent and both sit in the middle bands. The repair is narrowing: fewer claims, each carried further, with one genuine counterclaim taken seriously. It is a structural change rather than a content change, and six weeks of marked drafting usually shifts it.

faqs.question: Can my child change the wording of the prescribed title to make it easier to answer?
faqs.answer: No. The prescribed titles are published by the IB for each session and must be used exactly as written. The most common silent failure in a TOK essay is a student rewriting the title into something more comfortable in the opening paragraph and then answering their own version for 1,600 words. We check this on every draft by putting the published title and the student's thesis next to each other and asking whether the second genuinely answers the first. If it does not, that is a single session's work to fix and well worth doing early.

faqs.question: Which areas of knowledge should my daughter use in her essay?
faqs.answer: The ones where she already has specific examples, which usually means the ones she studies. A History student owns arguments about source selection and hindsight; a Biology student owns replication, controls and anomalous data; a Mathematics student owns proof and certainty within a system. Choosing an area of knowledge she finds intellectually attractive but has no material in produces general observations, which the instrument marks low. The best first session on an essay is often an inventory of what she already knows well enough to argue from.

faqs.question: What does a Theory of Knowledge session note actually contain?
faqs.answer: Four things: what the student submitted, what was marked and how, which milestone from the agreed ledger was due this week, and whether it was met. Nothing about effort or enthusiasm. A note saying the counterclaim paragraph was due and did not arrive is more useful than a note saying the session went well, because it lets a parent ask the next question. The notes accumulate into a record that can be read end to end, which is the point of writing them in that form.

faqs.question: How much does Theory of Knowledge support cost around Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Price it by the job. Published market rates put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200, and IB specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. A single diagnostic read is one hour; an exhibition block is two to four; a full twelve-week essay ledger is twelve. Those are other providers' published figures, read in October 2026, not ours. We quote after a free trial lesson, because the number of hours is what sets the bill.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Theory of Knowledge tutor to our home in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Sharjah sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with drafts shared and annotated on screen and written notes after every session. For this component that is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise: TOK is thinly timetabled in small cohorts, and the people who read these drafts week in and week out are not necessarily living within driving distance of your district.

faqs.question: We live in Al Taawun and both children are at Dubai schools. When can a draft review realistically happen?
faqs.answer: Weekend blocks work better than weekday evenings for this group. The return journey through the border crossings at the evening peak routinely pushes a 4pm plan to nearly 6pm, and a draft review needs a student who can still think. We tend to run ninety minutes at the weekend plus a short midweek check rather than two tired weekday sessions. Because everything is online there is no travel at either end, which is most of the reason a later or weekend slot is workable at all.

faqs.question: Our son is already in the last term of DP2. Is there any point buying TOK help now?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which submissions are still open. If the exhibition has been marked and the essay is near final, one diagnostic read is usually the right purchase and twelve sessions are not. If the essay has not been drafted, the final term is late but workable, and the plan has to be ruthless: fix the thesis in week one, accept fewer examples carried further, and cut rather than add in the last fortnight. We tell families which of those two cases they are in after reading the work, not before.

faqs.question: Do Theory of Knowledge sessions continue during Ramadan in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the timing moved. Most of our Sharjah families switch to post-iftar slots during Ramadan, and this component sits in that period better than most: discussing a draft at 9pm is far less punishing than sitting a timed paper. We shorten sessions and reduce the volume of writing expected in those weeks rather than pausing, because a four-week gap in the middle of an essay ledger costs more than it saves. The plan is agreed in advance so the milestones move with the schedule.

faqs.question: What happens if no Theory of Knowledge specialist is free in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting a general subject tutor and hoping. The core components are read by a smaller group than the main subjects, and at peak drafting season the evening slots in Gulf Standard Time fill. In that case we offer the nearest available slots, a different weekday, or a start date a fortnight out with the ledger recalculated from the school's deadline. If the deadline makes that impossible, we tell you that too, because a plan that cannot reach the submission date is not worth selling.

sharjah/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.closingHeading: Send the existing draft and the school's two deadlines
sharjah/ib-dp-theory-of-knowledge-tutor.closingBody: Those three items are enough to start. Whatever draft exists, however rough, plus the exhibition deadline and the essay deadline as your child's own school has set them. We read the work before the trial lesson, so the hour is spent on the title and the argument rather than on background. You get a written baseline naming which of the five common draft failures is live and how many weeks the repair usually takes, and a dated ledger counted backwards from the school's date. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and each one returns marked work you can read yourself.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach named Diploma and Middle Years subjects to Sharjah students over live video. Each works to the same routine: a question set, a question marked, a note written, so a parent who does not teach the subject can still see what happened.

intro.heading: The question behind the search: how will we know it is working?
paragraphs: Parents in Sharjah who search for a home tutor are rarely asking about furniture. They are asking for someone reliable, consistent and accountable, in a format where a parent can see what is going on. The assumption is that physical presence delivers that accountability, and it is a reasonable assumption: if the tutor is in the next room you can at least hear that work is happening. The problem is that hearing work happen is not evidence of progress, and plenty of families have paid for a year of pleasant sessions that produced no movement at all.

Real accountability is a paper trail. After a month, a family should be able to put four things on the table: the questions the student has attempted, those questions marked with the specific marks that were not awarded, a written note per session naming the topic and the next step, and the current draft of any coursework alongside the previous one. With those four things, a parent who has never studied Chemistry can tell whether the arrangement is working. Without them, nobody can, including the tutor.

What home tutoring costs in this market is worth stating plainly, because it is part of the decision. Bestimate's rate table for Dubai tutoring in 2026 puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and home tutors generally at AED 200 to 500, against a band of roughly AED 150 to 300 for qualified online one-to-one. Monthly packages advertised in the market include around AED 799 per month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 per month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those figures were read in October 2026 and they describe the market, not IB Gram's own price list. A meaningful share of the in-home premium is the tutor's car.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to Sharjah families over live video. It does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. That is stated here rather than buried, because a family looking specifically for someone to arrive at an address in Al Majaz deserves to know in the first thirty seconds. What the online format gives back is a wider pool of subject specialists, a slot that can move without anybody driving, and a session that is recorded in writing by default rather than by goodwill.

The rest of this page is the evidence framework in detail. A comparison of the two formats on the things that actually differ. The fortnightly artefacts a family should expect. How to read a marked paper without knowing the subject. How many Internal Assessment drafts are normal and what should change between them. What grade movement looks like over six weeks against two terms. The permit question. And the part most providers leave out: how to tell when the evidence says stop paying.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Evidence looks different in each IB programme, because each is assessed differently. What a parent should ask to see depends on which programme their child is in.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects graded 1 to 7 plus up to three points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay matrix. External papers carry most of the grade and the Internal Assessment typically 20 to 25 per cent. The evidence that matters here is marked past-paper questions with the lost marks identified, because that is the currency the final grade is paid in.
programmes.countryNote: For Sharjah Diploma students, including the large group attending Dubai schools, the fortnightly checkpoint should include where the school's own assessment calendar sits. Ask your Diploma coordinator for the internal deadlines in writing, then make sure the tutoring plan is scheduled around them rather than colliding with them.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked out of 8 and converted to a 1 to 7 grade. There are no public past papers to mark, so the evidence is different: the task, the criterion descriptors, the student's response and a note on which descriptor band the response currently sits in and why.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah families arriving from Indian or British systems often find MYP reporting opaque, because a grade of 5 gives no indication of what is missing. Asking a tutor to show the descriptor and the response side by side makes the gap legible, and that single habit changes how useful the sessions are.

programmes.name: Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge
programmes.description: Two assessed core elements graded A to E that combine for up to three points, both submitted as the student's own work. The only legitimate evidence trail here is draft history: version one, the criteria-referenced feedback, version two written by the student, and the change visible between them.
programmes.countryNote: Because the core sits outside subject lessons, it is where Sharjah students with long commutes most often run out of time. Keeping dated drafts is also a protection: a documented progression from rough question to finished essay is what demonstrates the work is genuinely the student's own.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Sharjah families most often ask for, noted here with the specific artefact that shows whether the work is landing. Ask for that artefact rather than for a progress report.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Ask to see calculation questions marked with the method marks circled. Progress here looks like working that becomes legible and ordered, units appearing consistently, and significant figures stopping being an issue. Those are visible changes on paper within three or four sessions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Ask for the long explanation questions. Progress looks like the first sentence of an answer naming the physical principle, and free-body diagrams drawn before any algebra. Both are easy for a parent to spot in a script without knowing the physics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Ask for non-calculator work. Progress looks like exact values retained rather than decimals, lines of algebra set out in order, and fewer answers appearing with no supporting method. Method marks recovered are the measurable change here.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Ask for modelling and statistics questions. Progress looks like every numerical answer followed by a sentence saying what it means in context, because that interpretation sentence is where the marks sit and where students habitually stop.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Ask for extended-response answers marked against the command term. Progress looks like shorter answers that use the technical term, rather than longer answers that paraphrase it. Length going down while marks go up is the signal to watch for.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Ask for diagrams. Progress is unusually visible: axes labelled, curves named, equilibrium points marked, and a stated judgement at the end of evaluation answers. A parent can audit this subject's improvement in about ninety seconds.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Ask for the guiding question and the answer together. Progress looks like one argument sustained through the response instead of a catalogue of devices, and a plan visible at the top of the page. Both are legible to a parent who has not read the text.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Ask for case-study answers. Progress looks like the stimulus material quoted and used rather than terms defined in the abstract, and evaluation that reaches a decision. The pre-released case means this subject's preparation is predictable and should be documented.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Ask for short-answer questions written to the clock. Progress looks like studies deployed as evidence for a stated argument instead of recounted, and answers that stop when the tariff is met rather than running on.

subjects.name: Arabic and language acquisition
subjects.description: Ask for a recording or transcript of oral practice and a marked written piece. Progress in languages shows across weeks rather than sessions, so the fortnightly artefact matters more here than in any other subject on this list.

sections.heading: What an in-home tutor costs in Sharjah, and what the hour actually contains
paragraphs: The published market numbers are reasonably consistent. Bestimate's 2026 rate table for Dubai tutoring puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with home tutors more broadly at AED 200 to 500, while qualified online one-to-one sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above. Advertised monthly packages include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. All of these were read in October 2026, and all describe the market rather than IB Gram's own rates.

The premium on a visit is not arbitrary. A tutor travelling to Al Nahda for a 6pm session during the Dubai-bound evening peak spends perhaps forty minutes each way, which is unpaid time unless it is priced into the hour. In a villa community such as Al Zahia the drive is shorter but the detour from the main road is real. Someone pays for that time. The useful question for a family is therefore not whether a visit costs more but how much of the premium buys teaching rather than transport.

The second question is the pool. A visiting tutor must live within a practical radius, which means the choice in Sharjah is whoever is both qualified in that exact subject and close enough to come. For Mathematics at Standard Level that may be a reasonable field. For Physics at Higher Level, or Economics HL Paper 3, or Arabic ab initio, it can narrow to nobody, particularly on the east coast. sections.heading: Why this is delivered online to Sharjah, stated plainly
paragraphs: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and that is true of every country page on the site. A family who wants someone physically present should hire locally, and this page is more useful to them as a cost and evidence framework than as a pitch. Saying so early is simply more honest than letting a form fill decide the conversation.

The case for the online format, made on its merits, has three parts. The first is subject depth: a student in Muwaileh taking Chemistry HL works with someone who teaches Chemistry HL, rather than with the best available generalist within a twenty-minute drive. The second is that the paid hour is entirely teaching, with no arrival or departure inside it. The third is that the record keeps itself. Screens hold the work, marking happens on the shared document, and the session note is written where both parent and student can find it.

There are honest limits. A student who will not sit at a desk without an adult in the room is harder to teach over video, and a family whose home has no quiet space will find the format frustrating. Very young learners generally need shorter sessions online than in person. None of those limits apply to a typical Diploma or senior Middle Years student, which is the group this page is written for, but they are worth saying rather than leaving a family to discover them in week two.

sections.heading: The evidence file: what you should be shown every fortnight
paragraphs: A tutoring arrangement that cannot be audited is a tutoring arrangement that drifts. The fix is a small, fixed set of artefacts produced as a by-product of ordinary teaching, not as extra reporting. Four items cover it: the work set, the work marked, a note of what happened, and the current state of any coursework draft. Nothing in that list requires a parent to understand the subject, which is the point of it.

Set the rhythm at the start rather than asking for it after a disappointing report. A reasonable expectation is a marked question or short paper after each session, a two or three line note naming the topic covered and the next step, and a fortnightly look at the whole file by the parent. Fortnightly is the right interval: weekly is too noisy to show a trend and monthly is long enough for a term to be half gone before anyone notices nothing is moving.

The table below is the version to agree in writing. It is deliberately modest, because a tutor producing elaborate reports is spending your money on documentation rather than teaching. What matters is that the artefacts exist, are dated, and are kept in one place where a parent can see them in sequence. By the third fortnight the file itself answers the question of whether to continue, which is a far better basis for the decision than a conversation about how the sessions feel.

sections.heading: How to read a marked paper when you do not teach the subject
paragraphs: Parents often assume they cannot judge a marked script without subject knowledge. In practice, the three most useful signals are visible to anyone. The first is whether lost marks repeat: if the same type of mark is missing in week one and week six, the teaching has not addressed it. The second is whether the student's answers are getting shorter and better rather than longer. The third is whether anything is blank, because blank questions are a timing problem rather than a knowledge problem and need a completely different fix.

A fourth signal takes slightly more effort and is worth it. Ask your child to explain one marked question to you, out loud, from the script. A student who can say what the question wanted, what they wrote and why the mark was not awarded has understood the feedback. A student who can only say the tutor explained it has not. That ninety-second check is the single most reliable audit of a tutoring arrangement available to a non-specialist parent.

What not to do is argue with the marking. The mark scheme is published and the examiner's standard is not negotiable, and a tutor who spends sessions disputing marks rather than teaching to them is wasting the hour. Equally, do not read a low mark as a verdict on the student. Early in a Diploma course a 40 per cent score on a past paper is normal, because the paper covers two years of content and the student has studied one. The trend across the file matters; a single script does not.
bullets: Repeating lost marks mean the teaching has not addressed the cause
Shorter, denser answers are usually a sign of progress

sections.heading: Internal Assessment drafts: how many, and what should change between them
paragraphs: The Internal Assessment is where families most often lose track of what is legitimate, so the draft history serves two purposes: it shows progress, and it documents that the work is the student's own. Three to four drafts is a typical progression, and each one should change in a specific way rather than simply getting longer. A tutor's role is to read, question and name the criterion that is failing. The student writes every word of every version.

In practice the sequence runs like this. The first version establishes a research question narrow enough to answer and a method that can actually produce data or evidence. The second applies the method and gets the analysis onto the page, usually badly. The third fixes the evaluation and reflection, which is where most of the available marks sit and where students habitually run out of energy. A fourth, if needed, tightens presentation, referencing and the word count.

The boundary is absolute and worth repeating. A tutor may explain each criterion, ask what a paragraph is trying to prove, point out that the conclusion does not follow from the data, and say which band the draft currently sits in. A tutor may not write sentences, rewrite paragraphs into finished shape, or hand over a template to be completed. Research for this project found an operator in this market selling completed Internal Assessments; a student submitting such work risks a malpractice finding and the Diploma itself. Keeping dated drafts is a parent's best protection against that risk, whoever is helping.

sections.heading: Grade movement: what changes in six weeks and what takes two terms
paragraphs: Families are frequently told that progress takes time, which is true and useless. The more honest version distinguishes between what kind of problem is being fixed. Technique problems move fast: command-term discipline, answer structure, working layout, calculator habits and timing can all show measurable change in four to six weeks because they are behaviours rather than knowledge. Content problems move slowly, because a term of missed material takes a term to replace.

That distinction should be made before the first paid session, from the marked mock. If the script shows good scores where the student answered and blanks at the end, expect visible change by week six. If the marks are evenly thin across every question, do not expect a grade to move before the next reporting cycle, and plan the budget for two terms rather than six weeks. Confusing the two is how families conclude that tutoring does not work, when what actually happened is that they bought six weeks for a two-term problem.

The planning figures below come from how arrangements of this shape usually run, not from any published study, and they are estimates rather than promises. One grade of movement in a Higher Level subject with two terms available is commonly ten to twenty hours. Two grades needs a full year. No quantity of hours makes a particular grade certain, and a provider who offers that certainty has told you something about their method rather than about your child.
