sections.heading: The permit question, and what to ask before the first paid hour
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page for private tutor licensing lists a two-working-day completion time with applications through its smart app, website and e-services system.

Because the permit costs nothing, there is no financial reason for a tutor working in the UAE not to hold one, which makes the question a fair and easy one to ask. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any specific amount quoted to a parent should be treated with caution, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

Four questions are worth asking before the first paid hour, whoever you hire. Do you hold the private tuition work permit? Which subject and level do you teach, specifically, and which components most recently? What will my child do between sessions, and who marks it? And what will you not do with the Internal Assessment? IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no UAE premises and no regulator endorsement of any kind; a tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a separate educational services permit, which is a different thing entirely and is not claimed here.

sections.heading: When the evidence says stop
paragraphs: The hardest part of any tutoring arrangement is ending one that is not working, and most providers have no incentive to help a family do it. The evidence file makes the decision less emotional. If the same marks are being lost in week eight that were lost in week one, if the set work is not being attempted, or if the school's next assessment shows no movement and nobody can explain why, the arrangement has failed and continuing it costs money and morale.

Three endings are legitimate and they are not the same. The first is a different tutor: the subject and the diagnosis were right and the match was wrong, which happens and is nobody's failure. The second is a different plan: the problem turned out to be content rather than technique, so six weeks becomes two terms, or the hours move to a different subject that is at greater risk. The third is stopping: the student is where they need to be, or the gap is not closable in the time left, and the money is better spent elsewhere or not at all.

The fourth ending, which is the one to avoid, is continuing because a block was bought. Prepaid packages create exactly that incentive, which is a reason to be cautious of long upfront commitments early in a relationship. Agree a review point at the next school assessment, write it down, and treat it as a genuine decision rather than a formality. A provider who is comfortable with that review is a provider worth working with.
bullets: The same marks lost in week eight as week one means the plan failed
A wrong match is common and is not a reason to abandon tutoring
Reclassifying a technique problem as a content problem changes the budget
Be wary of a long prepaid block agreed before any evidence exists

sections.heading: Keeping the rhythm through Ramadan and the Sharjah school week
paragraphs: An evidence routine only works if it survives the calendar, and the UAE calendar interrupts it twice. Ramadan shortens the school day and reorders family life. The winter break sits in the middle of coursework season for Diploma students. Both are usually handled by abandoning the routine for a month, which is how a January report arrives as a surprise.

The workable approach during Ramadan is to move the slot rather than cancel it. Post-iftar sessions suit older students well, and the shortened school day opens late weekend mornings. The hour before iftar is the one to avoid for analytical work. Because lessons run over live video, a slot can shift by three hours without anyone driving in Sharjah's evening traffic, and the marked-work routine continues unchanged even if the frequency drops to fortnightly for the month.

The December break is the opposite case: a rare uninterrupted block. For a DP2 student it is the last clear run at mock preparation; for DP1 it is the natural window for Extended Essay reading, which needs continuous time more than it needs instruction. Book those sessions in November, because the specialists in scarce Higher Level subjects are committed by late December rather than by March. Then resume the fortnightly file review in January, when the mock marks give it something real to measure.

One further calendar note is specific to Sharjah families with children at Dubai schools. The two emirates do not always align on term dates and in-service days, so a household can have one child on holiday while another is sitting an assessment. Ask each school for its published calendar at the start of the year and set the tutoring slots against the school's dates rather than the family's, because it is the school's assessment that the plan is measured by.
bullets: Move sessions during Ramadan rather than pausing the routine
Post-iftar suits older students; avoid the hour before iftar

faqs.question: How much does a home tutor in Sharjah charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 350, with home tutors more broadly quoted at AED 200 to 500, against about AED 150 to 300 for qualified online one-to-one. Advertised monthly packages include around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those were read in October 2026 from providers' own pages and describe the market rather than IB Gram's rates. A sizeable part of the in-home premium is travel time, which is worth weighing against what else the same budget could buy in teaching hours.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our home in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to Sharjah families over live video and does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service. If what you want is someone physically present, hire locally and use the cost comparison and evidence checklist on this page to judge the arrangement. If the priority is a specialist in a specific subject at a specific level, the online format usually gives you a wider field, because the tutor no longer has to live within driving distance of your community.

faqs.question: What evidence should I see after a month of paid tutoring?
faqs.answer: Four things, kept in one place and dated. The work set between sessions, with evidence it was attempted. That work marked in the mark scheme's own language, showing which marks were lost. A short note per session naming the topic covered and the next step. And, where coursework is involved, the current draft alongside the previous one. With those four, a parent who has never studied the subject can tell whether anything is changing. Without them, nobody can, and the conversation reduces to whether the sessions feel positive.

faqs.question: I do not teach Chemistry, so how do I judge whether the sessions are working?
faqs.answer: Three signals need no subject knowledge. Are the same types of mark being lost in week six as in week one? Are the answers getting shorter and denser rather than longer? Is anything left blank, which points to timing rather than knowledge? Then add a fourth: ask your child to explain one marked question out loud from the script, saying what the question wanted, what they wrote and why the mark was not given. A student who can do that has absorbed the feedback. One who can only say the tutor explained it has not.

faqs.question: How many drafts should my daughter's Internal Assessment go through?
faqs.answer: Three to four is typical, and each should change in a specific way rather than simply growing. The planning note narrows the research question. Draft one states and justifies the method. Draft two gets the analysis onto the page. Draft three develops the evaluation and reflection, which is where most of the available marks sit. A final pass fixes referencing, word count and presentation. Your daughter writes every word of every version; a tutor explains the criteria, asks what a paragraph is proving, and names which criterion is currently failing.

faqs.question: How long before a predicted grade actually moves?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is being fixed. Technique changes, such as command-term discipline, answer structure, working layout and timing, usually show measurable change in four to six weeks because they are behaviours. Content gaps take a term or more, because missed material has to be replaced. Predicted grades themselves move at the school's reporting cycle, which may lag the actual improvement by weeks. Decide which kind of problem you have from the marked mock before buying hours, because buying six weeks for a two-term problem is how families conclude that tutoring does not work.

faqs.question: What does a session report need to contain to be useful?
faqs.answer: Two or three lines, not a page. The topic actually covered, what the student did in the session, the specific next step, and what has been set for the week. A useful note says the student practised structured six-mark explanations in electricity and still omits the principle in the opening sentence, with three questions set. A useless note says good progress on physics. Elaborate reporting is your money being spent on documentation, so brevity with specifics is the standard to ask for rather than volume.

faqs.question: Our tutor is pleasant but nothing is improving, so what now?
faqs.answer: Look at the file before the relationship. If the same marks are being lost in week eight as in week one, and the set work is being attempted, then the diagnosis was probably wrong: a content gap was treated as a technique problem, or the hours went to the wrong subject. If the set work is not being attempted, that is the first thing to fix and no tutor can fix it alone. If both are fine and the marks still have not moved, change tutor rather than add hours. Good rapport without movement is still a failed arrangement.

faqs.question: Should I sit in on my son's online sessions?
faqs.answer: For a senior student, generally no. Most Diploma-age students work less freely with a parent listening, and the evidence routine makes attendance unnecessary: the work, the marking and the note tell you what happened. The exception is the first session or two with a new tutor, where ten minutes at the start is reasonable to confirm the tone is right. For a younger Middle Years student, more presence helps, mainly to establish that the session is a working hour rather than a chat. After that, read the file rather than the room.

faqs.question: How do we keep a record of what was covered each week?
faqs.answer: Keep it in one shared place, dated, and let the routine produce it. The marked work, the session note and the draft versions are the record, so nothing extra needs writing if those three exist. A simple shared folder or document is enough; elaborate tracking systems tend to be abandoned by week five. The value of keeping it in sequence is that a trend becomes visible: three notes naming the same recurring error is information, where the same observation made once a term is just a remark.

faqs.question: Is it a problem that the tutor has never met my child in person?
faqs.answer: For a Diploma or senior Middle Years student, rarely. The work is reading, writing, marking and explaining, all of which transfer to a shared screen without loss, and the time saved on travel goes into teaching. It matters more for a young learner, for a student who genuinely will not sit at a desk without an adult present, or where there is no quiet space at home. Those are real limits and worth testing in the free trial lesson rather than assuming either way. What the format cannot replace is the school's supervision and laboratory time.

faqs.question: What should the tutor send us after each session?
faqs.answer: The marked work and a short note. The marked work should show which marks were not awarded and why, in the language the mark scheme uses, because that is what the student has to act on. The note should name the topic, the specific weakness worked on, and what has been set before the next session. Anything beyond that is optional. If a tutor sends neither, you have no way of auditing the arrangement later, and the conversation at the end of term becomes a disagreement about impressions.

faqs.question: Can we pause the sessions over the school holidays and restart afterwards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some students it is the right call, but the timing matters. For a DP2 student the December break is usually the last uninterrupted run at mock preparation, so pausing it is the most expensive pause in the year. For a DP1 student it is the natural window for Extended Essay reading, which needs time rather than instruction, so a pause there costs little. Summer pauses are normal. Whatever you decide, book the restart slot before you pause, because a popular weekday slot will be gone by January.

faqs.question: What does a free trial lesson tell us that a tutor profile does not?
faqs.answer: Whether the explanation lands with your particular child, which no profile can show. Use the trial on the real work: your child's marked script or current topic, not a sample exercise. Watch for three things afterwards. Can your child say what they learned in one sentence? Did the tutor identify something specific rather than general? And was anything set to do before the next session? One lesson at no cost, with nothing paid beforehand and no obligation to book a block, is enough to answer all three.

faqs.question: How do we know the person teaching my child holds a UAE tuition permit?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask for it in writing. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years, with a two-working-day processing time listed on MoHRE's own service page. Because it costs nothing, there is no reason for a tutor working in the UAE to be without one. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-juraina.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma subjects to students across Sharjah, one-to-one over live video. Every arrangement starts with a free trial lesson, and every quote we give is for teaching hours with no travel priced into them.

intro.heading: What this actually costs, and where it leaks
paragraphs: Al Juraina sits in the older, central-southern part of Sharjah, off the Maliha Road, with schools and long-established tutoring supply close by. Families here are rarely short of options. What they are short of is a straight answer about money, because this market has a habit of discussing price only after a consultation.

So here are the numbers first. Across published UAE rate cards, budget online tutoring - usually delivered by university students - advertises from about AED 45 an hour. A qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300. An in-home one-to-one visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed. An IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist sits at AED 200 to 450 and above, and named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 or more. Monthly packages seen in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Those are market figures, read in October 2026 from competitor rate cards and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table. They are not our price list. Their purpose is comparison: once you know the bands, any quote you receive - including ours - can be judged rather than simply accepted or refused.

The more useful half of this page is about leakage, because the common problem in Al Juraina is not that families pay too much per hour. It is that they pay a reasonable rate for hours that could not have worked. Hours spent diagnosing what a marked script would have shown in twenty minutes. Hours in a quiet term with nothing dated to aim at. Hours of general revision in a subject that needed one topic repaired. Hours with a tutor who starts each session recapping the last one because nothing was written down.

There is also the travel premium, which is the only line in a tutoring budget that buys nothing academic. The gap between the online and in-home bands is a car. In central Sharjah that gap is smaller than on the outer corridors, and it is still the first place to look when a quote feels high. A longer drive does not improve anybody's understanding of an internal assessment criterion.

A word on why so few pages in this market will say any of this. Publishing a rate invites comparison, and comparison is uncomfortable when the premium in your model is travel or branding rather than teaching. Publishing bands with a source and a date is the opposite bet: it assumes a parent who can see the whole market makes a better decision, including the decision to buy from somebody else.

What follows sets out the four ways to read the same price, the five places money leaks, what a free trial should and should not mean, where group arrangements save genuinely and where they only appear to, and the things you should decline to pay for at any price.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-juraina.programmesIntro: The three IB stages cost different amounts to support properly, because they need different amounts of time. Here is what each typically requires before anybody quotes you an hourly rate.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The cheapest stage to support and the easiest to overspend on. Useful work is short - twenty-five to forty minutes on one skill - and finite: reading fluency, number facts, writing that answers the question asked. A rolling weekly hour through a whole primary year is usually buying reassurance rather than progress.
programmes.countryNote: In Al Juraina, with tuition centres and private tutors close by, primary support is often bought as a long-term habit. A better value test is whether the specific gap you started with has closed. If it has, stop; if nobody can tell you, the arrangement is not being measured.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed with task-specific descriptors, and each task marked once. Support here is best bought in short blocks before tasks rather than as a continuous hour, which makes it one of the most cost-efficient stages: three or four sessions aimed at one criterion often lift the achievement level, and the skill transfers.
programmes.countryNote: Families in this part of Sharjah frequently discover the Middle Years system late, because reports look reassuring until the Diploma arrives. Buying a few criterion-focused sessions at MYP 4 is substantially cheaper than buying a rescue in DP2.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The expensive one, because it runs two years and the pressure is uneven. Weekly support in a single subject across both years is roughly seventy hours. sections.heading: What families in this part of Sharjah are quoted
paragraphs: The spread is wide enough to confuse anybody: the same hour of tutoring is sold in this market anywhere between AED 45 and AED 650. Understanding what separates those numbers is most of what a parent needs, because the differences are not primarily about teaching quality.

At the bottom, budget platforms and university students. Published rate cards start from about AED 45 an hour, and the tutor is usually a capable undergraduate working from generic materials. For light homework support with a younger child this is often adequate. For a Diploma subject or an internal assessment it is not, and the gap shows up as hours spent pleasantly without marks moving.

In the middle, qualified subject tutors teaching online at roughly AED 150 to 300. This is where course-specific experience starts to be reliable: somebody who has taught the subject at the level your child is sitting, who marks against published criteria or mark schemes, and who keeps a record. For most Diploma and Middle Years work this band is where the useful teaching lives.

Above that, two different premiums. The in-home premium takes the same teaching to AED 180 to 500 an hour and buys travel. The brand premium takes it to AED 500 to 650 and above and buys reputation, often with a claim about examiner status that is rarely evidenced and never transfers to your child's paper. Neither premium changes what happens inside the hour, which is the only thing a family is really buying.

sections.heading: Five places the money reliably leaks
paragraphs: In our experience of enquiries from central Sharjah, families who feel they wasted money rarely overpaid per hour. They bought hours that could not have worked, usually for one of five reasons.

The first is paying a tutor to diagnose. A specialist can read a marked script and name the three things costing marks in twenty minutes. A generalist discovers the same information over three or four sessions, at full rate, and the family pays for the education of the tutor. Ask for a marked script to be read before the first paid hour.

The second is hours bought in quiet terms with nothing dated to aim at. A weekly slot in DP1 with no deadline in sight produces pleasant, unmeasured sessions. The fix is not to stop - DP1 is the cheapest time to close gaps - but to give the hour a target: a topic test, a proposal, a timed paper.

The third is general revision where a repair was needed. A student losing marks only on electrolysis does not need a chemistry course; they need three sessions and a question set. Providers rarely propose the smaller thing. The fourth is the undocumented tutor: if nothing is written down, each session starts by recapping the last, and a family pays for the same ground twice. The fifth is the travel premium, which is pure cost.
Taken together these five explain most of the dissatisfaction in this market. They are also all detectable within two sessions if a parent knows to look, which is the point of listing them.

sections.heading: Four ways to read the same price
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how this market quotes and not how families budget. The same arrangement looks different depending on the unit, and choosing the right unit prevents the two classic errors: starting at a rate that cannot be sustained into DP2, and underestimating the total by thinking in hours.

Per hour is useful for comparing providers. Per month is useful for cash flow, and the market's own monthly figures are informative: published packages at about AED 799 for eight online sessions, AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, with Bestimate's Dubai estimates putting a single weekly session at AED 600 to 1,200 a month with a qualified tutor.

Per term is the honest planning unit, because a term is the commitment a school year is made of. Twelve teaching weeks at one session a week is twelve hours - in the region of AED 1,800 to 3,600 at the qualified online band. Per programme is the number that should decide whether an arrangement is affordable at all: weekly support in one subject across a two-year Diploma is around seventy hours.

The table below sets out all four for the common patterns, so a family can see the same decision from each angle before committing. Note the last row: two focused blocks a year costs considerably less than weekly support across both years and, for a student who works between sessions, frequently achieves more.

Use the programme column as the affordability test and the term column as the planning tool. If the two-year figure is uncomfortable, the right response is to change the pattern now rather than to start weekly and stop in DP2, which is the worst of the available outcomes: the money is spent in the year that needed it least.

sections.heading: What a free trial should mean
paragraphs: Nearly everybody in this market offers something free, and the word covers a range of arrangements. Before accepting one, it is worth knowing what you are being given and what is expected in return.

A trial worth having is a full one-to-one lesson with the tutor who would actually teach your child, at no cost, with no card details taken and no obligation. Ours produces a marked script or a piece of written feedback that you keep whether you continue or not, which means even a declined trial leaves you with a diagnosis you did not have before.

A trial worth less is a fifteen-minute sales call with a coordinator, or a group demonstration class, or a lesson with a senior tutor who is not the person assigned afterwards. None of those is dishonest, and none of them answers the only question a trial should answer: will this particular tutor work with this particular child? Ask who is teaching the trial and whether they are the assigned tutor.

Two conditions worth checking anywhere. If 'free' has a condition attached - a minimum booking, a card held, a package commitment - it should be stated on the same screen as the word. And a trial is not the place for a grade prediction. A tutor who finishes a free lesson by promising a number is selling confidence, and nobody can know what a particular candidate will score.

Treat the trial as the cheapest hour you will ever buy in this process, because it is free and it produces evidence. Even if you decline afterwards, you leave with a marked script and somebody's professional view of what the remaining weeks can realistically change - information you can take to any other provider in Sharjah.

sections.heading: Group classes, pairs and siblings: real savings and false ones
paragraphs: The obvious way to reduce cost is to share the hour, and it works in some situations and not others. The distinction is whether the work being done is individual.

Content teaching shares well. Several students can be taught the same topic at once, which is what a school does all day and what a tuition centre sells at a lower price per student. If a Middle Years cohort is all weak on investigation structure, a small group session is good value.

Individual diagnostic work does not share. An error log is personal. A marked script needs reviewing with the student who wrote it. An internal assessment research question belongs to one project. A group arrangement cannot do these things, which is why group revision courses before a series often feel busy and change little - the student who needed three sessions on electrolysis spent six hours on everything else.

There is a middle option worth knowing about. A pair of students at the same stage in the same course can share content teaching and then take short individual slots for script review - half the cost of two full one-to-one arrangements, with the individual work preserved. It requires two families whose children are genuinely at the same point, which is rarer than it sounds but does happen within a year group.

Siblings are a special case. Two children in the same course and year can genuinely share a session; two children in different courses cannot, and the common attempt - one tutor teaching both, alternating attention - usually shortchanges the older one. The real saving for a household is scheduling: consecutive slots on one evening, two specialists, one supervised evening for a parent. That saves time rather than money, which for most families in Al Juraina is the scarcer resource.

sections.heading: Where to spend in DP1, and where in DP2
paragraphs: A Diploma is two years long, and the same dirham does different work depending on when it is spent. Getting the sequence right is worth more than negotiating the rate.

DP1 money buys prevention. A content gap closed in the first year costs one or two sessions. The same gap closed in DP2 costs five, and the five hours come out of revision time that has no spare capacity. DP1 is also when the exploration or investigation question is settled, and a well-chosen question saves a term of rework. Families almost never buy here, and the ones who do rarely need an emergency later.

DP2 money buys completion and technique. Internal assessments, the extended essay and Theory of Knowledge have to be finished in DP2's first half, and the final term is timed papers and error logs. Hours here are more expensive in real terms because they compete with everything else the student has to do, and because specialist availability tightens in the weeks before a session.

There is one exception to the spend-early rule. If a DP1 student is coping and the household budget is tight, holding a fortnightly slot purely to reserve a scarce specialist is reasonable, because that tutor will be unavailable by the time DP2 needs them. You are buying access as much as teaching, and saying so out loud is more honest than dressing it up as revision.

The practical allocation we suggest for a family watching cost: a fortnightly slot in DP1 in the one subject that genuinely needs it, short fortnightly check-ins for the core components, then a concentrated block in DP2 where the calendar demands it. That shape typically costs less than a weekly arrangement across both years and delivers more, because every hour has something dated to aim at.

sections.heading: Packages, VAT and the questions to ask before paying
paragraphs: Once a rate is agreed there are a handful of commercial details that decide whether the arrangement is good value in practice. None of them is complicated, and all are easier to raise before money changes hands.

Ask whether the quoted figure includes VAT, and if a provider claims to be registered, ask for the registration number. We will not tell you on this page how UAE tax treats tuition fees, because that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority and a tutoring site is not a source for it. What a parent can reasonably expect is clarity about whether the number they were quoted is the number they will pay.

Ask what happens to unused sessions in a package, how much notice a cancellation needs, and whether the rate is per hour or per lesson - a sixty-minute hour and a forty-five-minute lesson at the same price are different products. Ask who the tutor will be, whether they change between sessions, and what happens if the match is wrong. A provider with a pool can replace a tutor and carry the plan across; an individual arrangement means starting again.

Finally, ask what is written down. A written target list for the next six sessions, a note after each lesson, and a review at a fixed point are what make an arrangement measurable. Without them, renewal happens on feeling, and feeling in this market is heavily influenced by how pleasant the tutor is rather than by whether marks moved.
bullets: Is the quoted figure inclusive of VAT, and is there a registration number?
Per hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson?

sections.heading: What not to pay for at any price
paragraphs: Some things in this market are cheap at AED 45 and a bad purchase at AED 650, because the problem is not the price.

Do not pay for a grade guarantee. Nobody can know what a particular candidate will score, and a promise of a 7, a points total or a specific improvement is a sales instrument. Where a refund is attached to an outcome, read what triggers it; in practice the conditions usually make it unreachable.

Do not pay for assessed work. Services selling completed internal assessments, extended essays, Theory of Knowledge essays or coursework appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams. The malpractice consequence falls on the student's diploma rather than on the seller, and no fee compensates for that. A tutor may teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work, and nothing more. IB Gram does not sell completed work of any kind.

Do not pay a premium for claimed regulator approval. No tutoring service should describe itself as approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge unless it holds that specific permit and can show the number. For clarity about us: IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no UAE premises, and we hold no approval or accreditation from any education authority in this country. And do not pay for self-asserted ratings - a star score with no countable, dated reviews behind it is decoration.

process.description: Send a recent paper, test or draft. The matched tutor marks it against the criteria or mark scheme before you meet, so the free trial lesson is spent on diagnosis. You keep the marked work and the tutor's written view whether or not you continue.

process.title: A written plan with a number of sessions in it
process.description: You get a target list for the next six sessions and a note after each lesson. Both exist so the arrangement can be judged on movement rather than on how the sessions felt, and so nobody pays twice for the same ground.

process.description: We look at timed scores and criterion feedback. If the fit is wrong we change the tutor and keep the plan; if the target has been met we say so and stop. A provider who never recommends stopping is not reviewing anything.

whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page carries the month it was read. Three of the six top-ranked pages in our competitor research publish no price at all, and two of the others quote in dollars. You cannot judge a quote against something nobody will state.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the rate
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, so you are paying for teaching hours and nothing else. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE - that service exists only in India - so no part of the quote is a drive along the Maliha Road.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before the first paid hour
whyPoints.description: A marked script read before the trial means the first paid session starts with teaching. Paying a generalist to work out what the course requires is the most common leak in this market and the easiest to close.

whyPoints.title: Finite blocks where finite is right
whyPoints.description: Some problems need three sessions, not a term. We will propose the smaller thing and say when it is finished, because an arrangement that never ends is a product rather than a plan.

whyPoints.title: Nothing sold that should not be sold
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees, no completed coursework, no claimed regulator approval, no self-asserted star ratings. Those are the four things in this market that are a bad purchase at any price, and declining to sell them is a position rather than a disclaimer.

faqs.question: What does an IB tutor cost for a family in Al Juraina?
faqs.answer: Across published UAE rate cards, budget online tutoring starts around AED 45 an hour, a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed, and named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 and above. Bestimate's Dubai estimates, read in October 2026, put one weekly session at AED 600 to 1,200 a month with a qualified tutor. Those are market figures, not our price list - ask us directly and start with the free trial.

faqs.question: What exactly am I paying extra for when a tutor drives to Al Juraina?
faqs.answer: Because it includes a journey. The teaching inside the hour is the same; the difference between roughly AED 150 to 300 online and AED 180 to 500 in-home is travel time, priced in whether or not it appears as a line. Central Sharjah journeys are shorter than those to the outer corridors, so the premium here is smaller than for a family in Tilal City - but it still buys a car rather than better knowledge of an internal assessment criterion. We do not sell UAE home visits at all.

faqs.question: Where do families most often waste money on tutoring?
faqs.answer: Five places, in our experience of enquiries from this part of Sharjah. Paying full rate while a generalist works out what the course requires. Buying weekly hours in a quiet term with nothing dated to aim at. Buying a general course when a three-session repair on one topic was needed. Working with a tutor who writes nothing down, so each session recaps the last. And the travel premium. None of these is about the hourly rate being too high, and all five are visible within two sessions.

faqs.question: Is a cheap university-student tutor ever the right choice?
faqs.answer: For some jobs, yes. Light homework supervision for a younger child, keeping a routine, or working through practice questions a parent has selected - a capable undergraduate at the AED 45 to 150 band can do those well, and many hold the free MoHRE private tuition permit that the law requires. What that band rarely includes is somebody who has taught a Diploma subject to final-grade standard or supervised an internal assessment. Buying cheap hours for that work usually costs more in the end.

faqs.question: How many hours does a two-year Diploma subject actually take?
faqs.answer: Weekly support in one subject across both years is around seventy hours. Two well-placed blocks a year is nearer fifty. A DP2-only weekly arrangement is about thirty-five, and a final-stretch block is roughly twelve. At the qualified online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, those translate to very different totals, which is why we suggest deciding the pattern before negotiating the rate. The cheapest effective pattern is usually fortnightly in DP1 converting to a block when the calendar demands it.

faqs.question: What should a free trial lesson actually include?
faqs.answer: A full one-to-one lesson with the tutor who would be assigned, at no cost, with no card details and no minimum booking. Ours also produces a marked script or written feedback that you keep whether you continue or not. What is worth less is a fifteen-minute call with a coordinator, a group demonstration, or a lesson taught by somebody other than the assigned tutor. Ask who is teaching it, and treat any grade promise at the end as a reason to be cautious rather than reassured.

faqs.question: Do group classes save money for IB students?
faqs.answer: For content teaching, genuinely. A small group all weak on the same topic can be taught together at a lower cost per student. For everything individual, no: an error log is personal, a marked script needs reviewing with its author, and an internal assessment question belongs to one project. That is why group revision courses before a series often feel busy and change little - the student who needed three sessions on one topic spent six hours on everything else as well.

faqs.question: Can two of my children share a tutor to reduce the bill?
faqs.answer: Only if they are on the same course at the same level, in which case the saving is real. Across different courses - a Diploma higher level subject and a Middle Years class, say - one tutor alternating attention shortchanges both, usually the older child more. The saving that does work for a household is scheduling rather than sharing: consecutive slots on one evening with two specialists means a parent supervises once instead of three times, which for most families here is the scarcer resource.

faqs.question: Should I ask whether the quoted price includes VAT?
faqs.answer: Yes, and ask for a registration number if a provider says it is registered. We will not state how UAE tax treats tuition fees on this page, because that is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority rather than for a tutoring site. What you can reasonably expect from anybody is clarity about whether the figure quoted is the figure you pay, along with straight answers on whether the rate is per hour or per lesson, what notice a cancellation needs, and what happens to unused sessions in a package.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start tutoring in DP1 or wait until DP2?
faqs.answer: Starting in DP1 is cheaper in total, which is counterintuitive because it looks like more months of spending. A content gap closed in the first year costs one or two sessions; the same gap in DP2 costs five, and those five hours come out of revision time that has no spare capacity. DP1 is also when the exploration or investigation question is settled, and a good question saves a term of rework. A fortnightly DP1 slot plus a DP2 block usually beats weekly support across both years, for less.

faqs.question: What does a term of support cost if we only want one subject?
faqs.answer: A term is about twelve teaching weeks, so a weekly slot is twelve hours - in the region of AED 1,800 to 3,600 at the qualified online market band of AED 150 to 300 an hour. Fortnightly halves that. The in-home equivalent for the same twelve hours runs AED 2,160 to 6,000 at market in-home rates. Those are market figures published for comparison rather than our prices; ask us for ours, and the free trial lesson costs nothing in any case.

faqs.question: Are grade guarantees ever worth paying for?
faqs.answer: No. Nobody can know what a particular candidate will score, so a guaranteed 7, a promised points total or a specific improvement is a sales instrument rather than an educational commitment. Where a money-back condition is attached, read exactly what triggers it - the conditions usually make it unreachable in practice. We do not offer grade guarantees, and we would treat any provider that does as having told you something important about how it sells rather than how it teaches.

faqs.question: Someone offered to write my child's internal assessment. How much should that cost?
faqs.answer: Nothing, because it should not be bought at any price. Services selling completed internal assessments, extended essays and Theory of Knowledge essays appear in these search results charging thousands of dirhams, and the consequence of using one is a malpractice finding against the student's diploma rather than a problem for the seller. A tutor may read criteria, question a research question, teach a method and explain why a draft misses a criterion. Writing, redrafting or editing the submitted text is not permitted, and we do not do it.

faqs.question: How do I know whether the money is working?
faqs.answer: Ask for three things at the start: a written target list for the next six sessions, a short note after each lesson, and a fixed review point. Then judge on movement in timed scores and criterion feedback rather than on how the sessions felt. Pleasant sessions with a likeable tutor are easy to renew and hard to evaluate. We review at session six, change the tutor if the fit is wrong, and say so when a target has been met rather than letting an arrangement roll.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-juraina.closingHeading: Ask for the number, then ask what it includes
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-juraina.closingBody: The bands on this page are the market's, published with their source and month so that any quote - including ours - can be measured against something. Send us the programme, subject, level and the next dated assessment, and we will match a specialist, mark the script and run a free trial lesson over live video at no cost. Lessons for Al Juraina families are one-to-one and online, with no travel inside the rate.

That second detail is the one that decides value for money in this programme, because a component specialist and a subject generalist cost different amounts and do different work.

intro.heading: Two years of spending, planned once
paragraphs: Al Khan sits along the Sharjah lagoon, between Al Majaz and Al Taawun, with towers facing the water and the Dubai boundary a short drive west. Families here are generally paying school fees for more than one child and are careful with a second education bill. The Diploma, unfortunately, is the programme least suited to careful monthly budgeting, because its costs arrive in a shape that reactive spending handles badly.

Here is the shape. Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, each carrying internally assessed work. Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service running across both years, with up to three points sitting in the combination of the first two. Internal deadlines set by the school rather than the board, clustered in the middle of the second year. And a single main examination session at the end, with no resit route inside the same academic year for a UAE candidate.

A family that spends reactively meets all of that at once in the spring of the second year, which is the most expensive and least effective moment available. A family that plans across two years spends the same total, or less, and places it where it converts into points. That difference is the whole argument of this page, and it is arithmetic rather than opinion.

The published market gives the figures. Qualified online subject tutors advertise from roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase at around AED 270, and premium named or examiner-led provision advertised as high as AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits including travel run from about AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table placing the usual band at AED 180 to 350. Those belong to the providers and surveys named, read in October 2026.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. That removes the travel component of the rate and, on a corridor where afternoon arrival times are unpredictable, removes the waste that a visiting arrangement produces when a session is missed or cut short.

What follows is the budget. Term by term across two years. What one point actually costs in different scenarios, which is the only sensible unit for a Diploma family. Why deferring the core is the most expensive habit in the programme. What each price tier buys in a Diploma context specifically. And what the school already owes you before any money changes hands. None of it assumes a particular budget; the argument is about placement rather than amount.

sections.heading: What Diploma support costs a family in Al Khan
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Khan, as the phrase is used here, is a Diploma subject specialist working one-to-one with one student. IB Gram provides that over live video to Sharjah families and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. The cost question deserves published numbers rather than a brochure, so here they are with their sources.

Qualified online subject tutors advertise in this market from roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase listing around AED 270 and premium named or examiner-led provision advertised as high as AED 650. Entry-level online sessions are advertised from about AED 33 to 65. In-home visits including travel run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common band at AED 180 to 350.

For a Diploma family the specialist band is usually the relevant one, and the reason is structural rather than snobbish. Diploma marks sit substantially inside internally assessed components with published criteria, and reading a draft against those criteria is not something a subject generalist can do reliably. At Standard Level in a well-supplied subject a qualified tutor is often sufficient. At Higher Level with coursework, the component specialist is what the money is for.

IB Gram publishes no tariff on these pages. The rate depends on level, component, subject scarcity and session length, and it is quoted after a free trial lesson so both sides know what is being bought. What this page will do is show where across two years that money produces the most.

sections.heading: The two-year Diploma budget, term by term
paragraphs: Written out across two years, Diploma spending looks very different from how it is usually incurred. The common pattern is nothing until the second year and then a concentrated burst in the spring, which is the single most expensive way to buy the least.

The reasons are mechanical. In the spring of the second year, the coursework deadlines have passed, so the component marks are fixed. The syllabus is finishing, so content teaching has limited room to compound. Availability is tightest because every family in the region is buying at once. And the student has the least capacity to act on anything, because six subjects are converging.

Reversed, the same money buys considerably more. A bridging block before the first year. One weekly session in the spring of the first year, when the student can absorb it. A coursework block in the autumn of the second year, when deadlines can still be met. And a short triaged paper block in the spring. That distribution costs no more in total and leaves the family with a student who is not in crisis.

The table below uses published market bands to show the shape rather than to quote a price. Fill in your own numbers from the bands above; the point is the distribution across the six windows, and specifically that the biggest line is not the last one.

One caveat on reading the table. The session counts are typical rather than prescriptive, and a household with a strong student in five subjects and one weak one will spend far less than the shape implies. The distribution is the transferable part: early windows are cheap because the student can act on what they are given, and the final window is expensive because by then most of the grade is already decided.

sections.heading: Funding by points rather than by panic
paragraphs: A Diploma family's real unit of account is the point, not the hour, and switching to it changes almost every spending decision. The question is not which subject is weakest but where a point is cheapest to obtain.

Three scenarios dominate. A subject sitting one or two marks below a boundary, where technique work on papers can produce a point for a handful of sessions. A core component heading for a low grade, where up to three points sit in the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay and a small early intervention can protect the lot. And a subject genuinely two grades behind, where a point costs a term of weekly work because content has to be rebuilt.

Set out that way, the ranking is usually obvious and usually not what instinct suggests. The cheapest points are near boundaries and in the core. The most expensive are in the subject the student finds hardest, which is where most families spend first. A conversation about distance from boundaries, held with the subject teachers in the autumn of the second year, is worth more than any amount of comparison shopping on hourly rates.

The table below sets the scenarios side by side. The last column is the one to argue with: it is deliberately explicit about what a point costs, because that is the number no provider publishes and the only one that makes a Diploma budget rational.

The conversation that produces this ranking is short and free. Ask each subject teacher, in the autumn of the second year, roughly how far your child is from the next boundary and what would move them. Teachers answer that well when asked directly, and the answers across six subjects usually make the spending decision obvious without any further analysis.

sections.heading: Why deferring the core is the most expensive habit
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay have a structural disadvantage: nothing chases them weekly. Subject homework has a teacher asking for it on a known day. The core has internal deadlines months away and no weekly pressure, so in a busy household it loses every scheduling argument until it becomes an emergency.

The cost of that is larger than it looks. Up to three points sit in the combination of the two, and a low grade in either can create a failing condition that blocks the award of the diploma rather than merely reducing a total. So the downside is not one point; in the worst case it is the qualification. Against that, the intervention that prevents it is small and early: a session or two testing whether a research question can sustain four thousand words of argument, and whether the sources exist.

There is a second cost, in displacement. A core component deferred into the second year arrives in the same term as subject coursework, which means the student is writing three long pieces at once in the weeks when the syllabus is also finishing. That is how capable students end up with mediocre marks in four places rather than good marks in two.

The practical answer in a household on this corridor is to give the core a protected weekend hour from the first year, and to buy two or three sessions of coaching at the point the research question is being chosen rather than at the point a draft is late. That is both the cheapest and the highest-value money in the whole two-year budget.
bullets: Nothing chases the core weekly, so it gets deferred by default
A low core grade can block the diploma, not merely reduce it
Deferral displaces work into the busiest term of the second year
Two sessions at the question-choosing stage prevent most of it

sections.heading: What each price tier buys in a Diploma context
paragraphs: The tiers in this market mean something slightly different for a Diploma family than for an IGCSE one, because so much of the Diploma grade sits inside internally assessed work with published criteria.

At entry-level rates, advertised from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, a family is buying supervision and structure. For a student who is disorganised rather than behind, that has genuine value, and in a commuting household it can be the thing that gets homework finished. It cannot read a draft against criterion descriptors, because that requires somebody who has marked the component.

At qualified rates of roughly AED 150 to 300, the tutor knows the subject and can teach content properly. That is often enough at Standard Level in a well-supplied subject. At specialist rates from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, the tutor knows the component: the criteria, the mark allocations, the band boundaries, where students lose marks and why. For Higher Level coursework that is the tier the money is actually for.

One caution about the top of the market. Premium provision advertised as high as AED 650 an hour is sometimes presented as examiner-led. Examiner status for an individual is difficult for a parent to verify, and it should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. We do not describe tutors as examiners where we cannot evidence current status, and a family paying that premium is entitled to ask exactly what it buys.

Qualified rates are often sufficient at Standard Level
Specialist rates are for component and criteria work
Treat unverifiable examiner claims with scepticism

sections.heading: What the school owes you before any money changes hands
paragraphs: A page selling Diploma support should be clear about what the school already provides, because a family that collects it spends less and spends better. Three things are free and all three are routinely left on the table.

The Diploma coordinator holds the internal deadline calendar for the whole year. Ask for it in writing in the autumn of each year. On a commuting schedule that single document is worth several weeks of usable evenings, because it allows work to be moved into quieter weeks rather than colliding in one term. The coordinator also knows which Higher Level options actually ran in previous years, which matters if a budget was built around a subject that may not be staffed.

The subject teachers hold the marked work and the view that matters most: which two or three things they would prioritise if they had your child for an extra hour a week. Teachers answer that question well and are rarely asked it. For a coursework component, ask specifically which criterion the draft is weakest against, because that converts a vague worry into a targeted purchase.

And the university adviser holds the pattern of offers previous students in the school have actually received, which is better information than any general guidance about prerequisites. Collect all three before buying anything, and the eventual purchase is smaller, better aimed and easier to evaluate.

There is a fourth item for families who have recently moved school, which on this corridor is common. Ask the receiving school what mapping it did against your child's previous coverage. A vague answer is a reason to budget for a short mapping session of your own, because an unmapped transfer leaves gaps that surface in the second year when they are expensive.
bullets: Ask the coordinator for the internal deadline calendar, in writing
Ask which Higher Level options genuinely ran in past years
Ask subject teachers which criterion a draft is weakest against
Ask the university adviser what offers the school has seen

sections.heading: Permits, refunds and the claims to refuse
paragraphs: Before money moves, two regulatory questions are worth asking and one set of claims is worth refusing outright.

The permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, a page quoting an amount has invented it. The permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

The regulator. Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods; Dubai's answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. No tutoring provider, including IB Gram, holds approval, accreditation or a licence from either, and a KHDA educational services permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai.

The claims. Refuse any guarantee of a grade, a points total or a university place. Refuse any money-back promise tied to an outcome, because the terms are rarely published and never enforceable in the way a parent imagines. Refuse any school presented as a partner or client, any rating or satisfaction figure without the number, date and method behind it, and any offer to write, finish or complete an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay. That last one is academic malpractice, this region's market contains a provider selling it, and the consequence falls on your child rather than on the seller.

faqs.question: What does Diploma tutoring cost for a family in Al Khan?
faqs.answer: Using published market figures read in October 2026: qualified online subject tutors advertise from roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200; specialist IB tutors are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase at around AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision as high as AED 650. In-home visits including travel run from about AED 180 to 500. Those are other providers' rates. IB Gram quotes after a free trial, because component, level and scarcity all affect the figure.

faqs.question: How should we spread a Diploma tutoring budget across two years?
faqs.answer: Earlier than families do. The common pattern is nothing until the second year and then a burst in the spring, which is the most expensive way to buy the least: coursework marks are fixed by then, content teaching has no room to compound, and availability is tightest. A better distribution is a bridging block before the first year, one weekly session in the first spring, a coursework block in the second autumn, and a short triaged paper block in the second spring.

faqs.question: Where is a Diploma point cheapest to obtain?
faqs.answer: Usually near a boundary or in the core. A subject sitting one or two marks below a grade boundary can often gain a point from four to six sessions of paper technique. A core component heading for a low grade can be worth up to three points in combination and sometimes protects the diploma itself. The most expensive point is in the subject the student finds hardest, where content has to be rebuilt over a term — which is where most families spend first.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Diploma tutor to an apartment in Al Khan?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, with the draft or paper on a shared screen. In cost terms that removes the travel component that published in-home rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour include, and it removes the waste when an unpredictable afternoon shortens a visit.

faqs.question: Why is deferring the Extended Essay so costly?
faqs.answer: Because the downside is not one point. Up to three points sit in the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, and a low grade in either can create a failing condition that blocks the award of the diploma rather than merely reducing a total. Deferral also displaces the work into the busiest term of the second year, alongside subject coursework and the end of the syllabus. Two sessions at the point the research question is chosen prevent most of that, and they are cheap.

faqs.question: Is a qualified tutor enough, or do we need a specialist at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level in a well-supplied subject a qualified tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour is often sufficient, because the work is content and practice. At Higher Level with coursework, the marks sit inside internally assessed components with published criteria, and reading a draft against those descriptors reliably needs somebody who has marked the component. That is what the specialist band from AED 200 to AED 450 and above is for, and paying it for a motivation problem is waste.

faqs.question: Should we pay extra for a tutor advertised as an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Be careful. Premium provision in this market has been advertised as high as AED 650 an hour on the strength of examiner status, which a parent cannot easily verify and which should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. We do not describe tutors as examiners without current evidence. If you are paying that premium, ask precisely what it buys that a specialist at half the rate does not, and expect a specific answer.

faqs.question: What does the school owe us before we pay for anything?
faqs.answer: Three things, all free. The internal deadline calendar from the Diploma coordinator, in writing, at the start of each year — on a commuting schedule that is worth weeks of usable evenings. The subject teachers' answer to which two or three things they would prioritise, and for coursework which criterion a draft is weakest against. And the university adviser's account of the offers previous students have actually received, which beats general guidance about prerequisites.

faqs.question: Our DP2 child is struggling in three subjects. Should we fund all three?
faqs.answer: No. Spreading a limited number of sessions across three subjects in the spring of the second year reliably produces no visible movement in any of them. Fund the one or two nearest a grade boundary, or where a coursework band can still be lifted, and deliberately leave the third alone for the term. That advice is uncomfortable and it is what the points arithmetic supports. A provider who accepts all three without discussing priority is taking an order rather than planning.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package sensible for a Diploma family on this corridor?
faqs.answer: Only after marked work has been read, and only where a missed session is handled fairly. Advertised monthly plans in this market have included AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. On a corridor where afternoon arrivals are unpredictable, a plan assuming eight sessions a month will usually lose one or two. Ask what happens to a missed session, whether credit carries forward, and whether the arrangement can end at the midpoint.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a Diploma investigation without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary we state before the work begins. A tutor teaches the skill the component assesses, explains the published criteria and their command words, tests whether the topic carries enough depth, questions the student's reasoning and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor does not write any part of it, rewrite sentences or supply content for submission. This region's market includes a provider selling completed Internal Assessments, and that risk falls entirely on the student.

faqs.question: Does a Diploma tutor working with a Sharjah student need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and its code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

faqs.question: Are refund guarantees worth anything in this market?
faqs.answer: Treat them as a warning sign. A money-back promise tied to an outcome requires published, enforceable terms and a provider willing to honour them, and in practice the conditions are narrow enough that the promise functions as marketing. We do not offer one. What we do offer instead is a free trial lesson before any commitment, a scoped block with a stated finish date, and a midpoint review at which ending the arrangement is a legitimate outcome rather than a negotiation.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether the two-year spend worked?
faqs.answer: Component by component rather than in total. Each block should produce a specific deliverable: a coursework section lifted into a higher band against the same criteria, an extended-problem paper attempted with recovery from an early error, a research question narrowed into something answerable. Across two years the test is whether the student arrived at the final term with the core finished and two subjects secured, rather than whether the final grades matched a hope nobody could have guaranteed.

intro.heading: What a Diploma year actually looks like from Al Majaz, week by week
paragraphs: Al Majaz sits on Khalid Lagoon, between the Buhairah Corniche and Al Qasba, and most of its families live in towers rather than villas. That matters less than the calendar. A DP2 student in Al Majaz has roughly thirty teaching weeks between the start of the academic year and the moment the examination papers are sealed, and about eight of those weeks are already spoken for by mock examinations, internal assessment deadlines set by the school, Extended Essay checkpoints and the UAE public holidays that fall across the winter.

Parents search for an IB home tutor in Al Majaz because the alternative feels slow. The school has flagged a grade, the next report is six weeks away, and a tutor who comes to the apartment sounds like the fastest route. The honest position is that the travel is the slowest part of that plan. An in-home tutor crossing Al Wahda Street at four in the afternoon loses twenty-five to forty minutes each way, and a family pays for that time whether the invoice itemises it or not. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Al Majaz students are taught online, one-to-one, and the time that would have gone into the drive goes into the lesson.

The second reason the calendar beats the postcode is supply. Al Majaz is a dense residential district, not a tutoring market with depth in every Diploma subject. A parent looking for a Physics HL specialist who knows how Paper 3 behaves, or someone who has supervised more than a handful of Mathematics explorations, is not choosing from everybody with a teaching certificate in Sharjah. They are choosing from whoever is free at the right hour and lives close enough to drive. Online delivery removes the radius, and the radius was the only thing limiting the choice.

What we do with the calendar is simple and unusual. Before a block of lessons is agreed, the tutor writes down the dates that are fixed: the school's own internal assessment hand-in, the mock window, the Extended Essay reflection sessions, the final entry deadline the examinations officer is working to, and the examination window itself. Everything else is scheduled around those. If a student has eight weeks, the plan states what those eight weeks will cover and what they will not, because a plan that pretends to cover an entire Higher Level syllabus in eight weeks is a plan that quietly fails in week five.

The rest of this page is the calendar in detail: the Diploma year counted backwards, how a Sharjah school day leaves room for a session, what an eight-week block can realistically move, what tutoring costs in this market in dirhams, and where the line sits between coaching a student through an internal assessment and doing work that has to be theirs. None of it requires a tutor to park in Al Majaz.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-majaz.programmesIntro: Al Majaz families reach us at four different points in the IB continuum, and each one needs a different kind of help. A Primary Years child needs reading and number fluency; a DP2 student needs a triage plan. These are the four programmes we teach and what each one typically needs from Al Majaz.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units rather than subject textbooks, so a child can look fluent in class discussion and still be two years behind in written number work. Tutoring at this stage targets the skills the units assume: reading stamina, place value, written methods for multiplication and division, and the habit of showing a method rather than announcing an answer.
programmes.countryNote: Al Majaz children in PYP often come from households where English is a second or third language and Arabic is a school requirement under the federal rule that private schools teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies. Early sessions usually split between English comprehension and number fluency, with Arabic handled separately because the mandated class organisation differs for Arab and non-Arab learners.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP assessment runs on four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, and reported as a level from one to seven. Students lose levels for the things the criteria ask for and the classroom does not always drill: communicating in the right form, reflecting honestly on a method, and showing the inquiry rather than the conclusion. We teach to the criteria strands directly.
programmes.countryNote: MYP5 is the pressure point for Al Majaz families, because the step into DP1 is where a comfortable level 6 can turn into a struggling HL grade. We run a targeted MYP5 to DP bridge over the summer and the first term, concentrating on algebraic fluency, laboratory write-up conventions and the written style the Diploma expects from the first week.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The timetable is unforgiving: internal assessments for several subjects land in the same term, and the Extended Essay draft deadline rarely sits where a student expects. Tutoring here is scheduling as much as teaching, and the scheduling is what most families get wrong.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah Diploma candidates sit the May session, which means the real squeeze falls across the winter term when mocks, internal assessment deadlines and Extended Essay checkpoints collide. Al Majaz students on an evening schedule usually run two subjects at one session a week each from October, then drop to a single revision subject once mocks are returned.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP pairs DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Fewer UAE schools offer it, so students on the CP often find subject help harder to arrange than their Diploma classmates, particularly for the DP courses they take alongside the career study.
programmes.countryNote: Al Majaz students on a CP route most often need support in the two or three DP subjects they carry, plus the personal and professional skills component, where written reflection is marked and rarely taught explicitly. We teach the DP courses to the same standard as a full Diploma candidate and treat the reflective project as a supervised piece of the student's own work.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-majaz.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Al Majaz families ask for most, with the part of the course where marks actually go missing. Request lists in Sharjah skew towards the sciences and Mathematics, which is also where specialist supply is thinnest in any single neighbourhood.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marks go in the unseen algebra of Paper 1, where no calculator is allowed and a student who has learned procedures without fluency stalls. HL candidates also lose ground on proof and on the optional topic. We rebuild algebraic manipulation first, then work through past paper structure by question type.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI rewards modelling and penalises weak statistics. Students arrive confident with the graphic display calculator and vague about what a confidence interval or a chi-squared result actually claims. Sessions concentrate on interpreting output in words, since that is what the mark scheme credits.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The common failure is not mechanics but the data and uncertainty work that runs through every paper and the internal assessment. HL students also lose marks on Paper 3 practical questions, which ask about method rather than content. We drill uncertainty propagation and graph-gradient analysis to a fixed routine.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics take the blame; in practice most lost marks are in bonding and in explaining, rather than naming, a trend. Paper 2 extended response needs a structured answer, and we teach that structure explicitly using the command terms the syllabus defines.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology punishes imprecise language more than any other science. A student who writes about something getting bigger when the mark scheme wants surface-area-to-volume ratio loses the mark. We build subject vocabulary, then work through the statistical and data-based questions that carry the HL marks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the grade. Students draw a diagram, label it loosely, and then describe it instead of using it. We teach a fixed diagram routine, then the evaluation moves that lift a mid-band answer, and we coach the internal assessment commentaries as the student's own analysis.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The tools are easy to list and hard to apply to a case study under time pressure. HL students lose marks on the extension topics and on quantitative content they treat as optional. Sessions use unseen case material so application is practised rather than described.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 unseen analysis is where a capable reader can score poorly, because the task rewards a focused argument about how a text works rather than a summary of what it says. We work on thesis construction, close reading of non-literary texts, and the oral assessment structure.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Students who code well still lose marks on the written papers, where the questions test algorithms, data structures and systems concepts in prose. HL adds abstract data structures and the case study. We split sessions between written-paper technique and the practical solution development.

sections.heading: What parents in Al Majaz are actually asking for
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Majaz, read literally, is a Diploma or Middle Years subject teacher who works with one student in their own apartment. That service exists in Sharjah and in-home rates published by UAE providers run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour once travel is accounted for, against roughly AED 150 to AED 300 for the same qualification teaching online. The gap is not tutor quality. It is the car.

What the search usually means in practice is narrower: a parent wants one-to-one attention, at a time that fits the household, from somebody who knows the specific syllabus their child is sitting. Each of those three things is available online. Only the fourth, physical presence, requires a drive, and physical presence is the one element with no published evidence of a grade effect at Diploma level when the alternative is live video with a shared screen and a document camera.

So the answer we give Al Majaz families is direct. IB Gram does not run home visits in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE; that service exists only in our India operation. What an Al Majaz household gets instead is a specialist in the exact subject and level, usually within a few days, at an hour that suits a tower household on a school night, with the drive time converted into teaching time.
The rest of this page assumes you want the calendar answered rather than the sales pitch: which session your child is entered for, what has to happen before it, and how many weeks are actually left.
