sections.heading: The Diploma year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Nobody publishes this table, which is odd, because it is the single most useful thing a Diploma parent can see. Working forwards from today produces a plan that runs out of time. Working backwards from the session produces a plan that tells you which weeks are already gone.

The dates below are the structural milestones rather than published calendar dates. Your child's school sets its own internal deadlines, and those are the ones that bite first: a school internal assessment hand-in typically sits several weeks before the IB upload deadline, precisely so the coordinator has room to check and submit. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the school's dated internal calendar, and plan tutoring against that document rather than against the examination month.

One caution worth stating plainly. IB session and results dates in this project are not confirmed from the IB's own site, so we do not publish them. Secondary sources circulate windows and they are often close, but a date a parent acts on has to come from the coordinator or from ibo.org directly. What is safe to say is the shape: Sharjah schools sit the May session, results reach schools in early July, and the enquiry-upon-results window is short.

Cambridge and Pearson dates are a different matter, because both publish them. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and the February or March series is offered to India only, so a Sharjah candidate has two windows, not three. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

sections.heading: Where a Sharjah school day leaves room for a lesson
paragraphs: Al Majaz households run on a narrow evening. A Sharjah private school day typically finishes between 14:15 and 15:30, and the journey home for a child at one of the inland Muwaileh or University City schools takes twenty-five to forty minutes in afternoon traffic. Add a meal and the first realistic start for a secondary student is 16:30, and for a family whose child crosses into Dubai for school, closer to 18:00.

That leaves a usable window of roughly 16:30 to 21:30 on school nights, which is five slots a week per subject at most and realistically two. The arithmetic is why an in-home tutor's travel time is expensive in a way the hourly rate conceals: a tutor who can physically reach three Al Majaz homes in an evening has to charge for the hour and a half in the car, and the family furthest from where the tutor lives gets the last slot.

Online removes both constraints. A lesson begins at the agreed minute, the tutor is in the same session whether the student is in Al Majaz, Al Taawun or in a hotel room during a half-term trip, and a 20:30 start is as workable as a 16:30 one. During Ramadan the whole pattern moves: school hours shorten, and most families switch to post-Iftar sessions, which an in-home schedule across Sharjah traffic handles badly and a video schedule handles without comment.

We ask for the school's own term calendar at the start of a block, because the dates that break a tutoring plan are rarely the ones on the public calendar. Sports days, residential trips, inspection weeks and the week of internal examinations all remove sessions, and a plan that has not accounted for them simply runs short.

sections.heading: What eight weeks of tutoring can and cannot move
paragraphs: Parents in Al Majaz usually arrive with a horizon rather than a budget: eight weeks to mocks, six weeks to the examination window, a term to the next report. The useful question is not whether tutoring works but what a given number of weeks can carry, and the honest answer varies enormously by what the gap actually is.

A technique gap closes fast. A student who knows the Chemistry content but writes unstructured Paper 2 answers can gain marks in four weeks, because the fix is a routine rather than a body of knowledge. A content gap closes slowly: a DP2 student who has not understood the first term of Physics HL needs most of a term, and no amount of session frequency compresses that below the time it takes to build the underlying ideas.

The worst case, and the one we see most in exam term, is a diagnostic gap, where nobody including the student knows which of the two it is. That is what the trial lesson and the first two sessions are for. A tutor who starts teaching in lesson one without finding out where the floor is will spend the block at the wrong altitude, which is the single commonest way tutoring money disappears.

The table sets out what each block length realistically produces. It is deliberately conservative. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and nobody should offer to; what a plan can promise is a specific set of covered topics, a specific number of marked past papers and a written record of what changed.

sections.heading: Internal assessment deadlines are school deadlines first
paragraphs: The most common planning error in an Al Majaz Diploma household is treating the internal assessment as a single deadline rather than a sequence. Every Diploma subject carries internally assessed work, the school sets its own hand-in dates ahead of the IB's upload window, and those school dates arrive in clusters because the coordinator has to stagger the checking.

A DP2 student in Sharjah can face a Mathematics exploration, a science investigation, an Economics commentary and an Extended Essay draft inside the same six weeks of the winter term, on top of mock examinations. Each piece has published assessment criteria with named strands and a mark allocation, and the marks are lost in predictable places: a research question too broad to answer in the word limit, a method with no stated uncertainty, an analysis that describes a graph instead of interpreting it, and a conclusion that does not engage with the limitations the student has already listed.

Our supervision sessions work criterion by criterion on the student's own draft. The tutor reads what is there, states which strand is currently weak and why, and sets the next step. What the tutor never does is write, rewrite or edit the piece to completion. That is not a policy preference; under IB academic honesty rules it would expose the student to a malpractice finding, and a page that offers it is advertising a risk rather than a service.

The practical consequence for scheduling is that internal assessment support has to be booked early. A student who asks for help the week before the school hand-in gets proof-of-criteria feedback and nothing more, because there is no time left to collect better data or reframe a question. Booked eight weeks out, the same sessions shape the question, test the method, and leave room for a redraft the student does themselves.

sections.heading: What IB tutoring costs in the Sharjah market, in dirhams
paragraphs: Most pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars, which no Sharjah family transacts in. Here is the market in dirhams, attributed, so you can judge a quote against it. These are market rates from published UAE provider pricing, not an IB Gram price list; our own figure depends on subject, level and block length, and the trial lesson comes before any of it.

Read the bands from the bottom up rather than the top down, because that is the decision most Al Majaz families are actually making. At the lowest tier, a university student tutoring part time is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. That tier can work for Middle Years consolidation and almost never works for Higher Level content, because the tutor has not taught the course.

The middle band, roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour online, is where qualified subject teachers sit: Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that, published specialist rates for IB, IGCSE and A-Level run from AED 200 to AED 450 and higher, with TutorChase at AED 270 and named or examiner-led tutors quoted as high as AED 650 by BartyED. In-home visits carry their own band, roughly AED 180 to AED 500, and the top of that band is travel rather than teaching.

Monthly packages give a cleaner comparison for a household budget. Published UAE packages include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support.

sections.heading: SPEA, the regulator, and what it means for your tutoring plan
paragraphs: Sharjah private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority. The federal portal states that SPEA regulates private education in the emirate, and that Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone, and it is why a Sharjah school's assessment calendar can differ from a Dubai school's running the same programme.

The emirate matters for a tutoring plan in two concrete ways. First, a child who lives in Al Majaz but attends school across the boundary in Dubai is inside the KHDA's system for school matters, not SPEA's, and the two authorities publish different calendars and different inspection frameworks. Second, the mandatory UAE subjects sit on top of the international curriculum in both emirates, under the federal rule that private schools must teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies whatever curriculum they are licensed for.

On the tutor side, the relevant regulator is neither SPEA nor KHDA but the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform. It is not approved, accredited or licensed by SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and any tutoring page telling you otherwise is making a claim it cannot evidence. What we can tell you is which regulator governs your child's school, what the permit position is for a tutor, and where to check both for yourself.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The Sharjah search results for IB tutoring include at least one operator selling completed internal assessments. That is not a cheaper version of tutoring; it is a malpractice finding waiting to happen, and the consequence lands on the student rather than the seller. The IB treats work submitted as a student's own when it is not as academic misconduct, and the outcome can be the loss of the Diploma.

The line is clear enough to write down. A tutor may teach the content, explain the assessment criteria, question a research idea until it becomes answerable, read a draft and say which strand is weak, teach referencing conventions, and model how an argument is built using material that is not the student's assessment. A tutor may not supply the research question, write or rewrite any part of the submitted text, collect or generate the data, edit a draft to completion, or hand over a worked solution to be submitted.

We put it in writing at the start of an internal assessment or Extended Essay block, and we expect the student to keep their own record of drafts and reflection sessions. That record is also the student's protection: a supervisor who can see the development of the work from question to final draft has evidence of authorship, which matters more now that schools are checking for text a student did not write.

One more boundary worth naming. We do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to the boards. Tutors reference them, link the official page, and work from material the school has legitimately provided.

process.title: Tell us the dates, not just the subject
process.description: The first message that helps is the one with dates in it: year group, subjects and levels, the school's next assessment, the mock window and the session the student is entered for. That is enough to say honestly whether the time available matches the gap, before anybody is charged.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the specialist
process.description: The trial is a diagnostic, not a sales call. The tutor works through material at the student's current level, finds whether the gap is content, technique or confidence, and reports back in writing. If the fit is wrong, you see a different tutor rather than a discount.

process.title: A written plan counted backwards
process.description: Before a block is booked you get a plan listing the dates that are fixed, the topics each session covers, and what the block is expected to produce. It also states what the block will not cover, which is the part most plans leave out and the part that prevents an argument in week six.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a written record
process.description: Each session ends with a short note: what was covered, what was set, what still needs work. Across eight weeks that becomes a record a parent can read and a school can be shown, rather than a vague impression that things are improving.

process.title: Review against the plan, then decide
process.description: At the end of the block the tutor reports against the original plan rather than against a feeling. You decide whether to continue, change subject focus, or stop. Nothing rolls over automatically, and no block is extended without a conversation about what the next one is for.

whyPoints.title: The specialist, not the nearest available person
whyPoints.description: Matching by subject and level rather than by driving distance changes who is in the room. A Physics HL student in Al Majaz gets a Physics HL teacher instead of a general science tutor who happens to live four streets away, and the difference shows in the first lesson.

whyPoints.title: Plans built from the examination calendar
whyPoints.description: Sharjah IB candidates sit the May session, Cambridge candidates sit June and November, and Pearson candidates sit May/June and November. Every plan we write starts from the session the student is entered for and counts backwards, including the school's own internal deadlines.

whyPoints.title: Drive time becomes teaching time
whyPoints.description: An in-home tutor crossing Sharjah at four in the afternoon spends twenty-five to forty minutes each way, and that time is inside the price whether or not it appears on the invoice. Online lessons start at the agreed minute and the whole hour is taught.

whyPoints.title: An honest answer about availability
whyPoints.description: Some Diploma subjects have thin specialist supply in the UAE at particular hours. Where that applies we say so, name the alternative, and state whether the tutor is UAE-based before the trial rather than after. A coverage limit disclosed is a limit a family can plan around.

whyPoints.title: Clear boundaries on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge support is teaching, questioning and criterion-level feedback on the student's own work. We state that in writing at the start of a block, because the alternative puts a student's Diploma at risk.

whyPoints.title: Figures you can check
whyPoints.description: Market rates on this page are attributed to the provider that published them. Regulatory statements are attributed to the authority that issued them. Where a date is not confirmed, as with IB session dates, we say so instead of publishing a number that looks authoritative and is not.

faqs.question: Can we get an IB home tutor who visits our apartment in Al Majaz?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach UAE students one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we run only in India. In-home IB tutoring does exist in Sharjah through other providers, and published UAE rates for it run roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour once travel is included. What you lose by booking online is the physical presence; what you gain is a tutor chosen for knowing your child's exact subject and level rather than for living within driving distance of Al Majaz, plus a lesson that starts on the minute.

faqs.question: Which IB exam session do Sharjah students in Al Majaz sit?
faqs.answer: Sharjah IB Diploma candidates sit the May session, which is the main examination window for schools in the northern hemisphere. November exists as a smaller second session, used mainly by schools on a different academic year and by some retake candidates. We do not publish specific IB examination or results dates on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than none. Ask your school's Diploma coordinator for the dated internal calendar, which is the document your tutoring plan should actually follow.

faqs.question: How many weeks before mocks should we start IB tutoring in Al Majaz?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is the point where a block can do more than firefight. That gives one diagnostic session, six teaching sessions on specific weaknesses and one timed paper under conditions, which is enough to fix a technique fault and cover two or three weak topics in a single subject. Four weeks still helps if the problem is answer structure or timing rather than missing content. Less than three weeks before mocks, the honest use of tutoring is targeted past paper practice on the components where the student is closest to the next band.

faqs.question: Is a Diploma tutor in Al Majaz cheaper than one in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Online rates are the same, because the tutor's location stops mattering once the drive disappears. In-home rates do vary by district, and they vary with distance from where tutors live rather than with the postcode's reputation. A tower district like Al Majaz adds friction an invoice rarely itemises: visitor parking, lift waits and a tutor arriving ten minutes into a sixty-minute slot. Published UAE market rates for online qualified subject teachers run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, and that band holds across Sharjah and Dubai alike.

faqs.question: Our DP2 child has an IA and the Extended Essay due in the same month. What can a tutor do?
faqs.answer: Supervision sessions on each piece, scheduled so they do not collide, working criterion by criterion on what the student has already written. The tutor reads the draft, states which strand is weak and why, and sets the next step: narrow the research question, add an uncertainty treatment, interpret the graph rather than describe it. The writing and the data stay with the student, because IB academic honesty rules require it. Book this eight weeks out if you can; a week before the school hand-in there is no time left to collect better evidence.

faqs.question: Does Theory of Knowledge tutoring actually help, or is it unteachable?
faqs.answer: It is teachable, but not as content. Theory of Knowledge marks go to students who can hold a claim and a counterclaim in the same paragraph and show where the knowledge in question comes from. Most students lose marks by writing opinion essays with examples bolted on. Sessions work on the structure of a knowledge argument, on choosing examples that actually do work in the essay, and on the exhibition commentary format. The essay itself is the student's own, and a tutor who offers to draft it is offering a malpractice risk.

faqs.question: How late in the evening can lessons run for an Al Majaz student?
faqs.answer: We schedule up to about 21:30 on school nights, which matters in a district where a child attending an inland Sharjah school or a Dubai school may not be home and fed before 18:00. The practical window for secondary students in Al Majaz is 16:30 to 21:30, with the later slots in heavy demand during examination terms. During Ramadan most families move to post-Iftar sessions, and online delivery handles that shift without the scheduling problems an in-home tutor crossing Sharjah would face.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for a niche Higher Level subject at an Al Majaz family's usual slot?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than filling the slot with a generalist. Some Diploma subjects have thin specialist supply at particular hours, and the honest options are a different time slot with the right specialist, a tutor based outside the UAE teaching on Gulf Standard Time, or a wait. We tell you which applies, and whether the tutor is UAE-based, before the trial lesson rather than after the first invoice. A disclosed coverage limit is something a family can plan around; a concealed one is not.

faqs.question: Do private tutors working in Sharjah need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories include school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you are quoted with suspicion and check MoHRE's own service page.

faqs.question: Can a tutor follow our school's own assessment calendar rather than a generic plan?
faqs.answer: That is the plan we prefer to write. Send the school's dated internal calendar at the start of a block and the tutor builds around it: the internal assessment hand-in, the mock window, the Extended Essay reflection sessions, the week of internal examinations, the residential trip that removes a session. Generic plans fail in Sharjah because school calendars here differ by school and by emirate, and because SPEA approves assessment methods for schools inside the emirate while the KHDA framework applies across the boundary.

faqs.question: Which Diploma subjects do Al Majaz families ask about most?
faqs.answer: Mathematics at both Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, then Physics and Chemistry, then Economics and Business Management. The pattern follows university intentions: engineering and medicine routes drive the sciences and the Analysis course, while business and finance routes drive Economics and the Applications course. English A: Language and Literature appears less often than it should, given how many marks sit in the unseen Paper 1 analysis that students rarely practise under timed conditions.

faqs.question: Is one session a week enough for a Higher Level subject once Al Majaz school hours are counted in?
faqs.answer: For maintenance and technique, yes. For rebuilding a Higher Level subject from a weak DP1 foundation, one session a week across a single term is not enough, and a plan that claims otherwise is selling hope. The arithmetic is simple: twelve to fourteen sessions a term, against a two-year syllabus. Where the gap is large we recommend two sessions a week for a fixed block, then dropping to one once the foundation is secure, rather than spreading thin coverage across two subjects at the same time.

faqs.question: How do we know the trial lesson was useful rather than just pleasant?
faqs.answer: A useful trial produces a written diagnosis: which topics the student can handle, where the floor is, whether the problem is content, technique or confidence, and what the first four sessions would therefore cover. If the report back is a general impression that your child is capable and needs confidence, ask for specifics. A tutor who has actually diagnosed something can name the topic and the mark scheme behaviour that is costing marks, and can say what the next session will do about it.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor cover two Diploma subjects for one student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is usually worth checking. Mathematics with Physics, or Chemistry with Biology, are pairings a single specialist can often carry well. Mathematics with Economics is possible. Physics with English A is not a pairing we would arrange, because a tutor strong in both to Higher Level standard is rare enough that one of the two subjects would be taught at the wrong depth. Where a pairing does not work we match two tutors and coordinate the schedule so the student's evenings stay workable.

faqs.question: What should an Al Majaz parent ask before paying for a block of lessons?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which exact syllabus and level does the tutor teach, and when did they last teach it? What will the block cover, and what will it not cover? What record will we receive after each session? And do they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? Any provider who cannot answer those without hesitation is selling access rather than teaching. Ask for the written plan before the first payment, and check that the dates in it match your school's calendar rather than a generic one.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-majaz.closingHeading: Start with the dates, then the tutor
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-majaz.closingBody: If your child is in DP1 or DP2 at a school in or near Al Majaz, the useful first step is not a price list. Send the year group, the subjects and levels, and the dates that are already fixed: the next school assessment, the mock window, the internal assessment hand-in. We will tell you honestly whether the weeks available match the gap, arrange a free trial lesson with a specialist in that exact subject, and put a written plan in front of you before anything is booked. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and no tutor is sent to a UAE address.

intro.heading: What a subject specialist knows that a general tutor does not
paragraphs: A general tutor knows the subject. A subject specialist knows the assessment. That distinction sounds like marketing until you watch it in practice: the specialist can tell a student that Paper 3 carries a specific share of the Higher Level grade, that criterion C in the Extended Essay rubric holds more marks than any other criterion, and that the command term suggest obliges a different answer from explain. Those are the things that convert understanding into points, and they are not in the textbook.

Al Mamsha is a walkable mixed-use district in Sharjah near Muwaileh and University City, which means students here are close to schools and no closer than anybody else to a Higher Level examiner. The number of people in the emirate who have taught Higher Level Chemistry through two full assessment cycles is small, and they are not concentrated in any one development. So the useful question is not who is nearby but who knows this subject's assessment at this level.

IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE. Home tuition is a service we offer only in India, and for Sharjah families every lesson is live, one-to-one, over video, in a slot held in Gulf Standard Time. The reason that works for subject-level teaching is simple: what a specialist session actually consists of is a question attempted, a mark scheme opened and an answer corrected line by line, none of which needs anyone in the room.

This page is therefore built around assessment detail rather than reassurance. There is a table of paper structures and weightings at both levels, a table of the internal assessment criterion letters with their mark allocations, a table of command terms and what each one obliges, and a worked account of where marks are lost subject by subject. Check every rubric figure against your school's current copy of the subject guide, because the IB revises guides and a page cannot be the authority on that.

One honest caveat before the detail. We do not publish IB session or results dates anywhere on this site, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a confidently wrong date on a page a parent plans around is worse than none. UAE schools sit the May session. Ask your school's IB coordinator for the specifics, and for the internal deadline schedule, which is what actually governs a Diploma year. The same caution applies to every rubric figure quoted below: it is the published allocation as we understand it, it belongs to a particular version of a subject guide, and the habit of checking it in your school's own copy is worth more to your child than the number itself. Read the rubric, count the marks, and spend the time in proportion to where they sit.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mamsha.programmesIntro: Three programmes and one core, each assessed on a different model. Al Mamsha families arrive at all four, and the subject-level work looks genuinely different in each.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, each assessed by external papers and an internal assessment, plus the three core components, totalling 45 points. Grades run 1 to 7 per subject with up to three bonus points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination.
programmes.countryNote: For a Sharjah student the practical consequence is that no two subjects should be revised the same way. The internal assessment weighting differs by subject, the paper structures differ, and a student who spreads effort evenly across six subjects is over-investing in the ones where the marks are already secure and under-investing in the paper that will decide a grade.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of 8, converted to a 1 to 7 grade by published boundaries. The criteria are the whole assessment: a strong piece of work that does not address a criterion strand scores in the middle band regardless of quality.
programmes.countryNote: Most MYP tutoring in Sharjah should begin with reading the criterion descriptors aloud with the student. They are written in a particular register, they draw sharp distinctions between adjacent bands, and students who have never been shown the difference between the top two bands cannot aim at it. This is a two-session intervention with a disproportionate effect.

programmes.name: Extended Essay, TOK and CAS
programmes.description: The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent research piece assessed against five criteria. Theory of Knowledge is assessed by a prescribed-title essay and an exhibition of three objects. Together they contribute up to three bonus points, and badly handled they remove them.
programmes.countryNote: The core is where Sharjah students most often lose points to process rather than ability. The Extended Essay rubric rewards a narrow, answerable research question and sustained critical thinking, and penalises a broad topic however well written. Fixing a research question costs one session in July and cannot be fixed at all in February.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led with no external examinations, assessed through units of inquiry and the Year 6 exhibition. Support here is about numeracy fluency, reading stamina and the working habits that later assessment will assume rather than teach.
programmes.countryNote: Al Mamsha families with primary children have the easiest scheduling position in the district, because primary release is earlier and homework is light. It is also the stage where the budget market band is genuinely adequate, and we will say so rather than talking a family upwards into a specialist they do not need yet.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-mamsha.subjectsIntro: Each note below names the component where marks are actually lost at Higher Level, because that is where a specialist session should start rather than at the beginning of the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Marks go to unjustified steps and to algebraic slips under time pressure, not to misunderstanding. At Higher Level the proof questions reward a rehearsed structure. The exploration carries real weight and is routinely written in a rush in the final fortnight.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The calculator is examinable: students lose marks for procedures they understand but have not drilled. Modelling questions reward a fixed sequence of define, fit, test and interpret, which can be taught as a habit in two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The written-explanation questions are the loss point. A correct idea phrased loosely earns nothing where the mark scheme names a mechanism. Paper 3 rewards experimental reasoning, and the internal assessment rewards one tightly controlled variable over an ambitious design.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level failure rate because they are cumulative. Data questions require uncertainty to be propagated rather than mentioned, which is a specific, teachable technique worth two sessions on its own.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Marks are tied to exact terminology more tightly than in any other science: a loosely correct answer scores zero where the mark scheme names a term. Data-analysis questions catch students who revised content and skipped skills entirely.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy under time pressure decides a large share of the marks, and the evaluation command terms decide most of the rest. The internally assessed commentaries need theory applied to a real published article rather than the article summarised.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the named organisation separates a 5 from a 7 and is a rehearsable habit rather than a talent. The quantitative tools are examinable, mechanical and the most reliably neglected marks in the subject.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen analysis and improves measurably with one marked timed response a week. Strong bilingual Sharjah students plateau on analytical technique rather than language: commenting on effect instead of restating content.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies must function as evidence rather than be recounted, and the command terms draw sharp lines between describe, explain and evaluate. The internal assessment is a replication with strict reporting conventions that become easy marks once learned.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by a prescribed-title essay and an exhibition. The common failure is an essay that describes knowledge rather than arguing about it, which is a structural problem and therefore unusually responsive to a short block of coaching.

sections.heading: Paper structures and weightings at both levels
paragraphs: Revision planned without knowing the weightings is revision planned badly. A student who spends equal time on every component is over-investing in the small ones, and in most Diploma subjects the components are not remotely equal. The table below sets out the general structure at Standard and Higher Level for the subjects Sharjah families ask about most, and it is the first thing a specialist session should establish.

The pattern worth noticing is that Higher Level is not simply more content. In most subjects it adds a component, extends an existing paper or increases the depth demanded in the same paper, which means Higher Level revision has a different shape rather than a longer one. A student moving from Standard to Higher Level mid-course has a new component to learn, not just more pages.

The internal assessment column is the one families consistently underestimate. In several subjects it carries a share of the grade comparable to a whole paper, and unlike a paper it can be worked on calmly months in advance. A student who leaves it to the final fortnight has chosen to do the most recoverable part of the assessment under the worst possible conditions.

Check every figure against your school's current copy of the subject guide. The IB revises guides and component weightings change between guide versions, so a page cannot be the authority on this, and any provider who presents weightings as fixed for all time is telling you they have not looked recently.

sections.heading: The criterion letters, and where the marks actually sit
paragraphs: This is the gap nobody fills in this market. Every internal assessment is marked against lettered criteria with published mark allocations, and almost no page written for UAE parents names a single one. Yet the criterion letters are the whole assessment: a student who does not know that one criterion carries twice the marks of another cannot allocate their effort sensibly, and most do not know.

The science investigation is the clearest case. It is marked out of 24 across four criteria, each carrying an equal share: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The practical consequence is that a beautiful set of results with a weak evaluation loses a quarter of the available marks, and evaluation is the section students write last and fastest. Reversing that order is worth several marks for no extra work.

The Extended Essay rubric runs to 34 marks across five criteria, and critical thinking carries 12 of them, more than any other criterion and more than focus and method and knowledge and understanding combined. That single fact changes how an essay should be written, and students who learn it in July write a different essay from those who learn it in February. The Mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria, with use of mathematics the largest.

Verify these allocations against your school's current subject guide. The IB revises rubrics between guide versions and the numbers here are the published allocations as we understand them rather than a permanent fact. The habit we are arguing for matters more than any specific number: read the rubric, count the marks, and spend time in proportion.

sections.heading: Command terms are contractual
paragraphs: The IB publishes a list of command terms and defines each one, and the mark schemes apply those definitions strictly. A question that says suggest will accept a reasoned possibility; a question that says explain will not accept one. A student who answers every question with everything they know scores the marks for the question they were asked and nothing for the rest, which is why able students can sit in the middle of the mark range.

This is the fastest intervention available in subject tutoring, and it is almost entirely mechanical. Take six past-paper questions on the same topic with six different command terms, answer each one, and compare against the mark schemes. Most students see immediately that they have been writing the same answer to different questions, and the habit changes within two or three sessions.

The table below sets out the terms that cause most trouble in Sharjah classrooms and what each one obliges. The distinctions are not stylistic: the mark scheme awards credit for the specific operation named, and a student who describes when asked to evaluate has not produced a weaker answer but a different and unmarkable one.

Check the current definitions in the subject guide your school uses, because the glossary belongs to the guide and the IB revises guides. The point for a parent is narrower than the detail: ask the tutor in the trial lesson to explain the difference between two command terms in your child's subject. If they can do it crisply, they know the assessment. If they talk about confidence instead, they do not.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, subject by subject
paragraphs: In Physics the loss is concentrated in written explanation. A student can calculate competently and still lose six marks a paper by describing a mechanism loosely where the mark scheme names a specific chain of cause and effect. The fix is to collect the standard explanations from mark schemes and learn the phrasing until it is automatic, which feels mechanical because it is.

In Chemistry the loss is cumulative. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms each depend on the one before, so a gap in the first term of Higher Level produces failures in the third. Data questions demand that uncertainty be propagated rather than mentioned, and that single technique is worth two sessions on its own because it appears in every data-based question on every paper.

In Biology the loss is terminological. The mark scheme frequently names the exact word, and a loosely correct answer earns nothing. Students revise from notes written in their own words and then write those words in the examination. The correction is to revise from mark schemes rather than from notes, which is unglamorous and reliably effective.

In Economics and Business Management the loss is in application. A student who defines every term and then writes a textbook answer about a generic firm has produced work that cannot score in the top bands, because the assessment rewards engagement with the specific case or article in front of them. That is a rehearsable structure rather than an insight, and it moves grades inside a term.
bullets: Physics: learn the standard explanations from mark schemes, verbatim

sections.heading: How to use past papers so they do something
paragraphs: Most past-paper work is wasted, and it is wasted in a predictable way. A student does a paper, checks the answers, feels reassured or discouraged, and moves on. Nothing has been learned, because the information in a past paper is not whether the student got it right but exactly which operation they failed to perform, and that only becomes visible when the mark scheme is read line by line against their own words.

The session structure that works has three parts. Attempt cold and timed, because an untimed attempt measures knowledge rather than performance. Correct against the mark scheme with the tutor, phrase by phrase, identifying what the mark scheme wanted and what the student wrote instead. Then redo the same question type from scratch, in the same session or the next one, which is the step almost everyone skips and the step that builds the habit.

Papers should also be chosen rather than worked through in order. A student losing marks on data analysis should do the data-analysis questions from six papers rather than six whole papers, because that concentrates the correction on the failing operation. Whole papers belong in the last fortnight, when the thing being practised is stamina and pacing rather than any single skill.

We do not supply official past papers or mark schemes as downloads, and no provider should. Those are IB, Cambridge and Pearson materials and reproducing them is a copyright matter. We reference them, teach from them in session, and point to the official source so that you can obtain them through your school in the normal way.

sections.heading: What subject-level expertise costs in this market
paragraphs: Specialist knowledge is priced accordingly and it is worth knowing where the bands sit before you negotiate. Read in October 2026, a qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. An IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more.

Below that, the budget band of roughly AED 33 to 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, is supplied largely by university students, and University City is next door to Al Mamsha. For Middle Years criteria work and primary support that is often the right purchase and we will say so. For Higher Level criterion-level feedback on an internal assessment it is not, and no amount of enthusiasm substitutes for having marked the thing before.

At the top, premium named or examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. Our view is that this is rarely justified, principally because examiner status is extremely hard for a parent to verify and should not be used to imply any access to marking or boundaries. We do not describe our tutors as examiners, because we would not be able to evidence it for every individual.

In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to 500 with independent tutors. For the kind of work described on this page the travel premium buys nothing: a question attempted, a mark scheme opened and an answer corrected works identically on a shared screen. Every figure here is published by the provider named; none is an IB Gram price, and for ours you should take the free trial and ask.

sections.heading: Criterion-level help and the line that cannot move
paragraphs: Everything on this page points towards close work on a student's own draft, which makes the integrity boundary more important rather than less. This market contains providers who sell completed internal assessments; one page in this research advertises finished work at AED 3,750. The closer a tutor works to the rubric, the more clearly that line has to be drawn, so here it is.

A tutor may read the rubric with the student, explain what each criterion rewards and what the next band requires, discuss and sharpen a research question or a choice of variable the student proposed, model structure using a different example, read the draft the student wrote and say where each criterion is currently scoring and why, and teach referencing, data handling and uncertainty properly.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, complete or edit the work to a finished state, and may not produce a worked version of the student's own question or investigation. Criterion-level feedback on the student's own words is legitimate and valuable. Supplying the words is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student's whole diploma rather than one component.

Two further boundaries. We do not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link the official source. And ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, with the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also barring service to students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat that wording as press-reported and verify it; we will not arrange it regardless.

sections.heading: Starting with the assessment rather than the subject
paragraphs: Collect three documents before you contact anybody. The subject guide your school uses, or at least its name and year. One recent marked paper. And the internal assessment draft with the teacher's comments on it, if one exists. Those three let a specialist say something specific in the first hour instead of spending it establishing where the student is.

Then ask the tutor one question in the trial lesson: explain the difference between two command terms in this subject, or tell me which criterion in this internal assessment carries the most marks. A specialist answers immediately. A general tutor talks about confidence and rapport. That single question sorts the market faster than any credential check, and it costs you nothing to ask.

Expect the first session to produce a written list rather than a feeling. The specific marks being lost, named by component and by operation: explanation phrasing in Paper 2, uncertainty in data questions, evaluation in the investigation. Everything after that aims at the list, and the list is also how you judge whether the arrangement is working.

Then review at four weeks against it. Items should be disappearing. If the list is unchanged after four weeks the diagnosis was wrong, and we change the plan or the specialist rather than defending the first choice. Ask any provider you are considering what their version of that answer is, and notice whether they have one ready. A serious provider has thought about it before you asked, because it is the obvious question and the honest answer costs them nothing.

A marked script tells a specialist in two minutes what a description takes twenty to convey, and it is the difference between a first session that teaches and one that investigates.

Not one competitor page in this research names a single criterion, which is why most students cannot allocate effort sensibly.

whyPoints.title: One tutor, one subject, one level
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level Physics specialist and a Standard Level Economics specialist are different people. Matching by year group or by availability is how a family ends up with a competent generalist who does not know which paper decides the grade.

whyPoints.title: Mark schemes, not reassurance
whyPoints.description: Sessions consist of a timed attempt, a line-by-line correction against the published mark scheme and a redo of the same question type. The redo is the part everyone skips and the part that converts understanding into a habit that survives exam pressure.

whyPoints.title: We tell you when a cheaper band is right
whyPoints.description: For Middle Years criteria work and primary support, the budget band next door in University City is often the correct purchase and we say so. A provider who recommends their most expensive option for every problem is describing their pricing, not your child.

whyPoints.description: We do not describe tutors as IB or Cambridge examiners, because examiner status is hard to verify for every individual and must never be used to imply access to marking or boundaries. Competitors in this market use the word freely and should be asked for evidence.

whyPoints.title: Rubrics cited, not asserted as permanent
whyPoints.description: Every mark allocation here comes with an instruction to check your school's current subject guide, because the IB revises guides. A page that presents weightings as fixed facts is a page that has not looked at a guide recently.

faqs.question: Which criterion carries the most marks in the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Critical thinking, and by a wide margin. The Extended Essay rubric runs to 34 marks across five criteria, and critical thinking accounts for 12 of them, more than focus and method and knowledge and understanding combined. That changes how the essay should be written: a narrow, genuinely arguable research question supports critical thinking, while a broad topic however well written cannot. Check the allocation against your school's current copy of the guide, because the IB revises rubrics, and then plan the essay around that criterion rather than around the word count.

faqs.question: How is an IB science internal assessment marked?
faqs.answer: Out of 24, across four criteria carrying equal weight: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The practical consequence is the useful part. Evaluation is the section students write last and fastest, and it carries a quarter of the available marks, so reversing the order of effort gains marks for no additional work. A tightly controlled single variable also scores better than an ambitious design that produces messy data. Confirm the current allocations against the subject guide your school uses.

faqs.question: Does my child really lose marks for the wrong command term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the largest recoverable losses in the Diploma. The IB publishes command-term definitions and mark schemes apply them strictly: a question that says suggest will credit a reasoned possibility, while explain will not accept one and requires a causal mechanism. A student who writes everything they know scores for the question asked and nothing for the rest. Six past-paper questions on one topic with six different command terms, compared against the mark schemes, usually fixes the habit in two or three sessions.

faqs.question: What makes a Higher Level specialist different from a good subject teacher?
faqs.answer: Knowledge of the assessment rather than the subject. A specialist can tell you which component carries what share of the grade, which criterion letter holds the most marks in the internal assessment, and what the mark scheme accepts as an explanation in that subject. Test it directly in a trial lesson: ask them which criterion in your child's internal assessment carries the largest share, or to distinguish two command terms. A crisp answer tells you one thing, and talk about confidence and rapport tells you another.

faqs.question: How should past papers be used in a session?
faqs.answer: Three parts, and the third is the one everybody skips. Attempt cold and timed, because an untimed attempt measures knowledge rather than performance. Correct against the mark scheme with the tutor, phrase by phrase, identifying what the scheme wanted against what the student wrote. Then redo the same question type from scratch, which is what converts the correction into a habit. Choose questions by failing skill rather than working through whole papers, and save whole papers for the final fortnight when the thing being practised is pacing.

faqs.question: Can you give us official IB past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and nobody should. Those are IB materials and reproducing or distributing them is a copyright matter rather than a grey area, which also applies to syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables. We reference them, teach from them within a session and point to the official source so you can obtain them through your school in the normal way. If a provider offers you a bundle of official papers and mark schemes to keep, that tells you something about what else they treat as negotiable.

faqs.question: My child understands Chemistry but keeps losing marks. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With a marked paper rather than with the syllabus. In Higher Level Chemistry the recurring losses are concentrated in two places: uncertainty handled as a mention rather than propagated through a calculation, and cumulative gaps where energetics or equilibrium were never secure and now break the organic mechanisms. Uncertainty alone is worth two sessions, because it appears in every data-based question on every paper. A trial lesson on a marked script will tell you which of those two you have inside an hour.

faqs.question: Is Biology really about terminology?
faqs.answer: To a greater extent than any other science, yes. Biology mark schemes frequently name the exact term required, and an answer that is loosely correct earns nothing. The mechanism behind most Biology underperformance is that students revise from notes written in their own words and then reproduce those words under examination conditions. The correction is to revise from mark schemes rather than notes, learning the phrasing the scheme uses. It is unglamorous, it feels like rote learning, and it reliably moves grades.

faqs.question: How much does a Higher Level specialist cost in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Published rates read in October 2026 put an IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table in the same range. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200, and Bestimate's monthly estimate for specialist examination-year support is AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. Those are the providers' own figures. For ours, take the free trial lesson and ask against the specific subject and level.

faqs.question: Is the budget band ever adequate for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: For Middle Years criteria work and primary support, frequently yes, and University City next to Al Mamsha supplies a lot of it at roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour. For Higher Level criterion-level feedback on an internal assessment, no. Reading a rubric band descriptor against a student's own draft and saying precisely what the next band requires is a skill acquired by having marked the thing before, and enthusiasm does not substitute for it. We will tell you which of the two situations you are in.

faqs.question: What is the fastest improvement available in a Diploma subject?
faqs.answer: Command-term discipline, almost always, because it is mechanical and affects every paper in every subject. After that, in the sciences, learning the standard explanations verbatim from mark schemes, and handling uncertainty properly in data questions. In Economics and Business Management, applying theory to the specific case rather than writing a textbook answer about a generic firm. None of those require new content. All of them are habits, and habits change in weeks rather than terms.

faqs.question: How do we fix a weak Extended Essay research question?
faqs.answer: Early, in one session, and not at all once drafting is advanced. The rubric rewards critical thinking above everything else, and critical thinking requires a question narrow enough to argue about and open enough to have more than one defensible answer. A question that is really a topic produces a descriptive essay that cannot score in the upper bands however carefully it is written. A session in July on the question itself is the single highest-return hour in the whole Extended Essay process.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my child's internal assessment draft?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read it against the criterion letters and tell you where each criterion is currently scoring and what the next band requires, in writing, which is close to the most useful thing available. What they cannot do is write, rewrite, complete or edit it to a finished state, or produce a worked version of your child's own investigation. Criterion-level feedback on the student's own words is legitimate. Supplying the words is malpractice, and the risk falls on the entire diploma rather than one component.

faqs.question: Do you use tutors who are IB examiners?
faqs.answer: We do not describe tutors that way, deliberately. Examiner status is difficult to evidence for every individual, it changes from session to session, and it must never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. Several providers in this market use the word freely and should be asked to evidence it. What we do claim is specific and checkable: how many full assessment cycles a tutor has taught of a named subject at a named level. Ask us that question, and ask it of everyone else.

faqs.question: Which is harder, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: They are differently hard and the real question is which one the universities your child is considering expect. Analysis and Approaches is algebra-heavy with proof at Higher Level and is the route most engineering, mathematics and physics courses assume. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with the calculator genuinely examinable, and suits many economics, business and social-science routes. Choosing for comfort rather than for requirements is the error, and it is expensive because a mid-course change is close to impossible.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nahda-sharja.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below teaches a named Diploma subject at a named level and works to a fixed weekly slot. For a household on this corridor the fixed slot matters as much as the subject match, because a session that moves every week is a session that eventually stops happening.

intro.heading: The hour between the bus and the homework
paragraphs: Al Nahda in Sharjah is a wall of residential towers pressed against the Dubai boundary, with the Dubai district of the same name and Al Qusais immediately on the other side. It is one of the densest residential areas in the country and one of the most heavily commuted. Children living here attend schools in both emirates, and the single fact that shapes every tutoring conversation in this neighbourhood is what time they get home.

The answer is later than most providers assume. A child leaving a Dubai school in the early afternoon and travelling by bus across the boundary is frequently not through the door before half past four, and on a poor afternoon not before five. By the time the uniform is off and something has been eaten, the usable part of the evening starts at around half past five and competes directly with homework, Creativity, Activity, Service commitments and a coursework deadline nobody chases weekly.

This matters more for a Diploma student than for anybody else in the house. Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and internally assessed work inside every subject. The Diploma is not a programme that can be run on an hour of leftover attention, and the students who come unstuck in the second year are rarely the least able ones. They are the ones whose week never had a shape.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. On this corridor that is a direct answer to the timing problem rather than a general claim about convenience. A session can be set at half past five or six, it does not lose its first ten minutes to somebody arriving, and two children who get home forty minutes apart can both be taught on the same evening.

This page is therefore built around the school run rather than around the subject. Which schools this district actually feeds and when their days end. Where a Diploma week can realistically fit. Why the four-to-six window is the most contested hour in the country and what to do instead. How the Ramadan period and the Sharjah four-day working week change the available days. And how to sequence the second Diploma year so that the coursework does not land in the same fortnight as everything else.

On dates: we publish no International Baccalaureate examination or results dates on these pages, because the board's own site cannot be verified by automated checking and a wrong date is something a parent acts on. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, and your school's coordinator holds the internal calendar that actually governs the year.

A short block here, placed in the summer when the bus is not running, is the cheapest useful support in the whole programme.

programmes.description: Content at pace in six subjects while the core begins. The highest-value work is foundational: a research question that can carry the Extended Essay, an investigation with enough depth, and a weekly routine that survives a long commute. Nothing here is urgent, which is exactly why it is affordable.
programmes.countryNote: A DP1 student on this corridor has roughly two usable weekday evenings a week once the commute, sport and homework are accounted for. Deciding in advance which evening carries the hardest subject is more valuable than adding a session.

The work becomes triage and sequencing: clear coursework first, protect the subjects nearest a grade boundary, and deliberately leave something alone.
programmes.countryNote: Ask for the school's published internal deadline calendar in the autumn of the second year. On a commuting schedule the difference between knowing those dates in September and discovering them in January is several weeks of usable evenings.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Up to three points, their own failing conditions, and no weekly homework pressure to keep them moving. That last feature is why they get deferred, and why they so often collide with subject coursework in a single term.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nahda-sharja.subjectsIntro: Diploma requests from this district cluster in the sciences and mathematics, with English and Business behind them. Each entry names the component that generates the request.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 sat without a calculator, with a third paper at Higher Level worth twenty per cent. The Exploration carries another twenty, marked out of twenty across five criteria. Most losses are unclaimed method credit rather than misunderstood content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator permitted throughout, with heavier statistics and modelling. Marks are lost by producing a figure and not interpreting it in context, which is precisely what the scheme asks for, and by slow calculator technique under time pressure.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Papers plus the scientific investigation, marked across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Evaluation is lost most reliably, because limitations get listed without their effect on the conclusion being explained.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty and error analysis are the recurring loss point, and many paper questions are mathematics problems in physical clothing. A student weak in algebraic rearrangement will read as weak in physics.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heaviest content load of the sciences and the subject most sensitive to command terms. An analysis question answered with a description earns nothing, which is a training issue rather than a knowledge one.

sections.heading: What the school run actually looks like from these towers
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Nahda, Sharjah, as families here use the phrase, is a Diploma subject specialist working one-to-one with one student. IB Gram provides that over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. The reason this page spends its first pages on buses rather than on subjects is that in this district the bus is the binding constraint and the subject is not.

The pattern is consistent across the households we speak to. School finishes in the early afternoon. The bus leaves, collects, and crosses the boundary at the hour when the road is at its worst. Arrival is somewhere between half past four and five, occasionally later. Then there is a transition period that no schedule accounts for and every parent recognises: changing, eating, decompressing. Serious work starts at about half past five, and on a bad day it does not start at all.

A tutoring plan that ignores that will fail, and it will fail in a specific way. The four o'clock session gets booked because it is offered, missed twice, rescheduled, missed again, and then the family concludes that their child does not respond to tutoring. The child responded perfectly well; the hour did not exist.

The fix costs nothing and takes a week. Record the time your child actually walks through the door on three ordinary weekdays. Take the latest of those three times and add fifteen minutes. Book that. In these towers the number usually lands between half past five and six, which is later than any provider's standard slot and the only slot with a realistic chance of running every week for a term.
bullets: Measure arrival on three ordinary weekdays, not a good one
Add fifteen minutes for changing and eating, then book that
A four o'clock slot in these towers is a slot that will be missed
A session that moves weekly eventually stops happening

sections.heading: Which schools this district feeds, and when the day ends
paragraphs: Al Nahda in Sharjah does not have a single catchment. Children from the same tower attend schools in two emirates on three or four different curricula, and their days end at different times. For a family planning a Diploma week, the useful information is not the school's finishing time but the time its bus reaches this district, and those two numbers can be ninety minutes apart.

Broadly there are three patterns. Children at Sharjah schools within the emirate are home earliest, often by four o'clock, which gives them a genuine early-evening slot. Children at Dubai schools in Al Qusais, Mirdif and the surrounding districts are home between half past four and five on a normal day. Children travelling further into Dubai for a particular Diploma cohort can be considerably later, and for those households the weekend is not an option but the plan.

The second thing worth establishing is the school's own weekly rhythm. Diploma students carry Creativity, Activity, Service commitments, and schools place them differently: some after school on fixed days, some at weekends. A tutoring slot that collides with a fixed activity will lose, because the activity is a programme requirement and the session is not.

The table below is the version to fill in with your own school's numbers. It is written as a planning instrument rather than as a claim about particular schools, because bus times vary by route, by year and by how many stops a route carries.

sections.heading: Fitting a Diploma week around the bus
paragraphs: Six subjects, three core components and roughly two usable weekday evenings. That is the arithmetic a Diploma student in these towers is working with, and it explains why so many of them are behind without being weak.

The response that works is to stop treating the week as undifferentiated and assign each slot a job. One weekday evening carries the hardest current subject. The second carries whatever has a deadline inside the next fortnight. A weekend morning carries the core, which otherwise never gets written because nothing chases it. And one evening is deliberately empty, because a week with no slack produces a student who abandons the plan rather than adjusts it.

That allocation is more valuable than an extra session, and it is free. What a tutor adds on top is marked work between sessions and a diagnosis that narrows the effort: a student who knows that evaluation is costing them marks in two science subjects has a target, while a student who has been told to revise more has a mood.

The one thing to resist is buying hours to solve a time problem. Two sessions a week in a household where the student gets home at five does not double the teaching; it halves the independent practice, which is where the learning is consolidated. Where two subjects genuinely need support, the better answer on this corridor is usually one weekday session and one weekend session rather than two weekday evenings.
bullets: Give each available slot a specific job, in advance
Put the core on a weekend hour or it will not happen
Keep one evening deliberately empty as slack
Adding hours to a time problem removes practice, not pressure

sections.heading: The most contested hour in the country
paragraphs: Between four and six in the afternoon, every tutor, every tuition centre and every after-school activity in the northern emirates is competing for the same two hours, and so is every family. That is why the slot a parent most wants is the slot least likely to be available with the right specialist, and why flexibility on timing is the single biggest lever a family here controls.

The consequence is worth spelling out. A household that insists on a weekday session between four and six is choosing from whoever is free in the narrowest window of the week. A household willing to take half past six, or a weekend morning, is choosing from a far larger pool and frequently at the lower end of the specialist rate band. For a scarce Higher Level subject that difference can decide whether a match exists at all.

There is a quality argument as well as an availability one. A Diploma student who has spent ninety minutes on a bus is not at their best at half past four, whatever the timetable says. The same student on a Saturday morning is a different learner, and the hardest material belongs there. Families who move their Higher Level session to a weekend almost never move it back.

The practical ask is therefore to tell us the whole week rather than the preferred hour. Which evenings are genuinely free, when the fixed activities are, whether the household has a four-day Sharjah working pattern, and whether a weekend morning is possible. From that we can usually find a specialist match that a four-to-six request would have made impossible.
bullets: The four-to-six window is contested by every provider at once
Flexibility on timing widens the specialist pool substantially
A student after a long bus run is not at their best, whatever the clock says
Tell us the whole week, not the preferred hour

sections.heading: Ramadan, the four-day week and the Friday option
paragraphs: Two local features change the shape of an available week in ways a generic schedule will miss. The first is the Ramadan period, when the school day shortens. On paper that looks like extra study time and in practice it is not: children arrive home earlier with less energy, and a plan built on the apparent extra hours tends to fail in its second week.

What works during that period is deliberate maintenance. Shorter sessions, fixed in advance for the early evening or after Iftar rather than renegotiated weekly, with light retrieval practice instead of new content, and the weeks either side planned to carry the heavier work. Telling the student the fortnight is lighter by design matters as much as the schedule itself, because an abandoned plan does more damage than a few quiet days.

The second feature is the Sharjah public-sector working week, which runs four days. For households where a parent works that pattern, Friday becomes a genuinely available day rather than an awkward one, and a Friday morning session is often the best hour of the week: the student is rested, the roads are quiet, and nothing else is competing for the slot. Families rarely volunteer this, which is why we ask about the working pattern rather than only about the school.

Taken together, these two features mean the available week in this district is less standard than anywhere else in the country. A schedule copied from a Dubai Marina family will not fit a household here, and that is the main reason we set times after a conversation about the week rather than offering a list of slots.
bullets: Shortened school days lower energy rather than adding usable hours
Fix post-Iftar or early-evening sessions in advance, not weekly
A four-day Sharjah working pattern can make Friday the best day

sections.heading: Sequencing the second Diploma year on a commuter's budget
paragraphs: The second Diploma year is where a tight evening budget turns into a visible problem, because three things arrive at once: internal coursework deadlines, the end of the syllabus, and university applications. Students with plenty of evening hours absorb that. Students getting home at five do not, unless the year was sequenced in advance.

Sequencing means deciding, in the autumn, what gets done when and what is deliberately deferred. Coursework first, because a missed internal deadline cannot be reopened and because finished coursework reduces the load in the spring. Then the subjects nearest a grade boundary. Then, and only then, the subject the student finds hardest, which is often not the subject where a point is most available.

The first step is administrative and free: ask the school for its published internal deadline calendar at the start of the year. On a commuting schedule, knowing those dates in September rather than January is worth several weeks of usable evenings, because work can be moved into the quieter autumn weeks instead of colliding in a single term.

Where support is bought, it should follow the same order. Fund the coursework bottleneck first, then the boundary subject, and accept that a third subject will be left alone for a term. Spreading a limited number of sessions across three struggling subjects in the spring of the second year reliably produces no visible movement in any of them, and on this corridor the evenings to waste simply do not exist.
bullets: Get the school's internal deadline calendar in the autumn
Clear coursework first; a missed internal deadline does not reopen
Fund the subject nearest a boundary before the hardest subject
Accept leaving one subject alone rather than spreading thin

sections.heading: What a tutor can and cannot do about any of this
paragraphs: Honesty about scope matters on a page that has spent this long on logistics. A tutor cannot change a bus route, move a school's deadline, reopen a missed submission or guarantee a grade. What a tutor can do is make the hours that exist count, and tell a family plainly when the hours that exist are not enough.

On coursework the boundary is firm and worth stating. A tutor teaches the skill the component assesses, explains the published criteria and what their command words mean, tests whether a topic or research question can carry the work, questions the student about their own reasoning, and gives feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write any part of the work, does not rewrite the student's sentences and does not supply content for submission. This region's market includes a provider selling completed Internal Assessments outright; that is academic malpractice and the consequence falls on the student.

On regulation, private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. For a child schooled across the boundary, the applicable body is Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority instead. No tutoring provider, including IB Gram, holds approval, accreditation or a licence from either, and we claim none.

On permits, the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, no fine schedule is published, and the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.
bullets: A tutor makes existing hours count; it cannot create hours
The student writes every word of any submitted component
The regulator follows the school's emirate, not the family's address
