faqs.question: What time can a Diploma session realistically start for a family in Al Nahda, Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Later than most providers offer. A child at a Dubai school travelling by bus across the boundary is commonly home between half past four and five, and then needs time to change and eat. The first genuinely workable weekday slot is usually half past five, sometimes six. The method is simple: record the actual arrival time on three ordinary weekdays, take the latest, add fifteen minutes and book that. A four o'clock slot in these towers is a slot that will be missed.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Diploma tutor to an apartment in Al Nahda?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time. On this corridor that is a direct answer to the timing problem: the session does not lose its first ten minutes to somebody arriving, a later start is available, and two children who get home forty minutes apart can both be taught on the same evening.

faqs.question: How many usable evenings does a Diploma student on this corridor actually have?
faqs.answer: Usually about two, once the commute, fixed after-school activities and homework are accounted for. That is the arithmetic behind most of the difficulty we see here, and it explains why students in these towers are often behind without being weak. The response that works is to give each available slot a specific job in advance — hardest subject, nearest deadline, core work at the weekend — and to keep one evening deliberately empty as slack.

faqs.question: Is a weekend session better than a weekday one for a student crossing the boundary?
faqs.answer: Usually, and it should carry the hardest material rather than the leftovers. On a weekend the student is rested and the road is irrelevant, which makes it the best learning hour of the week. Where only one high-quality hour is realistic, put it on a weekend morning and use a short weekday slot purely to mark what was set and set the next piece. Households that move a Higher Level subject to the weekend rarely move it back.

faqs.question: Why does the Extended Essay never get written in a commuting household?
faqs.answer: Because nothing chases it weekly. Subject homework has a teacher asking for it on a known day; the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge have internal deadlines months away and no weekly pressure, so in a week with two usable evenings they lose every scheduling argument. The fix is to give the core a fixed protected hour, usually at the weekend, and to use it for the work that produces marks rather than for whatever feels most urgent that day.

faqs.question: Does the Sharjah four-day working week change what days are available?
faqs.answer: For many households here, yes. Sharjah's public sector works a four-day week, so where a parent follows that pattern, Friday becomes a genuinely available day rather than an awkward one. A Friday morning session is often the best hour of the week: the student is rested, the roads are quiet and nothing else competes for the slot. Families rarely mention it unprompted, which is why we ask about the household's working pattern rather than only the school day.

faqs.question: How should a Diploma student here handle the Ramadan period?
faqs.answer: As deliberate maintenance rather than a push. Shortened school days mean earlier arrivals with less energy, not extra usable hours, so a plan built on the apparent extra time tends to collapse in its second week. Shorter sessions fixed in advance for the early evening or after Iftar, light retrieval practice rather than new content, and the weeks either side planned to carry the heavy work. Saying plainly that the fortnight is lighter by design protects the plan more than any schedule does.

faqs.question: What should we ask the school about the bus before fixing a session time?
faqs.answer: Not what time the day ends but what time the bus reaches this district, which can be an hour or more later. Also ask which days carry fixed after-school activities, including Creativity, Activity, Service commitments, because a tutoring slot that collides with a programme requirement will always lose. And ask whether the route changes between terms, since a new stop added to a route can move arrival by twenty minutes without any notice to parents.

faqs.question: Can both my children be taught on the same evening if they get home at different times?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most households in these towers that is the arrangement that survives a term. Two consecutive slots, two different specialists, nobody travelling. The sequencing follows arrival times: the child at a Sharjah school takes the earlier slot, the child crossing the boundary takes the later one. It concentrates the disruption into one weeknight and leaves the rest of the week free for homework and sleep, both of which matter more than an extra hour of teaching.

faqs.question: How should we sequence the second Diploma year with so few evenings?
faqs.answer: Coursework first, then the subject nearest a grade boundary, then accept that a third subject is left alone for a term. Ask the school for its published internal deadline calendar in the autumn, because knowing those dates in September rather than January allows work to be moved into quieter weeks instead of colliding in one term. Spreading a handful of sessions across three struggling subjects in the spring reliably produces no visible movement in any of them.

faqs.question: Are Higher Level specialists available at the later times we need?
faqs.answer: More often than at four o'clock, which is the most contested hour of the week for every provider in the northern emirates. Flexibility is the lever here: a household willing to take half past six or a weekend morning chooses from a much wider pool, frequently at the lower end of the specialist rate band. Where no specialist is free for a scarce subject at any hour you can use, we say so at the first conversation rather than placing a generalist and hoping.

faqs.question: Which regulator applies if we live in Sharjah and our child studies in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The school's emirate decides it. A child at a Dubai school is in a KHDA-regulated school, so the inspection framework and published report come from there. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, a broader remit than inspection alone. No tutoring provider, including IB Gram, holds approval from either authority, and any page claiming such approval is making a dangerous and checkable claim.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do with a Diploma investigation or essay draft?
faqs.answer: Teach the skill the component assesses, explain the published criteria and what their command words require, test whether the topic or research question can carry the work, question the student about their own reasoning, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. What a tutor does not do is write any part of it, rewrite sentences or supply content for submission. We state that before coursework support begins, because the consequence of crossing the line falls on your child rather than on us.

faqs.question: Where should an Al Nahda family get the Diploma exam and deadline dates?
faqs.answer: Because we have not verified them from the International Baccalaureate directly. The board's site blocks automated checking, secondary sources circulate dates that disagree with each other, and a wrong examination date is the one error on a page like this that a parent would act on. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session. For the specific dates and for your school's internal coursework deadlines, ask the Diploma coordinator, who holds the calendar that actually governs your child's year.

intro.heading: Work backwards from when your child actually gets home
paragraphs: A Sharjah school day finishes early by international standards. For most private schools serving Al Nouf the last lesson ends somewhere between 1.30pm and 2.45pm, depending on the year group and whether an after-school activity runs. That sounds like an afternoon full of possibility. In practice the journey home is the part nobody budgets for, and it is the reason so many tutoring arrangements in this district quietly collapse by November.

Al Nouf sits in Sharjah's inland residential belt, away from the school clusters. The schools its families use are concentrated in Muwaileh, University City and central Sharjah, and the roads out of those clusters at pick-up time do not move. A parent collecting one child at 2.15pm and a sibling at 2.50pm is not home before half past three. Add food, a change of clothes and the twenty minutes of decompression every fifteen-year-old needs, and the first honest slot of the day starts at 4.30pm.

Then the Diploma Programme makes its own claim on the evening. A DP student carries six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, plus an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge course and an Internal Assessment in almost every subject. School homework is not the residual activity it was at MYP; it is two to three hours on an ordinary weekday. Any tutoring hour has to be carved out of that, which means the slot needs to be fixed, protected and short enough to survive a bad week.

This is where the home-visit model breaks in Al Nouf specifically. A tutor who drives in from Muwaileh at 4.30pm is sitting in the same traffic that delayed your own journey. A 4.30pm start becomes 4.50pm, the hour becomes forty minutes, and nobody logs the loss. IB Gram does not operate home visits anywhere in the UAE in any case; home tuition is a service we run only in India. Every Sharjah lesson is delivered live, one-to-one, over video, in a slot held in Gulf Standard Time.

What follows is the timetable version of this argument. There is an hour-by-hour map of the Al Nouf afternoon, a table of the school clusters and when they release, the Sharjah market rates with the travel premium separated out, and the Diploma Programme calendar read as a set of deadlines that arrive before you expect them. If you want the availability argument instead, the IGCSE page for this neighbourhood takes that line; this one is about time. One practical note before any of it: write down, for five consecutive days, the time your child genuinely walked through the door. Almost every parent who does this discovers they are thirty to forty minutes later than they believed, and that the slot they had been trying to defend was never going to hold in the first place.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nouf.programmesIntro: Al Nouf families come to us at three different stages of the IB continuum, and each stage has its own relationship with the clock. A PYP session can happen before dinner; a DP session is fighting for the same hour as the Extended Essay. Naming the stage is the first thing we ask about.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led programme without formal external examinations, assessed through units of inquiry and the Year 6 exhibition. Support at this stage is usually about literacy, numeracy fluency and the habits that make later study possible. Sessions are shorter, typically forty-five minutes, because concentration rather than content is the limiting factor.
programmes.countryNote: Primary finishing times in Sharjah are earlier than secondary, often around 1.30pm, so Al Nouf PYP families are the one group with genuine afternoon flexibility. A 3.30pm slot works here and does not work for an older sibling. Where both children need support, we stagger the two rather than trying to run them back to back, because an exhausted parent supervising two screens is a worse outcome than two separate days.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked A to D, with a Personal Project in the final year. The criteria matter more than the topic: a student who writes a good essay and ignores the criterion wording will score in the middle band. Most tutoring at this stage is teaching students to read what the criterion asks for.
programmes.countryNote: MYP years in Sharjah are when after-school activities peak, so the Al Nouf afternoon gets crowded by sport and music on two or three days a week. We ask families to name the two days that are genuinely clear and build the slot into one of them, rather than taking the day that looks best on paper in September and losing it by October when the fixture list starts.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, assessed by external examination and internal assessment, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Points run to 45. The load is not evenly spread: the first year ends with most Internal Assessment drafts outstanding, and the second begins with all of them due.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Nouf DP student the two-year shape is a scheduling problem more than a content one. Sessions in the first year should sit in the late afternoon and protect the IA process; sessions in the second year often move later and shorter, because the student is already working until eleven. UAE DP candidates sit the May session; confirm every specific date with your school's IB coordinator rather than with any page, including this one.

programmes.name: Extended Essay, TOK and the Internal Assessments
programmes.description: The core is where most points are quietly lost, because the deadlines are internal and therefore movable until suddenly they are not. The Extended Essay runs to 4,000 words on a research question the student chooses; TOK is assessed by essay and exhibition. Support here is process coaching: question framing, structure, evidence, referencing.
programmes.countryNote: A tutor may teach the skills, discuss the research question and read a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, complete or edit the work to a finished state. Providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments outright, and a Sharjah student who buys one is risking the whole diploma rather than one grade. We say the boundary out loud because in this market it is not obvious.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nouf.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma Programme subjects Sharjah families ask about most. The notes say what the assessment actually demands and roughly how much evening time each one tends to need, because that is the information a parent planning a week is missing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency under time pressure, with HL adding proof and deeper calculus. The exploration is internally assessed and routinely underestimated. Students who understand the maths and still lose marks are usually losing them to presentation and unjustified steps.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use. The calculator is part of the assessment, not a convenience, and students who have not drilled the specific calculator procedures lose marks they knew the method for. Check university prerequisites before choosing this route over Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 multiple choice, Paper 2 extended response, Paper 3 on experimental and option material. Marks are lost in the written-explanation questions, where a correct idea phrased loosely scores nothing. The internal assessment rewards a tightly controlled single variable, not an ambitious design.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the heaviest failure rate at HL. Data-based questions demand that uncertainty be handled properly rather than mentioned. The investigation needs a quantitative relationship the student can actually plot.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: High content volume with marks tied to exact terminology, plus data analysis that catches students who revised content and skipped skills. HL extension topics arrive late in the course and are often met for the first time during revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks, and the evaluation command terms decide the rest. The internally assessed commentaries require real published articles and a disciplined word limit; students lose marks by summarising the article instead of applying theory to it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven with a research project at HL. Application to the given organisation is what separates a 5 from a 7, and students who write textbook answers about a generic firm cap themselves. Quantitative tools are examinable and often neglected.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 comparative, plus the individual oral and, at HL, the essay. Strong bilingual Sharjah students often plateau on analytical technique rather than language: commenting on effect, not restating content.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source-based Paper 1, thematic Paper 2, regional Paper 3 at HL, plus a historical investigation. Marks turn on argument structure and use of evidence. Students who know the narrative and cannot build a line of argument sit in the middle of the mark range.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by a prescribed-title essay and an exhibition of three objects against a knowledge question. It is the component most often left too late in Sharjah schools, and the one where process coaching produces the clearest improvement for the time spent.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nouf.regionsTitle: Al Nouf and the districts that share its timetable
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nouf.regionsIntro: These neighbouring Sharjah districts send children to the same school clusters and therefore face the same afternoon. The notes are about release times and travel, because that is what decides when a session can begin.

regions.name: Al Nouf
regions.note: Inland residential Sharjah, away from the school clusters. Nothing in the district itself sets the schedule; the school run to Muwaileh and University City does, and it pushes the first workable slot towards 4.30pm.

regions.name: Muwaileh
regions.note: Dense school cluster and the destination for much of the Al Nouf run. Pick-up queues here are the single biggest delay in the afternoon, and families with two children at different schools lose a further half hour to the second collection.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: Campus district with school provision alongside the universities. Release and university traffic overlap, so the exit is slower than the distance suggests. It is also where the budget tutor supply comes from and where its limits show.

regions.name: Al Zahia
regions.note: Master-planned community closer to the schools, which gives families there roughly thirty minutes more afternoon than Al Nouf households get. Worth knowing if you are comparing notes with friends and wondering why their 4pm slot works.

regions.name: Al Majaz
regions.note: Central Sharjah on the lagoon, with a high share of families driving into Dubai schools. Those children finish later and arrive home later still, so evening slots after 6pm are normal rather than exceptional.

regions.name: Al Taawun
regions.note: Coastal central district, also heavily Dubai-facing. The Dubai-Sharjah return journey in the afternoon is the least predictable part of any schedule in the emirate and the strongest argument for a slot that does not depend on anyone arriving.

regions.name: Aljada
regions.note: Newer mixed-use development with a young school-age population and rapidly changing traffic patterns as it fills. Families here often hold a weekend-morning slot as a safety net against the afternoon.

regions.name: Tilal City
regions.note: Inland and still developing, with an Al Nouf-like profile: residential, car-dependent, no tutoring provision within the district. Online delivery is not a preference here so much as the only arrangement that reliably happens.

schoolClusters.city: Muwaileh and University City
schoolClusters.note: The main destination for Al Nouf secondary students. Release is early, but the exit is slow, and a parent doing two collections should assume a 3.30pm arrival home rather than 2.45pm.
schools: American School of Creative Science, Muwaileh

schoolClusters.city: Central Sharjah
schoolClusters.note: Serves the Al Majaz and Al Taawun side and takes a share of Al Nouf families who chose a school near a parent's commute. Victoria International School of Sharjah is the emirate's established IB continuum option.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai-side schools
schoolClusters.note: A meaningful minority of Sharjah families drive into Dubai for an IB continuum place. Those students finish later and arrive home much later, which is the group for whom evening slots and weekend mornings are the only options.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nouf.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named as context for where Al Nouf students study. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any school named, and none is implied.
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nouf.modesIntro: Three patterns, all delivered online. The choice is a timetable decision as much as an academic one, and the right answer changes between DP1 and DP2.

modes.title: The protected weekday hour
modes.description: One fixed hour a week, same weekday, same tutor, scheduled after the real arrival time rather than the nominal school finish. This is the backbone arrangement for a DP1 student in Al Nouf and the one that survives a busy term, because the household stops negotiating it after the second week.
bullets: Start time set from your actual arrival home, not the school bell
Same tutor all year so error patterns get tracked
Written notes after each session
Moves within the same week when a school deadline collides

modes.title: Two shorter sessions
modes.description: Forty-five minutes twice a week instead of ninety once. For a DP2 student working late most nights, two shorter contacts hold attention better and keep a subject ticking without a single large demand on an already full evening. It also gives two chances a week to catch a misunderstanding early.
bullets: Two 45-minute slots on separate days
Short homework set between them rather than one large task
Useful in the weeks around internal deadlines
Can compress into one longer session during holidays

modes.title: Weekend-morning block
modes.description: A longer Saturday or Sunday morning session for families whose weekday afternoons are genuinely gone, which in practice means most Dubai-commuting households and many two-child Al Nouf households. Weekend mornings are also when the strongest tutors have availability, so the trade is less painful than it sounds.
bullets: 90 minutes with a proper break, not a stretched hour
Shorter match times than peak weekday evenings
Suits timed past-paper work that needs an unbroken run
Keeps the weekday evening free for school homework

sections.heading: The Al Nouf afternoon, hour by hour
paragraphs: The short answer is that a secondary student in Al Nouf can start a session at 4.30pm, a primary student at 3.30pm, and a Dubai-schooled student not before 6pm. Everything else on this page follows from those three numbers. They are not guesses; they are what families in this district report once you ask them what time they actually walked through the door rather than what time school ended.

The table below maps the afternoon. The column worth reading twice is the last one, because it names what is lost if a session is booked into the wrong slot. A lesson that starts while a child is still eating is a lesson that spends its first fifteen minutes going nowhere, and over a term that is five wasted hours paid for at full rate.

There is a second-child effect that single-child households underestimate. Two collections at two schools with staggered release times routinely add thirty-five to fifty minutes to the journey. If you have one child in primary and one in DP, the DP student's slot is governed by the primary collection, which is why we ask about siblings before suggesting a time.

None of this is an argument for tutoring later and later. Attention declines sharply after about 8pm for most students, and a 9pm session is usually a waste of money dressed up as commitment. The window that works in Al Nouf is roughly 4.30pm to 7.30pm on weekdays, plus weekend mornings, and the honest conclusion is that there are fewer good slots in a week than most families assume.

sections.heading: Which schools set the clock for this neighbourhood
paragraphs: Al Nouf has no large school inside it, so its timetable is imported from wherever its children study. That makes the school cluster the real scheduling input. The table below lists the clusters Sharjah families use, the approximate release pattern, the journey back to Al Nouf and the resulting first workable slot, so that you can find your own row rather than taking an average.

Victoria International School of Sharjah is the emirate's established IB continuum provider and the reason a meaningful number of Sharjah families never need to look at Dubai. For others the IB place is in Dubai, which changes the afternoon completely: a Deira or Al Barsha finish plus the northbound return journey puts arrival home well after five, and often after six on a bad day.

The Muwaileh and University City cluster is the one that most affects Al Nouf. It is close in kilometres and slow in practice, because several schools release within the same half hour onto the same roads. Families who have found a way to delay their own collection by twenty minutes, or to use a school bus for the older child, consistently report a calmer evening.

Treat the last column as a planning figure rather than a promise, and check it against one real week of your own. Write down the time you got home each day for five days. Most parents discover they are thirty to forty minutes later than they believed, and the slot they had been trying to make work was never going to.

sections.heading: What the Diploma Programme does to an evening
paragraphs: A DP student is carrying six courses, three at Higher Level, plus three core components. On an ordinary Sharjah weekday that is two to three hours of school-set work before anything optional happens. The common error is to add a tutoring hour on top of a full evening and expect the student to absorb it; what actually happens is that the tutoring hour displaces sleep, and by week six attention in school starts to drop.

The load is also badly distributed across the two years. DP1 looks manageable until the spring, when Internal Assessment drafts, the Extended Essay research question and the first mock examinations arrive within weeks of each other. DP2 opens with everything that slipped from DP1 still outstanding. A family in Al Nouf planning a tutoring year should put more hours into the first half of DP1 than feels necessary, precisely because that is when there is room for them.

Higher Level choices change the arithmetic. Three HL sciences with Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at HL is a combination that leaves very little evening, and a student in that position needs fewer tutoring hours in more concentrated bursts rather than three weekly subjects. We will say so rather than sell the third subject, because three thin weekly hours in a packed term produce less than one properly used one.

The sensible structure for most Al Nouf DP families is one protected weekday hour in the strongest-need subject, with a second subject added only if the first is stable after six weeks. That is a slower build than anxiety wants, and it is the one that is still running in March.
bullets: Six subjects, three at HL, plus Extended Essay, TOK and CAS
Two to three hours of school-set work on a normal weekday

sections.heading: What Sharjah families pay, and what the travel premium actually buys
paragraphs: Begin with the in-home figure, because that is the one this search phrase implies. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one tuition at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500. Against that, a qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300; Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The difference between those bands is not entirely teaching.

Part of the premium is a car and the time it spends in it. A tutor driving to Al Nouf for a 4.30pm session has left somewhere else at 3.45pm and will not be free again until 6.15pm. That is two and a half hours of their working day for one paid hour, and the rate reflects it. You are buying presence, and presence in this district is expensive because of where the roads are at that hour.

At the other end, the budget band runs from roughly AED 33 to 65, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, largely supplied by university students from the University City pool. For PYP numeracy support that can be entirely appropriate. For HL Chemistry eight weeks before the session it is not, and the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above exists for a reason: TutorChase quotes AED 270 and Bestimate puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium examiner-led provision goes further, with BartyED at AED 650.

Monthly packages are where the two models separate most clearly. The market shows AED 799 per month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 per month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are the same eight contact hours at roughly double the price. Every figure here is published by the provider named and was read in October 2026; none of it is an IB Gram price list, and for ours you should take the free trial and ask.

sections.heading: A fixed online slot against a tutor arriving at 4.40pm
paragraphs: This is the comparison a scheduling-driven page owes the reader. In-home tuition has genuine advantages: physical presence, easier management of a distractible younger child, no reliance on a connection. We are not going to argue those away. IB Gram simply does not offer home visits in the UAE, and the table below sets out the trade rather than asserting a winner.

The column that matters most in Al Nouf is start-time reliability. A video slot at 4.30pm begins at 4.30pm. A home visit at 4.30pm begins when the tutor reaches the door, which in this district is a function of the Maliha Road and the Muwaileh pick-up queue. Ten lost minutes a week across a thirty-week year is five hours, and you paid specialist rates for all of them.

The second column is what happens when the week goes wrong, which it does several times a term. An online slot can move to Thursday when a school deadline lands on Tuesday. A home visit cannot easily move, because moving it means a second journey for the tutor, and so the session is simply cancelled. Cancellations rather than lateness are what actually break tutoring arrangements in Sharjah.

Nothing on this page is an offer to send a tutor to an Al Nouf address, and the in-home column is here so you can weigh the market option honestly against ours. If a home visit genuinely is the right answer for your child, book it from a provider who offers it, and ask that provider for the tutor's MoHRE permit and their record on the specific programme and level.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the rhythm of the Sharjah year
paragraphs: The UAE academic year does not run evenly, and a tutoring plan that ignores its shape will lose weeks at the worst possible time. Ramadan brings shortened school days, and for fasting students the useful study window moves to the late evening after Iftar or to the early morning. A 5pm session that worked in January is the wrong slot in Ramadan, and the families who plan for that keep their momentum while others simply stop for a month.

We move slots rather than pausing them. A post-Iftar session, typically between 8.30pm and 10pm, works well for DP students who are already keeping late hours, and a short early-morning session suits others. The point is to decide in advance which of those your household will use, because a month of improvisation becomes a month of nothing.

Eid holidays, the Sharjah school calendar's mid-term breaks and the long summer each create a different risk. Summer is the clearest opportunity in the whole year for a DP1 student: the Extended Essay research question and the first Internal Assessment can both be substantially advanced in July and August, when nothing else is competing for the time. Families who use the summer arrive in DP2 in a completely different position from those who do not.

Finally, plan around the internal deadlines rather than the external ones. The dates that actually govern a Sharjah DP student's year are the school's own IA and EE milestones, and those are set by the school, not by the IB. Ask the coordinator for the published schedule in September and build the tutoring year on it.
bullets: Shift the slot in Ramadan rather than pausing; post-Iftar or early morning
Use the summer for the Extended Essay research question and one IA
Build the year around the school's internal deadlines, not guessed exam dates

sections.heading: SPEA, the regulator map and what no regulator covers
paragraphs: Al Nouf's private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority. SPEA's remit is wider than inspection: in Sharjah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is why school-level patterns in this emirate, including timetable shape and subject availability, tend to be consistent across providers in a way parents moving from Dubai find surprising.

The wider map is worth knowing because families move within the UAE more often than between countries. Dubai schools fall under KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain under ADEK, Sharjah under SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. Moving from Al Nouf to a Dubai IB school means changing regulator, and the mandatory-subject requirements your child meets will be the ones KHDA publishes.

Those mandatory subjects are real and they occupy timetable space. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are required in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA calculates instructional time in forty-minute lesson units, advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes, requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in these subjects, and states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is not permitted.

What no regulator does is vet your tutor. SPEA regulates schools. Private tutoring sits with MoHRE: Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years and applied for through the MoHRE smart app and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE or the IB, and nobody in this market legitimately claims otherwise.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with an IA, an EE or a TOK essay
paragraphs: The IB core is where the integrity line gets crossed most often, because the work is produced at home over months and the deadlines are internal. This market contains providers who sell completed Internal Assessments outright, with one page in this research advertising finished IAs at AED 3,750. For the student that is not a shortcut, it is a malpractice finding and a risk to the entire diploma.

Here is the boundary in plain terms. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain how the assessment criteria award marks, discuss and refine a research question the student proposed, model structure on a different example, read a draft the student wrote and say where the argument is unsupported or the method unclear, and teach referencing and data handling properly.

A tutor may not write any part of the work, rewrite it, complete it, edit it to a finished state, or supply a worked exemplar for the student's own question. We also do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter rather than a grey area.

One more boundary concerns teachers. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document. The principle stands either way, and we do not arrange it.
bullets: Teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own draft: yes
Writing, completing or polishing assessed work: never, at any price
Supplying official papers or mark schemes as downloads: no, we link the source
A child tutored privately by the teacher who marks their school work: no

sections.heading: Booking a slot in Al Nouf that is still running in March
paragraphs: Spend one week measuring before you book anything. Write down the time your child actually walked through the door each day, not the time school finished. Note which afternoons carry an activity and which are genuinely clear. That single sheet of paper is more useful than any advice on this page, because it tells you how many workable slots your household really has, and the number is usually two.

Then put the session in the earlier of those two slots rather than the later one. Attention is better, the student has not yet started school homework, and there is room to overrun by ten minutes without eating into dinner. A 4.30pm slot that holds is worth more than a 6.30pm slot that gets moved twice a month, and the difference compounds across a year.

Use the free trial lesson as a diagnosis rather than an introduction. Send the subject, the level, the programme year and one recent piece of marked work. A specialist should be able to tell you after an hour whether the gap is content, technique or workload management, and those three problems need three genuinely different plans. If the trial is all rapport and no diagnosis, that tells you something.

Review at week four against evidence you agreed in advance: which errors have stopped recurring, what is happening on timed questions, whether the homework between sessions is being done. If the evidence is not there we move the student to a different specialist rather than defend the first match, and you should expect that of any provider you pay.
bullets: Measure one real week of arrival times before choosing a slot
Take the earlier workable window, not the later one
Judge the free trial on the diagnosis you receive
Agree what week four should look like, then actually check it

process.title: Tell us when the day really ends
process.description: We ask for the school, the year group, the usual arrival time at home and whether a sibling collection is involved. Those four answers decide the slot, and getting them right at the start is why arrangements in this district survive past October rather than quietly lapsing.

process.title: Name the programme and the level
process.description: PYP, MYP or DP, and for DP the subject and whether it is Higher or Standard Level. An HL Physics match and an SL Economics match are different searches. We also ask what the school's internal IA and EE deadlines are, because those govern the term more than exams do.

process.title: A free trial used as a diagnosis
process.description: The tutor works through a real question or a section of the student's own draft, then tells you whether the problem is content, technique or workload. You get that in writing. Nothing is paid before the trial happens, and the diagnosis is useful even if you go elsewhere.

process.title: Fix the slot and protect it
process.description: The time goes in the calendar as a standing commitment in Gulf Standard Time, with an agreed alternative day for weeks when a school deadline collides. Sessions that can move within the week get kept; sessions that can only be cancelled get cancelled.

process.title: Review at four weeks, adjust the plan
process.description: We compare against the evidence agreed at the outset and change what is not working, including the tutor. For DP students this is also when we decide whether a second subject is sustainable or whether the existing hour should go deeper instead.

whyPoints.title: The schedule is the product
whyPoints.description: Most tutoring in this district fails on logistics rather than teaching. We build the slot from your real arrival time, keep it in Gulf Standard Time, and move it within the week when school deadlines collide. An hour that actually happens thirty times beats a better hour that happens twenty.

whyPoints.title: A specialist per subject and level
whyPoints.description: One tutor for HL Chemistry, a different one for SL Economics. Distance-based matching forces Al Nouf families towards an all-rounder, because the pool of people willing to drive inland after four o'clock is small. Removing the distance filter removes the compromise.

whyPoints.title: Every rate attributed
whyPoints.description: The AED figures on this page carry the provider that published them and the month they were read. Three of six competitor pages in this research publish no price at all and two quote US dollars. You can verify each number here yourself before you talk to anyone.

whyPoints.title: Honest about IB dates
whyPoints.description: We describe the May session and point you to your school's IB coordinator for specifics, because IB session and results dates are not something we will restate as fact. Pages that publish confident IB dates without a source are the ones that will be wrong next year.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on the core
whyPoints.description: Tutors coach the IA, EE and TOK process and read drafts the student wrote. They do not write, complete or finish them, and we do not hand out official papers or mark schemes. In a market where completed IAs are sold openly, that line protects the qualification you are paying for.

whyPoints.title: Built for a UAE calendar
whyPoints.description: Ramadan moves the slot rather than ending it, summer is used for the Extended Essay and one Internal Assessment, and the plan runs on your school's internal deadlines. A provider working from a northern-hemisphere term calendar will be out of step with Sharjah twice a year.

faqs.question: What time can an IB session realistically start for a student in Al Nouf?
faqs.answer: For a secondary student collected from the Muwaileh or University City cluster, 4.30pm is the first reliable start. School releases between 1.30pm and 2.45pm, but the pick-up queue and the drive back inland take thirty to fifty minutes, and arrival, food and a change of clothes take another half hour. Primary students can start around 3.30pm. Students attending Dubai schools rarely manage anything before 6pm. If a sibling collection is involved, push the later child back by about forty-five minutes.

faqs.question: Why will IB Gram not send a tutor to our home in Al Nouf?
faqs.answer: Home visits are a service IB Gram runs only in India. Across the UAE every lesson is live, one-to-one and delivered over video. Two reasons sit behind that. First, an in-home arrangement in inland Sharjah selects tutors by who will drive there after four o'clock rather than by who can teach HL Chemistry. Second, a 4.30pm home visit in this district starts when the car arrives, and over a thirty-week year the lost minutes add up to several full sessions you paid for.

faqs.question: How much does in-home IB tuition cost in Sharjah compared with online?
faqs.answer: Published market rates read in October 2026 put in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, and AED 200 to 500 with independent home tutors. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. Monthly packages show the gap most clearly: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are the providers' own figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: My child has three Higher Level subjects. How many tutoring hours is sensible?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families expect. Three HL subjects plus the core already fill the evening with two to three hours of school-set work, so adding three weekly tutoring hours usually displaces sleep rather than adding learning. Start with one protected hour in the subject causing the most damage, hold it for six weeks, and add a second only if the first is stable. Three thin hours in a packed term produce less than one hour used properly, and we will tell you that rather than sell the third.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan for a fasting student in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should. School days shorten and the useful study window moves, so a 5pm slot that worked in January is the wrong slot in Ramadan. We typically shift to a post-Iftar session between about 8.30pm and 10pm, which suits DP students already keeping late hours, or to a short early-morning session for those who prefer it. Decide which before the month starts. Families who improvise usually lose the whole month, and a month out in DP1 is expensive.

faqs.question: Which Sharjah schools do students you support in Al Nouf attend?
faqs.answer: Students we support in this part of Sharjah study across the Muwaileh and University City cluster, including Wesgreen International School, the American School of Creative Science in Muwaileh and The Westminster School Sharjah, and in central Sharjah at schools such as Victoria International School of Sharjah and Sharjah English School. A minority travel into Dubai for an IB continuum place. We name schools as context for where students study; IB Gram has no affiliation or partnership with any of them.

faqs.question: Is a weekend-morning session better than a weekday evening one?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and for two reasons. A Saturday or Sunday morning gives you an unbroken ninety minutes, which is what timed past-paper work actually needs, and it does not compete with school homework. It also falls outside the peak weekday evening window when every family in Sharjah wants a slot, so match times are shorter and stronger tutors have availability. The trade is a piece of the weekend, and for Dubai-commuting households it is usually the only arrangement that holds.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go in supporting the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Further than families expect in the useful direction, and not at all in the direction that would invalidate the work. A tutor can discuss and sharpen the research question, teach how the assessment criteria award marks, show structure on a different example, read a draft your child has written and say where the argument lacks support, and teach referencing properly. They cannot write any part of it, rewrite it or edit it to a finished state. Providers in this market sell finished work; buying it risks the entire diploma.

faqs.question: What does SPEA actually control in a Sharjah school?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and its remit is broader than inspection. Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is why timetable shape and subject availability are more consistent across Sharjah schools than parents arriving from Dubai expect. SPEA does not regulate private tutors, though. That sits with MoHRE under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the permit it issues is free and valid for two years.

faqs.question: How do you handle a week when a school deadline lands on our usual slot?
faqs.answer: We move the session rather than cancel it. At the start we agree a primary slot and one alternative day, so when an Internal Assessment draft or a mock lands on a Tuesday, the Tuesday hour shifts to Thursday that week and returns afterwards. This is the practical advantage of an arrangement that does not depend on anyone travelling: a home visit usually cannot move, because moving it means a second journey, so in practice it gets cancelled instead and the momentum goes with it.

faqs.question: Should we use the summer holiday for IB work or let the student rest?
faqs.answer: Both, deliberately. The summer between DP1 and DP2 is the clearest opportunity in the whole programme, because nothing else is competing for the time. A student who settles the Extended Essay research question and substantially advances one Internal Assessment over July and August starts DP2 in a different position from one who does not. That does not require daily work. Two sessions a week for six weeks is enough, and it buys back the autumn evenings that would otherwise go to catching up.

faqs.question: Does my child's Sharjah school set the IB deadlines, or does the IB?
faqs.answer: In day-to-day terms the school does. The IB sets the external examination session and the final upload deadlines, but the dates that govern your child's year are the school's internal milestones for Internal Assessment drafts, the Extended Essay stages and TOK components. Those are published by the school, usually in September, and they are what a tutoring plan should be built around. Ask the IB coordinator for the schedule and bring it to the first session. We do not publish IB session dates ourselves.

faqs.question: Do you support the MYP Personal Project as well as Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, as process coaching. The Personal Project is assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and the product itself, and most students lose marks on the process documentation rather than the product. A tutor can teach what each criterion asks for, help the student structure the process journal and read what the student has written. The product and the writing must be theirs, which is both an IB rule and the thing that makes the project worth doing at all.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free for an unusual Higher Level option our school runs?
faqs.answer: We tell you before you commit anything. For mainstream Diploma subjects a match usually takes two to four days. For narrower combinations, particularly an HL option or a less common language, it can take longer, and in that case the realistic answer may be a specialist in another timezone whose working hours overlap the Sharjah evening or a weekend morning. We will say which it is. What we will not do is accept the booking and hand your child to someone learning the syllabus alongside them.

faqs.question: Is one hour a week enough to change a Diploma grade?
faqs.answer: It depends which problem you have, and it is worth being blunt. If content was never learned, one hour a week from October will help but will not rebuild a year, and the honest plan involves more hours earlier or fewer subjects. If the content is broadly known and marks are going to technique, timing and misread command terms, one protected hour used on timed questions and mark-scheme correction moves grades reliably. Ask for a diagnostic trial first so you are buying the right thing.

faqs.question: Do you teach Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects alongside the IB?
faqs.answer: We can support Arabic language work, and it is worth understanding the constraints. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in UAE private schools whatever the licensed international curriculum. KHDA calculates instructional time in forty-minute units, requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in these subjects, and states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is not permitted. That limits what any tutor can legitimately substitute for school material, and a provider promising a shortcut here is promising something they cannot deliver.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nouf.closingHeading: Measure one week, then book the earlier slot
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-nouf.closingBody: If you are searching for an IB home tutor in Al Nouf, the most useful thing you can do before contacting anyone is write down, for five days, the time your child actually walked through the door and which afternoons carry an activity. That sheet tells you how many workable slots your household has, and it is usually two. Send us those two, plus the school, the programme year, the subject and level, and one recent piece of marked work. We will match a specialist, hold the slot in Gulf Standard Time, and run a free trial lesson that ends with a diagnosis rather than a sales pitch. Lessons are live, one-to-one and online, every week.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-qasimia.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma subjects to students across central Sharjah. Each holds one fixed weekly slot per student, keeps a written target list, and teaches one-to-one over live video so a session starts when the student is at the desk rather than when a car arrives.

intro.heading: The hour is the hard part, not the tutor
paragraphs: Al Qasimia is central, dense and long established, with schools in every direction and a tutoring market that has existed for decades. Finding somebody who will teach your child here is not difficult. Finding an hour each week that both the student and the tutor can actually keep, through a Sharjah term, is the thing that quietly defeats most arrangements.

Look at what competes for a weekday evening. A Diploma Programme student has six subjects setting work. Their school day includes the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies lessons that every private school in the country must timetable, because private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies but must follow the Ministry's general regulations. Add a commute - many Al Qasimia families use schools across the emirate or over the Dubai boundary - and the window between arriving home and being too tired to think is narrow.

Now add a tutor who drives. Their slot has to sit after their own journey, which in central Sharjah at five o'clock is unpredictable. A twenty-minute delay turns a sixty-minute lesson into forty, and a cancellation in a deadline week costs more than the fee. Families absorb this as normal, and it is not normal; it is a scheduling defect with a straightforward fix.

Our answer is a slot that does not depend on anybody's drive. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and they start when the student sits down. If the school bus is late, the lesson shifts twenty minutes instead of disappearing. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE - that service exists only in India - and for a family trying to protect one hour a week, this is the practical reason the format works rather than a marketing line.

The second half of the problem is what the hour is for, and that changes through the year. A term in DP1 should be spent differently from the term before internal assessment deadlines, and differently again from the final revision term. Most tutoring arrangements use the hour the same way all year, which is why families reach May feeling that a lot of money went somewhere unspecified.

A note on who this page is not for. If your child is eight and needs an adult sitting beside them to stay on task, the in-home premium may genuinely be worth paying, and we are not the provider for that: we do not offer UAE home visits. This page is written for families whose constraint is the diary rather than supervision.

So this page maps both: where the hour fits in a central Sharjah week, and what each term of the Diploma and the Middle Years actually owes a student. It also covers the collision fortnight in DP2, how the UAE year - Ramadan, Eid, exam leave, the long summer - reshapes a plan, and what a term of support costs at market rates.

Weekly load is high and uneven, with several internal deadlines capable of landing in one fortnight. The hour has to be spent on whatever the next dated thing is, which means a plan that is revisited every few weeks rather than fixed in September.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Sets work continuously, so a weekly hour has a clear job: finish and correct the week's problems, then extend into the next topic. Higher level students need the calculus thread kept warm all year, because a gap left in DP1 surfaces during revision when there is no time for it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-heavy at higher level, with technology use expected. The weekly hour is best spent on interpretation rather than calculation - explaining what a result means is where marks are lost, and it is quicker to coach than arithmetic.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Content arrives in dense blocks, so weekly support should consolidate rather than preview. Energetics and equilibrium reward being revisited two weeks after teaching, which is a scheduling insight more than a subject one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Problem-solving improves with short, frequent practice rather than long sessions. Twenty minutes of multi-step problems weekly, with method written out, does more than a monthly two-hour session that covers four topics superficially.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content accumulates, so the risk is a two-year backlog. A weekly hour that ends with ten minutes of retrieval on older material prevents the last term becoming an attempt to relearn the first year.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries, each tied to a current article, spread across both years. The weekly hour should carry one commentary forward in small steps rather than leaving all three to collide with revision in DP2.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Reading has to happen outside the session, so the hour is for analysis and for rehearsing the individual oral to time. Rehearsal needs to be booked weeks ahead, because it is an event rather than a piece of writing.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the extended essay
subjects.description: Neither sets weekly homework, which is precisely why both slip. Short fortnightly check-ins with a named next step keep them moving; a single long session a term does not. Coaching here is sequence and criteria, never writing.

sections.heading: Where an IB session actually fits in a central Sharjah week
paragraphs: Begin with the honest audit. Between the end of the school day and a reasonable bedtime there are perhaps five usable hours for a Diploma student, and they are not empty hours. Homework from six subjects, mandatory UAE subject work, prayer, dinner, travel and the ordinary decompression a teenager needs all sit inside them. A tutoring slot has to be carved out of that, not added to it.

The practical consequences are specific. A session before five works only for students with a short commute; for the rest it is a fiction that collapses in the second week. A session after eight produces attendance without learning. For most central Sharjah families, the workable windows are five-thirty to seven-thirty on two or three weekdays, and mid-morning at the weekend, which is the most underused slot in the entire week.

Weekend mornings deserve more attention than they get. Nobody is tired, nothing else is scheduled, and a ninety-minute session is genuinely possible rather than nominally possible. For internal assessment work, which needs sustained concentration rather than quick drill, it is by far the best hour in the week. Families resist it because weekends feel sacred, and then spend four distracted weekday evenings achieving less.

The other variable is the sibling pattern. Households here commonly have children at two or three schools with different finish times, and the youngest child's session is always the one that gets moved. Placing slots back to back on one evening - older child first, while the younger does homework, then the younger - keeps the whole arrangement stable and means a parent supervises on one night rather than three.

sections.heading: What each term of the Diploma owes a student
paragraphs: A two-year programme has roughly six terms, and they are not interchangeable. Treating them as if they are is the most expensive mistake available, because it means spending the same hour the same way whether the next deadline is four months or four days off.

The first two terms of DP1 are content terms. The job is understanding, keeping pace and establishing the habit of written method. This is also when a tutoring hour is cheapest in real terms, because a gap closed here costs one session and the same gap closed during revision costs five and displaces something else. Families almost never buy support in this window, and the ones who do rarely need a panic block later.

The third term and the summer are proposal and planning time: an exploration question, an investigation method, an extended essay topic with a question narrow enough to answer. These decisions are made badly when they are made quickly, and they determine months of subsequent work. A few sessions here save a term of rework later, and the summer in particular is the quietest working window in the whole programme.

DP2's first two terms are where internal assessments, the extended essay and Theory of Knowledge must actually be finished, because they cannot be done during revision. The final term is revision and examinations: no new content, timed papers, error logs. A plan that still has assessed work outstanding at the start of that final term has created a collision which will cost marks on both sides of it.

DP1 term three and summer: proposals, questions and method decisions
DP2 terms one and two: assessed work finished, not started

sections.heading: The collision fortnight, and how to sequence it
paragraphs: Every Diploma student meets a fortnight in DP2 where several deadlines arrive at once: two internal assessments, a Theory of Knowledge draft, a set of tests, and revision that should already be under way. It is predictable, which means it can be planned for, and almost nobody plans for it.

The first move is information. Ask the coordinator for the school's internal deadline calendar at the start of DP2 - submission dates per subject, extended essay checkpoints, the Theory of Knowledge essay deadline, mock windows. Most schools will supply it; very few families request it. With that list, the collision is visible months ahead and can be defused by finishing one piece early.

The second move is sequencing, and it requires accepting that not everything can be done to the same standard in the same fortnight. The question is which piece carries the most marks, which is closest to finished, and which can be brought to an acceptable standard quickly. Deciding that deliberately beats working on whatever feels most frightening at ten o'clock at night, which is what happens without a plan.

The third move is reducing contact time rather than increasing it. In a collision fortnight, three short check-ins beat two long lessons: the student needs decisions and accountability, not more teaching. We shift to that pattern when a family tells us the window is coming, and we shift back afterwards.

Parents have a part in this that is easy to get wrong. The instinct is to increase pressure in the collision fortnight, and the effect is usually to add anxiety to a student who already knows what is outstanding. The more useful contribution is logistical: protecting two quiet evenings, moving a family commitment, and asking once a day what the next concrete step is rather than how the work is going.

sections.heading: The Middle Years task calendar, where habits are set
paragraphs: Middle Years assessment runs on a calendar of criterion-marked tasks spread through the year, each marked once against task-specific descriptors. There is no terminal paper, so a weak task cannot be revised away; it has to be outscored by later work. That changes what a parent should watch.

Watch the criterion letters, not the overall grade. A student can be diligent, produce neat work and still score poorly on the criterion that asks for evaluation or for justified conclusions, because nobody has shown them what a higher level of achievement looks like on that specific criterion. The descriptors are published and the school issues task-specific versions; reading them with the student before the next task is the single most efficient intervention available in these years.

The weekly rhythm should match that. A Middle Years student does not need an hour of general homework supervision; they need forty-five minutes aimed at the criterion their next task will be marked against. When that is the shape, three or four sessions before a task often lift the achievement level, and the improvement transfers because the skill is reusable.

There is also a transition dimension. Students moving from the Middle Years into the Diploma meet written method, independent research and real deadlines all at once. Students moving from the Middle Years into a British-curriculum Year 10 meet terminal papers for the first time. Both transitions benefit from a few sessions aimed at the new demands rather than at subject content, and both are usually left until the first disappointing report.

sections.heading: The UAE academic year: Ramadan, Eid, exam leave and the long summer
paragraphs: A plan written as though the year is twelve uniform months will lose six to eight weeks without anybody deciding to lose them. The UAE calendar has a shape, and the shape is knowable in advance.

Ramadan shortens school days and moves usable hours. Afternoons are low-energy; late morning at the weekend and after Iftar are productive. For a DP2 student with an internal assessment deadline inside the month, the plan has to be rewritten before it starts. Eid then removes several days at short notice from a term that may already be tight. Neither is a disruption if it is in the plan; both are if they are not.

Exam leave is the one families forget. Once study leave starts, school teaching stops, and a student who has relied on school structure suddenly has unstructured days. Some use them superbly; many do not. A short daily check-in through study leave is often worth more than a weekly lesson during term, and it costs less than a rescue in the final fortnight.

The long summer is the opportunity. It is the quietest working window of the programme, it falls between DP1 and DP2, and three or four sessions can settle an exploration question or clear a content backlog. Families on this corridor often travel for part of it; because lessons are online, the slot follows the student with a timezone adjustment rather than ending at the airport.

Added together, these periods account for a large part of the year, which is why a plan written in September and never revisited tends to deliver fewer sessions than the family paid for in attention and intention. Looking at the calendar twice a term takes ten minutes and is the cheapest quality control available.

sections.heading: What a term of IB support costs at market rates
paragraphs: The useful unit for a family is a term, because that is the commitment a school year is actually made of. A term is roughly twelve teaching weeks, so a weekly slot is twelve hours and a twice-weekly arrangement is twenty-four.

Market rates first, so the arithmetic is transparent. Across published UAE rate cards, budget online tutoring starts around AED 45 an hour, a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed, and named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 and above. Published packages include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's Dubai estimates, read in October 2026, translate a weekly session into roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month with a qualified tutor.

At term scale, that means a weekly slot with a qualified online tutor is in the region of AED 1,800 to 3,600 per subject per term. The in-home equivalent sits meaningfully higher for the same twelve hours, and the difference is travel. For a family in central Sharjah, where journeys are shorter than on the southern corridor, the premium is smaller - but it still buys a car rather than better teaching.

These are market figures, published so a family can judge any quote against something real, including ours. There is no IB Gram price list on this page; ask us and start with the free trial. What we would add is that the cheapest effective pattern is rarely the most expensive one: a fortnightly check-in for Theory of Knowledge plus a weekly hour in the one subject that is genuinely blocking the grade usually outperforms four weekly slots spread thin.
