Criteria explained by letter with marks attached before drafting
Feedback on the student's own draft, never a rewrite
No rolling subscription once the piece is submitted

modes.title: Exam-term intensity
modes.description: Raised frequency in the run-up to the May session, built on timed papers rather than new content. This is the expensive format and it should be short. Families who have done steady work through DP1 need weeks of it; families starting from nothing in DP2 need months, which is the single clearest illustration of why early spending is cheaper than late spending.
bullets: Two or three shorter sessions a week for a defined run
Every session opens with a marked paper, not a topic list
Mark-scheme language taught from official command terms
Slots shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan where needed

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Al Suyoh costs a month
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure because that is the figure a household actually feels. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for weekly one-hour sessions put the budget tier at roughly AED 240-600 a month, the middle tier at AED 600-1,200 and specialist exam-year support at AED 1,000-2,000 or more. Packages advertised in this market sit inside those bands: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. The online package therefore buys twice the contact hours for roughly half the money, and that gap is the subject of this whole page.

Convert those to hourly bands and the structure becomes visible. Published figures run from AED 45-65 at EdFlik's budget end and AED 33-52 at Tutopiya's, through AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, up to AED 180-350 for in-home one-to-one on Bestimate's table and AED 500 quoted by independent home tutors. TutorChase lists AED 270 and BartyED publishes AED 650 at the examiner tier. None of these are IB Gram prices; they are what the market publishes, and they are published here because three of six ranking pages in this cluster publish no price at all.

The table below converts the bands into monthly totals at the frequencies an Al Suyoh Diploma family actually books, so you can match a quote to a band rather than guess. Two points are worth holding. First, the jump from one session a week to two does not double the benefit but does double the cost, so the second session should be justified by something specific rather than general anxiety. Second, the exam-year specialist band exists because that is when demand concentrates, which means the same work bought a year earlier sits in a cheaper band.

sections.heading: Where the money stops reaching the teaching
paragraphs: Three components of a tutoring quote do nothing for your child's grade, and all three are avoidable. The first is travel. A tutor driving to Al Suyoh from Sharjah city or across the Dubai border absorbs a round trip through the E311 at the hour it is worst, and either prices it into the hour or limits how many students they take, which prices it in anyway. Bestimate's in-home band sits AED 30-200 an hour above the online band for a qualified tutor. That spread is the car, not the teaching.

The second is generalism. A tutor covering six subjects across three boards spends part of every session working out what the specification requires, and the parent funds that preparation in real time. The difference shows up in the first fifteen minutes of a trial lesson: a specialist asks whether your child is on Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation and which option topic the school chose, and then starts diagnosing. A generalist asks what the student finds difficult.

The third is late timing, and it is the most expensive of the three. Work bought at exam-term intensity in the spring of DP2 sits in the AED 1,000-2,000-plus monthly band on Bestimate's own estimates. The same material taught at one session a week through DP1 sits in the AED 600-1,200 band and produces better coursework, because an Internal Assessment taught over eight weeks can be taught, whereas one addressed ten days before a school deadline can only be hurried. Nothing about the hourly rate changes; the quantity of hours needed changes.

There is a fourth cost that is harder to see, which is a wrong tier decision made early. An IGCSE student entered for the Core tier when they could manage Extended, or a Diploma student taking HL in a subject they should take at SL, has a ceiling placed on their result before any tutoring happens. Two sessions spent on that decision in the term it is made is the cheapest money in this entire page, and almost nobody spends it.

A generalist bills preparation time as teaching time
The same syllabus costs more per grade point in DP2 than in DP1

sections.heading: What the in-home premium actually buys
paragraphs: It is worth being fair to the in-home option, because for some students it is the right purchase. Having an adult physically present enforces attention in a way a screen does not, particularly for younger children and for students who will not stay on task without supervision. Physical apparatus can be handled. A parent can see what is happening without asking. Those are real benefits and a family paying AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's band is not being defrauded; they are buying presence.

The question is whether presence is what your particular child needs. For a Diploma student working towards written papers, the limiting factor is almost always the quality of the diagnosis rather than the room. The tutor marks a timed paper on screen, annotates it live against the mark scheme, and the student keeps the annotated file. That is not a degraded version of a face-to-face lesson; for paper technique it is arguably better, because the artefact survives the session.

What the premium does not buy is subject depth, and this is the point the market avoids. Travel narrows the pool to specialists prepared to drive to a plotted suburb in southern Sharjah on a weekday evening. For Mathematics AA HL or Chemistry HL that pool may contain nobody at all, and a family paying the in-home premium can end up with a generalist at specialist prices. Remove the drive and the constraint becomes the timetable rather than the map.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE, which means this comparison is not a sales device dressed as advice. Home visits are offered only in India. If what your child needs is somebody physically in the room, the honest recommendation is to hire that locally and we will say so.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the context of a Sharjah school year
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means little until it sits next to the other education costs in the household. Dubai's regulator provides a useful anchor for the wider UAE picture: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Sharjah fees are approved by its own authority rather than KHDA, but the direction of the regional conversation matters when a family is planning a two-year Diploma budget.

Scale matters too. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for seven per cent of enrolment against thirty-seven per cent for the UK curriculum and twenty-six per cent for the Indian. That IB share explains the supply problem an Al Suyoh family runs into. IB specialists are a minority of a minority, and in an inland Sharjah suburb the local count of them approaches zero, which is why in-home IB quotes here sit at the top of the band.

The table puts the pieces side by side. The point is not that tutoring is cheap or expensive but that it is comparable in size to other decisions families make without agonising, and that its cost is far more controllable than most of them. A finite coursework block has a knowable total. An exam-term intensive does not, unless you set one before it starts.

One further item belongs in any honest cost table, which is the private-candidate route. A student sitting Cambridge or Pearson papers outside their school pays entry fees to a registered centre, and those fees are set by the centre rather than by any tutoring provider. Anyone quoting you a single figure that bundles tuition and entry is bundling two things with different owners.

sections.heading: How many hours a Diploma subject actually needs
paragraphs: Families ask how many sessions are required and are usually given a number that suits the seller. The honest answer is that it depends on the gap, and that the gap is diagnosable in one lesson. A student who understands the content but loses method marks needs technique work, which is a short run of marked papers and can be six to ten sessions. A student missing foundational material from an earlier year needs rebuilding, which is a term or more. Those two students look identical on a report card and need entirely different budgets.

The second variable is how many subjects. One subject at one session a week is a sustainable line in a household budget and produces a clear signal about whether tutoring is helping. Three subjects simultaneously produces a large bill and a muddy signal, because when a grade moves you cannot tell which intervention moved it. The sensible sequence for an Al Suyoh Diploma family is one subject, reviewed after six weeks, then a decision about the second.

The third is timing within the two-year course. Coursework is the predictable expense and it is predictable because the school publishes the deadlines. A Chemistry Internal Assessment, a Mathematics exploration, an Economics commentary set and the Extended Essay all have known dates, and each can be supported in a finite block booked in advance. Families who plan around those dates spend less in total than families who respond to them, for the same reason that booking a flight early costs less than booking it at the airport.

What a tutor should never do is tell you a number of hours before seeing your child work. If a provider quotes you a package length before the trial lesson, they are selling a product rather than diagnosing a problem, and the length will be whatever their packages come in.
bullets: Technique gaps: roughly six to ten sessions of marked-paper work
Foundational gaps: a term or more, with content rebuilt in order
Coursework: a finite block of four to eight sessions, booked ahead of the school deadline
Start with one subject and review after six weeks before adding a second

sections.heading: Spending the Diploma budget in the right term
paragraphs: The two-year shape of a Diploma gives an Al Suyoh family four distinct spending windows, and almost all avoidable overspend comes from skipping the first two. The first window is the term after subject selection, when HL and SL choices can still be reviewed. Two sessions here, reading the student's actual work rather than their predicted grades, can change a six-subject package that was never going to work. Nobody charges much for that and almost nobody buys it.

The second window is the middle of DP1, when Internal Assessment research questions are being chosen. A research question that cannot be controlled with the apparatus available, or an exploration topic with no mathematics in it, is a problem that compounds for a year. A finite block here is cheap and prevents the single most common late disaster. The third window is the start of DP2, when a student's genuine position across six subjects becomes visible and a decision about where to concentrate can be made on evidence.

The fourth window is the run-in to the May session, and it is the expensive one. Bestimate's specialist exam-year band of AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month exists because this is when everybody wants the same tutors. A family arriving here having used the first three windows needs a short, targeted intensive. A family arriving here having used none of them needs months of it across multiple subjects, at the top of the band, with coursework already submitted and unfixable.

This is not an argument for spending more overall. It is an argument for spending the same money earlier, which in this market reliably buys more. The free trial lesson exists partly so that a family can test the diagnosis before committing to any of these windows, and nothing obliges you to book afterwards.

sections.heading: Two checks worth running before any money changes hands
paragraphs: The first check is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. UAE government guidance records that it is granted free of charge for two years, and that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any amount quoted to you is somebody's invention. Because the permit is free, a tutor without one has no cost justification for the omission.

Eligibility is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, sets out the application route through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time and no fee. That page, not a tutoring site, is where to read the current position. One restriction catches families out: a school teacher may not take paid private work with students enrolled at their own school, a point Abu Dhabi's ADEK has made in professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff as reported by Gulf News.

The second check is the honesty boundary, and it is a cost question as much as an academic one. Ask what the tutor will do with a draft Internal Assessment. The acceptable answer is that they will read it, mark it against the published criteria and tell your child what to rewrite. Any answer involving producing, finishing or polishing the work to submission is describing something that puts your child at risk of a malpractice finding. The research behind this page found a provider in this market selling completed Internal Assessments outright at a four-figure price. That is not tutoring at a premium; it is a different transaction with the consequence transferred to the student.
Neither check costs anything and both take minutes. Together they eliminate most of the ways a tutoring budget can be genuinely wasted, as opposed to merely spent inefficiently.

sections.heading: What no amount of money should buy
paragraphs: A clear boundary is worth more to a parent than a discount, so here is ours stated plainly. A tutor teaches, explains, models, questions and gives feedback. A tutor does not produce assessed work. For a Diploma student that means the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition, and every commentary are the student's own, written by the student, start to finish. Where a draft is weak, the feedback names the criterion that is not met and the student goes back to it.

What is available is substantial and often undersold. The criteria explained letter by letter with their mark allocations before drafting begins. Three candidate research questions discussed and two of them ruled out for practical reasons. Referencing taught properly rather than bolted on. A worked example on a different topic so the student can see the shape without borrowing the content. A marked draft with criterion references. A rehearsal of the supervisor meeting. That is a real service and it is what the money buys.

Equally, nobody should sell you an outcome. No tutor can promise a grade, a points total or a university place, and the Diploma does not work that way in any case. What a tutor can do is make the next assessment better prepared than the last one, and say honestly after six weeks whether the sessions are producing that. If the answer is no, the right response is a different tutor or a different diagnosis, not more hours at the same rate.

The last item on this list is pressure. Tutoring is not required for Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry through its own channel; a tutoring service describes it and points you there, and that is the whole of its role.
bullets: Available: criteria by letter, research-question design, referencing, marked drafts
Not available at any price: drafting, rewriting to completion, supplying text
No tutor can promise a grade, a points total or an admission
Tutoring is not a requirement of equivalency, admission or progression

process.title: Send the subject, level and the monthly budget you have
process.description: Tell us the IB subject, whether it is HL or SL, the date of the next assessment and the monthly figure you are working with. A realistic budget shapes an honest recommendation: one subject done properly beats three done thinly, and we would rather say that at the enquiry than after two months.

process.title: Get a straight availability answer
process.description: Within the day you are told whether a specialist for that exact subject and level is free in your child's evening window, free at another time, or not available this term. Al Suyoh school runs usually decide which, so include the time your child is actually home and free to work.

process.title: Use the free trial lesson as a diagnosis
process.description: The first lesson costs nothing, takes no card details and is a real lesson. Send a recent marked paper beforehand. At the end, ask the tutor what the gap is and roughly how many sessions it implies. A specialist will answer with a range and a reason; a seller will answer with a package.

process.title: Book one subject, review after six weeks
process.description: A fixed weekly slot with a stated goal, written notes after each session, and an explicit review at six weeks on whether it is working. Expand to a second subject only if the first one produced evidence. If the match is wrong, say so and it changes rather than running on.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the competitor page or rate table it came from, with the tier it describes. There is no invented IB Gram price list here and no hidden quote. Three of six pages ranking for these queries publish no price at all, and two of the rest quote in US dollars.

whyPoints.title: The travel cost is removed, not disguised
whyPoints.description: Online delivery takes the round trip to a southern Sharjah suburb out of the hourly rate instead of burying it there. That is most of the AED 30-200 gap between Bestimate's in-home and online bands, and it is the part of a quote that does nothing for your child's grade.

whyPoints.title: A pool that is not limited by who will drive
whyPoints.description: Matching on syllabus and level rather than distance means an Al Suyoh family can reach a Mathematics AA HL or Chemistry HL specialist who would never appear on a local shortlist. In an inland plotted suburb that is the difference between a specialist and a generalist at specialist prices.

whyPoints.title: Finite blocks where the work is finite
whyPoints.description: Coursework support is sold as a defined run with a stated endpoint, so the total is knowable before it starts. Rolling subscriptions suit providers and not families, and an Internal Assessment has a submission date rather than an indefinite need.

whyPoints.title: An honest no when the answer is no
whyPoints.description: If no specialist covers the subject at the level needed, or none is free in your window, you hear that at the enquiry stage. If your child genuinely needs an adult in the room, you hear that too, because IB Gram sells no in-home option in the UAE and so has nothing to gain by pretending.

faqs.question: What does an IB home tutor in Al Suyoh cost per month?
faqs.answer: Working from published market figures rather than ours: Bestimate's 2026 estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget tier, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Advertised packages in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. For one IB subject at one session a week with a qualified tutor, the middle band is the realistic planning figure for an Al Suyoh household.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home rate in Al Suyoh higher than an online one?
faqs.answer: Mostly travel. Bestimate's 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Al Suyoh is an inland plotted suburb, so a tutor is committing to a round trip through the E311 corridor at peak. They either price that into the hour or restrict how many students they take, which prices it in anyway. The remainder of the gap is scarcity: few IB specialists will drive out here on a weekday evening.

faqs.question: Is one session a week enough for an IB subject?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes, provided it starts early enough. One sixty or ninety-minute session a week in a single subject is a sustainable household line and gives a clean signal about whether tutoring is helping, because nothing else changed. Two sessions a week doubles the cost without doubling the benefit, so the second should answer a specific diagnosis rather than general worry. Where one session is not enough is when a student is missing foundational material from an earlier year, which is a rebuilding job and visible in the first lesson.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects absorb the most tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at HL is the most expensive subject to leave late, because the method marks depend on written justification that has to be rebuilt rather than revised. Chemistry and Physics at HL follow, largely because the Internal Assessment concentrates hours. Biology is content-heavy but technique-light, so it responds to a short run on command terms. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are method problems and usually need only three or four well-aimed sessions each, which makes them the best value in the Diploma.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a home in Al Suyoh?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Al Suyoh families run one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Sharjah school day. That removes the travel component from the hourly rate and widens the tutor pool beyond whoever is prepared to drive to an inland plotted suburb. If your child genuinely needs an adult physically in the room, the honest recommendation is to hire that locally, and we will say so.

faqs.question: When in the Diploma is tutoring money best spent?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families spend it. The cheap windows are the term after subject selection, when HL and SL choices can still be reviewed, and the middle of DP1, when Internal Assessment research questions are chosen. Both are short interventions that prevent expensive problems. The costly window is the run-in to the May session, which sits in Bestimate's AED 1,000-2,000-plus specialist band precisely because demand concentrates there. The same material taught a year earlier needs fewer hours and produces better coursework, so early spending buys more at the same rate.

faqs.question: How do I tell a specialist from a generalist in one lesson?
faqs.answer: Listen to the first five minutes. A specialist asks whether your child takes Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, which option topic the school chose, and what the last marked paper showed, then begins diagnosing from it. A generalist asks what the student finds difficult and works from there. The difference matters financially as well as academically, because a generalist spends part of each paid session working out what the specification requires, and that preparation is billed to you as teaching time.

faqs.question: Is a budget tutor from University City worth considering?
faqs.answer: At the right level, yes. University students are explicitly eligible for the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and the budget end of the published market, around AED 45-65 at EdFlik and AED 33-52 at Tutopiya, is largely this group. For lower secondary maths or structured homework supervision that can be sensible and nearby, since University City is a short drive from Al Suyoh. For an HL science or a Diploma Internal Assessment it usually is not, because the work needs somebody who has marked those papers against the published criteria.

faqs.question: Can a tutor finish my child's Internal Assessment if time is short?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider that offers to is describing a malpractice route rather than a service. Under IB academic-honesty rules the work must be the student's own; submitting material produced by somebody else risks a finding against your child, not against the seller. What a tutor can do is teach the criteria letter by letter, help narrow a research question, explain what Evaluation rewards, and mark a draft your child wrote with instructions on what to rewrite. That takes weeks, which is why coursework blocks are booked a term ahead.

faqs.question: Do I pay for the trial lesson in Al Suyoh?
faqs.answer: No. The first lesson is free, takes no card details and carries no obligation to book afterwards. It is a real lesson rather than a sales call, so send a recent marked paper beforehand and expect the tutor to work from it. At the end, ask what the gap is and roughly how many sessions it implies; a specialist will give a range with a reason attached. If you decide not to continue, nothing further happens and no package is opened.

faqs.question: What school fee context should an Al Suyoh family plan against?
faqs.answer: Sharjah school fees are approved by the emirate's own authority rather than by Dubai's regulator, but the regional picture is useful. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai's sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, with the IB accounting for seven per cent of enrolment, which explains why IB specialists are scarce and in-home IB quotes sit high.

faqs.question: Does the permit a tutor needs cost them anything?
faqs.answer: No, which is why its absence is telling. UAE government guidance states that the private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE, is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time and no fee, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so any figure quoted to you is unverified.

faqs.question: Can an Al Suyoh child be tutored privately by their own class teacher?
faqs.answer: Not if the child is enrolled at that teacher's school. Abu Dhabi's ADEK has set professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibiting paid private tutoring of students at their own school, as reported by Gulf News, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct making the same point. So the apparent shortcut of hiring the class teacher after hours is not one. Treat the offer as a reason to look elsewhere, and verify the current policy wording with the school or the regulator rather than relying on a tutoring site.

faqs.question: Will more hours closer to the exams fix a weak DP2 position?
faqs.answer: Partly, and expensively. Timed-paper technique responds quickly, so a short intensive in the run-in to the May session can move marks that are being lost to method rather than knowledge. What an intensive cannot fix is submitted coursework, which is closed, or a missing foundation across a two-year syllabus, which needs time nobody has left. That asymmetry is the argument for spending in DP1 instead: the same money buys teaching there and buys triage here, and no honest tutor should promise a grade either way.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-suyoh.closingHeading: Set the monthly figure first, then book the trial
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-suyoh.closingBody: If you are weighing an IB home tutor in Al Suyoh, decide the monthly figure before you compare hourly rates, because the hourly rate is where the travel hides. Send the subject, the level, the next assessment date and the budget you are working with, and you will get an honest answer about whether a specialist is free in your child's evening window and what a sensible schedule looks like inside that figure. The first lesson is free, runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and should end with a diagnosis rather than a package. Every rate quoted on this page carries the source it came from, and none of them is ours.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-taawun.tutorsIntro: Tutors below are listed against the Diploma component they have actually marked, not against a subject in general. That distinction is what this entire page is about, because the commonest form of waste in this market is paying a good teacher to do the wrong job.

intro.heading: The second-time question
paragraphs: Al Taawun sits at the Sharjah end of the Al Mamzar lagoon, towers facing the water with the Dubai boundary a few minutes west and Al Khan immediately south. It is a settled, dense residential district, and a high proportion of the Diploma families who contact us from here have hired a tutor before. Their question is not what it costs. It is why the last one made so little difference.

That is a better question than the one most tutoring pages answer, and it has specific answers. Diploma tutoring money disappears in a small number of recognisable ways, and almost none of them involve a bad tutor. They involve a competent person doing work that was not the work required: explaining content when a component needed diagnosing, covering a syllabus when a deadline needed clearing, or providing company when a criterion needed reading.

The published rates set the stakes. Qualified online subject tutors advertise from roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase at around AED 270, and premium named provision advertised as high as AED 650. In-home visits including travel run from about AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table placing the usual band at AED 180 to 350. A term of weekly sessions at the middle of those ranges is a serious sum, and a term is also what gets lost when the work is misaimed.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. On this corridor that removes the travel component from the rate and removes the waste that comes from a visit cut short by an unpredictable afternoon, which is one of the seven ways money disappears.

What follows is a taxonomy and a tool. The seven failure modes, with how each one looks from a parent's side, what it costs and the counter to it. An audit you can run in twenty minutes on an arrangement you already have, or on one being proposed. An honest section on why a likeable tutor and a pleasant session are not the product. And a method for deciding in advance when to stop, which is the single discipline that prevents the most expensive failure of all.

One note on dates. We publish no International Baccalaureate examination or results dates on these pages, because the board's own site cannot be verified by automated checking and a wrong date is something a parent acts on. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session; your school's coordinator holds the internal calendar that governs the year.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-taawun.programmesIntro: The failure modes differ by stage, because what the student needs differs. These four are where money most often goes astray.

programmes.name: The summer before the Diploma
programmes.description: Rarely bought, and when it is bought it is rarely wasted. Four to six sessions on fluency, extended writing and research-question design. The waste here is of a different kind: not spending at all, and then paying several times as much for emergency work in the first autumn.
programmes.countryNote: In this district the move into a Diploma cohort often means a change of school and sometimes a crossing of the emirate boundary, which leaves coverage gaps nobody has mapped. One mapping session before term identifies them while they are still cheap to close.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 1
programmes.description: The commonest waste here is general weekly support bought because a report was disappointing, with no component named and no diagnosis made. It feels responsible and produces very little, because nothing in the first year is yet urgent enough to focus the work.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student crossing the boundary daily has roughly two usable weekday evenings. A weekly session that occupies one of them without a specific target is not neutral; it displaces the independent practice that converts teaching into marks.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 2
programmes.description: The expensive year for waste as well as for spend. Sessions spread across three struggling subjects, content taught after coursework deadlines have passed, and blocks continued past the point where the evidence said stop. All three are avoidable with a prior agreement about priority and stopping.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the school for its published internal deadline calendar in the autumn. Money spent teaching content in a subject whose coursework deadline has already passed is the clearest form of waste in the programme, and it is entirely preventable.

programmes.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
programmes.description: Waste here is usually in timing rather than in choice. Coaching bought when a draft is already late can only improve the draft; coaching bought when the research question is being chosen can change the ceiling. The same money, at two points in the year, buys very different outcomes.
programmes.countryNote: Up to three points sit in the combination of these two components, and a low grade in either can create a failing condition. That makes the core the place where under-spending is itself a form of waste.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches

subjects.description: The classic waste is a tutor defaulting to Analysis habits: algebraic drill for a student who loses marks by failing to interpret a figure in context, or who cannot drive a graphing calculator at speed.

subjects.description: Content revision bought for a student whose investigation is losing marks on the evaluation criterion. The criterion wants the effect of each limitation on the conclusion, and no amount of additional content addresses that.

subjects.description: The waste is timing. Coaching on a late draft improves the draft; coaching at the research-question stage changes what the component can reach. Same fee, very different return.

subjects.description: Thin supply makes a near-match tempting here, and a near-match in a language subject is the most complete form of waste in this list: the fee and the term both go.

sections.heading: What is actually being wasted
paragraphs: An IB home tutor in Al Taawun, in the sense families here use the phrase, is a Diploma subject specialist working one-to-one with one student. IB Gram provides that over live video to Sharjah families and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tuition is a service we run only in India. But the question most families in these towers arrive with is not about delivery. It is about why the previous arrangement achieved so little.

The answer is almost never that the tutor was bad. Teaching is a reasonably well-distributed skill and most people selling it can teach. The answer is usually that the work done was not the work required, and that nobody established what was required before the sessions started. A student loses marks on an evaluation criterion; a tutor revises content. A coursework deadline is three weeks away; a tutor works through the syllabus in order. A student cannot drive a graphing calculator; a tutor explains the mathematics.

That mismatch is invisible from the outside for a surprisingly long time. The sessions are pleasant, the student is engaged, homework gets done. What is absent is any evidence that the specific losses are closing, because nobody wrote down what the losses were. By the time a mock or an internal deadline exposes it, a term has gone.

Everything on this page is designed to make that mismatch visible early. The taxonomy below names the seven forms it takes. The audit after it is a twenty-minute test you can run on an arrangement you already have. And the stopping rule in the final sections is what turns the audit into a decision rather than a worry.
bullets: The problem is rarely a bad tutor; it is misaimed work

sections.heading: Seven ways Diploma tutoring money disappears
paragraphs: Each of these was observed repeatedly in families who came to us after a previous arrangement, and each has a cheap counter. They are listed in rough order of frequency rather than cost, although the last two are the most expensive.

The pattern across all seven is the same: a decision made without evidence, or a decision deferred until evidence arrived too late. The counters are correspondingly unglamorous — ask for marked work, name the component, agree a stopping rule, fix a time that holds. None of them require a better tutor; they require a better brief.

It is worth noticing which of the seven are the provider's responsibility and which are the family's. Placement into the wrong component and vagueness about coursework are ours. Buying before evidence exists, spreading across three subjects and continuing past the stopping point are usually the family's, and they are the three that cost most. That division is not an attempt to shift blame; it is where the leverage actually sits.
The table below is the version to keep. If an arrangement you are considering or already have contains two or more of these, it is likely to under-deliver whatever the hourly rate is.

A word about why these persist. None of the seven is anybody's deliberate choice, and several are produced by entirely reasonable instincts: a parent who buys quickly is responding to a disappointing report, a parent who funds three subjects is being fair between them, and a parent who keeps a likeable tutor is protecting a child's confidence. The failure modes survive because the honest alternative requires an awkward conversation at a point when nobody wants one. Writing the brief and the stopping rule down in advance is how a family avoids having to be unkind later.

sections.heading: The audit a parent can run in twenty minutes
paragraphs: This is a test rather than an argument, and it works on an arrangement you already have as well as on one being proposed. It needs no subject knowledge, which is the point: a parent should not have to understand Higher Level chemistry to tell whether chemistry is being taught usefully.

Ask your child six questions and look for specificity in the answers. What component are you working on with the tutor? Which criterion is costing you marks? How many marks does that criterion carry? What did you do differently in your last piece of work because of a session? What has the tutor refused to do with your draft? And what will you be able to do by the end of this block that you cannot do now?

A student in a well-aimed arrangement answers most of those in specifics, sometimes grudgingly. A student in a misaimed one answers in generalities: we go over the topics, he explains it well, it's helpful. Those are not complaints about the tutor and the student is not being evasive. They are evidence that nobody named a target, which is the diagnosis the audit exists to deliver.

Then ask yourself two questions. Can I name, in one sentence, what this block is supposed to change? And do I know what would make me stop? If either answer is no, the arrangement is at risk regardless of how good the teaching is, and the fix is a conversation rather than a different tutor.

sections.heading: Comfort is a real benefit and it is not the product
paragraphs: This section is the uncomfortable one. A likeable tutor who turns up, is patient with a tired teenager and makes a hard subject feel manageable is providing something genuinely valuable, particularly for a student under pressure in a six-subject programme. Families are right to want it and wrong to mistake it for the thing they are paying for.

The distinction matters because comfort is the reason blocks get extended past their useful life. A parent sees a child who is calmer about chemistry and concludes the money is working. A student who likes their tutor reports that sessions are helpful. Neither observation says anything about whether the evaluation criterion is still costing six marks, and that is the question the fee was meant to answer.

The practical test is whether anything in the student's written work has changed. Not their mood, not their confidence in conversation, but the work: a method line claimed, a limitation explained rather than listed, a figure interpreted in context, an essay planned to a word budget. Those are visible, and if none of them have appeared after four or five sessions, the arrangement is providing support rather than teaching.

Where comfort is genuinely the need — a student overwhelmed rather than behind — it is available more cheaply. Entry-level provision advertised in this market from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour supplies structure and company perfectly well. Paying specialist rates from AED 200 to AED 450 and above for reassurance is the most polite form of waste in this list, and the hardest to raise with a family who likes the person they have hired.

sections.heading: Group, centre or one-to-one for a Diploma student
paragraphs: Families here ask whether a cheaper format would have done, and for the Diploma specifically the answer is narrower than for IGCSE. The reason is where the marks sit.

A group class or a tuition centre course can retell a syllabus with structure, which helps a student who has fallen behind on content across a subject. For the examined papers that is a legitimate and cheaper purchase. What it cannot do is read one student's investigation against the published criteria, or test whether an Extended Essay research question can carry four thousand words. Those are one-to-one activities because they depend on one student's specific work.

Since internally assessed components sit inside every Diploma subject, and up to three points sit in the core, a family that uses only group provision is leaving the most improvable part of the grade untouched. The sensible combination, where budget is tight, is group or centre provision for content coverage and a small number of one-to-one sessions for the components. That is cheaper than weekly one-to-one across a subject and considerably more effective than group work alone.

On this corridor there is also a logistics argument. A centre course adds a round trip at exactly the hour the crossing is worst, which for a student already getting home after half past four is a meaningful cost in both time and energy. Where a centre option is chosen, a weekend timetable is worth seeking out for the same reason a weekend one-to-one session outperforms a weekday one here.

sections.heading: Deciding when to stop, before you start
paragraphs: The most expensive of the seven failure modes is continuing a block that is not working, and it is the one most easily prevented. The prevention is a sentence written before the first session: what evidence, by when, would justify continuing, and what evidence would justify stopping.

For a paper-based problem the standard is straightforward. A second timed paper at the midpoint, marked against the same criteria and compared with the first by topic. Movement in the areas the diagnosis named, not just in the total. For a coursework component it is a specific deliverable: a section lifted into a higher band against the same descriptors, or a research question narrowed into something answerable. For a technique problem, the student performing the specific task unaided.

Writing that down changes the conversation at the midpoint from a social one into an administrative one. Nobody has to decide whether they like the tutor; they have to read the evidence against a sentence everybody agreed to a month earlier. That is the only version of this decision that reliably gets made, because the alternative requires a parent to end an arrangement with somebody their child is fond of.

It also protects the provider from a different failure, which is being blamed for an outcome nobody defined. A block with a written target and a written stopping rule can succeed or fail honestly. A block with neither can only ever be continued, which is why so many of them are.
bullets: Write the continuing and stopping conditions before session one
Papers: a second timed paper compared by topic
Coursework: a section lifted into a higher band against the criteria

sections.heading: Permits, claims and the coursework boundary
paragraphs: Three things to check before money moves, all of which are free and none of which depend on judging teaching quality.

The permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, any page quoting an amount has invented it. The code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

The claims. Refuse any guarantee of a grade, a points total or a university place. Refuse any claimed approval, accreditation or licence from the Sharjah Private Education Authority, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Ministry of Education or an examination board — IB Gram holds none and claims none. Refuse any school presented as a partner or client, any rating or satisfaction figure without the number, date and method behind it, and any outcome-linked refund promise, which in practice is a marketing device rather than an enforceable term.

The coursework boundary. A tutor teaches the skill a component assesses, explains the published criteria and what their command words require, tests whether a topic or research question can carry the work, questions the student about their own reasoning and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor does not write, complete or rewrite any part of it. This region's market includes a provider advertising completed Internal Assessments for sale; that is academic malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. We also do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables.

faqs.question: We paid for a Diploma tutor last year and saw no difference. What went wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually that the work done was not the work required, rather than that the tutor was poor. The common versions: content revised while a coursework criterion kept losing marks; a subject named but no component identified; sessions spread across three struggling subjects; or a block continued past the point the evidence said stop. Run the audit on this page — six questions to your child about component, criterion, marks and what they changed — and the version that applied to you is usually obvious within twenty minutes.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether sessions are aimed at the right thing?
faqs.answer: Ask your child what component they are working on and which criterion is costing marks. A well-aimed arrangement produces specifics: the investigation, the evaluation criterion, six marks, and a named habit they changed in their last piece of work. A misaimed one produces generalities: we go over the topics, he explains it well. Neither answer is a complaint about the tutor; the second is evidence that nobody set a target, which is a brief problem rather than a teaching problem.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a Diploma tutor to a tower in Al Taawun?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, with the draft or paper on a shared screen. That removes the travel component from the rate and removes one of the seven failure modes on this page: a visit cut short or cancelled by an unpredictable afternoon on the crossing.

faqs.question: Our child likes the tutor but the grades have not moved. Is that worth keeping?
faqs.answer: It depends what you are buying. A likeable tutor who makes a hard subject feel manageable provides something real, particularly for a student under pressure in six subjects. But comfort is why blocks get extended past their useful life. Test for change in the written work rather than in the mood: a method line claimed, a limitation explained rather than listed, an essay planned to a word budget. If none of that has appeared in four or five sessions, you are buying support, which is available far more cheaply.

faqs.question: What is the single most expensive mistake in Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: Continuing a block that is not working, because the tutor is likeable and stopping feels like giving up on the child. It costs more than any hourly rate, and it is the easiest to prevent: write down before the first session what evidence by what date would justify continuing, and what would justify stopping. That turns the midpoint review into an administrative reading of evidence rather than a social decision nobody wants to make.

faqs.question: Should we fund all three subjects our DP2 child is struggling in?
faqs.answer: No. Spreading a limited number of sessions across three subjects in the second year reliably produces no visible movement in any of them, and it is one of the seven failure modes. Fund the one or two nearest a grade boundary, or where a coursework band can still be lifted, and deliberately leave the third for the term. A provider who accepts all three without discussing priority is taking an order rather than planning, and the result is predictable.

faqs.question: Would a group course at a centre have been cheaper and just as good?
faqs.answer: Cheaper, and good for one thing. A group course can retell a syllabus with structure, which helps a student behind on content for the examined papers. It cannot read your child's investigation against the published criteria or test whether an Extended Essay question can carry four thousand words, because those depend on one student's own work. Since internally assessed components sit inside every Diploma subject, group-only provision leaves the most improvable part of the grade untouched.

faqs.question: What should we ask a new tutor that we did not ask last time?
faqs.answer: Four things. Have you marked this specific component, and what are its criteria and mark allocations? What will you refuse to do with my child's draft? What is this block supposed to change, in one sentence? And what evidence would make you recommend stopping? The last question is the most revealing, because a provider who cannot describe a stopping condition is selling a subscription, and that is how the previous arrangement probably continued longer than it should have.

faqs.question: When is core coaching worth paying for, and when is it wasted?
faqs.answer: The same fee buys very different outcomes depending on timing. Coaching at the point a research question is being chosen can change what the component is capable of reaching, because a question that cannot carry four thousand words caps the essay however well it is written. Coaching on a draft that is already late can only improve that draft. Up to three points sit in the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, so under-spending early here is itself a form of waste.

faqs.question: How does a mistimed session time waste money on this corridor?
faqs.answer: Twice over. The fee goes, depending on cancellation terms, and the homework cycle breaks: work set at the previous session goes unmarked, so the next session is spent catching up and two weeks produce one week of progress. Worse, a student who sees a slot move twice stops treating it as fixed and stops preparing. Set the slot from measured arrival times across three ordinary weekdays and put the hardest work at the weekend, where the crossing is irrelevant.

faqs.question: Is a cheap tutor ever the right answer for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Where the need is structure rather than assessment, yes. Entry-level provision advertised in this market from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour supplies company and routine perfectly well, and for an overwhelmed student in a six-subject programme that can be exactly what is required. Where the marked work shows a criterion losing marks, it will not help, because reading a draft against band descriptors needs somebody who has marked the component. The marked work tells you which situation you are in.

faqs.question: Does a Diploma tutor working with a student in Al Taawun need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and its code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

faqs.question: Are money-back guarantees any protection against a wasted term?
faqs.answer: Very little. An outcome-linked refund requires published, enforceable terms and a provider willing to honour them, and in practice the conditions are narrow enough that the promise functions as marketing. It also returns only the fee, while the expensive loss in a wasted block is the term. We do not offer one. What protects a family instead is a free trial before commitment, a written target, a written stopping rule and a rematch mechanism if the match is wrong.

faqs.question: What should the first session with a new tutor produce?
faqs.answer: A written statement naming the component, the criterion or error type costing marks, and what the block will change. Not a reassurance that your child is capable, and not a plan to work through the syllabus from wherever the class has reached. Your child should be able to repeat the component and the criterion afterwards in their own words. If the first session produces none of that, the arrangement has already started down one of the seven failure modes on this page.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-taawun.closingHeading: Run the audit before you buy anything else
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-taawun.closingBody: Ask your child the six questions on this page, and ask yourself the two. If the answers are specific, keep whoever you have. If they are general, send us the marked work and any coursework drafts, tell us what the previous arrangement did, and we will name the component and the criterion, set a target and a stopping rule in writing, and arrange a free trial lesson with a specialist who has marked that component. Teaching runs one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time for Diploma families across Al Taawun and the Sharjah lagoon districts.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-zahia.tutorsIntro: Tutors are listed by Diploma subject and level, and matched to where a student is in the year as well as to what they study. A tutor taking on a Year 13 student in March is doing a different job from one taking on a Year 12 student in September, and the plan should say which.

intro.heading: The date decides what the hours can do
paragraphs: Two families in Al Zahia buy the same eight sessions of Diploma Chemistry. One starts in October of Year 12, the other in March of Year 13. They pay the same and they receive completely different value, because the work that is possible in each window is different and only one of them is still able to change the content picture.

This is the part of tutoring that almost nobody plans. Families decide on a subject, agree a rate, and start, and the question of what this particular term is supposed to achieve never gets asked. Then in May somebody is surprised.

The Diploma makes the problem sharper than most systems, because so much of the grade is settled before the exam. Internal Assessments are drafted, redrafted and submitted against the school's own internal deadlines. The Extended Essay has supervisor checkpoints running across more than a year. Theory of Knowledge has an exhibition and an essay with their own dates. By the time a student sits a paper, a substantial share of the points has already been banked or lost.

So the useful first question for an Al Zahia family is not "who is good at Chemistry" but "what does this term owe, and what is still movable". A Year 12 October has everything movable. A Year 13 March has papers movable, Internal Assessments largely fixed, and the Extended Essay gone. Buying the wrong work in the wrong window is the most common way Diploma tutoring money disappears.

Al Zahia itself shapes the weekly rhythm rather than the yearly plan. It is villa and townhouse housing immediately west of Muwaileh, with established routes to the Muwaileh and University City campuses, City Centre Al Zahia on the doorstep, and a dismissal journey that runs into the Maliha Road corridor congestion. In practice a household here is settled at around half past five, later with children at two schools.

None of this requires expertise in the subjects. It requires one document from the school and twenty minutes with a marked paper, and it puts a parent in a position to judge whether a proposed plan is aimed at something that is still movable.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. In-home visits are offered only in India, and there is no UAE office or centre. Al Zahia students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the draft or past paper on a shared screen. The calendar argument is part of why: a fixed weekly slot that cannot be lost to traffic is worth more in a deadline-driven year than a person in the room.

What follows is the Diploma year laid out as a plan — what eight weeks can achieve, what a term owes, the Extended Essay counted backwards, what to do with mock results, and how Ramadan and the Al Zahia week fit around it.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-zahia.programmesIntro: The programmes behind this search, described by what each one's calendar demands rather than by its philosophy. The deadline structure is the thing a family has to plan around.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked against lettered criteria added separately. The calendar consequence is that a Diploma year has three parallel timelines — taught content, internal coursework, and the core components — and they peak at different times, which is why a single weekly subject slot is sometimes the wrong purchase.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. This page deliberately publishes no IB exam or results date, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and a date a family plans around has to be right. Take every Diploma date from your school's IB coordinator, including internal deadlines, which are the ones that actually govern the term. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the Diploma in UAE private schools.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria per subject scored 0–8 and converted to a 1–7 grade. The calendar is gentler than the Diploma's, with assessment distributed through the year rather than concentrated, which is exactly why students arrive in Year 12 with no experience of managing parallel deadlines. The Middle Years Programme's own personal project in the final year is the first real rehearsal for that.
programmes.countryNote: The step into the Diploma is the most common reason Sharjah families start tutoring in Year 11, and the most useful timing for it is the summer term before Year 12 rather than the autumn after. A short block on the specific algebra, functions and proof the Diploma mathematics courses open with, plus practice at criterion-based marking, prevents the drop rather than reacting to it.

programmes.name: DP courses and partial routes
programmes.description: Not every student in a Sharjah IB school takes the full Diploma. Some take DP courses rather than the full certificate, which means subject exams and Internal Assessments but no Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge requirement. The calendar is correspondingly simpler and the tutoring plan should reflect that rather than importing a full-Diploma timeline.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency rules are published for the British and American tracks, and the sourced article states no IB points threshold, so no Diploma equivalency figure should be published without a Ministry page to cite. Families planning UAE university entry should take the equivalency question to the Ministry directly rather than to a tutoring service, which can describe the process but not perform it.

programmes.name: The A Level comparison
programmes.description: Often the real decision behind a Year 11 enquiry. Three or four subjects in depth, no Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge, and a calendar with far fewer parallel internal deadlines. For a student who manages content well but manages time badly, that simplicity is a genuine argument, and it is worth weighing honestly rather than treating the Diploma as automatically superior.
programmes.countryNote: The British-track equivalency route asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 — Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five — plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Those figures are sourced and may be relied on; the IB equivalent is not published in that source.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-zahia.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects Al Zahia families most often need, each with the point in the year at which it is most worth attention. Timing is part of the subject, not separate from it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is best started in the spring of Year 12, because a topic the student can genuinely own takes time to find. Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended investigation and needs dedicated work in the final two terms — it is the most common reason a predicted grade falls.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The exploration rewards genuine collected data, so the data-gathering decision has to be made early or the option disappears. Modelling questions are unfamiliar to students arriving from a British curriculum and are worth addressing in the first term rather than the last.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The Internal Assessment research question needs settling before the school's first internal deadline, and a weak question cannot be rescued by good analysis later. Organic mechanisms and energetics are the content priority once the coursework is submitted.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The Internal Assessment credits design and uncertainty handling rather than a correct result, which means the method needs critiquing before the data is collected. Higher Level extension topics are the exam-term priority because that is where candidates separate.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command-term technique is worth four to six sessions at any point in the year and lifts a plateau quickly. Content volume means the final term is about retrieval rather than new learning, so a late start should prioritise data-question practice.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Commentaries are written across the course against published articles, and choosing an article without diagram-able economics locks in a low mark at the time of choosing. Diagram and evaluation technique is the exam-term work and transfers across every paper.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral has a fixed school date and rewards rehearsal against the criteria rather than more reading. Paper 1 unseen analysis improves steadily with weekly practice, so it is the best use of a long run of sessions from early in Year 12.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The Internal Assessment needs real organisational data, and sourcing it is the first task and the one that stalls students for weeks. Evaluation technique for Paper 2 is the final-term priority and carries the top marks.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.levels: Language A, language acquisition and ab initio
subjects.description: Run alongside the Diploma in UAE private schools with their own assessment calendar inside the school. Separate streams exist for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ, so material from one route does not serve the other.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The longest timelines in the Diploma, with supervisor checkpoints running across more than a year, and the components where lateness costs most. Reflection-record marks are the easiest to secure honestly and the most commonly lost, because the record gets reconstructed at the end instead of kept.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can actually achieve
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the block most families buy, usually without deciding what it is for. It is enough time to change one thing properly and not enough to change three, and the difference between a useful eight weeks and a wasted one is whether that single thing was named on day one.

Technique objectives fit comfortably. Command-term discipline across a subject, structured extended-response writing, Economics diagram and evaluation habits, the structure of a Higher Level Paper 3 investigation, reading a mark scheme and self-marking — each of those is a four-to-eight-session piece of work with a visible outcome in the next assessment.

Content objectives fit only if they are narrow. Organic mechanisms. Equilibrium calculations. One strand of statistics. A whole syllabus does not fit into eight weeks alongside five other subjects, and a plan that implies it does is selling hours rather than outcomes.

Coursework objectives fit if the calendar allows them. Settling an Internal Assessment research question and critiquing a method is a genuine eight-week piece of work, but only before the school's internal deadline. After submission the same eight weeks has to go somewhere else, and a tutor who does not ask about the deadline will put it in the wrong place.

The table sets out what to expect from a block in each window. It is the thing to agree before the first invoice, because "we will see how it goes" is how three months of sessions end with the same marks disappearing.

sections.heading: The Diploma year as the school actually runs it
paragraphs: Parents plan around the exam. Schools run on internal deadlines, and those are the dates that decide whether a Diploma year goes smoothly. The two calendars are related but not the same, and a tutoring plan built on the wrong one is out of step from the start.

Across a Diploma, a student meets Internal Assessment draft deadlines in most of six subjects, Extended Essay supervisor checkpoints, a Theory of Knowledge exhibition, a Theory of Knowledge essay, and at least one full mock window — plus the Creativity, Activity, Service record, which carries no points but does carry a requirement. These cluster rather than spread, and the clusters are where students come apart.

The single most useful document a family can obtain is the school's internal deadline calendar for the year. It is not confidential, the IB coordinator will share it, and it converts a vague sense of pressure into a plan with dates on it. Most families have never asked for it.

What it changes in practice: a tutoring block can be positioned ahead of a cluster rather than inside it. Two Internal Assessment drafts due the same fortnight is a known event in October, not a crisis in February, and the hour that prevents the crisis is cheap while the hour that responds to it is not.

It also shows where there is slack. Most Diploma years have a quiet stretch, and that is when the slow-burn work — Extended Essay reading, exploration data collection, assessment-literacy teaching — actually gets done.

sections.heading: Internal Assessment deadlines belong to the school
paragraphs: A recurring misunderstanding worth clearing up: the deadlines that govern Internal Assessments are set by the school, not by the IB. The IB sets the criteria and the submission requirements on the school; the school sets the dates by which a student must produce drafts and final versions.

This has two consequences. The first is that your child's deadline is not the same as a friend's at another Sharjah school, so advice borrowed from another family's timeline may be wrong by a term. The second is that the school's date is the real one — missing it has consequences inside the school long before the IB is involved.

It also means the useful tutoring window is defined entirely by that date. Before it, the work is choosing a research question that can be answered, critiquing a method so the evaluation criterion has something to say, and reading the descriptors by letter so the student knows what each one wants. After it, that work is over and the hours have to move to papers.

The most expensive version of getting this wrong is a family buying Internal Assessment support in the term after submission because the mark was disappointing. The mark is banked. The hours are better spent on the written papers, where there is still a grade to change, and an honest tutor says so rather than taking the booking.
So the question to ask in the first conversation is simple and it is about dates: when is each Internal Assessment due at your school, and which of them have already gone?

sections.heading: The Extended Essay, counted backwards
paragraphs: The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece with a school supervisor, and its timeline runs across more than a year. It is also the component where lateness costs most, because several of its marks are awarded for a process that cannot be reconstructed.

The reflection record is the clearest case. Marks are available for engagement evidenced through reflection on the research process, and a record written in the final fortnight is a reconstruction rather than a record. Those are among the easiest marks in the Diploma to secure honestly and among the most commonly lost, purely through timing.

Counting backwards from submission: the final draft needs time with the supervisor; before that, a complete draft; before that, the research and reading; before that, a research question narrow enough to answer in 4,000 words — which is the decision that most often goes wrong, because a broad question feels safer and produces a descriptive essay.

The legitimate support at each stage is specific. Interrogating the research question before it is fixed. Questioning the argument. Reading the student's own draft against the published criteria and naming the gaps. Keeping the reflection habit alive. What never happens is text being supplied, paragraphs rewritten, or a draft edited to completion — IB rules treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate's diploma.
Practically, this is a component to book support for a term ahead rather than in the week a checkpoint arrives, because availability for it is seasonal and the whole value is in being early.

sections.heading: Mock results are the only free diagnosis you get
paragraphs: Mock exams are the single most valuable document in a Diploma year and the most wasted. Families look at the grades, feel something, file the papers, and buy tutoring based on the subject with the lowest number.

The grades are the least informative part. What matters is where the marks went, and a set of marked mocks across six subjects shows patterns a single paper cannot. If command-term losses appear in Biology, Economics and English alike, the problem is not three subjects; it is one habit appearing three times, and it is fixable in four to six sessions that improve all three.

The second pattern worth looking for is blank space against wrong answers. Blanks mean content was not reached or not known. Wrong answers mean understanding. Correct answers without reasoning mean marks thrown away by habit. Those three point at completely different purchases, and the mock papers tell you which one you have.

The third is timing. If marks drop sharply in the final third of every paper, the issue is pacing, and no amount of content teaching will touch it. That is an eight-week technique block with timed papers, which is a different product from weekly subject teaching.

Read the mocks before deciding what to buy, and take the reading to the first conversation. A tutor who sharpens your reading of them is worth hiring; one who ignores them and proposes to start from the beginning of the syllabus is proposing to sell you hours.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the UAE academic year
paragraphs: A plan that ignores the UAE calendar gets rewritten in practice, usually badly. Three features of the year matter enough to build around.

Ramadan shifts study patterns. School days shorten, evenings run later, and a post-Iftar study rhythm replaces the usual one. An intensive block scheduled straight through the month tends to be rescheduled session by session until it dissolves. The arrangement that survives is lighter sessions during the month, with the heavy work placed either side of it, and a post-Iftar slot for families who want continuity.

The long summer break is the other structural feature, and for Diploma students it is the most underused asset in the year. The gap between Year 12 and Year 13 is the only extended stretch with no school deadlines in it, which makes it the natural home for Extended Essay reading, exploration data collection, and the assessment-literacy teaching that nobody has time for in term.

Term holidays are shorter and have a different use: they are where a specific eight-week objective can be compressed into four, because there is no homework competing for the evening. Families who book a holiday block for technique work rather than content usually get more from it.

Travel is the fourth consideration and the one online delivery handles best. Households in this part of Sharjah travel during breaks, and a live-video slot follows a student rather than ending when they leave the emirate — which, in a year governed by internal deadlines, is often the difference between a draft arriving on time and arriving late.

sections.heading: Fitting the plan into a real Al Zahia week
paragraphs: A plan only counts if the sessions happen. More tutoring arrangements fail on scheduling than on teaching, and the failure is gradual: a slot is moved, moved again, and then quietly dropped while everyone agrees tutoring did not work.

Al Zahia's constraint is the Muwaileh dismissal journey. The community sits immediately west of the main campuses, with established routes in, but those routes feed into the Maliha Road corridor at the exact hour several large schools release. A household twenty minutes away by map is thirty-five minutes away at 2.45pm, and with children at two schools it is rarely settled before 5.15pm.

That makes 5.30pm the earliest honest option and 6pm the reliable one. Later slots work well for technique sessions, which need less fresh energy than new content, and weekend mornings are the best window for coursework blocks because they are long enough for a draft to be read and discussed in one sitting.

A home visit faces the same traffic from the other direction, and the time is paid for either as a surcharge or inside the rate. Market in-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure against AED 150 to AED 300 online for a qualified tutor, with Bestimate's Dubai table putting the usual in-home range at AED 180 to AED 350. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case; lessons are over live video.

The scheduling point that matters most in a deadline-driven year is the holding of the slot. A fixed weekly hour that cannot be lost to traffic is what makes a plan a plan, and it is worth more in March than any individual lesson.
