sections.heading: Dates we will not publish, and the regulator position
paragraphs: A page built on the calendar owes you an explanation of which dates it is willing to state and which it is not.

IB dates are not published here. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, which means no Diploma exam window or results date in this project has been confirmed from the organisation that sets it. A date a family builds a revision plan around has to be right, and a plausible date from a secondary source is worse than no date at all. UAE schools sit the May session; everything more specific comes from your school's IB coordinator, and the internal deadlines matter more to your plan anyway.

Board dates are published because the boards publish them. Cambridge runs its qualifications in June and November series for UAE candidates, with the February/March series offered to India only, and allocates every centre to one of six timetable zones with an explicit warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who used the wrong version. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026.

On regulation: Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Private tutoring is separately regulated — the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school and government-sector teachers, private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published.

And the disclosure: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed by or partnered with SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Students we support attend schools across Sharjah; that is the whole of the relationship.

process.title: Get the internal deadline calendar
process.description: Ask your school's IB coordinator for the year's internal dates — Internal Assessment drafts, Extended Essay checkpoints, Theory of Knowledge submissions, mock windows. It is not confidential and almost no family asks for it. It converts a vague sense of pressure into a plan with dates.

process.title: Read the last marked work or mocks
process.description: Look at where marks went rather than at the grades, and look for patterns across subjects. Command-term losses in three subjects are one habit appearing three times. Blanks, wrong answers and missing reasoning point at three different purchases.

process.title: Name the objective for the block
process.description: One thing, written down, before the first session: command-term discipline, Paper 3 investigation structure, an Internal Assessment research question settled before the school's deadline. Eight weeks changes one thing properly and three things not at all.

process.title: Take the free trial over live video
process.description: One session, no payment, at a time that survives the Al Zahia dismissal journey — 5.30pm at the earliest and 6pm where there are two school runs. Judge it on whether the tutor engaged with your calendar and your marked work rather than with the syllabus.

process.title: Review at the next school assessment
process.description: Not at a fixed number of weeks, but at the next real marked piece of work, because that is the only measure that counts. If the named objective has moved, continue. If it has not, change the plan or the tutor.

whyPoints.title: The plan starts from the calendar
whyPoints.description: What a term owes and what is still movable decides what the hours can achieve. A Year 13 March block and a Year 12 October block cost the same and can do entirely different things, and a plan that does not distinguish them is selling hours.

whyPoints.title: Internal deadlines drive the work
whyPoints.description: The school sets the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay dates, not the IB, and they differ between Sharjah schools. The first question in any plan is which of those dates have already passed, because a banked mark cannot be improved however many hours are bought.

whyPoints.title: The free stretches are used
whyPoints.description: The summer between Year 12 and Year 13 is the only extended period with no school deadlines in it, which makes it the natural home for Extended Essay reading and assessment-literacy teaching. Most families spend it waiting for term.

whyPoints.title: Dates are published only where sourced
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates appear here because those boards publish them. No IB exam or results date does, because the IB's own site could not be checked and a wrong date in a revision plan is worse than no date.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Al Zahia students are taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with the slot held weekly. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Sharjah or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is an India-only service and there is no UAE office.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line is explicit
whyPoints.description: Research questions interrogated, arguments questioned, the student's own draft read against the criteria. Never text supplied or a draft edited to completion. An operator in this market sells finished Internal Assessments, and the malpractice risk from that falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: We are halfway through Year 13. Is it worth starting IB tutoring now?
faqs.answer: Yes, but for different work than you may be imagining. Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay are largely banked by then, so the hours have to go to the written papers, where there is still a grade to move. That means timed-paper pacing, command-term discipline and retrieval rather than new content. A tutor who proposes to start from the beginning of the syllabus in the spring of Year 13 is proposing to sell you hours rather than a result.

faqs.question: What should an eight-week block of Diploma tutoring be aiming at?
faqs.answer: One named thing, agreed before the first session. Technique objectives fit well — command-term discipline, structured extended responses, Economics diagram and evaluation habits, Higher Level Paper 3 investigation structure. Narrow content objectives fit: organic mechanisms, equilibrium calculations, one strand of statistics. A whole syllabus does not fit alongside five other subjects. If nobody names the objective, the block ends with the same marks disappearing and everyone puzzled.

faqs.question: Who sets my child's Internal Assessment deadlines, the IB or the school?
faqs.answer: The school. The IB sets the assessment criteria and the submission requirements on the school; your school decides the dates by which drafts and final versions must be produced. Two Sharjah schools can therefore have deadlines a term apart, which is why advice borrowed from another family's timeline can be wrong. Ask your IB coordinator for the internal calendar — it is not confidential, and it tells you exactly which windows for coursework support are still open.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to our villa in Al Zahia?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits in Sharjah or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and there is no UAE office or centre. Al Zahia students are taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. In a year governed by internal deadlines, the practical argument is the holding of the slot: a fixed weekly hour that cannot be lost to the Maliha Road dismissal traffic is worth more in March than any single lesson.

faqs.question: What is the best use of the summer between Year 12 and Year 13?
faqs.answer: It is the only extended stretch in the Diploma with no school deadlines in it, which makes it the most underused asset in the two years. The work that belongs there is slow-burn: Extended Essay reading and a research question narrowed properly, exploration or Internal Assessment data collection, and the assessment-literacy teaching nobody has time for in term — reading criteria by letter, practising command terms, learning to self-mark against a scheme.

faqs.question: What should we look for in a full set of Diploma mock papers?
faqs.answer: Read them for patterns rather than grades. A set of marked mocks across six subjects shows things a single paper cannot: if command-term losses appear in Biology, Economics and English alike, that is one habit appearing three times and four to six sessions improves all three. Blank spaces mean content; wrong answers mean understanding; correct answers with no reasoning mean marks thrown away by habit. Marks collapsing late in every paper means pacing.

faqs.question: How should a Diploma revision block be planned around Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Lighter, yes; intensive, no. School days shorten, evenings run later, and a post-Iftar study rhythm replaces the usual one, so a heavy block scheduled straight through the month tends to be rescheduled session by session until it dissolves. The arrangement that works is maintenance sessions during the month, with the demanding work placed either side of it, and a post-Iftar slot for families who want continuity rather than a pause.

faqs.question: What time can sessions start for a family in Al Zahia?
faqs.answer: Half past five at the earliest, six o'clock reliably. Al Zahia sits immediately west of the main Muwaileh campuses, but the routes in feed the Maliha Road corridor at the hour several large schools release, so a journey of twenty minutes by map is thirty-five at 2.45pm. With children at two schools, households are rarely settled before 5.15pm. Later slots suit technique work, which needs less fresh energy than new content, and weekend mornings suit coursework.

faqs.question: Why will you not tell me when the IB exams are?
faqs.answer: Because the date could not be verified from the organisation that sets it. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no Diploma exam window or results date in this project has been confirmed at source, and a plausible date from a secondary site is worse than none when a family is building a revision plan on it. UAE schools sit the May session. For anything more specific, ask your IB coordinator, whose internal deadlines matter more to your plan in any case.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay this late?
faqs.answer: It depends what is left. If the research question is still open, a great deal — a question narrow enough to answer in 4,000 words is the decision that most often goes wrong. If the draft is complete, feedback against the published criteria is still useful. What cannot be recovered late is the reflection record, because marks there are awarded for engagement with the research process over time and a record written in the final fortnight is a reconstruction rather than a record.

faqs.question: My child is strong but keeps scoring mid-band on every Internal Assessment. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Almost always that the descriptors are being read as a task description rather than as a mark allocation. Internal Assessments are marked criterion by criterion, each lettered, with marks added separately — so a piece that answers the task without addressing every criterion sits mid-band regardless of quality. The useful fix is one piece of teaching rather than six: read the descriptors with the student, in their own words, before the next piece is drafted. The skill transfers across all six subjects.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a permit to teach my child in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts is published. Since it is free, there is no innocent reason to be without it.

faqs.question: Will the sessions continue if we travel during a school break?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in a deadline-driven year that is more useful than it sounds. Households in this part of Sharjah travel during breaks, and an in-home arrangement simply stops when the family leaves. A live-video slot follows the student, which often decides whether an Extended Essay draft or an Internal Assessment reaches the supervisor on time rather than late. The only thing to agree in advance is the time zone the session will run in while you are away.

faqs.question: When should I expect to see the plan working?
faqs.answer: At the next real marked piece of work rather than after a set number of weeks, because school assessments are the only measure that counts. Name the objective before the block starts — a criterion addressed, command terms answered to their own expectations, pacing holding to the end of a paper. Then read the next marked piece for that specific thing. If it has moved, continue. If it has not, change the plan or the tutor; leaving it is how a Diploma year is spent.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-zahia.closingHeading: Start with the calendar, not the subject
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-al-zahia.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB home tutor in Al Zahia, ask your school's IB coordinator for the internal deadline calendar before you ask anyone about rates. With those dates and your child's last marked work, you can see what this term still owes and what is already banked — and that tells you what to buy. Then take a free trial session over live video at a time that survives the Muwaileh dismissal journey, and judge it on whether the tutor planned from your calendar.

intro.heading: Three communities, one constraint
paragraphs: Aljada, Al Zahia and Muwaileh sit within a few minutes of each other in inland Sharjah, and a parent in any of them searching for an IB home tutor is effectively running the same search. The differences between the three are genuine. Aljada is newer, still filling, with its own school provision arriving in stages. Al Zahia is villa and townhouse housing with established routes to the Muwaileh campuses. Muwaileh itself holds the large school buildings and the dismissal traffic that comes with them.

Those differences change the commute by minutes, the school gate by a few hundred metres, and the time at which a household is settled enough to start a session. They do not change the thing that actually decides whether tutoring works, which is whether anyone in reach teaches your child's Diploma subject at your child's level and knows how it is marked.

That constraint is regional rather than local. The International Baccalaureate accounted for 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school students in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on UK curricula and 26 per cent Indian, across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula. IB provision in Sharjah is concentrated in a small number of continuum schools, and the specialist tutoring pool that follows a qualification is proportional to it. Moving from Aljada to Al Zahia does not increase the number of people who have taught Higher Level Chemistry Internal Assessments.

This matters because the instinct when a search returns little is to widen the radius. Widening the radius in inland Sharjah adds commute and adds almost no specialists, which is a bad trade. Widening the pool instead — the same tutor, reached over live video — adds specialists and no commute at all.

There is a reason to be explicit about this rather than write three cheerful neighbourhood pages. A page that invents a local specialist network is selling something nobody has, and a parent discovers the invention in the week the Internal Assessment is due. Stating where the real constraint sits lets a family plan around it a term early instead.

So this page is built as a comparison rather than a neighbourhood tour. It sets out what genuinely differs between Aljada and the communities around it, what genuinely does not, and then spends its length on the Diploma itself: where points come from, where they leak, what the core components need, and what a tutor may and may not do with work the student must own.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. In-home visits are a service offered only in India. Aljada students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the draft or past paper on a shared screen. The argument for it here is specific rather than general — in a community where the school provision is still arriving, the tutoring should not also be waiting on local supply.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-aljada.programmesIntro: Aljada households arrive at IB tutoring from three directions — a continuum school, a transfer in from a British curriculum, or a move between emirates mid-course — and each needs a different first month.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service alongside. Points come from subject grades plus up to three from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment marked against lettered criteria whose marks are added separately rather than pooled.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No Diploma exam or results date appears on this page: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a date a family plans around has to be right, so take every one from your school's IB coordinator. What is locally fixed is that Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the Diploma in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria per subject scored 0–8 and converted to a 1–7 grade by published boundaries. Process, communication and reflection are credited explicitly, which is why a capable student can sit at a 4 with correct work and an empty justification criterion. A tutor unable to name the four criteria for the subject is working from a general subject plan rather than the assessment.
programmes.countryNote: For families in a newly built community, the MYP question often arrives alongside a school move. A child transferring into an MYP year group from a British curriculum meets criterion-based marking for the first time and the first report looks worse than the learning is. A short diagnostic on the criteria, rather than on content, is the useful intervention in that first term.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations, which is why it rarely appears in tutoring searches. Where it does matter in a community like Aljada is continuity: a family planning a continuum route through to the Diploma is making a school decision now that shapes which assessment system their child meets at 11 and at 16.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. New communities across the region are where that expansion lands, so provision in a place like Aljada is a moving picture rather than a fixed one.

programmes.name: The A Level alternative
programmes.description: The route many Sharjah schools offer instead of the Diploma, and often the comparison a family in a new community is actually making. Three or four subjects in depth, no Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge, and a narrower profile. A student strong in two subjects and weak in languages usually does better here; one who wants breadth and a wide university list usually does better on the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency rules are published for the British track — five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five, plus one subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. The sourced article states no IB points threshold, so no Diploma equivalency figure should be published without a Ministry page to cite.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-aljada.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects Aljada families most often need, each with the component or criterion that decides the grade. These are the same subjects an Al Zahia or Muwaileh family needs, from the same pool.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended investigation rather than a question set, and it is the most common reason a predicted grade falls. The exploration is marked on communication, presentation, reasoning and personal engagement, and the last of those is routinely left empty by strong mathematicians.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-permitted work throughout, frequently misread as the easier route rather than the different one. The exploration rewards genuine collected data, which is a planning decision made in week one and not recoverable later.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the grade, with marks for state symbols, conditions and reasoning between steps. The Internal Assessment credits the student's own research question and method design; producing the textbook value earns nothing in itself.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth on shared topics and that additional material is where candidates separate. Extended responses reward stating the physical principle before the calculation. The Internal Assessment credits design and uncertainty handling rather than accuracy of result.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms do most of the damage. Outline, describe, explain, distinguish and discuss expect different structures and mark counts, and a student answering them identically settles near a 5 whatever they know. Data questions on unfamiliar experiments are trainable and seldom trained.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are credited piece by piece — axes, shift direction, new equilibrium stated — so a remembered sketch loses marks before the explanation begins. The Internal Assessment is commentaries on published articles, and choosing an article with no diagram-able economics in it locks in a low mark.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral and the Paper 1 unseen analysis move most under tutoring. Marks go to analysis of how meaning is constructed rather than to summary. Higher Level adds the essay, assessed on sustained argument rather than coverage.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the named organisation decides the band; a textbook-correct answer with no reference to the case sits at the bottom. Higher Level carries extension topics and a longer Paper 2. The Internal Assessment needs real organisational data, and sourcing it is the first real task.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.levels: Language A, language acquisition and ab initio
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the Diploma in UAE private schools. Separate streams exist for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ, so material from one route does not serve the other.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Worth up to three points between them and routinely under-supported. TOK is assessed through an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title; the Extended Essay is an independent 4,000-word piece with a school supervisor. Both are coached through feedback on the student's own drafts and never written for them.

sections.heading: Aljada against Al Zahia and Muwaileh: what actually differs
paragraphs: Worth doing this honestly rather than pretending each community is a distinct educational world. The differences across these three are operational, and they affect when a session can run and what an in-home visit would cost, not what is being taught.

Aljada's distinguishing feature is that it is still becoming itself. School provision is arriving in stages, which means a proportion of households are travelling to the established campuses in Muwaileh and University City, and a proportion are new to Sharjah entirely and have nobody local to ask about tutors. That second point is underrated: in an established neighbourhood the first tutor recommendation comes from a neighbour, and in a new one it comes from a search result.

Al Zahia's distinguishing feature is housing type. Villas and townhouses with gate security and driveways make an in-home visit slightly simpler to execute than a tower visit, which is why the in-home premium reads as marginally better value here. It does not change who is available to visit.

Muwaileh's distinguishing feature is the gates themselves. Several large campuses release into the same roads in a narrow window, so proximity to school is offset by dismissal congestion, and a household twenty minutes away by map is thirty-five minutes away at 2.45pm.

Set against those three differences is one similarity that outweighs all of them: the list of people who have taught Higher Level Diploma Chemistry, or coached an Economics commentary, or marked against Theory of Knowledge criteria, is the same list in all three communities. It is a short list, and it is short for regional rather than local reasons.

sections.heading: Why the specialist pool does not grow when you widen the radius
paragraphs: The instinct when a local search returns nothing is to search a wider area. It is the right instinct for a plumber and the wrong one for a Diploma tutor, and the reason is arithmetic.

Specialist supply follows qualification share. International Baccalaureate students were 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school population in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on UK curricula and 26 per cent Indian, across 227 schools offering 17 curricula. Sharjah's IB provision is concentrated in a handful of continuum schools. So the population of people who have actually taught a Higher Level Diploma science in this emirate is small in absolute terms, and it does not distribute itself evenly across communities waiting to be found.

Adding fifteen minutes of radius from Aljada reaches Al Zahia, Muwaileh and University City. It adds a meaningful number of capable content tutors — University City's undergraduate supply is real, and published budget rates of AED 33 to AED 150 an hour reflect it. It adds almost no Diploma assessment specialists, because they were never there to begin with.

Adding a wider pool instead changes the arithmetic entirely. The same specialist, reached over live video, is available to Aljada, Al Zahia and Muwaileh equally, at the market's online band of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour rather than the AED 180 to AED 500 that in-home visits command with travel inside the figure.

This is also why the answer on this page is the same as the answer on the equivalent page for the next community over. Not because the pages are interchangeable, but because the constraint being described is regional. A page that pretended Aljada had its own private supply of Theory of Knowledge coaches would be inventing something to sell.

sections.heading: Where Diploma points actually come from
paragraphs: Families comparing tutoring options often have no clear picture of where the 45 points are earned, which makes it hard to judge whether a tutoring plan is sensibly targeted. Worth laying out, because the answer tells you what to buy.

Six subjects contribute a grade from 1 to 7 each, giving 42, and the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination contributes up to 3 more. Within each subject, the Internal Assessment is a fixed share of the grade and is marked against lettered criteria whose marks are added separately rather than pooled — which is why a mathematically flawless exploration with no personal engagement loses those marks outright and nothing else compensates.

That structure has a practical consequence for how tutoring money should be allocated. A student two marks below a boundary in one subject is a different problem from a student whose Internal Assessments are all mid-band across six subjects. The first is a subject problem. The second is an assessment-literacy problem, and it is cheaper to fix because the same skill transfers across all six.

The core components are the most commonly neglected part of the structure and the easiest to improve from a low base. A student who has not kept a reflection record for the Extended Essay, or who has not unpacked the prescribed Theory of Knowledge title before planning, is losing marks to process rather than to ability.

This is the section to read before deciding how many hours to buy and in what. A Diploma plan built subject by subject without looking at the pattern across subjects usually buys the same lesson six times.

sections.heading: The components nobody in a new community can help with
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay are where families in a place like Aljada feel the thinness of local supply most sharply, because they are not subjects and almost nobody has taught them.

Theory of Knowledge is assessed through an exhibition and an essay written on one of the prescribed titles. The essay rewards engagement with knowledge questions and the development of more than one perspective, and the commonest failure is an essay that asserts a position and defends it without ever taking the counter-perspective seriously. That is a structural fault that a strong writer can commit cheerfully.

The Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece with a school supervisor, assessed on focus, knowledge, analysis, discussion and presentation, plus engagement evidenced through a reflection record. The reflection record is the part students leave until the end, at which point it is a reconstruction rather than a record, and the marks for it are the easiest in the entire Diploma to secure honestly and the most commonly lost.

What legitimate support looks like for both: the title or research question interrogated before planning, the argument questioned, the student's own draft read against the published criteria with specific gaps named, and the reflection record kept from week one. What it never looks like is text supplied, paragraphs rewritten, or a draft edited to completion. IB rules treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate's diploma rather than on anyone else.

Because these components are seasonal as well as scarce, they are worth booking a term ahead. The supervisor's internal deadlines, not an external calendar, set the timeline — so the first step is finding out what those deadlines are.

sections.heading: The IGCSE or MYP to Diploma drop, and why it is not a decline
paragraphs: A large share of first enquiries from these communities describe the same event: a student with a strong IGCSE or Middle Years Programme record arrives in Diploma Year 1 and the first report is two grades worse. Parents reasonably read that as something going wrong.

Usually nothing has. The systems reward different things. IGCSE rewards accurate answers to bounded questions under time, and a student who is fast and precise does well. The Middle Years Programme credits process and communication through four criteria per subject, which is closer to the Diploma but marked more generously. The Diploma rewards justified reasoning on open questions and assesses that reasoning explicitly.

In mathematics the break is visible within a term. A student who scored top grades on Cambridge 0580 by being quick meets Analysis and Approaches, where Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended investigation, and finds that speed is not the skill being measured. In the sciences the shift is from the right answer to the reasoning that produced it. In the humanities it is from describing to evaluating.

The intervention that works is short and early: four to six sessions on assessment architecture — what the criteria reward, what a 7-standard paragraph looks like next to a 5-standard one, what each command term expects — before the content tutoring begins. Done in the first term it is a small piece of work. Done in Year 13 it is a rescue.

For a family that has just moved into a new community and changed school at the same time, this is worth separating from the move itself. A worse report after a transfer is usually assessment unfamiliarity rather than a settling problem, and the two have different fixes.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: A Diploma student in Aljada is not only doing six IB subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools and appear on the report with everything else. Almost no tutoring provider in this market addresses them at all.

The requirements are specific. KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines require separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and state that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs.

Two consequences for tutoring follow. The stream is part of the match, because material written for the first-language route does not serve an additional-language student. And content is constrained: for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, so the work goes through the school's own material. KHDA calculates instructional time for these subjects on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

There is a checkable credential point here too. Schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a real standard a parent can reasonably ask about at a school level.

The federal baseline behind all of it: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Sharjah's own authority goes further than inspection — it approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

sections.heading: The permit, and what IB Gram is not
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and it is a reasonable question to put to anyone teaching your child weekly. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years.

Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, through the smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any figure quoted to you as unverified.

There is a related restriction worth knowing, press-reported rather than taken from the policy document itself: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE code of conduct carries a similar bar. Verify the exact wording against current policy before relying on it, but the principle holds — a teacher tutoring their own student is not a shortcut worth taking.

And the statement this page owes you. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed by or partnered with SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and holds no educational services permit. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. Naming a regulator here describes the system your child studies inside.

Nor does IB Gram operate an office, centre or branch in the UAE, and no named school on this page is a partner, client or endorser. Students we support attend schools across these communities; that is the whole of the relationship.

sections.heading: Starting from Aljada, and what to do if nobody is free
paragraphs: Begin with the last marked piece of work rather than the report. An Internal Assessment draft with comments, a marked paper or a teacher feedback sheet shows which criterion was empty or which command term was missed. A grade shows that something is wrong without saying what.

Send it with the subject and level, and ask your school's IB coordinator for the internal deadline calendar at the same time. Those internal deadlines, not an external exam date, are what a tutoring plan has to run against — particularly for Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay.

Then take a free trial session over live video, at a time that survives the inland Sharjah evening — in practice 5.30pm or later from Aljada, and 6pm where there are children at two schools. Judge the session on whether the tutor named a specific loss and said what the next four sessions would address.

If the specialism is thin — Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Economics evaluation coaching, Theory of Knowledge — you should be told plainly rather than offered a substitute. The honest options are a different slot with the right tutor, that tutor over live video from another time zone, or a statement that it is not available this term. Availability is seasonal too, so an exam-season slot is booked in autumn.

Finally, agree the review point before the first paid session. Six weeks in, read the next marked piece for the loss you started with. If it has moved, continue. If it has not, change the plan or the tutor, which is a normal thing to do rather than a complaint.

process.title: Send marked work and name the level
process.description: An Internal Assessment draft with comments, a marked paper or a feedback sheet, plus the subject and whether it is Higher or Standard Level. Those two facts are what let a tutor talk about a criterion or a command term rather than about confidence.

process.title: Get the school's internal deadlines
process.description: Ask the IB coordinator for the internal calendar — Internal Assessment drafts, Extended Essay checkpoints, Theory of Knowledge submissions, mock windows. A tutoring plan that runs against an external exam date and ignores these is out of step with the school from week one.

process.title: Ask the two IB questions
process.description: Name the criteria for this Internal Assessment and say what each rewards. Then: what will you refuse to do with my child's coursework? Neither answer can be bluffed, and together they separate a Diploma tutor from a capable subject tutor in about three minutes.

process.title: Take the free trial over live video
process.description: One session, no payment, at a time that survives an inland Sharjah evening — 5.30pm or later from Aljada. Judge it on whether the tutor named a specific loss and said what the next four sessions would cover, not on how the hour felt.

process.title: Agree a bounded block and a review date
process.description: A subject slot, a core components block, or a short school-move diagnostic, with the target written down. Six weeks later compare marked work against the starting point. If the named loss has not moved, the plan changes or the tutor does.

whyPoints.title: The comparison is made honestly
whyPoints.description: Aljada, Al Zahia and Muwaileh differ by commute and housing, not by Diploma tutor supply. Saying so is more useful to a parent than writing three pages that each claim a local specialist network nobody has.

whyPoints.title: Matched to subject and level
whyPoints.description: Higher and Standard Level are different courses with different papers and, in some subjects, different Internal Assessment expectations. Matching on "science" is how a Higher Level candidate ends up with a tutor learning the course alongside them.

whyPoints.title: Criteria before content
whyPoints.description: The first session on any Internal Assessment reads the published descriptors with the student, by letter, in their own words. A piece built around the wrong structure is a rewrite rather than an edit, so this order is not negotiable.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits published
whyPoints.description: The thin specialisms are named — Higher Level sciences, Maths AA HL, Economics evaluation, Theory of Knowledge — because knowing them lets a family in a new community book a term ahead instead of discovering a gap in April.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated on the page
whyPoints.description: Aljada students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Sharjah or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is an India-only service, and there is no UAE office or centre.

whyPoints.title: No claims that cannot be checked
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no unevidenced examiner status, no star ratings, no guaranteed grades, no satisfaction statistics. Every figure carries its source and the month it was read, and the IB dates that could not be verified are left off deliberately.

faqs.question: Is it worth looking for a tutor in Muwaileh or Al Zahia rather than Aljada?
faqs.answer: For content help, slightly — those areas and University City have a larger local pool, and published budget rates of AED 33 to AED 150 an hour are genuinely available there. For Diploma assessment specialism, no. The pool of people who have actually taught a Higher Level Internal Assessment is small across the whole emirate, so fifteen extra minutes of radius adds travel and almost no specialists. Widening the pool over live video is the only move that reaches the specialism.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to homes in Aljada?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits in Sharjah or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India, and there is no UAE office or centre. Aljada students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the draft or past paper on a shared screen. In a community where school provision is still arriving in stages, the practical point is that the tutoring does not also have to wait on local supply.

faqs.question: Why is IB tutoring harder to find than IGCSE tutoring in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Because specialist supply follows qualification share. International Baccalaureate students were 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school population in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on UK curricula and 26 per cent Indian, across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula. Sharjah's IB provision is concentrated in a small number of continuum schools. So the number of people in this emirate who have taught a Diploma subject at Higher Level and marked against its criteria is small in absolute terms, not just locally.

faqs.question: How should I split tutoring hours across six Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Six subject grades of 1 to 7 give up to 42, and the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination contributes up to 3 more. Inside each subject, the Internal Assessment is a fixed share of the grade and is marked against lettered criteria whose marks are added separately rather than pooled. That is why a mathematically flawless exploration with an empty personal engagement criterion loses those marks outright and strength elsewhere cannot compensate for them.

faqs.question: My child's Internal Assessments are all mid-band across six subjects. Is that six problems?
faqs.answer: Usually one. Six subjects each sitting mid-band suggests an assessment-literacy issue rather than six separate subject weaknesses — most often that descriptors are being read as a task description instead of a mark allocation. That is cheaper to fix than it looks, because the skill transfers across all six subjects once it is taught. A student two marks below a boundary in a single subject is the opposite case and should be treated as a subject problem.

faqs.question: What support is available for Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Feedback cycles against the published criteria: the prescribed title or research question interrogated before planning, the argument questioned, the student's own draft read against the descriptors with specific gaps named, and the reflection record kept from week one rather than reconstructed at the end. Those reflection marks are the easiest in the Diploma to secure honestly and the most commonly lost. What never happens is text being supplied, paragraphs rewritten or a draft edited to completion.

faqs.question: Should I worry that my child's grades dropped after moving school into the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Not immediately, and it is worth separating two things. A worse report after a transfer is often assessment unfamiliarity rather than a settling problem, and they have different fixes. The Diploma rewards justified reasoning on open questions and marks that reasoning explicitly through criteria and command terms, which a student arriving from a bounded-question system has never had to demonstrate. Four to six sessions on assessment architecture in the first term usually resolves what looks like a decline.

faqs.question: What time can a session start for a family in Aljada?
faqs.answer: Half past five at the earliest, and six o'clock where there are children at two schools. Students from Aljada largely travel to the established campuses in Muwaileh and University City, and dismissal congestion along the Maliha Road corridor is sharp because several large campuses release into the same roads in a narrow window. Slots are booked in Gulf Standard Time and held weekly, with most families moving to a post-Iftar time during Ramadan.

faqs.question: Is a villa community like Al Zahia better for in-home tutoring than Aljada?
faqs.answer: Marginally easier to execute — gate security and a driveway rather than visitor parking and a lift — which is why the in-home premium reads as slightly better value there. It changes nothing about who is available to visit. Market in-home rates run AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure, against AED 150 to AED 300 online for a qualified tutor, and Bestimate's Dubai table puts the usual in-home case at AED 180 to AED 350. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose between Mathematics Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: They can set out what each actually involves, which is the part most families lack. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra-and-proof route with Higher Level Paper 3 as an extended investigation, and it is what most engineering, mathematics and physics degrees expect. Applications and Interpretation is statistics, modelling and technology-permitted work throughout, and is different rather than easier. The decision should be checked against the entry requirements of the actual universities on your child's list.

faqs.question: What do Arabic and Islamic Education mean for a Diploma student in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: They run alongside the Diploma in UAE private schools and appear on the report with everything else. KHDA's guidelines require separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibit combined classes because expectations and the language of instruction differ, so material for one route does not serve the other. Tutoring works through the school's own material, since substituting content for mandatory subjects needs prior Ministry of Education permission.

faqs.question: Do tutors working in Sharjah need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts is published. Since it is free, there is no innocent reason for a working tutor not to hold it.

faqs.question: Will my child be able to stay with the same tutor if we move within Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Yes, which is one of the quieter advantages of an online arrangement in communities that are still filling. Households in this part of the emirate move between Aljada, Al Zahia, Muwaileh and the newer developments reasonably often, and an in-home arrangement usually ends with the move because the travel stops working. A live-video slot survives it intact, including a move between emirates, as long as the session time still fits the new school day.

faqs.question: How soon should I expect to see something change?
faqs.answer: Name the loss before the block starts and look at it after four to six sessions. The useful markers are specific: an evaluation criterion that was empty now addressed, command terms answered to their own expectations, a reflection record actually being kept. Compare the next marked piece against the one you began with. If the named loss has shifted, continue. If it has not, change the plan or the tutor — that is a normal adjustment, not a complaint, and leaving it longer is how a Diploma year gets spent.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-aljada.closingHeading: The same question, wherever you live inland
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-aljada.closingBody: If you are weighing an IB home tutor in Aljada against the same search for Al Zahia or Muwaileh, the comparison matters less than it looks. The commute differs by minutes; the Diploma specialist pool does not differ at all. Send your child's last marked piece of work, ask the IB coordinator for the school's internal deadlines, and take a free trial session over live video at a time that survives the inland evening. Judge it on whether the tutor can name the criterion that cost the marks.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-kalba.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Diploma and Middle Years subjects at the level your child is actually taking, working from the subject guide the school issues. Every lesson is one-to-one over live video, which is what makes a Diploma subject specialist reachable from the east coast at all.

intro.heading: Subject depth, when the nearest specialist is a long way off
paragraphs: Kalba sits on the Gulf of Oman, part of Sharjah but separated from the emirate's main urban area by the Hajar mountains and a drive that no tutor is making twice a week. Khor Fakkan is close; Fujairah city is close; Sharjah city is not. Families here know this better than anybody, which is why the practical question is not who is nearby but how to reach somebody who genuinely knows the course.

The IB makes that question sharper than most curricula would. A Diploma subject at higher level is a different teaching job from the same subject at standard level, and both are different from the Middle Years version. The internal assessment in each subject is marked against criteria by letter with published descriptors. Theory of Knowledge and the extended essay have their own demands again. The expertise required is specific, and specific expertise is thinly spread even in a city.

What that means for an east-coast family is straightforward. Local in-home tutoring, if it is available at all, will be general: somebody who can supervise homework and cover content across several year groups. That has value for a younger child. It does not help a DP2 student whose chemistry investigation is failing on its research design, or whose higher level mathematics paper is losing method marks.

Online delivery changes the arithmetic completely. Over live video, the pool is national: a tutor who has taught higher level chemistry for years and supervised dozens of investigations is as reachable from Kalba as from Al Majaz. Scheduling is in Gulf Standard Time, the session starts when the student is at the desk, and nobody is driving over the mountains. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE - that service exists only in India - so we are describing what we actually do rather than a fallback.

This page is therefore written as subject content. It sets out what changes between higher and standard level, where marks go in the sciences, how the two mathematics routes differ and why the choice has consequences at university application, what the language subjects demand alongside the mandatory UAE subjects every private school must teach, and what can and cannot be supported remotely in assessed work.

There is a cost point that follows from the geography and is worth stating early. Published UAE rate cards put a qualified subject tutor teaching online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 once travel is absorbed. On this coast, an in-home specialist would be priced at the very top of that range if one existed, so the online route is both the cheaper and the only genuinely available option for course-specific work.
It also covers the east-coast practicalities: which regulator applies, what school options families here actually use, and how examination arrangements work when the centre is not around the corner.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-kalba.programmesIntro: Three IB stages, with the east-coast consideration attached to each: what is realistically available locally and what has to come from further afield.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led with no external examinations, so expertise matters less than consistency. Reading fluency, number facts and writing an answer that addresses the question are the three things worth paying for, in short sessions that stop when the gap closes.
programmes.countryNote: For a family on the east coast, this is the stage where a local arrangement is most likely to work, because what is needed is presence and routine rather than course-specific knowledge. We are not the right provider if supervision is the actual requirement.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-assessed with task-specific descriptors. In the sciences the criteria cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on impacts - and diligent students routinely under-answer the last two because school tasks often reward the first two most visibly.
programmes.countryNote: Reading the descriptors with a student before a task is the highest-value hour at this stage and needs no local presence at all. It works perfectly over video, which makes the Middle Years the easiest stage to support well from a distance.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at higher or standard level, internal assessments marked against published criteria and moderated, plus Theory of Knowledge and an extended essay. The level choice shapes two years of workload, and the assessed work cannot be rescued late because deadlines pass.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision in this emirate sits in a small number of schools, none of them on the east coast, so a Kalba student on the programme is already travelling or boarding. The tutoring consequence is simple: course-specific help has to come over video, because nobody local has it.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-kalba.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by what it assesses and where students lose marks at each level, because the level is half the question when a family asks for a tutor.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the losses, with higher level adding depth rather than breadth. Extended responses are marked for precision: an observation rather than a conclusion, conditions rather than a gesture at them. The investigation lives or dies on its research design.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields, with sign conventions and unstated assumptions causing most avoidable losses in multi-step problems. Higher level extends the mathematics expected. Uncertainty treatment in the investigation is neglected almost universally and is quick to coach.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy at both levels, so command terms and data-based questions decide the grade. Higher level adds detail that rewards retrieval practice rather than rereading. Statistical treatment in the investigation is the recurring weak point.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, algebraic technique and calculus. Method must be written and justified rather than implied, which is the biggest adjustment for students arriving from a British-track background. Higher level is a substantial step in both content and pace.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use. Not the easy option at higher level, where the statistical content is demanding, and some university routes expect Analysis and Approaches instead - a check worth making before the choice is locked.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams and evaluation earn the marks, with higher level adding quantitative work that surprises students who chose the subject expecting essays. The commentaries need one syllabus section applied tightly to one current article.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis and the individual oral, with higher level adding an essay that needs a text chosen early enough to reread. Orals fail when the global issue is too broad to anchor in two extracts.

subjects.name: English B and language acquisition
subjects.description: Taken by many students for whom English is the language of instruction but not the home language. Productive skills are coachable to a formula - register, text type conventions, matching the task to its audience - and listening practice is routinely skipped.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the extended essay
subjects.description: Scheduled by the school, with internal deadlines well before anything the IB sees, and neither sets weekly homework - which is precisely why both slip. Coaching is sequence, question choice and criteria; the student writes every word.

sections.heading: Higher level against standard level, subject by subject
paragraphs: Parents are told that higher level means more content, which is true and incomplete. The differences that matter are in what the papers demand, how the workload distributes across two years, and which university routes expect which level.

Content is the obvious one: higher level covers additional topics and treats shared topics in more depth. Less obvious is the pace. A higher level subject consumes more of the week all year, which compounds across three of them and determines whether a student has time for the extended essay and internal assessments at all. A family choosing three higher levels is choosing a timetable, not just a set of subjects.

The assessment profile shifts too. Papers at higher level ask questions that combine topics rather than testing them in isolation, which rewards students who can see structure and punishes memorisation. The internal assessment is typically the same task at both levels, which means it is proportionally a bigger lever for a standard level student and a smaller one for a higher level student with more paper marks in play.

Then there are prerequisites. Some degree routes in engineering, mathematics, medicine and the physical sciences expect specific subjects at higher level, and the requirement is published by the university rather than negotiable later. The time to read those pages is before the choice, which for most students means during the pre-DP year. The table below sets out the comparison we work through with families.

sections.heading: The sciences: content, traps and what a tutor should do first
paragraphs: IB sciences lose marks in predictable places, and a tutor who names them in the first session is worth more than one who spends a month discovering them. This is the diagnosis an east-coast family cannot get locally and can get in a free trial lesson over video.

In chemistry the recurring three are energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms, with the additional problem that extended responses are marked for precision. A student who knows why a reaction is exothermic can still lose marks describing it loosely. The investigation adds a separate failure mode: a research design with variables that were never controlled cannot be rescued by good writing months later.

In physics, multi-step problems and fields dominate. Sign conventions cause more lost marks than conceptual misunderstanding, and unstated assumptions cost method marks that were available. In the investigation, uncertainty treatment is the criterion most often underdone - students collect data, process it, and then say nothing useful about how confident anyone should be in the result.

In biology, content is memorisable and marks still go on command terms and data questions. Students who revise by rereading plateau; students who answer past data questions under timing and check against the mark scheme improve. Statistical treatment in the investigation is the equivalent weak point to uncertainty in physics: tests chosen because they are familiar rather than because they answer the question asked.

A tutor's first session in any of the three should end with a written list of topics and question types, not with an impression. If it ends with encouragement instead, you have bought company rather than diagnosis, and that is worth noticing in week one rather than in March.

sections.heading: The two mathematics routes, and why the choice outlasts the Diploma
paragraphs: Mathematics in the Diploma is two subjects, not one, and the difference is the single most consequential choice a student makes in the pre-DP year. Analysis and Approaches is proof, algebra and calculus heavy, with method written out and justified. Applications and Interpretation is modelling, statistics and technology use.

The common error is reputational. Applications and Interpretation is widely described as the lighter route, and at higher level it is not: the statistical content is demanding and unfamiliar to most students arriving from a British-track background. Meanwhile some university routes in engineering, mathematics, physics and economics expect Analysis and Approaches, and a student who took the other course can find a published prerequisite unmet at application time, when nothing can be done about it.

The right method is unglamorous: read the stated requirements of the degree subjects under consideration, then attempt real questions from both courses with somebody who teaches both, then decide from the marked scripts. Two or three sessions is usually enough, and it is a small cost against a two-year commitment with consequences beyond school.

For an east-coast family there is an additional reason to take this seriously. If the local school offers only one of the two routes, or offers one of them thinly, the decision is partly made by provision rather than by fit - and knowing that in advance allows a family to plan support around it rather than discovering the gap in DP2.

sections.heading: Languages, and the subjects every private school must teach
paragraphs: Language subjects are where the IB's structure and the UAE's national requirements meet, and families are often surprised by how much of the week they jointly consume.

On the IB side, students take a language A - often English A: Language and Literature - and a second language, frequently English B or another language acquisition course. The first assesses unseen analysis and an individual oral; the second assesses productive skills that are coachable to a formula: register, text type conventions, and matching a task to its stated audience. Listening practice is almost universally skipped and almost always costs marks.

On the national side, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. Dubai's regulator publishes the most detailed version of these requirements and they are instructive everywhere: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies are mandatory regardless of the licensed curriculum, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of those subjects, and instructional time is calculated in forty-minute lesson units.

The practical consequence for a Kalba household is a full week and a tired evening. Support should be short and specific rather than long and general. Where a student arrived in the UAE mid-school and sits in Arabic as an additional language several years below their year group, that is a legitimate thing to support - and worth noting that content for the mandatory subjects is tightly controlled, so the honest offer is language and study-skill support rather than an alternative syllabus.

sections.heading: Supporting assessed work from a distance
paragraphs: A reasonable question from a family a hundred kilometres from the nearest IB school: how much of the internal assessment process can actually be supported by somebody who is not in the room? The answer is most of it, with one clear exception.

The exception is the practical work itself. Laboratory work for a science investigation happens at school, with the school's equipment and under the school's supervision, and no tutor substitutes for that. What a tutor can do is everything around it: question the research question until the available apparatus can actually answer it, identify which variables need controlling and how, and insist on a method that will produce data worth analysing. That conversation happens before the laboratory session and is where most investigation marks are won or lost.

Everything else transfers cleanly to video. Reading the criteria together. Narrowing a question. Teaching the statistics or the uncertainty handling the data needs. Reading a draft and explaining which criterion it fails and why. Rehearsing an individual oral to time with the criteria visible. Planning an extended essay's structure and checking that the research question can be answered in the length available.

What does not transfer, and would not be permitted in person either, is writing. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit any part of the submitted work, and IB Gram does not sell completed internal assessments, extended essays, Theory of Knowledge essays or coursework. Services that do appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the malpractice finding attaches to the student's diploma rather than to the seller.

sections.heading: East-coast practicalities: regulator, schools and examinations
paragraphs: Three administrative facts are worth having straight, because distance makes informal clarification harder and because families here deal with more than one authority.

First, the regulator. Kalba and Khor Fakkan are part of Sharjah, so private schools there fall under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fujairah's private schools, by contrast, are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education - which matters for any family whose child attends school across that boundary.

Second, school options. There is no IB Diploma provision on this coast, so families travel, board or choose another curriculum. Each of those has tutoring consequences: a boarding student needs support that fits a school timetable rather than a home one, a commuting student has very little weekday capacity, and a student on another curriculum may be preparing for different qualifications entirely.

Third, examinations. Entries are made by the school's centre, not by the family, and where a candidate sits is determined by that centre. For British-track siblings the relevant facts are published and checkable: Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, with the February/March series offered in India only, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November - the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session; we publish no IB dates because we could not verify them at source, and your coordinator holds the confirmed version.

sections.heading: What distance does and does not cost you
paragraphs: It is worth being even-handed about this. Living on the east coast genuinely costs a family some things in education, and the honest list is shorter than people fear.

What it costs: choice of school, informal access to teachers, the convenience of a neighbour's recommendation, and any realistic prospect of an in-home subject specialist. Those are real. A parent in Al Majaz can drop into a department at short notice; a parent in Kalba cannot, which is why asking for things in writing - the internal deadline calendar, the marked script, the department's view on a level - matters more here than anywhere else in the emirate.

What it does not cost: access to teaching. Over live video, the pool of tutors available to a Kalba family is the same as the pool available to a family in Dubai Marina, and the rate carries no travel component. Across published UAE rate cards a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, against AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit once travel is absorbed - and in-home on this coast would be priced at the very top of that range if anybody offered it at all.

The remaining honest caveat is the one we repeat on every page: for a young child who needs an adult physically present to stay on task, online tutoring is the wrong product and a local arrangement is better. We do not offer UAE home visits, so if that is your situation we are not the right provider, and saying so is more useful than taking the booking.

sections.heading: Limits, stated plainly
paragraphs: Everything on this page assumes a family making a careful decision at a distance, which is exactly the situation in which unclear claims do the most damage. So here are our limits, in one place.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring in a family's house is a service we offer only in India. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in this country.

No tutor can know what a particular candidate will score, so we offer no grade guarantees, no promised point totals and no refunds tied to results. A tutor may teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work, and may not write or edit any part of assessed work. We do not sell completed coursework of any kind, and we do not distribute boards' syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes - the school is the proper route to current versions.

We hold no approval, licence or accreditation from SPEA, the Ministry of Education, KHDA, ADEK, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we do not describe ourselves as approved by any of them. We also do not perform or guarantee Ministry of Education equivalency, which families complete themselves through the official channel - and tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression.

Finally, a limit on availability rather than on service. Narrow courses at popular hours sometimes have no specialist free, and when that happens we offer a different hour or a named date instead of a substitute. For a family at this distance there is no local fallback to catch a mismatch early, which is exactly why we would rather give you a clear no.
