faqs.question: Can we get an IB tutor to visit a home in Kalba?
faqs.answer: Realistically, not a subject specialist. There is no IB Diploma provision on this coast, so the pool of people nearby who have taught a specific DP subject to final-grade standard is very small, and the drive from the emirate's main urban area is not one anybody makes twice a week. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE in any case - that service exists only in India. What we do offer is one-to-one teaching over live video with a specialist matched to the subject and level.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring a compromise for a family this far from the city?
faqs.answer: It is the opposite. The further a family lives from a dense tutoring market, the more the online format adds, because it replaces a very short local list with the national pool. A Kalba student can work with a tutor who has taught higher level chemistry for years, at the same rate a family in the city pays, with no travel component - and across published UAE rate cards in-home visits cost AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor.

faqs.question: With a long commute already, is three higher level subjects realistic?
faqs.answer: It can be, but treat it as a timetable decision as much as an academic one. Higher level adds content, treats shared topics in more depth, asks paper questions that combine topics, and consumes a disproportionate share of the week - which compounds across three subjects and lands hardest on a student already spending two hours a day travelling or living away from home. Also read the published entry requirements of the degree routes under consideration, since several science and mathematics courses expect specific higher level subjects. Two or three sessions on genuine HL material produce better evidence than any amount of discussion.

faqs.question: Which IB maths route suits a student whose school offers only one properly?
faqs.answer: Decide from prerequisites and evidence, not reputation. Analysis and Approaches is proof, algebra and calculus heavy and is expected by several engineering, mathematics and physics routes. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics heavy and is not the easy option at higher level. Read the stated requirements of the degrees being considered, then attempt questions from both with somebody who teaches both. If your school offers only one route thinly, plan support around that rather than discovering the gap in DP2.

faqs.question: How much of an internal assessment can a tutor support remotely?
faqs.answer: Nearly all of it except the laboratory work itself, which happens at school with the school's equipment. Everything around it transfers cleanly: questioning the research question until the available apparatus can answer it, identifying variables that need controlling, teaching the statistics or uncertainty handling, reading a draft against the criteria and explaining which one it fails. What a tutor may never do, in person or remotely, is write, redraft or edit any part of the submitted work.

faqs.question: Where do IB marks actually get lost in the sciences?
faqs.answer: In chemistry: energetics, equilibrium, organic conditions, and loose wording in extended responses where precision is marked. In physics: sign conventions, unstated assumptions in multi-step problems, and uncertainty treatment in the investigation. In biology: command terms and data-based questions, plus statistical tests chosen because they are familiar rather than because they answer the question. In all three, an investigation whose variables were never controlled cannot be rescued by writing it up well.

faqs.question: Which regulator covers schools in Kalba and Khor Fakkan?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority, since both towns are part of Sharjah. SPEA regulates private education in the emirate and, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education instead, which matters if your child attends school across that boundary. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from SPEA or any other authority.

faqs.question: Our child boards in the city during the week. How does tutoring fit?
faqs.answer: Around the school's timetable rather than a home one, which usually means a weekend session and possibly one short weekday slot if the boarding house allows it. The advantage of a boarding pattern is that the school's own structure covers weekday evenings; the disadvantage is that a parent sees less of the work. We ask for the school's internal deadline calendar in that situation, because it replaces the informal awareness a day student's parent picks up.

faqs.question: How do the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect the week?
faqs.answer: They fill it. Private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, with instructional time counted in forty-minute lesson units, and schools organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of those subjects. So a Diploma student arrives home with work from two curricula. The practical effect is that short, specific sessions survive and long general ones do not. We can support Arabic as an additional language where a student sits below their year group.

faqs.question: Why do you not give IB exam dates anywhere?
faqs.answer: Because we could not verify them at source - the IB's own site blocks automated access, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. For a family planning around a distance and possibly a boarding arrangement, a wrong date would be worse than no date. UAE schools sit the May session, and your school's coordinator holds the confirmed dates for your child's cohort. Cambridge and Pearson dates, which the boards publish, we do cite.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with Theory of Knowledge and the extended essay from a distance?
faqs.answer: Yes, and these are among the easiest components to support remotely because they are entirely thinking and writing. Useful work is sequence and criteria: choosing a question that can be answered in the length available, agreeing checkpoints earlier than the school's, and reading drafts against the published descriptors. Both components set no weekly homework, which is why they slip - fortnightly short check-ins with one named deliverable each keep them moving. The student writes every word.

faqs.question: What should we ask the school for, given we cannot drop in?
faqs.answer: Four documents, all of which exist. The subject guide for each course, the task sheet for any assessed component, the internal deadline calendar - submission dates per subject, extended essay checkpoints, the Theory of Knowledge deadline - and the marked script from any mock. Distance means a parent here cannot pick things up informally in a corridor, so written documents do that job instead. Most schools supply them on request and very few families ask.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Sharjah need a permit, even for online lessons?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule. Since it costs nothing, asking a prospective tutor is reasonable.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is available in our subject at a workable hour?
faqs.answer: We tell you and offer alternatives rather than a substitute. Narrow courses - a higher level language, a less common science, Theory of Knowledge coaching at a popular hour - sometimes have nobody free, particularly in the weeks before a session. The options are a different hour, a weekend morning, or a named date when a slot opens. For a family at this distance a generalist substitution is especially damaging, because there is no local fallback to notice the mismatch early.

intro.heading: The Diploma year, as a school actually runs it
paragraphs: Parents in Khor Fakkan rarely go looking for a tutor in September. The search happens in the week after a report, or a fortnight before an internal assessment draft is due, or when a first-year Diploma student comes home with a predicted grade nobody expected. By then the year has a shape, and the useful question is no longer whether to get help but where in the calendar you currently stand.

The Diploma Programme runs over two years and its pressure is not evenly spread. The written examinations fall in a May session for schools in this region. Everything else is internal and earlier: six subject internal assessments, the Extended Essay with its own supervision meetings, Theory of Knowledge with an essay and an exhibition, and Creativity, Activity, Service running alongside. The school sets the deadlines for all of them, and those deadlines, not the examination timetable, are what crush a second-year student in the winter term.

The useful planning move is therefore boring and almost nobody does it: get every internal deadline for the year in writing, in one list, in the first fortnight of term. Diploma coordinators publish them. Once they are in one place, the clear weeks become visible, and tutoring can be bought into the gaps rather than into a panic. A family that does this in September buys half as much tutoring as one that starts in February and gets more from it.

Khor Fakkan adds its own constraint. The town sits on the Gulf of Oman with a deep-water container port that sets working hours for a lot of its parents, and the nearest concentration of Diploma schools is over the Hajar mountains in Sharjah city, well over an hour away, or south along the coast. Nobody with a Higher Level Physics background is going to make that drive twice a week for a single student at a sensible rate. So the local list is short, and the honest answer is to stop treating distance as the constraint.

Stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we provide only in India. Every Khor Fakkan lesson runs live online, one to one, with a shared whiteboard, the student's own draft or past paper on screen and a recording kept afterwards. The phrase "home tutor" is the search term, and it would be dishonest to let it suggest a car on its way.

What follows is the calendar in detail, with the mock season, the internal assessment sequence, what eight weeks can realistically deliver, the market rates in dirhams, and the academic-honesty line that governs what any tutor may touch on assessed work. Read the two-year sequence table first if you only read one part of the page, then look at where your child currently sits in it.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-khor-fakkan.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes and one transition route cover the Khor Fakkan enquiries we see. Each is described by the deadline pattern it imposes, because that is what a calendar-led plan has to fit around.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher and Standard Level with the three core elements. Internal assessments are marked by the teacher against published criteria and then moderated, so the quality of a draft submitted in the winter term affects a grade awarded in the summer. The written papers come in a May session for schools in this region, and the second year is front-loaded with internal deadlines rather than revision.
programmes.countryNote: East-coast Diploma students usually travel to school in Sharjah city or Fujairah, losing two hours a day to the road. That lost time is the hidden variable in every Diploma plan here, and it is the strongest practical argument for buying teaching that does not add a journey of its own.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight and converted to a one-to-seven grade. There is no external examination in most MYP schools, so the year is a sequence of criterion-assessed tasks rather than a build towards papers. A report showing strong knowledge and a weak analysis criterion is the classic signal that help is needed.
programmes.countryNote: For Khor Fakkan families the MYP question is usually about what comes next. A student who has never sat a timed written paper that counted will meet one in the Diploma Programme or in a Year 10 IGCSE cohort, and the technique gap is larger than the content gap.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-based primary framework assessed continuously rather than by examination. Support at this stage is about literacy and number fluency and about a child being willing to try something they might get wrong, which is as much a relationship as a curriculum question.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one age group where a nearby adult may genuinely beat a distant specialist. If your child is primary-age and needs someone in the room, we will say so rather than sell you a screen, because at that age the room matters.

programmes.name: The IGCSE and A Level alternative
programmes.description: Many east-coast students sit Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE courses before a sixth form, examined in a June series and a November series at Cambridge and in a May/June window and November at Pearson. Families comparing this route with the Diploma should compare the assessment style, not the reputation: tiered written papers against criterion-marked internal work.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track a student needs five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. No IB points threshold should be taken from a tutoring page, including this one.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-khor-fakkan.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects east-coast families ask about, with the internal assessment task named and the point in the year it bites. A calendar-led plan is built from this list and the school's deadline sheet.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is the internal assessment and it is the task students most often postpone. The Higher Level papers reward fluent algebra and proof technique; the exploration rewards genuine mathematical reasoning on a question narrow enough to be answered. Both are trainable, and neither improves in the fortnight before a deadline.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics with technology used throughout. The exploration suits students who can find real data and interpret it in context, and it punishes those who collect numbers without a question. Check which route named university programmes expect before the choice is locked.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is an individual piece of experimental work, planned and analysed by the student. Paper marks are lost on multi-step problems where a method has to be built rather than recalled, and on vague explanation answers in fields and waves.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are the recurring weak points, and the investigation needs a question that can actually be measured. A student whose uncertainty treatment is guesswork will lose marks under the analysis and evaluation criteria no matter how good the chemistry is.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume makes students answer from memory instead of from the question. Command terms are the fix. The investigation needs a measurable variable and enough repeats to say something, which is a planning conversation best had weeks before the laboratory session.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Internal assessment commentaries built on recent news articles, each with a word limit and a required diagram. Marks come from applying one syllabus concept properly rather than from summarising the article, and the commonest loss is a diagram that shows a movement where a shift was meant.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Marks live in the application to the named organisation and in evaluation that reaches a judgement. Students who define tools correctly and never apply them plateau in the fours and fives, which is a structural habit a tutor can change in a few sessions.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper analyses all require an argument about how a text produces its effect. Fluent writing with no analytical spine is the standard east-coast profile, and the repair is a repeatable structure applied until it stops feeling mechanical.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An essay against a prescribed title and an exhibition of three objects, both marked against published criteria. Support is scoping, structure and feedback on the student's own drafts. Left to the last month, it costs more marks than its weighting suggests because of what it does to everything else.

subjects.name: The Extended Essay
subjects.description: Four thousand words with a supervisor, a research question that has to be answerable, and reflection sessions that are themselves assessed. Nearly every problem with it is a scope problem set in the first fortnight, and nearly every rescue happens too late to fix the scope.

sections.heading: What an IB home tutor in Khor Fakkan can achieve from here
paragraphs: Families searching for an IB home tutor in Khor Fakkan want one of three things, and knowing which one changes what to buy. The first is a rescue: a deadline inside three weeks and a draft that is not working. The second is a repair: a subject where marks have slipped and a term in which to rebuild it. The third is a lift: a student who is at a five and wants a six, where the gap is technique rather than knowledge. All three are real jobs, and they need different numbers of hours in different parts of the term.

The rescue is the most expensive per mark and the most common purchase. It can be done, within limits: a draft can be scoped properly, a criterion-by-criterion read can redirect the effort, and a student can be taught what the evaluation criterion actually wants in a single session. What cannot happen is a tutor writing any part of it, which means the timeline is bounded by how fast the student can write, not by how much help is bought.

The repair is where tutoring earns its money. Eight to twelve weeks on a Higher Level subject, with marked evidence at the end of each fortnight, moves paper marks reliably because there is time to teach, practise and re-test. This is the purchase a family who has the school's deadline sheet in September can make calmly in October, and it is the one almost nobody makes.

The format, so there is no confusion: lessons are live online, one to one, over video. IB Gram does not place tutors in homes in Khor Fakkan or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. For a town this far from the Diploma school belt, that is the difference between a Higher Level specialist and whoever is within range.

sections.heading: The Diploma two years, counted forwards from term one
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes the Diploma calendar, and it is the thing parents most need. The table below is the sequence as schools in this region generally run it. Treat it as the shape of the two years rather than as a set of dates: every school sets its own internal deadlines, and the only authoritative list is the one your child's Diploma coordinator issues. Written examination dates and results dates for the IB should be confirmed with the coordinator or the IB directly rather than taken from any tutoring page, including this one.

Read it with one question in mind: where are the clear weeks? The first year has them, in the autumn and after the spring assessments. The second year has almost none between the start of term and the end of the internal deadline run, which is why a second-year family often finds there is no room left to add two sessions a week without removing something else. The plan has to be made in the space that exists.

The pattern that causes most damage is predictable. Internal assessment work slips by a fortnight in the first year because there is no immediate penalty, the Extended Essay scope is left loose, and both arrive in the second year on top of each other and on top of mocks. Each individual slip is small and the accumulation is what produces the February crisis. A calendar-led tutoring plan is mostly a device for preventing that accumulation.

sections.heading: Eight weeks before mocks: what is realistic
paragraphs: Mock results are the single most common trigger for a tutoring enquiry on the east coast, which is a shame, because the eight weeks before mocks are worth more than the eight weeks after. A mock paper is a diagnostic instrument the school provides free of charge, and a student who walks into it having already practised whole papers under timing gets a far more useful result from it.

A realistic eight-week block before mocks looks like this. Two weeks of diagnosis and content triage, using a past paper and the student's own marked work to decide which two or three topics are costing the most marks. Four weeks of teaching those topics properly and drilling them, mixed with earlier material so the gains hold. Two weeks of whole papers at exam timing with marks counted and lost marks grouped by cause rather than by topic.

The discipline that makes this work is refusing to add content late. If a Higher Level topic is still broken at week six, it stays broken for the mock, because the marginal mark is cheaper in technique. Families find this uncomfortable and it is the most reliable judgement in the whole plan. The broken topic goes into the post-mock block, where there is time for it.

One more thing specific to this coast. Students here lose roughly two hours a day to the school run, which is the equivalent of a whole study session. Recorded lessons get watched on that journey, and that is not a feature invented for a brochure; it is the single most-used thing about online delivery that east-coast families report.

sections.heading: What Diploma support costs here, read monthly first
paragraphs: Most pages in this market either publish no price or quote in dollars. Start with the monthly figure, because that is how a family actually budgets. Bestimate's Dubai rate work puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published monthly packages in this market include online plans around AED 799 for eight sessions and in-home plans at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. Those are market figures from published provider pages, not an IB Gram price list.

Convert to hours only afterwards. Budget online tuition, usually a university student, runs from about AED 45 to 65 an hour on EdFlik's published rates and from roughly AED 33 to 52 on Tutopiya's. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Board specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and a named premium tutor can reach AED 650 as BartyED's published rate does. Visiting in-home rates are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour.

The pattern worth noticing is that the monthly figure is driven by frequency far more than by tier. Two sessions a week with a mid-band specialist costs more per month than one session a week with a premium name, and for a second-year Diploma student in a deadline run it is usually the better purchase. Frequency buys contact with the work; tier buys precision about it. A deadline block needs frequency.

For context on the fixed side of a family budget: the Dubai authority confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in the emirate would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Tutoring is the part of the education budget a family can actually time, and timing it into the clear weeks rather than the crisis weeks is what makes it cheaper.

sections.heading: Online lessons against a tutor crossing the mountains
paragraphs: The comparison deserves honest numbers rather than rhetoric. Khor Fakkan to Sharjah city is a mountain crossing of well over an hour each way. Kalba is half an hour south. Fujairah city is closer than Sharjah city. A visiting tutor coming from the Sharjah school belt after their own working day cannot realistically be at a Khor Fakkan address before the evening is well advanced, and a late start on a school night is a worse lesson whoever is teaching it.

Then the supply question. Within range of this town, how many adults have taught Diploma Programme Higher Level Chemistry to examination classes and marked an investigation against its criteria? It is a short list, and it does not grow because a family wants it to. Online, the constraint disappears, and the tutor is chosen for the subject and level rather than for the postcode.

The in-home market is real and this page is not pretending otherwise. Rates for visiting tutors are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, and that premium over the online band is the travel. From the east coast that premium would be larger, because the journey is longer and unpaid. Families who want someone in the room will find providers who offer it; what they should check is who precisely is driving, how often, and what happens in week six when the novelty of the commute wears off.

To restate it so nobody is misled: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, and no tutor will arrive at a Khor Fakkan address. What is offered is the same one-to-one teaching over live video with a wider choice of specialist, a session that starts on time, and a recording afterwards.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the terms that are shorter than they look
paragraphs: A calendar-led plan has to account for the weeks that are not really there. School days shorten through Ramadan, the hour before iftar is poor study time regardless of discipline, and the Eid breaks remove revision days on both sides. A Diploma second year that looks like twelve clear weeks on paper often contains eight usable ones, and a plan built on the paper number produces a scramble.

What works on the east coast is moving rather than pausing. A post-iftar session, shorter than the usual length, keeps continuity through the month, and the heavy diagnostic work is scheduled into the weeks on either side. Families who pause entirely come back having lost not only the four weeks but the habit, and rebuilding the habit costs another fortnight.

The other calendar fact is the mandatory UAE subjects, which take real timetable space. Private schools here teach Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Those periods are not free study time, and counting them as such is how a plan overestimates capacity.

Sharjah's own authority adds the layer above: the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A Khor Fakkan family whose child attends school in Fujairah is under federal Ministry of Education supervision instead. Neither authority endorses any tutor, and no tutoring provider in this market should suggest one does.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on internal assessment, stated precisely
paragraphs: This is the section the essay mills in this market do not write. One provider found in the competitor set sells completed Internal Assessments outright for a fee. That is malpractice under IB rules, the consequence lands on the student rather than the seller, and it is not a service IB Gram will provide at any price or under any framing.

The permitted work is substantial and worth knowing precisely. A tutor may teach the underlying subject skills, explain the published assessment criteria and their mark allocations, discuss and challenge a proposed research question, talk through method, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may say an argument is unsupported, a method is unsound, a sample is too small, or a section is four pages long against a criterion worth few marks.

The prohibited work is equally clear. No tutor drafts the work, supplies paragraphs, rewrites sentences into a voice the student does not have, or edits a piece into something the student could not have produced. The school supervises these tasks, keeps records of drafts and meetings, and knows the student's written voice; a sudden change in register is exactly what that record exists to detect.

Materials follow the same logic. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and subject guides belong to the boards. We reference them and link to the official source rather than redistributing them. A provider offering a shared drive of papers and mark schemes is telling you something general about how it treats rules, and that is worth hearing before you hand over your child's coursework.

Prohibited: drafting, supplying paragraphs, rewriting, editing beyond the student's voice

sections.heading: Getting started from the east coast, including the honest limits
paragraphs: The first useful step costs nothing: ask your child's Diploma coordinator for the full internal deadline list for the year and put it in one calendar with the mock dates. Most families have never seen the whole list in one place, and seeing it usually changes the decision about how much tutoring to buy and when. If the clear weeks are in October, buy in October.

Then send three things: the subject and level, one piece of marked work or a criteria sheet with the teacher's comments, and the deadline you are most worried about. A marked script tells a tutor in two minutes what a phone call takes twenty minutes to approximate, and it determines which specialist we assign rather than which one is free.

The trial lesson is free, lasts forty-five minutes, uses your child's own material and is taught by the tutor who would continue. No card details are taken beforehand. What it tests is whether your child will tell this particular adult what they do not understand, which matters more than any credential and cannot be judged from a profile.

The honest limits, said before you pay rather than after. Narrow combinations take longer to match: a Higher Level science with a deadline inside two weeks, Theory of Knowledge at short notice, Arabic as a first language. When we cannot cover something well, we say so and name the alternatives: a different slot with the right specialist, a short declared bridging block, or a decline. For a Khor Fakkan family with few local fallbacks, a straight answer is worth more than an optimistic one.

process.title: Get the deadline sheet
process.description: Ask the Diploma coordinator for every internal deadline for the year, in writing, and add the mock dates. This one request reorganises more tutoring plans than any diagnostic does, because it shows where the clear weeks are and where there is no room to add anything.

process.title: Send marked work, not a description
process.description: A marked script, a criteria sheet with comments, or a report with criterion letters. It shows where marks were actually lost rather than where the student feels weak, and the two disagree more often than they agree. It also decides which specialist is the right match.

process.title: Free 45-minute trial
process.description: With the tutor who would continue, on your child's own material, with no card details taken first. The test is whether your child will admit confusion to this person. Credentials matter less than that, and a profile cannot show it.

process.title: Plan backwards from one date
process.description: Pick the deadline that matters most and build the block backwards from it: how many sessions, what the student writes between them, what marked evidence exists at the end. A block with no end date and no checkpoint turns into months of going over things.

process.title: Review on evidence at the halfway point
process.description: Halfway through, read the marked work rather than the reports. Continue if the gap has closed, change the tutor or the frequency if it has not. Changing at week four is normal, costs nothing, and is far better than changing at week twelve.

whyPoints.title: Built on the school's calendar
whyPoints.description: The plan starts from your child's internal deadline list and mock dates rather than from a generic package length. That is the difference between tutoring bought into the clear weeks and tutoring bought in February when there is no room left for it.

whyPoints.title: The east coast treated as itself
whyPoints.description: A mountain crossing of over an hour, a thin local pool of Higher Level specialists and two hours a day lost to the school run are the facts that shape tutoring here. This page starts from them instead of describing a Dubai neighbourhood with the name changed.

whyPoints.title: Criteria before content
whyPoints.description: On any internal assessment, the first session reads the published criteria against what the student has written. Analysis and evaluation carry the heavy marks and method description carries few, and most drafts have that balance backwards.

whyPoints.title: No in-person promise, anywhere
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live online, one to one. IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes; home visits are an India-only service. That appears in the first screen rather than in the small print, because a family this far out deserves to know before investing hope in a visit.

whyPoints.title: Limits disclosed before payment
whyPoints.description: If no specialist covers your subject, level and slot, we say so and name the alternatives rather than filling the hour. On a coast with few fallbacks, a straight no is more useful than a confident maybe.

faqs.question: Will an IB tutor travel to our home in Khor Fakkan?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Lessons for Khor Fakkan students run live online, one to one, over video with a shared whiteboard, the student's own draft or past paper on screen and a recording kept afterwards. The search term is "home tutor" because that is what parents type. The trade is a Higher Level specialist chosen for the subject instead of whoever can make an hour-long mountain drive twice a week.

faqs.question: When do Diploma students at east-coast schools sit their written papers?
faqs.answer: Schools in this region sit the Diploma written examinations in a May session. The internal deadlines matter more to your planning: six subject internal assessments, the Extended Essay with its reflection sessions, and the Theory of Knowledge essay and exhibition all fall earlier and are set by the school rather than by the calendar. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the full internal deadline list, and confirm any examination or results date with the coordinator or the IB directly rather than with a tutoring page.

faqs.question: My child's Khor Fakkan school deadline is in three weeks. Is it too late?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but the limits are worth knowing. In three weeks a draft can be rescoped, the criteria can be read against what exists, and effort can be redirected from the sections that pay little to the ones that pay most. What cannot happen is a tutor writing any part of it, so the timeline is bounded by how fast your child can write rather than by how many sessions you buy. Two or three well-spaced sessions with writing in between beats four sessions in a week.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a second-year Diploma student in Khor Fakkan need?
faqs.answer: Frequency matters more than tier in a deadline run. One session a week in a quiet term is enough to rebuild a subject; two a week is what a second year with internal deadlines stacked against mocks actually requires, and it is the reason monthly costs rise more from frequency than from choosing a more expensive tutor. Market monthly figures run roughly AED 600 to 1,200 for a weekly hour with a qualified tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

faqs.question: Is the eight weeks before mocks or after mocks more useful?
faqs.answer: Before, and it is not close. A mock is a free diagnostic instrument the school provides, and a student who has already sat whole papers under timing gets a far better reading from it. Eight weeks beforehand buys two weeks of diagnosis, four of teaching the two or three costly topics, and two of whole papers at exam timing. Eight weeks afterwards is spent repairing what the mock exposed, which is useful but reactive, and the clock has moved on.

faqs.question: What does the Extended Essay actually go wrong on?
faqs.answer: Scope, nearly always, and it is set in the first fortnight. A question too broad to answer in four thousand words produces a descriptive essay no amount of later work rescues, and a question with no accessible sources produces a stall. The reflection sessions with the supervisor are themselves assessed, so missing them costs marks directly. Support here is scoping, structure and feedback on the student's own drafts; no tutor may draft or rewrite any part of it.

faqs.question: How do internal assessment criteria differ from a mark scheme?
faqs.answer: A mark scheme awards marks for specified answers on a written paper. Internal assessment criteria are lettered descriptor bands, each with its own mark allocation, that a teacher applies to a piece of the student's own work before external moderation. Analysis and evaluation usually carry the heaviest allocations, and method description usually carries few, which is the opposite of how most drafts are balanced. Reading the criteria against the draft is the single highest-value hour of support on the task.

faqs.question: Can online lessons handle a Diploma science investigation?
faqs.answer: Yes for the parts that are assessed on paper, which is most of them: the research question, the variables, the method justification, uncertainty treatment, the analysis and the evaluation. All of that is worked on a shared screen with the draft and the criteria side by side. The practical handling of apparatus happens in your child's school laboratory, where it belongs. The marks come from the reasoning around the measurements rather than from the measurements themselves.

faqs.question: How should a Khor Fakkan family schedule tutoring through Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Move the slot instead of pausing. School days shorten, and the hour before iftar is poor study time no matter how disciplined the student is. A shorter post-iftar session keeps continuity, with the heavy diagnostic work scheduled into the weeks either side of the month. Families who stop entirely lose the four weeks and then the habit, and rebuilding the habit costs another fortnight. Agree the revised timing before the month begins rather than during it.

faqs.question: Which authority oversees schools in Khor Fakkan?
faqs.answer: Khor Fakkan is part of Sharjah, so its private schools come under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. If your child is enrolled in Fujairah instead, federal Ministry of Education supervision applies. No education authority in the UAE approves or accredits private tutoring providers, so treat any provider implying otherwise with caution.

faqs.question: Why does my child's Diploma timetable include Arabic and Islamic Education?
faqs.answer: Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, under federal regulations. Schools organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes are prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. For planning, count those periods out of your estimate of independent study time, because the usable total is lower than most families assume.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give feedback on a draft my child wrote?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the legitimate centre of this work. A tutor may teach the skills, explain the published criteria and mark allocations, challenge a research question, discuss method and respond in writing to a draft the student produced. A tutor may not draft it, supply paragraphs or rewrite it into a voice the student does not have. One provider in this market sells completed assessed work; buying it is malpractice and the student carries the consequence, not the seller.

faqs.question: Do lesson recordings actually get used on the east coast?
faqs.answer: More than anywhere else, because of the school run. East-coast students lose roughly two hours a day to the road, and a recorded session is the one piece of study that works in a moving car. The practical setup matters: a laptop or tablet rather than a phone, headphones, and a quiet hour for the live session itself. A phone camera pointed at a textbook is the only arrangement that genuinely does not work, because the shared document is the lesson.

faqs.question: What happens if no Higher Level specialist is free for our slot?
faqs.answer: We tell you before you pay. Common subjects in early-evening Gulf Standard Time slots match quickly; narrow ones take longer, including a Higher Level science with a deadline inside a fortnight, Theory of Knowledge at short notice, or Arabic as a first language. The alternatives are a different slot with the right specialist, a short declared bridging block with a strong generalist, or an honest decline. Booking outside the post-mock rush avoids the problem, which is the least exciting advice on this page and the most effective.

faqs.question: Is tutoring needed for UAE equivalency after a Diploma from a Sharjah school?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is a regulatory process run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authorities, and tutoring is not required for it, for university admission or for school progression. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. No IB points threshold should be taken from any tutoring page; verify it with the authority directly.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-khor-fakkan.closingHeading: Get the deadline list first, then decide
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-khor-fakkan.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB home tutor in Khor Fakkan, the free step that changes everything is asking the Diploma coordinator for the whole year of internal deadlines in one list, alongside the mock dates. Most families have never seen it assembled, and seeing it usually changes both how much tutoring they buy and when they buy it. Send us that list, the subject and level, and one piece of marked work, and we will say which weeks are worth buying and which are already full before you pay for anything.

intro.heading: What changes between Maryam Island and the district next door, and what does not
paragraphs: Maryam Island sits on the Sharjah lagoon between Al Khan and Al Majaz, a waterfront development of apartments and promenade rather than villas and compounds. It is a particular kind of place to live, and families there often assume it is a particular kind of place to find a tutor. In practice, the only things that change between Maryam Island, Al Khan, Al Majaz and Al Taawun are the housing type, the walk to the water and the drive to the Dubai border. The tutoring arithmetic is identical in all four.

That is worth saying plainly because a lot of effort gets wasted on the assumption that it is not true. Parents ask whether a more established district would have better supply, or whether being closer to Dubai helps, or whether somebody in the building might teach the Diploma. The honest answers are no, marginally and almost certainly not. The constraint on Diploma tutoring in Sharjah is not where you live. It is how few people have taught a given Higher Level subject through two full cycles, and those people are not distributed by neighbourhood.

What the waterfront districts do share is a particular evening. A high proportion of these households have at least one parent working in Dubai, and a meaningful number send children to Dubai schools, because the border is minutes away and the school choice there is wider. That means later arrivals home, a less predictable afternoon than an inland Sharjah family faces, and an evening that has to absorb a Diploma workload on top.

They also share an apartment-living constraint that villa districts do not. A Diploma student revising in a two-bedroom apartment with younger siblings has a space problem as well as a time problem, and a tutor arriving at the door makes that worse rather than better: another adult in a small living room, with the session audible to everybody. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE at all, since home tuition is a service we offer only in India, and for apartment households that turns out to be a practical advantage rather than a compromise.

The rest of this page makes the comparison explicit. There is a table setting Maryam Island against its neighbours on the things that genuinely differ, a section on where a session can happen in an apartment, the Sharjah rate bands read from the monthly figures first, and the regulator position for a household choosing between a Sharjah and a Dubai school. If you want the pure cost argument or the term-by-term calendar version, the sibling pages for this neighbourhood take those lines. Read the rate table from the monthly column rather than the hourly one, because the monthly figure is what a household actually commits to and the hourly figure is what gets quoted.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-maryam-island.programmesIntro: The IB continuum reaches Sharjah waterfront families at three stages, and the comparison between neighbourhoods matters least at the top end. A PYP tutor is findable almost anywhere; a Higher Level specialist is findable almost nowhere by distance.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, without external examinations, assessed through units of inquiry and the Year 6 exhibition. Support here is about literacy, numeracy fluency and the working habits that make later study possible. Sessions run shorter, around forty-five minutes, because concentration rather than content is the limit.
programmes.countryNote: This is the one stage where local supply genuinely is adequate across all the waterfront districts. A capable graduate tutor can support PYP numeracy well, and the budget band of roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour is a reasonable place to look. The comparison between Maryam Island and Al Khan is irrelevant at this level because the answer is yes in both.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked A to D, with a Personal Project in the final year. The criteria decide the band more than the topic does, and students who write fluently while ignoring the criterion wording settle in the middle and stay there.
programmes.countryNote: Supply starts to thin here, and it thins the same way in every Sharjah district. What a Maryam Island family needs is somebody who can read a criterion strand aloud and explain the difference between the top band and the one below it. That is a specific skill, it is not common, and nobody has it because they live nearby.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, assessed by external examination and internal assessment, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service, scored to 45 points. Internal assessment carries weight in nearly every subject, so the grade is built over two years rather than decided in a fortnight.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the neighbourhood comparison collapses entirely. The number of people within reach of the Sharjah waterfront who have taught Higher Level Chemistry through two cycles is small enough that distance cannot be the selection criterion. A Maryam Island family and an Al Majaz family are competing for the same handful of specialists, and both are better served by dropping the distance filter.

programmes.name: Extended Essay, TOK and internal assessment
programmes.description: The core is where points quietly disappear, because the deadlines are internal and therefore feel movable until they are not. The Extended Essay runs to 4,000 words on a question the student chooses; TOK is assessed by essay and exhibition. Support is process coaching rather than content teaching.
programmes.countryNote: The core is also the component that most rewards a tutor the student can reach between sessions, which an apartment-based household with one shared living space usually cannot arrange in person. A tutor may discuss the question, teach the criteria and read a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write, complete or edit the work, and providers in this market who sell finished work are selling your child a malpractice finding.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-maryam-island.subjectsIntro: The Diploma subjects Sharjah waterfront families ask about, with what the assessment actually demands. The pattern across these notes is that marks are lost to technique more often than to ignorance.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency under time pressure, with proof and deeper calculus at Higher Level. The exploration is internally assessed and consistently underestimated. Students who understand the mathematics still lose marks to unjustified steps and poor presentation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with the calculator part of the assessment rather than a convenience. Check the route against university requirements before committing, because some courses expect Analysis and Approaches specifically.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Multiple choice, extended response and a third paper on experimental and option material. Written explanations are where marks go: a correct idea phrased loosely earns nothing. The investigation rewards one tightly controlled variable over an ambitious design.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level failure rate. Data questions require uncertainty to be handled rather than mentioned, and the investigation needs a quantitative relationship the student can plot and defend.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Large content volume with marks tied to exact terminology, plus data analysis that catches students who revised facts and skipped skills. Higher Level extension material arrives late and is often first met during revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks and the evaluation command terms decide most of the rest. The internally assessed commentaries need real published articles, applied to theory rather than summarised.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven, with a research project at Higher Level. Application to the given organisation separates a 5 from a 7, and the quantitative tools are examinable and routinely neglected until too late.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen textual analysis, a comparative essay, the individual oral and a further essay at Higher Level. Strong bilingual students usually plateau on analytical technique rather than language: commenting on effect instead of restating content.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies must be used as evidence rather than recounted, and the command terms draw sharp distinctions between describe, explain and evaluate. The internal assessment is a replication with strict reporting conventions that are easy marks once learned.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A prescribed-title essay and an exhibition of three objects against a knowledge question. The component most often left too late in Sharjah schools, and the one where process coaching produces the clearest return per hour spent.

sections.heading: Maryam Island against Al Khan, Al Majaz and Al Taawun
paragraphs: Here is the comparison, made properly. These four districts differ in housing type, age, price and how far you are from the Dubai border. They do not differ in school access in any way that matters, and they do not differ at all in the depth of the Diploma specialist pool. If you have been wondering whether moving one district over would solve the tutoring problem, the table below is the answer.

The column to read is the last one. In every row it says the same thing, which is the point of the exercise. A waterfront apartment family and an inland villa family in Sharjah are drawing from one market of Higher Level specialists, and that market is not organised by neighbourhood. It is organised by subject, level and who happens to be free at a workable hour.

What does differ is the shape of the evening, and that is worth taking seriously. A household with a parent commuting from Bur Dubai is working with a different afternoon from one whose parents work in Sharjah, and a child at a Dubai school is home two hours later than a child at a central Sharjah one. Those variables change the slot, not the supply.

The practical conclusion for a Maryam Island family is a relief rather than a disappointment. You are not at a disadvantage relative to the next development over, and you do not need to find a local answer that does not exist. You need a specialist in the right subject at the right level, available at an hour your household can actually protect.

sections.heading: Why the answer is the same in every one of them
paragraphs: The reason the last column does not vary is arithmetic. A Higher Level Chemistry specialist needs to have taught the subject through at least two full cycles, which means several years in a Diploma school, which means a small number of people in any emirate. Spreading that small number across the districts of Sharjah leaves roughly nobody per district, whatever the search results suggest.

Distance-based searching therefore selects on the wrong variable. It keeps whoever lives nearby and is free in the late afternoon, and discards almost everybody with the relevant experience. The result feels efficient and performs poorly: three months in, the student is still losing the same marks, because the nearby tutor has been reteaching content the student already understood.

Searching by subject and level inverts it. The pool becomes smaller in the sense that fewer people qualify and much larger in the sense that geography no longer excludes anybody. For a Maryam Island family this is the whole argument, and it applies identically in Al Khan, Al Majaz and Al Taawun, which is why we have not written four different pages claiming otherwise.

IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE, so there is no version of our service that involves a tutor at your door in any of these districts. What we can offer is the specialist pool without the distance filter, taught live and one-to-one in a slot your household sets. That is the whole proposition, and it is the same proposition we would make to a family one street away.

sections.heading: Where a session actually happens in an apartment
paragraphs: This is the part of the problem that villa-district advice ignores. A Diploma student in a two or three bedroom apartment on Maryam Island has one desk if they are lucky, a shared living room, and siblings who are also at home at five o'clock. The time is not the only constraint; the space is, and a plan that ignores it produces a session the student cannot concentrate in.

A visiting tutor makes that worse, which is counter-intuitive until you picture it. Another adult in a small living room means the session is audible throughout the apartment, the rest of the household rearranges itself around it, and the student performs rather than works. Several families tell us this was the actual reason an in-person arrangement stopped, not the cost and not the traffic.

An online session needs a surface, a door that closes and headphones, and it can move to the hour when those three are available. In many waterfront households that hour is later than the obvious one, after a younger sibling is in bed, and that is a perfectly good time for a sixteen-year-old. We would rather set a 7.30pm slot that is genuinely quiet than a 5pm slot that is technically free.

Two practical details are worth getting right from the start. Test the connection before the slot rather than during it, and agree that the hour is fixed when something else comes up. Those two habits are the difference between thirty completed sessions and twenty-two, and only the household can supply them.

sections.heading: What the waterfront market charges, read monthly first
paragraphs: Most rate discussions start with an hourly figure, which is the least useful way for a household to think about it. Start with the month. Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget band, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. That is the number that goes in a household budget, and it is the number to decide on before any tutor is chosen.

The hourly bands behind those figures, read in October 2026, are these. Budget online tutors run roughly AED 33 to 65, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB tuition from AED 200. A specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's table, and AED 200 to 500 with independent home tutors. The monthly packages make the gap starkest: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. That is the same eight contact hours at roughly double the cost, and in an apartment the visit also costs you the quiet of the whole flat for the hour.

Every figure here is published by the provider named and is quoted so you can check it yourself. None of it is an IB Gram price list, and we are not going to invent one for a page; for ours, take the free trial lesson and ask against your child's actual subject and level.

sections.heading: The Diploma load against a waterfront evening
paragraphs: A Diploma student carries six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. On an ordinary weekday that is two to three hours of school-set work. In a Maryam Island household where a parent returns from Dubai at seven, the evening the student actually has is shorter than the timetable suggests, and the tutoring hour has to be carved out rather than added.

The load is also distributed badly across the two years. DP1 feels manageable until the spring, when internal assessment drafts, the Extended Essay research question and the first mocks arrive together. DP2 opens with everything that slipped still outstanding. The sensible response is to put more hours into the first half of DP1 than feels necessary, because that is the only part of the programme with room in it.

Higher Level choices change the arithmetic sharply. Three Higher Level sciences with Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level leaves almost no evening, and a student in that position needs fewer tutoring hours in more concentrated bursts rather than three weekly subjects. We will say so rather than sell the third subject, because three thin hours in a packed term achieve less than one used properly.

The structure that works for most waterfront households is one protected hour in the subject causing most damage, with a second added only once the first is stable after six weeks. It is slower than anxiety wants and it is the arrangement still running in March, which is the only test that matters.
bullets: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Extended Essay, TOK and CAS
Two to three hours of school-set work on an ordinary weekday

One subject done properly beats three done thinly

sections.heading: A video slot against a tutor at the door of an apartment
paragraphs: The comparison is worth making on its merits rather than being asserted. In-home tuition has real advantages: physical presence, easier management of a distractible younger child, independence from a connection. Those are genuine. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the in-home column below describes what the Sharjah market sells, and is here so you can weigh it honestly.

On a waterfront development the logistics cut differently from a villa community. A visiting tutor needs visitor parking, building access and a lift, and in practice the last five minutes of every session are spent on arrival and departure rather than teaching. None of that is a scandal; it is just friction, and across a thirty-week year it adds up to several sessions you paid for and did not receive.

The decisive column, as ever, is who can teach your child. An in-home arrangement on the Sharjah waterfront draws from people prepared to come to the lagoon in the late afternoon. An online arrangement draws from everybody teaching that subject at that level whose hours overlap your evening. For a Standard Level subject the two pools may both be adequate; for Higher Level Chemistry they are not comparable.

If a home visit genuinely is right for your child, book it from a provider who offers it, and ask two questions first: the tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit, and how many full Diploma cycles they have taught of that exact subject at that exact level. Both are fair questions and the answers are informative.

sections.heading: SPEA, KHDA and choosing between Sharjah and Dubai
paragraphs: Waterfront families sit close enough to the border that the school choice is genuinely open, and that choice carries a regulator with it. Sharjah private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and, in Sharjah's case, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai private schools answer to KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in that emirate.

Those are different kinds of oversight and they produce different experiences. Sharjah's broader approval remit means more consistency between schools and less variation in what is offered; a subject your child wants may simply not be available. Dubai's market is larger and more varied: 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate accounting for 7 per cent of students.

Two Dubai data points are useful for a family weighing the move. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. And Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places.

What neither regulator does is vet your tutor. Private tutoring sits with MoHRE under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023; the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years, is open to school teachers, public and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app and e-services system with a stated two-working-day completion time. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE or the IB.

sections.heading: What a tutor may do with the Diploma core
paragraphs: The core is where the integrity line matters most, because the work is written at home over months and the deadlines are internal. This market contains providers who sell completed internal assessments; one page in this research advertises finished work at AED 3,750. For a student that is not a shortcut but a malpractice finding, and the risk falls on the whole diploma rather than one subject grade.

The boundary in plain terms. A tutor may teach the subject content, explain how the assessment criteria award marks, discuss and sharpen a research question the student proposed, model structure using a different example, read a draft the student wrote and say where the argument is unsupported or the method unclear, and teach referencing and data handling properly.

A tutor may not write any part of the work, rewrite it, complete it, edit it to a finished state or produce a worked version of the student's own question. We also do not reproduce or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter.

One further rule concerns teachers. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and check the current policy document; the principle holds regardless, and we will not arrange it.
bullets: Teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own draft: yes
Writing, completing or finishing assessed work: never, at any price
Official papers and mark schemes as downloads: no, we link the source
A tutor who also marks your child's school work: no

sections.heading: Starting on the Sharjah waterfront
paragraphs: Begin with two facts rather than a search. First, the hour when your apartment is genuinely quiet, which may be later than the hour when your child is free. Second, the subject and level causing the most damage, which is not always the subject with the lowest grade; a Higher Level subject at 4 does more harm than a Standard Level subject at 3.

Then collect the school's internal deadline schedule and one recent piece of marked work. Those two documents let a specialist tell you something useful in the first hour, rather than spending that hour establishing where the student is. The internal schedule matters more than families expect, because it is what actually governs a Diploma year.

Use the free trial as a diagnosis. A good trial ends with a specific statement: this is a content gap in topic six, or this is a command-term problem across all papers, or this is a workload-management problem that more tutoring will not solve. Those three need genuinely different plans, and a trial that produces only warmth has told you about the provider rather than the student.

Then review at four weeks against evidence set in advance. If the agreed errors have not stopped recurring and the timed work has not moved, we change the specialist rather than defend the match. Ask any provider you are considering how they would answer that, and notice whether they have an answer ready. The question is reasonable and a serious provider will have thought about it before you asked.
