process.title: Tell us when the apartment is quiet
process.description: Not when your child is free, but when the flat is workable: siblings settled, a door that closes, no shared-room conflict. On a waterfront development that hour is frequently later than the obvious one, and choosing it honestly is what makes the arrangement last past half term.

process.title: Name the subject and the level
process.description: The programme year, the subject, and whether it is Higher or Standard Level. We also ask which subject is doing the most damage rather than which has the lowest grade, because a Higher Level 4 costs more points than a Standard Level 3 and the two should not be treated alike.

process.title: Send the internal deadline schedule
process.description: The school's own dates for internal assessment drafts, Extended Essay stages and TOK components. Those govern a Diploma year far more than the examination session does, and a tutoring plan built on them beats one built on guessed exam dates every time.

process.title: A free trial that ends in a diagnosis
process.description: The tutor works through a real question or a section of the student's own draft and tells you whether this is content, technique or workload. You get it in writing, nothing is paid beforehand, and the diagnosis is useful even if you take it elsewhere.

process.title: Fix the slot, agree a fallback day
process.description: A standing weekly time in Gulf Standard Time plus one alternative day for weeks when an internal deadline lands on it. Sessions that can move get kept; sessions that can only be cancelled get cancelled, and that is how arrangements quietly end.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you the comparison does not matter
whyPoints.description: A page that claimed Maryam Island had better tutor supply than Al Khan would be easier to sell and untrue. The Diploma specialist pool is thin across the whole emirate and is not organised by district, and knowing that saves you a month of looking for a local answer that does not exist.

whyPoints.title: Built for apartment households
whyPoints.description: No visitor, no parking, no access code, and a session contained in one room with headphones rather than filling a shared living space. For waterfront families that is frequently the deciding factor, and it is the one competitors in this market never mention.

whyPoints.title: Matched by subject and level
whyPoints.description: A tutor is chosen for having taught Higher Level Chemistry through two full cycles, not for living near the lagoon. Distance filtering keeps availability and discards experience, which is precisely the wrong trade when the problem is exam technique.

whyPoints.title: Rates you can check
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here carries the provider that published it and the month it was read, starting from the monthly estimate because that is what a household budgets. Three of six competitor pages in this research publish no price at all and two quote US dollars.

whyPoints.title: No invented IB dates
whyPoints.description: We describe the May session and send you to your school's IB coordinator for specifics, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification. A confidently wrong date on a page a parent acts on is worse than no date, and several pages ranking for these searches carry one.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on the core
whyPoints.description: Tutors coach the process, explain criteria and read drafts the student wrote. They do not write, complete or finish an internal assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay, and we do not hand out official papers or mark schemes. In this market that boundary is a differentiator rather than a platitude.

faqs.question: Would we find a better IB tutor if we lived in Al Khan or Al Majaz instead?
faqs.answer: No, and it is worth settling that before you spend a month looking. Maryam Island, Al Khan, Al Majaz and Al Taawun draw on one tutoring market, not four. The constraint on Diploma tutoring in Sharjah is how few people have taught a given Higher Level subject through two full cycles, and those people are not distributed by district. What does change between these neighbourhoods is housing type and the drive to the Dubai border, neither of which affects who can teach Higher Level Chemistry.

faqs.question: Is an apartment a problem for one-to-one tuition?
faqs.answer: It is a real constraint and it is solvable, though not by having a tutor visit. A Diploma student in a Maryam Island apartment needs a surface, a door that closes and headphones, which is achievable in most flats at some hour of the day. A visiting tutor makes the session audible throughout the apartment and the whole household rearranges itself around it. Several families have told us that was the actual reason their in-person arrangement stopped, rather than the cost or the traffic.

faqs.question: What hour works best for a waterfront household?
faqs.answer: Later than most advice assumes. If a parent commutes back from Dubai and a younger sibling is at home from mid-afternoon, the hour when the flat is genuinely quiet may be 7.30pm rather than 5pm, and that is a perfectly good time for a sixteen-year-old. We would rather set a slot that is quiet and holds than one that looks neat on a timetable and is interrupted twice a month. Pick for noise first and traffic second, which is the reverse of the usual order.

faqs.question: How much does IB tuition cost per month in this part of Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Start from the monthly figure rather than the hourly one. Bestimate's 2026 monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget band, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, read in October 2026. Market packages show about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are the providers' published figures, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Should we send our child to a Sharjah school or across the border to Dubai?
faqs.answer: That is a schooling decision rather than a tutoring one, and the regulator changes with it. Sharjah schools answer to SPEA, which approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, producing more consistency and sometimes less choice. Dubai schools answer to KHDA and sit in a larger market: 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula in 2024-25, with IB programmes at 7 per cent of students. Note also the longer afternoon: a Dubai-schooled child from the waterfront is home much later.

faqs.question: My child has three Higher Level subjects. Can they manage three weekly tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not, and we will say so rather than sell them. Three Higher Level subjects plus the core already fill the evening with two to three hours of school-set work, so three added hours displace sleep rather than adding learning. Start with one protected hour in the subject doing the most damage, hold it for six weeks, and add a second only if the first is stable. Three thin hours in a packed term produce less than one hour used properly, which is a harder sentence to sell and a truer one.

faqs.question: Which Sharjah schools do the students you support on the waterfront attend?
faqs.answer: Students we support in this part of Sharjah study across the central lagoon schools, including Victoria International School of Sharjah and Sharjah English School, with some at the inland Muwaileh cluster and a meaningful number travelling across the border to Dubai schools such as Deira International School. We name schools as context for where students study. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any of them and none should be inferred.

faqs.question: Does being close to Dubai help with finding a Diploma tutor?
faqs.answer: Marginally and not in the way families hope. A larger pool of Diploma teachers works in Dubai, but they are at work during the hours when a tutor is needed, and the drive north at five o'clock makes an in-person arrangement across the border unattractive to them at any rate you would want to pay. Proximity to Dubai changes your school options genuinely and your tutoring options hardly at all. The thing that actually widens the pool is removing the travel requirement altogether.

faqs.question: When should a DP1 student start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, because DP1 is the only part of the programme with room in it. The autumn of DP1 is cheap time: no internal assessment deadlines yet, mocks a long way off, and the student still has evenings. From the spring onwards internal assessment drafts, the Extended Essay question and the first mocks arrive together, and by DP2 the schedule is full of work that slipped. Families who front-load the first half of DP1 spend less overall and arrive in DP2 in a different position.

faqs.question: How much of the Extended Essay can a tutor legitimately be involved in?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is one of the most valuable things a tutor does. They can read what your child has written and say where the argument lacks support, where the method is unclear and where the research question has drifted, explain how the criteria award marks, and teach referencing properly. They cannot write any part of it, rewrite it, complete it or edit it to a finished state. Providers in this market sell finished essays outright; buying one risks the whole diploma rather than one component.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge worth paying for support on?
faqs.answer: It is one of the better returns per hour in the whole programme, mostly because it is the component students leave latest. TOK is assessed by a prescribed-title essay and an exhibition of three objects against a knowledge question, and the common failure is not weak thinking but an essay that describes rather than argues about knowledge. Four or five sessions of process coaching on structure and the use of examples moves that reliably, and it costs less than a term of subject tutoring.

faqs.question: Do you tutor the MYP Personal Project as well?
faqs.answer: Yes, as process coaching. The Personal Project is assessed against criteria covering planning, applying skills, reflecting and the product itself, and most students lose marks on the process documentation rather than on the product. A tutor can teach what each criterion asks for, help structure the process journal and read what the student has written. The product and the writing must be the student's own, which is both an IB requirement and the only reason the project is worth doing.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a Diploma specialist for a Sharjah student?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Diploma subjects, usually two to four days and often inside forty-eight hours. For less common Higher Level options or second-language subjects, five to ten days, and in those cases expect us to say whether the specialist is based in the UAE or teaching into your evening from another timezone. Households willing to take a weekend-morning slot are matched faster across every subject, because the weekday evening between about 4.30pm and 7.30pm is the most contested window in the emirate.

faqs.question: What do we do during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Move the slot rather than pausing it. School days shorten and the useful study window shifts, so a 5pm session that worked in January is the wrong slot in Ramadan. For waterfront households a post-Iftar session between roughly 8.30pm and 10pm tends to work well, particularly for Diploma students already keeping late hours, and a short early-morning session suits others. Decide which before the month starts. Families who improvise usually lose the whole month, and a month out of DP1 is expensive to recover.

faqs.question: Do you publish IB examination dates?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, and that is as specific as we will be on a page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and we are not prepared to restate a date we cannot verify. A confidently wrong date is worse than no date, especially one a parent acts on. Ask your school's IB coordinator for the session dates and, more usefully, for the internal deadline schedule, which is what actually governs the year. Cambridge and Pearson dates we do cite come from the boards' published material.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-maryam-island.closingHeading: The district is not the problem; the subject is
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-maryam-island.closingBody: If you have been searching for an IB home tutor in Maryam Island and wondering whether a different development would make it easier, it would not. The Diploma specialist pool is thin across the whole emirate and it is not arranged by neighbourhood. What will help is naming the subject and level doing the most damage, finding the hour when your apartment is genuinely quiet, and bringing the school's internal deadline schedule and one recent piece of marked work. Send us those and we will match a specialist, hold the slot in Gulf Standard Time with a fallback day, and run a free trial lesson that ends with a written diagnosis. Lessons are live, one-to-one and online.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-muwaileh.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years Programme subjects at named levels. A profile says Chemistry Higher Level or Mathematics Applications and Interpretation Standard Level rather than "science" or "maths", because the level is the job and the Internal Assessment criteria differ with it.

intro.heading: Why the IB breaks general tutoring
paragraphs: A tutor who taught maths for fifteen years can walk into an IGCSE paper and be useful immediately. The same tutor meeting an IB Diploma Internal Assessment for the first time is not useful, and it takes a parent about six weeks and several thousand dirhams to discover why. The Diploma does not mark answers the way other systems do. It marks against published criteria lettered A, B, C and onward, each with its own descriptor bands, and a student can produce correct mathematics and still score in the middle because one criterion is empty.

That is the real content of the question behind an IB home tutor search in Muwaileh: is there anyone close by who actually knows this. Muwaileh sits inland, next to University City, along the Maliha Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road corridor. It has large school campuses and a genuine local tutoring supply — the proximity of three universities means Sharjah's lower-cost tutoring band is real here in a way it is not in Dubai. What it does not have in depth is Diploma specialists, because the Diploma is a small share of the regional market. International Baccalaureate students made up 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school population in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on UK curricula and 26 per cent Indian.

So a radius search in Muwaileh will usually find you a competent subject tutor and present them as an IB tutor. The difference between the two is not politeness or qualifications. It is whether they can tell you, unprompted, what criterion B asks for in a Mathematics exploration, or why a Biology answer that says "explain" has a different mark expectation from one that says "outline".

This page is built to make that test easy. It sets out what IB-specific knowledge consists of, subject by subject and component by component, so a parent with no background in the course can run the check in one conversation. It also sets out the parts of the Diploma that sit outside subjects altogether — Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, and the mandatory UAE subjects running alongside — because those are where Muwaileh families most often find nobody local to help.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. In-home visits are offered only in India. Muwaileh students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the draft or the past paper on a shared screen. The argument for that is not cost. It is that the pool for a Higher Level Diploma science stops being whoever will drive out past University City and becomes whoever teaches that course properly.

What follows: the criteria explained by letter, command terms and what each one is worth, the Muwaileh school day and when a session actually fits, the honesty boundary on coursework, and what happens when no specialist is free.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-muwaileh.programmesIntro: Muwaileh families arrive at IB tutoring from three directions: a continuum school running the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma, a transfer in from a British-curriculum school, or a move between emirates mid-course. Each needs something different in the first month.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service alongside. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked against lettered criteria. Points come from subject grades plus up to three from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination, which is why those two components are worth real tutoring attention rather than being treated as admin.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. This page publishes no IB exam or results dates: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so every DP date should be confirmed with your school's IB coordinator rather than taken from a search result. What is locally fixed is that Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the Diploma in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria scored 0–8 and converted to a 1–7 grade by published boundaries. The MYP credits process, communication and reflection explicitly, which is why capable students sometimes carry a 4: the content is right and the justification or communication criterion is thin. A tutor who cannot name the four criteria for the subject in question is working from a general subject plan.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma step is the most common reason Muwaileh families start tutoring in Year 11. MYP mathematics samples topics the Diploma assumes fluency in, and the move into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level exposes that within a term. The useful work is a diagnostic on the specific algebra, functions and proof the DP course opens with, done before Year 12 starts rather than after the first assessment.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme and the IGCSE alternative
programmes.description: Not every student in a Muwaileh IB school takes the full Diploma. Some take DP courses rather than the full certificate, some sit a Career-related Programme where the school offers it, and some transfer to A Levels. The tutoring implication is that "doing IB" is not one thing: a DP courses candidate has subject exams and Internal Assessments but no Extended Essay, and the plan should reflect that.
programmes.countryNote: MoE equivalency rules are published for the British and American tracks but the sourced article states no IB points threshold, so no equivalency figure for the Diploma should be published without a Ministry of Education page to cite. Families planning UAE university entry should take the equivalency question to the Ministry directly; it is a process to describe, not one a tutoring service performs.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-muwaileh.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Muwaileh families request most, with the specific component or criterion that decides the grade. Read them as test questions: a tutor who knows the course can expand any line here without notes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, functions and calculus, with Higher Level Paper 3 an extended investigation rather than a question set. That paper is where predicted grades most often fall. The exploration is marked on criteria including presentation, mathematical communication and personal engagement, and strong mathematicians routinely lose marks on the last of those.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use throughout. Students arriving from a British curriculum often read it as the easier route and meet unfamiliar modelling questions. The exploration criteria are identical to Analysis and Approaches but reward genuine collected data, which is a planning decision made in week one.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the grade. Marks go for state symbols, conditions and reasoning between steps, not for the product alone. The Internal Assessment is assessed on the student's own research question and method; a tutor may question and critique it but never supply one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth on the same topics, and the additional material is where HL candidates separate. Extended-response marks reward stating the physical principle before the calculation. The Internal Assessment credits experimental design and uncertainty handling, with the result itself carrying no marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms do most of the damage. Outline, describe, explain, distinguish and discuss expect different structures and mark counts, and a student answering all of them identically settles around a 5 whatever they know. Data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments are trainable and almost never trained.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are credited piece by piece — axes, shift direction, new equilibrium stated — so a remembered sketch loses marks before any explanation. The Internal Assessment is commentaries built on published articles, and choosing an article with no diagram-able economics in it is a failure locked in at the start.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral and the Paper 1 unseen analysis move most under tutoring. Marks go to analysis of how meaning is constructed, not to summary of what happens. Higher Level adds the essay, assessed on sustained argument rather than coverage of a text.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the named organisation decides the band: a textbook-correct answer with no reference to the case sits at the bottom. Higher Level carries extension topics and a longer Paper 2. The Internal Assessment needs real organisational data, and sourcing it is the first real piece of work.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.levels: Language A, language acquisition and ab initio routes
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the Diploma in UAE private schools. Separate streams exist for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ, so material from one route does not serve the other.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together worth up to three points on the Diploma total, and routinely under-supported. TOK is assessed through an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title; the Extended Essay is an independent 4,000-word piece with a school supervisor. Both are coached through feedback on the student's own drafts and never written for them.

sections.heading: The criteria, by letter, and why a correct answer can score a 4
paragraphs: This is the single piece of IB knowledge that separates a Diploma tutor from a subject tutor, and it is explainable in a paragraph. Internal Assessments are not marked out of a total and then banded. They are marked criterion by criterion, each lettered, each with its own descriptor bands, and the marks are added afterwards.

The practical effect is that strengths do not compensate for absences the way parents expect. A Mathematics exploration with impeccable mathematics and no personal engagement loses the personal engagement marks outright; brilliance in one criterion cannot reach across. The same is true in the sciences, where the Internal Assessment credits research question, methodology, analysis and evaluation separately, and the experiment producing the textbook answer earns nothing on its own.

This is also why a student reports that they "did everything asked" and came back with a 4. They answered the task. They did not address every criterion. A tutor who knows the course opens by reading the descriptors with the student, in the student's own words, before a single paragraph is drafted — because once the piece is written around the wrong structure, fixing it is a rewrite.
Ask any prospective tutor to name the criteria for your child's subject and say what each rewards. There is no way to fake the answer and no way to give it without having taught the course.

One practical note for Muwaileh families whose child has already drafted something. A piece built around the wrong structure is a rewrite, not an edit, so the cheapest intervention is always the one that happens before week three. If the draft already exists, the first session should still read the descriptors first and only then look at the text.

sections.heading: Command terms: the cheapest marks in the Diploma
paragraphs: Every IB exam question starts with a command term, and each term has a defined expectation. Outline asks for a brief account. Explain asks for reasons or causes. Distinguish asks for differences made explicit between two things. Discuss asks for a balanced review with evidence on more than one side. Evaluate asks for a judgement supported by criteria.

Students who answer every question in the same register plateau. It is the most reliable ceiling in the Diploma and the easiest one to lift, because the fix is technique rather than content. A Biology candidate who knows homeostasis thoroughly but writes a description where an explanation was asked for loses marks that no further revision will recover.

This is also where a general subject tutor and a Diploma tutor diverge most visibly in a single session. A general tutor marks the content and says it is correct. A Diploma tutor marks against the command term and says the content is correct but the question asked for something else. One of those conversations changes a grade.

The training is mechanical and quick: take a marked paper, identify the command term on each lost mark, and rewrite three answers to the term rather than to the topic. Four sessions of that does more for a mid-band candidate than a term of content revision.

A parent can run this diagnosis without knowing the subject. Take the marked paper, find each lost mark, and read the first word of the question aloud. If the lost marks cluster on explain and discuss while the describe questions scored, the problem is not knowledge and no amount of revision will move it.
bullets: Outline, describe, explain, distinguish, discuss and evaluate are not interchangeable
A correct answer to the wrong command term scores in the lower band
Mark-scheme vocabulary is credited in the sciences; paraphrase often is not
Diagnose from a marked paper, term by term, rather than from the syllabus
This is technique work: four to six sessions, not a term

sections.heading: When a session actually fits in a Muwaileh evening
paragraphs: Scheduling is treated as an afterthought in most tutoring arrangements and it is the reason a good number of them quietly fail. A slot that does not survive the real school day gets moved, then moved again, then cancelled.

Muwaileh's particular problem is dismissal congestion on the Maliha Road corridor and around University City, where several large campuses release within the same window. A family twenty minutes away by map is thirty-five minutes away at 2.45pm. Add a sibling at a different school and the household is not settled before 4.30pm, which makes a 4pm session fiction and a 5pm session the first realistic option.

Compare that with a home visit. A tutor driving out to Muwaileh is in the same traffic, from the other direction, and the time is paid for either as a travel surcharge or inside the rate. The market reflects it: in-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for the same tutor online, with Bestimate's Dubai rate table putting the usual in-home range at AED 180–350. A live-video session starts at the stated minute because nothing has to arrive.

The second scheduling variable is the exam calendar. Sessions in October are doing different work from sessions in March, and the busiest hours in this market are the eight weeks before the main windows. A family that fixes its exam-season slot in the autumn keeps it; a family that waits for mock results takes whatever is left at whatever time.

sections.heading: What a local search finds, and what it misses
paragraphs: Muwaileh has a real local tutoring supply, and it would be dishonest to pretend otherwise. Three universities sit on its doorstep, and the result is a genuine pool of capable subject help at the lower end of the market — the sort that advertises from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, as EdFlik's AED 45–65 and Tutopiya's AED 33–52 bands illustrate.

What that pool is good at is content. A student who missed three weeks of mechanics and needs it taught again is well served by it. What it is not built for is Diploma assessment architecture, because almost nobody in it has marked against IB criteria or taught a Higher Level Paper 3 investigation. That is a specialism, and specialisms do not distribute evenly across a district.

The thin spots are consistent and worth knowing in advance: Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Economics with proper diagram and evaluation coaching, and Theory of Knowledge support. Those are narrow pools in Sharjah generally, and narrower still in a specific hour of a specific week in exam season.

There is no shame in using both. Several families in this catchment run a local or budget tutor for content catch-up and a specialist over live video for assessment technique, and that combination is often the best value available. What does not work is buying one and expecting the other.

Price is worth stating alongside that. The specialist end of this market is quoted at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour online, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 for specialist work, and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 500. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

sections.heading: The coursework boundary, in writing
paragraphs: The Diploma puts more assessed coursework in a student's hands than most systems, and that creates a market. In the researched set, one operator sells completed Internal Assessments outright, at a published price. Naming what that risks is not squeamishness; the consequence lands on the candidate.

IB academic-honesty rules treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and malpractice findings affect the diploma, not the vendor. So the line has to be stated before a parent asks: a tutor teaches the skill, explains the published criteria by letter, interrogates the argument, reads the student's own draft and says where it falls short of the descriptors. A tutor does not write, does not redraft to completion, and does not supply model text for submission.

The same applies to materials. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are their copyright and are available through the school. A tutor works through them with the student and cites the source rather than hosting a download library.

Put the question to any prospective tutor in Muwaileh directly: what will you refuse to do with my child's Internal Assessment? A tutor who has taught the Diploma answers it immediately and usually in more detail than you wanted. Hesitation there is the most informative thing you will hear all week.

There is one more reason to insist on this line beyond the rules. A student who has had a draft written for them has not learned the thing the component exists to teach, and they meet the same demand again in the next subject and again at university. The shortcut compounds.
bullets: Criteria explained and the student's own draft critiqued: legitimate
Writing, completing or supplying text for submission: never
Reproducing board materials as downloads: copyright and malpractice exposure
Keeping the reflection record from week one: the student's job, coached

sections.heading: SPEA, the permit and what you can verify yourself
paragraphs: Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate. Its remit is broader than inspection: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is why provision differs between a Sharjah school and a Dubai school a short drive away, and why a Muwaileh school's IB offer has to be read in the emirate's own context.

Private tutoring sits under a separate rule, and this one a parent can check by asking. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; the fine schedule is not published, so any figure quoted to you should be treated with suspicion. Applications go through MoHRE's own service for private tutor licensing.

Note the related restriction, press-reported rather than taken from the policy document: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE code of conduct carries a similar bar. A tutor offering to teach their own enrolled student is not a shortcut worth taking.

For clarity on our own position: IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed by or partnered with SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge, and holds no educational services permit. Naming a regulator here describes the system a Muwaileh student studies inside. It implies nothing about us.
bullets: SPEA regulates private education in Sharjah, including fee and curriculum approval
The MoHRE private tuition permit is free and valid for two years — ask whether a tutor holds it
No fine schedule is published, so treat quoted penalty figures as unverified
A tuition operation with premises in Dubai needs a separate KHDA Educational Services Permit

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects running alongside the Diploma
paragraphs: A Muwaileh Diploma student is not only doing six IB subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools, and they appear on the report with everything else. Almost no tutoring provider in this market addresses them, which is why a parent looking for Arabic grammar help finds a subject chip and nothing behind it.

The rules are specific enough to matter. KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines require separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and state that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs.

Two consequences for tutoring. First, the stream is part of the match: material for the first-language route does not serve an additional-language student. Second, content is constrained — for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, so the work goes through the school's own material rather than around it. KHDA's instructional time for these subjects is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with at least 25 minutes advised for any mandatory-subject lesson.

One more checkable standard worth knowing: schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. The federal baseline behind all of this is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.
bullets: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the Diploma

sections.heading: Starting, and what happens when nobody is free
paragraphs: The first useful document is not a report card. It is the last marked piece of work — an Internal Assessment draft with comments, a marked paper, a teacher's feedback sheet. A grade says there is a problem; marked work shows which criterion was empty or which command term was missed, and that is the only basis on which a tutor can say something worth paying for before being paid.

From there the sequence is short: confirm the subject and level, take a free trial session over live video at a time that survives a Muwaileh evening, and judge that session on one question — did the tutor name the specific loss and say what the next four sessions would cover? If not, you have spent an hour rather than a term's fees.

Coverage limits are real and should be stated rather than concealed. For a thin specialism, the honest options are a different slot with the right tutor, the right tutor teaching over live video from another time zone, or a plain statement that the match is not available this term. A general science tutor placed in front of a Higher Level Chemistry candidate is not a match, whatever it is called.

Then set a review point before the block starts. Six weeks in, read the next marked piece for the same loss you began with. If it has moved, continue. If it has not, change the plan or change the tutor. Sessions that feel useful while the same marks keep disappearing are how a Diploma year gets spent without a grade changing.
bullets: Send marked work, not the report card
Confirm the subject and level — HL and SL are different jobs
Judge the free trial on diagnosis, not rapport

process.title: Send the last marked piece of work
process.description: An Internal Assessment draft with comments, a marked paper, or a teacher feedback sheet, plus the subject and level. That document tells a tutor which criterion is empty or which command term was missed. A report grade tells them nothing they can act on.

process.title: Confirm subject and level with the school
process.description: Higher Level and Standard Level are different courses with different papers and, in some subjects, different Internal Assessment expectations. Ask the coordinator which level your child is registered at and which session the school is entering them for, and ask for the school's own internal deadline calendar.

process.title: Ask the two IB questions
process.description: Name the criteria for this subject and say what each rewards. Then: what will you refuse to do with my child's coursework? Neither answer can be faked, and together they separate a Diploma tutor from a competent subject tutor in about three minutes.

process.title: Take the free trial over live video
process.description: One session, no payment, at a time that survives the Muwaileh dismissal window — usually 6pm or later for a household with siblings at different schools. Judge it on whether the tutor identified the specific loss and named the next four sessions' work.

process.title: Agree the block and the review point together
process.description: Weekly subject work, a core components block, or a short transition diagnostic, with the target written down. Six weeks later compare marked work against the starting point. If the named loss has not moved, the plan changes or the tutor does.

whyPoints.title: Criteria before content
whyPoints.description: The first session on any Internal Assessment reads the published descriptors with the student, by letter, in their own words. A piece written around the wrong structure cannot be rescued by better content later, which is why this order is not negotiable.

whyPoints.title: Matched to subject and level
whyPoints.description: A profile says Chemistry Higher Level or Mathematics Applications and Interpretation Standard Level, because those are different jobs with different papers. Matching on "science" is how a Higher Level candidate ends up with a tutor learning the course alongside them.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits published
whyPoints.description: The coverage table on this page names where the Diploma pool is thin in Sharjah: Higher Level sciences, Maths AA HL, Economics evaluation, Theory of Knowledge. No competitor in the researched set discloses a coverage limit at all. Knowing the gaps lets you book a term ahead.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated up front
whyPoints.description: Muwaileh students are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Sharjah or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is an India-only service. That belongs on the page, not in a conversation after booking.

whyPoints.title: No unverifiable claims
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no unevidenced examiner status, no star ratings, no guaranteed grades or satisfaction percentages. Every figure here carries its source and the month it was read, including the IB exam dates this page deliberately does not publish because they could not be verified.

whyPoints.title: The coursework line is explicit
whyPoints.description: Teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own draft. Never writing it, never supplying text. Stated plainly because an operator in this market sells finished Internal Assessments, and the malpractice risk from that falls on the student's diploma.

faqs.question: Is there an IB home tutor in Muwaileh who actually knows the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Muwaileh has a genuine local tutoring supply, helped by the universities next door, and it is good at content. Diploma assessment specialism is a different and much thinner pool anywhere in Sharjah — International Baccalaureate students were 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school population in 2024-25 against 37 per cent on UK curricula. So a radius search usually finds a competent subject tutor rather than an IB one. The practical answer is to widen the pool instead of the radius: live-video teaching reaches the specialist even when nobody nearby teaches that level.

faqs.question: How can I tell whether a tutor really knows IB marking?
faqs.answer: Ask them to name the criteria for your child's subject and say what each one rewards. Internal Assessments are marked criterion by criterion, each lettered, each with its own descriptors, and the marks are added afterwards — which is why a mathematically perfect exploration with no personal engagement still loses those marks. A tutor who has taught the course answers without hesitating. One who has not will talk about confidence and exam practice instead.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to homes in Muwaileh?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Sharjah or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we provide only in India. Muwaileh students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the draft or past paper on a shared screen. The gain is the pool: for a Higher Level science or Theory of Knowledge, the choice stops being whoever will drive out past University City and becomes whoever teaches the component properly.

faqs.question: My child's work looks correct but keeps scoring a 4. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because a criterion is empty rather than because the content is wrong. IB Internal Assessments credit separate criteria — research question, method, analysis and evaluation in the sciences; communication, presentation, reasoning and personal engagement in a mathematics exploration — and strength in one cannot compensate for an absence in another. Students who say they did everything asked usually answered the task without addressing every descriptor. The fix is reading the criteria together before the next piece is drafted.

faqs.question: Which command terms cost Muwaileh students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Every IB question opens with one, and each has a defined expectation: outline wants a brief account, explain wants reasons, distinguish wants differences made explicit, discuss wants a balanced review, evaluate wants a judgement supported by criteria. A student who answers all of them in the same register plateaus regardless of how well they know the content. It is the most common ceiling in the Diploma and the quickest to lift, because the work is technique — four to six sessions on a marked paper, term by term.

faqs.question: What time can a tutoring session realistically start in Muwaileh?
faqs.answer: Six o'clock for most households, and 5pm only where there is a single child at a Muwaileh school. Dismissal congestion along the Maliha Road corridor and around University City is sharp, several large campuses release in the same window, and a household with siblings at different schools is rarely settled before 4.30pm. Students commuting back from Dubai schools are looking at 7.30pm. Slots are booked in Gulf Standard Time and held weekly, and during Ramadan most families move to a post-Iftar time.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they are worth more attention than they usually get — together they carry up to three points on the Diploma total. Support is structured as feedback cycles: unpacking the prescribed title, questioning the argument, reading the student's own draft against the published criteria, and keeping the reflection record on track from week one. What a tutor never does is write, redraft to completion or supply model text. The school supervisor's internal deadlines set the timeline, not an external one.

faqs.question: Is my child better off on Mathematics Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches is the algebra-and-proof route and is the one most engineering, mathematics and physics degree courses expect; Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended investigation and the most common cause of a predicted grade falling. Applications and Interpretation is statistics, modelling and technology-permitted work throughout, and students arriving from a British curriculum often misread it as easier rather than different. Check the entry requirements of the actual universities on your child's list, because the two routes are not interchangeable for every course.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Sharjah need to hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published. Since it costs nothing, there is no innocent reason for a working tutor not to hold it.

faqs.question: What does SPEA do, and does it regulate tutoring?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and its remit goes beyond inspection: Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That shapes what a Muwaileh school can offer. It does not license individual tutors, which falls under the MoHRE permit. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE or the IB, and naming them here describes the system rather than implying any endorsement.

faqs.question: Where should I get my child's IB exam and deadline dates from?
faqs.answer: Because they could not be verified from the source that sets them. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a date a parent plans around has to be right. UAE schools sit the May session; beyond that, confirm every date — exam window, internal deadlines, results release — with your school's IB coordinator. Cambridge and Pearson dates can be stated because those boards publish them: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January.

faqs.question: Should we use a cheap local tutor or an online specialist?
faqs.answer: Often both, for different jobs. The lower-cost local band — advertised from around AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik at AED 45–65 and Tutopiya at AED 33–52 — is genuinely useful for re-teaching missed content. It is not built for Diploma assessment technique, because almost nobody in it has marked against IB criteria. A specialist at the market's AED 150–300 online band does the criteria and command-term work. Buying one and expecting the other is the usual mistake.

faqs.question: My child is moving from the Middle Years Programme into the Diploma. What should we do first?
faqs.answer: A short diagnostic on assessment architecture, before Year 12 rather than after the first grade drop. The MYP credits process and communication through four criteria per subject; the Diploma raises the bar on justified reasoning and formalises it in Internal Assessment criteria and command terms. MYP mathematics also samples topics the Diploma assumes fluency in, so the specific algebra, functions and proof work the DP course opens with is worth four to six sessions on its own. Done early it is short; done late it is expensive.

faqs.question: How do I judge whether the tutoring is working after a month?
faqs.answer: On marked work, against the loss you named at the start. Get the failure mode in writing before the block begins — an empty evaluation criterion, command terms answered identically, diagrams unlabelled. After four to six sessions, read the next marked piece or school assessment for that same loss. If it has shifted, continue. If it has not, change the plan or the tutor. Sessions that feel productive while the same marks keep going is the most expensive pattern in this market.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-muwaileh.closingHeading: Send the marked work and ask about the criteria
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-muwaileh.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB home tutor in Muwaileh, the test that predicts everything is short. Send the last marked piece of work, say which subject and level, and ask any tutor you are considering to name the criteria and say what each rewards. Then take a free trial session over live video at a time that survives the Muwaileh dismissal window — usually six o'clock or later. You will know inside the hour whether the tutor sees what the examiner saw, and that is a cheaper test than a term of invoices.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-sharjah-garden-.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IB Primary Years, Middle Years and Diploma subjects to students across Sharjah. Each works to the deadline in front of the student - a mock, an internal assessment, a final series - and writes down what the next six sessions will cover, so a parent can check progress against something dated.

intro.heading: Start with the date, not the subject
paragraphs: Ask a parent in Sharjah Garden City why they are looking for an IB tutor and the answer almost always contains a date. The report came home in November. Mocks are in six weeks. The chemistry internal assessment draft is due before the holiday. DP2 starts in August and nothing was done over the summer. The subject matters, but the date is what creates the urgency, and the date is what should shape the plan.

That is not how tutoring is usually sold. The standard offer is a weekly hour, indefinitely, in a subject. It suits the provider because it is simple to schedule and it renews itself. It suits a student far less, because the Diploma Programme does not apply pressure evenly. There are weeks in DP1 where almost nothing is due and weeks in DP2 where an internal assessment, a Theory of Knowledge essay draft and three tests collide. A plan that ignores that shape wastes the quiet weeks and arrives short in the loud ones.

Sharjah Garden City sits on the emirate's southern corridor, which adds a practical constraint. Diploma Programme provision in this emirate is concentrated in a small number of schools, so children here often travel a distance to school. A tutor who also has to drive, in the same afternoon traffic, can usually offer only a late slot - and a late slot in the week before a deadline is worth less than a punctual one on the right evening. Teaching over video removes the journey from both sides of the arrangement.

So the shape of our work here is a backwards plan. Name the deadline. Work out what has to be true a fortnight before it, then six weeks before it, then now. Decide what the weekly hour is for in each of those phases, because it should not be the same thing in all three. Teaching content, practising under time and repairing specific errors are different activities, and ordering them correctly is most of what a good tutor contributes.

One consequence of planning this way is that we sometimes recommend fewer hours than a family expected to buy. A DP1 student with a settled exploration question and no immediate deadline may need a fortnightly session rather than a weekly one, with the saved budget held for the term when internal assessments and revision collide. A provider paid by the hour has no reason to say that, which is exactly why a plan with dates in it protects the family as much as it protects the student.

The rest of this page sets that out in detail: the Diploma Programme year counted backwards, what an eight-week block can and cannot achieve, how the Middle Years criteria shape the earlier years, where Ramadan and the holiday pattern change the arithmetic, what two years of support actually costs, and where the line sits on assessed work when a deadline is close.

Eight weeks is enough to change technique; it is not enough to teach two years

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-sharjah-garden-.programmesIntro: The three IB stages apply pressure at different points in the year, and a tutoring plan that works for one is wrong for another. Here is what each stage demands and when it demands it.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led, with no external examinations, so the calendar pressure is internal: unit assessments, the exhibition in the final year, and the reading and number fluency that the Middle Years will assume. Support at this stage should be short and frequent rather than intensive, and it should be stopped when the gap closes.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving into Sharjah Garden City from other systems often arrive mid-year, and a PYP class does not pause for them. The useful tutoring window is the first term after arrival, aimed at the specific gap the move created rather than at general enrichment.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria by letter, with task-specific descriptors issued per assignment. The calendar here is a sequence of criterion-marked tasks spread through the year, which means the student's grade is decided in pieces. A weak task in the second term cannot be revised away in the fourth; it has to be outscored by later work.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah schools timetable mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies alongside the Middle Years curriculum, so the week is full. Evening sessions here work best at forty-five minutes on one criterion rather than a long general hour.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, Theory of Knowledge, an extended essay and creativity, activity, service, finishing with terminal examinations in the session the school enters. Internal assessments are marked against published criteria and moderated. The characteristic failure is not difficulty but collision: several deadlines landing in one fortnight of DP2 while revision should already be under way.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. We do not publish IB examination or results dates on this page because the IB's own site could not be verified by us directly; your school's IB coordinator holds the confirmed dates, and those are the ones a plan should be built on.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is usually proposed late in DP1 and written over a holiday. Students who choose a broad question lose a term to rework. Calculus content builds through DP2, so a gap left in differentiation in the first year resurfaces exactly when revision should be starting.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical content is front-loaded at higher level and catches students who chose the course as the lighter option. The exploration needs data that genuinely exists, which is a decision to make early rather than a sentence to write late.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics and equilibrium in DP1, organic depth in DP2, and an internal assessment whose variables must be controlled rather than interesting. The practical work is typically done months before the write-up, so poor planning in the first year cannot be fixed by good writing in the second.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics in the first year decides how the fields and circuits content lands in the second. The investigation rewards honest uncertainty treatment over ambition, and the time to say so is at the proposal stage, not at the draft.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content accumulates steadily, so students who revise only before tests arrive at the final term with two years of unconsolidated material. Data-based questions and statistics in the investigation are where marks move fastest with targeted practice.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries spread across both years, each tied to a current article and one section of the syllabus. Students who leave all three to DP2 compromise both the commentaries and their revision. Diagram accuracy is quick to fix and routinely neglected.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral is a scheduled event, not a piece of writing, and rehearsal has to be booked into the calendar weeks ahead. The higher level essay needs a text chosen early enough to reread properly.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the extended essay
subjects.description: Both run alongside six subjects and both are scheduled by the school, with internal deadlines well before anything the IB sees. These are the two components most often left late, and the two where lateness is least recoverable. Coaching here is about sequence, questions and criteria - never about writing the text.

sections.heading: What a parent in Sharjah Garden City is really asking about time
paragraphs: The question behind the search is rarely 'who teaches chemistry'. It is 'is it too late'. That question deserves a straight answer, and the answer depends entirely on which deadline is in view. Eight weeks before a mock, a great deal is possible. Eight weeks before an internal assessment draft, a lot is possible but the practical work may already constrain it. Eight weeks before the final session, technique and error repair are available and reteaching two years of content is not.

This is where most tutoring conversations go wrong. A provider who says yes to everything will tell a family in March that a Diploma student can be transformed by May. A provider who says no to everything loses the family a term of useful work. The accurate answer is a list: these things can change in the time available, those cannot, and here is what the hours would be spent on.

There is a second time question specific to this corridor. A weekday session has to start after a school run that can be long, because Diploma provision in this emirate is concentrated in a few schools. If a tutor is also driving, the realistic start slips later, and a late start in a deadline week is when sessions get cancelled. Online lessons start when the student is home and ready, which sounds minor and is the difference between eight sessions and five in an eight-week block.

So before anything else, we ask for the date. Mock week, draft deadline, the school's internal submission date, the session the school has entered. From there the plan is arithmetic rather than optimism.

sections.heading: The Diploma Programme counted backwards
paragraphs: Almost nobody publishes this, which is strange, because it is the thing a parent most needs. The Diploma Programme is two years long and the pressure is unevenly distributed. Working backwards from the session a school enters, the shape is reliable enough to plan against even though the exact dates belong to each school's own calendar.

The final term is revision and examinations, with nothing new taught. The term before it is where internal assessments, the extended essay and Theory of Knowledge must be finished, because they cannot be done during revision. The year before that - DP1 - is when subject content is built, the exploration or investigation is proposed and the practical work is done. The quiet weeks in DP1 are therefore the most valuable tutoring weeks in the whole programme, and they are the ones families skip.

Two warnings about dates. First, the deadline that binds your child is the school's internal one, not the board's, and it is usually earlier than parents assume. Ask the coordinator for the written internal calendar at the start of DP2; most schools will supply it and most families never request it. Second, we deliberately do not publish IB examination or results dates on this page: we could not verify them from the IB's own site, and a wrong date on a page like this is worse than no date at all. Your school's IB coordinator has the confirmed version.

For British-track siblings in the same household, the comparable facts are published and verifiable. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November - the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can actually change
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the planning unit we use because it is long enough to show measurable movement and short enough that a family can see the end of it. Inside eight weeks, with one or two sessions a week, three things reliably improve: question technique, timing, and the specific errors a student repeats. Those are worth real marks, particularly in subjects where students know more than their scripts suggest.

What eight weeks does not do is replace a year of content. If a Diploma student has not understood differentiation, or has never securely learned the chemistry of equilibrium, the block can prioritise the highest-value topics and will have to leave others alone. Deciding which to abandon is uncomfortable and is exactly what a specialist is for. A tutor who promises to cover everything in eight weeks is planning to cover nothing properly.

The internal structure of a block matters more than its length. The first two or three sessions close the largest gaps and establish a baseline on a timed paper. The middle sessions are full timed work, marked against the published criteria or mark scheme, with an error log kept by question type. The last two weeks introduce nothing new; they review the log. Families who start this sequence too late end up doing the first phase in the week that should have been the last.

We write the block down and review at session six against marks, not effort. If the movement is not there, we would rather change the tutor or the approach than extend the arrangement quietly for another term.

sections.heading: The Middle Years calendar, where the damage is usually done
paragraphs: Parents arrive in the Diploma Programme worrying about the Diploma Programme. In practice a large share of DP difficulty is inherited from the Middle Years, and the inheritance is visible years earlier if anybody is reading the criteria rather than the grade.

Middle Years assessment is criterion-based, with achievement levels against criteria by letter and task-specific descriptors issued per assignment. A student can score respectably by being diligent and still never master the thing the criteria reward: using command terms precisely, structuring an investigation, and justifying a conclusion from the evidence actually collected. Those are the exact skills the Diploma then assumes, in subjects where there is no time to teach them.

The calendar point is that Middle Years tasks are spread through the year and each one is marked once. There is no terminal paper to rescue a weak term, so a poor task in the second term has to be outscored later rather than revised away. That makes early, specific intervention unusually efficient: a few sessions on investigation structure before the next science task is worth more than a term of homework supervision.

In Sharjah the week is also fuller than in many systems, because private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed curriculum under federal regulations. Short, criterion-focused sessions respect that reality. Long general ones compete with homework and lose.

The diagnostic question for a parent is simple enough to ask at the next parents' evening: which criterion is my child weakest on, and what would a higher level of achievement look like on that criterion in the next task? A teacher can answer that in a sentence. If nobody can, the grade on the report is not telling you what you think it is.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the weeks that quietly disappear
paragraphs: Every academic plan in this country has to survive Ramadan, and most tutoring plans are written as if it does not exist. School days shorten, afternoons are low in energy, and the useful working hours move. Families commonly shift sessions to after Iftar, or to late morning at the weekend, and a plan written in advance for that month keeps its momentum while an improvised one loses three weeks.

The same is true of the long summer break between DP1 and DP2. It is the single quietest working window in the Diploma Programme and the obvious time to settle an exploration question, do the reading for an extended essay, or close a content gap that has been dragging since the Middle Years. Most students do none of it, which is why the first month of DP2 so often starts with a backlog.

Holiday travel is the other recurring disruption on this corridor, where many families spend part of the summer abroad. An online slot follows the student, with the timezone adjusted, which is a genuine practical advantage over an arrangement that depends on somebody driving to an address. Three sessions during a six-week absence keep an internal assessment moving; zero sessions mean September starts behind.

Finally, the school's own calendar in Sharjah is approved in a regulated framework: the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private schools in the emirate and, with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The practical takeaway is that your school's dates and assessment pattern are not arbitrary, and asking for them in writing is a reasonable request.

sections.heading: What two years of IB support costs, not what an hour costs
paragraphs: Hourly rates are the wrong unit for a two-year programme. A family deciding whether to support a Diploma student needs the total, because the decision that matters is whether the arrangement can be sustained into DP2 when it is needed most. Starting at a rate that cannot be maintained is a common and avoidable error.

In market terms, published UAE rate cards put budget online tutoring from about AED 45 an hour, a qualified subject tutor teaching online between roughly AED 150 and 300, an in-home visit between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed, and named or examiner-branded tutoring at AED 500 to 650 and above. Bestimate's Dubai cost estimates, read in October 2026, translate a single weekly session into roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month with a qualified tutor and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Put across a Diploma, the useful comparison is not hour against hour but pattern against pattern. One subject supported weekly through both years costs considerably more in total than two focused eight-week blocks per year placed where the deadlines are, and for many students the blocks produce more because the hours arrive when they can be used. The table below sets out the arithmetic so a family can choose deliberately.

These are market figures, published so you can judge any quote you receive against them, including ours. There is no IB Gram price list on this page; ask us directly and begin with the free trial lesson. And note what the in-home premium is buying: a car on the southern corridor, not deeper knowledge of an internal assessment criterion.

sections.heading: Online lessons when the deadline is close
paragraphs: In a deadline week, the properties of a lesson that matter are different from the ones families weigh when choosing a tutor in September. Punctuality matters more. The ability to move a session by two hours matters more. Having last week's annotated work in front of both people matters more. Rapport matters less than it did, because the work is now specific.

Online lessons are stronger on all three of those. There is no journey to be late for, a slot can shift at short notice without renegotiating anybody's drive, and the archive of marked work sits in one place rather than in a notebook that stayed at school. Against that, a student needs a quiet room and a working headset, and some genuinely concentrate better with a person beside them.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE - home tutoring in a family's house is something we run only in India - so the honest framing is that online is what we do and the free trial lesson is how you find out whether it suits your child. That is a better test than any argument on a web page, and it costs nothing.

What we will not do is imply a car is coming. Several pages in this search result are vague about delivery and resolve into a video call after a deposit. For a family working to a dated plan, knowing exactly what is being delivered is part of the plan.

sections.heading: Deadline pressure and academic honesty
paragraphs: The week before an internal assessment deadline is when families are most tempted and most vulnerable. A student is behind, a parent is anxious, and the internet offers to solve it for a fee. This is the point at which the boundary needs to be known in advance, because nobody makes a good decision about it at eleven o'clock the night before.

The permitted help is substantial. A tutor may explain each criterion, question a research question until it can actually be answered, teach the statistics an investigation needs, point out that an evaluation does not address what the criterion asks, and demonstrate the same analytical move on different material. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit any part of the submitted work, and may not supply a ready-made topic with the thinking already done.

IB Gram does not sell completed internal assessments, extended essays, Theory of Knowledge essays or coursework. Operations that do appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams. The consequence of using one falls on the student, as a malpractice finding against their diploma, not on the seller. No grade is worth that, and no deadline justifies it.

The practical defence is calendar discipline, which is where this page started. Students who read the criteria in the first week, agree a deadline earlier than the school's, and show a draft to somebody three weeks out are not the students who end up negotiating with an essay mill. That sequence is cheap, and it is most of what our internal assessment coaching actually is.

whyPoints.description: Eight weeks changes technique, timing and repeated errors. It does not reteach two years of content. Saying which topics are being abandoned is part of the plan, and a provider who claims to cover everything in the final stretch is planning to cover nothing properly.
