faqs.question: Can an IB home tutor in Sharjah Garden City actually come to our villa?
faqs.answer: Some tutors in the Sharjah market do travel to homes, and in-home rates are quoted between roughly AED 180 and 500 an hour once the drive is absorbed. IB Gram does not: we run no home visits anywhere in the UAE, because that service exists only in India. For families on this southern corridor the practical consequence is positive, since Diploma specialists are scarce locally and online matching reaches them wherever they live. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and the free trial lesson lets you test the format before committing.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start IB tutoring before the final exams?
faqs.answer: It depends which deadline is in view. Eight weeks before a mock, a great deal is available. Eight weeks before an internal assessment deadline, the practical work may already limit what can change. Eight weeks before the final session, you can improve question technique, timing and repeated errors, and you cannot reteach two years of content. The useful answer from any tutor is a list of what will and will not change in the weeks available, with the topics being abandoned named explicitly rather than quietly skipped.

faqs.question: Which IB deadlines does a parent actually need in writing?
faqs.answer: Ask the coordinator for the school's internal calendar at the start of DP2: internal assessment submission dates per subject, the extended essay checkpoints, the Theory of Knowledge essay deadline, and the mock window. These internal dates bind your child and sit earlier than anything the board publishes. Most schools will provide the list and very few families request it. We do not publish IB examination or results dates on this page because we could not verify them from the IB's own site; the coordinator holds the confirmed version.

faqs.question: Is the summer between DP1 and DP2 really worth working through?
faqs.answer: It is the most efficient working window in the whole programme. Nothing is due, no tests compete for attention, and three or four sessions can settle an exploration question, do the reading for an extended essay, or close a content gap that has been dragging since the Middle Years. Students who use it start DP2 even; students who do not start behind and spend the first month catching up during the term when deadlines begin stacking. Because lessons are online, the sessions also survive a family travelling abroad for part of the break.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week should a Diploma student have?
faqs.answer: One a week per subject is the normal starting point and is sufficient when the student does the work between lessons. Two is justified inside a deadline block, when the work shifts to full timed papers that need marking and review. Beyond two in a single subject, the limiting factor becomes independent practice rather than teaching time, and the extra hour tends to produce dependence instead of marks. We review frequency at session six and will recommend reducing it when that is the honest call.

faqs.question: What does support across two years of the Diploma cost?
faqs.answer: Using market rates rather than ours: a qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour across published UAE rate cards. Weekly support in one subject across both years is around seventy hours; two focused eight-week blocks a year is nearer fifty, and the final eight weeks alone is about twelve. Bestimate's Dubai estimates, read in October 2026, put a weekly session at AED 600 to 1,200 a month with a qualified tutor. Choose the pattern you can sustain into DP2, since that is the year that needs it.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change an IB tutoring schedule?
faqs.answer: It moves the working hours rather than removing them. School days shorten, afternoons are low-energy, and most families shift sessions to after Iftar or to late morning at the weekend. The plan should be rewritten before the month starts, particularly for a DP2 student with an internal assessment deadline inside it, because improvising usually costs two or three weeks. An online slot can move by two hours without renegotiating a journey, which is the practical reason the format holds up better through Ramadan than an in-home arrangement.

faqs.question: My child's Middle Years grades look fine but their teachers mention criteria. Should I worry?
faqs.answer: Read the criterion letters rather than the overall grade. Middle Years subjects are assessed against criteria with task-specific descriptors, and a diligent student can score respectably while remaining weak at precisely what the Diploma will assume: using command terms accurately, structuring an investigation, and justifying a conclusion from the evidence collected. Those skills transfer directly, and they are far cheaper to fix in the Middle Years than in DP1. A few sessions aimed at one criterion before the next task is unusually efficient use of money.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do with an internal assessment that is behind schedule?
faqs.answer: Explain each criterion, question the research question until it can be answered with the data available, teach the statistics the investigation needs, read a draft and say which criterion is not being met, and model the same analytical move on different material. What a tutor cannot do is write, redraft or edit any part of the submitted work, or hand over a topic with the thinking already done. IB Gram does not sell completed internal assessments or extended essays. The malpractice consequence falls on the student, which is why the boundary is not negotiable.

faqs.question: Can you coach the extended essay and Theory of Knowledge to a school deadline?
faqs.answer: Yes, as coaching on sequence, question choice and criteria rather than as writing support. Both components run alongside six subjects, both are scheduled by the school with internal deadlines well before anything the IB sees, and both are routinely left late because neither has a weekly test to force progress. Useful sessions here look like project management: choosing a question that can actually be answered, agreeing checkpoints earlier than the school's, and reading drafts against the published descriptors. The student writes every word.

faqs.question: How do mock results change the plan?
faqs.answer: They should change it substantially, because a mock is the first honest timed evidence most students produce. We read the script rather than the grade: which question types lost marks, whether the paper was finished, whether errors are knowledge gaps or technique. A mock that reveals timing problems leads to a different eight weeks than one that reveals missing content. Bring the marked script to the trial lesson if you have it; it is worth more than any description of how the term has been going.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one of my child's IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, within a group - maths and physics, or two humanities - and rarely across distant subjects. The honest position is that Diploma subjects are specialised enough that the second subject is usually taught less well than the first, and higher level content exposes that quickly. Where a family wants one point of contact, we would rather provide two specialists with consecutive slots on the same evening than a single tutor whose second subject is approximate. You can test both in free trial lessons before deciding.

faqs.question: Does SPEA regulate what my child's school can do with assessment dates?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private schools in the emirate and, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. So the assessment pattern and fee structure at a Sharjah school have been through an approval process rather than being set freely. Practically, this means asking your school for its written assessment calendar is a reasonable request about something already documented. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from SPEA or any other UAE authority.

faqs.question: What if we need a specialist in a narrow subject at a specific hour?
faqs.answer: Tell us the hour and the subject and we will give you a straight answer. Narrow Diploma requests - a higher level language, Theory of Knowledge coaching at a peak evening slot, a less common science at short notice - sometimes have nobody free, particularly in the weeks before a session. We will offer a different time with the right specialist, or a named date when one becomes available. We will not fill the slot with a generalist, because in a deadline block that choice costs a family the weeks they came for.

intro.heading: When nobody is driving out here, the process matters more
paragraphs: Tilal City sits along the Sharjah–Dhaid corridor, past University City and well beyond the Muwaileh school cluster. For most daily purposes that distance is manageable. For a weekly one-hour tutoring visit it is close to decisive: a tutor making that round trip is giving up an hour of travel to sell one hour of teaching, and either the rate reflects it or the arrangement quietly collapses after a month.

That removes the usual question. A family in Al Taawun can at least weigh local candidates against online ones. A family in Tilal City is mostly choosing between an online specialist and nobody, which sounds bleak and is actually clarifying — because it shifts the whole question from where the tutor sits to whether the arrangement is any good.

Which is a question almost nobody asks properly. Most tutoring is bought on a rate and a reassuring conversation, and then runs for a term on goodwill, with nobody having defined what it was supposed to change or when that would be visible. The result is a parent six weeks in, vaguely dissatisfied, with no way to say whether the problem is the tutor, the plan or the student.

So this page is about mechanism. How a match should be made, from what evidence. What a tutor profile should state and what should be treated as a warning sign. What a trial session is for, and what a parent should take away from it. What a session note should contain. How to read progress after four sessions. And how to change a tutor without it being a confrontation.

The Diploma raises the stakes on all of this because its specialists are scarce. International Baccalaureate students made up 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school population in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on UK curricula, and Sharjah's IB provision is concentrated in a small number of continuum schools. A badly made match is not just a waste of money here; it is a waste of a scarce person's availability, and the replacement may not be free until next term.

It is also a short list of things to agree, not a project. Four facts to assemble, three documents to ask for, two review dates to fix. Half an hour of work before the first invoice, and it is the half hour that decides whether the next twenty hours are worth anything.

Everything on this page applies to any provider, including this one. A page that teaches you how to evaluate tutoring is making a bet that it survives being evaluated, which is a more useful offer to a Tilal City parent than a list of adjectives about quality.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. In-home tutoring is offered only in India, and there is no UAE office or centre. Tilal City students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the draft or past paper on a shared screen.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-tilal-city.programmesIntro: The programmes behind this search, with what each one requires a tutor to have actually done rather than studied. That distinction is the whole of a good match.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked against lettered criteria added separately. A tutor match for the Diploma therefore requires someone who has worked from those descriptors, not someone who has studied the subject to a higher level — those are different qualifications and only one of them diagnoses a mid-band Internal Assessment.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No Diploma exam or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and a date a family plans around has to be right; take every one from your school's IB coordinator. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the Diploma in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, scored 0–8 and converted to a 1–7 grade. Matching here needs someone who can name the four criteria for the subject in question, because the standard failure is a capable student sitting at a 4 with correct work and a thin justification or communication criterion. A general subject tutor will improve the content and leave the grade where it was.
programmes.countryNote: For families out along the Dhaid corridor, the Middle Years Programme years are when an arrangement has to be built to last, because starting again locally in Year 11 is not realistic. An online slot established in Year 8 survives a house move, a school change and a holiday, which in this part of the emirate is worth more than it would be closer in.

programmes.name: DP courses and partial routes
programmes.description: Not every student in an IB school takes the full Diploma. Some take DP courses rather than the full certificate, with subject exams and Internal Assessments but no Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge requirement. The match is simpler and the plan should be correspondingly narrower — importing a full-Diploma timeline onto a courses candidate buys hours that have nothing to do.
programmes.countryNote: Establishing which route a student is on is a question for the IB coordinator and it should happen before any tutoring is agreed. It changes the number of components in play, the internal deadline calendar, and whether core-component support is relevant at all, and it is the single most common thing a tutoring enquiry fails to establish.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led with no external examinations, so it rarely generates tutoring searches. Where it matters in a community like this one is continuity: a family choosing a continuum school now is choosing which assessment model their child meets at 11 and 16, and in a location where school options are a drive rather than a walk, that decision is harder to revisit later.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent. Provision across the region is expanding rather than static, so a school decision made for a young child is worth revisiting as new campuses open nearer.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-tilal-city.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects requested from this part of Sharjah, each with the thing a matched tutor should be able to say unprompted. If they cannot, the match has not been made on the right evidence.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Should be able to describe how Higher Level Paper 3 differs from Papers 1 and 2 before any rate is discussed, and to name what the exploration's personal engagement criterion actually asks for. Those two answers separate a mathematician from a Diploma mathematics teacher.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Should know that the exploration rewards genuinely collected data and that the decision is made in week one. A tutor who treats this route as the easier one has not taught it; the modelling questions are unfamiliar territory for students arriving from a British curriculum.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Should name the Internal Assessment criteria and explain why a tidy textbook result earns nothing by itself. Should also be able to say what a weak research question looks like, since that is the failure that cannot be fixed after the fact.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Should know the Internal Assessment credits design and uncertainty handling rather than accuracy, and should be able to describe how a Higher Level extended response is structured — principle first, then calculation. Both are checkable claims in one conversation.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Should distinguish what outline, describe, explain, distinguish and discuss each expect, and should mention data questions on unfamiliar experiments as trainable. A tutor who attributes a plateau to effort rather than command terms has not marked Biology.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Should say that diagram marks are awarded piece by piece and that the commentary article choice determines the ceiling. If they talk about economic theory and not about the judgement sentence, they are teaching the subject rather than the assessment.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Should separate the Individual Oral from Paper 1 unseen analysis as different jobs, and should be able to describe the move from summary to analysis of construction. Higher Level's essay is assessed on sustained argument rather than coverage.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Should mention that the Internal Assessment needs real organisational data and that sourcing it is the task that stalls students for weeks. Should also know that application to the named organisation is what separates bands in the written papers.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.levels: Language A, language acquisition and ab initio
subjects.description: Should ask which stream the student is on before anything else, because separate classes exist for Arab and non-Arab students and material does not transfer between them. A tutor who offers generic Arabic material has not worked in a UAE school.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Should ask for the school supervisor's checkpoint dates first, and should mention the reflection record unprompted. Those marks are the most commonly lost in the Diploma and the easiest to secure, purely through keeping the record rather than reconstructing it.

sections.heading: What a match should actually be made from
paragraphs: A tutoring match is usually made from three things: the subject, the year group, and whether a slot is free. That is enough to produce a plausible arrangement and not enough to produce a useful one.

The evidence that makes a match worth something is narrower. First, the programme and the level — Higher and Standard Level are different courses with different papers and, in some subjects, different Internal Assessment expectations, so matching on "Biology" is matching on half the information. Second, the specific loss visible in a piece of marked work: a criterion left empty, command terms answered identically, a research question too broad to answer.

Third, and most often skipped, the position in the calendar. A student with an Internal Assessment already submitted needs a different tutor plan from one still choosing a research question, because the first has a banked mark and the second has a live one. A match made without asking about internal deadlines will put the hours in the wrong place.

From a location like Tilal City there is a fourth: the time the session can actually run. A household commuting in from the Dhaid corridor is settled later than one in Muwaileh, and a tutor matched to a 5pm slot that nobody can keep is not matched at all. The slot has to be real before the person is chosen.

Those four facts take one email and twenty minutes with a marked paper to assemble. A provider who asks for all four before proposing a tutor is doing the job. One who asks for the subject and the year group is allocating, not matching.

sections.heading: What a tutor profile should say, and what should worry you
paragraphs: Profiles in this market are written to impress rather than to inform, and the difference is easy to spot once you know what a useful one contains.

A useful profile names the programme and level taught, the components the tutor has worked on, and the kind of student they are effective with. "IB Diploma Chemistry Higher Level; Internal Assessment feedback and Paper 2 extended response; strongest with students who know the content and lose marks on reasoning" tells a parent something. "Experienced IB tutor, passionate about science" does not.

Four claims should be read as warnings rather than credentials. Examiner status, where current status cannot be evidenced — and it should never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because no legitimate tutor has that. Regulator approval, because SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB and Cambridge do not accredit tutoring platforms in that way; a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai.

Third, star ratings and review counts that are not backed by real, countable, attributable reviews. Competitors in this market publish contradictory figures on the same page, and one shows a five-star average from twenty reviews against a separate claim about how many students it has taught. Fourth, any statistic without a sample size, a date and a method: satisfaction percentages, median tutor scores, proportions of students achieving a grade.

For completeness about us: IB Gram holds no regulator approval, accreditation, licence or partnership with any UAE authority or examination board, operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and publishes no ratings or outcome statistics it cannot evidence. Students we support attend schools across Sharjah; that is the whole of the relationship.

sections.heading: What a trial session is for
paragraphs: A free trial lesson is widely offered and widely misunderstood. Most families treat it as a chance for the child to meet the tutor and see whether they get on, which is worth something but is not the point.

The point is to test the diagnosis. Before the session, send the marked work and name the subject and level. During the session, the tutor should work on something real rather than conduct an interview. Afterwards, the test is whether they can say: here is the specific thing costing marks, here is what the next four sessions will do about it, and here is how you will see it in the next school assessment.

A tutor who cannot do that after an hour with marked work in front of them will not be able to do it after eight, and the trial has just saved a term's fees. A tutor who can has told you what you are buying, which converts the rate question from a guess into a judgement.

Two things a trial should not be. It should not require a card or carry a condition that is not stated on the same screen — if a trial is described as free, the length, the eligibility and any commitment attached to it belong in the same sentence. And it should not be a sales call with a teaching segment attached; the hour should be spent on the work.

Rapport matters, just less than people think and in a specific way: a student who dreads the session will not do the work between sessions, which halves the value of the hour. So rapport is a necessary condition and diagnosis is the sufficient one, and a trial should be judged on both in that order.

sections.heading: What should arrive after each session
paragraphs: This is the mechanism that makes an arrangement reviewable, and its absence is why so many tutoring relationships run for months with nobody able to say whether they are working.

A session note does not need to be long. Four lines is enough: what was covered, what the student did well, what is still wrong, and what they should do before the next session. The last two are the ones that matter, because they are the only parts a parent can check against the next piece of marked work.

What a note should not be is a summary of topics touched. "Worked on organic chemistry, good progress" is unfalsifiable and tells a parent nothing they can act on. "Still naming products without the functional group; practise the five conditions table before Tuesday" is checkable by anyone, including a parent who has never studied chemistry.

From a location like Tilal City the notes carry extra weight, because you are not going to bump into the tutor in the hallway or overhear the session from the kitchen in the same way. The written record is the visibility, and it should be part of the arrangement rather than something requested after a month of unease.

Over four sessions the notes should also start to repeat in a useful way: the same named loss, narrowing. If the notes name a different problem every week, nobody has made a diagnosis, and that is worth raising at session four rather than at the end of term.

sections.heading: Reading progress at four sessions and at eight
paragraphs: Progress in tutoring is read badly because it is read from feeling. The session was good, the child seemed happier, the tutor is nice — none of which predicts a grade.

At four sessions, the question is narrow: has the named loss started to appear less? Not has the grade moved, which is too slow a measure, but has the specific behaviour changed in the work. A student who was writing answers without method on multi-mark questions should be showing method, imperfectly. A student whose evaluation criterion was empty should be attempting evaluation, badly. Imperfect attempts at the right thing are the four-session signal.

At eight sessions, a school assessment should show it. This is where the review belongs, because school marks are the only measure that counts and the only one neither you nor the tutor controls. Compare the marked work against the piece you started from, looking for the same loss specifically rather than at the total.

If the loss has not moved at eight sessions, there are three explanations and they need separating. The plan was aimed at the wrong thing — fixable by re-diagnosing. The student is not working between sessions — fixable by changing what the sessions ask for. Or the match is wrong, which is common, says nothing about either party, and should be resolved by changing the tutor rather than by waiting.

The thing not to do is extend on hope. The most expensive pattern in this market is a term of pleasant sessions while the same marks keep disappearing, and from a location where the replacement tutor may not be free until next term, catching it at eight sessions rather than at twenty matters more than usual.

sections.heading: Changing a tutor without a confrontation
paragraphs: Mismatches are normal. A student and a teacher can both be good and still not work together, and in a scarce specialism the odds of the first allocation being ideal are not high. The problem is that families treat a change as an accusation and therefore delay it.

The fix is to agree the mechanism before it is needed. At the point of booking, ask one question: how does a tutor change work, and what does it cost? A reasonable answer is that it happens on request, without justification, and the slot is kept. An answer that involves a complaints process, a notice period or a fee is telling you something about how long you will be staying with a bad match.

When a change is needed, the useful framing is the named loss rather than the person. "The method-marks problem hasn't moved in eight sessions and we'd like to try a different approach" is a complete and honest reason, and it also gives the next tutor the brief. There is no need to critique anyone's teaching.

Carry the error log across. The accumulated record of what has been tried — which is what the session notes become — is genuinely valuable to a replacement and saves two sessions of rediscovery. A provider who does not hand that over is losing your money on your behalf.

And do it with the calendar in mind. A change in October is cheap. A change in April, in a thin specialism, may mean waiting, which is exactly why the eight-session review exists and why ignoring it costs more than the sessions themselves.

sections.heading: The coursework boundary and the data a tutor holds
paragraphs: Two things an arrangement should settle in writing at the start, because both are easier to agree before there is any pressure.

The coursework boundary first. A tutor may explain the published criteria by letter, question an argument, read the student's own draft and name where it falls short of the descriptors, and teach the skill the task requires. A tutor may not write submitted text, redraft to completion, or supply model answers to work from. IB rules treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate's diploma rather than on the tutor or the platform. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright at a published price.

A practical safeguard that costs nothing: ask for feedback as spoken comments or margin notes rather than as edits inside the document. It removes the ambiguity entirely, for the student's protection as much as anyone's, and a tutor who objects to it is telling you something.

Second, the data. Tutoring involves a provider holding information about a minor — name, school, year group, marked work, sometimes recorded sessions. A family is entitled to know what is collected, why, how long it is kept and how to have it deleted, and the UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection sits behind that expectation. A privacy policy should be linked from any page that collects a lead form, and a form should not be collecting a child's school, grades and photograph without a stated purpose.

Neither of these is a formality in practice. The coursework boundary protects a qualification the student has spent two years on, and the data question protects a child whose school, marks and image are being handed to a commercial service by a parent who assumed it was fine.

sections.heading: The permit, the regulator and honest scarcity
paragraphs: Three closing pieces of context, all of which a Tilal City family should have before agreeing anything.

The permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no schedule of amounts published, so treat any figure quoted to you as unverified. Because the permit is free, there is no innocent reason for a working tutor to be without it.

The regulator. Sharjah's private schools fall under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate, and Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods — a wider remit than inspection alone. Naming it here describes the system your child studies inside and implies nothing about any tutoring provider, including this one.

Scarcity. Diploma specialists are a thin pool regionally, not just locally: Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Economics with proper evaluation coaching, and Theory of Knowledge support are the narrowest. Availability is seasonal as well, and the eight weeks before the main window are the busiest hours in the market.

Which is why, from a community along this corridor, the honest advice is to establish the arrangement early and review it on schedule. The eight-session review is not bureaucracy; it is what stops a mismatch from consuming a term you cannot get back and a slot you may not be able to replace.

whyPoints.description: Four lines after each session: covered, went well, still wrong, do before next time. The third and fourth lines are the only ones a parent can check, and from a location like this the written record is the visibility.

whyPoints.title: The review points are fixed in advance
whyPoints.description: Four sessions for imperfect attempts at the right thing, eight for a school assessment showing the loss reduced. Fixing them before the first invoice is what prevents a term of pleasant sessions while the same marks disappear.

whyPoints.title: Changing tutors is a mechanism, not a complaint
whyPoints.description: On request, without justification, with the session notes and error log carried across. In a scarce specialism a mismatch is likely rather than surprising, and the cost of delay rises sharply as the exam window approaches.

whyPoints.title: No claims that cannot be evidenced
whyPoints.description: No regulator approval, no examiner status we cannot show, no star ratings, no guaranteed grades, no satisfaction percentages. Competitors in this market publish contradictory review counts on the same page; every figure here carries its source and the month it was read.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and data stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Tilal City students are taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE, operates no UAE office, and will tell you what personal data is held about your child, why, and how to have it deleted.

faqs.question: Will any IB tutor actually travel to Tilal City for a weekly session?
faqs.answer: Very few, and it is worth being clear why rather than dressing it up. Tilal City sits along the Sharjah–Dhaid corridor beyond the main school cluster, so a tutor making the round trip gives up roughly an hour of travel to sell one teaching hour. Either the rate carries that cost or the arrangement collapses after a month of rescheduling. For Diploma specialists, who are a thin pool regionally, it almost never happens. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case; lessons are over live video.

faqs.question: What information should a tutoring service ask for before proposing a tutor?
faqs.answer: Four things. The programme and level, because Higher and Standard Level are different courses. The specific loss visible in a marked piece of work. Where you are in the school's internal deadline calendar, since a submitted Internal Assessment is a banked mark and the hours belong elsewhere. And a session time your week can genuinely sustain. A provider asking only for the subject and year group is allocating a tutor rather than matching one.

faqs.question: What should a tutor profile tell me, and what should make me cautious?
faqs.answer: It should name the programme, the level, the components the tutor has actually worked on, and the kind of student they are effective with. Treat four things as warnings: examiner status that cannot be evidenced, regulator approval — SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry, the IB and Cambridge do not accredit tutoring platforms that way — star ratings not backed by countable attributable reviews, and any statistic published without a sample size, a date and a method.

faqs.question: What should I be looking for in a free trial lesson?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis, not a conversation. Send the marked work beforehand and judge the hour on three things: did the tutor name the specific behaviour costing marks, did they say what the next four sessions would do about it, and did they explain how you would see the change in the next school assessment? A tutor who cannot do that with marked work in front of them after an hour will not manage it after eight. Any condition attached to a free trial should be stated on the same screen.

faqs.question: What should arrive after each tutoring session?
faqs.answer: Four lines: what was covered, what went well, what is still wrong, and what the student should do before next time. The last two are the only ones you can check. "Worked on organic chemistry, good progress" is unfalsifiable; "still naming products without the functional group, practise the conditions table before Tuesday" is checkable by a parent who never studied chemistry. Across four notes the same loss should keep appearing and narrowing.

faqs.question: At what point should a Tilal City family expect visible progress?
faqs.answer: At four sessions, look for imperfect attempts at the right thing — method being shown badly rather than not at all, evaluation attempted rather than absent. At eight, look for the named loss reduced in a real school assessment, because school marks are the only measure neither you nor the tutor controls. Compare against the piece you started from, looking at that specific loss rather than at the total. A grade is too slow a measure to steer by.

faqs.question: What do I do if the tutoring is not working after eight sessions?
faqs.answer: Separate three explanations before deciding. The plan may be aimed at the wrong thing, which is fixed by re-diagnosing from marked work. The student may not be working between sessions, which is fixed by changing what the sessions ask for. Or the match is wrong, which is common in a scarce specialism and says nothing about either party. Do not extend on hope — from this part of Sharjah the replacement specialist may not be free until next term.

faqs.question: How should I raise changing a tutor without it becoming awkward?
faqs.answer: Agree the mechanism when you book: how does a change work and what does it cost? A reasonable answer is on request, without justification, with the slot kept. When the time comes, frame it around the named loss rather than the person — "the method-marks problem hasn't moved in eight sessions and we'd like a different approach" is complete and honest. Ask for the session notes and error log to be carried across, which saves the replacement two sessions of rediscovery.

faqs.question: Why does matching on Higher or Standard Level matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because they are different courses. The papers differ, the content depth differs, and in several subjects the Internal Assessment expectations differ too — Higher Level Mathematics Analysis and Approaches carries Paper 3, an extended investigation with no Standard Level equivalent. A tutor matched on "Mathematics" may be learning your child's level during the first paid sessions, which is a cost you are carrying rather than a service you are buying.

faqs.question: What should I ask about the data a tutoring service holds on my child?
faqs.answer: What is collected, why, how long it is kept, who can see it, and how to have it deleted. Tutoring involves a provider holding information about a minor — name, school, year group, marked work, sometimes recorded sessions — and the UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection sits behind the expectation that this is stated. A lead form should not be asking for a child's school, grades and photograph without a stated purpose, and a privacy link should be on the page.

faqs.question: Where is the line on Internal Assessment and Extended Essay help?
faqs.answer: A tutor may explain the published criteria by letter, question the argument, read the student's own draft and name where it falls short, and teach the skill the task needs. A tutor may not write submitted text, redraft to completion or supply model answers. IB rules treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice and the consequence lands on the candidate's diploma. A practical safeguard that costs nothing: ask for feedback as comments rather than as edits inside the document.

faqs.question: Does a tutor teaching my child from outside the UAE need the MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: The permit regime applies to private tutoring in the UAE and it is a fair question to ask of anyone teaching your child, wherever they sit. It was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school and government-sector teachers, private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Because it is free, a tutor working with UAE families has no cost reason not to hold one, which is why asking is worthwhile.

faqs.question: What time can sessions realistically start from Tilal City?
faqs.answer: Later than from the communities closer in. Students here travel to the Muwaileh and University City campuses, and the return journey runs through the Maliha Road dismissal congestion, so a household is often not settled before six o'clock and sometimes later with children at two schools. Slots are booked in Gulf Standard Time and held weekly, with later slots best used for technique work and weekend mornings for coursework blocks. Most families move to a post-Iftar time during Ramadan.

faqs.question: Which IB specialisms should I book earliest from here?
faqs.answer: Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay support first, because they are the scarcest and the most seasonal — plan a term ahead. Then Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and Economics with proper diagram and evaluation coaching. The eight weeks before the main window are the busiest hours in this market, so a slot held from autumn is a slot you keep. If a specialist is not free, expect to be told plainly rather than offered a general subject tutor.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-tilal-city.closingHeading: Agree the mechanism, then pick the person
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-tilal-city.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB home tutor in Tilal City, the realistic choice is an online specialist rather than a local visit, which makes the quality of the arrangement the only variable worth negotiating. Assemble the four facts — programme and level, the named loss, your position in the school's internal calendar, a session time that survives the commute — then agree the session notes, the review points and the tutor-change process before the first invoice. Then take a free trial and judge it on the diagnosis.

intro.heading: The school run decides the tutoring, not the other way round
paragraphs: University City sits on the eastern edge of Sharjah, built around the University of Sharjah and the American University of Sharjah, with Muwaileh immediately to the west and Al Zahia and Aljada to the north and south. Households here are a particular mix: university staff, postgraduate families, and long-settled Sharjah residents whose children are bussed out to schools in Muwaileh, Al Qulayaa, Al Ramtha and across the Dubai boundary. The common thread is that nobody's child finishes the day where they live.

That single fact is why the question of time of day comes before the question of tutor. A Sharjah secondary school day typically finishes between 2.30pm and 3.30pm, but a child who is bussed back into University City arrives considerably later, and a child attending a Dubai school on the other side of the Al Ittihad Road corridor can arrive after 4.30pm. A 4pm tutoring slot that looks sensible on a calendar is, for many families here, a slot that will be missed or cut short most weeks.

Diploma students have a second constraint the school run hides. A DP student is carrying six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, and in a Sharjah school the timetable also includes Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, which the federal framework requires private schools to teach alongside their licensed international curriculum. The week is already full before anybody adds an hour of tutoring to it.

So the honest shape of IB support in University City is one protected hour a week, in a slot the household can defend, with a tutor who can use the hour on what the student is actually losing marks for. Lessons from IB Gram are delivered one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visits are a service offered only in India. The practical gain for a University City family is that the hour starts when it is meant to and nothing is lost to University City Road. That phrasing is deliberate: an IB home tutor in University City is what parents type, and the service behind the phrase is a one-to-one lesson over video rather than somebody arriving at a door. Saying so before you book is more useful than discovering it afterwards.

There is a quieter gain too. Online delivery means the tutor is chosen for the subject rather than for the drive. A DP2 student who needs somebody who has read dozens of Mathematics Explorations, or who knows what the Economics Higher Level Paper 3 quantitative questions reward, gets that person at 7.30pm on a Tuesday. Under an in-home arrangement, the list of tutors willing to reach the campus belt at that hour is short, and in a thin-supply Higher Level subject it may be empty. Online delivery also means a tutor can stay with a student through a house move inside the emirate or a summer spent abroad, which in this part of Sharjah happens often enough to matter. One more thing follows from the format, and it is the part parents notice last: the session leaves a record. An annotated past-paper script and a short written note after the hour can be re-read on the weekend, which is worth more than a verbal comment nobody can reconstruct three days later.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-university-city.programmesIntro: University City families use all three IB programmes, usually across siblings rather than in sequence. What follows is each programme as a weekly time commitment, because that is the version a parent can plan around.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, a 4,000-word Extended Essay and CAS. Points run from 24 for an awarded diploma to a maximum of 45, with up to three bonus points available from the TOK and Extended Essay matrix. Internal Assessments carry 20% of the grade in the sciences and Mathematics and up to 30% in Economics at Standard Level.
programmes.countryNote: In University City the DP pinch point is the first term of DP2, when two Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay final draft and the first full mocks arrive within a few weeks. Families who book one weekly hour from the start of DP1 are mostly protecting that term. The slot matters as much as the subject: a DP2 student with a 4pm session will miss it during mock weeks, while a 7.30pm session survives the whole year.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against criteria A to D rather than as percentages, with the Personal Project in MYP 5. Students exit into the Diploma or into an IGCSE pathway, and the step into timed external papers is the point at which criterion-based study habits need rebuilding.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students here finish school earlier than Diploma students and have a genuine 4.30pm or 5pm slot available, which is worth using while it exists. An hour a fortnight aimed at writing to a command term and at reading the criterion wording costs little and removes the most common DP1 problem: a capable student who has never written to a mark scheme.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examinations, assessed through portfolios and the Year 6 exhibition. Support at this stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining thinking out loud, not about examination technique.
programmes.countryNote: For a primary child in University City the useful session is short and early: 30 to 40 minutes at around 4.30pm, before fatigue sets in, usually in English reading or number work. Parents of this age group are also the ones for whom an in-person arrangement can genuinely be better, and it is fair to say so even though IB Gram's UAE delivery is online.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-university-city.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects University City households ask about most, with the assessment structure and the place where the hour is best spent. Session length is 60 minutes unless a subject's paper practice needs longer, which the tutor will say rather than assume.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level is Papers 1 and 2 at 40% each with the Exploration at 20%; Higher Level is 30%, 30%, Paper 3 at 20% and the Exploration at 20%. The recurring loss is unjustified reasoning in proof questions and arithmetic slips on the calculator paper, both of which respond to weekly timed practice.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same weightings, different emphasis: statistics, modelling and technology use. Students who can calculate correctly still lose marks by failing to interpret the result in the context the question set, which is a writing habit rather than a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Paper 1 is 36%, Paper 2 is 44% and the Internal Assessment 20%. The extended-response questions reward explanation with a chain of reasoning; a correct formula with no explanation scores a fraction of the marks available.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Weighted 36% Paper 1, 44% Paper 2, 20% Internal Assessment. Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and the quantitative work early in the course are where Diploma students in Sharjah most often need the foundation rebuilt rather than revised.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Also 36 / 44 / 20. Command terms decide long-answer marks: outline, explain and evaluate each want a different structure, and a well-learned paragraph aimed at the wrong verb earns almost nothing.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Standard Level is Paper 1 at 30%, Paper 2 at 40% and the Internal Assessment at 30%; Higher Level adds Paper 3 and moves to 20 / 30 / 30 / 20. The Internal Assessment is three commentaries on published articles, marked on diagram accuracy and on applying one key concept properly.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Paper 1 at 35%, Paper 2 at 40%, Internal Assessment at 25%. Case-study answers that describe a tool score below shorter answers that use it to reach a supported judgement, which is the single most teachable habit in the subject.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 guided analysis, Paper 2 comparative essay and the Individual Oral, with an HL Essay added at Higher Level. Paper 1 marks are lost to paraphrase; the question asks how a text constructs meaning for an audience, not what it says.

subjects.name: Psychology and History
subjects.description: Both are essay subjects where structure and evidence selection carry the marks. Tutoring works on planning under time pressure and on using studies or sources as argument rather than as decoration.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and Internal Assessment supervision
subjects.description: Process coaching only: framing a question, understanding the assessment criteria, planning research, referencing, and feedback on the student's own drafts. A tutor reads, questions and comments. Writing or completing the work is malpractice under IB rules, and IB Gram does not do it.

sections.heading: When a tutoring session can realistically start in University City
paragraphs: The earliest workable online start for most University City secondary students is 5.30pm, and for Diploma students 7pm is more reliable. That is a scheduling answer, not a preference. Sharjah secondary schools typically finish between 2.30pm and 3.30pm, but the gap between dismissal and a student being free to concentrate includes a bus route through Muwaileh, a meal, and in many households a sibling's pick-up as well.

The campus belt adds its own pattern. University City is a destination for tens of thousands of university students each day, and the roads that serve it, University City Road and the Maliha Road approach, carry that load alongside the school-bus traffic. A tutor driving in for a 4.30pm appointment is budgeting for that journey twice, which is one of the reasons the in-home rate in this market sits above the online one.

The table below sets out what each year group can realistically hold. It is built from how slots are actually booked rather than from an ideal timetable, and the useful instruction inside it is simple: choose the slot from your child's arrival time, not from the school's finish time. A slot chosen optimistically gets missed, and a missed slot is the most common reason a tutoring plan quietly ends in week six. There is one more variable worth building in. Families with two or three children in different year groups cannot run both sessions in the same window, and the workable pattern is usually the younger child at 5pm on one evening and the older at 7pm on another, rather than back-to-back hours on a single night. Splitting the week that way also keeps one evening completely free, which is the thing a Diploma student needs most in the first term of DP2.

sections.heading: The Diploma week, counted in hours before tutoring is added
paragraphs: Before adding an hour, it is worth counting the hours already committed. A DP student in a Sharjah school sits six subjects, three at Higher Level, which at Higher Level is 240 recommended teaching hours per subject across the two years and 150 at Standard Level. On top of that sit Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay, CAS, and the Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies lessons the federal framework requires private schools to teach alongside their licensed curriculum.

The consequence is that tutoring is never added to free time. It is traded against something, and the honest conversation is about what. For most DP1 students the trade is screen time or a second CAS activity, and that is fine. For a DP2 student in the first term, the trade may be sleep, which is not fine, and the right answer is often two shorter sessions rather than one long one, or a pause during the fortnight when two Internal Assessments are due.

The table below lists the real commitments of a Diploma week so a household can see where an hour comes from. It is also the argument for starting early: an hour a week from the beginning of DP1 is cheap in time terms, while three hours a week in the last term of DP2 is taken straight out of the student's capacity to revise independently, which is the thing that actually produces marks. The same arithmetic explains why the second subject is a bigger decision than the first. Adding one hour a week is a trade a household can absorb; adding two means a student is working with a tutor on two evenings and revising on the others, and at that point the limiting resource is attention rather than money.

sections.heading: Why online fits a University City school run better than a visit
paragraphs: In-home tutoring exists in Sharjah and some families prefer it. For a household in the campus belt, three practical factors push the other way, and they are worth stating as factors rather than as sales points. The first is timing: an in-home session has to survive the tutor's journey, and a tutor coming into University City between 4pm and 7pm is crossing the same congestion the school buses are in.

The second is the tutor pool. An in-home arrangement limits you to tutors willing to drive to this district at a specific hour. For English or general maths that list exists. For Physics at Higher Level, Economics Higher Level with its Paper 3, Computer Science or a less-common Group 2 language, it may be very short, and a short list is how families end up with an approximately suitable tutor. Online removes the radius entirely, so the only constraint is the tutor's own calendar.

The third is the material. Diploma work from DP1 onwards is marked scripts, past papers and criteria, all of which read better on a shared screen with annotation than across a kitchen table, and which can be saved and re-read afterwards. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE, so the comparison below describes the market rather than a menu. The one fair point for the in-home format stands: a young primary child may genuinely do better with somebody in the room. From Year 10 upwards the balance tips the other way, because the work itself has become paper-based and technical. A tutor pointing at a mark scheme on a shared screen, highlighting the two words in a question that change the required answer, is doing something a kitchen table does not improve on.

sections.heading: Mapping the Diploma coursework calendar onto a Sharjah school year
paragraphs: A Diploma student's real deadlines are set by their own school, not by the examination session, and that is the calendar tutoring should follow. The school's internal dates for Internal Assessment drafts, the Extended Essay interim deadlines and the Theory of Knowledge essay sit months ahead of anything the IB publishes, and they are the dates that generate the stress in a University City household in the first term of DP2.

IB session dates are deliberately not published on this page. The IB's own site is the only source worth acting on for them, and the May session is the one UAE schools sit. Confirm every date with the school's Diploma coordinator rather than with a tutoring page. What a tutoring plan can do is work backwards from the school's internal deadlines: question framing early, methodology or source selection next, feedback on the student's own draft after that, and nothing resembling writing at any stage.

The ordering below is the one that reduces late-stage panic most reliably. It also keeps the academic-honesty boundary clean, because each step asks the student to produce something first and the tutor to respond second. Where a school's dates differ, the school's dates win, and a tutor who argues with a Diploma coordinator's calendar is a tutor to replace. The same calendar discipline helps with the Extended Essay, which fails most often on timing rather than on ability. A student who has a question agreed and a reading list started before the long summer between DP1 and DP2 writes a better essay than one who begins in September, and the tutoring hours needed drop by half.
bullets: Ask the Diploma coordinator for the school's internal coursework dates in writing
Extended Essay: 4,000 words maximum; Theory of Knowledge essay: 1,600 words
Mathematics Exploration is expected in the 12 to 20 page range
Internal Assessments carry 20% of the grade in the sciences and Mathematics, and up to 30% in Economics at Standard Level
Confirm IB session dates with the school or on the IB's own site, never from a tutoring page

sections.heading: What an hour of Diploma tutoring should contain
paragraphs: An hour is short, and the difference between a useful hour and a pleasant one is how it is spent. A good Diploma session has a shape: ten minutes on the work since last time, with a specific question the student brings; twenty-five to thirty minutes on the topic or technique that marked work shows is weakest; fifteen minutes of timed practice on that exact thing; and a closing instruction about what to do before next week.

What that hour should not be is a re-teaching of the lesson the school taught on Monday. Sharjah schools in this belt teach the Diploma competently, and paying a second person to deliver the same content is the most common waste in the market. The gap is almost always between knowing the content and producing it under a mark scheme, in the time allowed, in the form the command term requires.

That is why marked work matters more than confidence as a review signal. Every four to six weeks, look at a marked paper and ask whether the same errors are still appearing. If they are, the plan changes: different topic order, different balance of practice to teaching, or a different tutor. Most families who review properly end up reducing hours rather than adding them, which is the outcome an honest arrangement should produce. The closing instruction is the part most often skipped and the part that makes the week between sessions useful. One sentence is enough: attempt these four questions under time, or redraft this paragraph of the Internal Assessment and bring it. A session that ends without one leaves the student waiting for the next hour instead of working in between.
bullets: Student brings a specific question from the week's work
One technique or topic per session, chosen from marked work
Timed practice inside the hour, not set as homework only
A single clear instruction for the week ahead
Review against a marked paper every four to six weeks

sections.heading: What Diploma support costs in the Sharjah market
paragraphs: Take the cheapest end first, because that is where most families start. Budget online platforms publish from roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour: Tutopiya from about AED 33 to AED 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. That tier buys supervision and company, and for a student who simply will not sit down to work it can be the right purchase. It does not reliably buy somebody who knows what a Diploma Paper 2 mark scheme rewards.

A step up, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200, TutorChase lists about AED 270, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. In-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's figures, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500, the difference being travel. BartyED's AED 650 sits at the premium named-tutor end. Those figures were read in October 2026 and belong to the providers named.

Translated into a monthly plan, Bestimate's estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are roughly AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to over AED 2,000 for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in the UAE include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. None of these is an IB Gram quote: our arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a plan, and price follows a tutor seeing the student's work.

sections.heading: SPEA, the federal baseline and what it means for a Diploma student here
paragraphs: Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader remit than inspection alone, and it is different from Dubai, where the Knowledge and Human Development Authority oversees the quality of private education, and from Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, where the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. In Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools.

For a University City family, two consequences are practical. A school's programme offer is approved rather than assumed, so the sensible move before choosing subject levels is to check what the school is currently licensed to run instead of relying on a prospectus from three years ago. And the federal baseline requires private schools to teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, which is both a timetable fact and an often-overlooked tutoring need for a Diploma student whose Arabic is weak.

Tutors are regulated under a separate route. The private tuition work permit comes from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so none is quoted. IB Gram holds no SPEA, Ministry or examination-board approval and claims none.
bullets: SPEA approves Sharjah school fees, curricula and assessment methods
Private schools teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the IB
The MoHRE private tuition permit is free and valid for two years
