sections.heading: Equivalency and what a Diploma student should check in Year 11
paragraphs: Families planning on a UAE university place need the Ministry of Education's equivalency of the school certificate, and it is worth reading the requirement years before it applies. For the British track the published rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. A competitor page ranking for UAE tutoring queries states six IGCSE subjects are needed; the sourced figure is five.

On the American track, English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold is published here, because that number has to be read on moe.gov.ae or confirmed with the attestation authority. Publishing an unsourced figure on a page a parent acts on would be worse than publishing nothing.

The reason this belongs on a page about school-run timing is that it is a Year 9 and Year 11 decision, not a Year 13 one. A student who checks early shapes their subject choices around the requirement at no cost. A student who checks late may need an additional entry as a private candidate, with the tutoring and the November series that implies. Equivalency is a Ministry process: IB Gram does not perform it, guarantee it or have any role in it, and tutoring is not required for it.

process.title: Tell us the arrival time, not the finish time
process.description: The first useful piece of information is when your child is actually home and able to think, including the bus route and any sibling pick-up. Everything else in the plan is built from that, because a slot chosen from the school's dismissal time is a slot that gets missed by October.

process.title: Send the subject list with levels
process.description: Six subjects, which three are Higher Level, and the Mathematics route: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation. Add the last marked paper or school report. That is enough to match a tutor properly and it removes the diagnostic sessions you would otherwise pay for.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson in the real slot
process.description: Run the trial at the time you intend to keep, not at a convenient one-off hour. You are testing two things at once: whether the tutor knows where marks are lost in that paper, and whether your household can actually hold that hour every week.

process.title: Fix the slot and the review date
process.description: One subject, one hour, the same time each week in Gulf Standard Time, with a review date four to six weeks out written down at the start. A plan with a review date is a plan somebody will look at again, which is how hours get reduced when they are no longer needed.

process.title: Adjust around the school's coursework dates
process.description: When two Internal Assessment drafts fall in the same fortnight, the sensible move is often two shorter sessions, a temporary switch to coursework coaching, or a pause. Tutoring that ignores the school calendar adds pressure at exactly the wrong moment.

whyPoints.title: Built around the Sharjah school run
whyPoints.description: Slots are chosen from when a child reaches home in University City, not from when the school bell rings. That single piece of realism is the difference between a plan that lasts a term and one that fades after a month of missed sessions.

whyPoints.title: The hour is the whole hour
whyPoints.description: Online delivery removes the travel that sits inside every in-home quote here and the risk that congestion on University City Road shortens a session. Nothing is lost to the journey, in either money or minutes.

whyPoints.title: Subject specialists, not a local radius
whyPoints.description: A Diploma family here gets the tutor who knows the Economics Higher Level Paper 3 pattern or the Mathematics Exploration criteria, rather than the best tutor willing to drive to the campus belt at 7pm on a weekday.

whyPoints.title: Coursework handled inside the rules
whyPoints.description: Internal Assessment, Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge support is question framing, criteria explanation and feedback on the student's own drafts. Nothing is written, completed or edited to a finish, because that is malpractice and the student carries the consequence.

whyPoints.title: Figures and limits you can check
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is attributed and dated, every regulatory statement comes from the authority's own wording, and no IB examination date is published here because the IB's own site is the only place to read one.

faqs.question: What time can an IB tutoring session start for a child living in University City?
faqs.answer: For most secondary students 5.30pm is the earliest slot that holds all term, and for Diploma students 7pm is more reliable. Sharjah secondary schools typically finish between 2.30pm and 3.30pm, but a bus route back through Muwaileh, a meal and a sibling pick-up usually consume the next two hours. Choose the slot from your child's arrival time rather than the school's dismissal time. Primary children are the exception: 4.30pm for 30 to 40 minutes works better for them, because concentration rather than traffic is the limiting factor at that age.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a villa or apartment in University City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. UAE tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video, booked in Gulf Standard Time. The reason is practical rather than ideological: the tutor pool stops being limited to people willing to drive into the campus belt at 5pm, so a student who needs a Higher Level Physics or Economics specialist gets one. The search term is honest about what parents look for, and this answer is honest about what is sold.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a DP1 student in Sharjah actually have spare?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most plans assume. A Diploma student carries six subjects with three at Higher Level, which is roughly 15 to 21 taught hours a week, plus Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay work, CAS and the Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies lessons a Sharjah private school includes alongside its licensed curriculum. One tutoring hour a week is realistic from DP1. Three hours a week is usually taken out of independent revision time, which is the activity that produces most of the marks, so adding hours can reduce the result rather than improve it.

faqs.question: Is one long session or two short ones better for a Diploma student after a school day?
faqs.answer: Two shorter sessions usually win in DP2, and one longer session is fine in DP1. The deciding factor is fatigue: a student who has been in school since 7.30am and travelled home through Muwaileh has limited concentration left, and 45 focused minutes beats 90 distracted ones. Two sessions also give the student two chances a week to bring a problem rather than one, which matters when Internal Assessment drafts are moving. The arrangement can collapse back to a single weekly hour once the pressure point has passed.

faqs.question: Can lessons be arranged on a Friday morning in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some households here it is the best slot of the week. Sharjah's government sector moved to a Friday-to-Sunday weekend, so a family with a parent working in a Sharjah government role often has Friday morning genuinely free, which a Dubai-working household rarely does. A 90-minute Friday or Saturday morning block is long enough for a full timed paper plus review, carries no traffic or school-run exposure, and suits coursework supervision particularly well. It also leaves weekday evenings clear for school homework.

faqs.question: What should happen in the first four sessions with a new IB tutor?
faqs.answer: Session one works from a marked paper or report you have shared, so the tutor identifies where marks are actually lost rather than asking general questions. Sessions two and three take the weakest topic or technique and rebuild it, with timed practice inside the hour. Session four tests whether it held, using a past-paper question under time. By the end of the fourth hour you should have a written view of the student's three biggest mark losses and a plan addressing them in order. If you do not, change tutor.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in eastern Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Higher Level sciences, Economics at Higher Level because of Paper 3, Computer Science, and Group 2 languages beyond the common ones. That scarcity is the strongest practical argument for online delivery: an in-home arrangement limits you to tutors willing to drive to University City at a fixed hour, and in these subjects that list can be empty. Online, the constraint becomes the specialist's calendar instead of the map. Where no suitable tutor has availability in the slot you need, you are told plainly rather than matched to somebody approximately right.

faqs.question: Will the tutoring plan follow the internal deadlines a Sharjah school sets?
faqs.answer: By using the school's internal calendar as the plan. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the written dates for Internal Assessment drafts, Extended Essay interim deadlines and the Theory of Knowledge essay, then share them. Those dates, not the examination session, generate the pressure in the first term of DP2. A tutor then works backwards: question framing early, method or source selection next, feedback on the student's own draft after that. Where a school's date differs from a tutor's suggested schedule, the school's date wins without discussion.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do on an Extended Essay, and where is the line?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help a student narrow a researchable question, explain what the assessment criteria actually reward, suggest how to structure an argument, teach referencing, read the student's own draft and ask the questions a supervisor would ask. A tutor cannot write any part of it, cannot edit it to completion and cannot supply a model to be adapted. That line is IB academic-honesty policy, and the consequence of crossing it falls on the student: a withheld grade or a withdrawn diploma. IB Gram coaches the process and does not produce the work.

faqs.question: My son insists he needs somebody in the room. Is a video lesson still worth trying?
faqs.answer: For Diploma-level work, usually yes, because the material is marked scripts, past papers and criteria, all of which read better on a shared annotated screen than across a table, and can be saved and re-read afterwards. The honest exception is younger children, where somebody physically in the room can genuinely help. The test is cheap: take the free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep and watch the first fifteen minutes. If the student is engaged with the tutor's annotations, the format is working.

faqs.question: How much does one-to-one IB Diploma tutoring cost in the Sharjah market?
faqs.answer: Published figures, read in October 2026, run from about AED 33 to AED 65 an hour for budget online platforms, with Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase about AED 270, and Bestimate puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180 to AED 350 on Bestimate's figures because travel is inside the rate. Those are the providers' own figures, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Is it sensible to use the same tutor for two subjects out of the six?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it reduces coordination when it works. A Mathematics specialist can often take both Analysis and Approaches and a science at Standard Level; a Physics tutor may also handle Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation. The limit is paper-specific experience at Higher Level, where the Paper 3 formats diverge sharply between subjects. Ask which specific papers and levels the tutor has taught and judge the answer rather than the claim. Two subjects also means two hours a week, so check the student's capacity before the tutor's.

faqs.question: What happens to sessions during Ramadan and the Sharjah exam season?
faqs.answer: Both are handled by moving the slot rather than stopping. During Ramadan school hours shorten and families commonly shift tutoring to a post-Iftar time, which an online arrangement can do without renegotiating anybody's journey. In mock fortnights the usual change is a temporary switch from new content to timed-paper practice, or a short pause if the student's own revision schedule is tight. Because the tutor stays the same across those changes, nothing is lost in restarting, which is the main cost of disruption in a term.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether the tutoring is working before the next report?
faqs.answer: Look at marked work rather than at mood. Every four to six weeks, read a marked paper and ask whether the same mark-scheme errors are still appearing: the same missing justification in proof, the same command-term mismatch, the same unlabelled diagram. Improvement shows as different errors, not as a happier student, although that often follows. If the same losses repeat across two marked papers, the plan changes: different topic order, more timed practice, or a different tutor. Most families who review this way end up reducing hours rather than adding them.

sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-university-city.closingHeading: Pick the hour first, then the tutor
sharjah/ib-home-tutor-in-university-city.closingBody: Searching for an IB home tutor in University City usually ends in a practical decision about one evening hour. Choose it from when your child is actually home and able to think, protect it, and give it to a tutor who can name the weightings and the mark losses in the subject. IB Gram delivers that hour one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no travel inside the price and no visit to a UAE address. Send the subject list with levels, the last marked paper and the arrival time, take the free trial lesson in the slot you intend to keep, and decide from what you see.

intro.heading: Two children, two systems, two completely different kinds of evidence
paragraphs: The search that leads here is rarely about one child. A family in Al Suyoh or Al Jazzat has a Year 11 candidate three months from externally marked IGCSE papers and a Diploma student in DP1 whose first internal assessment deadline has just appeared on a shared calendar. Both need help. Neither needs the same help, and the common mistake is to buy one arrangement and apply it to both, which produces a tutor who is excellent for one child and underemployed for the other.

The difference is not difficulty, it is where the marks live. An IGCSE grade is decided almost entirely on exam day, by externally marked papers, which means the useful evidence is a marked script: what was credited, what was withheld, and whether the same habit is still costing the same marks six weeks later. A Diploma grade is partly decided months earlier, inside internally assessed work that the school marks and the IB moderates, which means the useful evidence is a draft with criterion-referenced feedback against it.

That distinction changes everything downstream. For the IGCSE child, progress is visible fortnightly in marked papers and is comparable across time. For the Diploma child, progress for several months is visible only in the quality of a research question, a method, and an argument, none of which produce a number. Parents who try to read both children on the same dashboard conclude that the Diploma student is making no progress, when what is actually happening is that the progress is not yet numerical.

So this page is built around artefacts rather than promises. It sets out what should exist on paper after four sessions in each system, how to read a 9-1 or A*-G against a 1-7 without inventing an equivalence that does not exist, what a tutor may and may not touch when the work is internally assessed, how mock season differs between the two, and what the IGCSE-to-Diploma jump actually costs in weeks. If you can see the artefacts, you can judge the spend. If you cannot, you are buying reassurance.

One practical matter stated early rather than discovered late. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service available only in India. Every session for a Sharjah family runs one-to-one over live video at a fixed time in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own work shared on screen and annotated during the hour. For a two-child household that turns out to be the easier arrangement anyway: two slots on one evening, two specialists, and no second car journey. Nothing on this page asks you to take that on trust, which is the whole reason it is organised around documents you can hold rather than qualities you cannot check.

sharjah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Four stages account for nearly every two-curriculum household in this emirate. Read them for what each one produces as evidence, because that is what determines whether tutoring can be judged or merely trusted.

programmes.name: IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Externally marked papers at the end of a two-year course, with Cambridge using four-digit codes and Pearson Edexcel using codes such as 4MA1. Several Cambridge subjects tier into Core and Extended, which sets the paper set and the grade ceiling. Because almost everything is decided on exam day, the evidence that matters is a marked script and the pattern across several of them. Report-card effort grades correlate poorly with what a paper will award.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah campuses set their own mock windows, often weeks apart from each other, so a household with children at two schools is working to two calendars. Collect both mock windows and both sets of internal deadlines in September. For the IGCSE child specifically, ask the school for the statement of entry, which names the board, code and tier, and hand that line to any tutor before the first session.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 4 and 5
programmes.description: Assessed against criteria labelled A to D in most subjects, with achievement levels rather than percentages, and a Personal Project in the final year. Parents arriving from a percentage-based system find the reporting opaque, because a level 5 against criterion C is not 5 out of 10 and does not map onto a mark. The useful evidence here is the criterion the student is weakest against, which is specific and actionable in a way an overall grade is not.
programmes.countryNote: MYP students in Sharjah often sit alongside IGCSE siblings in the same house, and the two reporting styles are routinely compared when they should not be. A tutor working with an MYP student should be naming criteria, not percentages. If feedback comes back as a mark out of ten, that is a sign the tutor is translating the system into one they find more comfortable.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subject groups studied simultaneously, each graded 1 to 7, with Higher and Standard Level routes carrying different content depth and different assessment weightings. Each subject carries internally assessed work marked by the school and moderated by the IB, alongside externally marked papers. The internal component is where most of the first year's visible evidence sits, which is why a DP1 student can be working hard for two terms without producing a single comparable number.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates in Sharjah are spread across a small number of campuses, and some commute into Dubai. Subject combinations can therefore be unusual, and a student may be the only person in their year taking a particular Higher Level subject. That is a supply problem for a local tutor search and not a problem at all for a code-matched remote match, which is the practical reason this page exists.

programmes.name: The Diploma core: internal assessment, the Extended Essay and TOK
programmes.description: The components that generate the most anxiety and the most academic-honesty risk. Each carries its own criteria, its own word or page limits, and its own internal school deadlines, which arrive earlier than families expect. Support here is strictly teaching, review and feedback on work the student has produced. No part of an assessed piece is written for a candidate, and a provider offering otherwise is offering a malpractice risk rather than a service.
programmes.countryNote: School deadlines for these components in Sharjah are set internally and vary between campuses by several weeks. Get the dates from the coordinator in writing in September. A tutor paced against the school's actual deadlines produces work that arrives finished; a tutor working to a generic calendar produces a good draft a fortnight after it was due.

sharjah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects first, with what each one's internally assessed component actually demands, because that is the part a parent can see progress in during the first year. IGCSE subjects follow in their own grid.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The exploration is where most visible early progress sits: a research question narrow enough to be mathematically substantial, a method the student can defend, and reflection that is genuine rather than decorative. Evidence of progress is a sharper question and a defensible method, both of which exist weeks before any grade does.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with technology integral rather than incidental. Students who choose it expecting an easier route find the data handling demanding. Early evidence looks like a dataset the student actually understands and a model they can justify choosing, rather than a longer piece of writing.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The internally assessed investigation rewards a controlled variable set and an honest uncertainty analysis far more than an ambitious topic. The commonest diagnosis after reading a first draft is that the method cannot answer the question asked. Fixing that is a one-session conversation and saves months.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth that changes how the whole subject must be revised, not just how much. In the internal component, data processing and propagated uncertainty carry marks that are routinely left on the table. Evidence of progress is a results table that survives scrutiny.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy with a data-driven assessment style. The marks that move fastest are in command-term discipline and in statistical treatment of results. A student who can explain why a particular statistical test was chosen is in a different position from one who ran the test the textbook showed.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Commentaries built on recent published articles, assessed against criteria that reward diagram accuracy and explicit evaluation. The most frequent loss is a commentary that summarises an article instead of applying a model to it. That is visible in a first draft and correctable in one session.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Assessment rewards application to a real organisation and a structured argument rather than breadth of theory. Students who know the frameworks still lose marks by listing them. Early evidence of progress is a narrowed research focus and a defensible choice of tools.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Oral and written components both reward close analysis of a specific extract over general thematic discussion. Progress shows up as shorter claims supported by more text. A tutor's main contribution across a term is usually getting the student to write less and evidence more of it.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies must be used as evidence rather than recounted, and the internally assessed experimental study rewards methodological precision over an interesting hypothesis. The earliest visible improvement is in how a student describes a study: aim, method, finding, limitation, in that order and briefly.

sharjah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE grid is organised around the marked script, because that is the evidence that counts in an externally examined course. Codes are listed so a tutor can be matched to the paper set your child will actually sit.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: The subject where evidence is clearest. Method marks either appear on the page or they do not, and the fortnightly comparison is straightforward. Most recoverable marks sit in unshown working on multi-step questions and in rounding before the end of a calculation.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson Edexcel 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Explanation questions are the largest recoverable block: candidates describe an observation where the command term asked for a mechanism. Progress across six weeks is measurable by counting how many explain marks were credited in each successive paper.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson Edexcel 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Balanced equations, state symbols and mole ratios account for a large share of lost marks, and all three are countable. A fix-list after each paper that names the specific slip, rather than the topic, is what produces movement here.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson Edexcel 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Data questions are where the evidence lives: axes, scale choice, units, and the difference between a described trend and a claimed cause. Recall gaps show up differently and are cheaper for a student to close alone with a structured list.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Untiered, so every candidate sits the same papers. Diagram accuracy and command-term discipline separate grades; evaluate questions require a judgement rather than a longer list. Marked data-response questions are the most informative single artefact in this subject.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Application to the case in the paper is an explicit assessment objective, so a technically correct generic answer scores poorly. The improvement is visible as an edit: a paragraph rewritten to anchor each point to the business described.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a First Language (Cambridge 0500)
igcseSubjects.description: Reading and directed writing assessed together. Summary that drifts into comment is penalised, and the writing paper rewards control of register over vocabulary display. Progress shows in timed work, which is the only honest way to assess it.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
igcseSubjects.description: Calculus, matrices and harder trigonometry, sat alongside Extended 0580 as a bridge to Higher Level or A Level mathematics. Thinly staffed locally, which makes it one of the subjects a distance-limited search in Sharjah usually fails to fill.

sharjah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: These notes are about households rather than schools: where families in Sharjah tend to be running more than one curriculum at once, and what that does to an evening. The scheduling consequence is the only local variable that changes the answer.

regions.name: Al Suyoh
regions.note: Newer villa communities with larger families, so two or three children at different stages in one house is the norm rather than the exception. Consecutive slots on a single evening work better here than spreading sessions across the week.

regions.name: Sharjah Garden City
regions.note: Lower-density housing set back from the central corridor, with longer school runs in most directions. The usable working window after the commute is short, which argues for a hard 60 minutes with a written agenda rather than an open-ended session.

regions.name: Al Jazzat
regions.note: Central residential Sharjah with reasonable access to several campuses. Families here frequently have one child in a local British-track school and an older one who moved to a Diploma campus, which is precisely the two-system situation this page is about.

regions.name: Al Riqa
regions.note: Established and compact, with short journeys to the central school belt. Earlier evening slots genuinely exist, which matters for a younger IGCSE child whose concentration fades before a Diploma sibling's does.

regions.name: Al Nabba
regions.note: Older central Sharjah, dense and close to long-established schools. The practical constraint here is a quiet room rather than travel time, and in a household with two students working at once it is the binding one.

regions.name: Al Ghuwair
regions.note: Central and well connected, with families split between Sharjah-licensed campuses and Dubai schools. Two commutes of very different lengths in one household means two different realistic start times, and fixing a single family hour fails for one of the children.

regions.name: Al Fisht
regions.note: Coastal western Sharjah with quick access along the Corniche road, which makes journeys shorter than the map implies. A 5pm start is realistic, and that early slot is usually best given to whichever child has internal deadlines rather than exams.

regions.name: Al Azra
regions.note: Inland residential Sharjah where the visiting-tutor model thins out noticeably, and where finding two tutors for two curricula within a driving radius is close to impossible. Removing travel changes the arithmetic here more than it changes the teaching.

schoolClusters.note: A small number of campuses in or near the emirate offer the Diploma, and several Sharjah households send an older child across the Dubai boundary for it while a younger sibling stays local. That is the single commonest shape of the two-system household.

modes.description: The standard shape for a household with children in both systems. Consecutive slots, a specialist per curriculum, and a shared written record so you can read both children in one place without pretending their grades are comparable. Protecting one quiet ninety-minute block is easier than protecting three separate hours across a week.

modes.description: A short series of sessions timed against the school's own internal deadlines for Diploma coursework. Work is read, discussed against the published criteria, and returned as feedback on what the student has produced. The boundary is written down before the first session, because that boundary is what keeps a candidate out of a malpractice investigation.

sections.heading: What a Sharjah household running two curricula is actually tracking
paragraphs: The literal search is for an IB IGCSE home tutor in Sharjah, and the literal answer is that the local market sells visiting tutors for both at published UAE rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel absorbed. What IB Gram sells is the same one-to-one hour over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the student's own work annotated on screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that service exists only in India.

The reason a two-system household should care about that distinction has nothing to do with cost. It is that two curricula need two specialists, and finding two specialists who will both drive to an inland Sharjah district on the same evening is a much harder search than finding either one. Families usually solve it by hiring one generalist for both children, and the generalist ends up strong in one system and improvising in the other.

What the household is really tracking is whether either child is moving. For the IGCSE candidate that question has a clean answer: compare two marked scripts six weeks apart and count whether the same habit is still costing the same marks. For the Diploma candidate, the first year produces almost no comparable numbers, so the answer lives in the quality of a research question, a method and an argument. Both are checkable. They are just not checkable in the same way.

That is the organising idea for the rest of this page. Each section is about an artefact: a marked script, a criterion-referenced draft, a fix-list, a counted comparison. If a tutoring arrangement does not produce artefacts, there is no way to decide whether to continue, and the decision defaults to how the sessions feel. Feelings are a poor guide here, because a pleasant hour and a productive hour look identical from the next room.
bullets: Two curricula need two specialists; one generalist usually serves only one well
IGCSE progress is countable in marked scripts six weeks apart
Diploma progress in the first year lives in questions, methods and arguments

sections.heading: Two grade scales, and what 'on track' means in each
paragraphs: The first thing to stop doing is converting. An IGCSE grade and an IB subject grade are produced by different assessment systems with different components and different purposes, and no honest conversion table exists between them. Parents build one anyway, because two children with numbers on the fridge invite comparison. The result is a household that has decided one child is doing better than the other on the basis of arithmetic that means nothing.

What does exist is a sense of what counts as on track within each system at a given point in the year, and that is the useful judgement. The table below sets it out for each scale, alongside the evidence that supports the judgement and the misreading that most often follows. The misreading column is the practical part: almost every mistaken conclusion a parent reaches about progress comes from one of those five rows.

Two of the rows deserve highlighting. A Diploma predicted grade is a professional judgement made by the school for university applications, and it is not a measurement of current attainment; treating it as one produces either complacency or panic depending on which direction it points. And an MYP achievement level against a criterion is not a mark out of ten, so dividing it to produce a percentage generates a number that corresponds to nothing.

The practical instruction is to ask for the right artefact per child and then read it on its own terms. For the IGCSE candidate that is the marked script with the mark allocation visible. For the Diploma candidate it is the draft with criterion-referenced comments against it. For an MYP student it is the weakest criterion named explicitly. None of those three is a single number, which is exactly why schools keep sending single numbers instead.

sections.heading: The fortnightly artefact: what should exist after four sessions
paragraphs: Four sessions is the right point to audit, because it is long enough for a competent tutor to have diagnosed something and short enough that a wrong match has not yet cost a term. The question to ask is not whether lessons are going well. It is what exists on paper that did not exist a month ago, and whether a stranger reading it could tell what the problem is.

The table maps this out per fortnight for each curriculum, because the artefacts differ. For the IGCSE child there should be marked questions with the mark allocation visible and a written list of the specific habits costing marks, ordered by how many marks each is worth. For the Diploma child in the first year there should be a narrowed research question, a method that can actually answer it, and feedback referenced to criterion letters rather than to a vague sense of quality.

A note on what does not count. A verbal summary at the end of a session does not count, because it cannot be compared with the one from three weeks earlier. A topic list does not count, because it says what was covered rather than what changed. A photograph of a page of working does not count unless someone has marked it. The test is whether the artefact supports a decision, and most of what tutoring produces does not.

Parents sometimes worry that asking for this is adversarial. It is the opposite: a tutor who is working properly already generates these things, and being asked for them costs nothing. A tutor who cannot produce them after four sessions either is not diagnosing or is not recording, and both of those are worth knowing in week four rather than in April. The request also gives you something to take to a parents' evening, which changes that conversation entirely.

sections.heading: Internally assessed work: the boundary, and the trail a legitimate process leaves
paragraphs: This is the area where the market behaves worst and where the consequences fall on the student rather than the provider. One operator researched for this project openly sells finished Internal Assessments. That is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger, and the candidate carries the outcome. A family buying tutoring for Diploma coursework needs to know exactly where the line sits, and a provider should be able to state it without being asked.

The line is this. A tutor teaches the skills the component assesses, explains the criteria, asks questions that make a student's thinking sharper, and gives feedback on work the student has already produced. A tutor does not write any portion of an assessed piece, does not supply text to be inserted, does not rewrite a paragraph into its finished form, and does not generate the data, the method or the argument. Candidates sign an authenticity declaration on this work, and that declaration is not a formality.

What a legitimate process leaves behind is a trail that supports the declaration rather than undermining it. Dated session notes naming what was discussed. The student's own successive drafts, each recognisably theirs. Feedback phrased as questions and criterion references rather than as replacement sentences. If a parent compared the first draft with the submitted version and found a change of voice, that is the warning sign, and it is one a school moderator is trained to notice too.

There is also a limit on drafts that varies by component and by school, and the school's coordinator is the authority on it rather than a tutoring provider. Ask the coordinator what the school's draft policy is, in writing, in the first term of DP1. Do the same for the internal deadlines, which arrive earlier than families expect and differ between Sharjah campuses by several weeks. A tutor paced against those real dates produces work that arrives on time.

sections.heading: Reading a predicted grade against the evidence you actually hold
paragraphs: Predicted grades cause more domestic confusion in Diploma households than any other single document. They are a professional judgement made by the school, formed from classwork and mock performance, and produced for a purpose: university applications. They are not a measurement of where a student is on the day they are issued, and they are not a promise. Both of the usual reactions to them, relief and alarm, tend to be based on reading them as something they are not.

The useful move is to ask what the prediction was formed from and then look at that. If it came from a mock script, read the script. A prediction two grades above the mock mark is a statement about trajectory and should be interrogated gently; a prediction below the mock mark usually reflects something about coursework that has not yet landed. Either way the underlying document is more informative than the number derived from it.

For the IGCSE child the equivalent document is the school's own forecast or centre-assessed judgement, and the same logic applies: ask what it was based on. In Cambridge's published key dates for a series, forecast grades fall due shortly before the exam period closes, which tells you something useful about when the school's internal judgement is formed. Work backwards from that and the mock becomes the most important script of the year.

None of this means school judgements should be discounted. Teachers see a student across five hours a week for two years and are usually closer to right than a tutor who has seen four papers. The point is narrower: a predicted grade is an input to a decision, not the decision, and the household that holds marked scripts can have a much better conversation at parents' evening than the household that holds only the prediction.

sections.heading: Mock season across two curricula, and what to do with the scripts
paragraphs: Mock windows are the most informative fortnight of the school year and the most frequently wasted. In most households the scripts come home, the grades are discussed, and the papers go into a drawer. The grade is the least useful part of that document. What matters is the distribution of lost marks across question types, and that information has a short shelf life, because it is most actionable in the weeks immediately afterwards.

For the IGCSE candidate, the job is to count. How many marks were lost to unshown method, how many to misread command terms, how many to content that genuinely was not known, and how many to running out of time. Those four categories need four different responses, and only one of them is more revision. A tutor who starts from the mock script rather than from the syllabus is working from evidence; one who starts at chapter one is working from a default.

For the Diploma candidate, mocks sit differently. They test external components while the internal ones are still in progress, so a mock result is a partial picture by design. It is still the best available external evidence, and it is what a predicted grade will largely be formed from. The useful output is the same kind of counted analysis, with the added question of whether weak external performance is partly a function of time spent on coursework.

Two scheduling notes for a Sharjah household. Mock windows differ between campuses by several weeks, so two children at two schools will have two separate intense fortnights, which is easier to handle than one overlapping one. And if one of your children is at a Dubai-side school, their window may be set by a different internal calendar entirely. Write both onto one sheet in September and the year becomes plannable.
bullets: Count lost marks by cause: method, command term, content, timing
Only one of those four causes is answered by more revision

sections.heading: The Year 11 to DP1 gap, subject by subject
paragraphs: The household running both curricula today is usually the household whose younger child will cross from IGCSE into the Diploma in a year or two, which makes this the most useful planning section on the page. The jump is real and it is uneven: the gap between Extended IGCSE and Standard Level is modest in some subjects and substantial in others, and between Extended IGCSE and Higher Level it is substantial in nearly all of them.

The table below maps the common routes. Read the final column as a planning figure rather than a promise, because it depends entirely on where the student finishes Year 11. A student with a comfortable Extended grade needs the shorter end; a student who scraped the tier needs more, and in one or two subjects needs to reconsider Higher Level altogether. That conversation is far cheaper in June than in the October of DP1.

The single most common failure is mathematics. Extended 0580 is a thorough course that does not include calculus, and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes a comfort with algebraic manipulation that the IGCSE does not build. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 exists precisely to bridge that, which is why students heading for Higher Level mathematics are often advised to sit it alongside 0580 if their school offers it.

The quieter failure is in the essay subjects, where the issue is not content but the form of writing. IGCSE rewards structured coverage; Diploma assessment rewards a narrower claim defended with more evidence. Students who were praised for breadth at Year 11 can spend a term writing well-organised answers that score moderately. Naming that early saves more marks than any amount of additional reading.

sections.heading: When the evidence says stop buying hours
paragraphs: A tutoring page that never discusses stopping is not giving advice, it is selling. There are three situations where the right call is to stop or change rather than to buy more sessions, and all three are identifiable from the artefacts this page has been arguing for. Knowing them in advance means the decision gets made on evidence rather than on frustration.

The first is no movement with good engagement. If three marked scripts across half a term show the same habit costing the same marks, and the student is turning up and working, the problem is the plan or the match rather than the quantity. More hours of the same thing will produce more of the same result. The honest response is a different tutor, a different approach, or a frank conversation about whether the target grade is the right one.

The second is a ceiling that cannot move. If an IGCSE candidate is entered for Core tier and the entry deadline has passed, the maximum grade is fixed regardless of how well the teaching goes, and buying sessions aimed at a higher grade is buying a disappointment. The useful work becomes securing the ceiling comfortably and planning the next step, which is a different and entirely legitimate purchase.

The third is capacity. A Diploma candidate carrying six subjects, internal assessment deadlines and the core, or a Year 11 candidate with ten subjects, has a finite number of usable evening hours. Adding a third or fourth tutoring hour a week past that point degrades everything, including sleep. The right move is to cut the number of subjects supported rather than to extend the week, and to pick the subject where the marks are closest to moving.
bullets: No movement across three scripts with good engagement means change, not more

sections.heading: The home-tutor question answered honestly, for a two-child household
paragraphs: Searching for a home tutor is a reasonable thing to do and this page should answer it rather than deflect it. In-home one-to-one tutoring is widely available in central Sharjah, published UAE rates sit around AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel absorbed, and monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits have been advertised in this market. For a single child in a widely taught subject in a central district, it works.

For a household with children in two curricula, the arithmetic changes, and the table sets out why. You now need two specialists rather than one, both free on the same evening, both willing to reach your district. In Al Azra or Sharjah Garden City that combination frequently does not exist at any price, and the usual compromise is one generalist covering both children, which means one child is being taught by someone improvising.

The comparison is not about enthusiasm for video. It is about which arrangement produces the artefacts this page has argued are the whole point. Annotated work on a screen is saved and reopenable, so a counted comparison across three scripts is trivial. Paper carried out of the house in a tutor's bag is not, and the household that wants to audit progress across two children ends up unable to.

The honest closing note on cost: IB Gram publishes no fixed per-hour figure here because the truthful number depends on subject, level and weekly load, and for a two-child arrangement it depends on both. What is fixed is that the first lesson is free and takes no card details, for each child separately. Judge the teaching and the written note before any money moves, and treat the published market figures above as the yardstick for whatever quote you receive.

sections.heading: Starting: what to send, and what comes back
paragraphs: Send three things per child and the first session becomes diagnostic instead of introductory. For the IGCSE candidate: the statement of entry naming board, code and tier, the most recent marked script, and the school's mock and entry dates. For the Diploma candidate: the subjects and levels, the most recent piece of marked or commented work, and the coordinator's internal deadlines for the core components.

What comes back from the free first lesson is a short written note per child: what the tutor saw, what they think the primary problem is, and what they would change first. That note is the thing to judge, and the two notes together will tell you whether you are dealing with one person stretching across two systems or two people who each know theirs. A vague note is informative, and it is informative early.

From there the pattern is weekly, with an artefact after each session and a deliberate review at four. The review question is narrow: what exists now that did not exist a month ago, and does it support a decision. If the answer is thin for one child and solid for the other, change the thin one. Running two arrangements means you get a built-in comparison, which is an advantage worth using.

The last thing, said plainly because no competing page in this market says it. Some combinations are thin, particularly unusual Higher Level subjects and IGCSE codes like Additional Mathematics 0606 or Accounting 0452 in exam term. Where no specialist is free, IB Gram will tell you with a realistic date rather than substituting a generalist. For a household already running two calendars, a quietly mismatched tutor costs more than the lessons did.

faqs.question: We have one child in Year 11 IGCSE and one in DP1. Can one arrangement cover both?
faqs.answer: One account and one evening, yes; one tutor, usually not. The two systems reward different things. An IGCSE grade is decided almost entirely on externally marked papers, so the work is paper craft and habit correction. A DP1 year is dominated by internally assessed components, so the work is research questions, methods, criteria and feedback on drafts. A tutor strong in one is typically improvising in the other, and because the hourly rate is the same either way, splitting the two costs nothing extra. The practical arrangement most Sharjah households settle on is two consecutive slots on a single evening with a specialist each.

faqs.question: How do I compare an IGCSE grade 6 with an IB subject grade of 5?
faqs.answer: You do not, and resisting the urge is genuinely useful. The two are produced by different assessment systems with different components, different weightings and different purposes, and no honest conversion exists. Households build one anyway because two numbers on the fridge invite comparison, and the usual result is a decision that one child is behind on the basis of arithmetic that means nothing. Read each child on their own scale against their own evidence: a marked script with mark allocations visible for the IGCSE candidate, a criterion-referenced draft for the Diploma candidate. Both are checkable. Neither is translatable into the other.

faqs.question: What should exist on paper after four tutoring sessions?
faqs.answer: For an IGCSE candidate: a marked question set, a named primary problem, a fix-list of habits ordered by how many marks each costs, and a second comparable script. For a Diploma candidate in the first year: a reading of existing work, a narrowed research question that can actually be answered, a method the student can defend in their own words, and feedback referenced to criterion letters. What does not count is a verbal summary, a topic list, or an unmarked photograph of working. The test is whether a stranger reading the artefact could tell what the problem is and whether anything has changed.

faqs.question: What exactly may a tutor do with an IB internal assessment draft?
faqs.answer: Teach the skills the component assesses, explain the criteria, ask questions that sharpen the student's thinking, and give feedback on work the student has already produced. What a tutor must never do is write any portion of an assessed piece, supply text to be inserted, rewrite a paragraph into its finished form, or generate the data, method or argument. Candidates sign an authenticity declaration, and a school moderator is trained to notice a change of voice between drafts. One operator in this market sells finished Internal Assessments outright; the student, not the seller, carries the malpractice consequence of using one.

faqs.question: How many drafts of internally assessed work is a student allowed to have reviewed?
faqs.answer: The school's coordinator sets that policy, not a tutoring provider, and it varies by component and by campus. Ask for it in writing during the first term of DP1 along with the internal deadlines, which arrive earlier than most families expect and differ between Sharjah schools by several weeks. What matters more than the number is the nature of the feedback: comments phrased as questions and criterion references support the authenticity declaration, while replacement sentences undermine it. Keep the student's own successive drafts and dated session notes, because that trail is what demonstrates a legitimate process if anyone ever asks.

faqs.question: My son's predicted grades look better than his mock marks. Which should I believe?
faqs.answer: Read the document the prediction was formed from. A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by the school for university applications, built from classwork and mock performance, and it is not a measurement of current attainment. A prediction two grades above the mock is a statement about trajectory, which is worth interrogating gently rather than either trusting or dismissing. Ask what it was based on and look at that script. Teachers see a student for five hours a week across two years and are usually closer to right than a tutor with four papers, but the prediction is an input to a decision rather than the decision itself.

faqs.question: We asked for a home tutor in Sharjah. Why is the lesson on video?
faqs.answer: Because that is what IB Gram actually delivers in the UAE, and saying so before a deposit is better than afterwards. Home visits are an India-only service. The reason the format is video rather than cost is pool size: a two-curriculum household needs two specialists free on the same evening within reach of your district, and in the inland Sharjah districts that combination frequently does not exist at any price. The usual local compromise is one generalist across both children. If a tutor in the room is genuinely what you want, hire locally and use the permit and evidence checks on this page, which work on anyone.

faqs.question: How does mock season differ between an IGCSE and a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: For the IGCSE candidate, mocks are a dress rehearsal for almost the whole grade, so the script is the most informative document of the year. Count the lost marks by cause: unshown method, misread command term, content genuinely missing, time. Only one of those four is answered by more revision. For the Diploma candidate, mocks test the external components while internal ones are still in progress, so the picture is partial by design. It is still the main evidence a predicted grade will be formed from, and weak external performance there sometimes reflects time spent on coursework rather than understanding.

faqs.question: What is the real gap between Extended IGCSE maths and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Substantial, and mostly about calculus and abstraction. Cambridge 0580 Extended is a thorough course that does not include calculus, while Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes confident algebraic manipulation and a willingness to work on unfamiliar problems and proof-style reasoning. Students frequently describe the first term as a different subject. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 exists precisely as the bridge, which is why students aiming at Higher Level are often advised to sit it alongside 0580 where the school offers it. Where that was not possible, plan on a sustained block of foundation work rather than a few catch-up sessions.

faqs.question: How many weeks of support does the Year 11 to DP1 jump usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on where the student finishes Year 11, which is why the planning table on this page gives ranges rather than figures. A comfortable Extended grade moving into Standard Level typically needs the shorter end, roughly six to ten weeks in mathematics. A borderline Extended grade moving into Higher Level mathematics or Chemistry needs considerably more, and in one or two cases the right conversation is about whether Higher Level is the correct choice at all. That conversation is far cheaper in June than in the October of DP1, when the timetable is already set and the first deadlines are visible.

faqs.question: Can two children share one tutoring slot to save money?
faqs.answer: For two children in the same subject, at the same level, with the same board and similar attainment, occasionally. In practice those conditions almost never hold, and in a two-curriculum household they cannot. A shared hour becomes teaching to the middle, which is exactly the failure mode that makes group classes poor at diagnosis: the specific habit costing one child four marks a paper never gets isolated. If budget is the constraint, the better economy is supporting one child properly this term and the other next term, chosen from the marked evidence rather than from whose exams feel closer.

faqs.question: What should I bring to a Sharjah parents' evening if we have tutoring evidence?
faqs.answer: Two marked scripts six weeks apart and the written fix-list between them. That changes the conversation from an exchange of impressions into a discussion about a pattern, and teachers generally respond well to it because it is the kind of evidence they work from themselves. Ask three questions: whether the pattern you are seeing matches what they see in class, whether the tier or level is right, and what the internal deadlines are for the next term. Avoid presenting the tutor's view as a counterweight to the teacher's; the point is to compare two readings of the same student.

faqs.question: Which signals tell us the tutoring has done what it can?
faqs.answer: Three situations. First, no movement with good engagement: if three marked scripts across half a term show the same habit costing the same marks while the student is turning up and working, more hours of the same will not help and the plan or the match needs to change. Second, a fixed ceiling: once an IGCSE entry deadline has passed, a Core-tier maximum will not move, and the work should be aimed at securing it. Third, capacity: past a certain weekly load, additional hours degrade sleep and everything downstream of it. Support fewer subjects properly instead of more thinly.

faqs.question: Who signs to say the coursework is my child's own work?
faqs.answer: The candidate does, and in most cases the supervising teacher countersigns that the work is authentic as far as they can judge. That declaration is the reason the boundary around tutoring matters so much: a tutor's contribution has to be the kind that leaves the work recognisably the student's. Dated session notes, the student's own successive drafts, and feedback phrased as criterion-referenced questions all support the declaration. Replacement text does not. If you ever compare an early draft with a submitted version and the voice has changed, that is the signal a moderator looks for too.

faqs.question: Should the tutor contact the school directly, or should I pass things on?
faqs.answer: You should, in almost every case. The school's relationship is with the family, and a tutor approaching a teacher or a Diploma coordinator unannounced tends to produce caution rather than cooperation. What works is the parent carrying documents in both directions: the school's internal deadlines and mock windows to the tutor, and the tutor's fix-list and marked comparison to the parents' evening. If a direct conversation would genuinely help, ask the school first and arrange it through them. The exception is nothing at all to do with tutoring: the coordinator's draft policy and deadlines should always come from the school in writing.

sharjah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Collect the artefacts, then book two free lessons
sharjah/ib-igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: A two-curriculum household has an advantage most families do not: a built-in comparison. Run both arrangements on evidence and you will see quickly which one is working. Send each child's documents separately, put both school calendars on one sheet, and book a free first lesson for each. No card details are taken either time, and each ends in a short written note on what the tutor saw and what they would change first. Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, usually as two consecutive slots on a single protected evening.

intro.heading: Proximity is the one thing you cannot verify
paragraphs: A proximity search gives you a map, a few directory listings and a distance in kilometres. None of those tells you whether the person at the other end has marked a Cambridge 0580 Paper 4 this term, or whether they can tell a Pearson 4MA1 Higher question stem from its Cambridge equivalent. Distance is easy to publish and almost impossible to use. What a Sharjah parent actually needs is evidence: the student's own marked script, the published mark scheme sitting beside it, and a sentence explaining which mark moved and why it moved.

Sharjah's school geography makes the map less useful still. Families in Al Nahda and Al Majaz often drive children across the border to schools in Al Qusais and Mirdif, then come home into the evening peak. Families in Muwaileh and University City sit minutes from the airport-road school cluster, but their board options are split between Cambridge and Pearson. Inland and on the east coast, in Al Dhaid, Kalba and Khor Fakkan, the local pool of IGCSE subject specialists is thin to non-existent. A twenty-minute radius means something different in each of those places.

So here is the delivery model stated plainly, before anything else on this page. Tuition for UAE families runs one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared whiteboard and a scanned script on screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE, because a tutor travelling to an address is a service that exists only in India. That is not a workaround dressed up as a feature. It is the thing that lets a family in Al Dhaid book the same 0620 Chemistry specialist a family in Al Zahia books.

The evidence model is the part worth reading twice. Every session produces three artefacts: the student's own attempt at a timed question, that attempt marked against the published scheme with the mark for each part written in, and a two-line instruction for the week. After four weeks you can lay the scripts side by side and see whether the same command word keeps costing marks. After twelve weeks you can see whether a forecast grade is defensible. Nothing in that file depends on trusting a tutor's self-description, and none of it is a satisfaction score.

Boards matter more than most Sharjah parents are told. A school can enter one cohort for Cambridge IGCSE and another for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE in the same subject, and the two sit different numbers of papers, report on different grade scales and tier differently. Tuition that ignores which of those your child is entered for produces practice on the wrong paper. The first thing a trial lesson establishes is the syllabus code on the entry, not the general topic, so ask your school's exams officer for it before you book anybody.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Sharjah schools run Cambridge, Pearson, IB and Indian curricula within a few kilometres of each other, and a single family often spans two of them. These are the four programme stages this page covers, with what each actually assesses and what each does to a Sharjah evening timetable.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, usually eight to ten subjects, examined externally at the end. Cambridge reports international IGCSE grades as A*-G and tiers maths and the sciences into Core and Extended. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on the 9-1 scale and tiers maths into Foundation and Higher. These grades set A-Level and Diploma entry, and on the British track they are the five grades counted for certificate equivalency.
programmes.countryNote: In Sharjah the entry decision belongs to the school rather than the family, and it is often split: the same year group can sit Cambridge 0580 maths and Pearson 4PH1 physics. Ask the exams officer for the code on each entry. The Sharjah Private Education Authority approves curricula and assessment methods for private schools in the emirate, so a mid-year board change is a school-level process, not a parent's choice.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked by the school and moderated by the IB. The jump from IGCSE is less about content than about command terms: evaluate and to what extent replace state and describe, and marks follow the reasoning rather than the final answer.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah has only a small number of IB World Schools, so many families on the Diploma route commute into Dubai or Ajman for school. That commute is why an IB Diploma Programme tutor in Sharjah is usually booked at 18:00 or later, and why a DP1 student who takes a 17:00 slot in September has normally given it up by half term. The weekend morning block is the more durable choice.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria scored 1-8 rather than as a percentage, then converted to a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. Parents arriving from an Indian or British system often read a 5 as a near-failure; it is not. The Personal Project in the final year is the first piece of long-form independent work most students meet.
programmes.countryNote: MYP families in Sharjah usually hear how the 1-8 scale works once, at a parents' evening, and never see a worked conversion. Putting the criterion descriptors next to your child's own submitted task is the quickest way to make a report readable, and it is the earliest warning you will get before a Year 11 board entry and tier are fixed.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before an IGCSE entry, ending in optional Checkpoint tests in English, maths and science. Cambridge runs Checkpoint in March, May and October, which makes it the only externally marked snapshot most students get before Year 10. The results are diagnostic rather than certificated, and they are the cheapest hour of real information a Year 9 parent can get.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah schools treat Checkpoint very differently: some enter whole cohorts, some skip it entirely. If your child's school enters them, the October window gives you a board-marked baseline a full year before the IGCSE Core and Extended tier decision is made. If it does not, a past Checkpoint paper marked inside a session does the same job at the same point in the year.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: The codes matter. A tutor who has marked Cambridge 0620 Paper 4 knows where the six-mark organic questions give marks away; a tutor who knows only IGCSE chemistry does not. Each entry below names the Cambridge and Pearson codes and what the paper actually rewards.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Extended 0580 is examined by a non-calculator Paper 2 and a calculator Paper 4; Core sits Papers 1 and 3. Most lost marks are method marks in multi-step questions where no working was written down, and exact-form answers surrendered to a rounded decimal.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 Extended by students heading for Analysis and Approaches. Calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities arrive a year early, and the usual failure is treating it as harder 0580 rather than as a different habit of proof and presentation.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Cambridge Extended candidates sit a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and either the practical test or the alternative to practical. Electricity, moments and ray diagrams carry the most recoverable marks, usually lost on units and on describing a method rather than naming apparatus.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis and the qualitative-analysis tables are where marks move fastest. The longer organic and industrial questions reward a named condition and a balanced equation; a general description of the process scores close to nothing.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: A content-heavy syllabus where marks go to imprecise language: the water goes in, instead of osmosis down a water-potential gradient. Data questions on enzyme and transpiration experiments need a trend, a figure quoted from the graph, and a reason.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences (Cambridge 0654 / 0653)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into two awards or one. The content cut is not uniform, so a tutor working from the full 0620 or 0625 syllabus wastes a student's hours on material they will never be asked about. The syllabus document is the only reliable map.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response reward audience and form before vocabulary. Most lost marks sit in reading: a summary that paraphrases the passage instead of selecting the points the question actually asked for.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A different syllabus from First Language English with a different mark scheme, often confused in Sharjah because the same department teaches both. Exercise-by-exercise timing is the usual fix; candidates overwrite the short tasks and run out of minutes for the longer ones.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455 / Pearson 4EC1)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is most of the game: axes labelled, the right curve shifted, the new equilibrium marked. Four-mark explain questions want a chain of reasoning, and the longer evaluations want a judgement that follows from what was actually written.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450 / Pearson 4BS1)
subjects.description: Application to the case-study business separates candidates. Generic answers about motivation or cash flow lose the application and evaluation marks even when the underlying theory is correct and well expressed.

subjects.name: Arabic (Cambridge 0508 and 0544)
subjects.levels: First language and foreign language routes
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic alongside their licensed curriculum, and the first-language and foreign-language routes are genuinely different qualifications. Families moving between emirates sometimes discover mid-year that a child has been placed in the wrong stream.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers data representation and networks; Paper 2 covers algorithms and pseudocode. Students who code fluently in Python still lose marks writing pseudocode in the syllabus's own notation, which is the first thing worth drilling.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (IB DP)
subjects.description: The usual destination for a strong 0580 Extended or 0606 candidate. Paper 3 at Higher Level is an extended investigation worth a fifth of the grade, and it rewards a student who can carry a proof through rather than one who recalls results.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IB DP)
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a single scientific investigation marked on the published criteria. Students arriving from 0620 underestimate how much of the mark sits in evaluating method and uncertainty rather than in getting a clean result.

sections.heading: What a proximity search returns, and what it cannot verify
paragraphs: Type the phrase into Google from a Sharjah address and you get a map pack, a handful of directory listings, and agency pages telling you a tutor is eleven kilometres away. That distance is the only genuinely verified fact on the screen. The board, the syllabus code, the tier, the permit and the marking record are all self-reported. Of the pages ranking for queries like this one, three in six publish no price at all, and the one competitor rate panel found in the research was close to two years out of date.

The checkable facts sit elsewhere. A tutor's right to give private lessons in the UAE is a permit question, answered by MoHRE. A school's curriculum and assessment methods are approved by the Sharjah Private Education Authority within this emirate. The grade scales and paper structures are published by Cambridge International and by Pearson. Every one of those can be read from a primary source in a few minutes, and not one of them appears anywhere on a map.

That turns the search into a shorter list of questions. Which board and which code is my child entered for? Has this tutor marked that paper to that scheme this year? What arrives after each session, and when? What happens if nothing has moved in six weeks? A tutor who answers those four in specifics is a better bet than one eleven kilometres away who answers none of them, and the four questions take about ten minutes to ask.
bullets: Distance is verified; board specialism, permit status and marking record are not

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: one subject, two different papers
paragraphs: Sharjah schools are split between Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel, and some are split within themselves by subject. The two are not interchangeable. Cambridge reports international IGCSE results as A*-G and tiers maths and the sciences into Core and Extended. Pearson's International GCSE reports on the 9-1 scale and tiers maths into Foundation and Higher. A student practising the wrong paper is practising a different examination with a different mark scheme, and the hours spent doing it do not transfer cleanly.

The practical differences compound. Cambridge Extended sciences sit a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper, and either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, so laboratory technique is examined directly. Pearson's International GCSE sciences are assessed through written papers, which changes what preparation looks like in the final eight weeks. Pearson also offers modular assessment in some subjects, letting a candidate bank a unit, while a Cambridge entry is linear within its series. Those choices change how a revision plan is sequenced, not just what is revised.

The table below is the version worth taking to your school's exams officer. The codes in it are the ones printed on an entry confirmation, and they are what any tutor should be asked about by name. The useful question is not whether somebody teaches IGCSE physics. It is whether they have marked 4PH1 Paper 1P or 0625 Paper 4 within the current academic year, and what the last candidate they marked lost marks on.
