sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks are actually lost, paper by paper
paragraphs: In maths the losses are structural rather than mysterious. On 0580 Paper 2, the non-calculator Extended paper, candidates who can do the arithmetic lose method marks by not writing the middle line, then lose accuracy marks by rounding an answer the question wanted in exact form. Multi-step questions are where a grade is won: four marks for a correct chain, one mark for a correct answer with no visible chain. A marked script shows this immediately, and the fix is a habit rather than a topic.

In the sciences the losses are linguistic. State wants a bare fact and nothing more. Describe wants what happens, in order. Explain wants a because. Suggest wants an application of principle to an unfamiliar context, and it is the command word Sharjah candidates most often answer with recall. Units and significant figures take the rest, and in practical questions the marks go to naming a variable and describing how it is controlled, not to listing apparatus. Each of these is diagnosable from one marked paper.

In English, economics and business studies the losses live in the question stem. A summary task that paraphrases a passage rather than selecting the points asked for scores low however well it is written. An eight-mark evaluation that lists arguments without reaching a judgement caps itself. A business answer that never names the case-study firm loses the application marks. None of this is about ability, and all of it is visible in the first marked paper, which is why the first session is a timed question rather than a lesson.
bullets: Method marks lost to missing working on multi-step maths questions
Exact-form answers surrendered to a rounded decimal on non-calculator papers
Suggest questions answered with recall instead of applied principle
Summaries that paraphrase the passage instead of selecting the required points

sections.heading: Counting backwards from a Cambridge series
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Those are the only two sittings open to a candidate at a Sharjah centre: the February and March series is run for India, and a timetable built on it describes somebody else's school year. Counted backwards from June, the real deadlines sit a long way ahead of the papers. Final entries close in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, on a date the centre prints on the statement of entry. Forecast grades follow weeks before the papers. Results reach Cambridge Direct in August, and certificates arrive at the centre after that. The November series repeats the same pattern half a year round and is the route a retake takes.

Two administrative details catch families out. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the exams officer must use the timetable version for that zone; Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination because the wrong version was used. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and in November, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Read backwards, those dates set the plan. Entry closes months before the paper, so a tier or subject change is a November conversation, not a January one. Forecast grades fall due a week before the exams, which is why marked papers from the preceding block matter so much. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always open the live official PDF rather than trusting a restated date. For IB sessions this page gives no dates at all: confirm them with your school's IB coordinator and with ibo.org.

sections.heading: The evidence file: what twelve weeks of marked work should show
paragraphs: A tutoring arrangement should produce a paper trail that a parent can read without being in the room. The unit of that trail is not a progress report. It is the student's own script, marked part by part against the published scheme, with the mark for each part written in and a short note where a mark was withheld. Three of those, four weeks apart, tell you more than a term of reassurance, because they let you compare like with like instead of comparing impressions.

What the file should let you see is movement in a specific place. If week two shows four marks lost to missing method and week six shows one, the habit is changing. If both show the same pattern, the plan is wrong and more hours will not fix it. That is the honest and uncomfortable part: a review at six weeks sometimes concludes that the subject, the tier or the tutor needs to change. Saying so early is cheaper for a family than discovering it after a forecast grade is submitted.

What the file should not contain is a satisfaction score, a star rating or a percentage improvement figure with no method behind it. Numbers of that kind are everywhere in this market and they are unverifiable by design. The research behind these pages found competitors publishing two different review averages on one page and a self-asserted rating in schema that did not match the visible figure. A marked script cannot be manufactured in the same way, which is exactly why it is the thing worth asking for.

sections.heading: Drafts, feedback and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Every assessed piece a student submits has to be the student's own. That applies to an IGCSE coursework component, to an IB internal assessment, to the Extended Essay and to the Personal Project. A tutor may read a draft, name the criterion a section fails to meet, ask the questions that expose a missing step, and teach the skill that closes it. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure the argument, or hand back a version the student did not produce. That boundary is not a matter of taste.

In practice a legitimate session looks slower than families expect. The criterion descriptors are read aloud. The student is asked which descriptor their paragraph currently meets, and why. The tutor points at the gap rather than filling it, and the student rewrites between sessions. What that leaves behind is a dated trail: the student's draft, the comments on it, and the student's own revision. If a family is ever asked by a school to show how support was given, that trail is the answer, and it is also the only version a board will accept.

The reason to be explicit about this is that the market is not. The competitor research behind these pages found a site selling completed internal assessments at a fixed price. A student who submits bought work faces a malpractice finding, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on the seller. No IB Gram tutor supplies assessed work, and none distributes past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents as downloads; those are published by the boards and should be read from the boards' own sites.

sections.heading: SPEA licenses the school, MoHRE licenses the tutor
paragraphs: The regulator map is simple once you see it written down, and almost nobody in this market writes it down. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in this emirate, and in Sharjah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Individual tutoring is a federal matter rather than an emirate one. Private tuition runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The MoHRE service is listed as private tutor licensing, shows no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and is applied for through the ministry's smart app, website and e-services system.

Two cautions follow from that. Individuals giving private lessons without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published, so any figure you see quoted should be treated as unverified. And a tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal again, needing an educational-services permit from the relevant emirate authority. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and claims none; a page that advertises tutors as approved by KHDA or by SPEA is making a claim you should ask it to evidence.

sections.heading: Five IGCSE grades, and what the Ministry actually counts
paragraphs: Certificate equivalency is the gap in this market that costs families the most and gets written about the least. On the British track, a student must show proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, together with either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

The American track is built differently, on test thresholds rather than subject counts. English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. The sourced reporting on these rules names no EmSAT requirement and states no IB points threshold, so MoE equivalency for IGCSE students is covered here while no IB figure is published on this page at all.

Three practical consequences. Subject choice in Year 10 is also an equivalency decision, because the five counted subjects exclude two of the ones a UAE school requires anyway. A page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects, which is one more than the sourced rule, so check the authority rather than the agency. And nobody should tell you that tutoring is required for equivalency: the process belongs to the Ministry and the emirate attestation channel, IB Gram does not perform it, and it is not something a tutor can accelerate.

If you do not have the code, the exams officer does, and a screenshot of the entry is enough. That one piece of information decides which specialist is the right match.

The tutor sets a timed question from the live syllabus, marks it on screen against the published scheme, and sends a written diagnostic afterwards. process.description: Choose a weekly time that survives the school run rather than the one that looks tidy on paper. Then agree what will be marked in each of the first six weeks. The plan names papers and question types rather than topics in syllabus order, so progress is measured against something specific and checkable.

process.title: Review at six weeks on the marked file
process.description: Lay the scripts side by side and read the mark breakdown rather than the commentary. If the same command word is still costing marks, the plan changes: a different question type, a different pace, or a different tutor. Changing tutor costs nothing and is a normal outcome rather than a complaint.

whyPoints.description: Work comes back with the part marks written in and the scheme's own wording beside them. That makes a disagreement about a grade an argument about a specific mark, which is a conversation worth having, rather than an argument about effort, which is not.

whyPoints.description: Matching starts from the syllabus code on the entry, because 0625 and 4PH1 are different examinations. A tutor is proposed for the paper your child actually sits, and if the specialist for that paper is not free, we say so instead of substituting quietly.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam board is my child's Sharjah school actually entering them for?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the entry confirmation rather than asking the department. It carries a syllabus code: four digits for Cambridge, such as 0580 for maths or 0620 for chemistry, and a code like 4MA1 or 4CH1 for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. Schools in Sharjah sometimes split boards by subject, so one child can sit Cambridge maths and Pearson physics in the same series. The code also tells you the tier, which sets the grade ceiling. Bring that code to any tutor you are considering and ask whether they have marked that specific paper this academic year.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is sitting Core or Extended IGCSE maths?
faqs.answer: It is printed on the entry, and the school usually decides it during Year 10 on the strength of internal assessment. Cambridge 0580 Core is examined by Papers 1 and 3 and caps the grade available; Extended sits Papers 2 and 4 and reaches the top grades. Pearson's equivalent split on 4MA1 is Foundation and Higher. The tier matters more than almost anything else a parent can influence, because a student placed on Core cannot reach a grade the Diploma or A-Level route may later require. If the tier looks wrong, ask for the evidence behind it and when it can be reviewed.

faqs.question: What does a marked past paper show that a school report does not?
faqs.answer: A report gives you a letter or a number and a sentence of comment. A marked past paper gives you the part marks: which step in a four-mark method was credited, which command word was answered with the wrong kind of sentence, which units went missing. Two students on the same reported grade usually lose their marks in completely different places, and only one of those problems is solved by more content revision. The script also carries timing evidence, because you can see how far through the paper the handwriting changes, and that is often the real cause.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start in December for a February exam series?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to change shape. With eight weeks or fewer, teaching new content rarely pays for itself, while marking whole papers almost always does. A pre-series block marks complete past papers to the published scheme and reports marks by question type, which usually reveals that one paper rather than the whole subject is holding the grade down. That becomes the revision order for the remaining weeks. What a short block cannot do is undo two years of gaps, and anybody suggesting otherwise should be asked how.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor handle both Cambridge and Pearson papers in one subject?
faqs.answer: Some can, and it is a fair question to put directly. The content overlaps heavily, but the papers, the mark schemes and the grade scales do not, and the modular option Pearson offers in some subjects changes how a year is sequenced. What matters is recent marking experience on the exact code your child is entered for. If a tutor has marked 0625 Paper 4 all term but has not seen 4PH1 Paper 1P, the honest answer is to say so and hand the match to the other specialist.

faqs.question: How many whole papers should my child have sat before the final series?
faqs.answer: There is no single correct number, but a useful floor is two complete papers per subject under timed conditions before the mocks, and three or four more inside the pre-series block. Volume is not the point. The point is that each paper is marked part by part and compared against the one before it, so that genuine movement can be separated from normal variation between papers. One paper tells you very little; four marked papers across eight weeks tell you whether a plan is working.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 in Sharjah and heading for the IB Diploma. What should we fix first?
faqs.answer: Command terms and written method, well before content. An IGCSE answer that states a correct result often scores full marks, while a Diploma answer that states a correct result without reasoning frequently does not. Students arriving in DP1 from 0580 Extended also meet Paper 3 at Higher Level, an extended investigation where marks follow a sustained argument rather than a recalled result. Spending the Year 11 summer on how an answer is constructed, using the IB's own command terms, is worth more than pre-reading the first topic of the new course.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals handled if the tutoring is on video?
faqs.answer: The practical assessment belongs to the school and the board, not to a tutor. Cambridge Extended candidates sit either a practical test paper or an alternative-to-practical paper, and both examine the same skills: describing a method precisely, identifying and controlling variables, reading a scale, and spotting a source of error. Those are written skills, and they are coachable on screen with the student's own lab notes and past questions open in front of you both. Handling apparatus cannot be replicated remotely, and that part remains the school's job.

faqs.question: What grades does the Ministry of Education count for secondary certificate equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no lower than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five. The American track works differently, on SAT and English-test thresholds. No IB points figure appears here because the sourced reporting gives none, so check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation channel before relying on a number from anywhere else.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education count towards the five subjects the Ministry requires?
faqs.answer: They do not. The equivalency rule reported for the British track excludes Arabic and Islamic education from the five accredited subjects a student must show. That does not make them optional at school: private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, and in Dubai the authority calculates instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit and requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. The two rules answer different questions, one about school compliance and one about certificate recognition.

faqs.question: How do I check that a private tutor in the UAE actually holds a permit?
faqs.answer: Ask, and expect a specific answer rather than a reassurance. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. The ministry's own service page states a two-working-day completion time and lists no fee. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do with a coursework draft, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor may read a draft, name the criterion a section fails to meet, ask the questions that expose a missing step, and teach the skill that closes it. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure the argument, or return a version the student did not produce. The boundary is not a style preference: boards treat work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student. Anything you receive should leave a dated trail showing the student's own revisions between sessions.

faqs.question: We commute from Al Rahmaniya into Dubai for school. What time should a session start?
faqs.answer: Later than most families first book. A Sharjah to Dubai school run in the afternoon peak routinely swallows an hour, and a 17:00 slot chosen in September is usually abandoned by half term. Families on the Dubai side of the emirate tend to settle at 18:00 or 18:30 on weekday evenings and move the heavier marked-paper work to a weekend morning block. Ninety minutes is the sensible ceiling for a single subject, because a tired student at 19:30 produces marks that tell you nothing useful.

faqs.question: Does SPEA regulate tutoring companies as well as Sharjah schools?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and in Sharjah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods for private schools. Individual private tutoring sits elsewhere, as a federal MoHRE permit matter. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a third thing again, needing an educational-services permit from the relevant emirate authority. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation of any kind and does not claim one; what it can show you is marked work and a tutor's permit status.

faqs.question: What should the first written diagnostic actually contain?
faqs.answer: Three things, in specific language. The topic gaps, named by syllabus section rather than as algebra or organic chemistry. The command words the student answered with the wrong kind of sentence, quoted from their own script. And a first six-week plan naming papers and question types rather than topics in syllabus order. If a diagnostic reads mainly as a description of your child's attitude and potential, it is a sales document rather than an assessment, and you should ask to see the marked script behind it.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the syllabus code. Get it from your school's exams officer, then book a free trial lesson and watch somebody mark a timed question from that exact paper against the published scheme. An hour later you will have a written diagnostic naming the topic gaps and the command words costing marks, and you will know whether online IGCSE tuition in Sharjah is answering a real problem or a vague worry. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and the decision to continue sits with you after you have read the evidence rather than before.

intro.heading: The hourly rate is the smallest part of the question
paragraphs: Two providers quote AED 220 an hour. One of them marks a piece of your child's work between every session, bills only for sessions taken, replaces a tutor free if the match fails, and holds its rate through the spring. The other marks nothing, bills a flat monthly figure regardless of how many sessions a month contains, charges for a rescheduled session, and raises its rate in January. Over a two-year IGCSE course those two arrangements differ by thousands of dirhams, and the hourly rate is identical.

That is the whole subject of this page. There are around nine items that reliably sit outside a quoted hourly figure, and families meet them one at a time, on invoices, over months. Each is small. Together they account for more variation in what a household actually pays than the difference between the mid band and the specialist band, which is the comparison everybody focuses on instead.

Nobody in this market publishes them. Three of the six highest-ranking tutoring pages in this cluster publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Sharjah family transacts in. Terms are published by nobody. One competitor's own frequently-asked-questions section asks what a tutor costs and then declines to answer. So a parent comparing quotes is comparing the one number providers are willing to state and none of the ones that move the total.

The published market figures, for context and from the providers named rather than from us: EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. The Bestimate survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialists at AED 200 to 450 or above, with BartyED advertising AED 650. Monthly packages circulate at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

What follows lists each hidden item, says what a reasonable answer sounds like, and gives the short list of things to settle in writing before a first invoice. None of it requires negotiation; it requires asking, and a provider unwilling to answer in an email has told you something before any money has moved.

One note on how to use it. Send the nine questions before asking about the rate rather than after, which inverts the usual order of the conversation. A provider who answers all nine clearly and quotes AED 280 an hour is frequently cheaper across a year than one who answers none and quotes AED 220, and the only way to see that is to have the answers in front of you when the figures arrive. Tuition for Sharjah families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Sharjah, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

sections.heading: Nine items that sit outside the headline rate
paragraphs: A quoted hourly figure covers one thing reliably: a tutor in a session with your child. Everything else is a question, and there are about nine of them. Marking between sessions. How many sessions a month contains. What happens to unused sessions. Rescheduling and lateness. Cancellation notice. Rate changes during the arrangement. Materials and platform access. Replacement if a match fails. And payment, refund and sibling terms.

None of these is exotic and none is unreasonable for a provider to charge for. The problem is that they are rarely stated, so a family comparing two quotes at the same hourly figure is comparing arrangements that may differ by a third in practice. Over a two-year IGCSE course that difference exceeds the gap between the mid band and the specialist band, which is the comparison everybody actually makes.

They are also, unusually for this market, entirely within a family's power to settle. Each one is answerable in a sentence, and a provider unwilling to answer in writing has told you something useful before any money has moved. There is no negotiation involved. The request is simply: before the first invoice, please confirm these nine things in an email.

The sensible order is to ask about them before asking about the rate, which inverts how the conversation usually goes. A provider who answers all nine clearly and quotes AED 280 is frequently cheaper in practice than one who answers none and quotes AED 220. The table below lists each item with what a reasonable answer sounds like, which is the whole of the checklist.

sections.heading: Marking: the single largest omission
paragraphs: Marking is where most of the hidden money lives, and it hides because it is invisible. The work that moves an IGCSE grade is the pupil producing something, somebody marking it against the published scheme, and the pupil re-answering the parts that lost marks. That loop requires marking to happen between sessions. Marking takes time. Time has to be paid for somewhere, and if it is not inside the rate then one of two things happens.

Either it is billed separately, in which case the real hourly cost is higher than quoted and the family discovers this on an invoice. Or it does not happen, in which case the session itself becomes the marking session: the tutor reads the pupil's work live, aloud, for twenty minutes of an hour that was bought for teaching. That second outcome is far more common and it is almost never noticed, because the session looked busy and productive.

The test is straightforward. Ask: between sessions, who marks my child's work, against what, and is that inside the rate? A good answer names a quantity - one piece a week, or a full past paper a fortnight - and says it is included. A vague answer about reviewing work together in the session is a description of the second outcome, and it means the teaching hour is partly a marking hour at a teaching price.

This bites hardest in the subjects with the highest markable volume. English is the clearest case, because the method is write, mark, rewrite and there is nothing else. Mathematics in a serious arrangement generates a timed paper a fortnight. The sciences generate written practical methods weekly. Biology generates least. An English arrangement where marking is billed on top is substantially more expensive than its hourly rate suggests, and the hourly rate is what it was compared on.

sections.heading: Cancellation, rescheduling and the session that started late
paragraphs: Three distinct things get conflated here and they have different costs. Cancellation is ending the arrangement. Rescheduling is moving a session. Lateness is a session that happened but started late. A provider may have a clear policy on one and nothing on the others, and families usually discover which in the week it matters.

Cancellation notice is the most expensive of the three and the least examined. A month's notice on a monthly arrangement means the arrangement can only ever be left at full price: a family that has concluded the work is not landing still pays for four more sessions nobody wants. A week is reasonable. None is better. The question is not whether notice exists but what leaving costs, and it should be in writing before the first invoice.

Rescheduling matters in proportion to how disrupted a household is, and a UAE school calendar guarantees disruption: trips, examination weeks, long weekends, travel, and in some years a Ramadan reshaping of the evening. A policy that charges for a session moved with two days' notice will cost a Sharjah family real money across a year. Ask how much notice is required and what happens with less.

Lateness is the one nobody raises. For an online arrangement it rarely arises, since there is no journey. For an in-home arrangement in Al Nahda or Al Taawun, where peak congestion is among the heaviest in the country and tower parking adds further time, a session that reliably starts twelve minutes late is a charge of a fifth of a lesson every week that no invoice will ever itemise. Over a term that is more than two full sessions.

sections.heading: Exam-season pricing and the January step-up
paragraphs: Demand for IGCSE tutoring across the UAE concentrates between January and April ahead of the June series, and the specialist end of the market responds. The people who can mark an Extended-tier script against the published scheme are finite, and by February they are booked. The practical consequence is that identical teaching costs more in March than it did in September, and is harder to schedule into the slot a household actually has.

That is not a criticism of anyone. It is a supply curve, and it is why the single most effective cost control available to a Sharjah family is to book the spring block in the autumn with the rate agreed in writing. A figure confirmed in October for a block starting in February is worth real money, and it costs nothing to ask for. Very few families do, because in October nothing feels urgent.

There is a second and sharper version of the same problem. A family that starts an arrangement in September at AED 220 an hour and finds in January that the rate has become AED 280 has not been treated badly unless the original figure was presented as fixed. The term to settle is whether the quoted figure holds for an agreed period, and the answer should be in writing. 'Fixed for this block' is a reasonable answer; silence is not.

The same seasonal logic creates an opportunity nobody uses. August is the loosest month in the market and the most useful for a pupil with a known content gap, because a topic can still be taught properly rather than revised around. Four sessions in August frequently achieve more than twelve in February, at a lower rate, with no scheduling difficulty. It is the best-value month of the year and almost nobody books it.

sections.heading: Materials, platforms and what should never be charged for
paragraphs: Some items appear on invoices that should not exist at all. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB own their syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides. Those documents are published on the boards' own sites and the correct behaviour is to link the official page, not to supply files and certainly not to charge for them. A provider selling a folder of mark schemes is selling something that is not theirs to sell.

The same applies to platform or software charges for an online arrangement. Shared-screen teaching requires a video call and a shared document, both of which are ordinary tools. A charge for access to a proprietary portal is a charge for the provider's own convenience, and it is worth asking what it buys that a video call and a shared file do not. Sometimes there is a good answer; often there is not.

Set text editions and revision guides are a different case and a legitimate family cost. A pupil studying Literature needs the edition the school uses, and a biology pupil benefits from a revision guide. Those are bought from a bookshop at a bookshop price. A provider marking them up, or supplying photocopies, has introduced both a cost and a copyright problem that a family does not need.

The most important thing never to pay for is also the clearest. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is a malpractice trigger rather than a service, and the exposure falls on the candidate whose whole qualification is at stake rather than on the provider taking the fee. No price makes written, edited or supplied coursework acceptable, and a provider offering it has answered every other question about their standards.

sections.heading: Replacement: what happens when a match fails
paragraphs: Matches fail, and reasonably often. A pupil and a tutor can both be entirely competent and not work together, and no amount of care at the matching stage eliminates that. What distinguishes arrangements is not whether it happens but what happens next, and this is the term families least often settle in advance and most regret not settling.

The question is simple: if the match is wrong, do we get a different tutor at no additional cost, and how quickly? A good answer is yes, and within a week. A poor answer involves paying again for the same requirement, or being told that the sessions already delivered were satisfactory and the pupil should persevere. The second is sometimes true and it is not the family's judgement to be overridden.

There is a scarcity dimension that matters particularly in Sharjah and in thinner specifications. For mathematics, English and the main sciences, a replacement is usually quick because the pool is deep. For Computer Science 0478 with Cambridge pseudocode conventions, Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a first language or an unusual literature text list, a replacement may genuinely take time, and the honest answer is a disclosed wait rather than a generalist substituted silently.

The related term is what happens when nobody is available at all. Three outcomes are possible and a family should be told which applies before any money moves: the brief is covered and a trial is scheduled within days; it is covered by a specialist working into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE, which is disclosed rather than hidden behind a local-looking telephone number; or it is not currently covered, in which case it is named. No competitor in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

sections.heading: Payment, refunds and tax, in writing
paragraphs: Four things belong in an email before a first invoice and they take a provider two minutes to answer. What payment methods are accepted. Whether payment is in advance or in arrears. What the refund position is on unused prepaid sessions. And whether the quoted AED figure includes VAT, excludes it, or is not subject to it, with a tax registration number if the provider holds one.

On that last point, this page states nothing about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because doing so would require a Federal Tax Authority citation and the position turns on a provider's own registration and the nature of the service. What a family can reasonably require is a plain written statement about the figure it has been quoted. A provider who answers that question in general terms about how tuition usually works has answered a different question.

Refunds on prepaid sessions deserve their own line because prepayment is common. A package bought in advance creates an obligation in one direction and a hope in the other, and a UAE school calendar guarantees disruption. Ask what happens to prepaid sessions if the arrangement ends - refunded, carried, or forfeited - and get the answer before the money moves rather than when you want it back.

There is also a data point worth settling that is not financial. Any form or onboarding process collects personal information about a minor, and a family is entitled to know what is collected, why, and how to have it deleted, with a privacy link available. The UAE has a federal personal data protection law, and a provider collecting a child's school, grades and photograph without a stated purpose is behaving poorly regardless of its rates.

sections.heading: Second subjects, siblings and the discount that is not one
paragraphs: Two situations invite a family to assume a discount that frequently does not exist. The first is a second subject. Adding a subject usually means a second specialist and a second hour, so the cost doubles rather than tapering. Some providers offer a two-subject figure and many do not, and assuming one is how a budget set at AED 1,200 becomes AED 2,400 without a decision having been taken.

The second is siblings. Two children in the same house are two arrangements unless they are genuinely at the same tier in the same subject, in which case a shared session at the small-group rate of roughly AED 100 to 150 per pupil is real value. Where they are at different stages, a shared session addresses the average of two gaps and therefore neither precisely, which is the opposite of what one-to-one rates are for.

The useful alternative for a two-child household is sequencing rather than sharing, and nobody sells it because providers price per child. The younger child usually has no fixed external deadline, so front-loading their work into the autumn and the following summer while the older child's intensive months concentrate into the spring flattens the household peak without reducing what either receives. The expensive collision is a Year 13 and a Year 11 in the same spring.

One further item in this category: the second-subject question interacts with the shared repairs that exist in an IGCSE timetable. A reading-analysis block bought for English also improves History source marks, and a practical-paper block improves all three sciences. Those are the only purchases in this market that cover several subjects for the price of one, and asking whether a provider recognises them is a reasonable test of whether they are selling hours or outcomes.

sections.heading: Permits, claims and the first session
paragraphs: One credential exists for an individual tutor in the UAE and a family is entitled to see it. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the smart app, website or e-services system. Because it costs nothing, a provider citing licensing costs in its rate has misread its own paperwork.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure circulating online should be treated as unverified. Separately, a tutoring business with premises and staff needs an educational services permit from the relevant emirate authority, which an online matching platform does not hold and should not imply.

On claims: no provider in this market publishes outcome data with a sample size, a date and a method, so satisfaction percentages, self-asserted star ratings and claims about the proportion of pupils reaching top grades are marketing figures rather than evidence. A promise of a specific grade is a reason to decline. IB Gram holds no SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or IB approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership and claims none, and has no office or centre in the UAE.

The first session is free, is one session, and requires no card details - and that condition is stated here rather than in small print, because 'free' with an unstated condition is the oldest hidden cost there is. The useful thing to bring is your child's last marked paper. The useful thing to send first is the nine-item list from this page, in an email, and to read the answers before the rate.

intro.heading: What a SAIS family is usually trying to fix
paragraphs: Sharjah American International School teaches an American programme, and most families who look for an IB or IGCSE tutor around it are not unhappy with that. They are planning for something. A sibling has a place at an IB school in Al Majaz. A Year 9 student wants to sit Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics as a private candidate alongside school. A Grade 11 student has accepted a place at a Dubai IB school for the next academic year and will arrive two terms behind on Theory of Knowledge and on the Internal Assessment calendar. The tutoring that helps is not generic revision; it is a specific bridge between two assessment cultures.

Those two cultures measure different things. An American report card rewards accumulated credit: homework submitted, quizzes passed, participation, a GPA that moves in small increments across a semester. A Cambridge IGCSE grade and an IB subject grade are decided almost entirely by terminal written papers marked against a published mark scheme, plus coursework assessed by criterion. A student can hold a strong GPA and still lose a third of the available marks on IGCSE Physics Paper 4, because nobody told them that describe and explain demand different answers and that a correct idea written in the wrong register earns nothing.

This page is built around evidence rather than reassurance. Every session a tutor runs here produces something you can look at: a past-paper question marked with the examiner's mark scheme beside it, a corrected IA draft with the criterion letter and the mark band named, a short list of the exact topics that cost marks this week. Over six weeks that becomes a record of movement rather than an impression of effort. A tutor who cannot show you that after a month is not measuring anything.

Delivery is online. IB Gram does not run home visits in Sharjah, because that is an India-only service, so every lesson described here happens over live video, one to one, with a shared screen and the question on it. For a Sharjah family that is usually the better trade anyway. The in-home pool within a twenty-minute drive of Al Nahda or Muwailih is whoever happens to live there, while an online pool is whoever teaches Cambridge IGCSE 0625 Physics Paper 6 well.

Sharjah's private schools sit under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That matters for a practical reason: a school's assessment calendar is not a free-floating choice, and a tutor needs to work to the school's dates rather than invent a schedule. It also matters for the exam route, because a student sitting Cambridge IGCSE outside their own school's entry sits as a private candidate at an exam centre, and the entry deadline falls months before the paper.

What follows is the full picture: what the papers ask, where the marks actually go, what the Sharjah market charges in AED and why, how the June and November entry windows work backwards from the written paper, and what a tutor is and is not allowed to touch on an Internal Assessment.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-for-sharjah-ameri.programmesIntro: SAIS students arrive at IB and IGCSE work from an American grade structure, so the mapping matters more than the label. The three programmes below are the ones Sharjah families actually move into, with the entry point an American-curriculum student usually joins at and the first piece of evidence a tutor produces.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses eight subject groups against four criteria each, marked zero to eight, with no terminal paper until the optional eAssessment at the end of the fifth year. A student moving from an American middle-school report meets command terms and criterion descriptors for the first time, and the difficulty is usually in the written reflection rather than in the content itself.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah and Dubai IB schools commonly admit MYP students mid-phase, which means a Grade 9 arrival is assessed against criteria the cohort has used for three years. The first evidence a tutor produces here is a single criterion-marked task, so you can see which of the four descriptors is actually costing the grade.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Two boards dominate UAE schools. Cambridge IGCSE uses codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0625 Physics, with Core and Extended tiers and a terminal paper set. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. In both cases the grade is decided by written papers marked to a published scheme rather than by classwork.
programmes.countryNote: For Sharjah families the practical question is the entry route. A student taking a subject their own school does not enter must register as a private candidate at an exam centre, and Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version. Cambridge states that using the wrong zone timetable is the candidate's risk.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment graded against criteria lettered A onwards. Subject grades run one to seven, with up to three further points from TOK and the Extended Essay, to a forty-five point total.
programmes.countryNote: A student arriving from an American Grade 11 into DP1 at a Sharjah or Dubai IB school usually has the subject content but not the IA calendar, which opens in the first term and closes well before the written papers. The first tutoring block is almost always spent narrowing a research question until it is small enough to be assessed.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-for-sharjah-ameri.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects SAIS families ask for by name, with what each assessment actually rewards. Where a Cambridge or Edexcel code applies it is named, because the code decides the paper structure and therefore decides which practice is worth doing at all.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: Extended covers functions, vectors, introductory calculus and harder trigonometry that Core omits. Most lost marks here are method marks: a correct final answer with no working scores less than a wrong answer with visible method. Sessions drill the writing of the method, not only the arithmetic.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: Paper 6, Alternative to Practical, is where a student who has never drawn a results table loses the most. Electricity and magnetism carry the heaviest conceptual load. Practice is built on marked Paper 6 questions, because the skill being tested is recording and interpreting rather than recalling.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations and the mechanics of writing ionic equations separate grades here. Students arriving from an American chemistry course usually know the concepts and have never been asked to include state symbols or to justify a choice of apparatus for two marks.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: Biology is marked on precision of language. The plant grows better earns nothing where the rate of photosynthesis increases because light intensity increases earns the mark. Sessions work directly from mark schemes, so the student learns which words are being counted.

subjects.name: First Language English and English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Two different qualifications that look almost identical on a timetable. First Language English assesses directed writing and reading analysis; ESL assesses comprehension and functional writing. Entering the wrong one costs a grade that has nothing to do with the student's ability.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: AA rewards algebraic fluency and proof. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers and a Paper 3 investigation. Students from an American calculus course often have the technique and no experience of a question that asks them to justify each step in writing.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is modelling, statistics and technology-active work, with a long data investigation in HL Paper 3. The common failure is treating a modelling question as a calculation question and never stating what the model assumes or where it stops being valid.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are where HL separates from SL. The Internal Assessment is a single scientific investigation assessed against criteria, and the mark is more often lost on the evaluation than on the practical work itself.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Assessed by a guided analysis of an unseen text, a comparative essay, and the Individual Oral. Students moving from an American English class have usually written personal-response essays and not timed comparative analysis against a two-hour clock.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Up to three of the forty-five points come from these two components. TOK is assessed on an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title; the Extended Essay is a four thousand word independent piece. A tutor coaches the question and the process and writes no part of either.

sections.heading: What this search usually means at SAIS
paragraphs: Sharjah American International School runs an American programme, so a search for an IB IGCSE tutor for Sharjah American International School students is almost never a complaint about the school. It is a transition question. In most cases one of four things is happening: a place has been accepted at an IB or British school for the next academic year, a student wants a Cambridge IGCSE subject their own timetable does not carry, a sibling is already in an IB school and the household wants one tutoring plan, or a Grade 11 student is looking at universities that read IB and A-Level grades more fluently than a GPA.

Each of those needs different work. A confirmed move into DP1 needs TOK vocabulary, the Internal Assessment calendar and one subject bridged hard, which is usually Maths. A private-candidate IGCSE entry needs the syllabus code, an exam centre and a paper-by-paper plan that starts months before the written exam. A household running two curricula needs scheduling more than it needs content. A university-driven question needs a realistic read of what the target courses actually ask for in grades.

What all four share is that progress has to be visible to a parent who does not teach the subject. That is why this page is organised around evidence: a marked question, a mark-scheme comparison, a dated raw score on a whole paper, a criterion letter set against an IA draft. You should not have to take anyone's word for whether the sessions are working, and after four weeks you should be able to point at the thing that changed.

sections.heading: Two assessment cultures, one transcript
paragraphs: An American high-school transcript and a Cambridge or IB grade are built from different raw material. The transcript accumulates: assignments, quizzes, tests, participation and a semester weighting, producing a GPA that moves gradually and rewards consistency over months. A Cambridge IGCSE grade is decided by terminal written papers marked against a published scheme, with an alternative-to-practical paper or a practical test in the sciences. An IB subject grade combines terminal papers with an Internal Assessment marked by criterion.

The consequence is specific rather than philosophical. A student used to the first system often writes a great deal and claims very little. Mark schemes pay for named points, and a paragraph that circles a correct idea without stating it earns nothing at all. The reverse failure is just as common: a student trained on multiple-choice drills gives a one-line answer to a four-mark explain question and loses three marks they could comfortably have answered for.

The table below sets the three systems beside each other on the points that change how a student should study. It is not a ranking of difficulty. A student can be genuinely strong in one system and unprepared for another, and the gap is almost always technique rather than content knowledge, which is why the first thing a tutor does is take a baseline on a real paper.

That baseline answers a question no report card can. One marked paper sat under timing tells you whether the problem is the physics or the paper, and those two problems need completely different terms of work. If the content is secure and the marks are leaking at the command term, six weeks is often enough. If whole topics are missing, the plan has to be longer and you deserve to be told that before you pay for anything.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go
paragraphs: In Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Mathematics the single largest avoidable loss is unwritten method. The scheme awards method marks for a recognisable route to the answer, so a student who does the algebra mentally and writes one line is throwing away marks they have already earned. The habit is fixable in about three sessions, and it is fixable in a way you can see: the same question, re-marked, with the method visible and the score higher.

In 0625 Physics the loss concentrates in Paper 6. Alternative to Practical asks a student to draw a results table with units in the headings, read an instrument to the correct precision, plot with a sensible scale and then identify a source of error that is actually a source of error rather than a generic mention of human mistake. None of that is physics knowledge. All of it is trained, and a student who has only sat multiple-choice science has usually never been asked for any of it.

In the IB sciences the Internal Assessment is where a strong student most often underperforms. The practical work tends to be fine; the evaluation is thin. A criterion that asks for a discussion of limitations wants named limitations with a stated effect on the result and a specific improvement, not a paragraph saying more trials would help. A tutor marks the draft against the criterion letter, names the band it currently sits in, and explains what would move it. The student then rewrites it themselves.

In the English qualifications the loss is structural. A guided analysis question is not an invitation to summarise the text, and a comparative essay that treats two works in two separate halves has not compared anything. These are answerable patterns, and they respond quickly to marked practice because the student can see the difference between the two versions of their own paragraph.

sections.heading: What IB and IGCSE tutoring costs in Sharjah, cheapest first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because that is where most Sharjah searches start. Budget online tutoring, often a university student working from a textbook, is advertised in the UAE from around AED 45 to AED 65 an hour by EdFlik and from roughly AED 33 to AED 52 by Tutopiya, on their own published pages. That buys supervision and company for homework. It does not usually buy somebody who has marked a 0625 Paper 6 against the scheme.

A qualified subject tutor working online sits higher. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for an IB specialist, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts a specialist at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with a premium named tier reaching AED 650 at BartyED. Those are figures those providers published, not an IB Gram price list; our own rate is quoted after the free trial lesson, with the session length and the marking stated.

In-home one-to-one is the most expensive line, and the reason is travel. Bestimate records AED 180 to AED 350 an hour for a home visit, and independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced in. What that premium buys is a person in the room. What it costs is choice, because the pool shrinks to whoever will drive to Al Nahda at 19:00, which in a niche Higher Level subject can mean nobody at all. IB Gram does not run home visits in Sharjah, as that is an India-only service, and online tutoring spends the same budget on specialism instead of on mileage.

Three things move the number in this emirate specifically. The level matters, because IB Higher Level and Diploma core work costs more than IGCSE Core. Proximity to a written series matters, because demand concentrates in the weeks before June and November. And whether the rate includes marking matters most of all, since marking happens outside the lesson and a rate that excludes it is not comparable with one that includes it.

sections.heading: The entry windows, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Nobody in this market publishes a calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what decides whether tutoring can still help. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in a May/June window and a November window. The February/March series that appears in search results is offered to India only and is not a route for a candidate sitting in the UAE.

The entry deadline is the part families miss. A centre must submit entries months before the paper, and once that date passes the next opportunity is the following series, which for a Cambridge candidate means waiting from June to November or from November to June. Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after working from the wrong zone's timetable. Always open the live official timetable rather than a copy on a tutoring site.

Results arrive later than most parents expect. For Pearson, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those published dates are the honest basis for planning a resit: a November candidate does not know their grade until the middle of the following January, which is after many university and school deadlines.

The table below counts backwards from a written paper so you can see where tutoring sits. The useful read is the row above the exam window rather than the exam window itself, because that is where a plan either exists or does not.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IA, EE or Personal Project
paragraphs: This is the most important paragraph on the page, and it is the one the essay mills in these search results never write. Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, the TOK essay and the MYP Personal Project must be the student's own work. The IB treats submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever was paid. One site competing for this query advertises completed Internal Assessments for a fixed fee. That is not tutoring and it is not a service IB Gram will provide.

Inside that boundary there is a great deal a tutor can legitimately do, and most of it is the part students find hardest. A tutor can read a proposed research question and say why it cannot be assessed as written. A tutor can explain what a criterion descriptor is actually asking for, in plain words, with an example that is not the student's own topic. A tutor can challenge a method, point out that a control variable is not controlled, and ask what the uncertainty in a measurement does to the conclusion.

A tutor can also comment on a draft the student has written: naming the criterion letter, naming the band the draft currently sits in, and describing what the next band up requires. The student then rewrites. The difference between that and a rewriting service is visible in the file history, which is one reason written feedback is better evidence than a verbal call. Your child's school supervisor is also entitled to ask what support was received, and an honest answer should never be a problem.

Where a school has set its own internal deadlines, the tutor works to them rather than to a schedule of our own. A Sharjah IB school typically runs IA drafts through the first Diploma year with a final submission well before the written papers, and planning backwards from the school's date is the only version that helps.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what that changes
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are regulated by emirate, not nationally, and the differences are real. Sharjah's private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai's schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to the Department of Education and Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education.

For a tutoring plan this matters in three ways. First, the school's assessment calendar is approved rather than invented, so a tutor who asks for the school's own dates is asking the right question. Second, mandatory subjects follow the emirate rather than the licensed curriculum: Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies run alongside an IB or IGCSE programme, and in Dubai the KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. Third, the regulator is where a parent can verify that a school exists and what inspection band it holds.

It is worth being precise about what regulation does not mean. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by SPEA, the KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education, and no tutoring platform should imply otherwise. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument issued to a training institute with premises in Dubai; an online one-to-one service with no UAE premises does not hold one and should not suggest it does. Individual private tutors in the UAE are covered by a different instrument, the MoHRE private tuition work permit.

That permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount you see quoted online is unverified.
