sections.heading: What a Sharjah IGCSE student must show for MoE equivalency
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process by which the UAE Ministry of Education recognises a foreign secondary certificate, and it is the step families discover late. For the British track, which is the one an IGCSE candidate is on, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details inside that rule save families money. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, so a student counting them towards the total may be a subject short without knowing it. And the figure is five, not six. One page currently ranking for UAE equivalency queries states that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which would have a family paying for an entry they do not need.

For the American track, which is where a SAIS student starts, the published requirement is different in kind. English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. If your child is moving between the two tracks, it is worth knowing which set of evidence the plan is now building towards.

For the IB there is a published position worth stating plainly: no IB points threshold for equivalency has been confirmed from an official Ministry source for this page, so none is quoted here. Any site publishing a specific IB points figure for UAE equivalency should be asked where it read it. Equivalency is also something the Ministry performs and IB Gram does not, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

process.title: Tell us the code, not only the subject
process.description: Send the syllabus code from the school's exam entry form, or a photo of it. 0580 and 4MA1 are both called IGCSE Mathematics and set different papers, so the code decides which tutor and which practice are useful. For IB students, the subject, level and the IA deadline the school has set are enough.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the tutor you would keep
process.description: The trial is a real sixty-minute lesson with the tutor who would continue, not a sales call with somebody else. No card details are taken before it. If the match is wrong, say so and we change the tutor rather than asking you to try harder with the same one.

process.title: Baseline on a real paper
process.description: In the first two weeks the student sits one whole past paper under timing, and the tutor marks it against the published scheme. That produces a raw score and a list of lost marks by topic. It is unpleasant and it is the single most useful hour in the plan, because everything after it is prioritised by that list.

process.title: Weekly marked work and a shrinking list
process.description: Each week the tutor sets two questions, marks them, and reports which items on the topic list have been cleared. You get the marked work, not a summary of it. The list getting shorter is the progress measure, and when it stops shortening we change the method rather than adding hours.

process.title: Review against the baseline at six weeks
process.description: At six weeks the student sits a comparable paper under the same conditions and the two raw marks are set side by side. That conversation is short and factual. If the number has not moved, we say so and explain what we think the cause is, which is sometimes a subject gap and sometimes a sleep schedule.

whyPoints.title: Evidence you can read without us
whyPoints.description: Marked scripts, mark-scheme comparisons and dated raw scores are yours to keep and to show the school. A parent who does not teach chemistry can still read a rising raw mark on a paper of similar difficulty, which is more than a progress call provides.

whyPoints.title: The syllabus code decides the practice
whyPoints.description: Matching starts from the code on the entry form rather than from the subject name. It sounds pedantic until a student spends four weeks on Cambridge 0620 structures for a Pearson 4CH1 paper, which happens in Sharjah households where siblings sit different boards.

whyPoints.title: Online because the specialist matters more than the postcode
whyPoints.description: A Khor Fakkan or Al Nahda family choosing locally is choosing from whoever is willing to drive. Choosing online means choosing a tutor who has marked that specific paper. For a Higher Level subject, that difference is the whole decision rather than a convenience.

whyPoints.title: Honest limits on coursework
whyPoints.description: A tutor here will narrow a research question, explain a criterion and comment on a draft, and will not write any part of an IA, Extended Essay, TOK essay or Personal Project. The limit is stated before you book, so nobody discovers it halfway through a submission week.

whyPoints.title: No invented numbers and no grade promises
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or source that published it. No success rate, satisfaction score or average grade is claimed, because none could be produced with a sample size and a method. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does is selling something else.

faqs.question: Does Sharjah American International School teach the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Sharjah American International School runs an American programme, not the IB Diploma. Families searching for an IB or IGCSE tutor around the school are usually preparing for a move to an IB or British-curriculum school, entering a Cambridge IGCSE subject as a private candidate, or running two curricula across siblings. Check the current programme offering on the school's own site and with the emirate regulator before you plan, because school licences change. The tutoring question is the same either way: which qualification is the student actually going to be assessed in, and what does that assessment reward?

faqs.question: My child is on an American programme at SAIS, so can they sit Cambridge IGCSE as well?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a private candidate at an exam centre that accepts private entries. The practical steps are to choose the syllabus code, find a centre taking private candidates for that subject, and submit the entry before the centre's deadline, which falls months before the paper. Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series. Budget for the entry fee separately from tuition, and confirm whether the subject has a practical component the centre can run, because some science specifications need a laboratory session that not every centre offers to private entries.

faqs.question: How do American letter grades compare with IGCSE grades 9 to 1?
faqs.answer: There is no official conversion, and anyone offering you a tidy table is guessing. The systems measure different things: a letter grade and GPA accumulate coursework over a semester, while an IGCSE grade comes from terminal papers marked to a published scheme. A student with an A average can land several grades below expectation on a first untimed-to-timed transition, almost always on technique rather than knowledge. The only reliable comparison is a real past paper sat under timing and marked against the scheme, which is why that is the first thing a tutor sets up.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam series do candidates in Sharjah actually sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in a May/June window and a November window. The February/March series you may find in search results is offered to India only and is not available to a candidate sitting in the UAE. Cambridge also places each exam centre in one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, so always check the live official timetable for your centre's zone rather than a copy on a third-party site.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to our home in Al Majaz or Muwailih?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. Every lesson for a Sharjah family is delivered online, one to one, over live video with a shared screen. The trade is deliberate. An in-home pool is limited to tutors willing to drive to your area at the time your child is free, while an online pool is limited only by the subject. For a Higher Level science or a specific Paper 6 skill, the second pool is the one with the right person in it.

faqs.question: What does IB and IGCSE tutoring cost per hour in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: The published market runs from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour for budget online sessions, through AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, to AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 500 once travel is priced in, and a premium named tier reaches AED 650. Those are figures the providers themselves publish. IB Gram quotes its own rate after the free trial lesson, with the session length and whether marking is included stated in writing, because an hourly rate without that detail cannot be compared.

faqs.question: What evidence will I actually see after four weeks of sessions?
faqs.answer: A baseline paper with a raw mark and the lost marks listed by topic, roughly eight marked questions with the mark scheme beside them, four sets of session notes naming what was covered, and an updated topic list showing which items have been cleared. That file is yours and you can show it to the school. If the list has not shortened in four weeks, that is a result too, and the honest response is to change the approach rather than to add more hours at the same rate.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's IB Internal Assessment draft?
faqs.answer: A tutor can narrow the research question until it is assessable, challenge the method, explain what a criterion descriptor is asking for, and comment on a draft by naming the criterion letter, the band the draft sits in, and what the band above requires. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or complete any part of it. The IB treats work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice and the consequence falls on the student, so a service offering a finished Internal Assessment is selling a risk rather than support.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Sharjah, and why should a tutor care?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A tutor should care because it means the school's assessment calendar is approved rather than arbitrary, so the right question at the first session is what dates the school has set. SPEA is also where a parent can confirm that a school is licensed. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by SPEA and does not claim to be; no online tutoring platform should.

faqs.question: Coming off an American transcript, how many IGCSE passes will the Ministry want to see?
faqs.answer: The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One competing page states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which would mean paying for an entry you do not need. Verify your own case on the Ministry's own channel, because equivalency is something the Ministry performs and no tutoring service does.

faqs.question: What time can a session start if we live in Al Nahda and my child studies in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Plan for 19:00 or later on a weeknight. An Al Nahda household with a Dubai school place is usually dealing with a bus that arrives after 16:30, followed by food and school homework, so an earlier slot gets cancelled rather than attended. Friday afternoons and weekend mornings work better for a longer paper-practice block, since a whole timed paper needs an uninterrupted two hours. Sessions are set on Gulf Standard Time and the tutor is matched to a slot that holds week after week, because a moving slot is the main reason plans fail.

faqs.question: My child moves from SAIS to an IB school next academic year, so when should tutoring start?
faqs.answer: Start in the term before the move, not in the first week of the new school. The content gap is usually manageable; the gap in assessment habits is not, and it is easier to build in a quiet term than during DP1. A sensible first block is one subject bridged hard, usually Maths, plus an introduction to criterion marking and the vocabulary of Theory of Knowledge. Arriving already able to read a criterion descriptor changes the first Internal Assessment considerably, and the first Internal Assessment sets the tone for the rest of the year.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both IGCSE Physics and IB Chemistry for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A tutor with a physical-sciences background can often cover IGCSE Physics 0625 and IB Chemistry at Standard Level competently. Higher Level Chemistry with an Internal Assessment is a different matter, and a student is better served by a specialist for that component even if it means two tutors. Where two tutors are used, they share the topic list and the session notes so the household runs one plan rather than two, and the scheduling is set so the two sessions do not land on the same evening.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Sharjah need a permit, and how do we check?
faqs.answer: Yes. A private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no official fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you read online as unverified. Ask a tutor directly whether they hold the permit, and apply or verify through the MoHRE smart app or website.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers the exact subject and level we need?
faqs.answer: You get told, before you pay. Some combinations are genuinely thin at any given moment, with Higher Level Further Mathematics, less common Language B options and specialist Group 3 subjects the usual examples. The honest options are to wait for a named date when a specialist is free, to start on an adjacent component that a current tutor can teach well, or to be told that we cannot help with this one. Taking a booking for a subject nobody on the platform teaches properly wastes the term that mattered.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-for-sharjah-ameri.closingBody: The fastest way to know whether tutoring will help your child is not a consultation; it is one past paper sat under timing and marked against the published scheme. That single hour tells you whether the marks are leaking at the content or at the command term, and those two problems need different plans and different lengths of commitment. Book the free trial lesson, bring the syllabus code from the school's entry form, and ask for the baseline in the first fortnight. Everything on this page, from the AED bands to the backwards calendar, exists so you can judge the answer yourself rather than take it on trust.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-for-sharjah-engli.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE across mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects, one-to-one over live video into Gulf Standard Time. Every arrangement starts from the mock script rather than the mock grade, because the two carry entirely different information.

intro.heading: A mock is a bad forecast and a very good diagnosis
paragraphs: Mock results arrive, a household reorganises itself around them, and the one document that would have been useful goes into a drawer. The grade gets read as a prediction and the script gets filed. That is exactly backwards. A mock grade is a weak forecast of a final grade for reasons that have nothing to do with the pupil, and a mock script is the single most informative piece of paper a candidate produces in two years.

The forecast is weak because the instrument is not the same instrument. A mock is sat on an incomplete syllabus, which means some questions were unanswerable rather than answered wrongly. It is often sat in a normal classroom rather than under examination conditions. It may be marked deliberately harshly to create urgency, or generously to maintain confidence, and a family is rarely told which. Any of those shifts a grade by a band without saying anything about June.

The diagnosis is strong because the script is specific. It shows which questions were attempted and which were abandoned, whether working was written, whether the command term was read, whether the final page was reached, and whether partial marks were earned before something narrow went wrong. Those are facts, and most of them a parent can read without knowing the subject. The marker has also written the diagnosis in the margin, repeatedly, where nobody collects it.

What this page does is set out the six ways a final diverges from a mock, because the divergence is patterned rather than random. Some pupils improve because the syllabus completes. Some improve because they sit the real paper under real conditions and rise to it. Some fall back because they revised for one known date and could not sustain it across nine subjects. Each pattern has a cause, and the cause determines what the next ten weeks should contain.

Ten weeks is the operative number because it is roughly what sits between a mock season and a June series for most Sharjah schools. It is long enough for technique to be installed and timed practice to bite, and too short for a syllabus to be taught from the beginning. Knowing which of those two a pupil needs is the whole decision, and the script answers it.

One more thing before any of it. The most expensive mistake available after a mock season is to book a term in three subjects within a week of the results arriving, before anybody has read a script or asked which topics had been taught. That purchase feels responsible and it is aimed at nothing in particular, which in a ten-week window is the one thing a family cannot afford. Read first, triage second, buy third. Tuition for Sharjah families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Sharjah, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

sections.heading: What a mock measures, and what it cannot
paragraphs: A mock measures performance on a particular paper, on a partially covered syllabus, under conditions that differ from the real series, marked to a standard a family is usually not told. Each of those four qualifications matters, and together they explain why the grade is a weak forecast. None of them makes the exercise useless; they make the grade the wrong output to read.

Syllabus incompleteness is the largest distortion and the easiest to check. If a third of the specification has not been taught, the questions on it were not answered wrongly - they were unanswerable. A pupil who scored poorly on those and well on everything else has a different problem from one who scored evenly badly, and the two produce the same grade. Ask the subject teacher which topics had been covered by the mock date, and the grade becomes interpretable.

Conditions matter next. A paper sat in a normal classroom with normal interruptions, at a normal lesson length, is not the same instrument as a paper sat in a hall under invigilation with a full time allowance. Some schools replicate examination conditions carefully and some cannot, for perfectly practical reasons. Which applies determines whether a timing failure on the mock means anything about June.

Marking standard is the one families almost never ask about and the one that moves a grade most invisibly. Some departments mark mocks harshly on purpose, to create urgency while there is still time to respond. Some mark generously to protect confidence. Some apply last year's boundaries, which may not be this year's. A single question to the head of department - how was this marked, and against which boundaries - makes the number mean something.

sections.heading: Six ways a final diverges from a mock
paragraphs: Movement between mock and final is patterned rather than random, and there are six recurring shapes. Recognising which one a pupil is in matters because each has a different cause and a different response. Families tend to assume only two exist - better or worse - and to attribute both to effort, which is almost never the main driver.

Three patterns improve. The syllabus completes, so questions that were unanswerable become answerable and the grade rises without anything else changing. The pupil installs technique in the intervening weeks, which is the pattern a good ten-week plan produces deliberately. Or the pupil simply performs better under real conditions than under classroom ones, which happens more often than people expect and is not something to count on.

Three patterns fall back. A pupil who revised intensively for one known mock date cannot sustain that across eight or nine subjects in a real series, so the mock overstated them. A pupil whose mock was marked generously finds the board less forgiving. Or the real paper is harder than the mock, which it frequently is, because a mock covering two thirds of a specification is an easier instrument by construction.

The practical use of this is predictive rather than retrospective. Ask which of the six is most likely for a given pupil before deciding what the next ten weeks contain. A pupil whose mock was depressed by syllabus incompleteness needs the remaining content taught. A pupil whose mock was inflated by intensive single-subject revision needs a sustainable plan across their whole timetable, which is a completely different purchase.

sections.heading: Reading the script for the gap rather than the grade
paragraphs: The procedure takes twenty minutes a subject and requires no subject knowledge. Start at the back. If the final questions are blank while comparable earlier ones were answered, the pupil ran out of time. If they were attempted and wrong, timing is not the issue. That single check separates the cheapest repair in the set from everything else, and it is the first thing to establish.

Then separate the untaught from the unknown. Take the list of topics covered by the mock date from the subject teacher and strike the questions on untaught material out of the lost-mark count. What remains is the real gap. Families routinely panic about a grade that was depressed by a third of a specification nobody had reached, and the correction costs one email.

Then look for partial marks. In mathematics and the sciences, method marks earned with the accuracy mark missing means the approach was right and a number went wrong - a narrow, cheap repair. In essay subjects, a tick for a point made with no credit for development means the pupil stopped where the mark scheme wanted more. Both are technique rather than knowledge and both move inside ten weeks.

Finally read the annotations rather than the marks. Teachers write the diagnosis in the margin, repeatedly: 'explain' circled, 'units?', 'evidence?', 'how does this answer the question?'. The marker has already done the analytical work and nobody collects it. Twenty minutes with a highlighter converts a set of mock scripts into a triage, and the triage is what the next ten weeks should be built from.

sections.heading: The ten-week closure plan, week by week
paragraphs: Ten weeks is roughly what sits between a mock season and a June series, and it has an internal structure that most revision plans ignore. The first two weeks belong to triage and remaining content. The middle four belong to installing one technique per subject. The following three belong to full timed papers with immediate correction. The last belongs to pacing and consolidation, with nothing new introduced.

That ordering is not arbitrary. Content has to come first because it cannot be installed late - a topic taught in week eight has no time to become secure. Technique has to come before practice because practising a flawed method entrenches it. And practice has to come before the final week because the value of a timed paper lies in the correction that follows it, which takes a session of its own.

The commonest failure is to compress everything into the final fortnight, which produces a pupil sitting papers they cannot correct and learning content they cannot consolidate. The second commonest is to spread evenly, which gives the content weeks to practice and the practice weeks to content. Both are avoidable by writing the ten weeks out at the start, which takes one conversation.

Two Sharjah-specific adjustments apply. Where the window overlaps Ramadan, school days shorten and evenings restructure around Iftar, so sessions move to a post-Iftar slot rather than pausing - a family that pauses loses six of the ten weeks. And specialist availability tightens across the country from January, so the slot should be booked at the start of the ten weeks rather than negotiated in week five.

sections.heading: Why some subjects move more than others
paragraphs: A ten-week window does not treat all subjects equally, and the difference is structural. Subjects whose typical gap is technique move a lot; subjects whose typical gap is content move little. That means a triage should put effort where the window can actually deliver, which sometimes means leaving the most alarming subject alone.

Mathematics moves well, because most of a mock gap is usually method, arithmetic and timing rather than content. Biology moves well, because terminology precision and command-term discipline install quickly and the content is largely learnable from a revision guide. English moves well, because the gap is almost always an assessment objective and installing the analysis sentence changes every reading answer. Computer Science moves well, because pseudocode conventions are technique.

Chemistry moves least reliably, because the common gap is moles and organic chemistry, which is content with a dependency chain behind it. Literature moves on structure and quotation economy and not at all on text knowledge, so a mock revealing an unread text is the one finding ten weeks cannot fix. History splits: source technique moves fast, case-study recall does not, and a combined grade hides which half failed.

The practical rule that follows is uncomfortable and correct. Put the ten weeks into the two subjects where the script shows a technique gap, even if a third subject has a worse grade caused by a content gap. The technique subjects will move and the content subject will not, so spreading the effort evenly produces less total movement than concentrating it. That is an argument a family has to make to itself, because instinct says otherwise.

sections.heading: The three things that make a final worse than a mock
paragraphs: A final that comes in below a mock is distressing and usually explicable, and the explanations are three. The first is over-preparation for a single date. A pupil who revised intensively for one mock in one subject performed at a level they cannot sustain across eight or nine subjects in a compressed real series. The mock did not lie; it measured something that will not be repeated, and the signal is a strong mock alongside weaker classwork across the term.

The second is marking. A mock marked more generously than the board marks, or against boundaries that have moved, produces a grade the final will not match. Nobody is being dishonest; a department making a judgement about confidence or urgency is making a reasonable professional choice. A family that asks how the mock was marked, and against which boundaries, converts a later shock into present information.

The third is the instrument itself. A mock covering two thirds of a specification is an easier paper than one covering all of it, so a pupil can be genuinely at the same standard and score lower on the real thing. This is the most common cause and the least discussed, because it requires no explanation about the pupil at all. The remedy is full whole-syllabus past papers in weeks seven to nine rather than more partial ones.

All three are predictable in advance from a script, a conversation with a department and a glance at the mock paper's coverage. None of them requires a pupil to have done anything wrong, and attributing a fall to effort when one of these three is operating is both unfair and unhelpful, because it directs the next ten weeks at the wrong thing entirely.

sections.heading: What the school's predicted grade does with the mock
paragraphs: A predicted grade is a forecast made for a purpose, and a mock result is usually one of its inputs. Which means the mock's distortions travel into the prediction, and a family that understands the first understands the second. A prediction built partly on a harshly marked mock sitting on an incomplete syllabus is a cautious number, and a prediction built on a generously marked one is optimistic.

The method matters more than the number. A prediction built from a pupil's performance on board past papers marked to the published scheme is a measurement. One built from classwork, effort and a department's experience of similar pupils is a judgement, often a sound one, calibrated against that department's own cohort history. In a school whose secondary phase is still filling, there is less of that history, which is structural rather than a failing.

Predictions also have a fixing point, and parents rarely know when it falls. Before it, a prediction can move on new evidence. After it, particularly once it has gone into an application, it is effectively settled. Knowing the date changes what is worth doing: a marked timed paper produced a fortnight before the fixing point can move a number, and the same paper a fortnight after cannot.

The useful posture is neither accepting nor disputing the figure but asking how it was built. Which assessments contributed. Whether any board past paper was involved. What the pupil would need to demonstrate for it to move. Departments answer those questions straightforwardly, and the answers tell you whether the prediction is a measurement to work with or a judgement worth supplementing with one.

sections.heading: Measuring the closure at week four and week eight
paragraphs: A ten-week plan needs two checkpoints or it becomes ten weeks of hope. At week four the indicator is behavioural rather than numeric: the technique being installed should be visible in the pupil's unprompted written work. Method written out without being asked. Units attached. The analysis sentence present. Marks may not have moved and that is normal, because a habit becomes automatic before it shows under timing.

That check requires no subject knowledge. Put a piece of work from week four beside one from week one and look for the targeted behaviour. If it is absent, one of three things is wrong and all three are fixable at week four: the target was never agreed with the pupil, so they do not know what to do differently; the between-session work is not happening, so the habit has too few repetitions; or the sessions have drifted onto content, which is more comfortable to teach than a drill.

At week eight the indicator should be numeric and narrow. Marks on the specific question types being worked on, from a full timed paper, compared against the mock script. Not the overall grade, which is noisy and depends on topic mix, but the targeted category. If the method marks were the target, the method marks should be there. If they are not, the remaining fortnight belongs to practice and pacing rather than to more of the same.

Both checkpoints also protect against the most common soft failure, which is scope creep. A plan that began with two subjects and one error category each, and now covers four subjects and general support, has drifted. A written plan from week one makes that visible without anybody having to raise it as a complaint, and in a ten-week window there is no time to recover from it unnoticed.

sections.heading: Honesty, coverage and the first session
paragraphs: The rules do not change in a compressed window and the pressure to bend them rises. A tutor teaches, questions, models on a different example and marks the pupil's own work. A tutor does not write, co-write or edit any submitted piece, including coursework where a specification uses it. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, which is a malpractice trigger whose exposure falls on the candidate.

Nor should board material be handed over as files. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB own their syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables, and the right behaviour is to link the official page. That matters practically in a ten-week plan, because the full timed papers in weeks seven to nine must come from the official source anyway and a family that knows where they live can check the plan for themselves.

On coverage: mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects at both Cambridge and Pearson tiers are well covered in this set and a match is usually quick. In a ten-week window speed matters, so the honest position is useful: the brief is covered and a trial lesson is scheduled within days, or it is covered by a specialist working into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE and that is disclosed, or it is not currently covered and is named rather than filled with a generalist.

The first session is free, is one session, and requires no card details. The useful thing to bring is the mock scripts rather than the mock results, plus a list from the subject teachers of which topics had been taught by the mock date. Within that hour it should be possible to produce a triage: two subjects, one error category each, and a written ten-week shape. If the honest answer is that one subject cannot move in the time available, that is said.

process.title: Ask for the scripts, not the results
process.description: Request every mock script from the school, and separately ask each subject teacher which topics had been taught by the mock date. The grade is a weak forecast; the script is the best diagnostic a candidate produces in two years, and the topic list is what makes the lost marks interpretable.

process.title: Ask how the mocks were marked
process.description: Harshly to create urgency, generously to protect confidence, or to board standard, and against which grade boundaries. A single question to the head of department converts a number into information. Families almost never ask, and it is the factor that moves a mock grade most invisibly.

process.title: Triage to two subjects, by movement available
process.description: Put the ten weeks where the window can deliver: mathematics, biology, English and Computer Science move well because their gaps are technique. Chemistry content and unread literature texts do not move in ten weeks. Concentrating produces more total movement than spreading, even when instinct says otherwise.

process.title: Write the ten weeks out at the start
process.description: Triage and remaining content in weeks one to four, technique installation in five and six, full timed papers with immediate correction in seven to nine, pacing and consolidation in ten. Content cannot be installed late and practice is worthless without the correction session that follows it.

process.title: Check behaviour at week four, marks at week eight
process.description: At week four look for the targeted habit in unprompted written work, which needs no subject knowledge. At week eight compare marks in the targeted category against the mock script. If week eight is flat, the final fortnight belongs to practice and pacing rather than to more of the same.

whyPoints.title: The script used, not the grade
whyPoints.description: A mock grade is distorted by syllabus incompleteness, conditions, marking standard and boundary choice. The script is specific: which questions were abandoned, whether working was written, whether partial marks were earned. Most of it a parent can read without knowing the subject.

whyPoints.title: Six patterns named in advance
whyPoints.description: Movement between mock and final is patterned, not random, and each pattern has a different cause and response. Predicting which one applies before planning the ten weeks is worth more than any amount of retrospective explanation after results.

whyPoints.title: Effort available where it can work
whyPoints.description: Mathematics, biology, English and Computer Science move substantially in ten weeks because their gaps are technique. Chemistry content and unread literature texts do not. Concentrating on the first group produces more total movement than spreading across both.

whyPoints.title: A written plan with an internal order
whyPoints.description: Content first because it cannot be installed late, technique before practice because practising a flawed method entrenches it, and practice before the final week because its value is in the correction that follows. Compressing it all into a fortnight is the commonest failure.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what ten weeks cannot do
whyPoints.description: A syllabus cannot be taught from the beginning, an unread set text cannot be learned reliably, and a chemistry content gap across a third of the specification will not close. Saying so is better than selling a rescue, and it protects the subjects that can still move.

faqs.question: How much should a Sharjah English School family trust a disappointing mock grade?
faqs.answer: As a forecast, not much. As a diagnosis, a great deal - but the diagnosis lives in the script rather than the grade. A mock is sat on an incomplete syllabus, so some questions were unanswerable rather than wrong. It may have been sat in a classroom rather than under full examination conditions. It may have been marked deliberately harshly to create urgency, or generously, against boundaries that have since moved. Any of those shifts a grade by a band without saying anything about June.

faqs.question: What should we ask the school after mocks?
faqs.answer: Three things, all factual. For the script itself, not the grade. For a list from each subject teacher of which topics had been taught by the mock date, so lost marks on untaught material can be struck out of the count. And for how the mocks were marked - harshly, generously, or to board standard - and against which grade boundaries. That third question is the one families almost never ask and the one that moves a mock grade most invisibly.

faqs.question: How can we read a mock script without knowing the subject?
faqs.answer: Start at the back. Blank final questions where comparable earlier ones were answered means time ran out; attempted and wrong means timing is not the issue. Then strike out the questions on topics not yet taught. Then look for partial marks, which mean the approach was right and something narrow failed. Finally read the margin annotations rather than the marks - 'explain' circled, 'units?', 'evidence?' - because the marker has already written the diagnosis and nobody collects it.

faqs.question: Why might the final grade come in below the mock?
faqs.answer: Three reasons, none of them about effort. The pupil may have revised intensively for one known date in one subject, at a level nobody sustains across eight or nine subjects in a compressed real series. The mock may have been marked more generously than the board marks, or against boundaries that have moved. Or the real paper is simply harder, because a mock covering two thirds of a specification is an easier instrument by construction. That last cause is the most common and the least discussed.

faqs.question: Can a grade genuinely improve between mocks and June?
faqs.answer: Yes, in three recognisable ways. The syllabus completes, so questions that were unanswerable become answerable and the grade rises without anything else changing - this is the most reliable of the three. Technique gets installed in the intervening weeks, which is what a good ten-week plan produces deliberately. Or the pupil performs better under real conditions than under classroom ones, which happens more often than expected and is not something to count on. The first two can be planned for; the third cannot.

faqs.question: Which subjects actually move in ten weeks?
faqs.answer: Those whose typical gap is technique rather than content. Mathematics moves well, because most of a mock gap is method, arithmetic and timing. Biology moves well, because terminology precision and command-term discipline install quickly. English moves well, because the gap is almost always an assessment objective. Computer Science moves well, because pseudocode conventions are technique. Chemistry moves least, because the common gap is moles and organic content with a dependency chain behind it.

faqs.question: Should we work on the subject with the worst mock grade?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and this is the uncomfortable part. Put the ten weeks where the window can actually deliver. A subject with a slightly better grade caused by a technique gap will move substantially; a subject with a worse grade caused by a content gap across a third of the specification will not. Concentrating on two technique subjects produces more total movement than spreading across three or four, even though instinct says the alarming subject deserves the attention.

faqs.question: What order should the ten weeks run in?
faqs.answer: Content first, then technique, then timed practice, then consolidation. Weeks one and two for triaging every script and teaching whatever content is still teachable. Weeks three and four finishing that. Weeks five and six installing one technique per subject. Weeks seven to nine on full timed papers with the errors re-worked in the following session. Week ten on pacing and re-reading the pupil's own annotated scripts, with nothing new introduced at all.

faqs.question: Why does the order matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because each stage depends on the one before. Content cannot be installed late - a topic taught in week eight has no time to become secure. Technique has to precede practice, because practising a flawed method entrenches it and then has to be undone. And practice has to finish before the final week, because the value of a timed paper lies entirely in the correction session that follows it. Compressing everything into the last fortnight produces a pupil sitting papers they never correct.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan affect a ten-week plan for a June candidate?
faqs.answer: It changes the timing rather than the content. Where the window overlaps Ramadan, school days shorten and evenings restructure around Iftar, so sessions move to a post-Iftar slot. A family that reschedules keeps all ten weeks; a family that pauses loses six of them, at precisely the point when timed practice with immediate correction is the only intervention still capable of moving a grade. Book the rescheduled slots at the start, because specialist availability tightens nationally from January.

faqs.question: How does a mock feed into the school's predicted grade?
faqs.answer: Usually as one input among several, which means the mock's distortions travel into the prediction. A prediction built partly on a harshly marked mock on an incomplete syllabus is a cautious number; one built on a generously marked mock is optimistic. The method matters more than the figure, so ask what evidence built it, whether any board past paper was involved, when it is fixed, and what the pupil would need to demonstrate for it to move.

faqs.question: How will we know at week four whether the plan is working?
faqs.answer: By behaviour rather than marks, and it requires no subject knowledge. Put a piece of the pupil's work from week four beside one from week one and look for the targeted habit: method written out unprompted, units attached, the analysis sentence present. Marks may not have moved yet, because a habit becomes automatic before it shows under timing. If the behaviour is absent, the cause is the target, the between-session work, or session drift onto content.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to Al Qasimia, Al Nahda or Al Ramtha?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service offered only in India. Tutoring for Sharjah families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. In a ten-week window that matters practically: a session lost to cross-boundary congestion at the Dubai line is a tenth of the plan, and the highest-value activity - annotating the mock script together and re-answering the questions - is a shared-screen task anyway.

faqs.question: What should we bring to the first session after mocks?
faqs.answer: The scripts rather than the results, and a list from each subject teacher of which topics had been taught by the mock date. Those two documents together make the lost marks interpretable, and nothing else does. Within an hour it should be possible to produce a triage: two subjects, one error category each, and a written ten-week shape. If one subject genuinely cannot move in the time available, that is said rather than sold around. The first session is free and needs no card details.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-for-victoria-inte.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE across mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects, one-to-one over live video into Gulf Standard Time. Work starts from the specification code and tier on your child's exam entry rather than from a generic subject brief.

intro.heading: One half of the budget is regulated; the other is not
paragraphs: Sharjah families are comparing tutoring quotes against nothing, which is the root of the difficulty. A figure of AED 200 an hour means very little on its own. It means something when it sits beside the school fee, the transport cost, the examination entries and the alternatives, and it means something quite different depending on which of those numbers are fixed and which are not. In Sharjah, unusually, one of them is approved by a regulator.

The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and its powers go further than inspection. Sharjah's authority, along with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. So curriculum and fee approval, not just inspection, sits with the emirate regulator. That is a different arrangement from a pure inspection regime and it has a practical consequence for a family: the largest line in the education budget is set through a regulated process rather than purely by a school.

Tutoring is the opposite. There is no approval process for a rate, no published schedule, and no outcome data anywhere in this market to justify one figure over another. Three of the six highest-ranking tutoring pages in this cluster publish no price at all, and two of the ones that do quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Sharjah family transacts in. So the regulated half of the budget is visible and the unregulated half is deliberately obscured, which is exactly the wrong way round for a parent trying to decide.

The figures that do exist come from providers and surveys rather than from us. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. The Bestimate rate survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and subject specialists at AED 200 to 450 or above, with BartyED advertising AED 650 for a named premium tutor. Monthly packages circulate at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

This page therefore puts tutoring next to the rest of the budget, explains why a Sharjah quote often differs from a Dubai one, and names the six things that actually move a figure - only one of which is about the tutor's ability. It also sets out what a family should settle in writing before a first invoice, because terms move a monthly total further than an hourly rate does. Tuition for Sharjah families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Sharjah, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3

A fluency or written-method repair here costs a fraction of the same repair in Year 11, when other subjects have inherited the weakness.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah schools set and stream in most cases, and the set a pupil occupies at the end of Year 9 often informs the IGCSE tier a department later proposes. Spending modestly in Year 8 to protect an Extended-tier entry is far cheaper than a Year 11 attempt to lift a capped grade.

The expensive months for a Sharjah family are therefore February to April, when specialist availability tightens across the whole country and rates at the upper end firm up.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Lumpier than IGCSE, because internal assessment deadlines cluster. A family may need two intensive months around an Internal Assessment or Extended Essay window and nothing for the two after it, so a flat arrangement across two years overpays substantially.

The published AED 200 to 450 specialist band applies and premium named tutors advertise up to AED 650, so a single subject in an examination year passes AED 1,000 a month comfortably.

Those thresholds give a family a numeric target, which is more useful for budgeting than any general sense of how a child is doing.

sections.heading: What SPEA actually approves, and why that is unusual
paragraphs: Most discussion of UAE education regulators treats them as inspection bodies, which undersells what Sharjah's does. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and it is one of two UAE authorities - the other being Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge - that approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fee and curriculum approval, not merely inspection, sits with the emirate regulator.

For a parent that has a direct consequence. The largest single line in the education budget passes through a regulated approval process, which means it is neither arbitrary nor purely a school's commercial decision. It also means a question about fees has an addressee: the authority that approved them. That is a more concrete position than families in some other arrangements enjoy.

It also sets up the contrast this page is about. Fees are approved; tutoring rates are not. There is no approval process for an hourly figure, no published schedule, and no outcome data in this market that would justify one rate over another. Not one of the researched providers publishes a statistic with a sample size, a date and a stated method, which means every rate above the floor is a claim about positioning rather than evidence of effect.

The wider regulator map is worth knowing because it is genuinely confusing and because competitors get it wrong or omit it entirely. Dubai has the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain have the Department of Education and Knowledge. Sharjah has SPEA. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. And the Ministry of Education plays a supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. SPEA appears once in an entire researched cluster, and ADEK not at all.

sections.heading: The whole education budget, itemised
paragraphs: A tutoring quote only becomes interpretable beside the other numbers, and almost nobody writes those out. The exercise takes twenty minutes and it changes decisions. List the school fee for the year, the transport charge, uniform and resources, any examination entries payable where a pupil sits a paper as a private candidate, and then the tutoring you are considering. Convert all of it to a monthly figure, because that is how the money actually leaves.

Two things usually become visible. The first is that tutoring at the specialist band across two subjects is a material fraction of a Sharjah school fee rather than a marginal addition, which is a different decision from the one a quoted hourly rate implies. The second is that the controllable line is the tutoring line. The fee is approved and fixed, the transport is what it is, and the entries are the school's arithmetic. Tutoring is the only item a family actually decides each month.

The examination entries item catches people out and belongs on the list. Entries are normally handled through the school for a registered candidate, but a pupil sitting a paper as a private candidate - including a November retake arranged outside their own school - may face separate charges through an approved centre. That cost arrives in a specific month, is not part of any tutoring quote, and is best established by asking the examinations officer rather than assuming.

The context also cuts the other way, and it should be said. Set against a year's fees, a short diagnostic block of three or four sessions is a very small number, and it is the item on the list most likely to prevent waste elsewhere. The argument for writing out the whole budget is not that tutoring is expensive; it is that an uncontrolled tutoring line is, and a controlled one is frequently the best value item on the page.

sections.heading: Sharjah's fee base, and what families do with the difference
paragraphs: International-curriculum school fees in Sharjah generally sit below comparable Dubai schools, which is one reason many families choose the emirate while working across the border. That difference is real and it produces a predictable behaviour: a portion of it is reallocated to tutoring, transport or activities. Whether that is a good trade depends entirely on whether the tutoring line is controlled.

An uncontrolled reallocation looks like this. The fee saving is notionally available, so a weekly arrangement in two subjects is agreed without a diagnosis, and it runs for eighteen months because nothing in it has a stated end point. The total exceeds the fee saving, nobody can say what it bought, and the family concludes that education in the UAE is simply expensive. That sequence is extremely common and it is a planning failure rather than a pricing one.

A controlled reallocation looks different. A diagnostic block establishes which subject and which error category is worth paying for. A defined arrangement with a stated target and an end point runs for a term. The final quarter before the series gets a reserved block. The total is a fraction of the fee difference and the outcome is attributable. Same money, different structure, and the structure is the whole of the difference.

There is a Sharjah-specific version of the same point worth naming. Because the emirate's fee base is lower, the tuition-centre market is comparatively well developed, particularly around Muwaileh and University City where student supply is close at hand. Group rates of roughly AED 100 to 150 per pupil are easy to find. That is good value for content coverage and it does not diagnose one child's specific lost marks, which is the thing that moves a grade.

sections.heading: Market rates in AED, and why a Sharjah quote can differ
paragraphs: The published national bands apply in Sharjah as elsewhere, and they are wide. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. The Bestimate survey puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialists at AED 200 to 450 or above, and BartyED advertises AED 650 for a named premium tutor.

Two Sharjah factors can shift a quote within those bands. The first is supply: a well-developed tuition-centre market and a large nearby student population push the lower bands down, so the floor is genuinely accessible here. The second is the Dubai boundary. A tutor based in Dubai quoting for an in-home arrangement in Al Nahda or Al Khan is pricing a cross-border journey at the worst possible hour, and that can take a quote above the national in-home band rather than below it.

Monthly packages are also common and worth dividing out before comparing. Packages circulating include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which works out near AED 100 an hour, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits, which is roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour. The in-home package delivers the same eight teaching hours as the online one at more than double the price, and the difference is travel.

None of these bands comes with evidence. No provider in this market publishes outcome data with a sample size, a date and a method. Competitor pages carry satisfaction percentages, self-asserted star ratings and claims about the proportion of students reaching top grades, with nothing checkable behind them - one shows a rating from twenty reviews beside a student figure orders of magnitude larger. A higher rate is a claim about positioning, and a family paying it should know that.

sections.heading: The Dubai boundary, and who pays for crossing it
paragraphs: This is the Sharjah cost factor that has no equivalent elsewhere in the country. A substantial share of the specialist tutoring supply in the northern emirates is based in Dubai, and the two cities are separated by some of the heaviest peak congestion in the region. A tutor travelling into Al Nahda, Al Khan or Al Majaz for a 5pm session is committing a journey that can exceed an hour each way, and it is priced into the rate whether the invoice itemises it or not.

The arithmetic is worth doing. A two-hour round trip to deliver a one-hour lesson is a three-hour commitment, and across a thirteen-week term that is roughly twenty-six hours of travel inside thirteen hours of teaching. No rate makes that attractive to a tutor on a sustainable basis, which is why such arrangements tend to be quoted at or above the top of the AED 180 to 500 in-home band, or to collapse into fortnightly sessions after a few weeks.

The second cost is the one that does not appear anywhere. When the cross-border arrangement is not viable, the family is offered somebody local and general instead, and the specialism quietly disappears while the in-home premium does not. A Sharjah family paying AED 300 an hour for a generalist because the Extended-tier Chemistry specialist would not drive from Dubai has made the worst trade available in this market, and they made it for geographic reasons.

Removing the journey removes both problems at once. IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to Sharjah households over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which means the tutor is selected for the specification and tier rather than for which side of a boundary they live on. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered in India only.

sections.heading: Six things that actually move a quote
paragraphs: Families assume the variable is quality and it usually is not. Six factors move a tutoring quote in this market, and only two of them concern the person's ability. Knowing which one is operating in a given conversation tells you whether the figure is negotiable and whether paying it buys anything relevant to your child's problem.

The first is scarcity of the specification. Extended-tier Computer Science 0478 with pseudocode conventions, Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a first language or an unusual literature set text all have thin pools, and a quote reflects supply. That is a legitimate thing to pay for and it is availability rather than excellence. The second is the calendar: specialist rates firm up from January as the June series approaches, so identical teaching costs more in March than in September.

The third is travel, which in Sharjah frequently means the Dubai boundary. The fourth is what sits inside the rate - whether marking happens between sessions, how many sessions a month contains, whether unused sessions roll over, and what notice ends the arrangement. Two providers at the same hourly figure can invoice a third apart on terms alone, which is why the terms matter more than the headline.

The fifth and sixth do concern the person. Diagnostic capability - the ability to mark a timed script against the published scheme and categorise the losses - is a narrower skill than subject teaching, and it is the clearest justification for paying above the qualified-teacher band. Reputation is the sixth, and it is the one with no evidence behind it anywhere in this market, which is worth knowing before paying for it.

sections.heading: What no invoice should include, at any band
paragraphs: Some items should not appear at AED 45 or at AED 650. Written, edited or supplied coursework is the clearest. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, which is a malpractice trigger rather than a service, and the exposure falls on the candidate whose whole qualification is at stake rather than on the provider taking the fee.

Nor should anybody supply Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides as files. Those belong to the boards and the right behaviour is to link the official page so a family reads the current version. A provider offering a folder of mark schemes as part of a package has told you how it treats rules in general, which is worth knowing before any commitment.

Claims nobody can substantiate should not be in a rate either. No provider in this market publishes outcome data with a sample size, a date and a method, so satisfaction percentages, star ratings and claims about the proportion of pupils reaching top grades are marketing figures. A promise of a specific grade is a reason to decline. And no provider holds regulator approval: IB Gram holds no SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or IB approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership and claims none.

On tax, this page states nothing about the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because that would require a Federal Tax Authority citation and the position turns on a provider's own registration and the nature of the service. What a family can reasonably require is a quoted AED figure with a plain statement of whether VAT is included, excluded or not applicable, plus a tax registration number where one is held, in writing before the first invoice.

sections.heading: Coverage, permits and the first session
paragraphs: Mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects at both Cambridge and Pearson tiers are well covered in this set, and a match is usually quick. Thinner briefs exist: Computer Science 0478 with pseudocode conventions, Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a first language, and unusual literature text lists. In a given week the honest answer may be that nobody suitable is free, and that is better stated than filled with a generalist at the same rate.

Three outcomes are possible and a family should be told which applies before any money changes hands. The brief is covered and a trial lesson is scheduled within days. The brief is covered by a specialist working into Gulf Standard Time from outside the UAE, which is disclosed rather than concealed behind a local-looking telephone number - and two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to numbers outside the country without saying so. Or the brief is not currently covered, in which case it is named.

Parents are entitled to check the one credential that exists. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system under the service name Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, a provider citing licensing costs in its rate has misread its own paperwork. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts has been published.

The first session is free, is one session, and requires no card details. The useful things to bring are your child's last marked paper and the itemised monthly education budget from earlier on this page. Within that hour it should be possible to say which subject and which error category is worth paying for, what that would cost against the published bands, and whether the answer is nothing. A recommendation of none is a legitimate outcome and a frequent one.

faqs.question: What does SPEA actually control for a Victoria International School of Sharjah family?
faqs.answer: More than inspection. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and it is one of two UAE authorities - with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge - that approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. So fee and curriculum approval sits with the regulator rather than solely with a school. For a parent that means the largest line in the education budget passes through a regulated process, and a question about fees has an addressee.

faqs.question: Are tutoring rates regulated in Sharjah the way fees are?
faqs.answer: No, and the contrast is the point. There is no approval process for an hourly tutoring figure, no published schedule, and no outcome data anywhere in this market that would justify one rate over another. Not one of the researched providers publishes a statistic with a sample size, a date and a stated method. So the regulated half of the education budget is visible and the unregulated half is largely obscured, which is the wrong way round for a parent trying to compare quotes.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tutoring cost per term in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: At the published national bands, one weekly hour across a thirteen-week term is roughly AED 1,950 to AED 3,900 for a qualified subject tutor at AED 150 to 300, and roughly AED 2,600 to AED 5,900 for a specialist at AED 200 to 450. A diagnostic block of three or four sessions is about AED 450 to 1,200 at the mid band. Those are market figures from Unitors, TutorChase and the Bestimate survey rather than an IB Gram price list, and they apply nationally rather than specifically here.

faqs.question: Why should we write out the whole education budget first?
faqs.answer: Because an hourly rate is uninterpretable on its own and becomes clear beside the other numbers. List the school fee, transport, uniform and resources, any examination entries payable through a centre, and the tutoring you are considering, all converted to monthly figures. Two things usually become visible: tutoring at the specialist band across two subjects is a material fraction of a Sharjah fee rather than a marginal addition, and it is the only line on the list you actually decide each month.

faqs.question: Sharjah fees are lower than Dubai's. Should the saving go on tutoring?
faqs.answer: Only if the tutoring line is controlled, and that is the whole of the answer. An uncontrolled reallocation looks like a weekly arrangement in two subjects agreed without a diagnosis, running eighteen months because nothing in it has an end point, with a total that exceeds the fee saving and an outcome nobody can attribute. A controlled one is a diagnostic block, a defined term against a stated target, and a reserved final quarter. Same money, different structure, and the structure is the entire difference.

faqs.question: Why might a Sharjah quote be higher than a Dubai one for the same work?
faqs.answer: Because of the boundary. A substantial share of specialist supply in the northern emirates is Dubai-based, and a tutor travelling into Al Nahda, Al Khan or Al Majaz for a 5pm session can spend an hour each way. A three-hour commitment to deliver one hour of teaching is priced into the rate, which can push an in-home quote to or above the top of the published AED 180 to 500 band. Against that, the local tuition-centre market and nearby student supply push the lower bands down.

faqs.question: What happens if a Dubai-based specialist will not travel to us?
faqs.answer: Usually a local generalist is offered instead, and the in-home premium does not fall to match. That is the worst trade available in this market: a family paying AED 300 an hour for somebody teaching a specification they have not taught, because the Extended-tier specialist would not cross the boundary. The alternative is to accept a screen and keep the specialism, which is why IB Gram delivers to Sharjah households over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre group class good value here?
faqs.answer: For content coverage, yes, and Sharjah's centre market is comparatively well developed, particularly around Muwaileh and University City. Group rates of roughly AED 100 to 150 per pupil are easy to find, against AED 200 to 450 for one-to-one specialist work. What a group cannot do is diagnose: a session pitched to several pupils addresses the average gap rather than your child's specific pattern of lost marks. Ask whether individual timed scripts are marked between sessions; often they are not.

faqs.question: Should we compare monthly packages or hourly rates?
faqs.answer: Divide every package out before comparing anything. Packages circulating include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which is near AED 100 an hour, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, which is roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour. The in-home package delivers the same eight teaching hours at more than double the price, and the difference is travel. Then ask the terms: session count, marking, rollover and notice, all of which move a monthly invoice materially.

faqs.question: Which six things actually change the figure we are quoted?
faqs.answer: Scarcity of the specification, the calendar, travel, what sits inside the rate, diagnostic capability, and reputation. Only the fifth is clearly about ability: marking a timed script against the published scheme and categorising the losses is a narrower skill than subject teaching, and it is the clearest justification for paying above the qualified-teacher band. Reputation is the sixth and has no evidence behind it anywhere in this market. The other four are supply, timing, distance and contract terms.

faqs.question: Do examination entry costs belong in the tutoring conversation?
faqs.answer: They belong in the budget rather than the tutoring quote, and they catch families out. Entries are normally handled through the school for a registered candidate, but a pupil sitting a paper as a private candidate - including a November retake arranged outside their own school - may face separate charges through an approved centre. That cost lands in a specific month and is not part of any tutoring figure. Ask the examinations officer rather than assuming, and put the answer on the monthly list.

faqs.question: Does a tutor in Sharjah need a permit, and does it affect the rate?
faqs.answer: A permit, and it should not affect the rate because it is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the smart app, website or e-services. So a provider citing licensing costs in its figure has misread its own paperwork. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published.

Tutoring for Sharjah families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. The cost consequence is direct: the cross-boundary journey priced into the published AED 180 to 500 in-home band is not in the figure at all, and the tutor is chosen for the specification and tier rather than for which side of the Dubai line they live on.

faqs.question: What should we bring to the first conversation about cost?
faqs.answer: Two things. Your child's last marked paper, which is what decides whether the problem is four sessions or a term, and the itemised monthly education budget. intro.heading: Nine subjects, two slots, one decision that matters
paragraphs: The arithmetic is unavoidable. A Year 11 pupil on a British curriculum is carrying nine or ten IGCSE subjects. At the published Dubai and Sharjah market bands of AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor, one weekly session in each of them is more than AED 5,000 a month before anything intensive happens. Nobody does that. What families actually do is fund two subjects, and the decision about which two is therefore the whole of the strategy.

That decision is almost always made badly, and for an understandable reason. The subject nominated is the one producing the most friction at home: the homework arguments, the tears, the slammed door. Friction tracks discomfort rather than distance from the next grade boundary, and the two correlate weakly. A pupil two marks short in a subject they tolerate is a better purchase than one fifteen marks short in the subject they dread, and the second pupil needs a different intervention anyway.

What should drive the choice is marks per hour: how many marks an hour of focused work can realistically recover in each subject, given what the pupil's marked work actually shows. That is a calculable quantity, roughly, and it is the only comparison that puts nine subjects on the same scale. It also produces counter-intuitive answers that families resist, which is why writing it down matters more than discussing it.

Two further considerations make the triage better. Some subjects share a repair, so one purchase pays twice: reading analysis in English improves History source questions, and a practical-paper block improves all three sciences simultaneously. And some subjects should be deliberately left alone, because the window available cannot deliver in them - a content gap across a third of a chemistry specification in the spring term is not a ten-week problem however alarming the grade is.

This page sets out a five-question rubric to score each subject, a way of ranking them by marks per hour, the pairings where one purchase serves two subjects, and the cases where the right answer is a conversation with the school rather than a tutor at all.

None of the material the rubric needs has to be bought. A marked script from each subject, a note from each teacher of which topics had been taught by the date of that assessment, the specification code and tier from the examinations officer, and one sentence from each teacher about what the pupil should practise. That is a morning's work, it is free, and it is the difference between a plan aimed at two specific error categories and a plan aimed at whichever subject was most recently mentioned at dinner. Tuition for Sharjah families is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram does not offer home visits in Sharjah, and home visits are a service offered only in India.

sections.heading: The triage problem, stated as arithmetic
paragraphs: Nine subjects, two fundable slots. At the published market bands - AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor and AED 200 to 450 for a specialist, according to the Bestimate survey and providers including Unitors and TutorChase - a single weekly hour in each of nine subjects runs past AED 5,000 a month. No household treats that as a sensible plan, so the real question has never been whether to triage. It is whether the triage is done deliberately or by default.

Done by default, the two subjects chosen are the ones generating friction at home. That is a reasonable instinct and a poor instrument, because friction measures how unpleasant a subject is to live with rather than how many marks are available in it. The subject producing arguments is often the one where the pupil knows they are behind on content, which is precisely the case where hours deliver least.

Done deliberately, the two subjects chosen are those with the highest marks per hour: the most marks recoverable per hour of focused work, given what the marked scripts actually show. That quantity can be estimated well enough to rank nine subjects, and the ranking is frequently uncomfortable. A subject with a grade 6 and a method problem outranks a subject with a grade 4 and a content problem, even though every instinct says otherwise.

There is a third input families forget: the ceiling. A subject entered at Core tier in a Cambridge route has a grade ceiling that no tutoring lifts, which makes its marks-per-hour score low regardless of what the script shows. That is not a reason to abandon the subject; it is a reason to have a tier conversation with the department instead, which costs nothing and can change more than a term of sessions would.
