sections.heading: A five-question rubric, applied subject by subject
paragraphs: Five questions, asked of each subject using the pupil's own marked work, produce a score that can be compared across a whole timetable. None of them requires subject knowledge and all of them are answerable from a script and a short conversation with a teacher. The point of writing them down is that an instinct cannot be compared across nine subjects and a score can.

First: is the gap procedural or content? Procedural gaps - method unshown, command term misread, precision lost, time run out - score high because they move in weeks. Content gaps score low in a short window and high in a long one. Second: how many marks are actually at stake? A pupil two marks below a boundary has more to gain per hour than one fifteen marks below, where the hours needed are many times greater.

Third: is there a ceiling? A Core-tier entry caps the grade regardless of performance, which pushes the score towards zero and redirects the action to the department. Fourth: does the repair transfer? English reading analysis pays in History; the practical component pays in all three sciences; algebra pays in physics and chemistry. A transferable repair scores roughly double. Fifth: is anybody available? A subject with a thin specialist pool scores lower in practice, because a brief nobody can staff delivers nothing.

Score each subject one to three on each question, add them, and rank. The exercise takes an hour with the scripts spread out and it is free. The ranking it produces will usually place one subject nobody was worried about in the top two, and one subject everybody was worried about near the bottom with a note saying 'talk to the department about tier' or 'this is a content gap and the window is too short'.

sections.heading: Marks per hour, and why it produces uncomfortable answers
paragraphs: Marks per hour is a crude measure and it is the only one that puts nine subjects on a single scale. The calculation is simple in principle: how many marks could an hour of focused, well-aimed work recover in this subject, given the error pattern the script shows? A method problem in mathematics might be worth two or three marks an hour for the first five hours. A content gap spanning a third of a chemistry specification might be worth a fraction of a mark an hour.

Those numbers are estimates and they do not need to be precise to be useful. An order of magnitude is enough, because the decision is a ranking rather than a budget forecast. What matters is that the comparison is made on the same basis across subjects, which immediately exposes the error families make: the subject with the worst grade frequently has the lowest marks per hour, because a bad grade often indicates a content gap and content gaps are slow.

The measure also exposes the ceiling problem in a way nothing else does. A subject entered at Core tier has a hard upper limit, so marks recovered beyond that limit are worth nothing at all. A pupil already near the Core ceiling has a marks-per-hour figure close to zero in that subject no matter how fixable their errors are, which is a strong argument for a tier conversation and a weak one for sessions.

The last thing it does is price a transferable repair properly. Reading analysis bought for English also raises History source marks, so the hours are divided across two subjects' gains and the figure roughly doubles. A practical-paper block divides across three sciences. Nothing else in this market offers that, and once the measure is on the page those pairings become obviously the first purchases rather than afterthoughts.

sections.heading: Subjects that share a repair
paragraphs: Four pairings exist in a standard IGCSE timetable where one purchase improves more than one subject, and they are the best value in the entire market. Families almost never exploit them, because tutoring is sold and bought subject by subject and nobody has an incentive to point out that one block covers three.

The first is reading analysis. The skill an English reading question rewards - selecting a short quotation, naming what is being done with it, stating an effect - is the same skill a History source question rewards under different labels: select, attribute, infer, evaluate. A pupil who installs it for English shows improvement in History within weeks without a single History session being bought. Geography extended answers benefit too.

The second is the examined practical component across the sciences. Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 all carry a practical or alternative-to-practical component worth around a fifth of the grade, and all three assess the same written skills: method with quantities and instruments stated, variables identified, scales read to precision, data tabulated and plotted, trends interpreted, specific improvements suggested. Six to eight sessions raises marks in three subjects at once.

The third is algebraic fluency, which is examined inside physics and chemistry questions as much as inside mathematics ones. Rearranging, substituting in non-standard units, giving sensible precision - a pupil weak in these loses marks in three subjects and the repair is one piece of work. The fourth is evaluation writing, which Economics, Business Studies, Geography and History all reward and which pupils who know their content routinely lose entirely.

sections.heading: The subjects to leave alone deliberately
paragraphs: A triage that funds two subjects implicitly leaves seven alone, and it is worth being explicit about which ones and why, because the alternative is a household that feels guilty about seven subjects for a year. Some subjects should be left alone because hours cannot deliver in them, and naming that is a service rather than a failure.

The clearest case is a set text that has not been read. Literature marks reward essay structure and quotation economy, both trainable, and text knowledge, which is the pupil's own reading work. No number of paid hours substitutes for reading the book, and a provider willing to summarise it has sold a shortcut that fails at the first unseen question. The honest instruction is that the pupil reads the text and the hours go elsewhere.

The second is content missing across a third of a specification in a short window. Chemistry is the usual example, because moles and organic chemistry carry a dependency chain, and a gap there found in the spring term of Year 11 is not a ten-week problem. The right response is to protect the subjects that can still move and, where it matters, consider whether the November series offers a contained retake route for that one subject.

The third is anything above a Core-tier ceiling, where recovered marks are worth nothing. The fourth is a subject the pupil is already comfortably meeting their target in, however much they enjoy the sessions. And the fifth is a subject where content volume rather than difficulty is the issue - biology at its most content-heavy - because a revision guide and a schedule do that job for nothing.

sections.heading: When the answer is the school rather than a tutor
paragraphs: Three outcomes of a triage point at the school and not at a purchase, and they are among the most valuable results the exercise produces. The first is a tier question. A pupil near a Core-tier ceiling has nothing to gain from sessions and a great deal to gain from a conversation about entry, backed by a timed Extended-tier script marked against the published scheme. That evidence is a document a head of department can read in five minutes.

The second is a set question. A pupil in a set that no longer reflects where they are is being taught at the wrong level, and in most departments there is a stated review point each term. Asking what triggers a review, and producing marked evidence before it, is free and can change a year's teaching. That is a better return than any single term of sessions.

The third is a feedback question. Where a triage shows a pupil losing marks to something specific - command terms, missing method, unlabelled answers - the subject teacher can often address it in class once it is named, and will usually be glad to be told. Asking what one thing the pupil should practise produces a precise brief from the best-informed person available, free of charge, and sometimes removes the need for a purchase entirely.

All three depend on timing, which is the part families get wrong. Evidence produced a full term before the decision it is meant to influence can change something. The same evidence produced after an entry has closed or a prediction has been fixed cannot. So the triage belongs in the autumn of Year 11 at the latest and ideally in Year 10, which is also when sessions are cheapest and specialist availability is loosest.

sections.heading: Re-running the triage, and when the answer changes
paragraphs: A triage is not a one-off. The ranking it produces is valid for the error pattern it was built from, and that pattern changes - which is the whole point of the work. A subject that scored highest because of a method problem drops down the list once the method problem is fixed, and the second-ranked subject becomes the right purchase. Re-running the exercise every term keeps the money aimed at the current gap rather than last term's.

Four events should trigger a re-run. A mock season, because it produces fresh marked scripts across every subject at once and is the single best moment for a whole-timetable ranking. A tier or entry decision, because a ceiling appearing or disappearing changes several scores. The completion of a syllabus, because content gaps that were unanswerable become answerable. And a target being met, because the subject should then leave the list.

The most common failure is the opposite: a ranking done once, in a crisis, and then never revisited, with the same two subjects funded for eighteen months by inertia. That is how an arrangement that began as a repair becomes a standing order. The second most common is adding a third and fourth subject when a new worry appears, without removing anything, which thins all four until none of them moves.

A practical rule holds both failures off. The list has two places. To add a subject, remove one. To extend a subject, show that its marks-per-hour score is still high. And to continue past a met target, demonstrate that a new target exists. Those three conditions take a conversation each term and they are the difference between a plan and a subscription.

sections.heading: What a per-subject evidence file contains
paragraphs: The triage needs material and the material is mostly free. For each subject under consideration, a family needs four things: a marked script, a note of which topics had been taught by its date, the specification code and tier on the entry, and one sentence from the subject teacher about what the pupil should practise. Nine subjects' worth of that is a morning's work and it is the foundation of every decision on this page.

The marked script matters more than the grade and that is worth repeating because the habit is strong. A grade compresses a term into a letter; a script shows which questions were abandoned, whether working was written, whether partial marks were earned, and where the margin annotations cluster. The marker has already done the diagnosis and it is written down where nobody collects it.

The topic list is what makes the script interpretable, and almost nobody asks for it. If a third of a specification had not been taught by the mock date, the questions on it were unanswerable rather than wrong, and striking them out of the lost-mark count changes a subject's score substantially. One email to each subject teacher produces it.

The teacher's sentence is the most underused free resource in the system. A subject teacher who sees a pupil several times a week usually has a precise answer to 'what is the one thing they should practise', and it is almost never 'work harder'. It is something like 'she writes explanations for describe questions' or 'he never writes the method when he can see the answer'. That sentence is a tutoring brief, and nine of them is a triage.

sections.heading: Honesty, coverage and the first session
paragraphs: A triage changes nothing about the rules. A tutor teaches, questions, models on a different example and marks the pupil's own work. A tutor does not write, co-write or edit any submitted piece, including coursework where a specification uses it. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, which is a malpractice trigger whose exposure falls on the candidate rather than the provider taking the fee.

Board material should not be handed over as files either. Cambridge, Pearson and the IB own their syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables, and the right behaviour is to link the official page. That matters for a triage in particular, because the comparison depends on past papers coming from the official source and a family that knows where they live can check the exercise themselves.

On coverage: mathematics, the sciences and the essay subjects at both Cambridge and Pearson tiers are well covered in this set, and a match is usually quick. Thinner briefs exist - Computer Science 0478 with pseudocode conventions, Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a first language, unusual literature text lists - and availability is part of the triage rather than an afterthought, because a subject nobody can staff scores low in practice however much is to be gained in it.

The first session is free, is one session, and requires no card details. The useful thing to bring is the per-subject file described above, or as much of it as exists: marked scripts, topic lists, specification codes, and whatever the subject teachers said. Within that hour it should be possible to produce a ranked list, two funded subjects, any shared repairs available, and the subjects to leave alone. If the honest answer is one subject rather than two, or none, that is said.

process.title: Build the per-subject file first
process.description: For each subject: a marked script, a note of which topics had been taught by its date, the specification code and tier from the examinations officer, and one sentence from the teacher about what the pupil should practise. Nine subjects' worth is a morning's work and almost all of it is free.

process.title: Score every subject against the same five questions
process.description: Procedural or content gap, marks at stake, whether a ceiling applies, whether the repair transfers, and whether a specialist is available. One to three on each, added and ranked. An instinct cannot be compared across nine subjects and a score can, which is the entire reason for writing it down.

process.title: Buy the shared repairs before the subject-specific ones
process.description: Reading analysis pays in English, History and Geography. The practical component pays in all three sciences. Algebraic fluency pays in mathematics, physics and chemistry. These are the only purchases that improve several subjects for the price of one, and they are rarely offered because nobody sells them that way.

process.title: Fund two subjects and name the ones you are leaving
process.description: Write down which seven subjects are deliberately not being tutored and why, so the household stops feeling guilty about them. An unread set text, a syllabus-wide content gap, anything above a Core-tier ceiling, and a subject already meeting its target all belong on that list with reasons.

process.title: Re-run the ranking each term, and swap rather than add
process.description: A mock season, a tier decision, a syllabus completing or a target being met should all trigger a re-run. The list has two places: to add a subject, remove one. That single rule is what keeps a repair from becoming a standing order funded by inertia for eighteen months.

whyPoints.title: A ranking, not an impression
whyPoints.description: Five questions applied to every subject from marked work, scored and ordered. The ranking is frequently uncomfortable, placing a subject nobody worried about in the top two and a subject everybody worried about near the bottom with a reason attached.

whyPoints.title: Marks per hour as the common scale
whyPoints.description: The only measure that puts nine subjects on one basis. It exposes the error families make - a bad grade often indicates a content gap, and content gaps are slow - and it prices a Core-tier ceiling correctly at close to zero.

whyPoints.title: Shared repairs identified
whyPoints.description: Reading analysis pays in English and History. The practical component pays in three sciences. Algebra pays in three subjects. Nothing else in this market improves several subjects for the price of one, and nobody sells it because tutoring is sold subject by subject.

whyPoints.title: Subjects left alone, with reasons
whyPoints.description: An unread set text, a syllabus-wide content gap in a short window, anything above a Core-tier ceiling, and a subject already on target. Naming these is a service, because the alternative is a household carrying guilt about seven subjects for a year.

whyPoints.title: Availability treated as part of the triage
whyPoints.description: A brief nobody can staff delivers nothing, so specialist availability is scored rather than assumed. Where a thin specification such as Computer Science 0478 or Additional Mathematics 0606 has nobody free, that is said before a plan is built on it.

whyPoints.title: Two places on the list, permanently
whyPoints.description: To add a subject, remove one. To extend a subject, show its score is still high. To continue past a met target, show a new target exists. Those three conditions are the difference between a plan and a subscription that runs for eighteen months.

faqs.question: With nine subjects, how should a Wesgreen International School family choose which to tutor?
faqs.answer: By marks per hour rather than by friction at home. Score every subject on five questions using its marked script: is the gap procedural or content, how many marks are at stake, does a grade ceiling apply, does the repair transfer to another subject, and is a specialist actually available. One to three on each, added and ranked. The exercise takes an hour with the scripts spread out, costs nothing, and usually places one subject nobody was worried about in the top two.

faqs.question: Why is the subject causing arguments at home usually the wrong choice?
faqs.answer: Because friction measures how unpleasant a subject is to live with rather than how many marks are available in it. The subject producing arguments is often the one where the pupil knows they are behind on content, and content gaps are exactly where hours deliver least in a short window. A pupil two marks below a boundary in a subject they tolerate has far more to gain per hour than one fifteen marks below in the subject they dread, who needs a different intervention anyway.

faqs.question: What does 'marks per hour' actually mean in practice?
faqs.answer: How many marks an hour of focused, well-aimed work could realistically recover in a subject, given the error pattern the script shows. A written-method problem might be worth two or three marks an hour for the first five hours, after which it becomes a habit and stops costing anything. A content gap spanning a third of a specification might be worth a fraction of a mark an hour. The estimates do not need to be precise, because the output is a ranking rather than a budget forecast.

faqs.question: Can one purchase improve more than one subject?
faqs.answer: Four of them can, and they are the best value in the market. Reading analysis bought for English also raises History source marks and Geography extended answers, because the underlying skill is identical. The examined practical component is common to Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, so six to eight sessions raises three subjects at once. Algebraic fluency pays in mathematics, physics and chemistry. And evaluation writing pays in Economics, Business Studies, Geography and History.

faqs.question: Should we fund a subject where our child is entered at Core tier?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and this is the clearest case where the right answer is the school rather than a purchase. A Core-tier entry in a Cambridge route caps the grade scale regardless of performance on the day, so marks recovered beyond that limit are worth nothing. A pupil already near the ceiling has a marks-per-hour figure close to zero whatever their errors are. What is worth doing is producing a timed Extended-tier script marked against the published scheme and taking it to the department before the entry closes.

faqs.question: Which subjects should we deliberately not tutor?
faqs.answer: Five categories. A set text the pupil has not read, because no hours substitute for reading the book and a provider willing to summarise it has sold a shortcut. Content missing across a third of a specification in a short window, chemistry being the usual example. Anything above a Core-tier ceiling. A subject already comfortably meeting its target, however enjoyable the sessions. And a subject where the issue is content volume rather than difficulty, which a revision guide and a schedule handle for nothing.

faqs.question: What should we ask each subject teacher?
faqs.answer: Four things, all factual. For the marked script rather than the grade. For a note of which topics had been taught by its date, so unanswerable questions can be struck out of the lost-mark count. For the specification code and tier from the examinations officer. And for one sentence on what the pupil should practise, which is almost never 'work harder' and is usually something precise like 'she writes explanations for describe questions'. Nine of those sentences is most of a triage.

faqs.question: Why does the topic list matter as much as the script?
faqs.answer: Because it decides whether a lost mark means anything. If a third of a specification had not been taught by the date of the assessment, the questions on it were unanswerable rather than answered wrongly, and leaving them in the count inflates a subject's apparent gap substantially. That single correction frequently moves a subject several places in the ranking, and it costs one email per subject. Families almost never ask for it, which is why so many triages are built on a distorted picture.

faqs.question: How often should the ranking be redone?
faqs.answer: Each term, and immediately after four specific events. A mock season, because it produces fresh marked scripts across every subject at once and is the best possible moment for a whole-timetable ranking. A tier or entry decision, because a ceiling appearing or disappearing changes several scores sharply. A syllabus completing, because content gaps become answerable. And a target being met, at which point the subject should leave the list rather than continue by inertia.

faqs.question: What if a new worry appears mid-term in a third subject?
faqs.answer: Swap, do not add. The list has two places, and funding four subjects thins all four until none of them moves measurably - which is the second most common way a tutoring budget produces nothing. To add a subject, remove one, and justify the removal from its score. That rule feels harsh in the moment and it is what preserves the thing that makes the plan work, which is that two subjects are being worked on properly rather than four being touched.

faqs.question: Is group tuition a way to cover more subjects on the same budget?
faqs.answer: For content coverage, yes, and Sharjah's tuition-centre market is comparatively well developed. Group rates run around AED 100 to 150 per pupil against AED 200 to 450 for one-to-one specialist work, so the arithmetic is real. What a group cannot do is diagnose: a session pitched to several pupils addresses the average gap rather than your child's specific pattern of lost marks. A sensible hybrid is group coverage where the triage says content, plus a few one-to-one diagnostic hours.

faqs.question: Does a subject nobody is available for still belong in the ranking?
faqs.answer: It belongs with a low practical score, because a brief nobody can staff delivers nothing however much is to be gained in it. Computer Science 0478 with Cambridge pseudocode conventions, Additional Mathematics 0606, Arabic as a first language and unusual literature text lists all have thin specialist pools. Ask about availability before building a plan around a subject rather than after, because discovering it in week three costs weeks the window may not have.

faqs.question: Do you send tutors to Al Ramtha, Muwaileh or Abu Shagara?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family's address is a service offered only in India. Tutoring for Sharjah families is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For a two-subject plan that matters in the household schedule as much as the budget: two sessions a week is sustainable without journeys and frequently is not with them, and the triage itself is a shared-screen exercise working through scripts.

faqs.question: What should we bring to the first session to get a ranking?
faqs.answer: As much of the per-subject file as exists: a marked script from each subject, a note of which topics had been taught by its date, the specification codes and tiers, and whatever each subject teacher said about what to practise. Within an hour that produces a ranked list, two funded subjects, any shared repairs worth buying first, and an explicit list of subjects to leave alone with reasons. If the honest answer is one subject rather than two, or none, that is said.

intro.heading: Start at the bottom of the ladder, not the top
paragraphs: Al Juraina families are not short of tutoring options. Central Sharjah has tuition centres, independent tutors, agency lists and a long word-of-mouth network, and the quotes range from about AED 45 an hour to more than AED 650. What is missing is a way to decide which rung of that ladder a particular child actually needs.

The default behaviour is to jump straight to the most expensive thing the household can afford, on the reasonable theory that a problem with a child's education deserves the best available. The outcome is often disappointing, not because the tutor was poor but because the problem on the table did not need that tutor. A student who has not been doing past papers does not need a premium specialist; they need past papers and somebody to mark them honestly.

So this page is organised as a ladder, cheapest first. At the bottom are things that cost nothing and that most families never request: the marked mock script, the department's view of weak topics, the published syllabus document, the school's own revision sessions. Above that, peer study and group classes. Then budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour. Then a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300. Then in-home at AED 180 to 500, where the premium is travel. At the top, branded tutoring at AED 500 to 650 and above.

The method is to climb only when the rung below has demonstrably failed or cannot address the problem. Some problems skip rungs legitimately: an IB internal assessment needs somebody who knows the criteria, and no amount of group revision substitutes. Exam technique in a higher level subject is similar. Knowing which problems those are is most of what this page is for.

Our own position on the ladder is the qualified-specialist rung, delivered online, which is the step most families should reach and the one many skip past in both directions. We publish the market bands with their source and the month they were read so that any quote - ours included - can be measured. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India, so no travel sits inside our rate.

A note on why the ladder is worth following in order even when a household can afford to skip it. Spending at the top rung on a problem the bottom rung would have solved teaches a student that the solution comes from outside, which is the opposite of what the Diploma rewards. The cheapest rungs - the marked script, the published criteria, timed practice - are also the ones that build independence, and that is worth more over two years than any hourly rate.

The sections below work through the rungs, then deal with splitting one budget across two systems, the small print that quietly costs money, and the handful of things that are a bad purchase at any price.

sections.heading: Rung one: what the school already owes you, for nothing
paragraphs: Before any money is spent, there is a set of things your child's school holds that most families never request. All of them are free, all of them are reasonable to ask for, and together they frequently change what needs buying.

The marked mock script comes first. A grade tells you there is a problem; the script tells you which problem. Some schools keep papers for departmental review and return only the mark, in which case a polite request usually produces the paper or a photograph. Without it, every subsequent decision is a guess, including the decision about how much to spend.

Then the department's view. A head of subject can usually say in two sentences which topics a particular student is weak on and whether their tier or level is appropriate. For an IB student, the coordinator can supply the internal deadline calendar - submission dates per subject, extended essay checkpoints, the Theory of Knowledge deadline - which is the single most useful planning document in the programme and is almost never requested.

Finally, the published material. The syllabus document for your child's course is issued by the school and is the authoritative version. Past papers and mark schemes are available through the school. Many schools also run their own revision sessions before a series, free, and attendance is often patchy because nobody at home knew they existed. Ask. It costs an email and sometimes removes the need for a purchase entirely.

sections.heading: The ladder, with prices
paragraphs: Having exhausted the free rung, the paid options form a reasonably clear sequence. The prices below are market figures from published UAE rate cards and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table, read in October 2026 - not our price list.

Peer study and group classes come next. A tuition centre class is the cheapest paid content teaching available per student, and it is the right purchase when a cohort shares a weakness. What it cannot do is keep an individual error log or review one student's script, which is why group revision courses before a series often feel busy and change little.

Budget online tutoring starts around AED 45 an hour. For homework supervision, routine-building and working through practice questions, a capable undergraduate is genuinely sufficient, and many hold the MoHRE private tuition permit the law requires. What this band rarely includes is someone who has taught a specific course to final-grade standard.

One caution about the budget rung: the tutor may change between sessions on some platforms, which quietly removes most of the value. Continuity is what lets anybody see a pattern in a student's errors, so if the person is different each week, you are buying supervision rather than teaching, and you should price it accordingly.

The qualified specialist rung, AED 150 to 300 an hour online, is where course experience becomes reliable: marking to published schemes or criteria, naming the three things costing marks, and triaging a final block. Above it, in-home at AED 180 to 500 adds travel, and branded tutoring at AED 500 to 650 and above adds reputation plus an examiner claim that is rarely evidenced. Climb only when the rung below cannot do the job in front of you.

sections.heading: When budget tutoring is genuinely enough
paragraphs: It is worth being specific about this, because most pages in this market have an interest in implying that cheap help is always a false economy. It is not.

A capable undergraduate at AED 45 to 150 an hour can supervise homework reliably, keep a routine for a student who will not work alone, work through practice questions a teacher has selected, and explain content that was taught badly or missed through absence. For a Year 9 student, or for a Middle Years child who needs company and structure rather than expertise, that is often the correct purchase - and buying a specialist instead is overpaying for capability that is not being used.

Where the band fails is anything that requires knowing the assessment. An internal assessment marked against criteria by letter. The decision about which topics to abandon in a ten-week block. The precise language the extended chemistry paper rewards. The alternative-to-practical technique. In each of those, a well-meaning generalist teaches the wrong thing competently, and the family discovers it from the next mock rather than from the tutor.

There is a hybrid worth considering. A single specialist diagnostic session produces a list of specific weaknesses and a set of practice tasks; a budget tutor can then supervise the work through them. That combination costs far less than a term of specialist hours and works well for a student whose problem is partly discipline and partly direction.

A useful test before buying at this band: write down what you expect to be different in six weeks. If the answer is 'the homework gets done and they feel less anxious', the budget rung is appropriate. If it is 'the Paper 4 mark improves' or 'criterion C is no longer the weakest', it is not.

sections.heading: Where the specialist rung becomes unavoidable
paragraphs: Some problems cannot be solved from a lower rung, however disciplined the family is. Recognising them early saves money, because the usual pattern is to spend a term at the wrong rung first.

The clearest case is criterion-based assessed work. An IB internal assessment, an extended essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay is marked against published descriptors, and help is only useful if the person giving it has read them. A generalist will improve the writing and leave the criterion unaddressed, which is the most expensive kind of near-miss: effort spent, marks unchanged.

The second is higher level subject technique. At higher level, the gap between knowing the content and scoring on the paper is widest, and closing it requires somebody who has marked those papers. The third is triage under time pressure: deciding, eight weeks out, which topics to abandon is a judgement that needs course experience, and getting it wrong wastes the whole block.

The fourth is the narrow subject nobody local teaches. Additional Mathematics 0606, computer science with its pseudocode conventions, a higher level language - for these, the local market around Al Juraina offers very little at any price, and matching nationally over video is not a preference but the only way the request gets filled at all.

In each of these four cases, the cost of being at the wrong rung is not just the fee. It is the term spent discovering the mismatch, usually confirmed by the next mock or the returned draft, at a point in the year when there is no spare time to start again. That is the real argument for recognising them early.

sections.heading: One budget, two systems: how to split it
paragraphs: A household with an IB student and an IGCSE candidate has one budget and two different optimal spending patterns, which is where most allocation errors come from.

The IB child needs hours earlier and spread, because internal assessments and core components cannot be rescued late and because a content gap closed in DP1 costs a fraction of the same gap closed in DP2. The IGCSE candidate needs hours later and concentrated, because the grade is made in the examination room and a dense block of timed papers before the series has the clearest relationship to marks of anything available.

Splitting equally therefore produces two suboptimal plans. A more effective allocation gives the IB child a modest continuous presence - fortnightly, plus short core-component check-ins - and the IGCSE candidate a light touch through the year with a concentrated block at the end. At the middle of the qualified online band, that shape typically costs less than two weekly arrangements and does more.

Timing within the year matters as much as the split. If both children need hours in the same eight weeks, book the scarcer specialist first - usually the Diploma subject teacher - because the British-track request is easier to fill at short notice. Leaving both to the peak means competing for the same narrow supply with every other family in central Sharjah.

One further point about fairness. Children notice allocation, and a younger sibling who sees their brother getting twice the hours draws conclusions. Explaining the reasoning - that their own hours will come later, concentrated, for the same reason - removes most of that. It is a small conversation that prevents a persistent resentment.

sections.heading: The small print that quietly costs money
paragraphs: Once a rate is agreed, several commercial details decide whether the arrangement is good value in practice. All of them are easier to raise before any money moves.

Ask whether the quoted figure includes VAT, and for a registration number if a provider says it is registered. We will not state how UAE tax treats tuition fees on this page, because that belongs to the Federal Tax Authority rather than to a tutoring site; what a parent can expect is clarity about whether the number quoted is the number payable.

Then the mechanics. Is the rate per hour or per lesson, and how long is a lesson? A sixty-minute hour and a forty-five-minute lesson at the same price are different products. What notice does a cancellation require, and what happens to unused sessions in a package? If a package is discounted, what is the position if you want to reduce frequency mid-term? Packages are a reasonable way to buy and a poor way to stay flexible.

Finally, who teaches and what is recorded. Will the tutor change between sessions? What happens if the match is wrong - a provider with a pool can replace and carry the plan across, while an individual arrangement means starting again. And is there a written target list and a note after each session? Without those, renewal happens on impression rather than on evidence, which in this market usually means on how likeable the tutor was.

sections.heading: The four things worth nothing at any price
paragraphs: Some purchases in this market are bad at AED 45 and worse at AED 650, because the problem is not the price.

A grade guarantee. Nobody can know what a particular candidate will score, so a promised 7, a points total or a specific improvement is a sales instrument. Where a refund is attached, read the trigger conditions - in practice they are usually unreachable. We do not offer guarantees of any kind.

Completed assessed work. Services selling finished internal assessments, extended essays, Theory of Knowledge essays and coursework appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams. The malpractice finding lands on the student's diploma, not on the seller's accounts. A tutor may teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work, and nothing beyond that. IB Gram sells no completed work.

Reproduced board material sold as an exclusive resource. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and your child's school is the proper route to the current versions. A drive full of 'exclusive' material is somebody else's copyright, and where the material is unreleased it is a malpractice question attached to your child.

Claimed regulator approval, and self-asserted ratings. No tutoring service should describe itself as approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge unless it holds that specific permit and can produce the number. For clarity about us: IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no UAE premises and no approval or accreditation from any education authority in this country. And a star rating with no countable, dated reviews behind it is decoration, not evidence.

sections.heading: Climbing down: when to stop paying
paragraphs: Almost no page in this market discusses ending an arrangement, which is strange, because knowing when to stop is as valuable as knowing when to start and considerably cheaper.

The simplest signal is the target. If the arrangement began to fix a named weakness - electrolysis, directed writing, criterion C - and that weakness no longer shows in timed work, the arrangement has done its job. Continuing is buying reassurance, which is a legitimate purchase if it is a conscious one and a waste if it is a drift.

The second signal is substitution. If a student has stopped working independently because a tutor will cover it on Tuesday, the hours are displacing the thing that actually produces marks. A good tutor notices this and reduces frequency; a provider paid by the hour has no incentive to mention it. Ask the tutor directly whether the student is doing enough alone.

A fourth signal is seasonal rather than individual. If a block was bought for a dated assessment and the assessment has passed, the arrangement should end by default and be restarted deliberately if needed. Rolling straight on is how a ten-week block becomes a two-year subscription that nobody chose.

The third is the review point. We check at six sessions on timed scores and criterion feedback, and we are willing to say that a target has been met or that a different shape would work better - fortnightly instead of weekly, a weekend morning instead of two tired evenings, or nothing for a term. A provider who has never recommended stopping is not reviewing anything, and that is worth noticing wherever you buy.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest thing that might fix my child's grade?
faqs.answer: Usually something free that nobody has asked for. The marked mock script tells you which problem you have rather than that you have one. The head of department can name the weak topics and say whether the tier or level is right. For an IB student, the coordinator's internal deadline calendar is the most useful planning document in the programme. Many schools also run free revision sessions before a series that families never hear about. Exhaust those before paying anybody, including us.

faqs.question: Is a university-student tutor at AED 45 to 150 an hour a false economy?
faqs.answer: Not always, and it is worth being specific. A capable undergraduate can supervise homework, hold a routine, work through practice questions and re-explain content missed through absence - and many hold the MoHRE private tuition permit the law requires. That band fails at anything requiring knowledge of the assessment: criterion-marked internal assessments, higher level technique, deciding what to abandon in a final block. Write down what you expect to be different in six weeks, and the right rung becomes obvious.

faqs.question: When does a specialist stop being optional for an IB student?
faqs.answer: At the internal assessment, and at higher level paper technique. Assessed work is marked against published criteria by letter, and help is only useful from somebody who has read them - a generalist improves the prose and leaves the criterion unaddressed, which costs effort and changes nothing. Higher level subjects have the widest gap between knowing content and scoring on the paper. Add triage in a final block, which is a judgement that needs course experience, and narrow subjects nobody local teaches.

faqs.question: How should we split one tutoring budget between two children on different systems?
faqs.answer: Not equally, because the systems need hours at different times. The IB child needs them earlier and spread, since internal assessments and core components cannot be rescued late and a DP1 gap costs a fraction of a DP2 one. The IGCSE candidate needs them later and concentrated, because the grade is made in the examination room. At the middle of the qualified online band, around thirty spread hours plus check-ins for the IB child and twenty-two concentrated hours for the other costs about AED 10,400 a year - less than two weekly arrangements.

faqs.question: Are group revision courses before exams worth the money?
faqs.answer: For a shared content weakness, yes, and they are the cheapest paid teaching per student. For an individual problem, no: a group cannot keep one student's error log, review the script they wrote, or decide that this candidate should skip a topic and drill another. That is why group courses before a series often feel busy and change little - the student who needed three sessions on one topic sat through six hours covering everything. Match the purchase to whether the problem is shared or individual.

faqs.question: What is the smallest sensible amount of specialist tutoring to buy?
faqs.answer: A single diagnostic session, which produces a marked script, a named list of what is costing marks and a written view of what the remaining weeks can change. Some families act on that themselves and buy nothing further, which is a legitimate outcome. After that, a two-to-four session repair block on one named weakness, with a diagnostic question set before the first session and an explicit end, is the cheapest way to buy real expertise without committing to a term.

faqs.question: Does the in-home premium ever make sense for a family here?
faqs.answer: Yes, for one group: younger children who need an adult beside them to stay on task, where presence is the thing being bought rather than expertise. For a Year 11 candidate or a Diploma student working through papers, the premium - roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 online - buys a journey along the Maliha Road and nothing academic. We do not offer UAE home visits in any case, so if presence is your real problem we are not the right provider.

faqs.question: What should I ask about packages before paying for one?
faqs.answer: Four things. Whether the quoted figure includes VAT, and a registration number if the provider claims to be registered. Whether the rate is per hour or per lesson, and how long a lesson is - forty-five minutes at an hourly price is a price rise. What notice a cancellation needs, applied in both directions. And what happens to unused sessions, and whether you can reduce frequency mid-term. Packages are a reasonable way to buy and a poor way to stay flexible.

faqs.question: What tells us an arrangement has done its job and should end?
faqs.answer: When the named target no longer shows up in timed work, the arrangement has done its job - continuing is buying reassurance, which is fine if it is a decision and wasteful if it is drift. Watch also for substitution: if your child has stopped working alone because a tutor will cover it on Tuesday, the hours are displacing the activity that produces marks. We review at six sessions and will say that a target is met or that frequency should drop.

faqs.question: Is a branded or examiner-led tutor worth AED 500 an hour or more?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the claim is the part to interrogate. Examiner status is seldom evidenced, cannot be relied upon to be current, and gives no access to marking, boundaries or paper content - the mark scheme a good tutor works from is published. What the premium reliably buys is scarcity and reputation. If a tutor at AED 200 an hour can name the three things costing your child marks from a script, the additional AED 300 is buying something other than that diagnosis.

faqs.question: Can a tutor finish an internal assessment if we pay enough?
faqs.answer: No, at any price, and a service that offers to is selling your child a malpractice risk. Permitted help is substantial: reading the criteria together, narrowing a research question so the available data can answer it, teaching the method or statistics required, and explaining which criterion a draft fails. Writing, redrafting or editing the submitted text is not permitted, and IB Gram does not sell completed work. The consequence attaches to the student's diploma rather than to the seller.

faqs.question: Why do so few tutoring sites in the UAE publish prices?
faqs.answer: Because publishing invites comparison, and comparison is awkward when the premium in a model is travel or branding rather than teaching. In our competitor research, three of the six best-ranked pages published no figure at all, two of the remaining ones quoted in US dollars - a currency UAE families do not transact in - and one asked the price in its own FAQ and declined to answer it. We publish market bands with their source and month so any quote, ours included, can be measured against something.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working in Al Juraina need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tutor work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published - so disregard any amount quoted at you.

faqs.question: Which exam series will each of my children sit?
faqs.answer: For the British track, Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates - the February/March series is offered in India only - and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with November results reaching students in January. For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session, but we publish no IB dates here because we could not verify them from the IB itself; your school's coordinator holds the confirmed dates. Use the zone timetable your exams officer issues for Cambridge papers.

intro.heading: Scarcity, not distance, sets the price
paragraphs: Al Khan occupies the lagoon strip between Al Majaz and Al Taawun, with schools in two emirates within reach and the Dubai boundary a short drive west. Families searching from here for a tutor near me are usually trying to solve two problems at once: find somebody reachable, and find somebody affordable. The uncomfortable fact is that in this market those two goals work against each other, and the mechanism is scarcity rather than geography.

Here is how it works. Common requests are cheap because supply is deep: IGCSE mathematics at either tier, Standard Level biology, English Language technique. Rare requests are expensive because supply is thin: Diploma Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, Higher Level Chemistry and Physics, minority languages, and anything at a specific hour on a specific day. Narrowing a search by distance as well as by subject multiplies the scarcity, and the price and the waiting time both rise.

The published market gives the bands. Entry-level online sessions are advertised from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour. Qualified online subject tutors publish from about AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at around AED 270 and premium named provision advertised as high as AED 650. In-home visits including travel run from roughly AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table placing the usual band at AED 180 to 350.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. That removes one source of scarcity entirely — the pool of people prepared to cross into Sharjah at five in the afternoon — and replaces it with the much larger pool of people who teach the relevant course at that hour, wherever they are.

Which brings this page to its real subject: disclosure. The thing a family cannot see when buying tutoring is whether a match actually exists. A provider under pressure to fill a booking can place the nearest available person into a scarce subject, and the family discovers the mismatch in week three. The fee is recoverable and the term is not, which makes concealment the most expensive practice in this market.

So what follows is an availability table rather than a sales argument, a straight account of what the scarcity premium buys, the real cost of a mismatched placement, and the one lever a family controls that genuinely lowers both the rate and the wait. None of that is flattering to this industry, and all of it is checkable in a few minutes by any parent who knows what to look at.

sections.heading: Why "near me" and "affordable" pull against each other
paragraphs: An IB IGCSE tutor near me, searched from Al Khan, is a request that contains a hidden constraint. Every filter a family adds narrows the pool: the subject, the level, the component, the hour, and then the geography. A family asking for Higher Level Chemistry at half past four within driving distance of the lagoon has applied five filters at once, and the intersection may be empty or may contain one person who can charge what they like.

IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For a family whose requirement is a person in the room, in-home provision exists in this market at published rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, and we are not the provider for it.

Dropping the geographic filter changes the arithmetic rather than the quality. The same subject, the same level, the same component, at a wider range of hours, from everybody who teaches it in the region rather than those willing to drive here at the worst time of day. That is why online rates for qualified subject tutors sit around AED 150 to 300 an hour while in-home rates including travel start higher: the pool is larger and nobody is being paid to sit in traffic.

What does not change, and should not be pretended away, is scarcity at the level of the component itself. There is no arrangement under which Higher Level Chemistry specialists become plentiful. What online delivery does is give a family in these towers the same access to that scarce pool as a family anywhere else, which is the most that can honestly be offered.

sections.heading: Availability and the fallback, disclosed
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit. Several conceal non-local delivery behind a foreign phone number, and one routes families in this country to an international contact without saying where anybody is. The table below is the opposite practice: an honest statement of where supply is deep, where it is thin, and what happens when a match does not exist at the hour a family wants.

The principle behind it is simple. A family is entitled to know, before a trial lesson rather than after, whether the person teaching their child specialises in the component, roughly how long a match will take, and where that person is based. We state tutor location up front because concealing it is a trust failure, and because a Diploma family in the second year needs to know whether their timetable can actually be served.

The fallback matters as much as the availability. Where no specialist is free at a requested hour, there are three honest options: a different time with the right person, which is usually correct; a wait with a date attached; or a tutor based outside the UAE with their location and working hours disclosed in advance. What is not an option is placing somebody who does not teach the component, however convenient that would be for everybody except the student.

One further note on rates in a fallback. Where a scarce subject is matched outside the usual pool, the rate reflects the specialism rather than the location, and it is quoted before the trial rather than discovered afterwards. A family should never learn a price after a child has started working with somebody.

sections.heading: What the scarcity premium actually buys
paragraphs: A premium only deserves to be paid if it buys something nameable, so here is what it buys and what it does not. In a scarce Higher Level subject, the specialist rate from AED 200 to AED 450 and above buys somebody who has taught that syllabus and marked that component: who knows the criteria by letter, the mark allocations, the band boundaries and the specific places students lose marks in that paper.

What it does not buy is a different grade by itself. The relationship that holds in this market is between accuracy of diagnosis and outcome, not between price and outcome. A cheap, correctly targeted three sessions beats an expensive term aimed at the wrong thing, which is why every recommendation on this site starts with marked work rather than with a rate card.

The premium also should not be taken as implying access to anything. Premium named provision in this market has been advertised as high as AED 650 an hour, sometimes on the strength of examiner status. Examiner status for an individual is difficult for a parent to verify, and it must never be used to suggest access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. We do not describe tutors as examiners without current evidence, and a family paying a premium is entitled to ask precisely what distinguishes that hour from one at half the price.

The honest summary is narrow. Pay the specialist rate where the marked work shows a criteria or mark-scheme problem at a level where supply is thin. Pay the qualified rate where the problem is content in a well-supplied subject. Pay the entry-level rate where the problem is organisation. Each of those is a defensible purchase; paying the top rate for the third is not.

sections.heading: The cost of a mismatched placement
paragraphs: This is the figure the market never publishes, and it is the largest cost available in it. A mismatched placement — a subject generalist in a Higher Level component, or a tutor working to the wrong board's specification — costs a family the fee and the term, and the term is the expensive half.

The pattern is recognisable. Weeks one and two feel fine, because any competent teacher can run two pleasant sessions. By week three the student is being taught content rather than having a component diagnosed. By week five a parent senses something is wrong but has no vocabulary for it. By week eight an internal deadline has passed or a mock has been sat, and the weeks are gone. A refund, if one is offered, returns the fee and nothing else.

In the second Diploma year that is close to irrecoverable, because internal deadlines do not reopen. In Year 11 it is survivable but expensive, since the weeks between a mock and study leave are the only ones in which technique work pays. In both cases the damage was done at the placement stage, by a decision made to fill a booking.

The protections are cheap and worth insisting on. Ask whether the tutor has marked the specific component, and expect criteria and mark allocations in the answer. Insist that the trial lesson runs on your child's own marked work. Ask where the tutor is based. And ask what happens if the match is wrong, because a provider with no rematch mechanism is asking you to carry the risk of their matching decision.
bullets: A mismatch costs the fee and the term; the term is the expensive part

sections.heading: Timing flexibility is the only real discount
paragraphs: Families look for discounts in package deals and rarely find one worth having. The genuine lever in this market is the hour, and it is free to use. Between four and six in the afternoon every tutor, tuition centre and after-school activity in the northern emirates competes for the same window, and the narrower the window a family offers, the smaller the pool and the higher the effective price.

Widening it does two things at once. It increases the number of specialists who could take the booking, which for a scarce Higher Level subject can be the difference between a match and no match. And it moves the rate towards the lower end of the relevant band, because availability and price move together.

For a household in Al Khan there is a quality argument as well. A student who has crossed the boundary from a Dubai school is rarely at their best at half past four. The same student on a weekend morning is a different learner, and the hardest material belongs there. Families who move a Higher Level subject to the weekend almost never move it back, and they usually pay less for it.

sections.heading: What concealment looks like in this market
paragraphs: A page about disclosure should describe the alternative, because the practices are specific and a parent can spot them. They were found repeatedly in the competitor set behind this page, and none of them is illegal — they are simply ways of not answering the question a family is asking.

The first is a contact route that reveals the delivery model by accident. Two pages competing for these searches route families in this country to foreign phone numbers, and one shows an address in a different emirate from the one the page targets. Neither states where the teaching happens. The second is pricing in a currency families do not transact in: two of the strongest pages quote United States dollars at parents who pay in dirhams, which makes comparison difficult and looks accidental.

The third is pricing silence. Three of the six strongest pages in this cluster publish no price at all, and one publishes an hourly figure in its visible copy that contradicts the figure in its own structured data. The fourth is self-asserted social proof: ratings and review counts with no number, date or method behind them, and in one case two different figures on the same page.

The fifth, and the one that should end a conversation, is a provider offering to produce assessed work. One in this region advertises completed Internal Assessments for sale. That is academic malpractice, the student carries the consequence, and no price makes it a reasonable purchase. A family can check for all five of these in about five minutes, and doing so is a better use of time than comparing adjectives.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Three facts hold regardless of which provider a family chooses, and they are stated here because parts of this market imply otherwise.

The permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so a page quoting an amount has invented it. The code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

The regulator. Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai's answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to the Department of Education and Knowledge, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. No tutoring provider, including IB Gram, holds approval, accreditation or a licence from any of them.

The coursework boundary. A tutor teaches the skill a component assesses, explains the published criteria and their command words, tests whether a topic can carry the work, questions the student's reasoning and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor does not write, complete or rewrite any part of it. We also publish no IB examination or results dates, because the board's own site cannot be verified by automated checking, and we do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables.

faqs.question: Why does a Higher Level subject cost more than an IGCSE one in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Supply, not delivery cost. Higher Level Chemistry and Physics, and the extended-problem paper in either Diploma mathematics route, are thinly staffed across the whole region, so a request for one at a specific hour may contain very few available people. IGCSE mathematics and the sciences at qualified level have deep pools, which is why published rates sit lower and match times are shorter. The premium reflects scarcity of the specialism rather than the difficulty of teaching it.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free at the hour we need?
faqs.answer: You get three options stated plainly rather than a vague promise. A different time with the right specialist, which is usually the correct answer and often costs less. A wait with an actual date attached, if the subject is genuinely scarce. Or a tutor based outside the UAE, with their location and working hours disclosed before the trial lesson rather than discovered afterwards. What we will not do is place somebody who does not teach the component in order to fill the slot.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an apartment in Al Khan?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time. If a person in the room is your requirement, in-home provision exists in this market from others at published rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, and we would rather say so than waste your trial lesson on a model that does not match what you want.

faqs.question: How much does a mismatched tutor actually cost us?
faqs.answer: The fee and the term, and the term is the expensive half. The pattern is predictable: two pleasant sessions, then content being explained rather than a component diagnosed, then a parent sensing something is wrong without the vocabulary for it, then an internal deadline or a mock arriving with the weeks gone. A refund returns the money and nothing else. In the second Diploma year it is close to irrecoverable, because internal deadlines do not reopen.

faqs.question: Can we lower the rate by changing the time of the session?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the only discount in this market worth chasing. Between four and six in the afternoon every provider in the northern emirates competes for the same window, so a narrow request means a small pool and a rate at the top of the band. Offering a later evening or a weekend morning widens the pool, moves the rate towards the lower end and shortens the wait. For a scarce Higher Level subject it can be the difference between a match existing and not.

faqs.question: What exactly does a specialist rate buy that a qualified rate does not?
faqs.answer: Component knowledge. At specialist rates from AED 200 to AED 450 and above you are paying for somebody who has marked the thing your child is being assessed on: the criteria by letter, the mark allocations, the band boundaries and the specific losses that recur in that paper. At qualified rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 you are paying for solid subject teaching, which is often enough at Standard Level or for a content gap. Match the tier to what the marked work shows.

faqs.question: Should we pay a premium for a tutor described as an examiner?
faqs.answer: Only with evidence and a clear answer about what it buys. Premium provision in this market has been advertised as high as AED 650 an hour partly on examiner status, which a parent cannot easily verify and which must never imply access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. We do not describe tutors as examiners without current evidence. If you are offered that premium, ask what distinguishes the hour from a specialist at half the rate and expect specifics rather than reassurance.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether a provider is concealing where teaching happens?
faqs.answer: Check the contact route and the currency. Two pages competing for these searches route families in this country to foreign phone numbers and never state where the teaching takes place; one shows an address in a different emirate from the one the page targets. Two quote United States dollars at parents who pay in dirhams. Three publish no price at all and one contradicts its own structured data. All five checks take about five minutes and tell you more than any list of adjectives.

faqs.question: Is a wait with a date better than taking whoever is available now?
faqs.answer: In a scarce subject, almost always. Families who accept a dated wait rarely regret it; families who accept a near-match in a Higher Level component frequently do, because the cost appears three weeks later as a term rather than immediately as a fee. The sensible interim is free school support: the marked script, the subject teacher's priority topics, and any departmental revision clinic, which is often under-attended simply because nobody mentions it.

faqs.question: Which subjects are genuinely hardest to match near this district?
faqs.answer: Computer Science and minority languages are the thinnest, followed by Diploma Higher Level Chemistry and Physics and the extended-problem paper in either mathematics route. Cambridge practical-skills paper work sits in the middle. IGCSE mathematics and the sciences at qualified level are the easiest matches in the market. Where a combination genuinely cannot be served at any hour you can use, we say so at the first conversation rather than offering a near-match and hoping.

faqs.question: Does the price change if the tutor is based outside the UAE?
faqs.answer: The rate reflects the specialism rather than the location, and it is quoted before the trial lesson rather than after. What changes with a non-UAE tutor is the working-hours overlap, which we disclose up front so a family can judge whether their timetable can actually be served. Nobody should learn either a price or a tutor's location after a child has started working with them; both belong in the first conversation.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with students in Al Khan need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and its code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

faqs.question: What should we ask before a trial lesson rather than after?
faqs.answer: Four things. Has the tutor marked this specific component, and what are its criteria and mark allocations? Where is the tutor based and what hours do they work? What is the rate, including if this is a scarce subject matched outside the usual pool? And what happens if the match is wrong? A provider with no rematch mechanism is asking you to carry the risk of their matching decision, which in a scarce Higher Level subject is measured in weeks.

faqs.answer: Where the problem is organisation rather than assessment, yes. A student who needs company and structure to finish homework is well served at entry-level rates advertised from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, and paying a specialist for that is waste. Where the marked work shows a criteria or mark-scheme problem, a near-match is not cheap at any price, because it consumes the weeks in which the right person could have fixed it. The marked script decides which situation you are in.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-maj.tutorsIntro: Profiles below are grouped by programme rather than by subject family, because the comparison that matters most is between systems. A Diploma Higher Level teacher and an IGCSE Extended teacher are doing different jobs against different mark schemes.

intro.heading: The comparisons a search result cannot make for you
paragraphs: Al Majaz occupies the stretch of Sharjah along the Khalid Lagoon, minutes from the Dubai boundary and within sight of it from the upper floors. Families here have an unusually wide menu: schools in two emirates, tuition centres along the corniche, agencies advertising across the border, freelance tutors circulating by word of mouth, and online platforms from three continents. That abundance is the problem. A search result ranks providers; it does not compare the things a parent is actually choosing between.

Four comparisons matter. The first is between the systems themselves, because a household with one child on IGCSE and another in the Diploma is dealing with two different kinds of assessment and should not expect one tutor or one plan to serve both. The second is between provider models, which differ far more in what they can diagnose than in what they charge. The third is between the Sharjah and Dubai tutor markets, which is mostly a question about what the boundary does to availability and price. And the fourth is between two trial lessons, which is where most families make the actual decision on the least useful evidence.

This page answers all four, including where the honest answer reflects badly on an option we offer. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. If a family's requirement is a person physically in the room, that is a legitimate requirement and we are not the answer to it. Saying so costs nothing and saves everybody a wasted trial.

What online delivery does buy on this corridor is substantial and worth stating plainly. The tutor is chosen by programme, course and component rather than by driving distance, which matters most for scarce Higher Level subjects. The session is decoupled from a boundary crossing at the worst hour of the afternoon. And two children on two school calendars can be taught consecutively on one evening without anybody getting into a car.

The fifth comparison, which families rarely run, is between buying something now and buying something later. Support bought in the autumn of Year 10 or the spring of the first Diploma year costs less and achieves more than the same spend in the spring of an examination year. That is a comparison across time rather than across providers, and it is the one with the largest effect on the eventual bill.

Everything below is written to be checkable. Rates carry the name of whoever published them and the month they were read. Regulatory facts carry the authority that states them. And where a figure has not been verified — an International Baccalaureate examination date, for instance — nothing is published rather than something plausible.
