sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-maj.programmesIntro: The four stages below are the ones a Sharjah household compares between, usually while managing two of them at once.

programmes.name: IGCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, a fixed specification per subject, no coursework on most mainstream boards, and a grade decided entirely by written papers. The tier on the entry caps the available grade. Because everything is recoverable by practice and technique, this is the system where a short, well-aimed block produces the most visible change.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah families frequently have children at schools in two emirates, which can mean two examination boards in one household. Cambridge and Pearson specifications differ on tiering and calculator rules, so the syllabus code has to be confirmed per child rather than assumed per family.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessment sits inside every subject, and up to three points come from the core. The binding constraint is time rather than ability, which makes sequencing the main skill.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma places near the Sharjah lagoon are fewer than British-curriculum places, so a number of Diploma students here cross the boundary daily. That commute shortens the usable evening and is the single most common reason a weekly plan fails in this neighbourhood.

programmes.name: Year 11 into the first Diploma year
programmes.description: The handover families most often underestimate. Strong IGCSE grades do not guarantee a comfortable first Diploma year, because the Diploma asks for independent reading, extended writing and sustained coursework rather than examination recall. Four to six sessions across the summer removes most of the autumn shock.
programmes.countryNote: In this part of Sharjah the transition frequently involves a change of school and sometimes a change of emirate, which means the receiving school's expectations were never mapped against what the student actually covered. One mapping session before term is worth a month of catching up afterwards.

programmes.name: Choosing between the Diploma and A Levels
programmes.description: A real choice in this area, because both routes are available within a reasonable radius. The Diploma rewards breadth and organisation; a British sixth form rewards depth and examination performance. Neither is better in the abstract, and the right answer depends on the student rather than on reputation.
programmes.countryNote: For families intending a UAE university route, the Ministry of Education publishes different requirements by curriculum. On the British track it is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at E.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-maj.subjectsIntro: Where two systems run in one household, requests cluster in the same subject names with different components behind them. Each entry below names the component rather than the topic.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Two papers, no coursework, tiered. Marks go to unwritten method lines, non-calculator arithmetic and combined-topic final parts. A tier error costs more than any topic weakness because it caps the grade outright.

subjects.name: Diploma Mathematics
subjects.levels: AA and AI, HL and SL
subjects.description: Four distinct routes. Higher Level adds a third paper worth twenty per cent, and the Exploration carries another twenty, marked out of twenty across five criteria. The course name on the transcript matters to admissions as much as the grade.

subjects.name: IGCSE Sciences
subjects.description: Core and Extended tiers, with a practical-skills paper for some Cambridge candidates. The marked skill there is writing a method precisely enough for a stranger to repeat, which takes several attempts with feedback rather than one explanation.

subjects.name: Diploma Sciences
subjects.description: Papers plus an internally assessed investigation marked across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Evaluation is the criterion lost most often, because limitations are listed without their effect on the conclusion.

subjects.name: English across both systems
subjects.levels: IGCSE First Language · Diploma English A
subjects.description: The IGCSE paper rewards planning and audience awareness; the Diploma rewards analysis of how a text works, with an oral component most students under-rehearse. The transferable skill is argument structure under time pressure.

subjects.name: Business and Economics
subjects.description: Both systems reward application and explicit evaluation rather than definitions. The Diploma adds internally assessed work with its own word limits, which is where the planning discipline is learned or not.

subjects.name: Diploma core components

sections.heading: What "near me" means when the border is two minutes away
paragraphs: An IB IGCSE tutor near me, searched from Al Majaz, is a request with an unusual geography behind it. The Dubai boundary is close enough that the available market is effectively two markets, and a provider advertising in Dubai may or may not be willing to serve a Sharjah address at a Sharjah hour. The result is that a proximity search returns plenty of names and very little clarity.

IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For a family whose requirement is a person in the room, that is a reason to look elsewhere, and this page says so rather than burying it. In-home provision exists in this market at published rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table placing the common band at AED 180 to 350.

What proximity cannot deliver, on either side of the boundary, is a specialist in a scarce component at a specific hour. Diploma Higher Level Mathematics Paper 3, Higher Level Chemistry, a minority language: those people are thin on the ground across the whole Gulf and are not clustered near the lagoon. A family filtering by driving distance is filtering out most of the supply before the search begins.

The sensible substitution is to stop asking who is nearby and start asking who teaches this programme, this course and this component at the hour the student is actually home. That is a question with good answers for a household in these towers, and the comparisons on the rest of this page are about using them well.

sections.heading: IGCSE against the IB Diploma, compared properly
paragraphs: Households running both systems need to understand how differently they behave, because the instinct to apply one mental model to both is where planning goes wrong. The two are not harder and easier versions of the same thing; they distribute risk in opposite ways.

IGCSE concentrates risk in the papers. With no coursework on most mainstream boards, a student's grade is decided on examination days, which means everything is recoverable until then and nothing is banked before then. The tier on the entry caps the grade. The implication for tutoring is that technique work close to the papers genuinely pays, and that a late start is survivable.

The Diploma spreads risk across two years. Internal assessment sits inside every subject, the core carries up to three points and its own failing conditions, and deadlines are set by the school throughout. The implication is the reverse: late help is much less effective, because a missed internal deadline cannot be reopened, and the highest-value interventions happen a year before anybody feels urgency.

The table below sets the two side by side on the axes that affect spending decisions. The last column is the practical consequence, which is that a household should usually fund the Diploma child early and the IGCSE child late, rather than funding both at the same moment.

There is a further asymmetry worth noting, which concerns second chances. An IGCSE candidate in this country has a November series available, so a disappointing summer result is not final and a resit can be planned deliberately rather than suffered. A Diploma candidate at a UAE school is working towards one main session a year, which makes the sequencing of the second year unusually unforgiving. That alone justifies treating the two children in a household as two separate planning problems rather than one shared budget.

sections.heading: Provider models, compared without a straw man
paragraphs: Almost every tutoring page in this market compares itself to an unnamed alternative that exists only to lose the comparison. A more useful exercise is to compare the models as models, including the one we are, with the real limitation of each stated.

There are five that a family in Al Majaz can actually choose between. A tuition centre with premises, which offers structure and group rates and sometimes individual sessions. An agency, which recruits tutors and manages the match. An international marketplace, which lists tutors and leaves selection to the parent. A freelance or independent tutor, found by word of mouth. And an online platform with matched specialists, which is what IB Gram is.

Each has a genuine failure mode. A centre cannot diagnose one student's error pattern in a group class and is bound by its own timetable. An agency's quality depends entirely on how it vets, and the parent cannot see that process. A marketplace transfers all the selection risk to the parent, who is usually not equipped to assess subject specialism. A freelance arrangement has no replacement mechanism if the match is wrong, and the permit question often goes unasked. An online platform cannot put a person in the room, and should say so.

sections.heading: Sharjah against Dubai: comparing the market, not the emirate
paragraphs: Families here assume Sharjah is cheaper, and the assumption is half right in a way worth unpicking. What is genuinely cheaper on this side of the boundary is anything priced against local overheads: centre packages, group classes, informal arrangements. Those reflect a different cost base and the saving is real.

What is not cheaper is specialist one-to-one work, because that is priced by a regional online market in which the boundary is irrelevant. Qualified online subject tutors publish from roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; specialists are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase around AED 270 and premium examiner-led provision advertised as high as AED 650. A family in Al Majaz pays the same as a family in Jumeirah for the same specialism.

The second difference is availability rather than price. A Dubai-based visiting tutor asked to cross into Sharjah at five in the afternoon will either decline or price the journey, and the pool prepared to do it is small. That turns into waiting time, which for a Year 11 student in the spring is a more expensive currency than dirhams.

The third is regulatory rather than commercial. Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods; Dubai's answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. For a child schooled across the boundary, the applicable framework is the school's emirate, not the family's.

sections.heading: What to compare in a trial lesson
paragraphs: Most families decide after a trial, and most judge the trial on the wrong evidence: whether the child enjoyed it and whether the tutor was pleasant. Both are worth knowing and neither predicts a grade. What predicts a grade is whether a diagnosis happened.

Three things to watch. Did the tutor ask for marked work before teaching anything, or did they begin explaining? A specialist wants evidence first; a generalist opens the textbook at the current chapter. Did they name the specification, the paper structure or the assessment criteria without prompting? A tutor who speaks in specifics has marked the thing; one who speaks in generalities has not. And at the end, could your child state their own weakest point in their own words?

A fourth question belongs to coursework, where it applies. Ask what the tutor will refuse to do with a draft. A clear answer — they will teach the criteria, question the reasoning, give feedback on the student's own writing, and write nothing — is the only defensible position under board rules. Vagueness here is not flexibility; it is a risk being transferred to your child.

Finally, compare two trials rather than one. It costs an hour and it is the only side-by-side evidence a family will ever get. Where one tutor produces a written list of error types and the other produces encouragement, the comparison has made itself, and it will have cost less than a single week of the wrong block.

sections.heading: Comparing the transition: Year 11 into the Diploma
paragraphs: For a household running both systems the transition is the moment the two comparisons collide, and it is handled badly almost everywhere. A student finishes IGCSE with strong grades, the family concludes that the groundwork is done, and the first Diploma term arrives with different demands entirely.

The differences are specific rather than vague. IGCSE rewards examination recall across a known specification; the Diploma rewards independent reading, extended writing and the management of long-form coursework across six subjects at once. A student who has never written four thousand words, never designed an investigation and never had to protect a deadline nobody chases weekly will find the first year harder than their grades predicted.

In this part of Sharjah the transition often adds a change of school and sometimes a change of emirate, which means the receiving school's expectations were never mapped against what the student actually covered. That mapping is a one-session exercise and it is the cheapest thing on this page: it identifies the gaps before the autumn term rather than during it.

Set against the alternative, the comparison is stark. Four to six sessions across the summer costs a fraction of the emergency support a struggling first Diploma term generates, and it is bought when the family has time to arrange it rather than in the middle of a crisis. Almost nobody buys it, which is why the autumn produces so many enquiries that begin with the words we did not expect this.

sections.heading: What no comparison changes
paragraphs: Some facts hold whichever provider, system, emirate or format a family chooses, and they are worth stating because parts of this market imply otherwise.

The permit position. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so a page quoting one is inventing it. The permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

The regulator position. Private schools in Sharjah answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, in Dubai to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to the Department of Education and Knowledge, in Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. No tutoring provider, including IB Gram, holds approval, accreditation or a licence from any of them, and a KHDA educational services permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai.

The coursework position. A tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria, questions the reasoning and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor does not write, complete or rewrite assessed work. This region's market includes a provider selling finished Internal Assessments outright; that is academic malpractice and the consequence falls on the student. No comparison of providers alters that boundary, and a provider offering to cross it is not a cheaper option but a risk transferred.

faqs.question: Should a household with one IGCSE child and one Diploma child use the same tutor?
faqs.answer: Rarely. The two systems distribute risk differently and are marked against different schemes, and a tutor strong in one tends to default to its habits in the other. The better arrangement on this corridor is two specialists in consecutive slots on the same evening, which costs nothing extra in travel because there is none. The exception is a shared underlying skill — argument structure, or the mathematics inside a science — where one tutor can genuinely serve both.

faqs.question: Which child should we fund first if we cannot fund both at once?
faqs.answer: Usually the Diploma child, and earlier than feels urgent. The Diploma spreads risk across two years with internal deadlines that cannot be reopened, so late help is much less effective. IGCSE concentrates risk in the papers, which means technique work close to the examinations genuinely pays and a later start is survivable. Funding the Diploma child in the first year and the IGCSE child after the mock is usually better value than splitting a budget across both at the same moment.

faqs.question: Is there an IB or IGCSE specialist genuinely available near Al Majaz?
faqs.answer: If the filter is driving distance, the available pool shrinks sharply once you add a course, a level and an hour, and the boundary makes it worse because a Dubai-based visiting tutor will often decline a Sharjah address at five in the afternoon. If the filter is the component, the pool is wide. IB Gram makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE and teaches over live video, so the practical answer is that a specialist is available for most courses at a realistic hour.

faqs.question: How do the five kinds of tutoring provider actually differ?
faqs.answer: By what each structurally can and cannot do. A tuition centre offers structure and group economics but cannot diagnose one student's script. An agency vets and matches, though the vetting is invisible to you. A marketplace offers breadth and puts all the selection risk on the parent. A freelance arrangement offers trust and flexibility with no replacement mechanism. An online matched service reaches scarce specialists and cannot put a person in the room. Compare on failure modes, not on adjectives.

faqs.question: Is tutoring cheaper on the Sharjah side of the boundary?
faqs.answer: For some things. Centre packages, group classes and informal local arrangements are generally cheaper here because they are priced against local overheads. Specialist one-to-one work is not, because it is priced by a regional online market where the boundary is irrelevant: published qualified rates run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialist rates from AED 200 to AED 450 and above on either side. What differs is willingness to travel across the boundary, which turns into waiting time rather than a discount.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an apartment in Al Majaz?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. If having somebody physically in the room is your requirement, we are not the right provider and this page would rather say so than waste your trial lesson. In-home provision does exist in this market from others at published rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate's 2026 table putting the common band at AED 180 to 350.

faqs.question: What should I judge a trial lesson on?
faqs.answer: Whether a diagnosis happened. Did the tutor ask for marked work before teaching anything, or start explaining? Did they name the specification, paper structure or assessment criteria without being prompted? Can your child afterwards state their own weakest point in their own words? And, for coursework, what will they refuse to do with a draft? A pleasant lesson where a child felt supported is worth knowing about and does not predict a grade. The written diagnosis does.

faqs.question: Why is the transition from Year 11 to the first Diploma year so difficult?
faqs.answer: Because the demands change rather than intensify. IGCSE rewards examination recall across a known specification; the Diploma rewards independent reading, extended writing and ownership of long-form coursework across six subjects. A student who has never written four thousand words or designed an investigation finds the first year harder than their grades predicted. In this area the transition often also involves a change of school or emirate, which leaves coverage gaps nobody has mapped until the autumn.

faqs.question: Which regulator applies to my child if we live in Sharjah and they study in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The school's, not the home's. A child at a Dubai school is in a KHDA-regulated school, so the inspection framework, published report and curriculum approval come from there. Sharjah's private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods — a broader remit than inspection alone. No tutoring provider, including us, holds approval from either body, and nobody should claim to.

faqs.question: Can the Diploma core really be coached, or is it unteachable?
faqs.answer: It can be coached legitimately and it matters, because up to three points sit in the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay and a low grade can create a failing condition. The coachable part is the thinking and the structure: whether a research question can carry four thousand words, whether a knowledge claim is defensible, whether the criteria are being addressed. The student writes every word. The highest-value session happens before any writing, which is when families least expect to need one.

faqs.question: How many weekly sessions should a two-system household commit to?
faqs.answer: One per child to begin with, reviewed after four weeks against marked work. In a pressured term the instinct is to buy more hours, and the effect is usually to crowd out the independent practice that converts teaching into marks. Where one child genuinely needs two sessions, pausing the other child's block is often better than running four sessions a week in one household. Staggering across the term costs the same and achieves more than running everything at once.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with students in Sharjah need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since it costs nothing to obtain there is no good reason for an independent tutor not to hold one.

faqs.question: What claims should end a conversation with any provider?
faqs.answer: A guarantee of a grade, a points total or a university place. Any claimed approval, accreditation or licence from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education or an examination board. Any school described as a partner or client. Any satisfaction figure or star rating without the number, date and method behind it. And any offer to write, finish or complete assessed coursework, which is malpractice and places the risk on your child rather than on the seller.

faqs.question: How do we compare the result after six weeks against having done nothing?
faqs.answer: With marked evidence on both sides. For an IGCSE child, a second timed paper on the same specification marked against the published scheme and compared with the first by topic. For a Diploma child, a specific deliverable: a coursework section completed to criteria, or a Paper 3 attempt showing recovery from an early error. In both cases the child should be able to describe their own weakest area unprompted. Where that has not happened, the comparison favours stopping and changing something.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mam.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover IB Diploma subjects and Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE subjects for Sharjah students. The first thing we establish is where in the two-year course the student sits, because that determines whether the session should be teaching, technique or process coaching.

intro.heading: Both qualifications are two-year projects, and the term you are in decides everything
paragraphs: Nobody plans a two-year project in one-term units, except in education, where almost everybody does. A family contacts a tutor in the third week of a term because a report arrived, buys a block of hours, and the block ends when the term does. Meanwhile the thing being prepared for is two years long, with its own front-loaded content, its own mid-course decisions and its own compressed final stretch. The term is the wrong unit, and using it is why so much tutoring money produces so little.

Al Mamsha is a walkable district in Sharjah beside Muwaileh and University City, and none of this is affected by where you live. The location decides what hour a session can start. It does not decide who is available to teach Extended-tier Chemistry or Higher Level Mathematics, because the specialists in those are few enough in this emirate that they are not distributed by development. IB Gram does not visit UAE homes in any case; home tuition is a service we run only in India, and every Sharjah lesson is live, one-to-one, over video.

The two-year shapes differ between the boards and it matters. An IGCSE student spends most of two years accumulating content that is then tested in a single examination fortnight, which makes the final term disproportionately about technique. A Diploma student accumulates assessed work throughout, with internal assessments and the Extended Essay carrying real weight long before any examination, which makes the middle of the course the dangerous part rather than the end.

Households running both are therefore running two different shapes that collide in the spring. That collision is predictable from September, and planning for it is the single most useful thing a two-board family can do. It is also the thing nobody warns you about, because by the time it happens you are too busy to ask why it happened.

What follows is the whole map. A table placing you at your current stage with what matters now and what to ignore, a term-by-term account for each board across both years, the three decision points that quietly determine the outcome, when hours are cheapest, and how the UAE calendar interrupts all of it. The sibling pages for this district go down to syllabus level for each board instead. One request before you read on, because it saves a wasted first session. Find the school's internal deadline calendar, the one issued in September with coursework dates or internal assessment milestones on it. That document governs your child's year far more tightly than any examination date, it is the thing a sensible plan is built from, and in our experience roughly half of families have never read it carefully even though the school sent it to them.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mam.programmesIntro: Four stages, each with its own two-year logic. Finding your stage is the first step, because the right plan for Year 10 term one is close to useless in Year 11 term three.

programmes.name: Year 9, the year nobody books

That makes it the one year where tutoring changes not only a grade but which paper your child will sit for the next two years. programmes.name: Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years of content assessed mainly in one examination fortnight, with coursework or practical components in some subjects. Because the grade arrives in a short window, technique in the final term is worth more per hour than at any other point, and content left to that term cannot be recovered.

Entries are confirmed months before the papers, mocks sit a term ahead, and coursework deadlines are earlier still. Put hours into the autumn of DP1 specifically because that collision is coming, and because the autumn is the only part of the Diploma with room in it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, second year

The realistic plan is fewer subjects supported more intensively, with the internal assessments cleared early so that the spring can be spent on papers. sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-mam.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects first, then IGCSE. The notes say when in the two years each subject tends to go wrong, which is more useful for planning than a description of the content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Goes wrong early at Higher Level, in the first term, when algebraic fluency assumed from IGCSE turns out to be shaky. Fixing it in DP1 autumn is straightforward; discovering it in DP2 is not, because everything since has been built on it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Goes wrong at the route-choice stage rather than during the course. Check the requirement of the universities your child is considering before DP1 begins, because some expect Analysis and Approaches and a mid-course change is close to impossible.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Goes wrong in the middle, when written-explanation questions start carrying real weight and the student is still answering them as calculations. The internal assessment is also commonly chosen too ambitiously in DP1 and cannot be rescued late.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Goes wrong cumulatively: a weak first term in energetics breaks equilibrium, which breaks the organic mechanisms a year later. This is the clearest case in the Diploma for spending money in DP1 rather than DP2.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Goes wrong late, because the content volume only becomes unmanageable once Higher Level extension topics arrive. Terminology discipline established early makes the final year considerably lighter than it otherwise is.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Goes wrong at the commentaries, which are internally assessed, need real published articles and are routinely written in a rush. Diarising them in DP1 removes most of the risk in the subject at no academic cost.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Goes wrong slowly and invisibly: analytical technique plateaus while the student feels fluent. One marked timed response a week from DP1 is the intervention, and it is cheap because it is short.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Goes wrong at the research project at Higher Level, and in the habit of writing generic answers about a notional firm rather than the one in the case. Both are structural and both are fixable in a term.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Goes wrong by being left, every time. It is the component with the latest start and the earliest deadline relative to effort, and a short block of process coaching in DP1 is worth more than the same block in DP2.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Comes apart in Year 10 term two, when algebra becomes the basis of everything else. A student who is shaky then will be shaky for two years, because nothing afterwards stops to revisit it.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Comes apart at the practical component, which is usually never taught as a separate skill and is first attempted properly in a mock. Diarise six sessions on it in Year 11 term one and the problem disappears.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Comes apart at moles, early, and stays broken because every quantitative topic afterwards assumes it. The cheapest intervention in the whole two years is rebuilding stoichiometry in Year 10.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Comes apart in Year 11 under content volume, when a student who has been revising from their own notes meets mark schemes that require exact terms. Changing the revision source early prevents it.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: Comes apart at the summary task, which has strict rules nobody explains until a mock. It is the single most trainable component in the subject and four sessions usually settle it permanently.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (0450 / 4BS1)
igcseSubjects.description: Comes apart at evaluation, usually in Year 11, when definitions stop earning marks and application starts deciding grades. A framework taught in Year 10 term three prevents a year of middling marks.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455 / 4EC1)
igcseSubjects.description: Comes apart at diagrams, mechanically and early. Axes, shifts and new equilibria drilled in Year 10 convert into marks on every paper for the rest of the course.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
igcseSubjects.description: Comes apart at pseudocode conventions and trace tables, which strong programmers often dismiss and then lose marks on. Specialist supply for this code is thin, so allow longer to match a tutor.

sections.heading: Find your stage, and what to ignore at it
paragraphs: Start by locating the student rather than the subject. The table below places each stage of the two years against what actually matters then and, just as usefully, what to stop worrying about. Most anxiety in this market is misdirected rather than excessive: a Year 10 parent worrying about examination technique, a DP2 parent still hoping to rebuild a weak first year.

The ignore column is the one worth reading carefully, because the hours in a week are finite and every hour spent on the wrong thing is taken from the right thing. A Year 10 student does not need timed-paper drilling; they need the content secure and the habit of showing method. A DP1 student does not need examination revision; they need the internal assessments and the Extended Essay question settled while there is time.

Notice how the advice inverts across the two years. In the first year, content and process; in the second, technique and triage. A plan that does not change between those two years is a plan that was never built for either of them, and a provider who sells the same weekly hour unchanged for twenty-four months has not thought about it.

Place yourself honestly rather than optimistically. A Year 11 student in January whose content is still missing is at a different stage from the calendar stage, and treating them as if they were on schedule is how a family spends a term on examination technique that the student cannot yet use.

sections.heading: The IGCSE two years, term by term
paragraphs: An IGCSE course accumulates content for two years and then tests it in a fortnight, which produces a predictable failure pattern: everything feels fine until the first mock, and the mock reveals gaps that were created eighteen months earlier. The table below sets out what each term is for, so that the gaps get found while they are still cheap to close.

The term worth the most attention is Year 10 term two, when algebra in Mathematics and moles in Chemistry become the basis of everything that follows. A student who is shaky at that point remains shaky, because the course never stops to revisit it. Half a term of support there is worth more than a full term of support in Year 11, and it costs less because it is ordinary teaching rather than crisis work.

Year 11 term one is the diarising term. Coursework and practical deadlines land, mocks arrive, and entries are confirmed. The single most valuable session of the year is the one immediately after mocks come back, spent going through the papers question by question against the mark scheme while the student still remembers their reasoning. Book it before the mocks start, because afterwards the window closes within a fortnight.

Year 11 term two is technique and nothing else. If content is still missing at that point, the honest conversation is about whether a November entry would produce a better outcome than a June one. Cambridge and Pearson both run a November series, and using it deliberately is a plan rather than a failure.

sections.heading: The Diploma two years, term by term
paragraphs: The Diploma fails differently. Because assessed work accumulates throughout, the damage is done in the middle rather than at the end, and a student can arrive in the final term with a perfectly good grasp of the subject and a set of internal assessments that have already capped their points.

DP1 autumn is the only stretch of the programme with genuine spare capacity. Nothing is due, the student still has evenings, and the two pieces of work with the longest lead times, the Extended Essay research question and the first internal assessment, can both be started calmly. Families who use it arrive at the DP1 spring with something in hand. Families who do not meet that spring with nothing.

The DP1 spring is the collision: internal assessment drafts, the Extended Essay stages and the first mocks within a few weeks. It is entirely predictable from September and almost never planned for. The right response is not more hours in the spring, when there is no room for them, but more hours in the autumn, when there is.

DP2 is triage. The realistic plan is fewer subjects supported more intensively, internal work cleared early, and the spring reserved for papers. We do not publish IB session or results dates anywhere, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a wrong date on a page a family plans around is worse than none. Ask the coordinator, and get the internal schedule in writing.

sections.heading: Three decisions nobody writes in a diary
paragraphs: Across two years there are three moments that shape the outcome more than any amount of weekly tutoring, and all three pass quietly. The first is tier placement at the end of Year 9, usually decided by the school on Year 9 evidence and communicated in a report. It determines which papers your child sits for two years and what grade ceiling applies, and most parents learn about it after the fact.

The second is the subject-set decision before the Diploma, or the subject drop in Year 11. Choosing mathematics routes for comfort rather than against the requirements of the universities a student is considering is the commonest expensive error in the Diploma, because a mid-course change is close to impossible. Dropping an IGCSE subject for timetable reasons without checking the equivalency requirement is the IGCSE equivalent.

The third is the resit decision after results. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the November entry window closes shortly afterwards. Families who debate it from scratch in late August regularly discover the deadline decided for them. Agree the trigger rule in advance: which grade in which subject means a November entry, written down before results day.

Each of these is worth four to six sessions of preparation rather than a term of general support, which makes them the best-value purchases in the whole two years. They are also the ones nobody sells, because they are short and they do not recur.
bullets: Tier placement at the end of Year 9 sets the ceiling for two years
Mathematics route choice must be made against university requirements, not comfort

sections.heading: When hours are cheapest, and what a term costs
paragraphs: Hours cost the same in October and April; what differs is what they buy. In October a session can teach content calmly, and the student has the evenings to consolidate it. In April the same session is triage, and the same money produces a fraction of the movement. The cheapest hours in the two years are therefore the ones bought earliest, which is the least popular true thing in this market.

The bands, read in October 2026. Budget online tutors run roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table in the same range. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session are the useful planning numbers: AED 240 to 600 at the budget band, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Across a two-year course at a weekly hour that is a substantial household commitment, which is exactly why the distribution matters more than the rate.

In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to 500 with independent tutors, with monthly packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions against about AED 799 for eight online sessions. Every figure here is published by the provider named; none is an IB Gram price, and for ours you should take the free trial and ask.

sections.heading: The UAE year, and the four interruptions to plan around
paragraphs: A two-year plan in this country meets four predictable interruptions, and absorbing them in advance is part of planning rather than an exception to it. Ramadan shortens school days and moves the useful study window. Eid removes days. The long summer removes a term's worth of momentum. And the UAE national holidays cluster in a way that takes out a working week in the autumn.

Ramadan is the one that most often ends an arrangement, because families pause and never restart. We move slots instead: a post-Iftar session between roughly 8.30pm and 10pm suits older students already keeping late hours, and a short early-morning session suits others. Decide which before the month begins, because improvisation across a month becomes nothing across a month.

The summer is the opportunity rather than the problem, particularly between DP1 and DP2. The Extended Essay research question can be settled and one internal assessment substantially advanced when nothing else competes for the time, at two sessions a week for six weeks. Students who do that arrive in DP2 in a visibly different position, and it is the single clearest return on a summer in either qualification.

Travel is easier to absorb than families expect, because nothing in our arrangement depends on a journey. The slot is held in Gulf Standard Time and the lesson follows the student, so a fortnight abroad shifts times rather than losing sessions. Over two years that difference is worth several weeks of continuity.
bullets: Move the slot in Ramadan; do not pause it
Use the DP1 to DP2 summer for the Extended Essay and one investigation
Plan the autumn holiday cluster into the term rather than losing it
Lessons follow the student, so travel shifts times instead of losing weeks

sections.heading: Entries, zones and the dates that are actually fixed
paragraphs: Two sets of dates genuinely constrain a two-year plan, and only one of them is published by an awarding body. The first is the examination series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and UAE candidates sit June and November. The February and March series is offered to India only.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November each year. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so any plan should link the live official timetable rather than rely on restated dates.

The administrative point Cambridge makes about itself is worth repeating because it has consequences. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your school which zone it sits in.

The second set of dates is the school's own internal calendar: coursework and practical deadlines, mock windows, Diploma internal assessment and Extended Essay milestones. Those are issued by the school, usually in September, and they govern a year more tightly than any examination date. Get them in writing and build the two-year plan on them.

sections.heading: The boundary that holds across both boards
paragraphs: Over two years there will be at least one week where a deadline and a capacity problem meet, and that is when the integrity line gets tested. This market contains providers who sell completed assessed work; one page in this research advertises finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. The offer looks most reasonable at exactly the moment it is most dangerous.

What a tutor may do, on either board: teach the content, explain how the criteria or mark scheme award marks, discuss a research question the student chose, model structure on a different example, read the draft the student wrote and say where it is unsupported or unclear, and teach referencing and data handling properly.

What a tutor may not do, at any price: write, rewrite, complete or edit assessed work to a finished state, or produce a worked version of the student's own task. We also do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link the official source.

One further rule concerns teachers. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document; we will not arrange it regardless. Al Mamsha sits in Sharjah, where private schools answer to SPEA rather than ADEK, but the permit's own code of conduct carries the same prohibition emirate by emirate, so the answer for a teacher at your child's school does not change by moving across the border.
bullets: Teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's own draft: yes
Writing or completing assessed work: never, and least of all near a deadline
Official papers and mark schemes as downloads: no, we link the source
A tutor who also marks your child's school work: no

sections.heading: Starting mid-term, which is when everybody starts
paragraphs: Almost nobody begins in week one of a two-year course, so the practical question is how to start well in week seven of term two. The answer is to place the student on the map first, then build forwards from where they actually are rather than from where the calendar says they should be. Those two are often a term apart.

Send three things: the board and syllabus code or the subject and level, the school's internal deadline calendar, and one recent piece of marked work. The marked work does most of the diagnostic job, the internal calendar sets the constraints, and the code decides the specialist. With those the first session can plan rather than investigate.

Then agree the distribution explicitly rather than by default. How many terms of support, at what frequency, with which terms deliberately lighter. A plan that says one weekly hour until further notice is not a plan; it is a subscription, and it will quietly continue through the terms where the money would be better saved for a decision-point block.

Finally, diarise the three decisions now, even if they are eighteen months away. Tier placement, the subject-set choice and the resit trigger rule. Writing them in a calendar costs nothing, and each one has more leverage on the final grade than a term of weekly sessions. That is the whole argument of this page, compressed into one instruction. If the school year starts the student on a half-day timetable, note that too, because it decides whether the weekly hour sits late morning or after the Sharjah evening traffic.
bullets: Place the student on the map before buying any hours
Send the code, the internal calendar and one marked paper
Agree which terms are heavy and which are deliberately light
Diarise the three decision points today, however distant

process.title: Tell us the stage, not just the subject
process.description: Which year, which term, and whether the content is genuinely on schedule or a term behind. Those two are frequently different, and a plan built for the calendar stage rather than the real stage spends a term on technique the student cannot yet use.

process.title: Send the school's internal calendar
process.description: Coursework and practical deadlines for IGCSE, internal assessment and Extended Essay milestones for the Diploma. Those dates govern the year more tightly than any examination date, and they are issued by the school rather than by the board.

process.title: A free trial that places you on the map
process.description: The tutor works a real question or reads a section of the student's own draft and tells you which stage the student is actually at and what the current term should therefore be for. You get it in writing, and nothing is paid before it happens.

process.title: Agree the distribution across terms
process.description: How many terms, at what frequency, and which terms are deliberately light. We would rather sell you a front-loaded plan with gaps in it than a flat weekly subscription that runs through the terms where the money should have been saved.

process.title: Diarise the decision points
process.description: Tier placement, the subject-set choice and the resit trigger rule go in the calendar at the start, with a short block of sessions attached to each. These are the highest-leverage purchases in the two years and the ones nobody thinks to make.

whyPoints.title: We plan in years, not terms
whyPoints.description: Both qualifications are two-year projects and the term is the wrong unit to buy in. A plan that does not change between the first year and the second was never built for either, and a flat weekly subscription across twenty-four months is a billing arrangement rather than a plan.

whyPoints.title: We tell you which terms to skip
whyPoints.description: Some terms are worth heavy support and some are worth none. Saying so costs us revenue and it is the only honest version of this advice, because the money saved in a light term is what funds the decision-point block that actually moves the outcome.

whyPoints.title: The decision points get flagged early
whyPoints.description: Tier placement, mathematics route choice and the resit trigger rule each have more leverage than a term of weekly sessions, and all three pass quietly. We put them in the plan at the start rather than discussing them after they have gone.

whyPoints.title: The right calendar for this country
whyPoints.description: UAE Cambridge candidates sit June and November; the February and March series is India only. Several pages ranking for these searches publish February dates to Gulf families, and that is a deadline a parent acts on and loses an entry over.

whyPoints.title: No invented IB dates
whyPoints.description: We describe the May session and send you to your school's IB coordinator, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification. Diploma plans are built on the school's internal schedule instead, which is the calendar that governs the year in practice.

whyPoints.title: Rates attributed, distribution explained
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider that published it and the month it was read, and the table shows what the same hour buys in different terms. Three of six competitor pages in this research publish no price at all.

faqs.question: When in the two years should we actually start tutoring?
faqs.answer: Earlier than nearly everybody does. The highest-value hours in an IGCSE course are in Year 9 and Year 10 term two, when the load-bearing content is being laid down and a weakness can be fixed as ordinary teaching rather than crisis work. For the Diploma it is DP1 autumn, the only stretch with genuine spare capacity. The hours cost the same in October and April; what differs is what they buy, and an April hour spent on triage produces a fraction of the movement an October hour does.

faqs.question: Which term of the Diploma is the most dangerous?
faqs.answer: The DP1 spring, by a wide margin, and it is entirely predictable from September. Internal assessment drafts, the Extended Essay stages and the first mocks arrive within a few weeks of each other in every school we work with. A student with nothing in hand meets all three at once. The correct response is not more hours in the spring, where there is no room for them, but more hours in the preceding autumn, which is the least intuitive piece of planning advice in the whole programme.

faqs.question: Does it matter that we are starting in the middle of a term?
faqs.answer: Not at all, since almost everybody does. What matters is placing the student honestly on the two-year map rather than on the calendar. A Year 11 student in January whose content is still missing is at a different stage from the calendar stage, and treating them as if they were on schedule means buying a term of examination technique they cannot yet use. Send one recent marked paper and the school's internal deadline calendar, and the first session can plan instead of investigate.

faqs.question: What is the single highest-leverage thing we can do over two years?
faqs.answer: Diarise the three decisions and prepare for them: tier placement at the end of Year 9, the subject-set or mathematics route choice before the Diploma, and the resit trigger rule before results day. Each is worth four to six sessions of preparation and each has more effect on the final outcome than a term of weekly tutoring. They are also the purchases nobody sells, because they are short, specific and do not recur into a monthly fee.

faqs.question: How do we decide the mathematics route before the Diploma starts?
faqs.answer: Against the requirements of the universities and courses your child is considering, not against which route feels more comfortable. Analysis and Approaches is algebra-heavy with proof at Higher Level and is what most engineering, mathematics and physics courses assume. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with the calculator genuinely examinable. A mid-course change is close to impossible, so the decision is effectively final. Additional Mathematics 0606 at IGCSE is the best available signal of whether Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is realistic.

faqs.question: Should we keep tutoring through the examination fortnight?
faqs.answer: Barely, and not for content. In the final fortnight the useful work is pacing, logistics and light review, and the single best purchase a family can make is sleep. Students who cram the night before each paper arrive tired for a three-hour cognitive task, which costs more marks than the cramming gains. If a session happens in that fortnight it should be short and should rehearse nothing new. Everything that was going to be learned has been learned by then.

faqs.question: What should we do in the summer between the two Diploma years?
faqs.answer: Settle the Extended Essay research question and substantially advance one internal assessment, at roughly two sessions a week for six weeks. Nothing else competes for the time, and students who do it arrive in DP2 in a visibly different position from those who rest entirely. It is the clearest single return on a summer in either qualification. It does not require daily work and it buys back autumn evenings that would otherwise be spent catching up on exactly those two things.

faqs.question: Is a flat weekly hour for two years a good arrangement?
faqs.answer: It is better than nothing and it is not the best use of the same money. Some terms are worth heavy support and some are worth none, and a flat subscription runs through the light terms where the money should have been saved for a decision-point block or a front-loaded first year. We would rather sell a plan with deliberate gaps in it. Ask any provider which terms they would recommend skipping, and notice whether the answer is none.

faqs.question: How quickly does an Al Mamsha family have to decide about a November resit?
faqs.answer: Within days of results. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the autumn entry window closes shortly afterwards; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 for context on the return cycle. The practical answer is to agree the trigger rule in July: which grade in which subject would mean a November entry, written down. Families who begin the discussion from scratch in late August regularly find the deadline made the decision for them.

faqs.question: What does the school control and what does the board control?
faqs.answer: The board sets the examination series, the entry deadlines it gives centres, and the results dates. The school sets everything you will actually live by: coursework and practical deadlines, mock windows, Diploma internal assessment and Extended Essay milestones, and which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre sits in. Ask for the internal calendar in writing in September. It governs the year far more tightly than any published examination date, and it is the document a tutoring plan should be built on.

faqs.question: How do Ramadan and the holidays affect a two-year plan?
faqs.answer: They remove more time than families budget for, and the losses are avoidable. Ramadan shortens school days and shifts the useful study window, so we move the slot rather than pausing: a post-Iftar session between roughly 8.30pm and 10pm, or a short early-morning one. Decide which before the month starts, because a month of improvisation becomes a month of nothing. Eid and the autumn holiday cluster each take out working days, and planning them into the term rather than reacting to them preserves several weeks across two years.

faqs.question: Can we support two children on two different boards over the same two years?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the structure matters more than the budget. The two calendars collide in the spring, when Diploma internal deadlines, May session revision, IGCSE mocks and June series preparation all land together. Front-load the autumn for the Diploma child and keep the IGCSE child on steady weekly continuity, then decide each term which child the hours belong to. Two back-to-back online slots on one evening with two specialists is usually the workable arrangement, and no amount of travelling produces it.

faqs.question: Why will you not give us IB examination dates?
faqs.answer: Because we cannot verify them and a confidently wrong date is worse than none on a page a family plans around. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools sit the May session, and that is as specific as we are prepared to be in writing. Ask your school's IB coordinator and cite them. Cambridge and Pearson dates we do give come from the boards' own published material.

faqs.question: Is Year 9 tutoring really worth paying for?
faqs.answer: It is the best value in the two years and almost nobody buys it, because nothing feels urgent. Three things cost IGCSE marks later and all three are addressable in Year 9: algebraic manipulation, written explanation against a command term, and the habit of checking work. Year 9 is also when most Sharjah schools decide tier placement, which sets the grade ceiling for two years. A weekly hour at the budget band here changes which papers a child will sit, which no amount of Year 11 support can do.

faqs.question: How do we know the plan is working if there is no exam for eighteen months?
faqs.answer: By agreeing observable evidence at the start, per term, rather than waiting for a grade. In the first year that means specific errors no longer recurring in school work, method shown without prompting, and homework completed independently. For the Diploma it means an internal assessment at draft stage on schedule and an Extended Essay question settled. Review it at four weeks and then each term. If the evidence is absent we change the plan or the specialist rather than waiting eighteen months to find out.

intro.heading: Two timetables, one evening, and the bus in between
paragraphs: Al Nahda in Sharjah is one of the most heavily commuted residential districts in the country. Towers sit directly on the Dubai boundary, the Dubai district of the same name and Al Qusais are immediately across it, and children from the same building are schooled in two emirates on several different curricula. Families here are logistics managers before they are anything else.

The search phrase that brings most of them to a page like this contains the words near me, and it is worth saying plainly what that produces. A proximity search returns a list of people who may or may not teach your child's course, may or may not be free at the only hour your child is home, and may or may not be willing to cross the boundary in the late afternoon. It is a list of names rather than an answer.

The answer, for a household here, starts with a timetable rather than a tutor. Which child gets home when. Which afternoons carry a fixed school activity. Which evenings already have homework that cannot be moved. Whether anybody in the household works the four-day Sharjah public-sector week, which makes Friday genuinely available. Only once that week is on one page does the question of who teaches what become answerable.

IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the country; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For a two-child, two-system household on this corridor that is the structural answer to the logistics problem: two specialists can teach consecutively on a single evening, at times set to match two different arrival times, with nobody in a car and no ten minutes lost at the start of either session.

This page is therefore about household engineering rather than pedagogy. Mapping one week on one page. Sequencing two children on two systems so their heavy periods do not collide. What to ask the school transport office, which is a conversation almost nobody has. When the school run itself is the real problem rather than the teaching. And what changes if a family moves school or emirate, which on this boundary is a live option rather than a theoretical one.

Two things are fixed throughout and stated here rather than buried. We publish no International Baccalaureate examination or results dates, because the board's own site cannot be verified by automated checking. And a tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student wrote; nobody here writes any part of an assessed component.

A last word on why the logistics come before the teaching here rather than after it. In most of the complaints we hear about tutoring not working for a family on this boundary, the teaching was never the failure. A slot was booked at an hour the child could not reliably reach, it was missed twice, the homework cycle broke, and the student quietly stopped treating the arrangement as real. Fix the hour and the ordinary business of diagnosis, marked work and weekly practice does what it normally does. Leave the hour wrong and no specialist, at any rate, can rescue it.

sections.heading: What "near me" means when the bus decides the day
paragraphs: An IB IGCSE tutor near me, searched from these towers, is a request for reachability. The honest reading of it is that the family wants somebody who will actually be there, week after week, at a time that works. Proximity is a proxy for that, and on this particular corridor it is a poor one, because the thing that breaks a weekly arrangement here is not distance but the unpredictability of a boundary crossing at the worst hour of the day.

IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. Where a family's requirement is a person physically in the room, that is legitimate and we are not the provider for it; in-home provision exists in this market at published rates of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel.

What online delivery changes for a household with two children at two schools is specific. The session starts at the minute agreed rather than when somebody arrives. A later slot is available, because nobody is scheduling a drive home afterwards. Two children arriving half an hour apart can be taught consecutively. And the tutor is chosen from everybody who teaches the relevant course rather than from those willing to cross into Sharjah at five in the afternoon.

So the substitution worth making is from who is nearby to who can hold this hour, every week, in this course. That question has good answers for a family here, and the rest of this page is about getting the household week into a shape where the answer can be used.

sections.heading: Mapping one household week on one page
paragraphs: The single most useful hour a parent in these towers can spend costs nothing and involves a sheet of paper. Write the week out, with both children's arrival times, their fixed school activities, the evenings that already carry heavy homework, and the days the household itself is free. Almost nobody does this, and almost every scheduling failure we see could have been predicted from it.

Three things usually emerge. First, there are fewer usable slots than the family assumed: two weekday evenings and a weekend morning is a common total, not five evenings. Second, the two children's best slots are not the same, because their arrival times differ by half an hour or more. Third, the slot everybody instinctively wanted — four or half past four — does not exist for the child who crosses the boundary.

Once the map exists, matching becomes straightforward and the conversation with any provider changes character. Instead of asking what times are available and accepting one, a parent can say which three windows are real and ask who can teach the relevant course in one of them. That framing also widens the pool, because the specialist who is unavailable at half past four may be entirely free at six.

sections.heading: Sequencing two children on two systems
paragraphs: Where both children need support, the instinct is to buy for both at once. On this corridor that is almost always the wrong call, because it doubles the weekly load on a household that has two usable evenings and produces two half-attended blocks instead of one well-used one.

The sequencing rule follows the structure of the two systems. The Diploma spreads risk across two years with internal deadlines that cannot be reopened, so a Diploma child's support should come earlier and should prioritise coursework. IGCSE concentrates risk in the papers, so an IGCSE child's support can come later and should prioritise technique after the mock. Those two needs rarely peak in the same fortnight, which is what makes staggering possible.

In practice that means running one child's block, finishing it, reviewing it and then running the other's. It costs the same in total, fits the evenings that exist, and has the useful side effect that each child gets a parent's attention as well as a tutor's. Households that try to run both simultaneously usually report that the second child's sessions became homework supervision within a month.

The exception is a genuine emergency in both systems at once, which does happen: a Diploma coursework bottleneck in the same term as an IGCSE mock disaster. Even then the answer is usually one weekday slot each plus a weekend anchor rather than four weekday sessions, because the constraint is the student's attention rather than the budget.

sections.heading: Questions for the school transport office
paragraphs: This is the conversation almost nobody has, and it produces the numbers a schedule depends on. The school office knows the day's finishing time; the transport office knows when the bus actually reaches this district, and those two figures can differ by an hour or more depending on the route and the number of stops before yours.

Ask five things. What time does the route serving Al Nahda reach this district, on an ordinary day rather than a good one? How many stops precede ours? Does the route change between terms, and will we be told? Is there an alternative route or a later pick-up that would shorten the run? And on which days do after-school activities, including Creativity, Activity, Service commitments for Diploma students, change the arrival time?

The answers are worth having in writing, because a route that gains a stop in January moves your arrival time by twenty minutes without anybody informing parents, and a tutoring slot set in September then starts failing for reasons nobody attributes to the bus. Families who recheck this each term keep their schedules intact; families who set it once usually find it drifting.

There is a second-order benefit. Having the real numbers makes a conversation with a provider concrete rather than aspirational, and it removes the guilt that attaches to a missed session. A slot that was never achievable was a planning error, not a failure of effort by a tired fifteen-year-old.

sections.heading: When the school run is the actual problem
paragraphs: Occasionally a family arrives asking for a tutor when the honest diagnosis is that the commute is the issue. A child losing ninety minutes a day to a boundary crossing has roughly seven and a half hours a week less than a classmate living in the school's own catchment, and across a two-year course that is a substantial deficit that no weekly hour recovers.

The symptoms are recognisable. The student is capable in class and unproductive at home. Homework is late rather than wrong. Sleep is short. Weekends are spent catching up rather than resting, and the student describes themselves as always behind rather than as finding the work hard. None of that is a teaching problem, and buying teaching will not fix it.

The options are uncomfortable and worth naming. A school nearer home, which on this boundary is often available in the same curriculum. A different route or a private arrangement that shortens the run. Dropping a subject or an activity to free time, where the entry allows it. Or accepting the commute and restructuring the week around a weekend anchor, which is the choice most families here make and the one this page is written to support.

Where tutoring genuinely helps a commuting student, it helps by raising the yield of the hours that exist: diagnosis so effort is targeted, marked homework so nothing is wasted, and a fixed slot so the week has a spine. That is a real service and a limited one, and saying so is better than selling an hour as a solution to a transport problem.

sections.heading: What changes if you move school or emirate
paragraphs: On this boundary a move is a live option, and families consider it more often than in most of the country. It is worth knowing what actually changes, because some of what parents expect to change does not.

What changes: the commute, and therefore the number of usable evenings, which is the biggest single variable in this district. The applicable regulator, because private schools in Sharjah answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority while Dubai's answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, and inspection frameworks and published reports differ accordingly. And potentially the examination board, since a new school may enter Cambridge where the old one entered Pearson Edexcel, which affects practice material for the remainder of the course.

What does not change: the examination series, since candidates in this country sit the June series with November available either way; the Ministry of Education equivalency requirements, which depend on the curriculum rather than the emirate; and the specialist tutoring market, which is priced regionally and is unaffected by which side of the boundary a family lives on.

The risk in a mid-course move is coverage. Two schools teach the same specification in a different order, so a student transferring in Year 11 or the second Diploma year arrives with gaps that nobody owns. Ask the receiving school what mapping it does for transfers, and treat a vague answer as a reason to budget for a short mapping block of your own.

sections.heading: The fixed facts behind all of this
paragraphs: Some things hold whatever a household decides about schools, buses and tutors, and they are worth stating because parts of this market imply otherwise.

Regulation. Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai's are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. No tutoring provider, including IB Gram, holds approval, accreditation or a licence from any of them.

Permits. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge, for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, no fine schedule is published, and the code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

Coursework. A tutor teaches the skill a component assesses, explains the published criteria and what their command words require, tests whether a topic can carry the work, questions the student's reasoning and gives feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor does not write, complete or rewrite any part of it. This region's market includes a provider selling finished Internal Assessments; that is academic malpractice and the risk falls on the student. We also do not reproduce or supply board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables, which belong to the boards and are published on their own sites.
