faqs.question: How do I plan tutoring for two children on two curricula in one household?
faqs.answer: Map the week first, then stagger. Write out both children's real arrival times, their fixed activity days and the evenings already carrying heavy homework; most households here find they have two usable weekday slots and a weekend morning rather than five evenings. Then run one child's block, finish it, review it, and start the other's. Two intensive blocks at once halve the attention available to each, and on this corridor the constraint is attention rather than budget.

faqs.question: Which child should take the earlier session slot?
faqs.answer: The one with the shorter run. A child at a Sharjah school inside the emirate is often home by four, which makes a half past four slot realistic for them. A child crossing the boundary from a Dubai school is commonly home between half past four and five, so their first workable slot is half past five. Because teaching is over video and nobody travels, the two can run consecutively on the same evening, which concentrates the disruption into one weeknight.

faqs.question: Is there an IB or IGCSE specialist genuinely available near these towers?
faqs.answer: If the filter is driving distance, the pool shrinks sharply once you add a course, a level and an hour, and a Dubai-based visiting tutor will often decline a Sharjah address at five in the afternoon. If the filter is the course and a realistic time, the pool is wide. IB Gram makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE and teaches over live video, so the practical question becomes who can hold your hour weekly in that course rather than who lives closest.

faqs.question: What should we ask the school transport office before fixing a slot?
faqs.answer: Five things. What time the route serving this district arrives on an ordinary day, not a good one. How many stops precede yours. Whether the route changes between terms and who informs parents. Whether a different route or later pick-up would shorten the run. And which days carry after-school activities, including Creativity, Activity, Service commitments. Get the answers in writing, because a route that gains a stop in January moves your arrival time without anybody telling you.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to an apartment in Al Nahda, Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. We make no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Teaching here is one-to-one over live video at a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time. For a two-child household that is the structural advantage: two specialists can teach consecutively at times matched to two different arrival times, no session loses its first ten minutes to somebody arriving, and a later start is available.

faqs.question: Our child is capable in class but always behind at home. Is a tutor the answer?
faqs.answer: Possibly not. Late homework rather than wrong homework usually points at time rather than teaching, and a child losing ninety minutes a day to a boundary crossing has several hours a week less than a classmate in the school's own catchment. The options are a nearer school, a shorter route, fewer commitments, or restructuring the week around a weekend anchor. Where tutoring helps a commuting student it does so by raising the yield of existing hours, not by adding hours.

faqs.question: Can both children be taught on the same evening without a clash?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the arrangement most households here settle on. Two consecutive slots, two different specialists, nobody travelling. The earlier slot goes to the child with the shorter run and the later to the child crossing the boundary. It uses one weeknight rather than three, which leaves the rest of the week for homework and sleep — both of which matter more to an examination year than an extra hour of teaching does.

faqs.question: Does the Sharjah four-day working week open up Friday for sessions?
faqs.answer: For many households here, yes. Sharjah's public sector works a four-day week, so where a parent follows that pattern Friday becomes a genuinely available day. A Friday morning session is often the best hour of the week: the student is rested, the roads are quiet and nothing else competes for the slot. Families rarely volunteer this, which is why we ask about the household's working pattern as well as the school day when setting times.

faqs.question: What changes for my child if we move to a school inside Sharjah?
faqs.answer: The commute changes, and with it the number of usable evenings, which is the biggest variable in this district. The regulator changes from KHDA to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. The examination board may change, which affects practice material. What does not change is the examination series or the Ministry's equivalency requirements. The main risk is coverage: two schools teach the same specification in a different order.

faqs.question: Which regulator applies if we live in Sharjah and our children study in Dubai?
faqs.answer: The school's emirate decides it. Children at Dubai schools are in KHDA-regulated schools, so the inspection framework and published report come from there, while Sharjah's private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority. In a household with children on both sides, both frameworks are in play at once. No tutoring provider, including IB Gram, holds approval from either body, and a page claiming such approval is making a checkable and dangerous claim.

faqs.question: How do we stop a weekly slot drifting after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Set it late enough to survive a bad afternoon, keep it at the same time with no exceptions for the first fortnight, and recheck the bus arrival each term. The decay pattern is predictable: a slot moves once for a good reason, then again, and after that the student stops treating it as fixed and stops preparing for it. Protecting the time matters more than the length of the session, and a shorter session that always happens beats a longer one that does not.

faqs.question: Should the Diploma core get its own time in a week this tight?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the single most effective scheduling decision available here. Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay carry up to three points and their own failing conditions, but nothing chases them weekly, so in a household with two usable evenings they lose every argument. Giving them a protected weekend hour means they get written in the autumn rather than colliding with subject coursework in a single term later on.

faqs.question: Do tutors working with children in these towers need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and its code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school.

faqs.question: What should each child's block produce before we continue it?
faqs.answer: Different evidence, reviewed separately. For the IGCSE child, a second timed paper marked against the published scheme and compared with the first by topic. For the Diploma child, a specific deliverable: a coursework section completed to criteria, or an extended-problem paper attempted with recovery from an early error. In both cases the child should be able to name their own weakest area unprompted. Where one block shows that and the other does not, only one should continue.

A household with children on two boards gets two specialists rather than one tutor asked to straddle both, because the mark schemes and assessment models are genuinely different jobs.

intro.heading: Near is a relative word in an inland Sharjah district
paragraphs: Al Nouf has no large school inside it. Its children travel out to Muwaileh, University City or central Sharjah, and a few go further again into Dubai. So when a parent here searches for a tutor near me, the honest translation is not within walking distance. It is somebody who can be here at a usable hour without the arrangement collapsing by half term. Measured that way, the nearest competent option is frequently a video call, and this page explains why without pretending the trade-off does not exist.

The second thing behind this search is usually a household with two curricula. Sharjah families move schools more often than families in most places, because the emirate has good provision in several systems and because work takes people between Sharjah, Ajman and Dubai. The result is common and awkward: a Year 12 student on the Diploma Programme and a Year 10 sibling on Cambridge IGCSE, under one roof, on one evening, with one parent coordinating.

Those two children need different tutors. An IGCSE Extended-tier Chemistry session is about terminal-paper technique against a specific mark scheme. A Diploma HL Chemistry session is about papers plus an internally assessed investigation with its own criteria. A single tutor offered as covering both will be stronger at one than the other, and in an in-person arrangement that compromise is forced on you by geography, because the pool of people prepared to drive inland after four o'clock is not deep enough to supply two specialists.

IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tuition is a service we offer only in India. For Sharjah families every lesson is live, one-to-one, over video, in a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot. The practical effect for a two-child household in Al Nouf is that both children can be taught properly on the same evening, back to back, by two different specialists, which is an arrangement no amount of driving can produce.

What follows deals with the specific problems of running two boards: how the IGCSE years feed the Diploma, where the three exam calendars collide, what proximity actually costs you when you filter for it, and how the emirate regulators differ if you move school. If you want the pure scheduling argument, the IB page for this neighbourhood takes it; the IGCSE page covers session shape and cost per received hour. This page is about running both at once. One thing to settle before you read further: decide which child this term's budget is actually for. Two thin arrangements that neither child notices is the commonest way a two-board household spends a year's tutoring money and sees no grade move, and the decision is easier to make deliberately in September than to discover in March.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-nou.programmesIntro: A household running both boards is really running two assessment models. These are the four stages Al Nouf families ask us about, and the differences between them are what make a single all-rounder tutor a poor idea.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Seven to nine subjects over two years, tiered Core and Extended with Cambridge or Foundation and Higher with Pearson, assessed mainly by terminal examination with some coursework and practical components. The grade is decided in a fortnight of papers, which makes paper technique disproportionately valuable in the final term.
programmes.countryNote: Several Sharjah schools run Cambridge for some subjects and Pearson for others, so one child can sit two boards in a single year. Read the statement of entry rather than the textbook: Cambridge Mathematics is 0580, Pearson Specification A is 4MA1, and the tier names and paper structures are not interchangeable between them.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service, scored to 45 points. Internal assessment carries real weight in almost every subject, so the grade is built across two years rather than decided in one fortnight.
programmes.countryNote: Victoria International School of Sharjah is the emirate's established IB continuum provider, and a number of Sharjah families drive into Dubai for a Diploma place instead. Those students arrive home late, so for an Al Nouf household the Diploma child usually takes the later of the two evening slots and the IGCSE sibling takes the earlier one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each, marked A to D, with a Personal Project in the final year. The criteria matter more than the topic, and students who write well while ignoring the criterion wording sit in the middle band wondering why.
programmes.countryNote: An MYP student and an IGCSE student of the same age are being assessed on different things, which routinely confuses Sharjah families comparing siblings or cousins. MYP rewards process and reflection; IGCSE rewards precision against a mark scheme in timed conditions. Neither is harder, and the tutoring looks different.

programmes.name: IGCSE into the Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The step from IGCSE to DP is where most Sharjah families first ask for help, and the gap is rarely about content. It is about volume, internal deadlines and the shift from answering questions to building arguments. A student with strong IGCSE grades can still struggle for a term while that change lands.
programmes.countryNote: The subject-by-subject version of this transition is set out in a table below. The short form: Mathematics needs the route decision made against university requirements, the sciences need a working understanding of internally assessed investigations, and the essay subjects need a new habit of sustained argument that no IGCSE paper ever asked for.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-nou.subjectsIntro: Diploma Programme subjects first, then the IGCSE grid below it. If your household is running both, read the two together: the IGCSE notes say where the foundation is laid and the Diploma notes say what it is laid for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency under pressure, with HL adding proof and deeper calculus. The exploration is internally assessed and routinely underestimated. Students who understand the maths still lose marks to unjustified steps and weak presentation.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with the calculator part of the assessment rather than a convenience. Check the route against the university requirements before choosing it, because some engineering and economics courses expect Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Multiple choice, extended response, and a third paper on experimental and option material. Written-explanation questions are where marks disappear: a correct idea phrased loosely scores nothing. The investigation rewards one tightly controlled variable.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the HL failure rate. Data questions require uncertainty to be handled rather than mentioned. The investigation needs a quantitative relationship the student can plot and defend.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Large content volume with marks tied to exact terminology, plus data analysis that catches students who revised facts and skipped skills. HL extension material often arrives late and is first met during revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides a large share of the marks and the evaluation command terms decide most of the rest. The internally assessed commentaries need real published articles and disciplined word counts, applied rather than summarised.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, comparative essay, individual oral, and at HL a further essay. Strong bilingual Sharjah students usually plateau on analytical technique rather than language: commenting on effect instead of restating content.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study driven with a research project at HL. Application to the given organisation separates a 5 from a 7, and quantitative tools are examinable and regularly neglected until the final term.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: A prescribed-title essay and an exhibition of three objects against a knowledge question. The component most often left too late in Sharjah schools, and the one where process coaching produces the clearest return per hour.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-nou.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE side of the same household, with syllabus codes where the code is what decides the tutor match.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Two equally weighted papers and no coursework. Extended candidates lose marks to algebra under time pressure and to problems that combine topics without signalling it. Timed papers with the mark scheme open are the fix.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Theory papers plus, for Cambridge, an alternative-to-practical paper testing experimental reasoning rather than recall. It is the paper Sharjah Extended candidates most often underperform on and it needs its own sessions.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry carry the heaviest weight and failure rate. Qualitative-analysis tables and organic nomenclature are learnable by drill and usually left until April, which is too late to be comfortable.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: High volume with marks tied to precise terminology. A loosely right answer scores zero where the mark scheme names a term, and transport in plants, genetics and homeostasis recur as weak areas year after year.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: Comprehension, a disciplined summary task and directed writing with a stated purpose and audience. Summary marks are lost by lifting sentences from the passage rather than reformulating in the student's own words.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (0450 / 4BS1)
igcseSubjects.description: Case-study led, with marks in application and evaluation rather than definition. A student who knows every term and cannot apply it to the stimulus stalls at a C and stays there until the technique changes.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455 / 4EC1)
igcseSubjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries a large share of the marks: axes labelled, correct shift, new equilibrium identified. Data-response answers must quote the extract rather than reason in general terms.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
igcseSubjects.description: Taken by stronger Sharjah candidates as a bridge towards A Level or Diploma mathematics, covering calculus and trigonometry beyond 0580. It is the clearest early signal of whether a student will cope with HL Analysis and Approaches.

sections.heading: What filtering for proximity actually costs you
paragraphs: Searching for a tutor near me applies a filter, and it is worth seeing what the filter removes. In Al Nouf it removes everybody who cannot drive inland in the late afternoon, which is most of the people who have taught your child's exact specification. It keeps everybody who can, regardless of whether they have ever seen a Diploma internal assessment or a Cambridge Extended-tier mark scheme.

That trade is invisible at the point of booking, which is what makes it expensive. A parent who finds somebody twelve minutes away feels they have solved the problem efficiently. Three months later the student is still losing the same six marks a paper, because the nearby tutor is teaching content the student already knows rather than correcting technique they were never taught to see.

The alternative filter is the syllabus code. Ask for somebody who has taught 0625 Extended, or HL Chemistry through two full cycles, and the pool is entirely different: smaller in the sense that fewer people qualify, and much larger in the sense that distance no longer excludes anybody. For a household running two boards, this is the only filter that can supply two specialists on one evening.

None of this says in-person tuition is bad. It says that in an inland district with no school inside it, proximity and expertise do not arrive together, and if you have to choose, the thing that moves grades is the second one. IB Gram does not visit UAE homes in any case, so the choice we can offer you is the specialist one.

sections.heading: The IGCSE to Diploma step, subject by subject
paragraphs: The household running both boards eventually runs the transition too, and it is worth preparing rather than enduring. Most Sharjah students with good IGCSE grades still have a difficult first Diploma term, and the reason is almost never the content. It is the volume of six subjects, the arrival of internal deadlines nobody enforces until suddenly they do, and the shift from answering a question to building a case.

Mathematics is the one decision that cannot be undone casually. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation lead to different university options, and a student placed in the wrong route in DP1 loses a year. Additional Mathematics 0606 at IGCSE is the clearest early signal of whether HL Analysis and Approaches is realistic, which is why it is worth taking even when the school presents it as optional.

The sciences change shape rather than difficulty. IGCSE practical work is assessed through a paper; Diploma practical work is assessed through an investigation the student designs, runs and writes up against published criteria. A student who has never chosen their own variable finds the first attempt genuinely hard, and that is a skill gap that can be closed in the summer before DP1 rather than in the spring of it.

The essay subjects ask for something new. An IGCSE answer is a correct response to a prompt. A Diploma essay is a sustained argument with evidence and counter-argument, and in TOK it is an argument about knowledge itself. That habit takes a term to build, and the students who build it in the summer start DP1 ahead of the ones who meet it in November.

sections.heading: Three exam calendars in one household
paragraphs: A family with an IGCSE child and a Diploma child is tracking two or three calendars, and they do not align. Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series is offered to India only, so ignore any page quoting a February window to a Sharjah parent. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

On the Diploma side, UAE schools sit the May session. We will not publish a specific IB date, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a page a parent acts on is worse than no date. Ask your school's IB coordinator for the session dates and, more importantly, for the internal deadline schedule, which is what actually governs the year.

The collision point is the spring. Diploma internal assessments, the Diploma examination session, IGCSE mocks and the IGCSE June papers all sit within a few weeks of each other. A household that has not planned for it discovers in March that both children need maximum support simultaneously, which is the single most expensive month to be caught unprepared in.

The answer is to front-load. Use the autumn and the winter break for the Diploma internal assessments and the Extended Essay, and keep the IGCSE child on a steady weekly hour rather than saving the effort for spring. Pearson's published pattern helps with the detail: its November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: What the Sharjah market charges across both boards
paragraphs: A two-child household doubles the exposure to pricing, so it is worth knowing the bands properly. Read in October 2026, the budget band runs roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya advertising from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which is the one place where the two boards are priced differently by a provider who publishes figures at all.

Above that, an IB, IGCSE or A Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Premium named or examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to 500 with independent tutors, which is the travel premium made visible.

For a household, the useful planning figures are the monthly ones. The market shows AED 799 per month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 per month for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Two children at the mid band is a real household commitment.

Which is why the sensible structure is rarely two weekly subjects all year. Weekly continuity where the foundation is still being built, blocks where a deadline sits, and a deliberate decision each term about which child needs the money more. sections.heading: Moving school, changing regulator
paragraphs: Households running two boards are often households that have moved, and in the UAE moving school can mean changing regulator. Sharjah's private schools answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and, in Sharjah's case, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a broader remit than parents moving from Dubai expect.

The full map is worth carrying. Dubai is KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah is SPEA. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge, which also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in those three emirates.

The mandatory UAE subjects follow the child regardless. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are required in UAE private schools whatever international curriculum is licensed. KHDA's published requirements calculate instructional time in forty-minute lesson units, require separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and state that using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is not allowed.

What no regulator covers is your tutor. Private tutoring sits with MoHRE under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years to applicants including school teachers, public and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Applications run through the MoHRE smart app and e-services system. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB.

sections.heading: Where the integrity line sits on both boards
paragraphs: Both boards have assessed work produced at home, and both treat outside authorship as malpractice. The IB side is the more exposed, because internal assessments, the Extended Essay and the TOK essay are written over months. This market contains providers selling completed Internal Assessments, with one page in this research advertising finished IAs at AED 3,750. The consequence for a student is not a lower grade; it is a finding against the qualification.

The boundary is the same on both boards. A tutor may teach content, explain how criteria or mark schemes award marks, discuss a research question the student proposed, model structure on a different example, read a draft the student wrote and say where the argument is unsupported, and teach referencing and data handling properly.

A tutor may not write, rewrite, complete or edit assessed work to a finished state, and may not produce a worked version of the student's own task. We also do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. We reference them and link the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter rather than a judgement call.

One further rule applies to teachers. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document; the principle holds regardless and we will not arrange it.

sections.heading: Starting when two children need different things
paragraphs: Begin by deciding which child the money is for this term. That sounds cold and it is the most useful decision a two-board household makes, because the alternative is two thin arrangements that neither child notices. Usually the answer is the one closer to a terminal assessment, with the other child picked up in the following term.

Then collect four things per child: the board and syllabus code or the subject and level, the tier or Higher and Standard Level choice, the school's internal deadline schedule, and one recent piece of marked work. With those we can match specialists rather than guess, and a specialist who has seen the marked work will tell you something useful in the first hour.

Book the two trials on the same evening, back to back. You will learn more from comparing two diagnoses an hour apart than from two conversations a fortnight apart, and you will also find out immediately whether the back-to-back structure works for your household or whether one child needs a different day entirely.

Then review at four weeks against evidence agreed in advance, per child, separately. The commonest failure in a two-child arrangement is that one is working well and the other is drifting, and an undifferentiated review hides it. If a match is wrong we change that specialist and leave the working one alone.

Expect the balance between the two children to shift at least twice across a year, and plan for that rather than resisting it. A Diploma student who was stable in October can be overwhelmed in February when three internal deadlines arrive together, and an IGCSE student who needed nothing in the autumn needs a great deal in April. Reviewing which child the hours belong to at the start of each term, rather than once at the start of the year, is what keeps the spending proportionate to the problem.

sections.heading: Honest limits on what we can cover
paragraphs: Some combinations are harder to staff than others and you should hear it before you pay. Mainstream Diploma subjects and Extended-tier IGCSE subjects match within two to four days, often inside forty-eight hours. Less common Higher Level options, second-language subjects and narrow IGCSE subjects such as Computer Science 0478 or Additional Mathematics 0606 take five to ten days and sometimes longer.

When no UAE-based specialist is free in your evening window, the realistic answer is a specialist in another timezone whose working hours overlap Sharjah's evening, or a weekend-morning slot. We say which it is, and we say it before any commitment. No competitor researched in this market discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers without mentioning where delivery actually happens.

The weekday evening between 4.30pm and 7.30pm is the most contested window in the entire schedule, because that is when every family in Sharjah wants a lesson. A household willing to take a weekend morning for one of its two children will see shorter match times and usually a stronger tutor. For a two-child household that is the cheapest piece of leverage available.

We also will not pretend about dates. Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page come from the boards' own published material with the source's framing. IB session dates are not restated here, because the IB's site blocks automated verification and a wrong date is worse than an absent one. Ask your school's IB coordinator and work from the internal deadline schedule they publish.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both my IGCSE child and my Diploma child in Al Nouf?
faqs.answer: They can, and we would rather they did not. An IGCSE Extended-tier session is about terminal-paper technique against a specific mark scheme; a Diploma Higher Level session adds an internally assessed investigation with its own published criteria. A tutor who offers both will be stronger at one. An in-person arrangement in this district tends to force the compromise, because the pool prepared to drive inland after four o'clock is not deep enough to supply two specialists. Online, both children get their own.

faqs.question: Is anyone in Al Nouf itself available to teach the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and that is not the right question to ask first. Al Nouf is residential, with no school inside it, so the people who teach the Diploma locally are either at work until the afternoon or living elsewhere. Searching by distance keeps whoever is free and nearby and discards most people who have actually taught Higher Level through two full cycles. Searching by subject and level keeps the specialists and discards nothing except physical presence, which is the trade we would make.

faqs.question: How do we fit two children's tutoring into one Sharjah evening?
faqs.answer: Back-to-back slots, younger child first. A typical Al Nouf arrangement puts the IGCSE child at 4.30pm, once they are home from Muwaileh or University City and have eaten, and the Diploma child at 6pm, which allows for a later finish and a longer journey. One parent supervises one stretch of the evening instead of two. Each child has their own specialist, and the two sessions share a single agreed fallback day for weeks when a school deadline lands badly.

faqs.question: What should we do in the summer before the Diploma Programme starts?
faqs.answer: Three specific things, none of which require daily work. Settle the mathematics route against the universities your child is considering, because Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation lead to different options and a wrong placement costs a year. Learn how an internally assessed investigation works before the first one is due. And practise sustained argument, which no IGCSE paper ever asked for. Six to ten sessions across July and August does this, and it changes the whole first term.

faqs.question: Which exam series does each of my children sit?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge IGCSE in the UAE, the June series and the November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, so disregard any page quoting it here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with its November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026. UAE Diploma candidates sit the May session, and we deliberately publish no specific IB date because the IB's site blocks automated checking. Ask your school's IB coordinator for both the session dates and the internal deadline schedule.

faqs.question: When in the year do both children need support at the same time?
faqs.answer: March and April, reliably. Diploma internal assessment deadlines, the May session revision period, IGCSE mocks and the June series preparation all land within a few weeks. A household that has not planned for it finds both children needing maximum support in the same month, which is the most expensive way to buy tutoring. Front-load instead: use the autumn and the winter break for Diploma internal assessments and the Extended Essay, and keep the IGCSE child on a steady weekly hour from September.

faqs.question: Does Additional Mathematics 0606 matter if my child wants IB Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: It is the single most useful signal available. Additional Mathematics 0606 covers calculus and trigonometry beyond the 0580 syllabus, which means a student who copes with it has already met the kind of material Higher Level Analysis and Approaches assumes. A student who struggles with 0606 will find HL Analysis and Approaches very hard, and that is worth knowing in Year 11 rather than in the second term of DP1. Take it even where the school presents it as optional.

faqs.question: How much should a Sharjah household budget for two children?
faqs.answer: Double the single-child figure and then decide whether that is sustainable, because most families find it is not all year. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget band, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, read in October 2026. The workable structure is usually weekly continuity for one child and concentrated blocks for the other, with the priority reviewed each term rather than set once.

faqs.question: We moved from a Dubai school to a Sharjah one. What changed?
faqs.answer: The regulator, and possibly the subject availability. Dubai private schools fall under KHDA; Sharjah's fall under SPEA, which in this emirate approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That broader remit means a subject your child was taking may simply not be offered, which is worth checking before the transfer rather than after. The mandatory UAE subjects follow the child either way: Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are required whatever curriculum is licensed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at my child's Diploma internal assessment and the IGCSE coursework?
faqs.answer: They can read what each child has written and say where the argument is unsupported, the method unclear or the brief unanswered, explain how the criteria or mark scheme award marks, and teach referencing and data handling. They cannot write, rewrite, complete or finish either piece, and cannot produce a worked version of the student's own task. The rule is the same on both boards. Providers here sell completed internal assessments outright, and buying one converts a grade worry into a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: How long does it take to match tutors for two different boards?
faqs.answer: For mainstream combinations, two to four days each and often inside forty-eight hours, which means both children can usually be matched in the same week. For narrower requirements, a less common Higher Level option or an IGCSE subject such as Computer Science 0478, allow five to ten days and expect us to tell you whether the specialist is UAE-based or teaching into your evening from elsewhere. Taking a weekend morning for one of the two children shortens both timelines noticeably.

faqs.question: Is the MYP easier than IGCSE for a student of the same age?
faqs.answer: Neither is easier; they measure different things, and comparing siblings or cousins across the two causes a lot of unnecessary worry in Sharjah households. The Middle Years Programme assesses eight subject groups against four criteria each, rewarding process, reflection and application. IGCSE rewards precision against a mark scheme under timed conditions. A student who thrives in one may need real adjustment in the other, and the tutoring for each looks different in both content and habit.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody local can teach an unusual Higher Level option?
faqs.answer: We tell you before you commit, and then we offer a specialist whose working hours overlap the Sharjah evening or a weekend-morning slot, saying plainly which one it is and where the tutor is based. What we will not do is accept the booking and hand your child to someone learning the option alongside them. No competitor researched in this market publishes a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE families to overseas numbers without saying where delivery actually happens.

faqs.question: Do you support Arabic alongside both curricula?
faqs.answer: We can support Arabic language work, within real constraints that are worth knowing. Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies are mandatory in UAE private schools whatever international curriculum is licensed. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that using different or additional content for the mandatory subjects without prior Ministry permission is not permitted. Note also that Arabic does not count towards the five subjects required for Ministry equivalency on the British track.

faqs.question: Which child should we start with if we can only afford one?
faqs.answer: Usually the one closer to a terminal assessment, because that is where a term of work converts into a grade that gets recorded. A Year 11 IGCSE student in January has a harder deadline than a DP1 student in January, even though the DP1 student has more work. The exception is an internal assessment at risk: a Diploma internal assessment that goes in badly cannot be repaired later, while an IGCSE paper can be resat in November. Decide explicitly, and revisit it next term.

intro.heading: The year is the unit, not the week
paragraphs: Al Qasimia households often run two education systems at once. An older child in the Diploma Programme, a younger one working towards Cambridge or Pearson papers, two sets of deadlines, two sets of jargon, and one evening in which both have to happen. The search that brings a parent here is usually prompted by one child's crisis, but the useful conversation covers the year and both children.

The two systems have different rhythms, and that is the single most useful thing to understand before booking anybody. An IGCSE candidate's grade is decided almost entirely in the examination room, which means their calendar is dominated by one series and the ten weeks before it. A Diploma student's grade is assembled over two years from internal assessments, core components and terminal papers, which means their calendar has deadlines scattered across twenty-four months and very little slack in DP2.

A tutoring arrangement that treats both children identically - one weekly hour each, all year, in whichever subject looks weakest - gets both wrong. The IGCSE candidate's hours are spread thinly through months where papers would do more good concentrated at the end. The Diploma student's hours arrive in the quiet terms and then run out when internal assessments collide with revision.

There is also a supply dimension that families on a tight budget should know about. Specialist availability is not constant through the year. In the eight to ten weeks before a series, demand concentrates and the people who have actually taught a specific course at a specific level get booked. A family that starts looking at that point is choosing from whoever is left, which is the worst moment to be making a quality decision.

Our approach is to map the year, place hours where each system needs them, and be straightforward about what we can and cannot verify. Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page are sourced and checkable. IB dates are not published here at all, because we could not verify them from the IB's own site and a wrong date on a page like this is worse than no date. Your school's coordinator holds the confirmed version.

One habit makes everything that follows easier: write both children's dated commitments on a single sheet at the start of each term. Mock weeks, internal assessment submissions, the extended essay checkpoints, the school's internal entry deadline. Households that do this spot the collisions months ahead and buy hours deliberately; households that do not end up buying them in a panic, at the point in the year when the right specialists are least available.

Delivery is online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE - that service exists only in India - which is also what makes two children's slots on one evening practical in a central Sharjah household rather than theoretical.

sections.heading: What 'near me' really means when the clock is the constraint
paragraphs: In a district as central as Al Qasimia, the search phrase 'near me' is not doing much work. Tutors are available; several will come to your building. The scarcity is not in supply, it is in the overlap between three things: somebody who has taught the exact course, at an hour your child can actually use, in the weeks when it matters.

Each of those three narrows the field. Course specificity cuts hardest for Diploma subjects, because Sharjah has few schools authorised for the programme and therefore few local adults who have taught it to final-grade standard. The hour cuts hardest for families whose children travel across the emirate or into Dubai for school. And timing cuts hardest in the two months before any series, when the specialists who do exist are already committed.

Distance, by contrast, is the easiest of the constraints to remove, which is why we remove it. Lessons are delivered one to one over live video, so the tutor can be the person who has taught your child's course rather than the person whose car can reach your street before six. For a household running two systems, that also makes consecutive slots on one evening possible without anybody driving between them.

None of which means in-home tutoring is a bad product. It solves supervision, and for a younger child that may be the real problem. It is simply not what IB Gram sells in the UAE - home visits are a service we run only in India - and for a Diploma or Year 11 candidate the specialist match matters more than the presence.
bullets: Supply is not the scarce resource in central Sharjah; the right match at the right hour is

sections.heading: Twelve months mapped across both systems
paragraphs: Here is the map a household with children in both systems actually needs. It is written by period rather than by month, because school calendars differ and because a page that pins a month to a year goes stale. The pattern, however, repeats reliably.

Early in the academic year, both systems are in content mode. For the IB child this is the cheapest time to buy support, because a gap closed now costs one session and the same gap closed in DP2 costs five. For the IGCSE candidate it is the time for light-touch work on the structural weaknesses - algebra, writing, graph work - that limit every subject.

Mid-year brings mocks for the British track and the first serious internal assessment deadlines for the IB. This is the period when most families start looking for a tutor, and it is already late for the IB child's core components. It is well timed for the IGCSE candidate, provided the block that follows is paper-led rather than content-led.

The final stretch divides the two completely. The IGCSE candidate should be doing timed papers and nothing else. The Diploma student should have finished assessed work and be revising, which only happens if the earlier periods were used. Then results arrive - for Pearson, June results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026 - and the resit question opens for anybody who needs it.

sections.heading: Two children, two calendars, one household
paragraphs: The practical difficulty in a mixed household is not academic, it is logistical. Two children with different schools, different finish times and different deadline calendars generate more scheduling conflict than either would alone, and the younger child's session is almost always the one that moves.

The arrangement that survives is consecutive slots on one evening. The older child goes first while the younger does homework, then they swap. A parent is present and available for one evening rather than being on duty across four. Because nobody is driving, the handover is immediate, and a late school bus shifts both sessions by twenty minutes rather than destroying one.

The second thing worth doing is comparing the two calendars once a term, side by side. Mock weeks at two different schools can fall a fortnight apart, and an internal assessment deadline for the older child can land in the younger one's revision week. Knowing that in advance lets a family move a slot deliberately instead of cancelling under pressure.

A small thing that helps: tell each child what the other's plan is. Siblings notice allocation keenly, and a younger child who understands that their brother's hours are concentrated before a series - and that their own will be later, for the same reason - is far less likely to read the difference as favouritism.

The third is resisting the urge to buy symmetrically. It is natural to want each child to have the same support, and it is usually wrong. The two systems need hours at different times and in different densities. A fair arrangement is one where each child's hours arrive when their own calendar needs them, not one where both get an identical weekly hour all year.

sections.heading: The dates we will publish, and the ones we will not
paragraphs: A page offering calendar advice should be precise about its sources, because dates are the thing parents act on. Here is the division we apply, and why.

Cambridge and Pearson information is published by the boards and verifiable. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series; the February/March series is offered to India only, so it is irrelevant to a UAE candidate and quoting it to Sharjah parents is a factual error. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and must use the correct version of the timetable - Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

Results dates are equally checkable and worth having. For Pearson, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026. Because Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and those can be revised, the correct instruction is always to work from the live official timetable rather than a date copied from a tutoring page.

IB dates are different. The IB's own site blocks automated access, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the source. We therefore publish none of them. UAE schools sit the May session, and your school's IB coordinator holds the confirmed dates for your child's cohort. A wrong date in an FAQ answer is exactly the text an AI assistant quotes back to a parent, which is why the omission is deliberate rather than lazy.

sections.heading: Mock season: read the script, not the grade
paragraphs: Mocks are the most useful event in the school year and the most wasted. A grade comes home, a conversation happens about effort, and the script - which contains the actual diagnosis - goes into a bag. For both systems, the script is where a tutoring plan should start.

Three different problems hide behind a disappointing mock. The first is missing content: topics genuinely not understood, which need teaching and then practice. The second is technique: command terms misread, method not shown, observations written as conclusions. The third is timing: an unfinished paper, or minutes spent on a question worth two marks. Each has a different fix, a different cost and a different timescale, and only the script distinguishes them.

For a Diploma student, criterion feedback on internal assessment drafts plays the same role. A comment that an evaluation does not address the criterion is specific and actionable; a grade is not. Students who read the descriptors alongside the feedback improve on the next piece, and students who read only the mark usually repeat the error.

Ask the school for the script if it has not come home. Some schools keep mock papers for departmental review and return only the mark, and a polite request usually produces the paper or a photograph of it. Without the script, any tutoring plan is guesswork dressed up as a diagnosis, whoever is writing it.

So the first thing we ask a family for is a marked script or a draft with feedback, and the matched tutor marks or reads it before the free trial lesson. That turns the trial into a diagnosis rather than an introduction, and it is the cheapest hour available in this whole process because it costs nothing.

sections.heading: Why specialists disappear eight weeks out
paragraphs: Tutoring supply is not constant through the year, and nobody tells families this. Demand is intensely seasonal: it rises after mock results, peaks in the eight to ten weeks before a series, and collapses afterwards. The people most affected by that peak are exactly the ones worth having - the specialists in a particular course at a particular level.

The arithmetic is simple. A tutor who teaches a narrow course has a limited number of weekday evening slots. In the peak, those fill with students who booked earlier. A family arriving at that point is choosing from the residue, which skews towards generalists and towards awkward hours. The quality decision has effectively been made by the calendar rather than by the parent.

The remedy is unglamorous: book the specialist before the peak, even at a lower frequency. A fortnightly slot held from the start of the year converts easily into a weekly one in the final block, because the tutor already has the student and the student already has the plan. Starting from zero in the peak is the expensive way to do it, in both money and choice.

We also tell families when nothing is available, which is a small thing that matters. Narrow requests - Additional Mathematics 0606, a higher level language, Theory of Knowledge coaching at a popular hour - sometimes have no specialist free in the peak. We offer a different hour or a named date, and we do not fill the slot with somebody who has not taught the course.

sections.heading: Cost, timed across a year rather than quoted by the hour
paragraphs: A household running two systems needs an annual figure, not an hourly one, because the decision is about allocation. The question is not what a tutor costs but which child's hours go where, and when.

Market rates, published so the arithmetic is transparent: across UAE rate cards, budget online tutoring starts around AED 45 an hour, a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed, and named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 and above. Published packages include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's Dubai estimates, read in October 2026, put a weekly session at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month with a qualified tutor and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Applied to a household, a sensible annual shape might be: thirty hours for the Diploma child spread across the year with fortnightly core-component check-ins, and twenty-two hours for the IGCSE candidate, mostly concentrated in a ten-week block. At the mid-point of the qualified online band that is around AED 10,400 for both children for the year, which is less than a symmetrical weekly arrangement for both and considerably more effective.

These are market figures for comparison rather than our price list; ask us directly and start with the free trial lesson. The one thing worth repeating is where money leaks: into the travel premium, into generalist hours spent diagnosing what a specialist would have seen in one script, and into weekly slots held through terms when nothing was due.

sections.heading: The fixed parts: permits, regulators and honest limits
paragraphs: Some things do not move with the calendar, and they are worth settling once so they never have to be revisited under pressure.

The permit. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount quoted at you. MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service is the application route.

The regulators. Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods; Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall under the federal Ministry of Education; Dubai has KHDA and Abu Dhabi has ADEK. Knowing which applies to your child's school tells you whose published information is relevant. IB Gram holds no approval, licence or accreditation from any of them, and has no UAE premises.

The limits. No tutor can guarantee a grade, and anybody offering a number is selling confidence. No tutor may write, draft or edit assessed work - internal assessment, extended essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or coursework - and we do not sell completed work of any kind. Essay mills appear in these search results charging thousands of dirhams, and the malpractice finding lands on the student's diploma rather than on the seller's accounts.

process.title: Send both children's details at once
process.description: Programme and level or syllabus code for each child, their schools, finish times and the next dated assessment for both. In a two-system household this is what lets us place consecutive slots on one evening instead of scattering four sessions across a week.

process.title: Ask the schools for their deadline calendars
process.description: The IB coordinator's internal deadline list and the British-track school's mock dates and internal entry deadline. Both are documents the schools already hold, and together they show the collisions months before they happen.

process.title: A marked script or draft before the trial
process.description: We mark a recent paper against the published mark scheme, or read an internal assessment draft against the criteria, before the free trial lesson. That makes the trial a diagnosis, and you keep the marked work whether or not you continue.

process.title: Hours allocated by calendar, reviewed each term
process.description: The IB child's hours spread with fortnightly core-component check-ins; the IGCSE child's concentrated into a block. We revisit the allocation each term rather than running the same weekly hour from September to June and hoping it lands well.

whyPoints.title: The plan covers a year and a household
whyPoints.description: Two systems need hours at different times and in different densities. We allocate across both children and both calendars rather than selling two identical weekly slots, which is the arrangement most families default into and few are happy with by DP2.

whyPoints.title: Booked before the peak, not during it
whyPoints.description: Specialist availability tightens eight to ten weeks before any series. We tell families to hold a scarce course early at a low frequency and convert it later, because arriving in the peak means choosing from whoever is left.

whyPoints.title: Only verifiable dates get published
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson information on this page is sourced and checkable. No IB session or results date appears, because we could not confirm one from the IB itself. The coordinator at your child's school is the correct source, and we say so instead of guessing.

whyPoints.title: One evening, two specialists
whyPoints.description: Consecutive online slots mean a parent supervises once rather than three times, and each child still gets somebody who has taught their actual course. Nobody is driving between the two, so a late bus moves both sessions instead of cancelling one.

whyPoints.title: Hard limits stated once
whyPoints.description: No grade guarantees, no writing of assessed work, no claimed regulator approval, no UAE premises, no home visits in this country. Those are commitments we would rather make on the page than have a family discover halfway through a term.

faqs.question: We have one IB child and one IGCSE child. Can both be tutored on the same evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the arrangement we recommend in a two-system household. Two specialists take consecutive slots - the older child first while the younger does homework, then they swap - so a parent is on duty one evening rather than three or four. Because lessons are delivered over live video, the handover is immediate and a late school bus shifts both sessions by twenty minutes instead of cancelling one. Each child gets their own written plan, and you get one point of contact and one review conversation.

faqs.question: When in the school year should we start looking for a tutor?
faqs.answer: Earlier than feels necessary, especially for a scarce course. Specialist availability tightens sharply in the eight to ten weeks before a series, so a family starting in the peak chooses from whoever is left - usually generalists at awkward hours. Holding a fortnightly slot from early in the year costs little and converts easily into a weekly one in the final block, because the tutor already knows the student. The best-value window of all is the long summer, when the scarcest tutors have open diaries.

faqs.question: You list Cambridge dates but no IB dates - why the difference?
faqs.answer: Because we could not verify them from the IB itself; its site blocks automated access, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source. A wrong date in an FAQ is precisely the text a parent acts on and an AI assistant quotes back, so we leave it out deliberately. UAE schools sit the May session, and your school's IB coordinator holds the confirmed dates for your child's cohort. Cambridge and Pearson dates, which are published by the boards, do appear here.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge and Pearson dates can we actually rely on?
faqs.answer: The series pattern and the published results dates. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 Pearson results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the next day, and the November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the timetable itself, use the version your school's exams officer issues, since zones differ.

faqs.question: Should both children get the same number of tutoring hours?
faqs.answer: Fairness in hours usually produces unfairness in outcomes, because the two systems need support at different times. An IGCSE candidate's marks respond most to a concentrated block of timed papers before the series. A Diploma student needs hours spread across two years so internal assessments and core components are finished before revision begins. A sensible household plan gives the IB child fewer hours more often and the IGCSE child more hours later, which usually costs less than two symmetrical weekly slots.

faqs.question: A mock came back badly. What is the first thing to look at?
faqs.answer: Read the script rather than the grade. Three different problems hide behind one mark: missing content, weak technique - command terms misread, method not shown - and poor timing, such as an unfinished paper. Each needs a different fix with a different cost and timescale, and only the script separates them. Send it to us and the matched tutor marks it against the published scheme before the free trial lesson, so the trial is spent on diagnosis. You keep the marked script either way.

faqs.question: How early do IB internal assessment deadlines really start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families expect, and they are set by the school rather than the board. Ask the coordinator at the start of DP2 for the internal submission dates per subject, the extended essay checkpoints, the Theory of Knowledge deadline and the mock windows. With that list in hand, the fortnight where several deadlines collide becomes visible months ahead and can be defused by finishing one piece early. Without it, families discover the collision while it is happening, which is the expensive way.

faqs.question: Is the summer break worth using for either child?
faqs.answer: For both, and for different things. The IB child can settle an exploration question, plan an investigation's method or read for the extended essay - decisions that take months of subsequent work in the wrong direction if they are rushed. The IGCSE candidate can close the content gap that would otherwise surface in the final term. It is also the period when the scarcest specialists have open diaries. Because lessons are online, the slot follows a family who travels, with a timezone adjustment.

faqs.question: What does a year of support for two children cost in central Sharjah?
faqs.answer: At market rates rather than ours: a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour across published UAE rate cards. A calendar-timed allocation - around thirty hours spread for the IB child plus fortnightly core-component check-ins, and around twenty-two concentrated hours for the IGCSE candidate - comes to about AED 10,400 for the year at the middle of that band. A symmetrical weekly arrangement for both children costs more and delivers less. Ask us directly and begin with the free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both children to save money?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is usually a false economy. A Diploma higher level subject and a Year 10 IGCSE course are different teaching jobs, and the tutor who is strong at one is typically approximate at the other - usually to the older child's cost, in the year that matters most. Where the courses are genuinely close, such as two Cambridge sciences, it can work. Otherwise two specialists in consecutive slots give you better teaching for a similar total, with one point of contact.

faqs.question: What if our evening slot stops working when school activities change?
faqs.answer: We move it, usually within the same week and with the same tutor. Sport seasons start, a commute lengthens, a school adds a late club, and a slot that worked in September stops working in January. Because nobody is driving to an address, rescheduling is a matter of finding another hour rather than renegotiating a journey. If the tutor's own diary no longer fits, we match another specialist and carry the written plan across so the student does not restart from a diagnosis.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working in central Sharjah need a permit, and who issues it?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation issues the private tutor work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule. Because it costs nothing, asking a prospective tutor whether they hold it is entirely reasonable.

faqs.question: Which regulator covers our school, and does it matter for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Sharjah's private schools are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall under the federal Ministry of Education, Dubai under KHDA and Abu Dhabi under ADEK. It matters for school processes - fees, calendars, published information - rather than for tutoring, which is governed federally through the MoHRE permit. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of these authorities and has no UAE premises.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help finish an internal assessment that is late?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help the student finish it; a tutor cannot finish it for them. Permitted help includes reading the criteria together, narrowing the research question so the available data can answer it, teaching the method or statistics the work needs, and explaining which criterion a draft fails. Writing, redrafting or editing the submitted text is not permitted, and IB Gram does not sell completed assessments. The malpractice consequence attaches to the student's diploma, which is why no deadline changes the answer.

intro.heading: What "near me" is really asking, and the honest answer
paragraphs: A search for an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Al Rahmaniya almost never means what it says. Parents are not hoping for somebody on the next street. They are hoping for somebody who has marked a Cambridge 0580 Paper 4 often enough to know that candidates lose three marks on the same transformation question every June, or who can look at an MYP Criterion C comment and translate it into what the Diploma will expect in eighteen months. Proximity is a proxy for competence, and in a Sharjah villa community of this size it is a poor one.

Al Rahmaniya sits inland from the Sharjah corniche, off Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, next to Al Tai and a short run from Muwaileh and University City. Sharjah Sustainable City is inside it. Families here are a mix of long-settled Sharjah households and newer arrivals who moved out of the Al Majaz and Al Khan towers for space. Their children are spread across British-curriculum, IB and CBSE schools in three directions, which means the subject combination in any one villa is unlikely to match the villa opposite.

That spread is exactly why a radius search fails. A parent needing Physics 0625 Extended and a parent needing Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL are both told the same thing by a map: here are four tutors within six kilometres. Neither of them is told the thing that decides the outcome, which is whether any of those four has taught the paper their child is sitting. Nobody advertises the gap, so parents book on distance, change tutor in week five, and lose a term.

IB Gram works the other way round. The enquiry starts with the board, the subject, the level and the assessment that is closest, and the match is made against tutors who teach that specific combination. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the Sharjah school day. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and pretending otherwise would be the fastest way to waste your evening.

What follows is the information a parent in Al Rahmaniya would otherwise have to assemble from six websites: what the Sharjah market charges per hour and why the in-home figure is higher, how to check in two minutes that a tutor is permitted to teach privately in the UAE, which exam series your child's board actually runs here, what a tutor is allowed to touch on an Internal Assessment, and what happens when no specialist is free for a narrow subject. Every figure is attributed. Nothing on this page is a price list of ours.
