sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-rah.programmesIntro: Al Rahmaniya children sit across three overlapping stages, and the tutoring that helps at each one looks different. These are the three that generate most enquiries from this part of Sharjah, with what the stage actually demands rather than a brochure description.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, usually eight or nine subjects, assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE does not tier the same way and uses its own codes, such as 4MA1 for Mathematics. The practical difference for a tutor is which paper your child is entered for, because the same topic is examined to a different depth in each.
programmes.countryNote: Sharjah schools near Al Rahmaniya use both boards, sometimes in the same building for different subjects, so the first question in a trial lesson is which syllabus code appears on your child's entry. For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, Gulf Today reported that candidates must pass five accredited IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, and that Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced rather than paper-driven. Each subject group is marked against four criteria, A to D, on an eight-point scale, and a report that reads 5-6-4-5 tells you far more than a percentage would. Students who cruise through MYP on classroom participation often meet the Diploma's written demands unprepared, which is the single most common reason an MYP 5 family in Sharjah starts tutoring.
programmes.countryNote: Victoria International School of Sharjah runs the IB continuum, and families in Al Rahmaniya who choose it are usually planning a Diploma two or three years ahead. Tutoring at MYP 4 and 5 here works best aimed at the criteria the Diploma will reuse: structured written argument, the command terms, and the research discipline that the Personal Project exposes before the Extended Essay does.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across HL and SL, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Internal Assessment carries roughly a fifth to a quarter of the grade in most subjects and falls due while teaching is still running, so DP1 collapses for students who treat coursework as a later problem. The May session is the one UAE schools sit; November exists as a route but is rare here.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student in Al Rahmaniya typically commutes out of the community to school, which compresses the usable evening to a narrow window. Online one-to-one fits that window where a travelling tutor cannot, because the lesson starts when your child sits down rather than when a car clears the Maliha Road junction. Subject specialists for HL sciences and Mathematics AA are the scarcest part of the Sharjah pool.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-rah.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Al Rahmaniya enquiries concentrate in. Each note says what the assessment actually rewards and where marks leave the page, because that is the information a parent cannot get from a subject list.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The proof-heavy IB maths route. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers and a far deeper calculus option. Marks leave on unjustified steps rather than wrong answers: a correct final line with no working earns a fraction of the method marks. Students arriving from a CBSE or MYP background usually need the written reasoning rebuilt before any new content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-active work. The graphical display calculator is not optional and the examiner expects it used, cited and interpreted. The common failure is treating AI as the easy route: SL AI still demands clear interpretation of regression and hypothesis testing in sentences, which is where answers go thin.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and the data-based paper decide grades. HL candidates lose marks describing a mechanism in words where arrows, charges and lone pairs are required. The Internal Assessment needs a research question narrow enough to control one variable properly, which is where most Sharjah students need the earliest help.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward students who draw the situation before writing an equation. Paper 2 extended response marks go to candidates who state the assumption they are making; the rest write a correct number and stop. Uncertainty treatment in the practical work is a reliable source of lost IA marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume is the trap rather than the difficulty. Command terms separate grades: outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each demand a different shape of answer, and a student who writes everything they know about a topic scores less than one who answers the verb that was used.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks that prose cannot recover. Axes labelled, equilibrium shifted, the new point named. HL adds calculation and the policy evaluation that most candidates leave as assertion. The commentaries need real sourced articles and a clear link to one syllabus concept, not a summary of the news.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE 0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.description: Cambridge 0580 Extended and Pearson 4MA1 cover similar ground with different paper structures. Extended candidates lose marks on transformations, bounds and the non-calculator arithmetic that nobody practises. A tiering decision made wrongly in Year 10 caps the grade before the student has sat anything.

subjects.name: Physics (IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the widest mark spread. Candidates describe a circuit instead of calculating it, or quote a formula without rearranging. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards students who have actually handled apparatus, which is a real consideration for anyone studying online.

subjects.name: Chemistry (IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and the qualitative analysis tables are where Extended marks concentrate. Students who learn the ion tests as a list rather than as observations forfeit easy marks. The six-mark extended answers need a structure, not a longer paragraph.

subjects.name: English Language and Literature
subjects.levels: IGCSE First Language and IB Language A
subjects.description: Directed writing and the unseen commentary both test control of register. Marks move when a student stops retelling the text and starts naming the effect of a specific choice. For IB Language A, the Individual Oral collapses without two well-chosen extracts and a global issue that is genuinely arguable.

sections.heading: What a "near me" search actually returns in Sharjah
paragraphs: A local search for an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Al Rahmaniya returns three kinds of result, and only one of them is what the parent wanted. The first is a directory listing filtered by distance, which ranks a university student in University City above a Chemistry HL specialist in another emirate purely on kilometres. The second is an agency page naming every area in Sharjah in a footer list, where Al Rahmaniya appears because a template inserted it. The third is a tuition centre with premises, which is a genuinely local option but a group one, with a fixed timetable your child's school day may not fit.

None of those three results tells you the thing that determines whether the tutoring works, which is whether the person teaching has taught the exact paper your child is entered for. That gap is not an accident. Distance is easy to publish and subject depth is not, so the market publishes distance. A parent in Al Rahmaniya then does the sensible thing with the information available and books the closest option, which is how a family ends up with a general maths tutor working on a student entered for Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 4.

The honest reframing is to treat the question as a supply question. Al Rahmaniya is a villa community, not a city centre, and the pool of people within a short drive who have taught Physics 0625 Extended or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL is genuinely thin. Widen the radius to all of Sharjah and it improves. Drop the radius entirely and match on subject and board instead, and the pool becomes large enough that your child gets a specialist rather than a generalist who happens to live nearby.

That is the trade this page is making the case for. You give up the idea of someone arriving at the villa, which IB Gram does not offer in the UAE in any case, and in exchange your child gets a tutor chosen for having taught the syllabus rather than for a postcode. The lesson happens over live video on Gulf Standard Time, the first one is free, and if the match is wrong you say so and the match changes rather than the schedule limping on.

sections.heading: Three questions that test whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Parents are told to check qualifications, and qualifications are worth checking, but a degree certificate does not reveal whether somebody has taught the current specification. Three questions do, and they take four minutes in a trial lesson. Ask them of any tutor, including ours. The point is not to catch anybody out; it is that a tutor who has genuinely taught the paper answers these instantly and specifically, and one who has not gives you an answer about enthusiasm.

The first question is which syllabus code your child is sitting. A tutor who teaches IGCSE Chemistry should want to know whether it is Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1 before discussing anything else, because the papers differ and so does the practical assessment route. The second is where candidates lose marks in that subject. A specific answer names a topic and a mark-scheme behaviour. A vague one names revision. The third is what the Internal Assessment or coursework criteria are called, letter by letter, with the marks attached.

The table below sets out what a thin answer and a strong answer sound like, so you can tell them apart in real time. Use it in the free trial lesson. It is also a reasonable filter for a tuition centre or an independent tutor you found through a community group, and it is more useful than a star rating, because a rating tells you about somebody else's child and this tells you about the person who will be teaching yours.

One more practical note for Al Rahmaniya families specifically. Bring your child's most recent marked paper to the trial lesson, not the report card. A report card is a summary written for a parent; a marked paper shows a tutor exactly which marks were available and which were left behind, and a specialist will start diagnosing from it within a minute or two.

sections.heading: Is the tutor legally permitted to teach privately in the UAE?
paragraphs: This is the question almost nobody asks and it is the one with real consequences. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The u.ae guidance is explicit that it is granted free of charge for two years, and that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure you see quoted for it is somebody's guess.

The eligibility list is wider than parents expect. It includes teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. That last category matters in this part of Sharjah, because University City sits a short drive from Al Rahmaniya and undergraduate tutoring is a visible local market. A university student with a permit is operating properly; the question is whether they have taught your child's paper.

There is a separate restriction that catches families out. A school teacher may not take paid private tutoring work with students enrolled at their own school. Abu Dhabi's ADEK has set professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff to that effect, as reported by Gulf News, and the permit itself carries a code of conduct on the same point. So the offer of your child's own class teacher, privately, after hours, is not the inside track it sounds like. Treat it as a reason to look elsewhere.

MoHRE's own service page, "Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing", lists the application route through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a two-working-day completion time and no fee. That page is where a parent can read the current position rather than taking a tutoring website's word for it, including this one.

sections.heading: Online one-to-one against an in-home visit in Al Rahmaniya
paragraphs: The in-home option is real and parents are right to weigh it. What they are rarely shown is the arithmetic. Market rates reported for in-home one-to-one tuition in the UAE run roughly AED 180-350 in Bestimate's 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 an hour, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. The gap between those bands is not a quality premium. It is travel, priced into the hour.

For Al Rahmaniya that travel is a specific number rather than an abstraction. A tutor coming from Sharjah city or across the Dubai border is committing to a round trip through the Maliha Road and E311 junctions at exactly the hour they are busiest. A tutor absorbing ninety minutes of driving for a sixty-minute lesson either charges for it or restricts how many students they take, and in both cases the parent pays. Online, that ninety minutes stays in the day and the lesson can start at the hour your child is actually ready.

The second effect is the one that matters more. Travel caps the pool. If the tutor has to reach your villa, your choice is limited to specialists willing to drive to Al Rahmaniya on a Tuesday, which for Chemistry HL or Mathematics AA HL may be nobody at all. Remove the drive and the constraint becomes the timetable instead of the map. That is the whole argument, and the table below sets it out without flattering the online option on the points where it genuinely loses.

To be plain about those losses: a very young child, a student who needs physical apparatus in front of them, or one who cannot be left to work independently between sessions is better served face to face, and we say so when an enquiry looks like that. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE, so there is no version of this page where that recommendation is a sales pitch.

sections.heading: Where subject cover runs thin, and what happens then
paragraphs: No tutoring platform covers every subject at every level at every hour, and the ones that imply otherwise are the ones you discover the truth about in week three. The honest position is that cover is deep in the subjects most students take and thin in the ones few take. For an Al Rahmaniya enquiry, mathematics, the three sciences, economics and English are reliably covered at both IB and IGCSE level. Narrower combinations are where the answer sometimes has to be no, or not this term.

The subjects that go thin in the Sharjah pool are predictable: Further Mathematics, Computer Science at HL, Music, Design Technology, Global Politics, the second and third languages beyond French and Spanish, and Business Management at HL during coursework season. Arabic as a first language is a specific case, because KHDA requires that teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education in Dubai private schools hold the appropriate approval from KHDA, which sets a genuine standard for anyone teaching those subjects seriously.

What we do when cover is thin is say so at the enquiry stage rather than booking you in and improvising. In practice there are three outcomes. The subject is covered and a specialist is free, in which case a trial lesson is scheduled. The subject is covered but the only specialist has no slot in your child's window, in which case you are told what the realistic alternative times are. Or the subject is not covered at the level you need, in which case the answer is no, with a suggestion of where else to look.

That third outcome is published deliberately. The competitor audit behind this page found no UAE tutoring site that discloses a coverage limit anywhere, and several that route UAE parents to overseas phone numbers rather than admit where delivery happens. A disclosed limit is worth more to you than an undisclosed promise, because it is the one you can plan around.

sections.heading: SPEA, and what the Sharjah regulator actually controls
paragraphs: Parents in Sharjah hear three regulator names and are rarely told which one applies to them. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, as the UAE government's own private-schools guidance states. Dubai's equivalent is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which oversees the quality of private education there. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in those three emirates, and Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge.

The Sharjah position has a feature that matters more than inspection ratings. The same government guidance records that the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum and fee approval, not merely inspection, sits with the emirate. For an Al Rahmaniya parent that means a question about why a school teaches a particular board, or why a fee has changed, has an address in Sharjah rather than in Dubai or at federal level.

This also explains why your neighbour's experience may not transfer. A family that moved from Al Nahda into a Dubai school is now dealing with KHDA; a family whose child is at a Sharjah school is dealing with SPEA; and a child sitting exams as a private candidate deals with the exam board directly regardless of either. Three different bodies, three different processes, one community. Knowing which one you are actually under saves a great deal of misdirected effort.

One thing a tutoring service cannot do is borrow any of that authority. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB or Cambridge, and no honest page would imply it is. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. It is not something an online matching service holds, and the phrase "regulator-approved tutors" should make any parent close the tab.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch on an IA or Extended Essay
paragraphs: This is the boundary that decides whether tutoring helps a Diploma student or ends their Diploma. IB academic-honesty rules make the assessed work the student's own, and a student who submits material they did not produce faces a malpractice finding. The research behind this page found a site in this market selling completed Internal Assessments outright. That is not a cheaper version of tutoring. It is a different product with a different outcome, and the student carries the consequence rather than the seller.

The useful line is between method and product. A tutor can teach the criteria and what each letter actually rewards. A tutor can discuss three candidate research questions and explain why two of them cannot be controlled with school apparatus. A tutor can read a draft the student wrote and mark it against the published criteria, then say which paragraph fails to meet Evaluation and why. A tutor can teach referencing properly, model a worked example on a different topic, and rehearse the supervisor meeting. None of that touches the student's authorship.

What a tutor must not do is supply text. Not a paragraph to insert, not a rewritten conclusion, not a method section drafted on the student's behalf, not an edit so heavy that the voice changes. The student writes every word of the exploration, the essay and the commentary. Where a draft is weak, the feedback names the criterion and the problem and sends the student back to it. That is slower than the alternative and it is the only version that is safe.

For an Al Rahmaniya family the practical consequence is scheduling. Coursework support has to start early enough that the student has time to do the writing themselves. A Chemistry IA begun eight weeks out can be taught properly; the same IA begun ten days before the school deadline leaves no honest route, and anyone promising one at that point is promising something else. Start the research-question conversation in the term before the deadline, not the week of it.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies alongside IGCSE
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed for. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidelines required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Sharjah families see the same subjects on the timetable.

Parents in Al Rahmaniya often treat these as the subjects that do not count, and then discover in Year 11 that they occupy real timetable hours and real homework evenings. The organisational rules are specific. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language.

There is also a content restriction worth knowing before buying any material. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. So a tutor working in this space teaches the school's own prescribed material and the skills around it, rather than importing a parallel syllabus. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided weekly totals are met, and the guidance advises at least twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

The equivalency angle closes the loop. Gulf Today reported that for the British track, Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five accredited subjects required at grade E or 3 for Ministry of Education equivalency. So these subjects matter for the school report and the timetable, and separately your child needs five other subjects at the stated grade for the equivalency count. Those are two different requirements and conflating them is a common and expensive mistake.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB or IGCSE tutor near me in Al Rahmaniya?
faqs.answer: There are tutors near Al Rahmaniya, including independent tutors and undergraduates from nearby University City, and tuition centres a short drive away in Muwaileh and Sharjah city. Whether one of them has taught your child's exact paper is a separate question, and in a villa community this size the honest answer for HL sciences or Extended-tier maths is often no. IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes; lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That removes distance from the shortlist so the match can be made on syllabus experience instead, which is the variable that changes a grade.

faqs.question: How do I check a Sharjah tutor is allowed to teach privately?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and ask to see it. UAE government guidance states the permit is granted free of charge for two years, so there is no cost reason for a tutor not to have one, and people tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. MoHRE's own service page, Private Tutor Licensing, lists the application route and a two-working-day completion time. Separately, a school teacher may not take paid tutoring work with students enrolled at their own school.

faqs.question: What do tutors around Al Rahmaniya charge per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market figures, not ours. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180-350, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500. Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 online. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 at the budget end, usually meaning a university-student tutor. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. The spread between the in-home and online bands is largely travel priced into the hour rather than a difference in teaching quality, which is worth knowing before you compare quotes.

faqs.question: Which exam series will my child in Sharjah actually sit?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge International, UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The February/March series is offered in India only, so any UAE page quoting a February exam window or a late-November entry deadline for it is giving you a date for another country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. For the IB Diploma, the May session is the one UAE schools sit, with November as an uncommon alternative. Always confirm the current dates on cambridgeinternational.org, qualifications.pearson.com or with your school's exams officer, because provisional timetables are revised.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work as well for a Sharjah student?
faqs.answer: For a secondary student working towards written papers, the evidence from how these lessons actually run is that it works well, because the limiting factor is the quality of the diagnosis rather than the room. The tutor marks a paper on screen, annotates it live, and the student keeps the file. Where online is weaker is with young children, students who need physical apparatus in front of them, and students who will not work between sessions without supervision. IB Gram offers no in-home option in the UAE, so when an enquiry looks like one of those cases we say so rather than selling around it.

faqs.question: My child is at a school in Muwaileh. When can a session start?
faqs.answer: Most British-curriculum schools in the Muwaileh and Al Tai arc finish in the early-to-mid afternoon, and the run back to Al Rahmaniya is short outside peak. In practice that puts a realistic first slot somewhere from late afternoon, with Diploma students usually better served after seven once they have eaten and done school homework. Because lessons are online there is no travel to absorb on either side, so a ninety-minute session at eight in the evening is as workable as one at five. Tell us the time your child is actually home and we schedule from there.

faqs.question: What can an Al Rahmaniya tutor do on a Chemistry Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the assessment criteria letter by letter, help your child narrow a research question to something controllable, explain what Evaluation actually rewards, and read and mark a draft your child produced. A tutor cannot supply text, rewrite a section, or edit to completion. Under IB academic-honesty rules the work must be the student's own, and submitting material produced by somebody else risks a malpractice finding against your child. Some sites in this market sell finished Internal Assessments; that is a different product with a serious consequence attached, and the student carries it rather than the seller.

faqs.question: Which regulator covers my child's school in Al Rahmaniya?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, so a Sharjah school sits under SPEA. UAE government guidance also records that the Sharjah authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is broader than inspection alone. If your child commutes to a Dubai school the relevant body is KHDA instead; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under ADEK, Ras Al Khaimah under its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah under the federal Ministry of Education. Knowing which applies saves a lot of misdirected enquiries.

faqs.question: Is a university-student tutor from University City good value?
faqs.answer: At the right level, yes. University students are explicitly eligible for the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and the budget end of the UAE market, around AED 45-150 an hour on published competitor rates, is largely this group. For Year 7 to Year 9 maths or structured homework supervision that can be sensible. For a Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 4 entry or a Chemistry HL Internal Assessment it usually is not, because the work needs somebody who has marked those papers against the published mark scheme. Match the tier of tutor to the tier of assessment.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist covers my child's subject?
faqs.answer: You are told at the enquiry stage. Cover is reliable in mathematics on both IB routes, Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Economics and English at IB and IGCSE level. It runs thin in Further Mathematics, Computer Science at HL, Music, Design Technology, Global Politics and the less common languages. When the subject is covered but no slot fits your child's evening, you get the realistic alternative times instead of a booking that quietly fails. When it is not covered at the level you need, the answer is no and a suggestion of where else to look.

faqs.question: Does Al Rahmaniya have an IB World School inside it?
faqs.answer: No. Al Rahmaniya is a villa community and its children travel out to school, with the nearest IB continuum provision at Victoria International School of Sharjah in Al Hoshi and most British-curriculum options sitting in the Muwaileh and Al Tai arc. That geography is part of why tutoring supply inside the community is thin: tutors cluster where schools cluster. It is also why an online match makes more practical sense here than in a dense school district, since the constraint on a Diploma evening is the commute home rather than the tutor's address.

faqs.question: From Al Rahmaniya, how many IGCSE passes does the equivalency count need?
faqs.answer: Gulf Today reported the Ministry of Education requirement for the British track as passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One competitor page in this market publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring service performs, so confirm the current rule on the Ministry's own channel before acting.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan or the Sharjah mock season?
faqs.answer: Yes, and both are planned for rather than worked around. During Ramadan families commonly move sessions to a post-Iftar slot, which an online lesson can absorb without anyone rearranging a drive. Mock weeks usually mean pausing new content and switching to marked-paper work, or dropping a week and picking the same tutor up afterwards. The fixed weekly slot exists so there is something to move; it is not a contract to sit in the same chair at the same minute for a year. Tell the tutor the mock dates as soon as the school publishes them.

faqs.answer: No, and no tutoring service should claim otherwise without the permit number to show. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument for training institutes with premises in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. What matters for a parent is the individual tutor's MoHRE private tuition work permit and their subject record. Treat the phrase "regulator-approved tutors" as a warning sign rather than a credential.

faqs.question: What should I bring to the free trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Your child's most recent marked past paper or assessment, with the marks and comments still on it, and the syllabus code from their exam entry. A report card summarises; a marked paper shows exactly which marks were available and which were left behind, and a subject specialist will start diagnosing from it in the first few minutes. Bring the school's assessment calendar too, if you have it, because the next deadline shapes what the first few sessions should cover. The trial lesson is free, with no card required and no obligation to book afterwards.

intro.heading: Sorting by syllabus instead of by distance
paragraphs: Al Ramtha is in the older central-western part of Sharjah, with schools nearby and a long-established tutoring market around it. A parent here can find somebody to teach their child quickly. What a distance-sorted list cannot tell you is whether any of those people knows where marks are actually lost in the course your child is taking, which is the only question that affects the grade.

Marks in these qualifications go in specific, repeatable places. In IGCSE chemistry, mole ratios taken from the wrong species, electrolysis products guessed rather than reasoned, and observations written as conclusions. In physics, parallel circuits and gradients read off a graph rather than calculated. In an IB science internal assessment, a research design with uncontrolled variables and an evaluation that lists limitations without weighing them. None of that is mysterious, and all of it is diagnosable from one marked script by somebody who has taught the course.

The internal assessment side deserves particular attention, because it is where IB marks are quietly lost and where the least help is available locally. Assessment is against criteria by letter, each with published descriptors, and students who have not read them write earnestly in the wrong direction. A tutor who has supervised the component knows which criterion a draft is failing and can say so in one sentence; a generalist improves the prose and leaves the criterion untouched.

There is also a mechanical layer that families rarely see: word and page limits per component, the mapping between a syllabus topic and the paper it appears on, and the way a mark scheme allocates marks inside a single question. Each of those is public, checkable and useful, and knowing them changes how a student prepares. A four-mark explain question wants four linked statements, not one statement written four ways.

So this page is written from the syllabus up. It sets out where marks go topic by topic, what each internal assessment criterion rewards, where to confirm the limits that apply to your child's cohort, how to use a mark scheme at home, and the one habit - writing method out - that pays in both systems at once.

None of this requires a parent to learn any chemistry. The checks in the sections below are structural - does the tutor name topics or talk about confidence, does the student read the mark allocation before writing, has anybody read the criteria descriptors - and a parent can apply every one of them without opening a textbook.

Our delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with the match made on board, code and level. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring in a family's house is a service we offer only in India. For course-specific work that is an advantage, because the specialist in a narrow subject rarely lives within a short drive of any particular address.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-ram.subjectsIntro: IB subjects described by their failure modes rather than their content lists, because that is what a tutor needs to know and what a parent can check.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the lost marks, and extended responses are marked for precision rather than enthusiasm. In the internal assessment, uncontrolled variables in the research design cost more than an unambitious topic ever would.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields, with sign conventions and unstated assumptions causing most avoidable losses. Uncertainty treatment is the most neglected part of the investigation and among the quickest things to coach, which makes it efficient early work.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy, so the grade turns on command terms and data-based questions. Statistical treatment in the investigation is a recurring weakness: students collect data and then describe it rather than testing anything with it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Method must be written and justified, not implied - the single biggest adjustment for students arriving from a strong IGCSE background. The exploration fails most often on a question too broad to analyse properly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics, with technology expected. Interpretation is where marks go: explaining what a result means about the situation rather than restating the calculation.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy - axes labelled, shifts drawn - plus evaluation that reaches a judgement. The commentaries need one syllabus section applied tightly to one article rather than a general discussion of the news.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis and the individual oral. Orals fail when the global issue is too broad to anchor in two extracts, which is a selection problem rather than a writing one and therefore fixable in advance.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tools must be applied to the case rather than described. Students lose marks writing everything they know about a concept instead of using it to reach a judgement about the organisation in the question.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-ram.igcseSubjectsIntro: The Cambridge and Pearson side, described the same way - by where the marks go rather than by what the syllabus covers.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Mole ratios from the wrong species, electrolysis products guessed, organic conditions written vaguely, and the observation-versus-conclusion problem. The extended paper marks wording strictly, so precision recovers marks the student has already earned.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended · Single tier at Edexcel
igcseSubjects.description: Parallel circuits and gradients taken by reading a value rather than calculating over a large interval. The alternative-to-practical paper wants named instruments, variables, repeats and sources of error, and rewards a student who can narrate method.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Marks sit in command words and diagram work. Describe, explain and suggest ask for different things, and a candidate who answers all three the same way caps their long-answer marks regardless of knowledge.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Bounds, rearrangement under time pressure, and multi-step problems abandoned one operation early. Method marks are available in most structured questions and are routinely forfeited by candidates writing only an answer.

igcseSubjects.name: Coordinated Sciences (0654)
igcseSubjects.description: Three sciences in two grades with less teaching time per strand. The first job in any block is identifying which strand is dragging the grade, because there is no time to treat all three equally.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (0500)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing assessed on effect rather than summary, and a register that must shift with the task. Writing the same task twice and comparing against the mark scheme moves marks faster than reading more.

sections.heading: Where marks go in the sciences, topic by topic
paragraphs: A tutor's first useful act is to replace 'needs to revise more' with a list. The list is remarkably stable across cohorts and across schools, which is why a specialist can produce it from one marked script while a generalist needs a term to arrive at the same place.

In chemistry, three recurring problems. Mole calculations where the ratio is taken from the wrong species in the equation. Electrolysis where the product at each electrode is guessed from memory rather than reasoned from the ions present. And the language problem: a question asking what you would see wants 'a white precipitate forms', not 'it goes cloudy' and certainly not the conclusion 'so it is a sulfate'. The first is conceptual, the second is procedural and the third is a writing habit, and they need different treatment.

In physics, the losses cluster around circuits and graphs. A candidate who can state Ohm's law still mishandles a parallel branch. A candidate who has drawn a line of best fit still reads a value off it instead of calculating a gradient across a large interval. And on the alternative-to-practical paper, answers about 'measuring carefully' go unrewarded where the scheme wants a named instrument, a repeat and a control.

In biology, command words dominate. Describe asks for what happens, explain for why with a mechanism, suggest for a reasoned possibility in unfamiliar context - and a candidate who treats them as synonyms limits their long-answer marks regardless of how well they know the content. Data questions compound it: students describe a trend when the question asks them to account for it.

sections.heading: What each internal assessment criterion rewards
paragraphs: IB internal assessments are marked against criteria identified by letter, each with published descriptors, and the single most useful hour a tutor spends on assessed work is reading those descriptors with the student before anything is written. Students who meet the criteria only after a first draft comes back have usually written in the wrong direction for weeks.

In the sciences, the criteria cover the design of the research, the analysis of the data, the conclusion and the evaluation. Each fails in a characteristic way. Research design fails on uncontrolled variables and a question too vague to answer. Data analysis fails when processing is presented without uncertainty. Conclusions fail when they state what the student expected rather than what the data supports. Evaluation fails as a list of limitations with no weighing of which mattered.

In mathematics, the exploration is assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The failure pattern differs: students choose a topic too broad for genuine analysis, then narrate rather than reflect. Reflection in particular is widely misunderstood as describing what was done instead of evaluating what it showed and what it could not show.

In the Middle Years sciences the criteria address knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on impacts. The last two are where diligent students lose levels, because school tasks often reward the first two and students generalise from that. The exact descriptors and any mark allocations for your child's cohort are in the subject guide and task sheets the school issues - ask for them, and read them, because they change between syllabus cycles and the school's version is the authoritative one.

sections.heading: Limits, lengths and where to confirm them
paragraphs: Every assessed component has a length constraint, and students meet them late and inaccurately - usually from a rumour in a group chat rather than from the subject guide. Getting this right is administrative rather than intellectual and it protects marks.

The practical rule is that the only limits worth working to are the ones in the current guide and task sheet your school issues for your child's cohort. These documents change between syllabus cycles, so a figure quoted on a tutoring site, including this one, can be out of date by the time a student reads it. We therefore name the components and tell you where to confirm the number rather than publishing figures that might age badly.

What is generally true across components is worth knowing. Exceeding a stated limit does not usually earn a penalty in the form of lost raw marks so much as it costs the student the marks in the sections an examiner stops reading, and it signals an inability to select - which several criteria specifically reward. Under-length work is a clearer problem: it usually means a criterion has not been addressed at all.

The second mechanical point is mark allocation inside a question, which applies to papers rather than coursework. A four-mark explain question wants four linked statements. A two-mark calculate question usually has a method mark and an answer mark, which means a bare answer forfeits half of it. Students who read the mark allocation before writing make measurably fewer structural errors, and it takes one session to establish the habit.

sections.heading: Reading a mark scheme at home
paragraphs: A parent does not need subject knowledge to be useful here. Mark schemes are written for markers, and they are more readable than they look: each acceptable point is listed, with alternatives in brackets, and the mark allocation sits beside it.

The practical method is to have your child complete a question under timing, then sit with the scheme and ask them to award their own marks aloud, point by point. Two things happen. The student discovers that a vaguely correct sentence does not earn a listed point, which is the whole lesson about precision. And you discover whether the problem is knowledge, wording or time - which decides what kind of help to buy.

Resist the temptation to be generous, which is strong and understandable. A mark awarded for effort now is a mark not earned in June. If you cannot tell whether a point is close enough, note the question and ask a specialist to arbitrate; that is exactly the kind of thing a single diagnostic session resolves quickly.

One constraint to respect: syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. Your child's school is the proper route to the current versions, and we cite the official sources rather than distributing copies. A tutoring service offering a shared drive of 'exclusive' board material is handing out somebody else's copyright, and where the material is unreleased it creates a malpractice question attached to your child rather than to the seller.

sections.heading: The habit that pays in both systems: write the method
paragraphs: If a single behaviour change were available across the IB and the British track, it would be this one: write the method out, every time, in full sentences or in labelled working, whether or not the answer seems obvious.

On a British-track paper, structured questions carry method marks. A candidate who writes a bare answer to a four-mark question is competing for one mark. In IB mathematics, method must be written and justified rather than implied, which is the biggest adjustment for students arriving from a strong IGCSE background where speed was rewarded. In an IB science investigation, method is a criterion in its own right.

The reason students resist is that writing method feels slower, and in the short term it is. In practice it saves time in exactly the situations where time is lost: a long multi-step problem where an arithmetic slip early on would otherwise force a complete restart. With method written, the error is visible and the remaining marks are intact. Without it, the student starts again and the clock wins.

This is also the clearest example of why course experience matters more than subject knowledge. A professional engineer can solve the physics; a teacher who has marked the papers knows that the mark is for the line of working the engineer skipped. Those are different kinds of expertise, and only one of them raises a grade.

A parent can enforce this habit without knowing the subject. Look at a page of your child's working and ask whether a stranger could follow the reasoning from the first line to the answer. If the page is mostly numbers with no visible steps, the marks are being left on the table, whatever the final answer says.

sections.heading: Why the specialist is rarely the nearest person
paragraphs: Everything above describes a narrow kind of expertise: a specific course, its paper structure, its criteria and its mark scheme. The population holding that expertise for any one course is small and distributed by where those people happen to live, not by where demand appears.

For Diploma subjects the arithmetic is stark in this emirate. Sharjah has a limited number of schools authorised for the programme, so the number of adults here who have supervised a particular DP internal assessment through a full cycle is low. The subset willing to drive to a central-western district on a weekday evening is lower still. Requiring both proximity and criterion-level experience usually means getting neither.

The money points the same way. Across published UAE rate cards, a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, while an in-home visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed, and named or examiner-branded tutoring reaches AED 500 to 650 and above. The in-home premium pays for a journey; it does not buy knowledge of a criterion descriptor, and examiner status is seldom evidenced and never transfers to your child's paper.

So we match on the course and deliver one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE - that service exists only in India - and the free trial lesson is how a family establishes whether the format suits their child before committing to anything.

sections.heading: What a tutor must not do, however the deadline looks
paragraphs: A page this focused on criteria and mark schemes should be equally precise about limits, because the pressure to cross them arrives late and dressed as practicality.

A tutor may read criteria with a student, question a research question until the available data can answer it, teach a statistical or practical technique, review a draft and explain which criterion it fails, model the same analytical move on different material, mark papers against the published scheme, and drill command terms. That is a wide and genuinely useful remit.

A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit any part of assessed work, nor supply a topic with the analysis already done. IB Gram does not sell completed internal assessments, extended essays, Theory of Knowledge essays or coursework. Services that do appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the malpractice finding attaches to the student's diploma rather than to the seller's accounts. No deadline alters that arithmetic.

Two further limits. No tutor can know what a particular candidate will score, so there are no grade guarantees here and no promised improvements. And we claim no approval, licence or accreditation from any education authority or board: IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform with no premises in this country. Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods - a body we can describe and would never claim to be endorsed by.

faqs.question: What does a subject specialist know that a good general tutor does not?
faqs.answer: Where the marks are. A specialist can say that chemistry candidates lose marks taking a mole ratio from the wrong species, that physics candidates read gradients instead of calculating them, and that an IB evaluation criterion fails when limitations are listed without being weighed. A general tutor teaches the content competently and leaves those habits in place. You can test this in one conversation: ask for the three topics where candidates lose the most marks and listen for a list rather than a reassurance.

faqs.question: How do I find out which criteria my child's internal assessment is marked against?
faqs.answer: From the subject guide and the task sheet the school issues for your child's cohort. In IB sciences the criteria cover research design, data analysis, the conclusion and the evaluation; in mathematics the exploration is assessed on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Descriptors and any mark allocations change between syllabus cycles, so the school's current documents are the authoritative version - not a tutoring page, including this one.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks when their science answers look correct?
faqs.answer: Usually precision or method. A question asking what you would observe wants the observable change - 'a white precipitate forms' - not the conclusion drawn from it. Equations want state symbols, organic reactions want conditions, and multi-step calculations want working because the method carries marks. None of that is difficult science; all of it is a writing habit that changes within a few sessions once somebody marks strictly against the real scheme rather than generously.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper really testing?
faqs.answer: Practical skill expressed in writing: identifying variables, describing a method precisely, naming instruments, spotting sources of error and suggesting improvements. Candidates who have done plenty of laboratory work still lose marks here because they have never had to narrate a method, and answers about measuring carefully earn nothing where the scheme wants a named instrument, a repeat and a control. It is among the most coachable components in either system - three or four focused sessions usually show up in the next mock.

faqs.question: How should a parent use a mark scheme at home?
faqs.answer: Have your child complete a question under timing, then sit with the scheme and ask them to award their own marks aloud, point by point. They discover that a vaguely correct sentence does not earn a listed point, and you discover whether the problem is knowledge, wording or time. Mark strictly: generosity now costs marks in the series. Where you cannot judge whether a point is close enough, note it and have a specialist arbitrate - that is a good use of a single diagnostic session.

faqs.question: Why is 'show your method' such a big deal in both systems?
faqs.answer: Because marks are allocated to it. British-track structured questions carry method marks, so a bare answer to a four-mark question competes for one. In IB mathematics, method must be written and justified rather than implied - the biggest adjustment for students arriving from a strong IGCSE background. In an IB science investigation, method is assessed in its own right. Writing it also protects a student when an early arithmetic slip would otherwise force a complete restart under time pressure.

faqs.question: What are the word limits for the extended essay and other components?
faqs.answer: Each has one, and we deliberately do not publish figures here: limits and guidance change between syllabus cycles, so the only reliable source is the current subject guide and task sheet your school issues for your child's cohort. Ask for both. What is generally true is that exceeding a limit costs the student the sections an examiner stops reading and undermines criteria that reward selection, while under-length work usually means a criterion has not been addressed at all.

faqs.question: How many marks does a four-mark 'explain' question actually want?
faqs.answer: Four linked statements, not one statement written four ways. Reading the mark allocation before writing is one of the cheapest habits available: it tells a student how many distinct points to make, and it prevents the common pattern of one good idea expanded into a paragraph while three available marks go unclaimed. For calculate questions, assume a method mark and an answer mark unless the scheme shows otherwise, which means a bare numerical answer typically forfeits half the question.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover my child's IB science and IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if they have genuinely taught both. The courses fail differently: an IB investigation is marked against criteria by letter, while a Cambridge candidate faces an alternative-to-practical paper and a tiered written structure. A tutor fluent in one may never have read a criterion descriptor or taught the practical paper's technique. Ask what each has taught and how recently, and where the honest answer is only one of the two, two specialists in consecutive slots give better teaching for a similar total.

faqs.question: My child picks a huge topic for every project. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the highest-value hour in the whole assessed-work process. Over-broad questions are the commonest cause of weak explorations and investigations: a question that cannot be answered with the data available produces narration instead of analysis, and no amount of later writing rescues it. A tutor's legitimate job here is to question the research question until it is answerable, and to do that at the proposal stage rather than after a draft has absorbed three weeks.

faqs.question: Where should past papers come from?
faqs.answer: Your child's school, which has access to the current versions and knows which syllabus cycle applies. Papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB; we cite the official sources and point families to the school rather than distributing copies. Be cautious of any tutoring service offering a shared drive full of board material - that is somebody else's copyright, and where material is unreleased it creates a malpractice question attached to your child rather than to the seller.

faqs.question: Is a tutor allowed to rewrite a paragraph of my child's assessed work?
faqs.answer: No. A tutor may explain which criterion a paragraph fails, ask what the data actually supports, teach a technique the work requires, and model the same analytical move on entirely different material. Writing, redrafting or editing the submitted text is not permitted, and IB Gram does not sell completed assessments of any kind. The consequence of crossing that line is a malpractice finding against the student's diploma, so the boundary holds regardless of how close a deadline is.

faqs.question: How quickly do topic-level fixes show up in a mark?
faqs.answer: Technique changes - command terms, precision of language, method written out, mark allocation read before answering - usually appear in the next timed assessment, often three to six weeks away. Topic repairs take a little longer because they need teaching and then practice. What we will not do is quote a grade or a timeline for one: nobody can know what a particular candidate will score. The honest measure is movement on comparable timed work, reviewed at session six.

faqs.question: What if no specialist in our exact course is free when we need one?
faqs.answer: We say so and offer alternatives: a different hour with the right person, or a named date when one frees up. Narrow combinations - a higher level language, Additional Mathematics, a specific board's business paper at a peak evening hour - sometimes have nobody available, particularly in the weeks before a series. We will not substitute a generalist into course-specific work, because for criterion-level and paper-technique teaching that substitution is the entire problem this page describes.

intro.heading: The question behind the search box
paragraphs: Nobody typing IB IGCSE tutor near me in Al Suyoh actually wants the nearest person. They want somebody who has taught the paper their child is entered for, and they are using distance as a stand-in for competence because distance is the only thing the search box understands. The substitution is reasonable and it fails here more than in most places, because Al Suyoh is a plotted inland residential district rather than a school quarter, and its local pool of IB and IGCSE specialists is correspondingly thin.

It is worth being concrete about what thin means. Mathematics at Year 9 level has genuine local supply, including undergraduates from University City a short drive away. Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 4 has less. Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level has very little. Chemistry HL with an Internal Assessment in progress has almost none within a comfortable drive of Al Suyoh on a weekday evening. The pool does not shrink gradually as the level rises; it falls off a cliff at the point where the work stops being general and starts being specific.

This page does three things with that. It counts the pool honestly by subject and level, so you can see where a local search will work and where it cannot. It gives you a better search than near me, including the terms that actually surface specialists. And it sets out the checks worth running on anybody you find, whether through this page or a community group, because a tutor's permit position and their familiarity with the criteria are both verifiable in minutes and neither appears in a directory listing.

IB Gram's own position should be plain before any of that. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Sharjah school day. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is offered only in India. The URL you arrived on uses the phrase parents search, and the answer it gives is that the match is made on the syllabus rather than the map, which for this district is the only way a specialist becomes reachable at all.

One more thing belongs in an honest version of this page. There are enquiries that cannot be filled, and they are named rather than absorbed. If no specialist covers your child's subject at the level needed, or none is free in the evening window your school run leaves, you are told at the enquiry stage. The competitor research behind this page found no site in this market that discloses a coverage limit anywhere, which is precisely why a disclosed limit is worth considerably more to a parent than an undisclosed promise.

sections.heading: Counting the specialists actually within reach of Al Suyoh
paragraphs: A near me search returns a list without telling you how long it is, which is the single most misleading thing about it. The table below does the opposite: it states, subject by subject, how deep local supply around Al Suyoh realistically runs and where the specialist for that combination is more likely to be found. It is an honest assessment rather than a count of names, because any count published on a page like this would be unverifiable and this page does not publish unverifiable numbers.

The pattern is consistent across every inland Sharjah district. Supply is adequate where the work is general and the student population is large, which means lower secondary mathematics, English, and Core-tier IGCSE subjects. It thins where the work becomes specific: Extended-tier sciences, HL mathematics on either route, Additional Mathematics, and anything involving a live Internal Assessment. It effectively disappears in the genuinely narrow subjects, where even a city-wide search in Sharjah returns nobody.

What the table implies for a parent is a decision rather than a disappointment. Where local supply is adequate, a local tutor is a perfectly sensible choice and worth pursuing through school parent groups and community boards. Where it is thin, a distance-based search will produce either nobody or a generalist presenting as a specialist, and the better route is to drop the distance filter entirely. Knowing which category your child's subject falls into is most of the decision, and nobody else in this market will tell you.

sections.heading: What to search instead of "near me"
paragraphs: If the search term is the problem, a better term is the cheapest possible fix. Searching the syllabus code rather than the subject changes the results immediately: 0580 Extended, 0625, 4MA1, 4CH1. Anybody who writes about those codes has taught the papers, because nobody markets using a number they do not use daily. The same is true of criterion language. A page that explains what Criterion D of a science Internal Assessment rewards was written by somebody who has marked one.

Searching the assessment rather than the subject works similarly. An exploration, a commentary, an Individual Oral, a Paper 3 option topic: each of these is a phrase used by teachers and students and essentially unused by lead-generation sites. It filters out the directory listings that rank for every area name in Sharjah, including Al Suyoh, because a template inserted it rather than because anybody there teaches your child's paper.

The third improvement is to stop treating a star rating as information. A self-published rating tells you what somebody else's child experienced in a subject that may not be yours, and in this market the research found providers displaying two different ratings and review counts on the same page, and one showing five out of five from twenty reviews against a claim of thousands of students. None of that is checkable. A tutor's answer to a question about the criteria is checkable in four minutes, which is why it is worth more.

Finally, search for the thing most sites hide, which is the delivery model. A UAE page that routes you to an overseas phone number is delivering from somewhere other than where it implies. A page that states plainly how lessons happen is giving you the information you need to plan. This one states it: one-to-one over live video, Gulf Standard Time, no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

sections.heading: IB and IGCSE in one household: one tutor or two?
paragraphs: Al Suyoh households frequently have both boards running at once, often because children started at different schools or a move happened mid-education. The natural instinct is to find one tutor who can cover both, and in a narrow set of cases that works. In most cases it does not, and the table sets out which is which. The deciding factor is whether the two children are working towards the same kind of assessment, not whether they are studying the same subject.

Where one tutor is viable is in the mathematics continuum at the lower end: a Year 9 student and a Year 10 Core-tier student can reasonably share a tutor, because the content overlaps and the assessment demands are similar. Where it stops being viable is the moment one child's work involves criterion-marked coursework. A Diploma exploration and an IGCSE terminal paper need different expertise, and a tutor doing both is doing one of them less well.

The scheduling argument usually pushes families towards one tutor, and that argument is weaker than it looks. Two specialists booked consecutively interrupt the evening once, not twice, which is the only practical benefit a single tutor offered. Because nobody is travelling, back-to-back slots cost nothing to arrange, and each child gets somebody who has actually taught their paper.

What should never drive the decision is a bundle price. A package covering two children in three subjects looks efficient and usually means one of the five combinations is being taught by somebody working it out as they go. Buy the matches you need separately and keep the ability to stop one without disturbing the other.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, for both routes
paragraphs: Families in Al Suyoh with children on either board eventually meet the equivalency question, usually when a university application makes it urgent. The British-track requirement was set out clearly in Gulf Today's July 2026 report: candidates must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, and must show either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That detail matters because at least one competitor page ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong against the reported rule. A parent planning a subject load on a wrong number either over-enrols a child or panics unnecessarily. The exclusion of Arabic and Islamic education from the count also surprises families, who reasonably assume that mandatory subjects count towards everything.

The American track has its own thresholds, also reported in the same article: English proficiency via a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in that reporting, and nothing on this site publishes one, because any figure for the IB route would need to be read on the Ministry's own channel first. An unsourced number in a place like this is worse than no number.

Two further points are worth stating plainly. Equivalency is a Ministry process and a tutoring service neither performs it nor guarantees an outcome in it; this page describes it and points you to the official channel. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, so any page implying urgency about it is manufacturing pressure about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: What the first six weeks should produce
paragraphs: Parents in Al Suyoh ask how long before they see something, and the honest answer is that six weeks is enough to know whether the match is right, and not enough to see a grade move. Those are different things and conflating them leads families to abandon tutoring that was working or persist with tutoring that was not. The useful question at six weeks is whether the tutor can tell you something specific about your child that you did not already know.

A right match produces that. After six sessions a specialist should be able to name the topics that have settled, the topics that have not, and the specific behaviour costing marks: unjustified steps in a maths proof, command terms ignored, a mechanism described in words where arrows are required, a conclusion that restates rather than evaluates. That is a diagnosis, and it is checkable against your child's next marked paper. If instead you hear that your child is working hard and improving steadily, you have a report rather than a diagnosis.

The second thing six weeks should produce is a changed agenda. The topics covered in weeks five and six should not be the ones anybody planned in week one, because the first fortnight should have revealed something. A schedule that follows its original plan unchanged is a schedule nobody is reading the evidence from.

The third is a decision point. At six weeks there should be an explicit conversation about whether to continue, change frequency, change subject or stop. Tutoring that renews by default is tutoring nobody is evaluating, and in a household budget it becomes a standing cost with no review. If the honest answer at six weeks is that the sessions are not the intervention this student needed, that is worth hearing, and a service with nothing to sell beyond the next session has no reason to say it.
bullets: Six weeks tells you whether the match is right, not whether the grade moved

sections.heading: Verifying a tutor in three checks
paragraphs: Whoever you hire, including through this page, three checks are worth running and none of them takes long. The first is the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE. UAE government guidance states it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists application through its smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Because it is free, there is no cost explanation for a tutor not holding one.

The second is the specification. Ask which syllabus code your child is entered for and listen to whether the tutor already wanted to know. A tutor who treats Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 as the same subject has not taught both, and a tutor who asks which option topic the school chose has. This check takes one question and separates the pool more reliably than any credential on a profile page.

The third is the criteria. Ask what the coursework criteria are called and what they are worth. For a Diploma science Internal Assessment the answer involves criterion letters and a mark total; for an IGCSE the answer depends on whether the subject carries coursework at all, and a tutor who knows that it does not is demonstrating the same knowledge. People who use the criteria weekly have them memorised. People who have read about them do not.

One restriction belongs alongside these checks. A school teacher may not take paid private work with students enrolled at their own school. Abu Dhabi's ADEK has set professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff to that effect, as reported by Gulf News, and the permit carries a code of conduct making the same point. The apparent shortcut of hiring your child's own teacher privately is not available, and the current wording should be confirmed with the school or the regulator rather than taken from any tutoring site.

sections.heading: Moving from IGCSE into the Diploma, and the gap to close
paragraphs: A good proportion of Al Suyoh enquiries that arrive as near me searches are really transition questions. A student finishing IGCSE is choosing Diploma subjects, or has started DP1 and found the step larger than expected. The gap is real, it is predictable, and it is subject-specific rather than general, which means it can be closed deliberately instead of absorbed over a year of struggling.

In mathematics the step is from procedural fluency to written justification. An Extended-tier candidate who could execute methods reliably meets a Higher Level course where the marks sit in the reasoning between the steps, and the first set of DP1 assessments punishes that. In the sciences the step is from recall to analysis, with the Internal Assessment demanding an experimental design the student has never been asked to produce. In the humanities it is from describing to evaluating, which is a writing problem rather than a knowledge one.

The practical consequence is that the most useful tutoring in a transition year is often short and early. Two or three sessions before subject selection, looking at real marked IGCSE work rather than predicted grades, can change an HL choice that was going to cause two years of difficulty. A further block in the first term of DP1 on written justification or experimental design closes the gap while it is still small. Both are cheap compared with rescuing a position in DP2.

Choosing between Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation deserves its own conversation, and it should be driven by the student's intended degree as well as their current fluency. Some university courses expect the analysis route; an Al Suyoh family should check the specific requirement with the universities on their child's list rather than relying on a general rule, because the requirements differ by institution and by programme and they change.
bullets: Maths: procedural fluency to written justification, which is a technique gap
Sciences: recall to experimental design, exposed first by the Internal Assessment

Check the AA or AI expectation with the actual universities on the list

sections.heading: Where authorship ends and tutoring begins
paragraphs: Any page offering both IB and IGCSE help has to be explicit about this, because the boundary is where the market's worst behaviour lives. The research behind this page found a provider in the UAE selling completed Internal Assessments at a four-figure price. A student who submits work they did not produce risks a malpractice finding, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on the seller. That is not a premium tier of tutoring; it is a different transaction with the risk transferred.

The legitimate version is substantial. A tutor explains the criteria letter by letter with the marks attached, before any drafting starts. A tutor discusses candidate research questions and rules out the ones that cannot be controlled with available apparatus. A tutor teaches referencing properly, models the method on an unrelated topic, reads a draft the student wrote and marks it against the published criteria, then names the criterion that is unmet and sends the student back to it. A tutor rehearses the supervisor meeting.

What a tutor does not do is supply text, in any quantity or disguise. Not a paragraph to insert, not a rewritten conclusion, not an edit heavy enough to change the voice. The student writes every word. This is slower than the alternative and it is the only version in which the qualification the student receives is earned and safely their own.

For Al Suyoh families the scheduling implication is the same one that runs through this page: start early. A coursework block begun eight weeks before a school deadline can be taught. The same block begun ten days before cannot, and at that point the only remaining offers are the ones no honest service makes. Ask about the research question in the term before the deadline, not the week of it.
