faqs.question: Are there really IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Al Suyoh?
faqs.answer: Some, and the count depends entirely on the level. Lower secondary mathematics and English have genuine local supply, including undergraduates from nearby University City. Core-tier IGCSE subjects are reasonably covered. Extended-tier sciences, HL mathematics on either IB route, and anything with a live Internal Assessment have very little local supply in an inland plotted district like this one. IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes; lessons run one-to-one over live video, which removes distance from the shortlist so the match can be made on who has taught the paper.

faqs.question: What should I search for instead of a tutor near me?
faqs.answer: Search the syllabus code rather than the subject: 0580 Extended, 0625, 0620, 4MA1, 4CH1. Nobody markets using a code they do not use daily, so it filters out directory pages that list every Sharjah area from a template. Search the assessment too, using the words teachers use: exploration, commentary, Individual Oral, Paper 3 option topic. And ignore self-published star ratings, which are unverifiable and in this market sometimes contradict each other on the same page. A tutor's answer about the criteria is checkable in minutes.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover an IGCSE child and a Diploma child in Al Suyoh?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but less often than families hope. Two children on overlapping content with similar assessment demands, such as Year 9 maths and Year 10 Core-tier maths, can share a tutor sensibly. The moment one child has criterion-marked coursework the answer changes, because a Diploma exploration and an IGCSE terminal paper are different expertise. The scheduling argument for one tutor is weaker than it looks: two specialists booked consecutively interrupt the evening once, and since nobody is travelling, back-to-back slots are easy to arrange.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does the Ministry equivalency count need?
faqs.answer: Gulf Today reported in July 2026 that the British track requires passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One competitor page in this market publishes a six-subject figure, which conflicts with that reporting. Equivalency is a Ministry process, so confirm the current rule through its own channel before planning a subject load.

faqs.question: Why is there no IB equivalency points figure on this page?
faqs.answer: Because no official source for it has been read. The reporting used for the British and American tracks states no IB points threshold, and the IB's own site returns an access error to automated checking, so publishing a number would mean guessing on a page a parent might act on. Any site that quotes an IB equivalency figure should be asked where it read it. The right route is the Ministry of Education's own channel or the emirate attestation authority, and tutoring is not a requirement of that process in any case.

faqs.question: What should six weeks of tutoring have produced?
faqs.answer: A diagnosis, not a grade. After six sessions a specialist should be able to name which topics have settled, which have not, and the specific behaviour costing marks: unjustified steps in a proof, a command term ignored, a mechanism written in words where arrows are required. That is checkable against the next marked paper. If what you hear instead is that your child is working hard and improving steadily, you have been given a report rather than a diagnosis, and it is worth asking a sharper question.

faqs.question: How do I check an Al Suyoh tutor holds the right permit?
faqs.answer: Ask to see the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. UAE government guidance states it is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists application through its smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Because the permit costs nothing, there is no cost explanation for its absence. People tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule is published, so quoted amounts are unverified.

faqs.question: Is the step from IGCSE to the IB Diploma as big as people say?
faqs.answer: It is real and it is specific rather than general. In mathematics the step is from executing methods to justifying them in writing, and the first DP1 assessments punish students who cannot. In the sciences it is from recall to experimental design, which the Internal Assessment exposes immediately. In the humanities it is from describing to evaluating, which is a writing problem. Because the gap is predictable it can be closed deliberately, usually with a short block before subject selection and another in the first term of DP1.

faqs.question: Should my child take Mathematics AA or AI?
faqs.answer: It depends on the intended degree as much as on current fluency. Analysis and Approaches is the proof-heavy route with a deeper calculus option; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics with the graphical calculator used throughout. Some university courses expect the analysis route, and the requirement differs by institution and by programme and does change, so an Al Suyoh family should check with the actual universities on their child's list rather than relying on a general rule. A session reading real marked work is more useful than predicted grades here.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram visit homes anywhere in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. Lessons for Al Suyoh families are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Sharjah school day. For this district that is also the format that solves the real problem, since the constraint is the thinness of the specialist pool within driving distance rather than the availability of somebody general. If your child needs an adult physically present, the honest advice is to hire that locally.

faqs.question: What if no tutor covers my child's subject at the level we need?
faqs.answer: You are told at the enquiry rather than booked in and improvised with. Cover is reliable in mathematics on both IB routes, Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Economics and English across both boards. It is thin in Further Mathematics, Computer Science at HL, Music, Design Technology, Global Politics and the less common languages. Where a subject is covered but no slot fits your child's window, you get the realistic alternative times. Where it is not covered at that level, the answer is no with a suggestion of where else to look.

faqs.question: Can a tutor in Sharjah finish an Internal Assessment under time pressure?
faqs.answer: No, and the offer is a warning sign rather than a service. Under IB academic-honesty rules the work must be the student's own, and submitting material produced by somebody else risks a malpractice finding against the student, not the seller. The research behind this page found a UAE provider selling completed Internal Assessments outright. What is legitimately available is the criteria explained with their marks, help narrowing a research question, referencing taught properly, and a marked draft with instructions on what to rewrite.

faqs.question: Can my child's class teacher tutor them privately in Al Suyoh?
faqs.answer: Not if the child is enrolled at that teacher's school. Abu Dhabi's ADEK has set professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibiting paid private tutoring of students at their own school, as reported by Gulf News, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct making the same point. A teacher may tutor other students outside school hours with the permit in place. Confirm the current policy wording with the school or the regulator rather than relying on any tutoring website, including this one.

faqs.question: Which exam series should an Al Suyoh family plan around?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge International, the June series with November as the resit route; the February/March series is offered to India only, so any date quoted for it belongs to another country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. For the IB Diploma, UAE schools sit the May session. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, so get the version your child's centre uses from the school's exams officer before fixing a revision plan.

intro.heading: What "near me" is really standing in for
paragraphs: The phrase "tutor near me" is a proxy. Nobody actually wants proximity for its own sake. What a parent in Al Taawun wants is someone reliable, someone who will turn up, and above all someone who knows the specific course their child is failing. Distance got used as a filter because for decades it was the only filter available, and a tutor who lived in Al Majaz could be checked on by asking a neighbour.

That filter has a cost, and in a Sharjah tower district the cost is sharp. Restrict the search to tutors willing to drive to Al Taawun at 5pm and the list shrinks to perhaps a dozen people across all subjects and both curricula. Ask that list for a Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606 specialist, or an IB Diploma Chemistry HL tutor who can coach the Internal Assessment without crossing the integrity line, and the list usually shrinks to zero. The proxy has filtered out the thing it was meant to find.

Al Taawun's own geography makes this worse than it sounds. The district is a band of residential towers along the Al Khan lagoon, close to the Al Mamzar crossing into Dubai. Many children here attend Dubai schools and come home through that crossing, which puts the end of their day past 6.30pm. A tutor who must also drive is competing with the same traffic. The slots that remain are the ones nobody wants.

So the honest answer to "is there anyone near me who actually knows this syllabus" is: possibly, for the common subjects, and probably not for the specific paper your child is losing marks on. Which is why this page spends its length on a different question — how do you test syllabus knowledge before you pay for it? That test takes one conversation and it works regardless of where the tutor sits.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. In-home visits are offered only in India. Al Taawun students are taught one-to-one over live video, with the past paper on a shared screen and the session timed in Gulf Standard Time. The point of that model is not convenience. It is that the pool stops being a dozen people who will drive to the lagoon and becomes everyone who teaches the course properly.

One framing worth keeping while you read. A tutor cannot be verified on distance, years of experience or a list of schools, because none of those can be checked from your side of the conversation. A tutor can be verified on whether they know the paper, and that is checkable in five minutes by anyone, including a parent who has never studied the subject.

Below: the four questions that separate a subject tutor from a syllabus tutor, what the IB and IGCSE routes in Sharjah schools actually require, where this tutor pool is genuinely deep and where it is thin, and what a parent can verify independently before any money changes hands.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-taa.programmesIntro: An Al Taawun search that names both IB and IGCSE usually comes from a household where the two sit side by side — siblings in different schools, or a student who moved from one system to the other. The programmes below are the ones that actually appear in this catchment, with what each demands of a tutor.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment marked against published criteria lettered A onward. A DP tutor has to know those criterion descriptors by letter, because that is how the work is marked and how a draft is diagnosed.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. IB exam and results dates are not restated on this page because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than none — confirm every DP date with your school's IB coordinator. What is verifiable locally is the mandatory-subject requirement: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the Diploma in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each scored 0–8 and converted to a 1–7 grade by published boundaries. The MYP marks process and communication as well as answer accuracy, which is why strong students sometimes score 4s: the mathematics is right and the justification criterion is empty. A tutor who cannot name the four criteria for the subject is guessing.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP-to-DP step is the most common reason Sharjah families start tutoring in Year 11. MYP mathematics samples topics the Diploma assumes fluency in, and the jump into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level exposes that gap within a term. Al Taawun students moving between the two systems benefit from a diagnostic on the specific algebra and function work the DP course opens with.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two separate qualifications that parents and even school reports often merge. Cambridge codes are four digits — 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry. Pearson codes start with 4 — 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1. Tiering differs: Cambridge runs Core and Extended, Pearson Mathematics Specification A runs Foundation and Higher. The papers, the weightings and the question styles all differ with them.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November series for UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The November 2026 Pearson final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January — November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: The alternative post-16 route in several Sharjah schools, and often the comparison a family is making against the Diploma. Three or four subjects in depth rather than six in breadth, with no Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge. A student strong in two subjects and weak in languages usually does better here; a student who wants breadth and a university application narrative usually does better on the DP.
programmes.countryNote: MoE equivalency on the British track asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at a grade no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five. The equivalent IB figure is not published in that source, so it should not be stated without a Ministry page to cite.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-taa.subjectsIntro: These are the IB Diploma subjects Al Taawun families most often need, each with the thing a tutor must be able to name on first contact. If a prospective tutor cannot name it, they are learning the course at your expense.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-heavy route. At Higher Level, Paper 3 is an extended investigation and the single most common reason a predicted 6 becomes a 4. A tutor should be able to say what Paper 3 asks for and how it differs from Papers 1 and 2 before discussing rates.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-permitted work throughout. Students arriving from IGCSE Extended often assume it is the easier route and find the modelling questions unfamiliar. The exploration is marked on the same criteria as AA but rewards genuine data, which is where most of the lost marks sit.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level adds depth rather than breadth, and the additional topics are where HL students separate. Extended-response marks go to candidates who state the physical principle before the calculation. The Internal Assessment is assessed on experimental design and analysis, not on the result being correct.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the grade. Students lose marks writing equations without state symbols and describing mechanisms without curly arrows where they are required. A tutor coaching the IA must work on the student's own research question, never supply one written up.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms do the damage. Outline, explain, distinguish and discuss carry different mark expectations, and students who answer all four the same way plateau at a 5. The data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments are trainable and routinely untrained.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy plus the evaluation paragraph decide the grade. The Internal Assessment is a set of commentaries built on published news articles, and the recurring failure is choosing an article with no diagram-able economics in it. That choice is made in week one and cannot be fixed later.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral and Paper 1 unseen analysis are the two components tutoring moves most. Students lose marks by summarising a text rather than analysing how meaning is constructed. HL adds the essay, which is assessed on sustained argument rather than coverage.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the named organisation is everything; a textbook-perfect answer with no reference to the case scores in the bottom band. HL adds extension topics and a longer Paper 2. The Internal Assessment requires real organisational data, and sourcing that is the first real task.

subjects.name: Arabic (language acquisition and language A routes)
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools and available as a Diploma subject in its own right. Separate streams exist for Arab and non-Arab students because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, so material from one stream does not transfer to the other.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Both are coached, never written. TOK is assessed on an exhibition and an essay on a prescribed title; the Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece with a supervisor. A tutor's legitimate role is teaching the structure, questioning the argument and giving feedback on the student's own draft.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-taa.igcseSubjectsIntro: Alongside the Diploma, these are the IGCSE subjects most requested in this catchment, with the code to confirm with the school before any tutoring starts.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics
igcseSubjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: The tier decides the grade ceiling: Cambridge Core caps at C. Extended Paper 4 carries the structured questions where method marks are won and lost, and unshown working on a four-mark question typically scores one.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism account for most dropped marks, usually because a potential divider is read as a plain series circuit. Which practical route the centre uses — timetabled practical or alternative-to-practical — changes the revision plan substantially.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry
igcseSubjects.description: Mole calculations and organic pathways decide the grade. Cambridge examines qualitative analysis tables in detail and those are among the cheapest marks on the paper; Pearson leans harder on calculation.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology
igcseSubjects.description: Volume rather than difficulty. Extended-response marks go to students using mark-scheme vocabulary — partially permeable, active transport, selective reabsorption — rather than paraphrasing it in their own words.

igcseSubjects.name: English Language and Literature
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing is marked on audience, register and form as well as content. Reading questions require quotation plus explanation; a quotation on its own scores nothing. The Pearson anthology differs, so revision material does not cross over.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
igcseSubjects.description: Evaluation questions carry the top marks and need a judgement with a reason. Economics diagrams are credited separately for axis labels, shift direction and the new equilibrium, so a remembered sketch loses marks before the explanation begins.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science
igcseSubjects.description: Theory on data representation and networks is learnable and chronically under-revised while students spend their time coding. Pseudocode is marked against the syllabus's own conventions, not Python, which costs marks on trace tables.

igcseSubjects.name: Additional Mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Calculus, logarithms and trigonometric identities that 0580 never reaches. Treating it as harder 0580 practice is the standard mistake. Students who do well have drilled differentiation and the factor theorem deliberately.

sections.heading: Four questions that reveal whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: This is the whole test, and it takes about five minutes. Ask these four questions of anyone — local, online, agency or independent — and the answers sort the field faster than any credential list.

First: which board and which code does my child sit? A tutor who knows the course asks you this before you ask them, because it determines everything that follows. Second: what does the hardest component look like? For IB Diploma Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Paper 3 is an extended investigation and a tutor should be able to describe how it differs from Papers 1 and 2 without hesitating. For Cambridge 0580 Extended it is Paper 4 and the structured long questions.

Third: where do students usually lose marks in this subject, and how do you know? The useful answer is specific and diagnosable — unshown method on multi-mark questions, missing mark-scheme vocabulary in extended responses, potential dividers read as series circuits. The useless answer is "exam nerves" or "they need to build confidence". Fourth: what will you not do with my child's Internal Assessment? A tutor who cannot answer that cleanly is a risk, not a bargain.

Notice what is not on this list. Nothing about distance, nothing about years of experience in the abstract, nothing about how many students they have taught. Those are the easiest things for a weak tutor to be impressive about, and the hardest for a parent to verify.
bullets: Ask for the board and code first; a syllabus tutor asks you before you ask them
Ask them to describe the hardest component and what it rewards
Ask where marks are lost and how they diagnose it from marked work
Ask what they will refuse to do with coursework
Decline to be reassured by experience claims you cannot check

sections.heading: Where the Sharjah tutor pool is deep and where it is thin
paragraphs: This is the part of the "near me" answer nobody publishes, and it is the part that matters. Coverage is not uniform, and a parent who knows where the thin spots are can plan around them instead of discovering them in April.

Depth is real in IGCSE Mathematics, the three separate sciences, English Language and English as a Second Language. These are the subjects every curriculum needs and every tutor can teach, and in Sharjah the proximity of University City adds a genuine supply of competent subject help at the lower end of the market. For those subjects, a local search will find someone, and the four questions above will tell you whether the someone is any good.

Thinness starts where specialisation starts. Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 taught to the syllabus's own pseudocode, Accounting 0452, and IGCSE Arabic as a first language are all narrow pools. On the Diploma side, Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Economics with proper diagram coaching, and Theory of Knowledge are narrower still, because the DP is a small share of the UAE market — International Baccalaureate students were 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school population in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on UK curricula.

The practical consequence for Al Taawun: for a thin specialism, a radius search is the wrong tool entirely. The right tool is a wider pool and live video, and the right question to ask a provider is not "do you cover this" but "who specifically, and when are they free".

sections.heading: What a parent can verify independently, before paying
paragraphs: Most of what tutoring providers say about themselves cannot be checked. A few things can, and those are worth your ten minutes more than any amount of marketing.

The permit is checkable by asking. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Because it costs nothing, there is no innocent reason for a working tutor not to hold one.

The board and code are checkable with one email to your school's exams officer. The timetable is checkable the same way, and this one has teeth: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Any tutor quoting dates from a generic PDF is working from a document that may not apply to your child's centre.

Two claims are not checkable and should be treated as warnings rather than credentials. One is examiner status, which no provider should assert for an individual without evidence, and which should never be used to imply access to marking or paper content. The other is regulator approval. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed or partnered with SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises. Any tutoring service describing itself as regulator-approved should be asked to show the permit number.
bullets: Ask directly whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition permit
Get the board, code and tier from the exams officer in writing
Use only the zone-correct Cambridge timetable your centre issues
Treat unevidenced examiner claims and regulator-approval claims as red flags
Apply for the permit through MoHRE's own 'Private Tutor Licensing' service

sections.heading: Why distance stopped being a useful filter in a tower district
paragraphs: There is a version of the "near me" search that made perfect sense: a small town, one school, a maths teacher two streets over. Al Taawun is not that. It is a few hundred apartments per building in a district whose children attend schools in two emirates on two or three different curricula.

Run the arithmetic on a home visit here. The tutor approaches on Al Ittihad Road at the hour it is slowest, finds visitor parking that may be full, clears a security desk, and takes a lift in a building with several hundred flats. Fifteen minutes is a good run; forty is ordinary on a Sunday or Monday evening. That time is paid for either as a surcharge or inside an hourly rate, and the market reflects it: in-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 for the same tutor online, with Bestimate's Dubai table placing the usual in-home range at AED 180–350.

The erosion is not only financial. A session that starts twenty minutes late either finishes twenty minutes short or pushes the rest of the evening back, and in an exam year the evening has no slack to give. A live-video session starts when it says it starts. The student is at the table with the paper open; the tutor is on screen.

None of which means in-home tutoring is wrong for everyone. A younger child who cannot hold attention on a screen without an adult present is a genuine case for it. A Year 11 or Diploma student who already does all their homework on a laptop is not. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case, and says so here rather than after a booking.

sections.heading: IGCSE to Diploma: the transition that brings most Al Taawun families here
paragraphs: A disproportionate share of tutoring enquiries from this catchment come from one specific moment: a student who did well at IGCSE Extended arriving in Diploma Year 1 and dropping two grades in a term. It is not a mystery and it is not a sign the student has stopped working.

The gap is structural. IGCSE rewards accurate answers to bounded questions. The Diploma rewards justified reasoning on open ones, and it assesses that reasoning explicitly through Internal Assessment criteria and command terms. A student who scored A* on 0580 by being quick and accurate meets Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, where Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended investigation, and finds that speed is not the skill being tested.

The same break appears in the sciences. IGCSE Chemistry asks for the right product; Diploma Chemistry asks why the mechanism proceeds that way, with marks for state symbols, conditions and the reasoning in between. In Biology the command terms do the damage — outline, explain, distinguish and discuss expect different things, and a student answering all four identically settles around a 5 regardless of how well they know the content.

Tutoring that works on this transition spends its first sessions on the assessment architecture rather than the content: what the criteria actually reward, what a 7-standard paragraph looks like against a 5-standard one, and how to plan a Paper 3 investigation. That is a short piece of work done early, and an expensive one done late.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects nobody mentions in a tutoring search
paragraphs: A student in Al Taawun is not only doing IGCSE or the Diploma. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools, and they appear on the report card with everything else. Yet almost no tutoring provider in this market has a section on them, which is why a parent looking for help with Arabic grammar often finds nothing useful.

The requirements are specific. KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines state that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students, and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs. Those rules sit under a federal baseline: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must follow the Ministry's general regulations.

Two consequences follow for tutoring. First, the stream matters as much as the subject: material written for the first-language Arabic route does not serve a student on the additional-language route, and offering it does more harm than good. Second, content is constrained — for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so tutoring works through the school's own material rather than substituting its own.

Worth knowing as a credential point too: schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects. That is a real, checkable standard, and it is the kind of thing a parent can reasonably ask about.
bullets: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed curriculum
Separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students are required; combined classes are prohibited
Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from the five-subject MoE equivalency count
Tutoring works through the school's own material for these subjects, not substitute content
KHDA's instructional-time rules are built on a 40-minute lesson unit, with a 25-minute minimum advised

sections.heading: The honesty line on coursework, stated before you ask
paragraphs: Every family that reaches an Internal Assessment or an Extended Essay eventually meets an offer to make the problem go away. In this market that offer is explicit: one operator in the researched set sells completed Internal Assessments outright. It is worth naming what that actually risks, because the person who carries it is the student.

IB academic-honesty rules treat submitted work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the consequences land on the candidate's diploma, not on the seller's business. A page that is vague about this boundary is being vague deliberately, so here it is plainly: a tutor teaches the skill, explains the published criteria by letter, reads the student's own draft and says where it falls short. A tutor does not write, does not redraft to completion, and does not supply model text for submission.

The same boundary covers materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. They are available free through the school and from the boards themselves. A tutor's job is to work through them with the student and cite the source, not to host a download library.

This is a differentiator worth asking about explicitly, because it is the one question an essay mill cannot answer well. Ask a prospective tutor what they will refuse to do. A good tutor has the answer ready, and usually gives you more detail than you asked for.
bullets: Teaching the criteria and giving feedback on the student's own draft: legitimate
Writing, completing or supplying coursework text: never, at any price
Reproducing board materials as downloads: a copyright and malpractice exposure
Working through an official past paper together with the source cited: legitimate
Any grade promise attached to coursework support: a claim nobody can honour

sections.heading: How a match is made when the answer is honest
paragraphs: The least useful thing a tutoring service can say is "we cover everything". Coverage claims are free to make and impossible to check, and they are how families end up with a general science tutor in front of an Additional Mathematics candidate.

A match that means anything starts from three facts: the board and code, the tier or level, and the specific loss visible in the student's last marked paper. With those, the question becomes narrow enough to answer honestly — who teaches this paper, and are they free at a time an Al Taawun student can actually use after the school run or the Dubai commute home.

When the answer is no, there are three honest responses and one dishonest one. The honest ones: a different time with the right specialist, the right specialist teaching over live video from another time zone, or a plain statement that the match is not available this term. The dishonest one is a substitute presented as a match. Availability is also seasonal — the eight weeks before the main exam windows are the busiest hours in this market, and a tutor free in October may not be free in April at 5pm Gulf Standard Time.

The free trial lesson exists to test all of this at no cost. One session, no card, no commitment. The thing to judge it on is narrow: did the tutor identify the specific failure mode and say what the next four sessions will cover? If not, you have spent an hour instead of a term's fees finding out.
bullets: Match on board, code, tier and the loss visible in marked work
Slots are held weekly in Gulf Standard Time, including post-commute evening times
Thin specialisms get a wait or a different slot, not a substitute

process.description: One line: which board does my child sit for each subject, which syllabus code, and which tier. The answer takes a day and changes which tutor is right. It also gets you the zone-correct Cambridge timetable, which is the only version that applies to your centre.

process.title: Put the four questions to the tutor

process.title: Set the review point before the block starts
process.description: Agree in writing what each block is meant to fix and when you will look at it. Six weeks later, compare the next marked paper against the first. If the named loss has not moved, the plan changes or the tutor does.

faqs.question: Is there actually an IB or IGCSE tutor near me in Al Taawun who knows my child's syllabus?
faqs.answer: For common subjects — IGCSE Maths, the sciences, English — yes, a local pool exists, helped by University City nearby. For specialisms it is much thinner: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 taught to the syllabus's pseudocode, Higher Level Diploma sciences and Theory of Knowledge are narrow pools anywhere in Sharjah. Restricting the search to people willing to drive to a tower at 5pm narrows it further. The practical answer is to widen the pool rather than the radius: live-video teaching makes the specialist reachable even when nobody nearby teaches that paper.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor in the first five minutes to see if they know the course?
faqs.answer: Four things. Which board and syllabus code does my child sit, and what tier? What does the hardest component look like, and what does it reward? Where do students usually lose marks in this subject, and how do you diagnose that from marked work? And what will you refuse to do with my child's Internal Assessment or coursework? A tutor who knows the course asks you the first question before you ask them. Vague answers about confidence and exam nerves are the signal to stop.

faqs.question: Do you send a tutor to apartments in Al Taawun?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Sharjah or anywhere else in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Al Taawun students are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run or the return journey from a Dubai school. The gain is not convenience alone. The tutor pool stops being the handful of people who will drive to the lagoon and becomes whoever teaches your child's specific paper properly.

faqs.question: How do I find out which exam board my child's Sharjah school uses?
faqs.answer: Email the school's exams officer and ask for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for each subject. Schools in this catchment enter both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel, sometimes different boards for different subjects within the same year group, and a report card showing "Mathematics" tells you none of it. The same email should get you the centre's own timetable, which matters because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and says it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong version.

faqs.question: My child got A* grades at IGCSE and is struggling in Diploma Year 1. What went wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually nothing about effort. IGCSE rewards accurate answers to bounded questions; the Diploma rewards justified reasoning on open ones and assesses that reasoning explicitly through criteria and command terms. A student who scored top grades by being fast and accurate on 0580 meets Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, where Higher Level Paper 3 is an extended investigation, and discovers speed is not the skill being measured. The fix is short if done early: work on the assessment architecture first, content second.

faqs.question: Are tutors in Sharjah legally required to hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Since the permit costs nothing, a working tutor has no innocent reason not to hold one, so ask.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who lives in another country really teach my child's Sharjah syllabus?
faqs.answer: The syllabus is set by Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, not by the emirate, so a tutor who teaches 4PH1 or Diploma Chemistry at Higher Level teaches the same specification wherever they sit. What has to be local is the operational detail: the school's own assessment calendar, the centre's zone-correct timetable, Gulf Standard Time scheduling, and the mandatory UAE subjects running alongside. Those are things a tutor is briefed on. What cannot be imported is subject depth, which is exactly why widening the pool helps.

faqs.question: What subjects are hardest to find a tutor for in this part of Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Cambridge Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 marked against the syllabus's own pseudocode conventions, Accounting 0452, and IGCSE Arabic as a first language. On the Diploma side, Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and Theory of Knowledge support. International Baccalaureate students were 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school population in 2024-25 against 37 per cent on UK curricula, which is why DP specialists are a smaller pool across the region. Book these early; April availability is not October availability.

faqs.question: Is a tuition centre in Sharjah better than one-to-one for an IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: A centre is good at broad syllabus revision and genuinely cheaper per hour, at roughly AED 90 to AED 180 in this market. It is poor at individual misconceptions, because the group moves at the syllabus's pace rather than the student's. If your child's problem is that they do not show method on multi-mark questions, a group will not catch it. There is also a logistics cost that rarely gets counted: a centre is a second school run, in the evening, on the roads the first one used.

faqs.question: What does a tutor do about Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the main curriculum?
faqs.answer: First, establish which stream the student is on. KHDA's mandatory-subject guidelines require separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibit combined classes because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Material from one stream does not serve the other. Second, work from the school's own material: for mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited. These subjects are also excluded from the five-subject equivalency count.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's Extended Essay or Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: With the thinking, the structure and the feedback — yes. With the writing — no, at any price. A tutor explains the published criteria by letter, questions the argument, reads the student's own draft and says where it falls short of the descriptors. A tutor does not write it, redraft it to completion, or supply model text for submission. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; the malpractice consequence of that falls on the candidate's diploma, not on the seller.

faqs.question: How quickly can a tutor start for a student in Al Taawun?
faqs.answer: For a common subject at a standard evening time, days. For a thin specialism or a specific slot in exam season, longer, and you should be told so rather than offered a substitute. The sequence is: send the last marked paper, confirm board and code with the school, take a free trial session over live video, then agree a block. Slots are held weekly once agreed. Families who book the exam-season hour in autumn keep it; those who wait for the mocks take what is left.

faqs.question: Should I be worried that a tutor claims to be an examiner?
faqs.answer: Treat it as a claim to evidence, not a credential. Examiner status should not be asserted for an individual whose current position cannot be shown, and it should never be used to suggest access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because no legitimate tutor has that. The same applies to regulator approval: SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB and Cambridge do not accredit tutoring platforms in that way, and a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to institutes with premises.

faqs.question: How do I know after six weeks whether the right tutor was found?
faqs.answer: Look at marked work for the specific loss you started with. Before the block begins, get the failure mode in writing — unshown method on structured questions, missing mark-scheme vocabulary, command terms answered identically. Six weeks later, read the next marked paper or school assessment for that same loss. If it has moved, the match is right. If it has not, change the plan or the tutor. Sessions that feel productive while the same marks keep vanishing are how a term gets spent for nothing.

intro.heading: Two comparisons, very different stakes
paragraphs: There are two questions inside this search and they get tangled together. The first is geographic: would we be better served in Muwaileh, or Aljada, or further into Sharjah? The second is curricular: our child is on one system and could have been on the other, so which tutoring actually matters, and does a tutor who claims both really have both?

The geographic comparison resolves quickly, and this page does not pretend otherwise. Al Zahia is villa and townhouse housing immediately west of Muwaileh, with City Centre Al Zahia alongside and established routes into the main campuses. Those routes feed the Maliha Road corridor at the hour several large schools release, which puts a settled household at around half past five. Move to Aljada and the picture is near identical. Move to Muwaileh and you are closer to the gates and inside the worst of the dismissal traffic. Move out to Tilal City and an in-home weekly hour stops being practical at all.

What does not move across any of those streets is the pool of people who have taught IB Diploma Physics at Higher Level, or marked a Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper, or coached an Economics commentary against its criteria. That supply is set emirate-wide by how many people have ever taught those specific courses, and in the IB's case it is small: International Baccalaureate students were 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school population in 2024-25, against 37 per cent on UK curricula, across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula.

So the geographic answer converges, which leaves the curricular comparison as the one worth real space. It matters because the two systems are genuinely different products, assessed differently, recognised slightly differently by the UAE Ministry of Education, and supported by different kinds of tutor.

That difference is also where families get misled. A tutoring service that lists both the IB and IGCSE as capabilities is making a claim that costs nothing to make. The useful test is specific and this page sets it out: ask what each system's marking unit is, and whether the tutor has worked from a mark scheme or from lettered criteria. One answer belongs to each system, and someone who has only ever seen one of them will hedge.

The other thing this page carries, because nobody else in this market does, is the regulator map. Which authority governs private schools in each emirate, what each one controls, and what that means if your family moves within the UAE — a question households in these newer Sharjah communities ask constantly and find no answer to.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. In-home tutoring is offered only in India, and there is no UAE office or centre. Al Zahia students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-zah.programmesIntro: Four routes appear in this catchment and families regularly hold two of them at once. Described below by what each demands rather than by what it promises.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across six groups, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, with Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service alongside. Breadth is compulsory: a language, a humanity, a science and mathematics all have to be carried. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked against lettered criteria whose marks are added separately, and up to three further points come from the TOK and Extended Essay combination.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No Diploma exam or results date is published here because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than none; take every one from your school's IB coordinator. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the Diploma in UAE private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, which adds to an already wide load.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The two-year pre-16 stage on the British route, assessed by terminal written papers. Cambridge uses four-digit codes with Core and Extended tiering; Pearson uses codes beginning with 4 and reports grades 9 to 1. Subject count is flexible — typically eight to ten — and there is no compulsory breadth rule, so a student can weight heavily towards the sciences or the humanities from the age of fourteen.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November series for UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026 and results reaching students in January. Cambridge assigns every centre to one of six timetable zones and cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong version.

programmes.name: AS and A Level
programmes.description: The British post-16 route and the Diploma's direct alternative. Three or four subjects in depth, no compulsory breadth, no Extended Essay and no Theory of Knowledge. Entry to a subject usually assumes a strong Extended or Higher tier grade in it. For a student who is excellent in two areas and weak elsewhere, the ability to drop the weak areas entirely is the central difference from the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor states six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's pre-16 stage and IGCSE's structural counterpart, assessed internally against four criteria per subject scored 0–8 and converted to a 1–7 grade. Where IGCSE produces external certificates at 16, the Middle Years Programme generally does not, which is the practical difference families notice when moving schools or countries mid-stage.
programmes.countryNote: Some UAE schools run the Middle Years Programme alongside IGCSE entries in certain subjects, giving students external certification as well as internal criteria grades. Whether your child's school does this is worth establishing, because it changes what evidence they carry if the family moves, and it changes what a tutor should be working towards in Years 10 and 11.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-al-zah.subjectsIntro: The subjects most requested across both systems in this catchment. Each entry names what the assessment rewards, because that is where the two routes genuinely diverge.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, functions and calculus, with Higher Level Paper 3 an extended investigation. The exploration is marked on communication, presentation, reasoning and personal engagement, and the last of those is routinely left empty by capable mathematicians who treat it as decoration.

subjects.name: IB Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-permitted work throughout. Different from Analysis and Approaches rather than easier, and the choice between them should be checked against the entry requirements of the actual universities on the student's list.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms carry the grade, with marks for conditions and reasoning rather than products alone. The Internal Assessment credits the student's own research question and method design, which is a planning skill rather than a chemistry one.

subjects.name: IB Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level extension topics separate candidates, and extended responses reward stating the physical principle before calculating. The Internal Assessment credits design and uncertainty handling, so the accepted value carries no marks by itself.

subjects.name: IB Biology
subjects.description: Command terms do most of the damage: outline, describe, explain, distinguish and discuss expect different structures and mark counts. Data questions on unfamiliar experiments are trainable without content knowledge and are rarely trained.

subjects.name: IB Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Both are decided by evaluation: a judgement with a reason attached. Economics credits diagrams piece by piece — axes, shift direction, new equilibrium — and Business Management credits application to the named organisation above all else.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics — 0580 / 4MA1
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge's structured paper carries the multi-mark questions where method is credited independently of the answer. Pearson splits marks evenly across two papers, so pacing failures are unrecoverable. Tier sets the ceiling: Cambridge Core caps at grade C.

subjects.name: IGCSE Sciences — 0625 / 0620 / 0610 and 4PH1 / 4CH1 / 4BI1
subjects.description: Cambridge centres run either a timetabled practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, which changes half the revision plan. Pearson concentrates most routes into written papers. Mark-scheme vocabulary is credited in all of them.

subjects.name: IGCSE English — 0500 / 0510 / 4EA1
subjects.levels: First Language and Second Language routes
subjects.description: Reading answers need quotation plus explanation of effect; writing is marked on audience, register and form as well as content. Set texts and anthologies differ by board, so revision does not transfer across a school or board change.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.levels: First language and additional language routes
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside either curriculum in UAE private schools. Separate streams exist for Arab and non-Arab students because expectations and the language of instruction differ, so material does not transfer between them.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: The components with no British-route equivalent, worth up to three points between them. Both are coached through feedback on the student's own drafts against published criteria, and the reflection-record marks on the Extended Essay are the most commonly lost in the whole Diploma.

sections.heading: The area comparison, resolved quickly
paragraphs: Taking this first so the rest of the page can be about the thing that matters. Three variables genuinely differ between Al Zahia and its neighbours, and all three are logistical.

Session timing is the first. Al Zahia households are typically settled around half past five because the routes into the community feed the Maliha Road corridor at dismissal. Muwaileh families are nearer the gates and inside the worst of it. Aljada is near identical to Al Zahia. Tilal City and the Dhaid-corridor communities are later again.

In-home visit practicality is the second. A villa or townhouse with gate security and a driveway is the easiest visit to execute; an apartment adds visitor parking and a lift; a community far out adds travel the tutor has to be paid for. Market in-home rates run AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel inside the figure against AED 150 to AED 300 online for a qualified tutor, with Bestimate's Dubai table putting the usual in-home case at AED 180 to AED 350.

Group provision is the third, and the only one where geography genuinely decides availability, because a group needs a room and enough students nearby to fill it. That clusters around established schools, so Muwaileh wins and the newer communities do not.

None of those three changes who has taught IB Diploma Physics at Higher Level or marked a Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper. That is the point of this section: the area comparison is real, small, and not the reason your child's grade is where it is.

sections.heading: The comparison that matters: IB against the British route
paragraphs: This is the real question behind a lot of searches that name both systems, and it is usually asked badly — as though one route were better. They are different, and the right answer depends on the student in front of you.

The Diploma requires breadth. Six subjects across six groups means a language, a humanity, a science and mathematics are all carried to the end, and a student who is excellent at three things and weak at two cannot drop the two. A Levels allow exactly that: three or four subjects chosen freely, and the weak areas disappear at sixteen.

Assessment differs more than most parents realise. IGCSE and A Level grades come from terminal written papers marked against a mark scheme, point by point. The Diploma puts a substantial share of each grade in internally assessed work marked against lettered criteria added separately, plus up to three points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination. One system rewards performance on a day; the other rewards sustained production across two years.

Workload shape follows from that. The British route concentrates pressure into exam season. The Diploma spreads it across parallel internal deadlines that cluster unpredictably, which suits an organised student and punishes a disorganised one much harder than A Levels do.

Neither is easier. The honest version is that the Diploma is harder to manage and the British route is harder to specialise out of a weakness on — and that a student's organisational habits are a better predictor of which suits them than their raw ability in any subject.

sections.heading: What the UAE Ministry of Education actually asks for
paragraphs: Equivalency is the part of this comparison families worry about and get least reliable information on, including from ranking competitor pages that publish the wrong figure.

On the British track the requirements are published and specific. Students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Alongside that, equivalency asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

The American track has its own published thresholds, which is worth knowing because households in these communities often hold more than one curriculum between them. English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT; mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For the IB, the position has to be stated honestly: the source that publishes the British and American figures states no IB points threshold, so no Diploma equivalency number appears on this page. Anyone quoting one to you should be asked which Ministry page it came from.

And the boundary of what any tutoring service can do here: equivalency is a process to describe, not to perform or guarantee. Take your own case to the Ministry or the emirate attestation authority, and treat tutoring that implies it is required for equivalency as making a false-urgency claim about a regulatory process.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what happens if you move
paragraphs: Households in these newer Sharjah communities move more than average — between emirates, between schools, sometimes both in a year — and the regulator question comes up every time. Almost nobody in this market answers it, so here it is.

Five authorities cover UAE private schools between them. Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain fall under the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education there. And the Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The remits are not identical, which is the part that matters practically. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods — so curriculum and fee approval, not just inspection, sits with the emirate regulator. That is why a Sharjah school's subject offer can differ from a Dubai school's a short drive away.

Dubai's own position is worth knowing for comparison, since many families here consider a move across the border. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6 per cent.

What none of this means is that any tutoring service is approved by any of these bodies. IB Gram is not approved, accredited, licensed by or partnered with SPEA, KHDA, ADEK, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific licence issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai.

sections.heading: Switching systems mid-course, and what it costs
paragraphs: Families in this catchment switch more often than the brochures suggest — a move between emirates, a school place that opens, a realisation in Year 11 that the Diploma's breadth will not suit. The switches are survivable and they are not free.

The commonest is IGCSE into the Diploma, which is a change of assessment model rather than content. A student who scored top grades by being fast and accurate on bounded questions meets criterion-marked internal work and open questions, and the first report is often two grades worse without anything having gone wrong. Four to six sessions on assessment architecture in the first term usually resolves it.

The reverse switch — Middle Years Programme into IGCSE, or Diploma Year 1 into A Levels — has a different gap. The Middle Years Programme generally produces no external certificates at 16, so a student moving into an IGCSE year group may be entering exams with less familiarity with terminal written papers and with mark-scheme precision than classmates who have been drilled on them for two years.

Changing exam board inside IGCSE is the most underestimated switch of all. Cambridge and Pearson cover overlapping content with different papers, different tiering language and, in English, entirely different set texts and anthologies. A year of literature revision does not transfer, and a term of practice on the wrong board's archive teaches question shapes that will not appear.

In every case the first action is the same: establish exactly what the new school enters and at what level or tier, in writing, before buying any tutoring. The cost of not doing that is a term of the wrong preparation, which is more expensive than any rate difference on the page.

sections.heading: Testing a tutor who claims both systems
paragraphs: A tutoring service listing both the IB and IGCSE as capabilities is making a claim that costs nothing. Testing it costs about three minutes and the test is the same whether the person is an agency, an independent or an undergraduate.

Ask what the marking unit is in each system. For IGCSE the answer is the mark scheme, awarded point by point, with method marks independent of the final answer. For the Diploma the answer is lettered criteria with their own descriptor bands, added separately, which is why strength in one criterion cannot compensate for another being empty. Someone who has worked in both systems gives both answers immediately. Someone who has worked in one hedges or merges them.

Then ask a system-specific follow-up. For IGCSE: what does the structured Mathematics paper reward that the short-answer paper does not, or what does the alternative-to-practical paper want beyond describing a result? For the Diploma: name the criteria for this Internal Assessment and say what each one rewards.

Then the boundary question, which matters in both systems: what will you refuse to do with my child's coursework? A tutor may explain criteria, question an argument, read the student's own draft and name where it falls short. A tutor may not write submitted text, redraft to completion or supply model answers. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, and the malpractice consequence of using that falls on the candidate's diploma rather than on the seller.

A candidate who passes all three is worth hiring for either system. One who passes for a single system is worth hiring for that system, which is a perfectly good outcome — it just means a two-system household needs two people.

sections.heading: The mandatory subjects and the permit, in either system
paragraphs: Two pieces of local context that apply identically whichever curriculum your child is on, and which almost no page in this market covers.

First, the mandatory subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools. KHDA's guidelines require separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and state that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is taught in Arabic for Arab students and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs.

The tutoring consequences are concrete. The stream is part of the match, because material for the first-language route does not serve an additional-language student. And content is constrained: for the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, so the work runs through the school's own material. KHDA calculates instructional time for these subjects on a 40-minute lesson unit, advising at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson, and requires that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach them.

Second, the permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any figure quoted to you as unverified.

One related restriction, press-reported rather than taken from the policy document: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE code of conduct carries a similar bar. The principle is sound whichever emirate you are in.

sections.heading: Starting, and what honest availability looks like
paragraphs: Four steps, and the first two cost nothing.

Establish what your child actually sits. For the Diploma: subject, level, and the school's internal deadline calendar from the IB coordinator. For IGCSE: board, syllabus code, tier and the science practical route from the exams officer, plus the centre's own exam timetable. Those documents decide which tutor is relevant and which archive is useful.

Then send the last marked piece of work and read it yourself first. Where marks went matters more than the grade, and the patterns point at different purchases: blanks mean content, wrong answers mean understanding, right answers with no reasoning mean habit, and marks collapsing late in a paper mean pacing.

Then take a free trial session over live video, at a time that survives the Al Zahia dismissal journey — 5.30pm at the earliest, 6pm with two school runs. Judge it on whether the tutor engaged with your documents and named a specific loss rather than discussing confidence.

And expect honesty about availability. Diploma Higher Level sciences, Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Theory of Knowledge support, Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 pseudocode and Accounting 0452 are all thin pools, and the eight weeks before either system's main window are the busiest hours in the market. The honest options when a match is not free are a different slot with the right specialist, that specialist over live video from another time zone, or a plain statement that it is not available this term.

faqs.question: Would we find a better tutor in Muwaileh or Aljada than in Al Zahia?
faqs.answer: For group classes and content help, marginally — provision clusters around established schools and University City's undergraduate supply keeps the budget band genuinely low nearby. For specialist teaching in either system, no. The pool of people who have taught IB Diploma Physics at Higher Level or marked a Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper is the same short list across the whole emirate. Moving fifteen minutes adds travel and content tutors, not specialists.

faqs.question: Which is harder for a student, the IB Diploma or IGCSE and A Levels?
faqs.answer: Neither, and the honest framing is different. The Diploma is harder to manage: six subjects with compulsory breadth, parallel internal deadlines that cluster unpredictably, plus Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. The British route is harder to specialise out of a weakness on at sixteen, but then lets a student drop their weak subjects entirely. A student's organisational habits predict which suits them better than their raw ability in any single subject does.

faqs.question: Does a tutor visit homes in Al Zahia?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits in Sharjah or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and there is no UAE office or centre. Al Zahia students are taught one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the mark scheme or criterion descriptors on a shared screen. Since the specialist pool does not vary between these communities anyway, the online format is what makes the specialist reachable at all.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry of Education require?
faqs.answer: Five on the British track: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among those five. Alongside them, equivalency asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor page states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. Verify your own case with the Ministry directly.

faqs.question: Is there a published IB points threshold for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not in the source that publishes the British and American figures, which is why no Diploma number appears on this page. The same article sets out five GCSE or IGCSE subjects at E or grade 3 for the British track and SAT and English-proficiency thresholds for the American track, and states nothing for the IB. If a provider quotes you an IB points figure, ask which Ministry of Education page it came from. Equivalency is a process to describe, not one any tutoring service performs.

faqs.question: Which authority governs an Al Zahia school, and how does that differ nearby?
faqs.answer: Five bodies between them. Dubai is KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah is the Sharjah Private Education Authority. Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

faqs.question: We may move to Dubai. What changes for our child's schooling?
faqs.answer: The regulator changes from SPEA to KHDA, and so does the approval model — Sharjah's authority approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods, while KHDA's stated role is enhancing and overseeing quality. Practically, subject offers can differ between emirates, which matters if your child needs a specific syllabus. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven new schools creating 16,846 places.

faqs.question: My child did well at IGCSE and is struggling in Diploma Year 1. Why?
faqs.answer: The assessment model changed, not the ability. IGCSE rewards accurate answers to bounded questions marked against a scheme point by point. The Diploma rewards justified reasoning on open questions and marks internal work against lettered criteria whose marks are added separately, so a piece that answers the task without addressing every criterion sits mid-band. Four to six sessions on criteria and command terms in the first term usually resolves what looks like a decline.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach both my children, one on IGCSE and one on the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it should be tested rather than assumed. Ask what the marking unit is in each system: a mark scheme awarded point by point, with method marks independent of the answer, for IGCSE; lettered criteria with their own descriptor bands, added separately, for the Diploma. A tutor who has worked in both answers both immediately. One who has worked in one will hedge or merge them, and that is a perfectly good tutor for one child.

faqs.question: How risky is changing exam board inside IGCSE?
faqs.answer: More than families expect. Cambridge and Pearson cover overlapping content through different papers with different tiering language, and in English the set texts and anthologies differ entirely, so a year of literature revision does not transfer. Cambridge science centres choose between a practical test and an alternative-to-practical written paper. A term of practice on the wrong board's archive teaches question shapes that will not appear. Confirm the new school's entries in writing before buying any tutoring.

faqs.question: What happens to coursework marks if we arrive at a school mid-year?
faqs.answer: Anything already submitted is banked, and that changes where tutoring money should go. If Internal Assessment deadlines at the new school have passed, those marks cannot be improved however many hours are bought, so the hours belong on the written papers where there is still a grade to move. The first question to put to the new school's coordinator is which internal deadlines have already gone, and an honest tutor asks it before taking a coursework booking.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education work differently on the IB and the British route?
faqs.answer: No — they run alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools either way, and the same rules apply. KHDA's guidelines require separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibit combined classes because expectations and the language of instruction differ, so material for one stream does not serve the other. Substituting content for these subjects without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited.
