The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts is published, so treat quoted penalty figures as unverified.

intro.heading: What an Aljada parent is really asking when they search for a tutor nearby
paragraphs: The search phrase is about distance, but the problem almost never is. A family in Aljada who needs help with Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 does not need someone who lives eight minutes away. They need someone who knows that the Extended route changed shape: Paper 2 is now sat without a calculator and Paper 4 with one, each lasting two hours and each carrying half the grade. A tutor who still prepares students for the old Paper 2 plus Paper 4 pairing from a decade ago will produce neat work and a disappointing result.

Aljada sits in Muwaileh, close to University City Road and a short hop from Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road. The practical effect is that children living in one tower may attend four different schools, following three different syllabuses, with three different homework calendars. One sibling may be doing Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, another the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE 4MA1 maths paper, a third the IB Middle Years Programme with criterion-based reporting instead of percentages. A single neighbourhood tutor cannot credibly cover that spread.

So this page is written from the syllabus up. Each section below names the component, the weighting and the specific place marks are lost. For Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 that means Paper 6, the alternative to practical, where students lose marks for describing a method in the wrong tense or omitting the variable they were told to control. For IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches it means Paper 3 at Higher Level, a problem-solving paper worth twenty per cent that rewards students who can read a long unfamiliar stem and keep going when the first part does not resolve cleanly.

IB Gram's answer to the distance question is straightforward. We do not offer home visits in Sharjah; visiting a student's home is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Aljada families are delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, a screen the student writes on, and a past-paper question open side by side with the mark scheme's command terms. That removes the travel premium from the price and removes the geographic limit from the pool, which is the only reason a Chemistry Higher Level specialist can be the person teaching your child on a Tuesday evening.

Everything that follows is checkable. Where we quote a rate, it is the rate a named provider published and we say so. Where we name a regulator, we explain what it governs and link you to its own page. Where a date is unverified, we say it is unverified rather than guess, because a parent who acts on a wrong exam date has been badly served by a page that looked confident. Sharjah families get one extra check for free: SPEA publishes the school calendar the emirate's private schools work to, so an internal deadline can be read against it before a term of hours is bought.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-aljada.programmesIntro: Aljada children sit across the full range of international programmes, and the tutoring question changes completely depending on which one. A Middle Years Programme student is graded against criteria out of eight; an IGCSE student is graded against raw marks converted to a 9-1 or A*-G scale. Here is what each programme actually asks for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and the creativity, activity, service strand. Forty-two points come from the six subjects at seven each, and up to three more from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay grade matrix, giving the familiar ceiling of forty-five. Higher Level courses carry roughly 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard Level, and that gap is where most private tuition is spent.
programmes.countryNote: Aljada families with a Diploma student usually need help on two fronts at once: a Higher Level subject where the content has outrun the class, and an internal assessment with a school deadline that arrives months before the exam. Those are different kinds of work. The first is teaching; the second is process coaching on the student's own writing, which is the only form of help IB academic honesty rules permit.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria, each marked out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. There are no percentages and no raw mark totals, which is why a parent reading an MYP report often cannot tell whether a four is a problem. Criterion A is typically knowledge and understanding; the later criteria reward investigation, communication and reflection, and those are the ones students lose because nobody taught them the format.
programmes.countryNote: For an Aljada student moving from MYP into the Diploma, the gap that matters is algebraic fluency and the habit of showing a full method. MYP rewards a well-explained approach; Diploma Paper 1 rewards an efficient, correct one under time pressure. Six to ten sessions over a summer closes most of that, worked through past Diploma questions rather than more MYP tasks.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by terminal papers, with Cambridge syllabuses carrying four-digit codes and Pearson Edexcel using the 4XX1 pattern. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended tiers with different grade ceilings; Pearson Edexcel tends to run a single tier with tiered content inside the paper. Entry decisions made in Year 10 therefore cap the grade available in Year 11, which is a conversation worth having early.
programmes.countryNote: The first question an Aljada parent should answer is which board their child's school actually enters. Schools in and around Muwaileh use both. A tutor preparing a student for Cambridge 0620 Chemistry when the school enters Pearson Edexcel 4CH1 will teach the right chemistry and the wrong paper discipline, and the difference shows up in the practical-skills component.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: An inquiry-led framework with transdisciplinary units rather than subject timetables, finishing in the Year 6 exhibition. Reading fluency, number sense and written structure are the three things that transfer forward, and they are also the three that a transdisciplinary report can mask. A PYP report describing strong engagement is not telling you whether a child can subtract across a zero reliably.
programmes.countryNote: Primary tuition for Aljada families is deliberately short and diagnostic: establish what is actually missing, fix it, stop. Long open-ended primary contracts are where families waste the most money in this market, because progress is easy to feel and hard to measure without a baseline taken at the start.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-aljada.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects Aljada families ask for most, described by what the papers test rather than by a one-line label. Where a syllabus code is given it is the code to check against your child's school entry sheet before booking anything.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Standard Level sits Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with one, at forty per cent each, plus the exploration at twenty. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a two-question problem-solving paper worth twenty per cent. Marks go missing in proof by induction, in complex numbers and in the long-stem Paper 3 questions where a student stops after part (a).

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The same weightings as Analysis and Approaches, with statistics, modelling and technology use in place of abstract proof. Graphical calculator fluency is assessed, not assumed, and students lose marks for untidy regression reporting and for quoting a correlation coefficient without saying what it means for the context in the question.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended candidates sit Paper 2 without a calculator and Paper 4 with one, two hours each, fifty per cent each. The non-calculator paper is where the grade is usually decided: surds, index laws, fraction arithmetic and bounds all appear, and a student drilled only on calculator methods arrives unprepared for half the qualification.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Extended candidates take Paper 2 multiple choice at thirty per cent, Paper 4 theory at fifty, and either Paper 5 practical or Paper 6 alternative to practical at twenty. Electricity and the equations of motion generate most lost marks, closely followed by Paper 6 answers that describe an experiment without naming the control variable.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Same paper architecture as physics. The reliable mark-losers are moles and reacting masses, qualitative analysis tests written from memory with the wrong observation, and organic chemistry answers that give a product without the conditions. Past-paper work with the mark scheme visible is worth more here than any amount of re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content-heavy and marked strictly on terminology. Students who say a substance moves from high to low concentration without naming diffusion, or who describe natural selection without the word variation, lose marks they knew the biology for. Paper 6 rewards drawing a results table before the experiment is described.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers of equal weight, both with a calculator, which makes the paper discipline genuinely different from Cambridge 0580. Higher-tier candidates meet vectors, histograms with unequal class widths and iterative methods; the common failure is working shown so sparsely that method marks cannot be awarded.

subjects.name: IB Chemistry
subjects.description: Under the current syllabus, Paper 1 combines multiple choice with a data-based section, Paper 2 carries the extended response, and the scientific investigation is worth twenty per cent. Energetics, equilibrium and the Higher Level organic mechanisms account for most of the gap between a five and a seven.

subjects.name: IB English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis, Paper 2 a comparative essay on studied texts, and the individual oral is assessed internally. Higher Level adds the HL essay. Students lose marks by summarising rather than analysing, and by writing a Paper 2 comparison that treats the two texts in sequence instead of together.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-aljada.igcseSubjectsIntro: A second grid, because Aljada households frequently have one child mid-IGCSE and another in the Diploma. These are the IGCSE options families here add alongside the core sciences and maths.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language 0510 and 0511
igcseSubjects.description: Reading, writing, listening and speaking, with the speaking component separately endorsed. Students in Sharjah schools often sit this rather than First Language English 0500, and the two syllabuses reward different things: 0510 rewards accuracy and register control, 0500 rewards argument and stylistic range.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
igcseSubjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics compressed into a double award. The content is thinner per subject but the papers move faster, and students coming from a triple-science background often over-answer. Knowing which statements the syllabus has removed is half the preparation.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Business Studies 0450
igcseSubjects.description: Case-study driven, with marks allocated for application to the business in the stem rather than for textbook recall. Analysis and evaluation bands are where grades are made, and the most common loss is a well-written answer about businesses in general rather than the one on the paper.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Computer Science 0478
igcseSubjects.description: Paper 1 covers computer systems, Paper 2 algorithms and programming. Pseudocode must follow the syllabus conventions, not a student's preferred language, and trace tables are the single most reliable source of easy marks for students who practise them.

igcseSubjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Arabic as a First Language 0508
igcseSubjects.description: Sat alongside the Ministry-mandated Arabic provision that private schools must deliver whatever their licensed curriculum. Reading comprehension and directed writing dominate, and students educated mainly in English frequently have the vocabulary but not the formal register the mark scheme expects.

sections.heading: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580: the two papers and where the grade is decided
paragraphs: An Extended candidate sits two papers of two hours each, worth fifty per cent apiece. Paper 2 is taken without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. That split is the single most useful thing a parent in Aljada can know, because it tells you what to look for in a tutor's first session. If the first hour is spent on calculator-driven trigonometry, half the qualification is being ignored.

The non-calculator paper rewards arithmetic the student can carry out cleanly: fraction operations, index laws, standard form, surds left in exact form, upper and lower bounds, and percentage reverse problems. None of that is conceptually hard. It is fragile, which is different. A student who has used a calculator for three years will get the method right and the arithmetic wrong, and the mark scheme awards the method mark and withholds the accuracy mark, which is how a confident student lands on a grade six.

The calculator paper is where the longer structured questions live: cumulative frequency, histograms with unequal widths, vectors, transformations, and the multi-step problems that chain two topics together. The recurring loss here is not knowledge but presentation. Students write a single line of working and a final answer. If the answer is wrong, there is nothing on the page to credit. Teaching a student to write enough working to be rescued is worth more marks than teaching them another topic.

Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3, ninety minutes each, with a grade ceiling that the school sets at entry. If your child is capable of a grade above that ceiling, the conversation to have is with the school in Year 10, not with a tutor in Year 11.

table.caption: CAMBRIDGE IGCSE MATHEMATICS 0580 - PAPERS, WEIGHTINGS AND COMMON LOSSES
rows: Fraction and decimal arithmetic; misread scales on graphs
Multi-step money and percentage problems; no working shown
Surds, index laws, bounds, exact-form answers

sections.heading: The sciences: Paper 6 is twenty per cent and almost nobody practises it
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 share one architecture. Extended candidates sit a multiple-choice paper worth thirty per cent, a theory paper worth fifty, and a practical component worth twenty. Most schools in Sharjah enter students for Paper 6, the alternative to practical, rather than the laboratory-based Paper 5. That means a fifth of the qualification is a written paper about experiments.

Paper 6 has a grammar of its own. Answers must name the independent variable, the dependent variable and at least two controlled variables. Readings must be described as repeated, with a mean taken. Tables must be drawn with headings and units before any data exists. Anomalies must be identified and excluded from the mean rather than quietly averaged in. None of this is physics, chemistry or biology. It is a format, and a student who learns the format in four sessions moves several grade boundaries without learning any new content.

The theory papers lose marks for different reasons in each subject. In physics it is the equations of motion applied without checking whether acceleration is constant, and circuit questions where a student computes a total resistance and forgets which component the question asked about. In chemistry it is moles: a student who can define a mole but cannot convert between mass, moles and concentration under time pressure. In biology it is terminology, where the mark scheme wants the word and accepts no paraphrase.

The practical-skills question to ask any prospective tutor is simple. Ask which paper your child's school enters for the practical component, and ask what the mark scheme wants in an evaluation answer. A tutor who answers both precisely has taught this syllabus. A tutor who talks about building confidence in science has not.
bullets: Name one independent, one dependent and two controlled variables, every time
Draw the results table before describing the method, with units in the headings
Identify anomalies explicitly and exclude them from the mean
Evaluation answers need a specific improvement, not 'repeat for accuracy'

sections.heading: IB Mathematics for Aljada students: choosing between AA and AI, then surviving Paper 3
paragraphs: The Diploma offers two maths routes. Analysis and Approaches is the proof-and-calculus route; Applications and Interpretation is the statistics-and-modelling route. Both exist at Standard and Higher Level, and both are weighted the same way: at Standard Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 at forty per cent each plus the exploration at twenty; at Higher Level, Paper 1 and Paper 2 at thirty per cent each, Paper 3 at twenty, and the exploration at twenty.

The route choice is not a difficulty ranking, it is a fit question with a university consequence. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics courses expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Courses in business, psychology, design and the life sciences commonly accept Applications and Interpretation. Before a student in Aljada commits, the sensible step is to read the entry requirements for two or three target universities directly and work backwards, because the requirement is set by the admitting department and changes between them.

Paper 3 at Higher Level deserves separate attention because it is unlike anything in the IGCSE experience. It presents two extended problems, each building through many parts from a concrete starting point towards a general result. Students who are strong on technique and weak on persistence do badly on it. The teaching is explicit: read the whole question first, accept that part (c) may be unreachable until part (b) is done, and write down the pattern you observe even when you cannot prove it, because description earns marks before proof does.

The exploration is twenty per cent and is marked against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics, which carries the largest single allocation. Students lose the communication marks for undefined notation and the reflection marks for describing what they did rather than evaluating whether it worked. A tutor may teach a student to read those criteria and may give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not write any part of it.

sections.heading: What tutoring actually costs around Aljada, and who publishes the numbers
paragraphs: Start with the monthly figure rather than the hourly one, because that is the number a household budget has to absorb. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Converted to an hourly rate, the published bands look like this. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, both online and both at the university-student end of the market. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Bestimate puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with premium named tutors reported as high as AED 650 at BartyED. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted at AED 180 to 500.

The gap between the online band and the in-home band is the travel premium, and it is worth being precise about what it buys. It buys a person in the room. It does not buy a better subject match, and in Sharjah it frequently buys a worse one, because the pool shrinks to whoever is willing to drive to Muwaileh at six in the evening. A family paying AED 350 an hour for a visiting generalist is paying more for less subject depth than a family paying AED 220 for a live video session with a Chemistry Higher Level specialist.

IB Gram does not publish a fixed price list on these pages, and will not quote the market's figures as its own. The honest route is a free trial lesson and a consultation where the subject, level, session length and frequency are agreed, and the figure is given against that. Every rate above is a market rate published by the named provider; none of them is ours.

sections.heading: Online against in-home for an Aljada household, argued on the specifics
paragraphs: The case for in-home tuition is real and worth stating properly. A tutor in the room can see a student's page without being shown it, can intervene the moment a pen stops moving, and can hold the attention of a younger child who will not sit still in front of a screen. For a Year 4 student with a reading difficulty, those are decisive advantages. Nobody should pretend otherwise.

The case against it in Sharjah is logistical and it compounds. A tutor who travels builds the journey into the fee, which is most of the gap between the AED 150 to 300 online band and the AED 180 to 500 in-home band. The tutor can realistically serve a small radius, so the pool a family in Aljada can draw from is whoever covers Muwaileh at the hour they want. If a session has to start at seven because of traffic on Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, and the student's attention runs out at eight thirty, the usable window is ninety minutes a week. A cancellation cannot be refilled, because the next slot is a different drive.

Online removes each of those constraints in turn. The pool is every specialist available at that hour anywhere, which is why a Diploma Physics Higher Level request can be matched at all. There is no travel premium in the rate. A session missed on Tuesday can move to Thursday without anybody rearranging a route. Work stays in one shared folder rather than in a stack of paper nobody can find in April. Screen sharing puts a past paper and its mark scheme side by side, which is awkward in a living room and natural on a screen.

The honest limit: online needs a quiet corner, a reliable connection and a device with a keyboard. It works least well for a child who genuinely cannot focus on a screen, and we will say so on a trial call rather than take the booking. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Sharjah; home visits are a service we run only in India, and no sentence on this site should suggest otherwise.
bullets: Travel premium: roughly the difference between the 150-300 and 180-500 published bands
Tutor pool: everyone free at that hour, rather than everyone free and nearby
Rescheduling: a missed slot moves within the week instead of being lost
Not for everyone: a young child who cannot work on screen is better served in person

sections.heading: Past papers, mark schemes and the one thing families get wrong about them
paragraphs: Past-paper practice is the highest-return activity available to an IGCSE or Diploma student, and it is routinely done in a way that wastes most of the benefit. A student downloads a paper, answers it with notes open, checks answers against the mark scheme, counts a score, and feels reassured. Almost none of the value has been collected.

The value sits in the mark scheme's wording, not in the score. A Cambridge mark scheme shows exactly which words earn the mark and which are rejected. It shows where a method mark survives a wrong answer and where it does not. It shows that explain requires a because and that describe does not. A student who reads three mark schemes carefully, in the company of someone who can say why the examiner drew the line where they did, learns more than a student who sits six papers alone.

The second common error is sequencing. Papers sat too early, before the content is covered, produce a low score and a demoralised student. Papers sat too late leave no time to act on what they reveal. The workable pattern is topic-level questions during the year as each topic finishes, full timed papers from the point the syllabus is complete, and the final weeks spent exclusively on the specific error types that keep recurring in that student's own work.

One boundary matters here. IB Gram does not host, reproduce or supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Those belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and they are available through your school or the board's own site. A tutor works with you from the official material; nobody emails you a library of it.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from the UAE series that actually apply
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March examination series is offered to India only, so a page telling a Sharjah parent to prepare for a spring Cambridge sitting is giving them another country's calendar. UAE candidates sit June, with November available as the resit route.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That is a sentence worth taking literally. The timetable to work from is the one your child's school gives you, not a PDF found by search.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations run in May/June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking facts with dates attached, which is what makes them checkable. Future windows are published as provisional timetables and get revised, so the only responsible instruction is to work from the live official timetable rather than from a date restated on a tutoring page.

For the IB Diploma, UAE schools sit the May session. We do not publish a specific IB examination or results date anywhere on this site: the IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no date in our research was confirmed at source. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the authoritative version, including the internal upload deadlines, which almost always bite months earlier than parents expect.

sections.heading: SPEA, academic honesty and checking that a tutor may legally teach here
paragraphs: Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate. Sharjah's authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not merely inspection sits at emirate level. Dubai's schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Abu Dhabi's and Al Ain's to the Department of Education and Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. That matters for an Aljada family whose children attend schools in two emirates.

Private tutoring itself is regulated separately, by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted to you. The application route is the Ministry's own private tutor licensing service.

Academic honesty is the other boundary, and it is the one the worst pages in this market cross. A tutor may teach content, explain assessment criteria, discuss a student's chosen research question, model how to structure an argument and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not write, part-write, rewrite to completion or supply text for an exploration, a scientific investigation, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or any coursework. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own. One operator in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments for sale; that is a malpractice trigger for the student, and the consequences land on the child, not the seller.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from SPEA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. We have no office or centre in Sharjah. What we have is a matching service and tutors who work to named syllabuses, which is a smaller claim and a true one.

faqs.question: Is there an IB or IGCSE tutor near me in Aljada who comes to the apartment?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits in Sharjah; visiting a student's home is a service we run only in India. Lessons for Aljada families are one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. The reason is not cost-cutting: online matching lets an Aljada student work with a specialist in their exact syllabus rather than with whoever will drive to Muwaileh at six. The in-home market does exist here, and published rates run from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, which is the premium you would be paying for presence in the room.

faqs.question: Which maths papers does my child sit for Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Extended?
faqs.answer: Two papers, each two hours and each worth half the grade. Paper 2 is taken without a calculator and Paper 4 with one. The non-calculator paper is usually where the grade is settled, because it tests fraction arithmetic, index laws, surds in exact form and bounds, all of which decay fast in a student who has used a calculator for three years. Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3 instead, at ninety minutes each, with a grade ceiling the school sets at entry. Check your child's entry sheet for the tier before booking any tuition.

faqs.question: What is Paper 6 in IGCSE science and why does it matter so much in Aljada schools?
faqs.answer: Paper 6 is the alternative to practical, a written paper about experiments, and it carries twenty per cent of Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610. Most schools in this part of Sharjah enter it rather than the laboratory-based Paper 5. It is marked on format as much as science: name the independent, dependent and controlled variables, draw the table with units before describing the method, identify anomalies and exclude them from the mean, and give a specific improvement in evaluation answers. Four focused sessions on that format typically move more marks than four on content.

faqs.question: Should an Aljada student take IB Maths Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: It depends on the degree, not on which looks easier. Analysis and Approaches is the proof and calculus route and is commonly expected for engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics courses, often at Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation is the statistics and modelling route and is widely accepted for business, psychology, design and life-science courses. The reliable method is to read the entry requirements for two or three target universities directly, because the requirement is set by the admitting department and varies between them. Decide before the option sheet goes in, not after.

faqs.question: How much do families around Muwaileh and Aljada pay for IGCSE tuition?
faqs.answer: Published market rates give the range. Online university-student tutors advertise from AED 33 to 65 an hour, with Tutopiya from 33 to 52 and EdFlik from 45 to 65. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from 150 and IB from 200. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel. Monthly, a weekly one-hour arrangement is estimated at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for exam-year specialist support. Those are the market's figures, not ours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child write the IB exploration or Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the assessment criteria letter by letter, help a student narrow a research question, explain what mathematical communication means in practice, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor cannot write it, part-write it, or supply text for it. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own, and the consequence of breaching that falls on the student. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; buying one puts a diploma at risk, and no grade is worth that trade.

faqs.question: Does my child in Sharjah sit the Cambridge February or March exam series?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge offers the February and March series to India only. Candidates in the UAE sit the June series, with November available as the resit route, and Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests running in March, May and October. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk, so work from the timetable your child's school issues rather than one found through a search. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November.

faqs.question: Which schools do the students you support in Aljada attend?
faqs.answer: Families we work with in and around Aljada have children at schools across the Muwaileh and University City cluster, including Victoria International School of Sharjah, The Sheffield Private School, Delhi Private School Sharjah, Wesgreen International School and the American School of Creative Science, and a number drive across to Dubai schools such as Deira International School. We name them as context for the syllabuses and timetables a tutoring plan has to fit around. No affiliation, partnership or endorsement with any school is implied, and none exists.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in Sharjah need a permit, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted figure as unverified. Ask a prospective tutor directly whether they hold the permit.

faqs.question: How does an online lesson actually work for a Year 11 student in Aljada?
faqs.answer: The student joins a video call at the agreed time with a device, a keyboard and a quiet corner. The tutor shares a whiteboard and the student writes on it, so working is visible the way it would be on paper. A past-paper question sits open beside the official mark scheme, and the two are read together so the student can see which words earn marks. Each session finishes with a timed question, marked against the real criteria. Notes and the marked question are sent afterwards, which is how you see progress rather than hear about it.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 with the June series close. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, but the work changes. With a full year available, a tutor teaches content ahead of the class. With weeks available, the only sensible plan is error-type work: identify the three or four mistakes that recur in that student's own papers and drill those specifically, under timed conditions, with the mark scheme open. For Cambridge sciences that often means the Paper 6 format; for 0580 Extended it is usually non-calculator accuracy. Spending the last weeks on topics the student has never met is where families waste the most money.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both maths and physics for the same Aljada student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A tutor comfortable with Cambridge 0580 Extended and 0625 Extended can genuinely carry both, because the mathematics inside the physics is the overlap. At Diploma Higher Level the two diverge, and a Physics HL specialist is usually a different person from a Maths Analysis and Approaches HL specialist. Where one person cannot credibly cover both, we say so and match two, rather than stretching one tutor across a subject they half know.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for the subject I need?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we tell you when. Niche combinations, such as Higher Level Further Mathematics or a less common second language, have a smaller pool and a longer match time, and some requests we cannot fill at the hour you want. The alternatives are a different slot, a different tutor with adjacent expertise clearly described, or a wait with a date attached. What we will not do is take the booking and hope. A disclosed limit is more useful to you than a confident guess.

faqs.question: Which Sharjah regulator oversees my child's school, and does IB Gram answer to it?
faqs.answer: Private schools in Sharjah are regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and also approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. If your child attends school in Dubai, the regulator is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority instead. IB Gram is a tutoring service, not a school, and holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Sharjah Private Education Authority or any other regulator or examination board, and does not claim one. Private tutors are regulated separately, through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation permit.

intro.heading: What "near me" is actually worth on the east coast
paragraphs: A search for a tutor near you is a proxy for four separate things, and they are worth separating. Convenience: no journey, no parking, lessons that start on time. Accountability: a person who can be looked in the eye. Familiarity: someone who knows the local schools. Trust: a recommendation from a neighbour. Only two of those four actually require physical proximity, and in Kalba both come at an unusual price.

Kalba sits on the Gulf of Oman, below Khor Fakkan, separated from the rest of Sharjah by the Hajar mountains. The drive to Sharjah city runs well over an hour each way. Fujairah city is nearer. What that geography does to tutoring is simple arithmetic: the pool of adults within reasonable travelling distance who can teach Diploma Programme Chemistry at Higher Level, or mark a Cambridge 0580 Extended Paper 4 against the published scheme, is a short list. Proximity has a cost and on the east coast it is paid in expertise.

The two things proximity genuinely gives you can be rebuilt online. Accountability comes from recorded sessions, written notes after each lesson and marked work you can read yourself, which is more evidence than a neighbour's recommendation ever provided. Familiarity with local schools comes from a tutor working to your child's own scheme of work, deadlines and assessment criteria rather than from having once driven past the building. Convenience is the one online wins outright, because a session at 17:00 begins at 17:00 instead of whenever a car clears the mountain road.

The delivery position needs stating before anything else, because the search phrase invites a misreading. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are an India-only service. Lessons for Kalba students are one to one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, documents on screen and a recording afterwards. We would rather lose the enquiry than let a family believe somebody is coming.

Because this page covers both boards, it sets out where they differ in ways that change a tutoring plan. The Diploma Programme is assessed partly through internal assessment marked against published criteria with letters and mark allocations, which rewards a completely different kind of support from an IGCSE theory paper. IGCSE is tiered, examined twice a year, and won largely on command terms and method marks. A tutor who treats the two the same is teaching one of them badly.

The rest of the page is organised around decisions rather than features: how to compare a nearby generalist with a distant specialist, what the internal assessment criteria actually require, which regulator governs what, where the mandatory UAE subjects sit in the week, and what a Kalba family should ask before paying anyone.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-kalba.programmesIntro: Three programmes cover almost every east-coast enquiry that mentions both boards. Each is described with the assessment mechanism that drives the tutoring, because that mechanism is what differs.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked by the teacher against published criteria and then moderated. The written examinations fall in a May session for schools in this region, and the internal deadlines a school sets for internal assessment drafts arrive long before them.
programmes.countryNote: East-coast families in the Diploma Programme are usually enrolled in Sharjah city or Fujairah, which means a long school run on top of a demanding programme. The internal assessment deadlines are where that pressure shows first, because they fall in term time rather than in a revision period, and they are the component a distant specialist can support best.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each scored out of eight and reported as a one-to-seven grade after conversion. There are no external examinations in most MYP schools, which means a parent reading a report sees criterion letters rather than percentages, and a student who is strong on knowledge can still carry a low overall grade from a weak criterion elsewhere.
programmes.countryNote: The transition out of MYP is the live issue for Kalba families. A student moving from MYP into either the Diploma Programme or a Year 10 IGCSE cohort meets timed written examinations for the first time, and the gap is examination technique rather than content. Two terms of deliberate work on it changes the first year considerably.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: A two-year course examined externally, tiered in many subjects between Core and Extended at Cambridge, and sat in a June series and a November series. Pearson's International GCSE runs in a May/June window and in November. Marks turn on command terms, shown method and paper timing far more than on raw knowledge, and the tier is fixed on the entry form rather than in the examination hall.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the school for every syllabus code and tier in writing at the start of Year 10. On the east coast the commonest avoidable loss is a term spent revising the wrong code, because the family bought a popular revision guide rather than checking whether the entry was Combined Science or three separate sciences.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-kalba.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones east-coast families most often need across both boards. Where the two boards teach overlapping content, the difference in what the assessment rewards is named, because that difference is the plan.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Diploma route for students heading towards engineering, physics, economics or mathematics itself. Proof, calculus and algebraic manipulation carry the Higher Level papers, and the internal assessment exploration is where students either show genuine mathematical reasoning or describe a topic they have read about.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-led work. Easier to start and no easier to finish: the modelling questions punish students who cannot interpret output in context. Check which route named university programmes expect before a Year 11 student commits, because the two are not interchangeable prerequisites.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL, IGCSE Core and Extended
subjects.description: At Diploma level, energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are the recurring weak points, with the internal assessment investigation close behind. At IGCSE, electrolysis half-equations and mole calculations dominate the lost Extended marks. Same subject, two different repair jobs.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL, IGCSE Core and Extended (0625, 4PH1)
subjects.description: Diploma students lose marks on the multi-step mechanics and fields questions where a method must be constructed rather than recalled. IGCSE candidates lose them on electricity, moments and the Alternative to Practical paper. Both respond quickly to working-out discipline rather than to more content.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: DP HL and SL, IGCSE Core and Extended (0610, 4BI1)
subjects.description: Volume is the difficulty in both. Diploma students need to answer the command term rather than empty their memory onto the page; IGCSE candidates need to use the data in front of them instead of recalling a textbook graph. Both are technique problems with content symptoms.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Marks come from applying a concept to the stimulus rather than defining it, and from accurate diagrams. Diploma Economics adds the internal assessment commentaries built on real news articles, which are a writing-discipline task as much as an economics one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the written paper analysis both require a controlled argument about how a text works rather than what it says. Students who write fluently but unanalytically plateau here, and the fix is structural: claim, evidence, mechanism, effect, repeated until it is automatic.

subjects.name: First Language and Second Language English
subjects.description: Directed writing rewards a clear structure and an audience-appropriate register. Reading responses lose marks when a student retells instead of selecting and commenting. The word limits on summary tasks are enforced, and students regularly lose marks by writing more rather than less.

subjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies
subjects.description: UAE private schools teach these alongside the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Support has to match the stream the school has placed the student in rather than the family's preference.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Both are assessed against published criteria, and both are routinely left too late. Support here is process coaching: question formulation, scope, structuring an argument, and feedback on the student's own drafts. No tutor may draft or rewrite either one.

sections.heading: Nearby generalist or distant specialist: how to choose
paragraphs: This is the actual decision behind an IB IGCSE tutor near me search in Kalba, and it has a right answer that depends on the student rather than on the geography. A nearby generalist is the better buy when the problem is organisation, homework completion, confidence at Years 7 to 9, or a primary-age child who needs an adult in the room. A distant specialist is the better buy when the problem is a named component of a named course: a Higher Level paper, an Extended-tier science, an internal assessment against published criteria, Additional Mathematics.

The reason is that specialism is not interchangeable. A capable graduate can supervise homework in any subject. Marking a Diploma Programme Chemistry internal assessment against its criteria, or diagnosing why a student loses eleven marks on a Cambridge Paper 4, requires having done it before. Within driving range of Kalba, the number of people who have is small. Online, it is not a constraint at all, and that is the entire trade this page is about.

There is a third option families rarely consider and it is often the best one: a nearby adult for structure and a distant specialist for the subject, used in different weeks for different purposes. A Year 11 student who needs both supervision and Extended physics teaching is badly served by buying one of them twice.

To be unambiguous about what is on offer here: lessons are live online, one to one. IB Gram does not place tutors in UAE homes, in Kalba or anywhere else. The comparison table below prices the alternatives honestly so the choice can be made on its merits rather than on a sales line.

sections.heading: Higher Level against Standard Level, and Extended against Core
paragraphs: Both boards sell the same subject at two intensities, and families regularly discover the consequences of that choice too late. In the Diploma Programme, Higher Level courses carry more content, longer papers and an additional paper in the sciences, and the grade ceiling is the same seven as Standard Level. Taking a subject at Higher Level does not raise the maximum; it raises the amount of work needed to reach it, and it is only worth doing where a university route or a genuine interest requires it.

At IGCSE the mechanism is harder, because the tier is a cap rather than a workload. A Cambridge Core entry limits the available grades, which means a student entered at Core and aiming higher cannot get there however well they are taught. The tier appears on the entry form months before the papers. This is the single most consequential administrative decision in a British-track school year, and it is routinely made without the family being consulted.

What this means for a tutoring plan is a sequencing question. Work on the tier and level decisions first, in writing, with the school. Then plan teaching inside whatever those decisions allow. A family that spends eight weeks on Extended content for a Core entry has bought nothing, and a family that discovers in the final term that Higher Level was the wrong fit has limited options left.

The table sets the two systems side by side on the things that change a plan: paper structure, internal assessment weight, grade ceiling and the signal that the level is wrong for a given student. Ask your child's school where their current marked work sits against those signals.

sections.heading: Internal assessment criteria, by letter and mark
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market names a single internal assessment criterion, which is remarkable, because the criteria are the whole of the task. A Diploma Programme internal assessment is not marked on impression or on effort. It is marked against lettered criteria, each with a published mark allocation and descriptor bands, and a student who has not read them is working blind. The first useful session on any internal assessment is reading the criteria aloud and matching them to what the student has written.

The pattern is consistent across subjects even though the letters differ. There is always a criterion for the framing of the task: a research question, an aim, or a focus that must be sharp enough to be answerable. There is always a criterion for method or process, where a student explains and justifies what they did. There is always a criterion for analysis, where data or evidence is interpreted rather than described. There is always a criterion for evaluation, where limitations and improvements are discussed honestly. Several subjects carry a communication criterion covering structure, terminology and presentation.

The marks follow a predictable pattern too. Analysis and evaluation usually carry the heavy mark allocations, and students usually spend their time on the method description instead, because it is the easiest part to write. A tutor's most valuable intervention is to look at a draft and say: you have written four pages against a criterion worth a few marks and half a page against the one worth the most. That conversation moves grades more than any amount of extra content.

The boundary is firm. A tutor may teach the skills, explain the criteria, discuss a plan and respond to a draft the student has written. A tutor may not draft the work, supply paragraphs or edit it into something the student could not have produced. The student's school holds supervision records and submission history, and the consequence of a malpractice finding falls on the student.

sections.heading: Who regulates what, across the emirates
paragraphs: Five separate authorities regulate private schools in the UAE, and families on the east coast cross between two of them routinely. Dubai schools sit with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah, including Kalba and Khor Fakkan, sits with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah come under the federal Ministry of Education.

The remits differ in a way that matters. For Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah, the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is more than inspection: the curriculum your child studies has local approval even though the examination papers are set abroad. A Kalba family whose child is enrolled in Fujairah is dealing with federal oversight instead, with different published material and a different route for a complaint or a fee query.

Underneath all five sits a federal rule worth knowing: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, provided they adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is why every private school week in the country contains lessons that appear on no Cambridge or IB timetable, and why study-time calculations that ignore them are optimistic.

What none of this does is endorse a tutor. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any of these authorities, and no tutoring provider in this market should imply otherwise. A permit to tutor privately comes from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and belongs to the individual. An educational services permit for a training institute with premises is a separate thing issued by the Dubai authority to organisations that hold it.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects, and the time they take
paragraphs: Every private school in the country teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies alongside its licensed international curriculum, and almost no page in this market mentions them at all. They occupy real timetable space, they are assessed, and they appear on the report your child brings home, so a tutoring plan built as though the week contains only IB or IGCSE subjects is working from a false timetable.

The rules are specific where it counts. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, with Arabic the primary language for social studies for Arab students. Non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and moral, social and cultural studies in the language of the school's licensed curriculum.

Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic require the relevant approval from the Dubai authority to teach those subjects, which is a credential point a parent can actually check. Using different or additional content for these subjects without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, which constrains what any tutor can legitimately offer in them.

For a Kalba family the practical consequences are two. First, count these periods when you work out how much independent study time actually exists, because the honest number is usually smaller than the assumed one. Second, if support in Arabic is needed, match it to the stream the school has placed the student in rather than to the one the family would prefer, because the assessment follows the stream.

sections.heading: What a Kalba family should ask before paying anyone
paragraphs: This market makes checking hard, so here is a short list that separates the real from the advertised. Ask which syllabus code and level the tutor has taught to examination classes, and listen for a specific answer. Ask them to name the assessment criteria for the internal assessment your child is working on. Ask what evidence you will receive after each session. Ask what the rate is in dirhams, whether it is per hour or per lesson, and what happens if you stop after one lesson. A provider who answers all five in plain language is unusual in this cluster.

Then check the claims. Nobody in private tutoring is approved, accredited or licensed by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Sharjah authority, the Ministry of Education or any examination board, and a provider implying otherwise is making a claim worth questioning. Individual tutors need the private tuition work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Ratings are also worth testing: one page in this market publishes two different review averages in the same document, and another a perfect score from a count that cannot support it.

Be sceptical about examiner claims in particular. Examiner status for an individual is hard to evidence and easy to assert, and it is often used to imply access to marking standards or paper content that no examiner has. A tutor who knows the published mark scheme thoroughly and can show you a marked script is more useful than one with an unverifiable title.

Finally, ask about the thing nobody volunteers: availability. If a provider cannot cover Additional Mathematics 0606 or a specific board variant in your preferred slot, you want to hear that before you pay, not after a week of silence. We will tell you, and we will say which of the alternatives applies.

sections.heading: Equivalency and university entry, from an east-coast school
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the step that turns a school certificate into something a UAE university or employer will accept, and it is almost entirely absent from this market's pages. On the British track the requirement is a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which is wrong.

On the American track, English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL internet-based test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying. For the IB track, no points threshold should be taken from a tutoring page: the figures circulating are not sourced to the Ministry, and this page will not publish one. Check with the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation authority directly.

The planning consequence for a Kalba family is that subject choices in Year 11 constrain what equivalency looks like two years later. A student who drops to four examined subjects, or who counts Arabic towards the five, can meet a university offer and still have an equivalency problem. Raise it with the school while the choices are still reversible, which is the start of Year 11 rather than the end of Year 13.

What a tutoring provider cannot do is perform or guarantee equivalency or attestation. It is a regulatory process run by the authorities, and tutoring is not required for it, for university admission, or for school progression. Anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a government procedure.

sections.heading: How an online session actually runs from Kalba
paragraphs: The mechanics are worth describing plainly, because families who have not tried it imagine something worse than it is. A session runs on live video with a shared digital whiteboard. The tutor and the student work on the same document: a past paper, a marked script, an internal assessment draft, a diagram being annotated. Both can write. The session is recorded, and the recording is kept so a student can rewatch the part they lost.

What makes it work is the material being on screen rather than on paper. A mathematics working-out line the student got wrong can be rewritten next to the mark scheme, side by side. A chemistry mechanism can be built in stages and left on the board. For an internal assessment, the criteria sit in one window and the draft in another, which is exactly how the work is actually marked and almost never how a student writes it.

Connection quality on the east coast is adequate for this, and the practical requirements are modest: a laptop or tablet rather than a phone, headphones, and a quiet corner for an hour. A phone camera pointed at a textbook is the one setup that does not work, because the shared document is the lesson.

The honest limits are two. A student who will not speak to a screen is better served by an adult in the room, and that is worth finding out in a trial lesson rather than after a month. And a practical science skill, handling apparatus, is school laboratory work; what online lessons teach is the reasoning the written papers assess. Nobody travels to Kalba, and pretending otherwise would waste your time and ours.

process.description: A marked script, a criteria sheet with the teacher's comments, or a report with criterion letters. Two minutes of reading that tells a tutor where marks were actually lost, which is often not where the student thinks. It also tells us which specialist to assign.

process.description: With the tutor who would continue, on your child's own material, with no card details taken first. What you are testing is whether your child will admit confusion to this particular person. That, rather than the credentials, is what determines whether the next twenty sessions work.

process.title: Fix the plan and the slot
process.description: Agree the subject focus, the number of weeks, the slot in Gulf Standard Time and what marked evidence will exist at the end. For internal assessment work, agree the school's deadlines first and plan backwards from them rather than from today.

process.title: Check the evidence, not the feeling
process.description: Review at the halfway point using marked work. Continue if the gap has closed, change something if it has not. Switching tutor is a normal step, costs nothing, and is better taken at week four than at week twelve.

faqs.question: Is there an IB or IGCSE tutor near me in Kalba, honestly?
faqs.answer: Not many, and that is the useful answer. Kalba's international-curriculum provision is limited and the drive to Sharjah city runs well over an hour each way, so the pool of adults within range who have taught Diploma Programme Higher Level or marked Extended-tier papers is short. For homework supervision at Years 7 to 9, a local adult is a sensible choice. For a named course component, the realistic options are a long journey or live online lessons. IB Gram provides the second: one to one over video, with no travel either way.

faqs.question: My child prefers a person in the room. Can live video lessons still work from Kalba?
faqs.answer: Often, but it is worth testing rather than assuming. The thing that makes it work is a shared screen: the past paper, the marked script or the internal assessment draft sits in front of both people and both can write on it, which is closer to how the work is actually marked than a textbook on a table. Recordings let a student revisit the part they lost. The genuine exception is a student who will not speak to a screen, and a free trial lesson shows that within twenty minutes.

faqs.question: Should a Kalba student use one tutor across both boards, or two specialists?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it depends on the pairing. Mathematics and physics across both boards is a combination many tutors genuinely hold. Diploma Chemistry Higher Level alongside IGCSE English is not, whatever a profile claims. Ask which syllabus codes and levels the tutor has taught to examination classes, and listen for named papers rather than subject lists. Where a pairing is not credible, two specialists in alternating weeks usually costs the same and teaches more than one person spread thin.

faqs.question: What are the IB internal assessment criteria and why do they matter so much?
faqs.answer: Each Diploma subject marks its internal assessment against lettered criteria with published mark allocations, covering the framing of the task, the method or process, the analysis, the evaluation, and in many subjects communication. Marks are awarded strictly against those descriptors rather than on effort. Analysis and evaluation usually carry the heaviest allocations, and students usually spend their time on the method description, which pays least. Reading the criteria against the draft is the highest-value hour of support available on the whole task.

faqs.question: Where is the line between coaching and malpractice on an IB internal assessment?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the skills, explain the published criteria, discuss a plan and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not draft it, supply paragraphs or edit it into something the student could not have produced. One provider in this market sells completed assessed work; buying it is malpractice and the student carries the consequence, not the seller. Your child's school keeps supervision records and knows their written voice, which is precisely what those records exist to check.

faqs.question: Who regulates a school in Kalba, and what if we move to Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Kalba is part of Sharjah, so its private schools come under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A move to Fujairah, Ajman or Umm Al Quwain puts the school under federal Ministry of Education supervision instead. Dubai schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority and Abu Dhabi schools to the Department of Education and Knowledge. The examination boards are unaffected by any of it.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level worth taking if my child is already struggling at Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and the arithmetic is worth doing honestly. Higher Level adds content, papers and length without raising the grade ceiling, which stays at seven. It is worth taking where a university route genuinely requires it or where the student has a real appetite for the subject. A student already behind on Standard Level content before the internal assessment begins will meet the same work with less time. Ask the school what the marked evidence says before the choice is locked in.

faqs.question: How does a Core or Extended tier decision affect what tutoring can achieve?
faqs.answer: Decisively, and earlier than families expect. A Cambridge Core entry caps the grades available, so a student entered at Core cannot reach the top grades however well they are taught. The tier is fixed on the entry form months before the papers. That makes it the first thing to settle, in writing, with the school's exams officer, and the reason tutoring plans should be built after the tier is confirmed rather than before. Any teaching bought against a tier the entry does not allow is wasted.

faqs.question: What does the MYP to Diploma Programme step actually require?
faqs.answer: Less new content than families fear and far more examination technique than they expect. MYP assesses against four criteria per subject with no external papers in most schools, so a student arriving in the Diploma Programme may never have sat a timed written paper that matters. The useful bridge is six to ten weeks of graded timed practice, plus algebraic fluency work before the mathematics course needs it. Content gaps show up as symptoms; the technique gap is the cause.

faqs.question: Why do Arabic and Islamic Education appear on my child's timetable alongside the IB?
faqs.answer: Because private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum under federal regulations. Schools organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, as combined classes are prohibited where curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Count those periods when estimating how much independent study time your child actually has, because the real figure is usually lower than the assumed one.

faqs.question: What should I ask a tutor in this market before paying?
faqs.answer: Five questions. Which syllabus code and level have you taught to examination classes? Can you name the criteria for my child's internal assessment? What evidence do I receive after each session? What is the rate in dirhams, per hour or per lesson? What happens if we stop after one lesson? Then test the claims: no tutoring provider holds approval or accreditation from a UAE education authority or an examination board, and self-published star ratings in this cluster contradict each other on the same page.

faqs.question: Are examiner-marketed tutors worth the premium quoted in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Only if the status can be evidenced, and it usually cannot. Published premium rates in this market reach AED 650 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. Examiner status for an individual is easy to assert and hard to verify, and it implies nothing about access to marking standards or paper content. A tutor who knows the published mark scheme thoroughly and will show you a marked script is more useful than a title. Ask for the script.

faqs.question: Does my child need tutoring to get UAE certificate equivalency?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is a regulatory process run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authorities, and tutoring is not a requirement for it, for university admission, or for school progression. What tutoring can do is help a student reach the grades the requirement asks for. On the British track that means five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. Verify current requirements with the authority directly.

faqs.question: How quickly can a Kalba family start, and what if the slot is full?
faqs.answer: Common subjects in early-evening Gulf Standard Time slots are usually matched quickly. Narrow combinations take longer: Additional Mathematics 0606, a specific board variant late in a series, Arabic as a first language, or a Higher Level science with an internal assessment deadline inside a fortnight. When the right specialist is not free for your preferred slot, we offer a different slot with the right tutor, a short declared bridging block, or we say we cannot cover it well. Booking outside the post-mock rush avoids the question entirely.

faqs.question: What equipment does a Kalba student need for live online lessons?
faqs.answer: A laptop or tablet rather than a phone, headphones, and a quiet place for an hour. The shared whiteboard and the on-screen document are the lesson, so a screen big enough to read a past paper matters more than bandwidth. A phone camera pointed at a textbook is the one arrangement that does not work. Sessions are recorded and the recording is kept, which is useful for a student travelling the east-coast school run and for a parent who wants to see what was taught.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-kalba.closingHeading: Decide what proximity is worth, then choose
sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-kalba.closingBody: If you have been searching for an IB IGCSE tutor near me in Kalba, the useful next step is to name the problem precisely. Supervision and routine for a Year 8 student is a different purchase from a Higher Level internal assessment eight weeks from a school deadline, and only one of them is improved by the tutor living nearby. Send the board, the level, the subject and one piece of marked work, and we will tell you which of those you are dealing with, and whether a specialist over live video is the right answer or not.

intro.heading: Comparing four places when the examination is the same in all of them
paragraphs: Khor Fakkan is a port town on Sharjah's east coast, administratively part of the emirate and physically separated from it by the mountains. Families here comparing tutoring options are really comparing four places: Khor Fakkan itself, Kalba just south, Fujairah city a short drive away, and Sharjah's main urban area on the other side of the range.

Three of those comparisons are about supply and journeys. Khor Fakkan and Kalba have small local markets with general tutoring and no course-specific depth. Fujairah city has more schools and a slightly deeper market, under the federal Ministry of Education rather than Sharjah's authority. Sharjah city has the emirate's deepest tutoring pool, several IB schools, and a journey nobody is making twice a week for a one-hour lesson.

The fourth comparison is the one that matters, and it is not geographic at all. Whatever your address on this coast, your child sits the same paper as a candidate in Al Majaz or Dubai Marina, marked against the same scheme, in the same series. Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates; Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November; the IB's May session is what UAE schools use. There is no east-coast edition of a mark scheme and no local variant of an internal assessment criterion.

That single fact reframes everything. If the examination is fixed and national, then the variable worth optimising is who teaches your child - and the only way to optimise it from Khor Fakkan is to stop filtering by distance. Over live video, a tutor who has taught higher level physics for a decade or marked Cambridge 0620 papers for years is as available here as in the city, at a rate with no journey priced into it.

The cost comparison makes the same point. Across published UAE rate cards, a qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, while an in-home visit is quoted between AED 180 and 500 once travel is absorbed - and on this coast an in-home specialist, if one existed, would sit at the very top of that band. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India.

One qualification before the comparisons. Local general tutoring on this coast is a real and useful service, and for a younger child who needs an adult beside them to stay on task it is the better choice than anything we sell. The comparison below is aimed at families whose problem is course-specific - a criterion, a tier decision, a paper technique - because that is where local supply genuinely cannot help.

What follows compares the four places on the things that genuinely vary, then compares the schooling options an east-coast family actually chooses between, then sets out what is identical wherever you live and a short checklist for deciding.
