sections.heading: The four options, compared on what varies
paragraphs: Begin with the honest version. On this coast, local tutoring exists and is general: people who can supervise homework, keep a routine and cover content across several year groups. That is a real service and it suits younger children and students whose problem is discipline rather than direction.

What does not exist locally is course-specific depth. Nobody in Khor Fakkan or Kalba has supervised thirty IB chemistry investigations or marked Cambridge 0620 papers against the published scheme for a decade, because there is no local institution that would have produced that experience. Fujairah city improves the odds slightly and does not change the picture. Sharjah city has those people and is unreachable for a weekday lesson.

The journey arithmetic settles it. The drive from the emirate's main urban area to this coast crosses the Hajar mountains, and a tutor doing it for one lesson is spending a large part of their evening in a car. Nobody runs that arrangement at a sane price, and the in-home band on this coast - if anybody offered it - would sit at the top of the AED 180 to 500 range published across UAE rate cards.

So the comparison resolves to a choice between general help nearby and specific help from anywhere. For homework supervision, choose nearby. For an internal assessment criterion, a tier decision, an alternative-to-practical technique or a final-block triage, choose specific. The table sets out the four places on the dimensions that actually differ.

sections.heading: What a mountain range does to an in-home arrangement
paragraphs: It is worth doing the arithmetic rather than asserting the conclusion, because families here are entitled to see the working.

A tutor based in the emirate's main urban area who agrees to teach in Khor Fakkan is committing to a mountain crossing in each direction for a single sixty-minute lesson. Even at generous assumptions, that is most of an evening. A rational tutor prices it accordingly or, far more commonly, declines. The result is not an expensive option; it is an absent one, which is why the local list contains general tutors rather than specialists at a premium.

Fujairah city is close enough to make a short-journey arrangement plausible, and that is where most east-coast in-home tutoring actually comes from. But the pool there is small, and it has the same composition problem: capable generalists, very few people with examination-level experience in a specific course. Paying a travel premium to reach a generalist is the least efficient purchase available.

Against that, published UAE rate cards put a qualified subject tutor teaching online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with no travel component because nobody travels. Bestimate's Dubai cost estimates, read in October 2026, translate one weekly session into about AED 600 to 1,200 a month with a qualified tutor. Those are market figures for comparison rather than our price list - ask us directly, and the trial lesson costs nothing in any case.

The conclusion is not that distance is irrelevant. It is that distance now costs a family choice of school and informal access to teachers, rather than access to teaching - and those are very different losses with very different remedies.

sections.heading: Boarding, commuting or staying local: comparing the schooling decision
paragraphs: Tutoring questions on this coast are usually downstream of a schooling decision, so the comparison is worth making explicitly. Three routes dominate, and each has a different tutoring consequence.

Staying local on another curriculum is the simplest. The child is at home, the week is normal, and the qualification being sat may not be the IB at all. Support must match whatever the school actually enters them for, which makes the first question - which board, which code, which qualification - more important here than anywhere.

Commuting to Fujairah city keeps the family together and consumes the afternoon. Weekday capacity after a long return journey is low, so the realistic pattern is one short weekday session and a weekend morning for anything substantial. Note also the regulator change: Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, while Khor Fakkan's and Kalba's fall under the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods.

Boarding in the main urban area buys access to IB provision and costs a parent visibility. The school's structure covers weekday evenings, which is an advantage, but a parent a hundred kilometres away sees far less of the work and hears about problems later. For boarding families we ask for the internal deadline calendar and recommend short, frequent check-ins rather than long weekly lessons, because the missing ingredient is accountability rather than teaching.

Whichever route a family takes, the document to ask for is the same: the school's internal deadline calendar, plus the subject guide and any task sheets. Those replace the corridor conversation a city parent has without noticing, and every school holds them already.

sections.heading: Two boards, two systems and one set of national rules
paragraphs: An east-coast household frequently runs more than one system, because children were placed in different schools at different times. The comparison between those systems matters more than the comparison between towns.

The IB builds a grade over two years from internal assessments marked against published criteria, core components and terminal papers. The British track decides the grade almost entirely in the examination room, with published mark schemes and, at Cambridge, Core and Extended tiering. The consequence is that IB support needs to be earlier and more continuous, while British-track support can be concentrated into a block before the series with the clearest effect on marks.

What is identical is the administration. Entries for Cambridge and Pearson are made by the school's centre, not by the family. Each Cambridge centre belongs to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used - that is a property of the centre, not of your town. Pearson publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, so the live official version is the only one to work from.

Dates worth keeping: Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates, with the February/March series offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the next day, and the November 2025 series results reached students on 22 January 2026. For the IB, UAE schools sit the May session and we publish no IB dates, because we could not verify them at source - your coordinator holds the confirmed version.

sections.heading: Comparing the realistic options for getting help here
paragraphs: Set aside geography for a moment and compare the actual delivery options available to a family in Khor Fakkan. There are five, and they are not interchangeable.

Self-study with honest marking is free and effective for a disciplined British-track candidate: papers and mark schemes exist, and a student who completes a paper under timing and marks it strictly learns most of what a tutor teaches about technique. It does far less for an IB student facing criterion-based assessed work, where the descriptors need interpreting by somebody who has used them.

Local general tutoring supplies presence and routine. A Fujairah-based in-home tutor adds a modest travel premium for the same thing. A group class, where one is available, is the cheapest paid content teaching per student and cannot keep an individual error log or review one student's script - which is most of what matters in a final block.

Online one-to-one with a matched specialist is the only option on this list that does diagnosis, triage, criterion coaching and paper technique for a specific candidate. It is also the only one whose price contains no journey. For most families here the sensible combination is self-study for volume plus a small number of specialist hours for direction, which costs less than a term of weekly local sessions and achieves more.

The one option on that list we cannot provide is supervision. A young child who needs an adult in the room to stay on task is better served by a local arrangement, and we would say so rather than take the booking - we do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, since that service exists only in India.

What families here should resist is the middle option that looks reasonable and is not: paying a travel premium to bring a generalist across a distance. It is the most expensive way to buy the cheapest kind of help, and it is the arrangement east-coast families most often end up in by default.

sections.heading: What is identical on both coasts
paragraphs: Having compared what differs, the longer list is what does not - and this is where the comparison stops being about geography.

The examinations. Cambridge's June and November series, Pearson's May/June and November, the IB's May session. The mark schemes, which have no local editions. The command terms, which mean the same thing in Khor Fakkan as in Al Majaz. The internal assessment criteria and their published descriptors. The three topics in each subject where candidates lose most marks. All national or international, none local.

The permit. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those operating without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

The academic-honesty boundary. A tutor may teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work. A tutor may not write, draft or edit assessed coursework, an internal assessment, an extended essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay, and IB Gram sells no completed work of any kind. Services that do appear in these search results at prices in the thousands of dirhams, and the malpractice finding attaches to the student wherever the student lives.

So the only genuinely local variables are the ones this page has already compared: schools, journeys and the depth of the nearby market. Everything that decides a grade is national, which is why we match on the course and let the format take care of the geography.

sections.heading: A decision checklist for a family here
paragraphs: Comparisons are only useful if they end in a decision, so here is the sequence we would suggest for a household on this coast.

First, identify the qualification precisely: programme, subject, level, or board, code and tier. In a region where children are placed in different schools for practical reasons, this is genuinely uncertain more often than families expect, and every later decision depends on it. The statement of entry or the school's exam information carries it, and the exams officer can confirm it in one reply.

Second, decide what kind of problem you have. Presence and routine, which local help can supply. Or course-specific technique, criteria and triage, which it cannot. Being honest about this is what prevents paying a travel premium for the wrong service.

Third, get documents in writing, because distance removes the informal channel: the subject guide, task sheets, the internal deadline calendar, and a marked script. Fourth, test rather than argue - a free trial lesson over live video with a specialist, built around that marked script, resolves in an hour what weeks of discussion will not. And fifth, place the session where the student can actually use it, which on this coast usually means a weekend morning for anything substantial.

Sixth, write both of those decisions down somewhere a family can revisit: the qualification and the problem type. Households on this coast make tutoring decisions less often than city families do, and twelve months later nobody remembers why a particular arrangement was chosen - which is how a block bought for one mock quietly becomes a two-year subscription.

Finally, review on evidence rather than on feeling. A marked script at the start and a comparable one six sessions later tells you whether the arrangement is working, and it is the same test wherever you live.

faqs.question: Is there any realistic chance of an in-home IB specialist in Khor Fakkan?
faqs.answer: Honestly, no. A tutor from the emirate's main urban area would cross the Hajar mountains in each direction for a single lesson, which is most of an evening, so the arrangement is absent rather than merely expensive. Fujairah-based in-home tutoring exists and is general rather than course-specific. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE in any case - that service exists only in India - and we teach one-to-one over live video, which is what makes a specialist reachable here at all.

faqs.question: How does Khor Fakkan compare with Fujairah city for tutoring?
faqs.answer: Fujairah has more schools and a slightly deeper tutoring market, and it is close enough that an in-home arrangement from there is plausible. What it does not have is course-specific depth: the composition problem is the same, with capable generalists and very few people who have supervised a specific IB internal assessment or marked a particular board's papers for years. So Fujairah improves your school choice more than it improves your tutoring choice.

faqs.question: Do east-coast students sit the same papers as students in Sharjah city?
faqs.answer: Exactly the same. Cambridge runs June and November series for UAE candidates, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and UAE schools use the IB's May session. Mark schemes, command terms and internal assessment criteria are national or international - there is no east-coast edition of anything. Entries are made by your school's centre, and the administrative zone that determines which timetable version applies belongs to that centre rather than to your town.

faqs.question: Our child boards in the city. What kind of support actually helps?
faqs.answer: Accountability more than teaching. The school's structure covers weekday evenings, so the gap is usually that a parent a hundred kilometres away hears about problems late. Short, frequent check-ins - twenty to thirty minutes, each ending with one named next step and a date - work better than a long weekly lesson, with a weekend morning reserved for substantial work like an internal assessment or a full paper. We also ask for the school's internal deadline calendar in that situation.

faqs.question: Can a disciplined student here prepare for IGCSE without a tutor?
faqs.answer: A good deal of the way, yes. Past papers and mark schemes exist, and a student who completes a paper under timing and marks it strictly against the scheme learns most of what a tutor teaches about technique. The two failure modes are generous self-marking and avoiding the hardest papers. Where self-study does far less is IB assessed work, because criterion descriptors need interpreting by somebody who has used them, and that is where specialist hours earn their cost.

faqs.question: Which regulator applies to schools in Khor Fakkan?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority, because Khor Fakkan and Kalba are part of Sharjah. SPEA regulates private education in the emirate and, with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, so a family whose child attends school there deals with a different authority. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from either.

faqs.question: What does tutoring cost here compared with the city?
faqs.answer: Online, exactly the same, because nothing in the rate pays for a journey: published UAE rate cards put a qualified subject tutor teaching online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, and Bestimate's Dubai estimates, read in October 2026, translate a weekly session into about AED 600 to 1,200 a month. In-home is where distance shows: the market band is AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel absorbed, and on this coast it would sit at the top of that range if anybody offered it.

faqs.question: We run both IB and IGCSE in one household. Does that change the plan?
faqs.answer: It changes the timing. The British-track child's marks respond most to a concentrated block of timed papers before the series, because the grade is made in the examination room. The IB child needs hours earlier and spread, since internal assessments and core components cannot be rescued late. Buying identical weekly slots for both is the common default and gets both wrong. We would place consecutive slots on one evening or a shared weekend morning, with separate specialists and separate plans.

faqs.question: How do we judge a local tutor when we cannot easily compare options?
faqs.answer: Ask what they have taught rather than what they studied, and listen for specifics: which board and code, how recently, and the three topics where candidates lose the most marks in that subject. Ask whether they will mark a recent script before the first session. Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free and valid two years, so there is no good reason not to. None of those questions needs subject knowledge from you.

faqs.question: Is a weekend morning really better than a weekday evening for us?
faqs.answer: For substantial work, almost always, and more so here than in the city. A student returning from Fujairah or boarding in the main urban area has very little usable weekday capacity, and pushing an internal assessment or a full paper into a tired evening produces attendance rather than progress. A ninety-minute weekend morning session - nobody tired, nothing else scheduled - is the most underused hour available on this coast and the one we usually recommend first.

faqs.question: Why do you publish Cambridge dates but no IB dates?
faqs.answer: Because the boards publish theirs and we could verify them, while the IB's own site blocks automated access, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed at source. For a family planning around a commute or a boarding arrangement, a wrong date would be worse than none. UAE schools sit the May session, and your school's coordinator holds the confirmed dates. Cambridge's June and November series and Pearson's published results dates are checkable, so we cite them.

faqs.question: Can you help with the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education subjects?
faqs.answer: With language and study skills, yes, within limits worth knowing. Private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, with instructional time counted in forty-minute lesson units and separate classes required for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of those subjects. Content for them is tightly controlled - additional or different material needs prior Ministry permission - so the honest offer is support with the language and with study technique rather than an alternative syllabus.

faqs.question: What will a tutor refuse to do with assessed work?
faqs.answer: Write any part of it. A tutor may read the criteria with the student, question a research question until the available data can answer it, teach the statistics or practical technique required, review a draft and explain which criterion it fails, and model the same move on other material. Writing, redrafting or editing the submitted text is not permitted, and IB Gram sells no completed assessments. The malpractice finding attaches to the student's diploma, which settles it regardless of distance or deadline.

faqs.question: What if nobody is free in our subject at the only hour that works?
faqs.answer: We say so and offer alternatives rather than a substitute: a different hour, a weekend morning, or a named date when a slot opens. Narrow courses sometimes have nobody available, particularly in the weeks before a series. For a family on this coast a generalist substitution is especially costly, because there is no local fallback and nobody nearby to notice the mismatch early - so a clear no, delivered quickly, is worth more than an optimistic yes.

sharjah/ib-igcse-tutor-near-me-in-khor-f.closingBody: Khor Fakkan, Kalba, Fujairah and Sharjah city differ in schools, supply and journeys. They do not differ in the paper your child sits, the scheme it is marked against, or the criteria behind an internal assessment. So identify the qualification precisely, ask the school for the subject guide, task sheets, internal deadline calendar and marked script, and send them to us. We will match a specialist nationally, read the work first, and run a free trial lesson over live video at no cost, scheduled around your real week.

intro.heading: Start from the date, not from the subject
paragraphs: Almost nobody searches for a tutor in the abstract. They search in week three of a term when a report has landed, or eight weeks before a paper, or the day after a mock came back. The useful first question is therefore not which subject but which date, because a plan built for eight weeks out looks nothing like a plan built for eight months out, and buying the wrong one is how tutoring money disappears without a grade moving.

Maryam Island is a waterfront development on the Sharjah lagoon, close to the Dubai border, and it has no bearing on this at all. The location changes the hour a session can start and nothing else. Whether a specialist can be reached from this address is not the constraint, because IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tuition is a service we offer only in India. Lessons are live, one-to-one, over video, in a slot held in Gulf Standard Time.

What does matter is which calendar you are on. A Cambridge IGCSE candidate in Sharjah is working towards the June series or the November series. A Pearson Edexcel International GCSE candidate is working towards May/June or November. A Diploma candidate is working towards the May session, with internal deadlines set by the school that bite considerably earlier than the examinations do. Households running both boards are tracking two calendars that collide in the spring.

The most important date in a Diploma year is not published by the IB at all. It is the school's own internal schedule for internal assessment drafts, Extended Essay stages and TOK components, which is usually issued in September and then quietly governs everything. Ask the coordinator for it. We will not publish IB session dates here, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a confidently wrong date on a page a parent acts on is worse than no date at all.

This page is organised as a countdown. There is an eight-week block set out week by week, a month-by-month read of where each kind of student should be, the Cambridge and Pearson dates with their published framing, what eight weeks of support actually costs at Sharjah market rates, and the places where the two calendars collide. The sibling pages for this development take the neighbourhood comparison and the provider-model comparison instead. Before any of it, one piece of advice that costs nothing and saves a great deal: find a recent marked paper or a returned draft with the teacher's comments on it and have it to hand. A specialist learns more from two minutes with a marked script than from twenty minutes of description, and when the window is short that difference decides whether the first session is useful or exploratory.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years of content assessed mainly in one examination fortnight, with coursework and practical components in some subjects. Because the grade is decided in a short window, paper technique in the final two months is worth more per hour than at any other point in the course.
programmes.countryNote: For a Sharjah candidate the live decisions are the June series and, after August results, the November resit window. Entry is handled by the school months ahead. Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct timetable for the zone, so ask the school which zone it sits in before working from any timetable.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service, scored to 45 points. Internal assessment carries weight in almost every subject, so the grade accumulates across two years rather than arriving in one fortnight.

Process documentation carries more marks than families expect, and the journal cannot be reconstructed afterwards. A short block of process coaching in the term before submission is the highest-return intervention available at this stage.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: In an eight-week block, drill the algebraic manipulation that fails under time pressure and work past papers by topic rather than by paper. The exploration should already be in draft; if it is not, it takes priority over revision.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator procedures are the fastest marks available late in the course, because they are mechanical and examinable. Modelling questions reward a rehearsed structure: define, fit, test, interpret.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Late in the course, written-explanation questions are where the marks are. Work through mark schemes for the standard explanations until the phrasing is automatic, then attempt Paper 3 under timed conditions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms repay concentrated late work because they are heavily weighted and pattern-based. Data questions need uncertainty handled rather than mentioned, which is a two-session fix.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: With eight weeks left, terminology precision and data-analysis technique move more marks than re-reading content. Higher Level extension topics are usually the ones met most recently and least securely.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy under time pressure and the evaluation command terms are the two late-stage priorities. Commentaries should be finished; if they are not, they come before revision in any sensible plan.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis improves with volume: one timed response a week, marked properly, for eight weeks. The individual oral rewards rehearsal of structure rather than memorised content.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Application to the given organisation is what separates a 5 from a 7, and it is a rehearsable habit. Quantitative tools are examinable, mechanical and the most commonly neglected marks in the subject.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: The prescribed-title essay and the exhibition both reward structure over content, which makes them unusually responsive to a short block of coaching. This is the component most often left too late in Sharjah schools.

igcseSubjects.description: Timed papers with the mark scheme open, twice a week, for eight weeks. Extended candidates should work the multi-topic problems specifically, because those are where the method marks are lost under pressure.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Give the alternative-to-practical paper its own sessions. It tests experimental reasoning, cannot be revised by reading notes, and is the paper Sharjah Extended candidates most often underperform on.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry first, because they carry the heaviest weight and the highest failure rate. Qualitative-analysis tables and organic nomenclature are pure memory and worth two late sessions.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Terminology precision is the quickest win: a loosely right answer scores nothing where the mark scheme names a term. Work the past-paper phrasing rather than the textbook phrasing.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
igcseSubjects.description: The summary task has strict rules and is highly trainable in a short block. Directed writing improves with one timed piece a week against a stated purpose and audience, marked properly each time.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (0450 / 4BS1)
igcseSubjects.description: Case-study application and evaluation structure, rehearsed on past stimulus material. A student who defines well and applies poorly can move a grade in eight weeks because the fix is a framework, not knowledge.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455 / 4EC1)
igcseSubjects.description: Diagram accuracy drilled until automatic: axes, correct shift, new equilibrium labelled. Data-response answers must quote the extract, which is a habit rather than an insight.

igcseSubjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
igcseSubjects.description: Pseudocode conventions, trace tables and number-base conversion are mechanical marks recoverable quickly. Theory of computer systems rewards past-paper phrasing over textbook reading.

sections.heading: What eight weeks can and cannot achieve
paragraphs: An eight-week block, used properly, reliably moves a grade when the problem is technique. It does not rebuild two years of missing content, and any provider who implies otherwise is selling you hope. The distinction is the single most useful thing on this page, because the two situations need opposite plans and families routinely buy the wrong one in a hurry.

Technique problems look like this: the student understands the topic in conversation, scores well on homework, and loses six to eight marks a paper to misread command terms, unshown method, poor timing and answers that are loosely right where the mark scheme wants a specific term. That is extremely responsive to timed practice with line-by-line correction, which is why the block below contains almost no teaching.

Content problems look different: the student cannot start the question, cannot recall the relationship, or has never met the topic because they transferred school or the class ran out of time. Eight weeks of timed papers will produce eight weeks of failed attempts and a demoralised student. The right plan there is content teaching, prioritised by mark weight, and an honest conversation about whether a November entry is the better route.

The trial lesson exists to tell you which you have. A specialist should set a real past-paper question, mark it against the mark scheme and name the problem in writing within the hour. If a provider cannot do that, they are guessing, and in an eight-week window there is no time to be wrong about the diagnosis.

sections.heading: The eight-week block, week by week
paragraphs: Here is the plan we actually run, so you can judge it or run it yourself. It assumes two sessions a week, one subject, and a student whose content knowledge is broadly intact. The structure matters more than the content: diagnosis first, correction in the middle, full papers at the end, and nothing new introduced after week six.

Week one is not teaching and parents sometimes object to that. It is a diagnostic: two past-paper sections attempted cold, marked properly, and a written list of the specific recurring errors. Everything afterwards is aimed at that list. A block that starts teaching in week one is a block that never finds out what was actually wrong.

Weeks two to five are the working weeks, and the pattern repeats: attempt, correct against the mark scheme, redo the same question type. The redo is the part that gets skipped and the part that does the work, because correction without repetition produces understanding without habit, and under exam pressure only habit survives.

Weeks six to eight shift to whole papers under timed conditions, with the error list reviewed after each. By week eight the list should be visibly shorter, and if it is not, the diagnosis in week one was wrong and we say so rather than running the clock down. That is the honest version of what a countdown block is.

Two practical rules hold the plan together. Nothing new is introduced after week six, because a topic met for the first time a fortnight before a paper will not be secure and will displace revision of things that were. And the student rests the night before each full paper rather than cramming, because the point of weeks six to eight is to rehearse the real conditions, and the real conditions include arriving tired or not.

sections.heading: Where you are in the year, and what to do about it
paragraphs: If you are not eight weeks from a paper, the plan is different, and the table below is the month-by-month version for a Sharjah household. Read your own row rather than the general advice, because the same amount of money buys very different outcomes depending on when it is spent.

The cheapest months in the whole year are September to November. There are no imminent deadlines, the student has evenings, and content can be taught properly rather than patched. A weekly hour starting in October costs less across the year than an emergency block in April and achieves considerably more, which is the least popular true thing in this market.

The most expensive stretch is March and April, particularly for a household running both boards. Diploma internal assessment deadlines, May session revision, IGCSE mocks and June series preparation all land within a few weeks, and a family that has not planned for it finds both children needing maximum support at once. The planning answer is to front-load the autumn, not to budget more for the spring.

August deserves its own note because it is a decision month rather than a working one. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the November entry window closes shortly afterwards. Agree the resit trigger rule in advance and act within days. Families who deliberate for three weeks commonly discover the deadline made the decision for them.

sections.heading: Counting back from the Cambridge and Pearson series
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The February and March series is offered to India only, and a page quoting it to a Sharjah parent has handed them a date that is wrong for their country.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November each year. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any session plan should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can be revised.

The administrative point Cambridge makes itself is worth repeating. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask your school which zone it sits in. A generic timetable found online is not good enough.

Working backwards from those fixed points gives the whole shape of a year: entries months ahead, coursework and practicals a term ahead, mocks a term ahead, the revision peak eight to twelve weeks out, and the resit decision in the days after results. Everything on this page is an attempt to put the right activity in the right one of those slots.

sections.heading: Counting back from the May session, without inventing dates
paragraphs: For the Diploma we will not publish a session or results date. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, which means no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and an unverified date on a page a parent plans around is a liability rather than a service. UAE schools sit the May session; for anything more specific, ask your school's IB coordinator and cite them.

That is less of a limitation than it sounds, because the examination date is not the date that governs a Diploma year. The internal schedule is: the school's own deadlines for internal assessment drafts, Extended Essay stages, TOK components and the Creativity, Activity, Service record. Those are published in September, they are enforced by the school, and they are what a tutoring plan should be built on.

Ask the coordinator for the schedule in writing and bring it to the first session. A tutor working from the real internal calendar will plan the block around a draft deadline in three weeks rather than an examination in seven months, which is almost always the correct priority. A draft submitted badly cannot be repaired later; a topic revised badly can be revised again.

The one date pattern worth planning for without any official source is the DP1 spring. Internal assessment drafts, the Extended Essay research question and the first mocks arrive within a few weeks of each other in every Diploma school we work with. Put hours into the autumn of DP1 specifically because that collision is coming, and nobody will warn you about it in September.

sections.heading: Mock fortnight and the session nobody books
paragraphs: Mocks are the best diagnostic a student gets all year and most families waste them. The marks come back, there is a conversation about effort, and the papers go in a drawer. Everything useful in them is in the detail of where the marks were lost, and that detail has a short shelf life, because within a fortnight the student no longer remembers what they were thinking when they wrote the answer.

The session to book is the post-mortem: one session, as soon as the papers are returned, spent going through them question by question against the mark scheme while the reasoning is still fresh. It produces a specific, short list of fixable habits, which is exactly the input an eight-week block needs. It is also the single highest-return session in the academic year, and almost nobody schedules it in advance.

During the mock fortnight itself, the sessions should change purpose rather than pause. Revising for tomorrow's paper is of limited value; reviewing yesterday's is of considerable value. Families often cancel tutoring during mocks on the grounds that the student is busy, which removes the one input that would make the mocks worth sitting.

For Diploma students the equivalent is the returned internal assessment draft with teacher comments. That document is a mark scheme applied to your child's own work, and a session spent reading it properly with a specialist is worth more than three sessions of general subject support. Keep it, and bring it.
bullets: Book the post-mock session before the mocks begin
Review yesterday's paper rather than revising for tomorrow's
Do not cancel tutoring during mock fortnight; change its purpose
A returned internal assessment draft is the Diploma equivalent

sections.heading: What a countdown block costs at Sharjah market rates
paragraphs: An eight-week block at two sessions a week is sixteen hours, so the arithmetic is easy to do once you know the bands. Read in October 2026, a qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase quoting AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more.

Sixteen hours at the qualified band is therefore roughly AED 2,400 to 4,800, and at the specialist band roughly AED 3,200 to 7,200. Bestimate's monthly estimate for specialist examination-year support is AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for a weekly session, which is consistent with those figures at double frequency. The budget band of AED 33 to 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, is not the right band for a technique block before a series.

In-home visits add the travel premium: AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's table and AED 200 to 500 with independent tutors, with monthly packages at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions against about AED 799 for eight online sessions. In a countdown block the travel premium is particularly poor value, because what you are buying is marked attempts and correction, which do not need anyone in the room.

The comparison worth making is against the alternative use of the same money: a weekly hour from October at the qualified band is about thirty hours across the year and costs more in total but considerably less per grade moved, because it prevents the situation the block exists to rescue. Every figure here is published by the provider named; none is an IB Gram price.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the breaks that interrupt a countdown
paragraphs: A countdown block rarely runs through eight clean weeks. Ramadan shortens school days and moves the useful study window, Eid takes days out, mid-term breaks arrive, and families travel. Planning for those interruptions is part of the plan rather than an exception to it, and a block that ignores them loses a quarter of its sessions.

During Ramadan we move slots rather than pausing. A post-Iftar session between roughly 8.30pm and 10pm works well for older students already keeping late hours, and a short early-morning session suits others. Decide which before the month begins, because a month of improvisation becomes a month of nothing, and in a countdown that is fatal rather than inconvenient.

Travel is easier to absorb than families expect, because nothing in the arrangement depends on a journey. The slot is held in Gulf Standard Time and the lesson follows the student, so a week away shifts the times rather than cancelling the week. This is the specific advantage of an arrangement with no travel in it, and in an eight-week window it is worth more than it would be in a year-long one.

The summer is the other calendar feature worth using deliberately. For a DP1 student it is the clearest opportunity in the programme: the Extended Essay question can be settled and one internal assessment substantially advanced when nothing else competes for the time. Two sessions a week for six weeks does it, and it buys back autumn evenings that would otherwise go to catching up.
bullets: Shift the slot in Ramadan rather than pausing; post-Iftar or early morning
Plan the interruptions into the eight weeks rather than around them

sections.heading: The line a tutor does not cross, whatever the deadline
paragraphs: Deadline pressure is precisely when the integrity line gets tested, and it is worth being explicit before you are under it. This market contains providers who sell completed assessed work; one page in this research advertises finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. A deadline in three days is the moment that offer looks reasonable, and it is the moment it is most dangerous.

What a tutor may do, even with a deadline tomorrow: teach the content, explain how the criteria or mark scheme award marks, discuss the research question the student chose, model structure on a different example, read the draft the student wrote and say where it is unsupported or unclear, and teach referencing and data handling.

What a tutor may not do, at any price and at any proximity to a deadline: write, rewrite, complete or edit the work to a finished state, or produce a worked version of the student's own task. We also do not reproduce or supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we reference them and link the official source.

There is a further rule about teachers. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Treat the ADEK wording as press-reported and verify it against the current policy document. We will not arrange it either way.

process.title: Tell us the date you are working to
process.description: The series or the internal deadline, and how many weeks away it is. That single answer determines whether you need a countdown block, a deadline rescue or weekly continuity, and it is the question most providers do not ask before quoting.

process.title: Send the evidence, not the summary
process.description: One recent marked paper or a returned draft with teacher comments, plus the board and code or the subject and level. A marked paper tells a specialist more in two minutes than a description does in twenty, and in a short window that difference matters.

process.title: A free trial that is the diagnosis
process.description: Week one of a countdown is diagnostic rather than instructional, and the trial lesson is where it starts. The tutor sets questions cold, marks them against the mark scheme and gives you a written list of the specific recurring errors the block will target.

process.title: Two slots a week, plus the interruptions
process.description: We fix two weekly times in Gulf Standard Time and plan around Ramadan, Eid, travel and the school's own deadline weeks at the outset, rather than losing sessions to them one at a time. In an eight-week block there is no room to lose four.

process.title: Review at week four against the list
process.description: Halfway through we check the error list from week one. Errors should be disappearing from it. If they are not, the diagnosis was wrong and we change the plan or the specialist immediately, because running the remaining weeks on a wrong diagnosis is the one thing that cannot be recovered.

whyPoints.title: We ask the date first
whyPoints.description: The plan for eight weeks out and the plan for eight months out are different products, and buying the wrong one is how tutoring money disappears without a grade moving. Most providers quote an hourly rate before asking what you are working towards.

whyPoints.title: We will tell you eight weeks is not enough
whyPoints.description: If the content was never learned, a countdown block produces failed attempts and a demoralised student. We say that and discuss a November entry instead, which costs us a sale and is the correct advice. A provider who says yes to every timeline is telling you about their pipeline.

whyPoints.title: The right calendar for this country
whyPoints.description: UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June and November series; the February and March series is India only. Several pages ranking for these searches publish February dates to Gulf families, which is a date a parent books around and loses money on.

whyPoints.title: No invented IB dates
whyPoints.description: We describe the May session and send you to your school's IB coordinator, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification. We plan Diploma work from the school's internal deadline schedule instead, which is the calendar that actually governs the year.

whyPoints.title: Rates you can check, costed as a block
whyPoints.description: The table prices sixteen hours at every published band, with the provider and the month for each figure. That is the number you are actually deciding on, and nobody else in this market publishes it in a form you can compare.

whyPoints.title: The line holds under deadline pressure
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, explain criteria and give feedback on the student's own draft, including the day before a deadline. They do not write or complete assessed work at any price. In this market finished work is openly sold, and a deadline is exactly when that offer gets accepted.

faqs.question: Is eight weeks enough to change my child's grade?
faqs.answer: If the problem is technique, yes, reliably. If the content was never learned, no, and we will say so rather than take the booking. Technique problems look like a student who understands the topic in conversation but loses six to eight marks a paper to misread command terms, unshown method and loose terminology. That responds very well to timed practice with line-by-line correction. A student who cannot start the questions at all has a content problem, and eight weeks of papers would produce eight weeks of failed attempts.

faqs.question: What should the first session contain if we are short of time?
faqs.answer: Diagnosis, not teaching, however counter-intuitive that feels when the clock is running. The first session should be two past-paper sections attempted cold and marked properly, producing a written list of the specific recurring errors. Everything after that aims at the list. A block that starts teaching in session one never finds out what was actually wrong, and in an eight-week window there is no time to discover in week five that you targeted the wrong thing.

faqs.question: How much does a sixteen-hour block cost in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: At published October 2026 rates, roughly AED 2,400 to 4,800 at the qualified online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, and roughly AED 3,200 to 7,200 at the specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; TutorChase quotes AED 270. Two monthly online packages at about AED 799 each would cover sixteen sessions for roughly AED 1,598. Those are the providers' own figures; for ours, take the free trial and ask.

faqs.question: We have mocks next week. Should we pause tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, change what the sessions are for. Revising for tomorrow's paper has limited value; reviewing yesterday's has considerable value, because the student still remembers their reasoning. The session worth booking is the post-mortem, as soon as the papers come back, going through them question by question against the mark scheme. It produces exactly the error list a countdown block needs, and it is the highest-return session in the year. Almost nobody schedules it in advance.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE series should we aim at if the student is behind?
faqs.answer: That is a real decision rather than a formality, and it is better made in March than in May. If content is substantially missing, entering the June series to see what happens often produces a grade nobody wanted and a resit anyway. A November entry with a properly paced build can be the better route. Pearson's June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026 and the autumn entry window closes shortly after, so if the plan is November, decide early and tell the school.

faqs.question: When do Diploma internal deadlines actually fall?
faqs.answer: Whenever your school says, which is why that schedule matters more than any date on this page. The school publishes internal milestones for internal assessment drafts, Extended Essay stages and TOK components, usually in September, and those are what govern a Diploma year. Ask the coordinator for it in writing and bring it to the first session. The one predictable pattern is the DP1 spring, when drafts, the Extended Essay question and the first mocks arrive within a few weeks of each other in every school we work with.

faqs.question: Why will you not tell me the IB exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because we cannot verify them, and a confidently wrong date on a page a parent plans around is worse than no date. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, which means no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools sit the May session, and that is as specific as we are prepared to be in writing. Ask your school's IB coordinator and cite them. Cambridge and Pearson dates we do give come from the boards' own published material.

faqs.question: Can we fit two sessions a week around a Sharjah school day?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, often with one weekday evening and one weekend morning. The weekday evening window between about 4.30pm and 7.30pm is the most contested slot in the emirate, and for a lagoon-district household with a Dubai-schooled child it may start later still. The weekend morning is easier to get, draws stronger tutors and gives an unbroken ninety minutes, which is what a full timed paper actually needs. Plan the pair together rather than hunting for two evening slots.

faqs.question: What happens to the block during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: The slots move rather than stopping. School days shorten and the useful study window shifts, so a 5pm session that worked in January is the wrong slot in Ramadan. A post-Iftar session between roughly 8.30pm and 10pm suits older students who are already keeping late hours, and a short early-morning session suits others. Decide which before the month starts, because in a countdown block a month of improvisation is not an inconvenience, it is the difference between the plan working and not.

faqs.question: Will tutoring follow us if we travel mid-block?
faqs.answer: Yes, because nothing in the arrangement depends on a journey. The slot is held in Gulf Standard Time and the lesson follows the student, so a week in another country shifts the session times for that week rather than losing them. In an eight-week block that matters more than it would across a year: losing two of sixteen sessions to a half-term trip removes an eighth of the plan, and an arrangement that requires a tutor to travel to an address simply cannot absorb it.

faqs.question: Our Diploma draft is due in four days and it is not good. What can a tutor do?
faqs.answer: A great deal, within a firm limit. They can read what your child has written and say where the argument is unsupported, where the method is unclear and where the brief has drifted, explain criterion by criterion where the marks sit, and teach referencing properly. They cannot write, rewrite, complete or edit it to a finished state. Four days before a deadline is exactly when the offer to produce the work starts looking reasonable, and exactly when accepting it risks the whole diploma rather than one component.

faqs.question: How fast can you match a tutor if we need to start this week?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Diploma subjects and Extended-tier IGCSE subjects, usually inside forty-eight hours and often the same day for a trial. For narrower requirements, a less common Higher Level option or a subject such as Computer Science 0478, allow five to ten days and expect us to say whether the specialist is UAE-based or teaching into your evening from another timezone. If you can take a weekend morning, the first available slot is almost always sooner.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting a block with four weeks left rather than eight?
faqs.answer: Four weeks can still recover specific mechanical marks: method shown, terminology precision, calculator procedures, diagram labelling, timing. Those are habits rather than knowledge and they respond quickly. What four weeks cannot do is close a content gap or rebuild confidence. So the honest answer is that a four-week block is worth buying if the trial lesson identifies mechanical losses, and is not worth buying if it identifies missing content. The diagnosis decides it, not the calendar.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest time of year to buy tutoring?
faqs.answer: September to November, by a wide margin, and almost nobody does. There are no imminent deadlines, the student still has evenings, and content can be taught properly rather than patched. A weekly hour from October costs more in total across the year than an emergency block in April but considerably less per grade moved, because it prevents the situation the block exists to rescue. The expensive months are March and April, when every family in Sharjah wants the same slots at once.

faqs.question: How will we know in week four whether the block is working?
faqs.answer: Against the error list written in week one, which is why that list exists. By week four two things should be visible: errors from the list no longer appearing in new attempts, and a timing problem quantified in minutes rather than described as rushing. If neither has happened, the week-one diagnosis was wrong, and we change the plan or the specialist immediately rather than running the remaining weeks on it. That is the one failure in a countdown that cannot be recovered later.
